question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Dhanya Varga, Chapter 8, verse 840):

प्रसाधिका तु नीवारस्तृणान्नमिति च स्मृतम् । नीवारः शीतलो य्राही पित्तघ्नः कफवातकृत् ।।८६।। यावनालो हिमः स्वादुर्लोहितः श्लेष्मपित्तजित् । अवृष्यस्तुवरो रूक्षः स्वेदकृत्कथितो लघुः ।।८७११ वर्षोषित सर्वधान्यं गौरवं परिमुञ्ठति । न तु त्यजति वीर्यं स्वं क्रमान्मुञ्ठत्यतः परम् ।।८९।। एतेषु यवगोध्मतिलमाषा नवा हिताः । पुराणा विरसा रूक्षा न तथा गुणकारिणः ।।९०।।
answer_text: Menstural disorders: The roots are useful. Digestive disease: A decoction of the root has been used to cure Kṛmi (Worms infestations), Anaha (Flatulence), Vibandha (Constipation) and Atīsāra (Diarrhea). External uses: It is use to relieve Sandhivāta (Osteoarthritis) and Āmavāta (Rheumatism) etc. painful conditions. NĪVĀRA Hin: Tīnī. Fam: Gramineae. Latin: Hygroryza aristata Nees. Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Prasādhikā and Trṇānna. Guṇa karma (Properties and indication): Nīvāra is Śītavīrya (Cold in potency), Grāhī (Absorbent), subsides Pitta doṣa, Increases Kapha and Vaṭa. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): South and South-east Asia found in still water, ponds and Lakes. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a crepping annual aquatic grass with slender culms. Leaves long linear, ovate- oblong. Flowers in pannicals 3-5cm.long spikelets 1-2cm.long. Grains oblong. Chemical constituents: Protiens and Aminoacids. Amayikaprayoga (Therepeautic uses): It is useful in diseases of Pitta and Mutragata vikar (Diseases of Urinary tract). YAVANĀLA Fam: Gramineae Hin: Juvar Latin: Sorghum vulgare Linn. Guṇa karma (Properties and indication): Yāvanāla is Śīta vīrya (Cold in poten- t cy), Swādu (Palatable), Subsides Kapha and Pitta, Avṛṣya (Mild Aphrodisiac), Kaṣāya (Astringent) in taste, Rūkṣa (Drying), Kledhakṛt (Increases moisture) and Laghu (Light for digestion). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is cultivated in most parts of India. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a strong perennial grass reaches upto 0.62.4 m. Leaves are 5- 75 cm. across resemble!ike maize. Flowers are in loose to dense spikes. Grains are small growing upto 3-4 mm. across. Chemical constituents: Carbohydrates, Fats, Proteins, Fibres, Hydrocyanic acid and Glycosides- Dhurin. Amayika prayoga (Therapeutic uses): It is useful in Pāṇḍu (Anemia), Prameha (Diabeties) and digestive disorders such as Śūla (Abdominal colic), Ānāha (Bloating), Admāna (Flatulance), Vibandha (Constipation). Dhānya when fresh they are Swādu (Palatable), Guru (Heavy for digestion) and Increases Kapha. When become one year old, acts as good Pathya (Diet) and Laghu (Light for digestion). When they are more than one year old, becomes old and losses it’s potency. But Yava, Godhūma, Tila and Māsa are best durning fresh state and benficial, when becomes old they are dry and Ineffective

वातबस्तिमाहवेगमित्यादि । बस्ति-कुक्षिनिपीडित इति बस्ती कुक्षौ च निपीडितः सम्पिण्डितो वायरिति सम्बन्धः बस्ति-कक्षी निपीडयन् इति पाठान्तरे बस्ति-कक्ष्यो रुजाकर इति - चिरंग - धारयतो - मूत्रं - त्वरया - नाम प्रवर्तते । मेहमानस्य मन्दं वा मूवातीतः समाउच्यते ॥॥

The former passage means the vāta trapped in the lower abdomen and stomach while the other term refers to the vāta causing morbidity in the lower abdomen and stomach. Thus, implication wise both of these passages are identical. Mūtrātīta (Incontinence of urine) That condition in which the person, who has suppressed the urge of urination for a long time, fails to void the urine with the normal speed but voids it very slowly is known as Mutrafita. 7

answer_text: As per the mythology, it is belived that when ejaculated seman of Lord Shiva fell on earth surface, Parad was formed. Based on the place of orgin, It is of four types white, red, yellow and black and in orderly it belongs to four races Brāhmana, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya and Sudra respectively. explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Visa-Upavisa Varga, Chapter 7, verse 734.

राजयक्ष्मणस्नैदोषिकस्यैकादशरूपाणि विभज्य व्याधिप्रभावाज्जायन्ते न तु सन्निपात- ज्वरलिङ्गवत् सर्वदोष्ट सर्वाणीत्याह स्वरभेदोऽनिलादित्यादि । शूलमंसपार्श्वयोरेव अंस- पार्क्षयोः सड्कोच एक एवं गणनीयः । अभक्तच्छन्दो भक्तारुचिः । कण्ठस्योद्ध्वंसः कण्ठभेदः उत्कासिका इति कार्तिकः - एकादशभिरेभिर्वा पड़भिर्वाडपि समन्वितम् । कासातीसार-पार्श्वार्ति-स्वरभेदारूचि-ज्वरीः - त्रिभिर्वा पीडितं लिहेेः कास-श्रासुगामयेः जह्याच्छोपार्दितं जन्तुमिच्छन् सुविमलं यशः ॥॥ सर्वेरर्धेस्त्रिभिर्वाडपि लिड़ैर्मांस-बलक्षये । युक्तो वर्ज्यश्चिकित्स्यस्तु सर्वरूपोऽप्यतोऽन्यथा ॥१ ॥ क्षीयमाणमतीसारनिपीडितम् । महाशनं चैव यक्ष्मणं परिवर्जयेत् ॥१ १ ॥ शूनमुष्कोदरंग क शुक्लाक्षमन्नद्वेष्टारमूर्ध्वश्वासनिपीडितम् कृच्छूपा बहुमेहन्तं यक्ष्मा हन्तीह मानवम् ॥१ ॥ असाध्यलक्षणमाह एकादशभिरित्यादि । एकादशभिरेभिरिति स्वरभेदादिभिः कण्ठो- द्ध्वसान्तेः । षड्भिरिति सुश्रुतेन षड्रूपाणि पठितानिभक्तद्वेषो ज्वरः श्वासः कासः र्शाणितदर्शनम् । स्वभेदश्च जायेत षङ्रूपं राजयक्ष्मणि सु०उ० इति । कासातिसार-पार्श्वार्ति-स्वरभेदारुचि-ज्वरैः इति तु कस्यचितन्त्रस्य षड्रूपाणि माधवकरेण लिखितानीति । एतानि चैकादश षड्वा त्रिरूपाणि वा प्रायोभावित्वादुक्तानि अन्यतमरूप- परिहारात् रूपान्तरयोगेऽप्येकादशतं षट्त्वं च स्यादेव तथाहि चरको निदाने एकादशरूपाणि पाठेत्वा चिकित्सितेऽपि वेगरोधादिकारणचतुष्टयजे प्रतिकारणं चतुर्घा एकादशरूपाणि पठित- वान् । यथा कासोंऽसतापो वैस्वर्य ज्वरः पार्श्व-शिरोरुजा । छर्दने रक्त-कफयोः श्वासो वचांप्रहोऽरुचिः ॥ रूपाण्येकादशैतानि यक्ष्मणि षडिमानि च । कासो ज्वरः पार्श्वशुले स्वर- वचंग्रहोऽरुचिः ॥ चचि - इति । एकादशवचननैवं बोधयतिसम्पूर्णे यक्ष्मण्येकादशैव रूपाणि भवन्तीति जह्मादिति बलमांसक्षये सति इति शेषः तथा च चरकः- वातव्याधिरपस्मारी कुष्ठी व्रध्नी चिरज्वरी । गुल्मी च मधुमेही च राजयक्ष्मी च यो नरः ।। अचिकित्स्या भवन्त्येते बल-मांसपरिक्षयात् । स्वल्पेष्वपि विकारेषु भिषगेतान विवर्जयेत् ॥ च०इ० - इति । सर्वेरित्यादि । ननु सर्वरूपाण्येकादश एका- दशानामधं सार्धपञ्च भवन्ति तत्र कतमस्य रूपस्यार्धत्वं किम्भूतं वा भवति उच्यतेएकस्य रूपस्यार्धत्वासम्भवे षट्पञ्चरूपयोरर्धयोरुकृष्टत्वात् षड्रूप एवार्धो ग्राह्यः । लिङ्गैर्युक्त इति सम्बन्धः । अतोऽन्यथेति बल-मांसक्षयाभावे सति । महाशनं क्षीयमाणमित्येकमसाध्यलक्षणमु अरिष्टरूपत्वात् अतीसारपीडितमिति द्वितीयं यक्ष्मणो मलायत्तजीवितस्योक्तत्वात् शूनमुष्को- दरमिति तृतीयं मुष्कशोथस्य विरेकसाध्यत्वेन विरुद्धोपक्रमत्वात् । शुक्लेत्यादि । शुक्लाक्ष- त्वादय एकैकशोऽसाध्यलक्षणानि ।।- बलवन्तं का प्रक्रियासहम् । ज्वरानुबन्धरहितं दीप्ताग्निमकृशंक नाम नरमू ॥१३॥ उपक्रमेदात्मवन्तं - answer_text: Tridoşa - aggravation causes rajyakşmā (consumption). Eleven features have been counted here as per the dosa-relation. It is understandable that as in the case of the fever of Iridoşa-origin, those features are connected to Tridosa consumption. There is pain in the scapular area and flanks only. Painfulness and shrinking are separate features of these parts. Abhaktacchanda relates to distaste of food. Kanṭhasyodhvamsa refers to damaging or irritation of the throat. According to Kārtika, cough is caused due to situation of utkāsikā. Prognosis of consumption The physicians desiring reputation should avoid cases of tubercu¬ (SS., Ut. 41.14, 15) losis that manifests presence of all the eleven features of the disease described above. Even if there is a case reflecting the six features viz, cough, diarrhoea, pain in the flanks, hoarseness of voice, anorexia and fever the wise physicians should not take up the case. The wise should also discard the cases of tuberculosis that manifest the three features including cough, dyspnea, and appearance of blood in sputum. 8-9 (CS. Ci. S. 8.47) Moreover, a patient who suffers from wasting of muscles and strength is also fit for refusal if he manifests all the eleven, six or the three features described above. However, the patient even if he is having all the 11 symptoms described above could be cured if he retains his muscles and strength. 10 SS. Ut. 41.31) The patients of yaksmā who eat large quantities of eatables but still undergo wasting; who are having diarrhoea, oedema of the scrotum and abdomen are also to be avoided. 11 (SS. Sū. 33.20) Yakyma kills such persons who have developed whiteness of eyes, have aversion to food, have a difficult breathing and urination. 12 The eleven features as mentioned above are from Svarabheda (hoarseness of the voice) to Kanthodhvamsa (irritation in the throat) (as per 6th and 7th stanzas). Six features of Rājyakṣmā have been included in the statement of Suśruta quoted in the parantheses in this chapter. These features include bhaktadvesa, jvara, svasa, kasa, raktasthi- vana and the sdvarabheda (SS. Ut. 41.11). In the opinion of some texts, kāsa (cough), atisāra, pārśvaśūla, aruci and fvara and the like features as per stanza 8 have been quoted by Madhavakara from other texts. These sets of cleven, six, or three symptoms have been presented in probability as some of these may be seen in the patients. The transformation from eleven to six or vice-versa can always occur. Caraka assigned the origin of these eleven features to the four reasons, i.e. Vegarodha or suppression of natural urges etc., in Nidānasthāna and in Cikilsāsthāna, he states, 'cough, pain in the scapular region, hoarseness of voice, fever, pain in flanks and head, vomiting of blood and phlegm, dyspnea, constipation and distaste are the eleven features of consumption and the six features of this disease are cough, fever, pain in the flanks, hindrance of voice hoarseness), constipation and distaste (CS, Cf. 8, 44 - 45). It is clear that manifestation of consumption is complete when eleven features are visible. The patient should be discarded when the individual has been emaciated in his strength and muscles. Also in the it is stated that the individuals suffering from vala vyadhi (neurological disorder), epilepsy, leprosy, chronic fever, vatik oppression, diabetes and consumption, become incurable due to emaciation of strength and musculature. Their treatment should be avoided by a wise physician (CS. In. 9. 8-9). In fact, half of eleven are to be five and a half of the features. How can there be a half symptom? It is to be understood that the half of eleven should be taken to mean six features only. Excessive eating by an emaciating person is a bad omen. Atisara (diarrhoea) is also considered as a complication of consumption as its patient is left with only mala after losing all the important tissues and the stool to support his life. Swelling of the testes is also considered as a complication of the disease. It has only one way to be managed and that is by purgation that is contra-suggested in consumption. Turning the colour of eyes into white, etc. are the features of incurable consumption. Curability of consumption (SS. Ut. 41. 20), Treatment can be given to the patients of yakṣmā who do not have fever, who are strong, able to withstand the discomforts of treatments, who are of a strong will and proper digestive capacity, and who has not been emaciated. 13

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 67):

विशस्तेष्वपि गात्रेषु यथा शुक्रं न दृश्यते। सर्वदेहाश्रितत्वाच्च शुक्रलक्षणमुच्यते॥ १॥ तदेव चेष्टयुवतेर्दर्शनात्समरणादपि। शब्दसंश्रवणात्समर्शात्संहर्षाच्च प्रवर्तते॥ २॥ सुप्रसन्नं मनस्तत्र हर्षणे हेतुरुच्यते। आहाररसयोनित्वादेवं स्तन्यमपि स्त्रियाः ॥ ३ ॥ तदेवापत्यसंस्पर्शाहर्शनात्मरणादपि। ग्रहणाच्च शरीरस्य शुक्रवत्संप्रवर्तते। स्नेहो निरन्तरस्तत्र प्रस्त्रवे हेतुरुच्यते॥ ४॥ ) ( सु.उ. १०) गुरुभिर्विविधेरन्नैर्दुष्टैर्दोषैः प्रदूषितम्। क्षीरं मातुः कुमारस्य नानारोगाय कल्पते॥ १॥ मधुकोशः स्तनाश्रितत्वेन स्तन्यदुष्टिमाह-गुरुभिर्विविधैरित्यादि। गुरुभिरत्नैहेंतुभूतैयें दुष्टा दोषास्तैः प्रदूषितम्॥ १॥ कषायं सलिलप्लावि स्तन्यं मारुतदूषितम्। कट्वम्ललवणं पीतराजीमत् पित्तसंज्ञितम्॥ २॥ कफदुष्ट घनं तोये निमज्जति सपिच्छलम्। द्विलिङ्गं द्वन्द्वजं विद्यात् सर्वलिङ्गं त्रिदोषजम्॥ ३॥ मधुकोशः स्तन्यदुष्टिलक्षणमाह-कषायमित्यादि। सलिलप्लावीति सलिले यदुत्पलवते लाघवात् तत् सलिलप्लावि। एतदुपलक्षणं, तनुत्वाद्यपि बोद्धव्यम्। कट्वम्ललवणमिति कट्वतिक्तं, तिक्तेऽपि कट्शब्दप्रवृत्तेरिति वदन्ति। पीतराजीमदिति पीतरेखायुक्त, तत्रापि नीललोहिताश्च राज्यो ज़ेयाः। पित्तसंज़ितमित्यत्र संयुतमिति पठान्तरम्। तोये निमज्जति गुरुत्वात्। अतिमाधुर्याद्यपि बोध्यम्। प्रसन्नस्य तु साधारणं मधुरपाण्डुत्वम्। अभिघातेनापि स्तन्यं दुष्ट संभवत्येव, किन्तु तस्य वातिकस्तन्यलक्षणैरेव संग्रहणं कर्तव्यम्। स्तन्यस्वरूपं च सुश्रुतेनोक्तं-तद्यथा-'रसप्रसादो मधुरःपक्काहारनिमित्तजः। कृत्स्नदेहात् स्तनौ प्राप्तः स्तन्यमित्यभिधीयते॥’ (सु.नि. १०) इति॥ २–३॥ अदुष्ट चाम्बुनिक्षिप्तमेकीभवति पाण्डुरम्। मधुरं चाविवर्णं च प्रसन्नं तत् पशस्यते॥ ४॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने स्तन्यदुष्टिनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ६७॥ मधुकोशः अविकृतस्तन्यमाह-अदुष्टमित्यादि । अम्बुनिक्षिप्तमेकीभवति सर्वात्मना जलेन सहैकीभवतीति बोध्यं, वातादिदुष्टस्याप्येकदेशेनैकीभावोपलम्भात् । अविवर्णमिति अविद्यमानवातादिदुष्टवर्णम् । एतत् समदोषप्रकृति- क्षीरस्य प्रसन्नस्य लक्षणम्। अन्येत्वविवर्णमित्यत्र नञ् ईषदर्थे, तेन यद्वातादिप्रतिवर्णानुविद्धमंपि पाण्डुरमल्प- दुष्टत्वात्तद् गृह्नन्ति। केचित् पाण्डुरस्थाने ‘सर्वशः’ इति पठन्ति, तदा सर्वात्मना जलेन सहैकीभवतीति व्यक्तोऽर्थः। अत्र पक्षे अविवर्णमित्यनेनैवादुष्टाशुक्लवर्णता ज्ञेया । प्रसन्नं प्रकृतिस्थम्॥ ४॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां स्तन्यदुष्टिनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥ ६७॥
answer_text: Diagnosis of the disorders of Breast-milk) The comparison of breast-milk with semen with regards to origination and discharge (Though it exists all over the body, the semen is not seen on cutting any part of the body. The same ejaculates out by the pleasure caused by appearance, remembering, hearing the signs of her presence, touch (coitus) of an young lady of one’s own liking. The reason here for this is - pleasant condition of the mind. Since it is originated from the āhararasa, the breast milk in the women is also like this. By touch of the progeny, by looking at them, remembering them holding them-the breastmilk due to mental attachement-discharges out from the breasts.) Su.Ni.10, Due to consumption of heavy foods, the dosas aggravate and ultimately vitiate the breast-milk which in turn causes many diseases to the child. 1. Since the breast is the seat of breast-milk, the disorders of breast-milk are being explained after those of breast are mentioned in the previous chapter. The breast milk is vitiated by the dosas aggravated due to heavy foods etc. 1. Signs of breast milk as per dosa - affliction Stanya Dusti Nidāna The breast-milk vitiated by vāta tastes kaṣāya (Astringent) and floats on water; due to pitta affliction, it tastes kaṭu (pungent), sour and salty and putting in water shows yellowish lines and that breast-milk afflicted by kapha is heavy and sticky and sinks in water. Both the signs are observed when affected by two of the dosa and all are seen when the breast-milk is vitiated by tridosa. 2, 3. Salilaplāvi means that which floats on water due to lightness. The thin nature is also to be included here. katu pungent; bitterness also should be included here. Pitarajimat means showing yellow coloured lines on putting in water; bluish and reddish lines are also seen here. It sinks due to heaviness. This happens due to over sweetness. Blemishless breastmilk is in ordinary (mild) sweet taste and pale in colour. Due to abhighāta injury also the breastmilk gets vitiated. There the vāta afflicted signs are seen. Susruta said about the breast milk, "The breastmilk pro¬ duced by well digested food comes (into the breasts) from the whole body. It looks pleasant, clear and sweet in taste". (Su.Ni.10) 2-4 Signs of pure breast-milk The pure (unvitiated) breastmilk is in pale colour, sweet in taste, not having any particular colour, clear, and gets mixed up with water (readily). 4. Thus ends the chpater on diagnosis of vitiated breast milk in the Madhava's book on diagnosis written by Śrīmādhavakara. 67. Mādhavanidānaṃ Ambunikṣiptamekībhavati means when put in water, the breast milk completely gets mixed up with water and does not float or sink. The vāta etc., - afflicted breastmilk also mixes to some extent. Avivarnam means does not have any colour that is seen when afflicted by vāta etc.. This clarity is the feature of the proper breastmilk. Some take avivarṇa as having slight discolouration; then in the case of normal Vāta - dominated also pale colour is seen and that is taken as slightly vitiated. In the place of pāṇḍura, some read, sarvaśaḥ. Then it is clearly understood that it mixes with water completely. In that case avivarna should mean pure white colour; prasanam means in natural condition. 4. Thus ends the diagnosis of vitiated breast-milk in the Madhukosa commen¬ tary written by Śrikaṇathadatta. 67. ****
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 67.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 3):

पित्तज्वरेऽतीसारपाठाज्ज्वरातीसारयोरन्योन्योपद्रवत्वाच्च ज्वरानन्तरमतीसारमाह- गुर्वित्यादि । गुरुशब्देन मात्रागुरु गृह्वते यथाऽतिमात्रोपष्टुक्तो रक्तशाल्यादिः तथा स्वभावगुरु च मापादिः अथवा गुणतः पाकतश्च । अतिशव्दः स्थूलातेः सह सम्बध्यते । स्थूलं संहतावयवं यथालड्डुक-पिष्टकादि । शीतलं स्पराहियाच्च । विरुद्धमिति संयोग-देश-काल- मात्रादिभिर्विरुद्ध यथाक्षीरमत्स्यादि तच्च वहुप्रकार्र सुश्रुते हिताहितीयेऽध्याये सु०सू० चरके चात्रेयमद्रकाप्यीयाध्याये च०सू० द्रष्टव्यम् । अध्यशने पूर्वदिनाहारेऽजीर्णि भोजनम् । उक्त हि चरकेभुक्त पूर्वानशेषे तु पुनरध्यशनं मतम् । चचि इति एवं सर्वत्र । अजीर्णम् अपक्वमन्नम् । विषमम् अकालादिभोजनम् । उक्ते हि सुश्रुत क वहु स्तोकमकाले वा तज्जेयं विषमाशनम् सु०सू० इति एवं सवंत्र विपमैः इत्यत्र स्थाने असात्म्यैः इति पाठान्तरम् । भोजनैरिति विरुद्धादिभिः सर्वैः सम्बध्यते । स्नेहाद्वैरिंति के स्नेहा के स्नेहपानं के स्नेहाद्वैरिंद येषां के तेज स्नेहाद्वाः के स्वेद-वमन- विरेचनानुवासननिरूहाः तैरतियुक्तैरिति अतियोगयुक्तैः । एतच्च यथायोग्यं बोध्यं वमनाति- योगस्यातिसारकारणत्वायोगात् । मिथ्यायुक्तैरिति हीनयोगयुक्तैः वमनादिकर्मणां मिथ्यायोगा- भावात् हीनयोगात्तु ते दोषानुत्क्लेश्यातीसाराय स्युः । ननु कदाचिद्वमनं प्रयुक्तं विरेकं करोति विरेकश्च वमनमिति दर्शनातेषां मिथ्यायोगः सम्भवत्येव । न सोऽप्ययोग एवेति सिद्धान्तः । यदक्तं चरकेयोगः सम्यक् प्रवृत्तिः स्यादतियोगोऽतिवर्तनम्। अयोगः प्रातिलोम्येन न चाल्पं वा प्रवर्तनम् ।। च०सि० इति । विषमत्र स्थावरमुच्यते अधोगत्वातु कार्तिकस्त्वाहविषं दूषीविषं तल्लक्षणेष्वतीसारपाठात् । दुष्टाम्बुमद्यातिपानैरिति दुष्ट व्यापन्ने दृष्टयोरम्बुमद्ययोः पानात् अदुष्टयोरप्यतिपानात् । यदा चरकः दुष्टमद्यपानीयातिपानात् च०चि० इति । सात्म्यर्तुपर्यायैरिति सात्म्यविपर्ययैर्र्रतुविपर्ययैश्व सात्म्य- विपर्ययोऽसात्म्यम् । न च पूर्वक्तिन असात्म्यैः इत्यनेन पौनरुक्त्यमु उक्ते हि चरके आत्रेयभद्रकाप्योये द्विविधं हि सात्म्यं प्रकृतिसात्म्यमभ्याससात्म्यं च । इति आहाराचार भेदादन्नपानभेदाद्वा न पौनरुक्त्यमित्यन्ये । जलाभिरमणेरिति जलक्रीडादिभिः । वेगविधातैरिति मूत्रपुरीषादीनाम् । क्रिमिदोषत इति क्रिमिंभिः पक्वामाशयदूषणात् क्रिमिजनितवातादिकोपादा । एतानि च निदानानि यथासम्भवं वातादीना वोद्धव्यानि दोष-व्याधिहेतुत्वख्यापनाथं पठितानि । एवमन्यत्रापि निदानविशेषपाठे प्रायो द्रष्टव्यमिति - संशम्यापां धातुरम्निं प्रवृद्धः शक्रन्मिश्रो वायुनाऽधः प्रणुन्नः । सरत्यतीवातिसारं तमाहव्याधिं घोरं षड्विधं तं वदन्ति ॥ एकैकशः सर्वश्रश्रापि दोषैः शोकेनान्यः षष्ठ आमेन चोक्तः ॥॥ - - - answer_text: The presentation of the discussion on atisara after the description of the diseases jvara has been done on account of 1. reference to atisāra in the context of pitta jvara as above; and 2, the fact that jvara and atisara are implications of each other. The term guru refers to the heaviness in general. In the present context, the term has been used to indicate extra amount of food taken. It is suggested here that excess intake of cereals as red paddy that are light in property may produce heaviness. The term guru also refers to the consumption of items that possess heaviness in terms of their natural quality e.g. the black- gram. The term sthula refers to solid consistency like sweetmeats and foods that are made with flour. The coldness (śītala) referred to here implies coldness that manifests both by touch and by naturally inherent potency in the item of food related. The term viruddha or incompatibility relates to the disharmonious combination in terms of natural properties of the items, related place, time, dosage etc., e.g. combination of milk and fish etc. Numerous combinations prove incompatible like this. They have been detailed by Caraka in the section Atreyabhadrakāpyīya (CS, Sī, 26) and Suśruta in the section Hitāhitāya (SS. Sū. 20). The term Afīrṇa bhojana signifies the food that has not been properly cooked. The term adhyaśana refers to the habit or act of taking meals before allowing the previously taken meal to digest (CS, Ci. 15.236). Vişama is untimely consumption of food. In the opinion of Suśruta either small quantity of food or untimely food is to be considered as Visama or irregular (SS. Sii. 46.508). In some readings of the term visama has been replaced by the term asatmya. The term snehādyaih etc. refers to the atiyoga or over-adoption of measures like application of oil on the body, sudation, emesis, purgation, nasal medication, unctuous enema, and decoction-enema. Proper movement of dosas is Yoga, over movement is Atiyoga and reversal, a little or no movement of dosas is called Ayoga, according to Caraka (CS. Si. 6.31). The term visa or poison should be taken in this context to be the poison of herbal origin as it is only that has the property of downward movement and thus, produces diarrhoea. The commentator Kārtika opines that the term viṣa here refers to the duṣīviṣa as it is considered one of the regular causes of diarrhoea. The term dusta generally means polluted. In the present context, the term has been used in reference to the prohibition of the consumption of polluted water and alcohol even in lesser quantity as it causes diarrhoea. It may also be noted that as per the instruction of Caraka over-consumption of liquor and water may also produce diarrhoea (CS. Ci. 19.10). The passage starting from the satmyarturparayayaih refers to the taking of incompatible foods and indulging in habits that are antagonistic to the seasonal compatibility. The term asaimya has been referred to again in order to stress this factor. It may be noted that satmya has been divided into two types by Caraka: 1. Prakṛti sātmya and 2. Abhyāsa sātmya (CS, Vi. 1. 20-22). As this reference pertains to the foods and regimen, scholars opine that the reference of term satmya here does not make a case of repetition. The other causes of diarrhoea have been referred to through the terms vegavighāta and krimidoṣa. The term vegavighāta means holding of the call of nature like the urge to pass urine and to defecate. The term krimidoşa suggests the instrumentality of worms in causing the disease. The term also involves the vitiation of vāta and the like dosas through the worms. All the above factors have been detailed in order to suggest the significance of the dosas only. Thus, the significance of dosas should be stressed in reference to pathogenesis in all the diseases. Pathogenesis of diarrhoea (SS. Ut. 40.6, 7.1) When the liquid ingredients of the body increase in quantity, they subdue the digestive fire and get mixed with the faecal matter which moves downwards and comes out by vāta and passed out repeatedly. This condition is called diarrhoea (atisūra) which is severe and of six types. The six varieties are identified through the following: one from each of the three dosas, one from the combination of the three dosas together, the fifth one from grief and the sixth from the ama or undigested food. 4

Fam: Menispernaceae Hin: Patha, Lagupatha Eng: Velvet leaf Paryāyanāma (Synonymes): Ambaṣṭhā, Ambaṣṭhakī, Prācīnā, Pāpacelikā, Ekāṣṭhīlā, Rasā, Pāthikā and Varatiktikā Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Pāṭhā is Uṣna vīrya (Hot in potency), Kaṭu rasa (Pungent in taste), Tīkṣṇa (Penetrating), Subsides Vāta and Kapha, Laghu (Light for digestion), It cures Sūla (Abdominal colic), Jvara (Fever), Chardi (Vomiting), Kusṭa (Leprosy), Atisāra (Diarrhoea), Hṛdruja (Cardiac pain), Dāha (Burning sensation), Kandu (Itching), Viṣa (Poisonous manifestation), Swāsa (Dyspnoea), Krimi (Worm infestations), Gulma (Abdominal tumours), Udararoga (Abdominal disorders) and Vrna (Wounds). Bheda: There are two varieties of Pāṭhā has been mentioned ā. Laghu pāṭhā b. Rajapāṭhā. Cissampelos pareira Linn, is taken as Laghupāṭhā. The source drugs are used in the name of Rājapāṭhā are cyclea peltata Hook.f., Stephania glabra Miers. and Stephania japonica glabra Miers. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Tropical and sub tropical parts of India. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a climber with tomentose branches. Leaves simple, 2.5-10cm.long, ovate or orbicular, alternately arranged, obtuse apex and more or less cordate base. Flowers unisexual small yellow- white in axillary panicles. Fruit drupe 6mm. in diameter, red when ripe contains many discrete seeds. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Mūla (Roots). Chemical constituents: Alkaloids Bererine and Classampeline saponin and quarternary ammonium bases, Flavonol and Sterol

question:

answer_text: In continuation of the diseases of sense organs now the diseases of nose are being explained. To begin with, apīnasa is explainòd. Anahyate means being blocked by kapha which is dried up by vāta. Praklidyate means gets wet. Dhūpyati means experiencing burning sensation. Gandhān means the odours good or bad felt due to blocking of the nose. The dosa causing nāṣāroga would also vitiate the tongue; that is why the taste perception is also hindered. Anila slesmabhavam means caused by Vātakapha. But somewhere it is mentioned that apīnasa is caused by pitta and kapha; as per that statement, the slesma that exists in the brain, when afflicted (boiled) by pitta, there will be blood and copious, sticky discharge of phlegm Nāsā Roga Nidāna through the nostril associated with itching, burning sensation and ulceration - this condition is known as apinasa. Then how is this non-controversial? It is like that - because of the pathogenesis says Kārtika. As per the above text and symptoms, the relation of pitta can also be assumed. Gadādhara reads it as “analaśleṣma bhava” and clears the controversy by saying it is judicious to label it as caused by pitta-slesma. pratiśyāyasamāna lingaṃ - similar to the symptoms of pratisyāya - means similar to vātakaphaja pratiśyāya symptoms. Pūtinasya (Atropic Rhinitis) When the over boiled/baked/burnt dosa at the throat and roof of the palate get mingled with vāta - it will discharge putrified matter from the mouth and nose this condition is called Pūtinasya. 2. (Su.u. 22)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 58, verse 2.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 61):

मधुकोशः आर्तवातिप्रवृतौ उपद्रवानाह-तस्यातिवृत्तौ दौर्बल्यमित्यादि। रोगाश्च वातजा इति आक्षेपककम्पादयः॥ २॥ आमं सपिच्छाप्रतिमं सपाण्डु पुलाकतोयप्रतिमं कफात्तु। सपीतनीलसितरक्तमुष्णं पित्तार्तियुक्तं भृशवेगि पित्तात्॥ ३॥ रूक्षारुणं फेनिलमल्पमल्पं वातार्ति वातात् पिशितोदकाभम्। सक्षौद्रसर्पिर्हरितालवर्णं मज्जप्रकाशं कुणपं त्रिदोषात्॥ ४॥ तं चाप्यसाध्यं प्रवदन्ति तज्ज्ञा न तत्र कुर्वीत भिषक् चिकित्साम्। शश्वत् स्त्रवन्तीमास्त्रावं तृष्णादाहज्वरान्विताम्। क्षीणरक्ता दुर्बलां च तामसाध्यां विनिर्दिशेत्॥ ५॥ मधुकोशः श्लैष्मिकादिभेदेन विशेषलक्षणान्याह-आममित्यादि। आममामरसानुविद्दम्। सपिच्छाप्रतिममिति पिच्छा शाल्मल्यादिनिर्यासः, तत्सदृशं पिच्छिलमित्यर्थः, सशब्द ईषदर्थे। पुलाकतोयप्रतिमं प्रक्षालितपललतोयसदृशम्, अन्ये पुलाकं गवेधुकमाहुः। पित्तर्तियुक्त दाहचिमिचिमादयिक्तम्। भूशवेगि बहुवेगि। वातार्ति तोदादिलक्षणम्। पिशितोदकाभ मांसप्रक्षालनजलसदृशम्। सक्षौद्रसर्पिर्हरितालवर्णमिति नानावर्णत्वं त्रिदोषकोपादेव। क्षौद्रवर्ण मनाक्कपिलं, सर्पिवर्णं विलीनघृतवत्' किश्चिदरुणं च, मजप्रकाशं मजा अस्थिस्नेहः तत्समं, कुणपं शवगन्धि। तच्चाप्यसाध्यमिति चिकित्सानिवृत्त्यर्थम्॥ ३-५ ॥ मासान्निष्पिच्छदाहार्ति पञ्चरात्रानुबन्धि च । नैवातिबहुलात्यंत्यंत्यमार्तवं शुद्धमादिशेत् ॥ ६ ॥ शशासृक्प्रतिमं यच्च यद्वा लाक्षारसोपमम्। तदार्तवं प्रशंसन्ति यच्चाप्सु न विरज्यते॥ ७॥ ( सु.शा. २) इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदानेऽसृग्धरनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ६१॥ मधुकोशः विशुद्धार्तवलक्षणमाह-मासादित्यादि। अपिच्छिलमदहामशूलादिवेदनम्, निष्पिच्छदाहार्तीति एतेन विकृतवातादिलिङ्करहितमित्यर्थः । पञ्चरात्रानुबन्धीति पञ्चरात्रं प्रभूतप्रवृत्त्याऽनुबध्नातीत्यर्थः । अल्पप्रवृत्त्या पञ्चरात्रात् परतोऽप्यनुबध्नाति। तुक्तं हारीते-‘षोडशदिवासान्यूतुकालः’ इति। विदेहेऽप्युक्तम्-‘स्त्रीणामृतुर्भवति षोडशवासराणि' इति । शशासुगित्यादिना वर्णद्वयं वातादिप्रकृतिभेदात्। यच्चाप्सु न विरज्यत इति येनार्तवेन रक्नितं वस्त्रमप्सु प्रक्षालितं सल्लेहितं न भवति तद्विशुद्धम्। तथा च हिरण्याक्षः–‘सुरेन्द्रगोपसङ्काशं स्त्रिग्धं च मधुगन्धि। अपिच्छिलमशीतं च यद्वासो न विरञ्नयेत्’ इति॥ ६–७॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायामसृग्दरनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥ ६१ ॥
answer_text: Vata diseases means - Aksepaka (convulsions), Kampa (trembling) etc.. Specific symptomatology of dosa based asrgdara and incurability The discharge in kaphaja asrgdara is in the form of undigested stuff, sticky, pale in colour and looking like water - that is obtained by washing pulaka (coix barbata). In pitta type, the discharge is yellowish - blue, black, red in colour, warm, associated, with pitta troubles excessive in flow. In vata type of discharge, it will be not oily, froathy less in quantity, associated with vāta disorders and looks like meat - washed water and in tridosa dominant asygdara the discharge looks like mixture of honey and ghee, in the colour of Haritāla (orpiment); it also looks like the bone marrow and has putrified smell. This sannipata type of asrgdara is told to be incur¬ Mādhavanidānaṃ able and therefore the physician should not take it up for treatment. When the discharge is continuous, associated with thirst, burning sensation and fever, when the women suffers from loss of blood and is emaciated, such condition is also to be known as incurable. 3-5. Amaṃ means mixed with undigested stuff. Sāpicchā pratimaṃ looks as if mixed with gum (of trees like Bombax malabaricum). The prefix sa in this word indicates lesser such appearance. Pulaka is gavedhuka (coix barbata). Pittarti burning sensa¬ tion and feeling of cimacima etc. Bhrsavegi means fast in flow. Vātārti Vāta - provoked troubles - means pinning sensation etc. Pisitodakabham means like meat washed water. The colour of mixture of honey, ghee, orpiment is typical mixed colours which is due to Sannipata alone. Honey-colour is slightly blackish, ghee colour means as if mixed with ghee and slightly redish. Majjā prakāśa means look¬ ing like bone-marrow. Kunapa means swelling like that of dead body (dead-tissue). That is also incurable" means to deny treatment. 3-5. The charecteristics of pure menstural blood The menstrual blood that flows for five days, once in a month, without stickiness, burning sensation and pain, not excessive and net very less in quantity -is to be known as pure menstruation. It should look like the blood of the rabbit and lac - water solution. It should not stain the cloth on washing with water. Such artava is considered healthy. 6. 7. Thus ends the chapter on diagnosis of Asrgdara (menorrhagia) in the Madhava’s book on diagnosis written by Sri Madhavakara. 61. Asrgdara Nidāna Nispicchadaharti means - having no stickiness, no burning sensation and no pain. This shows the absence of the symptoms of aggravated dosas. Pañcarātrānubandhi means continuosly flowing for 5 nights. Minute discharge is observed after 5 nights also. As said in Hārīta, “Sixteen days is the time of menstrual discharge”. In Videha also it is said, “There will be menstrual discharge for 16 days in the women”. Comparing with the colour of rabbit’s blood and that of lac-water solution is on the basis of physical temparament of the women. yaccapsu na virājyate” means if a cloth is drenched with pure ārtava and when it is washed with water, the blood-stain should not be left on the cloth. Hiranyākṣa also said, the pure menstrual blood should look like the indragopa insect - silky red insect, slightly oily, with the odour of honey not sticky and does not stain the cloth. 6 -7. Thus ends the diagnosis of asrgdara in Madhukosa commentary written by Srīkaṇṭhaḍatta, 61. ****
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 61.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 33, verse 4):

मधुकोशः कफपित्तवातजमेहानां क्रमेण संप्रातिमाह—मेद इत्यादिना। अन्न कफजा एव मेहा भूयस्त्वेन साध्यत्वेन चादावुच्यन्ते। तानेवेति। मेदोमांसशरीरद्जक्लेदान्। उष्णैरिति। उष्णवीर्यस्पर्शेंद्रव्यैंः। क्षीणेषु दोषेष्विति। प्रवृद्धत्वेनेव क्षीणेषु, न तु समानापेक्षया, क्षीणेषु, अनेन वृद्धे कफे पित्ते वा यो.वायुर्लङ्जनादिना क्रमेण वृद्धो भवति, स नेहासाध्यमेहचतुष्टयप्रकरणे विवक्षित इति सूच्यते। तत्र हि चिकित्साविधानात् साध्यत्वमस्ति। यदुक्त,‘ या वातमेहान् प्रति पूर्वमुक्ता वातोल्वणानां विहिता किया सा। वायुर्हि धातुष्वतिकर्षितेषु कुप्यत्यसाध्यान् प्रति नास्ति चिन्ता॥’ ( च. चि. अ. ६ ) इति। दोषेष्विति। कफपिन्नेषु, द्वयोश्व बहुवचनं व्यक्तयपेक्षया बहुत्वात्। अवकृष्येति बस्तिमुखं नीत्वा। धातूनिति। वसामजौजोलसीकाख्यान्। समक्रियत्वादिति। कफस्य दोषस्य दृष्यस्य च मेदःप्रभृतेः समानत्वात् कटुतिक्तादिक्रियायाः । अत्र व्याधिमहिप्ना तुल्यदृष्यता साध्यताया हेतुः । तेन ‘न च तुल्यगुणो दृष्यो न दोषः प्रकृतिर्भवेत्।’ (च. सू. अ. ११) इति चरकवचनं कष्टसाध्यतार्थं चोद्धावनीयम्। ‘यदुक्त—च्वरं तुल्यतुदोषत्वं प्रमेहे तुल्यदूष्यता। रक्तगुल्ये पुराणत्वं सुखसाध्यस्य लक्षणम्॥’ इति। विषमक्रियत्वादिति। पित्तस्य प्रमेहप्रधानदूष्यस्य च मेदःप्रभृतेश्रान्योन्यविपरीतक्रियत्वात्; पित्तहरं हि मधुरादि मेदस्करं, मेदोहरं च कटुकादि पित्तकरमिति क्रियावैषम्यम्; अन्न व्याधिस्वभावो हेतु; तेनान्येषु व्याधिषु परस्परविरुद्धदोषदुष्य संसगेंडप्युभयप्रत्यनीकभेषजविधिरविरोधीति। महात्ययत्वादिथि, मजादिगम्भीरधात्वपकर्षकत्वेन बहुव्यापक्तिकरत्वात्; आशुकारित्वादितीशानः । चकाराद्विषमक्रियत्वं च वात जानां समुचीयते॥ २–३॥ कफः सपित्तः पवनश्च दोषाः, मेदोऽस्त्रशुक्राम्बुवसालसीकाः। मज्जारसौजः पिशितं च दूष्याः, प्रमेहिणां विंशतिरेव मेहाः॥ ४॥. वा. नि. १०)
answer_text: Madhukos̉a: The pathogenesis of kaphaja, pittaja and vātaja premehas are being explained here. Since the number of kaphaja pramehas is more and also in view of the curability of these, they are detailed first. The same factors means the fat, muscle tissue and the wetness of the body. uṣṇaih - by hot - means by hot - natured substances - in potency and touch. The depleted dosas - state is in comparison with other increased dosas and not with that of normal dosas. By this, in the background of the increased kapha or pitta, the role of vāta - that is increased due to b fasting etc., is not ruled out here. Only then there is curability in the management. As said by Caraka “The management indicated in aggravated vāta condition can be applied in vatajaprameha; because vāta aggravates in highly depleted state of dhātus even here and the incurability need not be worried about” Ca. ci 6. Doseşu means in kapha and pitta. How can the plurality be applied to two factors? Because it is viewed in terms of the more number of manifestations of these two dosas. Avakrsya means bringing them to the bladder. Dhātūn means the tissues -vasā (fat) majjā (bone-marrow), ojas (essential immune substance) and Lasīkā the liquid underneath the skin. Samakriyatvāt means the commonality of the treatment of both the dosa (kapha) and dusya (the above vibiated factors) i.e, the pungent and bitter tasted drugs cure the aggravation of these two. Hence the typical nature of the disease of having commonness in vitiator and vitiated is the cause for curability. The statement of Caraka, the commonality of the vitiated can not be the nature of Mādhavanidānaṃ the vitiator (ca. sū. 11) should not be taken as reason for incurability - as said, “the example for curability - equality of dosa and season in juara (fever), ” The equality of dosa and dūsya in Prameha and Rakta gulma (abcess seated in the uterus due to vitiation of blood). “Visamakriyatva” means the treatment to pacify pitta (by hot natured drugs) is aggravating to the Dūṣyas i.e fat etc., and hence the antagonism in treatment and vice versa, e.g., the antipilla drugs, sweet tasted ones increase Medas the dūṣya and the antidūṣya drugs, the pungent tasted ones increase the doṣa the pitta. Here, hetu, the reason is vyadhisvabhava - specific quality of this disease. In other diseases where there is antagonism in between the dosa and dūṣya, the ubhayapratyanīka bheṣaja treatment that affects both of them without contradiction, is not impossible. “Mahātyayatvāt” means- “due to very acute state”. This is due to depletion of important tissue factors like majjā etc., which is highly complicated. Acording to Isana, it is asukari (fatal) condition. By using the word Ca, visamakriyatva is applicable here also. The factors involved in the pathogenesis of prameha The dosas involved in this diesease are kapha along with pitta and vata and the dusyas- medas (fat), Asra (blood), Sukra (semen), ambu (watery part of the body), Vasa (oily content of the muscle tissue), Lasika (The liquid underneath the skin), majja (bone-marrow), rasa (chyle), ojas (immunity factor) and pisita (muscle tissue). And the varieties of prameha are twenty. 4. (Ca. Ci. 6)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 33, verse 4.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Madhu Varga, Chapter 21, verse 1056):

किश्चित्सूक्ष्मैःप्रसिद्वेभ्यःषट्पदेभ्योऽलिभिश्चितम् । निर्मलं स्फटिकाभं यत्तन्मथु भ्रामरं स्मृतम् ।।९।। भ्रामर रक्तपित्तघ्न मूत्रजाड्यकर गुरु । स्वादुपाकमभिष्यन्दि विशेषात्पिच्छिलं हिममू ।।१०।। मक्षिकाः कपिलाः स्रक्ष्माः क्षुद्राऽऽ ख्यातस्तत्कृत मधु । मुनिभिः क्षौद्रमित्युक्त तद्वर्णात्कपिल भवेत् ।। गुणैर्माक्षिकवत्क्षैद्रं विशेषान्मेहनाशनम् ।।१.१.।। कृष्णा या मशकोपमा लघुतराः प्रायो महापीडिका वृक्षाणां पृथ्यकोटरान्तरगताः पुष्पासवं कुर्वते । तास्तज्जैरिह पुत्तिका निगदितास्ताभिः कृतं सर्पिषा तुल्यं यन्मधु तद्दनेचरजनैः सङ्कीर्तितं पौत्तिकम् ।।१२।। पौत्तिक मधु रूक्षोष्णं पित्तदाहास्रवातकृत् । विदाहि मेहकृच्छुघ्नं यन्थ्यादिक्षतशोषि च ।।१३।। वरटाः कपिलाः पीताः प्रायो हिमवतों वने ।। १४।। कुर्वन्ति छत्रकाकारं तज्जं छात्रं मधु स्मृतम् । छात्रं कपिलपीतं स्यात्पिच्छिलं श्रीतलं गुरु ।।१५।। कृमिश्चित्ररक्तपित्तप्रमेहजित् । भ्रमतृण्मोहविषहृत्तर्पणञ्च गुणाधिकम् । । १ ६ । । स्वादुपाक मधूकवृक्षनिर्यासं जरत्कार्वाश्रमोद्धवम् । स्रवत्याघ्यं तदाख्यातं श्रेतक मालवे पुनः ।।१७।। तीक्ष्णतुण्डास्तु याः पीता मक्षिकाः षटपदोपमाः । अर्घ्यास्तास्तत्कृतं यत्तदार्घ्यमित्यपरे जगुः ।।१८।। आर्घ्य मध्वतिचक्षुष्यं कफपित्तहरं परम् । कषायं कटुकं पाके तिक्तञ्च बलपुष्टिकत् ।।१९।। प्रायो वल्मीकमध्यस्थाः कपिलाः स्वल्पकीटकाः । कुर्वन्ति कपिलं स्वल्पं तत्स्यादौद्दालकं मधु ।।२०1। - औद्दालक रुचिकर स्वर्यं कुष्ठविषापहम् । कषायमुष्णमम्लञ्च कटुपाकञ्च पित्तकृत् ।।२१।। संख्रत्य पतितं पुष्पाद्यत्तु पत्रोपरि स्थितम् । मधुराम्लकषायञ्च तद्दालं मधु कीर्त्तितम् ।। २ २ ।। दालं मधु लघु प्रोक्तं दीपनीयं कफापहम् । कषायानुरसं रूक्षं रुच्यं छर्दिप्रमेहजित् ।।२३।।
answer_text: The honey is collected by Pingala varna large honey bees is called as Mākṣika. This honey is said to be the best. It is useful in Netraroga (Eye diseases), Kāmala (Jaundice), Arśas (Piles), Kṣhata (Trauma), Swasā (Dyspnoea), Kāsa (Cough) and Kṣaya (Emaciation). It is Laghu (Light for digestion). hrämara: These bees will have six limbs, the honey collected will be clean and clear like spatika is called as Bhrāmara. Bhrāmara is Raktapittaaghna (Cures haemorrages), Mūtragādakara (Reduces the output of urine), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Madhura vipāka (Sweet in post digestion), Abhiṣyanḍi (Blocks the channels), specially it is Picchala (Sticky) and Sīta vīrya (Cold in potency). Kṣaudra: The honey bees is of Kapila varna, sūkṣma and smaller in size. The honey collected from these bees are called as Kṣaudra. The properties of Ksaudra is similar to the Māksika. Pauttika: The honey bees are small, black, resembles like mosquito, causes extreme pain on bite. The hives are found in hollows of tree and honey collected will be like a ghṛta. It is know as Pauttīka by the tribes. Pauttīka is Rūkṣā (Drying), Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), Increases Pitta and Vāta, Dāhakāraka (Causes burning sensation), Vidāhi (Irritant), Leads to diseases of Rakta. It cures diseases of Pitta, Rakta, Dāha (Burning sensation), Prameha (Diabeties), Mūtrakṛcchra (Dysuria), Granti (Tumors) and Kṣata (wounds). Chātra: These honey bees hives are found in forest areas of Himalayan mountains. These are Kapila varna, and hives will be in the shape of umbrella. The honey collected by such bees is called as Chātra. Chātra honey appear like reddish, brown colour, Picchala (Sticky), Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Madhura vipāka (Sweet in post digestive) and Tarpaṇa (Nourshing) and posses good qualities It cures Kṛmi (Worms infestations), Svitra (Vitiligo), Raktapitta (Haemorrages), Prameha (Diabetes), Bhrama (Vertigo), Tṛṣṇā (Thrist), Mohā (Stupor) and Viṣa (Poisonous manifestations). Ardhya: The honey obtained from the bee hives found over Madhūka trees, which secreted like resin, in the residence of sage Jaratgāru is know as Ārdhya. In mālva deśa it is called as śvetaka. Some acharyas has an opinion that, honey collected from which are similar to wild bees, yellow coloured and has strong penetrating string is know as Ardhya. Ardhya is Cakṣuṣya (Good for eyes), Subsides Kapha and Pitta, Kaṣāya (Astringent) andTikta (Bitter) in taste, Kaṭu vipāka (Pungent in post digestion), Balya (Promotes strength) and Puştikara (Nutritious). Auddālaka: Honey bees build their hives inside the anthills. Smaller, kapilāvarṇa and gives rise to small amount of honey is know as Auddālaka. Auddālaka is Rucya (Promotes taste), Svarya (Good for voice), it cures Kuṣṭa (Leprosy), and Viṣa (Posionious manifestations). It is Kaṣāya (Astringent) and Amla (Sour) in taste, Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency), Kaṭu vipāka (Pungent in post digestion) and Increases pitta dosa. Dālam: A PORTANT AND BHĀVAPRAKĀŚA NIGHANȚU and the control of the Honey bees collect honey from flowers that fall on the surface of leaf is know as Dālam. Dālam is Madhura (Sweet) in taste, Amla (Sour) and Kaṣāya (Astringent) secondary taste, Laghu (Light for digestion), Dīpana (Appetizer), subsides Kapha doṣa, Rūkṣā (Drying), Rucya Promotes taste), it cures Chardi (Vomiting) and Prameha (Diabetes). it is excessive Madhura (Sweet) in taste, Snigdha (Oilyness), Bṛhmaṇa (Stoutning) and Guru (Heavy for digestion)
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Madhu Varga, Chapter 21, verse 1056
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Madhu Varga, Chapter 21, verse 1056.
context: किश्चित्सूक्ष्मैःप्रसिद्वेभ्यःषट्पदेभ्योऽलिभिश्चितम् । निर्मलं स्फटिकाभं यत्तन्मथु भ्रामरं स्मृतम् ।।९।। भ्रामर रक्तपित्तघ्न मूत्रजाड्यकर गुरु । स्वादुपाकमभिष्यन्दि विशेषात्पिच्छिलं हिममू ।।१०।। मक्षिकाः कपिलाः स्रक्ष्माः क्षुद्राऽऽ ख्यातस्तत्कृत मधु । मुनिभिः क्षौद्रमित्युक्त तद्वर्णात्कपिल भवेत् ।। गुणैर्माक्षिकवत्क्षैद्रं विशेषान्मेहनाशनम् ।।१.१.।। कृष्णा या मशकोपमा लघुतराः प्रायो महापीडिका वृक्षाणां पृथ्यकोटरान्तरगताः पुष्पासवं कुर्वते । तास्तज्जैरिह पुत्तिका निगदितास्ताभिः कृतं सर्पिषा तुल्यं यन्मधु तद्दनेचरजनैः सङ्कीर्तितं पौत्तिकम् ।।१२।। पौत्तिक मधु रूक्षोष्णं पित्तदाहास्रवातकृत् । विदाहि मेहकृच्छुघ्नं यन्थ्यादिक्षतशोषि च ।।१३।। वरटाः कपिलाः पीताः प्रायो हिमवतों वने ।। १४।। कुर्वन्ति छत्रकाकारं तज्जं छात्रं मधु स्मृतम् । छात्रं कपिलपीतं स्यात्पिच्छिलं श्रीतलं गुरु ।।१५।। कृमिश्चित्ररक्तपित्तप्रमेहजित् । भ्रमतृण्मोहविषहृत्तर्पणञ्च गुणाधिकम् । । १ ६ । । स्वादुपाक मधूकवृक्षनिर्यासं जरत्कार्वाश्रमोद्धवम् । स्रवत्याघ्यं तदाख्यातं श्रेतक मालवे पुनः ।।१७।। तीक्ष्णतुण्डास्तु याः पीता मक्षिकाः षटपदोपमाः । अर्घ्यास्तास्तत्कृतं यत्तदार्घ्यमित्यपरे जगुः ।।१८।। आर्घ्य मध्वतिचक्षुष्यं कफपित्तहरं परम् । कषायं कटुकं पाके तिक्तञ्च बलपुष्टिकत् ।।१९।। प्रायो वल्मीकमध्यस्थाः कपिलाः स्वल्पकीटकाः । कुर्वन्ति कपिलं स्वल्पं तत्स्यादौद्दालकं मधु ।।२०1। - औद्दालक रुचिकर स्वर्यं कुष्ठविषापहम् । कषायमुष्णमम्लञ्च कटुपाकञ्च पित्तकृत् ।।२१।। संख्रत्य पतितं पुष्पाद्यत्तु पत्रोपरि स्थितम् । मधुराम्लकषायञ्च तद्दालं मधु कीर्त्तितम् ।। २ २ ।। दालं मधु लघु प्रोक्तं दीपनीयं कफापहम् । कषायानुरसं रूक्षं रुच्यं छर्दिप्रमेहजित् ।।२३।।

context: वार्षिकं तदहर्वृष्ट भूमिस्थमहितं जलम् । त्रिरात्रमुषितं तत्तु प्रसन्नममृतोपमम् ।।५८ ।। हेमन्ते सारसं तोयं तडागं वा हित स्मृतम् । हेमन्ते विहित तोयं शिशिरेऽपि प्रशस्यते ।।५९।। वसन्तग्रीष्मयोः कौपं वाप्यं वा नैईरं जलम् । नादेयं वारि नादेयं वसन्तग्रीष्मयोर्बुधैः ।।६०।। विषवद्वनवृक्षाणां पत्राद्यैर्दूषितं यतः । औद्भिद वाऽऽन्तरिक्षं वा कौपं वा प्रावृषि स्मृतम् । शस्तं शरदि नादेयं नीरमंशूदकं परम् ।।६१।। दिवा रविकरैर्जुष्ट निशि शीतकरांशभिः । जेयमंशूदकं नाम स्निग्धं दोषत्रयापहम् ।।६२।। अनभिष्यन्दि निर्दोषमान्तरिक्षजलोपमम् । बल्यं रसायनं मेध्यं शीतं लघु सुधासमम् ।।६३।। शरदि स्वच्छमुदयादगस्त्यस्याखिलं हितम् ।।६४।। पौषे वारिसरोजातं माघे तत्तु तडागजम् । फाल्गुने कूपसम्भूतं चैत्रे चौड़यं हितं मतम् ।।६५.।। बैशाखे नैझरि नीरं ज्येष्ठे शस्तं तथौद्विदम् । आषाढे शस्यते कौपं श्रावणे दिव्यमेव च ।।६६।। भाद्रे कौपं पयःशस्तमाश्चिने चौझ्यमेव च । कार्त्तिके मार्गशीर्षे च जलमात्रं प्रशस्यते ।।६७।।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 56, verse 14):

मधुकोशः शीतादमाह-शोणितमित्यादि। दन्तवेष्टेभ्य इति दन्तबन्धनमांसेभ्यः। अकस्मादिति अभिघातादिनिमित्तं विना । ‘शीर्यन्त’ इत्यस्य स्थाने, ‘पच्यन्त’ इति गदाधरः, व्याचष्टे च-‘स्वयं’ इति शेषः । पचन्ति च परस्परमित्यन्योन्यं पचन्ति, पाकोष्मदूषितशोणितसंचरणेन ॥ दन्तयोस्त्रिषु वा यस्य श्वयथुर्जायते महान्। दन्तपुप्पुटको नाम स व्याधिः कफरक्तजः॥ १२॥ ( सु.नि. १६ ) मधुकोशः दन्तपुप्पुटकमाह-दन्तयोरित्यादि। अयं च दन्तयोस्त्रिष्वित्यभिधानात् द्वित्रिदन्तनियतः, कफरक्तजत्वेऽपि शौषिराद्मिन्नोऽयं, रुजालालास्त्रावाभावात् ॥ १२ ॥ स्त्रवन्ति पूयरुधिरं चला दन्ता भवन्ति च। दन्तवेष्टः स विज़ेयो दुष्टशोणितसंभवः॥ १३॥ ( सु.नि. १६ ) मधुकोशः दन्तवेष्टमाह-स्त्रवन्तीत्यादि। स्त्रवन्ति पूयरुधिरमित्यत्र ‘दन्तमूलानि’ इति शेषः। चला दन्ता भवन्ति चेति चकारेण पचन्ति चेति द्रष्टव्यम्॥ १३॥ श्वयथुर्दन्तमूलेषु रुजावान् कफरक्तजः। लालास्त्रावी स विज्ञेयः शौषिरो नाम नामतः॥ १४॥ ( सु.नि. १६ )
answer_text: Dantavesta is the muscular layer that stabilises the teeth at the root. Akasmat suddenly - implies that even without injury etc., causative factors. Gadādhara uses the term pacyante in the place of Sīryante which means that the gums get ulcerated, by themselves"; pacanti ca parasparam means - the ulceration spreads from one to another of the gums. 10, 11. Dantapuppuṭaka When there is severe swelling in the roots of two or three teeth of an indi¬ vidual, that condition is known as dantapuppuṭaka caused by kapha and rakta. 12. (Su.Ni.16) The swelling is limited to the gums of two or three in this diseases. This is different from Sausira, though it is also caused by kapha and Rakta. Pain occurs due to lack of salivation. 12. (pain is not mentioned in dantapuppaṭaka, while it is salivation that causes pain in sauşira as per 14th stanza). Dantāveṣṭa There will be discharge of pus and blood from the gums and the teeth be¬ come shaky in the disease called Dantavesta, which is caused by vitiated blood. The discharge of pus and blood is from the gums. the word ca in "Cala danta bhavanti ca" implies that the teeth keep shaking and also there will be ulceration. 13. Śausira Mādhavanidānaṃ There is painful swelling in the gums and excessive salivation in a condition named “Šauṣira” which is cuased by kapha and rakta. 14. ( Su. Ni. 16)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 56, verse 14.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Purvārdḍha, Chapter 2, verse 21):

चतुर्थकविपर्ययज्वरस्य लक्षणं विस्तरेणोक्तम् ।।२१।।
answer_text: The signs and symptoms of Caturthaka Viparyaya (reversal quartan) fever are described in detail. This type of fever has a specific pattern of recurring every fourth day with reversed symptoms. Raktātisāra (diarrhoea of blood) is given here as an extension of Pittātisāra to avoid the seventh number in diarrhoea. Likewise the repeated defaecation caused in Snehajirna (indigestion of unctuous substances), Visucika (gastro enteritis?) Visa (poisonous affliction), Arsa (piles), Krimi (worm infestation) etc., should be attributed to the aetiology originated and as a symptom of that particular condition and not as separate type of atisāra (diarrhoea). Pravāhikā (Dysentry) When an individual has Kapha accumulation and indulges in incompatible foods. Vata aggravates in his body and brings down the Kapha through the other end, the anus and causes Pravāhikā (dysentry) in which the Kapha is passed repeat- edly stained with faeces in small quantities 21. Su. u. 40
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Purvārdḍha, Chapter 2, verse 21.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 61):

मधुकोशः नकुलान्ध्यसंज्ञामाह-विद्योतते यस्येत्यादिं। नकुलस्य यद्वद्यथा द्वृष्टिर्विद्योतते वर्णेन प्रतिभासते तथाऽस्येत्यर्थः। अतः सर्वदृष्टिमण्डलगतो रागः सर्वदोषवर्णश्र, दोषाभिपन्नेत्यत्र दोषशब्दस्याविशेषित्वादाभि- शब्दस्याभिव्याप्त्यर्थस्य प्रयोगात्। एतौ 'ह्रस्वजाड्यनकुलन्ध्यौ चतुःपटलस्थिदोषजन्यौ सरागौ च साध्यौ। तथा च विदेहः-‘नक्तमन्थास्तु चत्वारो ये पुरस्तात् प्रकीर्तिताः। तेषामसाध्यो नकुलो ह्रस्वजाड्यस्तथैव च॥ विशेषेण भवेयातां द्वौ चतुःपटलाश्रितौ। तौ च संप्राप्तरागत्वादसाध्यौ परिकीर्तितौ॥’ इति । एतौ च रात्र्यन्धौ, प्रत्येतव्यौ दिवा हस्वचित्ररूपदर्शनाभिधानेन रात्रावदर्शनप्रतीतेः। विदेहेन तु नक्तान्थत्रित्वेपि चत्वार इत्युक्त, नक्तान्थबाहुल्येन दिवान्धेऽपि तत्प्रयोगात्, छत्रिणो गच्छन्तीतिवत्॥ ६०॥ दृष्टिर्विरूपा श्वसनोपसृष्टा संकोचमभ्यन्तरतस्तु याति॥ ६१॥ रुजावगाढा च तमक्षिरोगं गम्भीरिकेति प्रवदन्ति तम्ज्ञाः ।
answer_text: The affected eye of the individual appears with different colours, like that of a Nakula (mangoose). Hence the colours of all the dosas spread over the complete drstimandala and get afflicted by all the dosas. Here dosa is to be taken as all the doşas. Hrasva jādya and Nakulāndhya are curable as they are caused by the doşa settled in the four layers of the eye and manifested with colour. Videha says, “All the above four types are distinct varieties of night blindness; Nakula and Hrasvajadya, out of these, are incurable as they are caused by affliction of four of the layers of the eye and also as they attain colour”. These are to be understood as Rātryandha (night blindness) as it is said that during day time, there will be perception of short and multicoloured objects in the respective conditions. Videha has mentioned that Naktandhatas night-blindness are four inspite of their number being three. He in¬ cluded divāndhya (day blindness) also in this group. Gambhīrikā (Pthisis bulbi) Irregular sight, which is afflicted by vāta, constriction of dṛṣṭimaṇḍala and deep pain are the features of the eye disease, called gambhirikā. 61. (Su. u. 7)

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 14):

मधुकोशः यावता कालेन मिथ्याचाराद् दृष्टि हन्ति तमाह-हन्यादित्यादि। सद्य एवेति श्लेष्मणि सप्तरात्रस्योक्तत्वात् सद्यःशब्देनात्र व्याधिस्वभावात् ॥ ११ ॥ उदीर्णवेदनं नेत्रं रागशोथसमन्वितम्। घर्षनिस्तोदशूलाश्रुयुक्तमामान्वितं विदुः ॥ १२ ॥ ( सु.उ. ६ ) मधुकोशः च, नेत्ररोगस्य सामत्वलक्षणमाह उदीर्णवेदनमित्वादि । लङ्वनप्रलेपादिविधानार्थमझनादिनिषेधार्थं उदीर्णवेदनमुद्रतबहुवेदनम् । घर्षः करकरिका। लङ्कनादिविधानार्थमझनादिनिषेधार्थ च तन्त्रान्तरम्-'स्वेदः प्रलेपस्तिक्ताव्रं धूमो दिनचतुष्टयम्। लङ्कनं चाक्षिरोग्मणामामानां पाचनानि षट्॥ अअन्ञनं सर्पिषः पानं कषायं गुरुभोजनम्। नेत्ररोगेषु सामेषु स्नानं चापि विवर्जयेत्’॥ १२॥ मन्दवेदनता कण्ड्रः संरम्भाश्रुप्रशान्तता। प्रशस्तवर्णता चाक्ष्णोः संपक्रं दोषमादिशेत्॥ १३॥ ( सु.उ. ६ ) मधुकोशः निरामलक्षणमाह-मन्देत्यादि। संरम्भाश्रुप्रशान्ततेति संरम्भः शोथस्तस्य, अश्रुणो नेत्रजलस्य च प्रशमः ॥ १३ ॥ कण्ड्रपदेहाश्र्युतः पक्कोदम्बरसंनिभः। संरम्भी पच्यते यस्तु नेत्रपाकः स शोथजः। शोथहीनानि लिङ्गानि नेत्रपाके त्वशोथजे ॥ १४॥ ( सु. उ. ६)
answer_text: The time taken for destroying the sight by the mistreated adhimantha is given here; sadya eva should be taken as three nights because kaphaja type lasts for seven days. In medical terms Sadya is taken as three or seven. The time limitation is specific effect of this disease. 11 Sāma (associated with incompletely formed doṣa) Netraroga Severe pain, redness, oedema, friction, pinning sensation and painful tears are the feature of eye disease associated with āma (unripe doṣa). 12 (Su.u.6) For adopting the therapies of fasting, external application etc., and to avoid añjana (internal application) etc., the features of eye-diseases associated with āma are being given here; udīrṇa vedana means very severe pain; ghạrṣa means the sensation of friction (as if sand entered the eye). In other treatises also it is said, “In Mādhavanidānaṃ the sāma condition of Netra rogas, one should adopt sudation, external application, consumption of bitter tasted foods, dhūmapāna for four days, fasting and digestive foods for digestion. We should avoid, anjana (applications) and heavy foods and also even taking bath, when afflicated with netrarogas which are in āma state”. 12. Features of mirama state of eye-diseases Dull pain, itching senstion, palliation of swelling and production of tears and regaining original lustre of the eye are the features of eye-disease in which the dosas are fully ripened (become devoid of āma or unripe condtion). 13. Samraṃbhāśṛpraśāntatā - palliation of swelling and tears. Feature of Saśotha pāka (Ulceration alongwith swelling) The ulceration of the eye caused by swelling is featured by itching, sticky tears, looking like ripened fig-fruit and the ripening or ulceration follows swelling. When the paka (ulceration) has all the above features excepting swelling, that con¬ dition is known as Aśothaja pāka. 14. (Su.u.16)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 14.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Mamsa Varga, Chapter 10, verse 910):

कूलेचराः प्लावाश्रापि कोशस्थाः पादिनस्तथा । मतस्या एते समाख्याताः पञ्चधाऽऽनूपजातयः ।।७।। अनूपा मधुराः स्निग्धा गुरवो वह्निसादनाः । श्लेष्मलाः पिच्छिलाध्यापि मांसपुष्टिप्रदा भूशम् । तथाऽभिष्यन्दिनस्ते हि प्रायः पथ्यतमाः स्मृताः ।।८।। हरिणैणकुरङ्गष्यपृषतन्यङ्कशम्बराः ।।।९।। राजीवोऽपि च मुण्डी चेत्याद्याजङ्कालसंज़काः । हरिणस्ताप्रवर्णः स्यादेणः कृष्णः प्रकीर्त्तितः ।।१०।। कुरङ्न ईषत्ताम्रः स्यादेणतुल्याकृतिर्महान् । ऋष्यो नीलाङ्गको लोके स रोझ इति कीर्त्तितः ।।१ः१।। पृष्ठतश्चन्द्रबिन्दुः स्याद्धरिणात्किश्चिदल्पकः । न्यङ्डर्बहुविषाणोऽथ शम्बरो गवयो महान् ।।१२।। राजीवस्तु मृगो ज़ेयो राजिभिः परितो वृतः । यो मृगः श्रुङ्गहीनः स्यात्स मुण्डीति निगद्यते ।।१३।। जङ्वालाः प्रायशः सर्वे पित्तशलेष्महराः स्मृताः । किश्चिद्वातकराश्चापि लघवो बलवर्द्वनाः ।। १४।।
answer_text: lt is divided into following five types: Külecara: Which lives on the banks of river, stems, ponds etc. Palva: Birds which floats or swim over the water. Kośastha: Animals who lives in the shells. ādi: Animals which crawl. Matsyā: The Fishes which are aquatic in nature. Guna karma (Properties and indications): Anupa mamsa is Madhura (Sweet) in taste, Snigdha (Oilyness), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Agnisāda (Decrease the digestive activity), increases Kapha, Picchala (Sticky), Mamsapuṣ ṭipradā (Nutrious to the muscles tissues), Abhiṣyandi (Blocks the channels) and Always used as an ideal diet, Janghāla means different kinds of deers they are Harina, Ena, Kuranga, Rṣya, Prsata, Nyanku, Sambara, Rājīva and Mundī. Harina is coppery red in colour, Ena is black, Kuranga is mild copped red coloured, shape like Ena but much larger in size. Rṣya is blue coloured and popularly know as Rojha. Prsata it possess spot like moon and it is comparetively much smaller than Harina and Nyanku, it has many large sharp horns, it is know as Baharasingh. Sambara it is larger than Cow (Nīl gāy). Rājīva is a kind of deer it has lot of strips on its body. Mundī is variety of deer it doesn’t having horns. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Jaṅghāla meat subsides Pitta and Kapha, slightly increases Vāta, Laghu (Light for digestion) and Balavardaka (Promotes strength)
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Mamsa Varga, Chapter 10, verse 910
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Mamsa Varga, Chapter 10, verse 910.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Nidanasthana, Chapter 10, verse 2):

मधुकोश: राजयक्ष्मरूपेषु पित्ताद्रक्तस्य चागम इति वचनाद्रक्तपित्तानन्तरं यक्ष्मनिदानम् । चिकित्सोपयोगिविप्रकृष्टकारणं चतुर्विधमाह-वेगरोधादित्यादि वेगोऽत्र वातमूत्रपुरीषाणां, नतु नवेगान्यारणीयोक्तानां जृम्भादीनां सर्वेषाम् । यदुक्त चरके—‘हीमत्त्वाद्वा घृणित्वाद्वा भयाद्वा वेगमागतम् । वातमूत्रपुरीषाणां निगृह्वाति यदा नरः’ (च. चि. ८) इत्यादि । क्षयादिति, क्षीयते अनेनेति क्षयः, तेनातिव्यवायानशनेर्ष्याविषादादयो धातुक्षयहेतवो गृह्यन्ते । साहसादिति, साहसं बलवद्विग्रहादिरुरःक्षतहेतुत्वेन कारणम् । विषमाशनादिति, सुश्रुतोक्तद्वादशाशनप्रविचारव्यतिरेकेणोपयोगः, तस्य शीघ्र स्रोतोरोधकत्वात् उक्त हि चरके, – ‘विविधान्यन्नपानानि वैषम्येण समश्नताम् । जनयन्त्यामयान् घोरान् विषमा मारुतादयः । रुद्ध्वा स्रोतांसि धातूनां वैषम्याद्विषमं गताः । दोषा रोगा कल्पन्ते पुष्यन्ति न च धातव:’ (च. चि. ८) इति । त्रिदोष इति, मिलितत्रिदोषज एक एव, नतु कारणभेदादनेक: । यदाह सुश्रतः— ‘एक एव मतः शोषः संनिपातात्मको यतः । उद्रेकात्तत्र लिङ्गानि दोषाणां निपतन्ति हि’ (सू. उ. ४१) इति । ननु, वेगरोधादयो वात प्रकोपयन्ति, तज्जनितो यक्ष्मा कथं त्रिदोषज इति चेत् ? उच्यते, वातप्रकोपादेवाग्निदुष्ट्या कफपित्तयोरपि प्रकोप इत्याहु: । हेतुचतुष्टयादित्यनेनासंख्येया अपि हेतव उक्तचतुष्टयेऽन्तर्भवन्तीति दर्शयति । शोषादिनानाशब्दवाच्यत्वेन चौस्य सुश्रुतान्वयमकार्षीत् । यथा—‘संशोषणाद्रसादीनां शोष इत्यभिधीयते । क्रियाक्षयकरत्वाच्च क्षय इत्युच्यते बुधै: ।। राज्ञश्चन्द्रमसो यस्मादभूदेष किलामयः । तस्मात्तं राजयक्ष्मेति केचिदाहुर्मनीषिण:' (सु. उ. ४१) इति । वाग्भटे तु—‘यक्ष्मणां राजा राजयक्ष्मा’—इत्युक्तम् । ‘राजदन्तादिषु परम्’ इति उपसर्जनस्य यक्ष्मशब्दस्य परनिपातः ।।[१]। ‘संज्ञां स्वयमेवाकार्षीत सश्रुत:’ इति पा. । २. वाग्भटे तु ‘नक्षत्राणां द्विजानां च राज्ञोऽभूद्यदयं पुरा । यच्च राजा च यक्ष्मा च राजयक्ष्मा ततो मत:’ इति पठ्यते (वा. नि. ५) कफप्रधानैदोंषैस्तु रसवर्त्मसु । रुद्धेषु अतिव्यवायिनो वाऽपि क्षीणे रेतस्यनन्तरा: । क्षीयन्ते धातवः सर्वे ततः शुष्यति मानवः ।। २।।
answer_text: Suppression of natural urges, emaciation, over doing the daring deeds and ir¬ regular eating habits are the four aetiological factors causing the disease of con¬ sumption in which tridosas are involved. 1 As spitting blood due to pitta is seen in the symptomatology of Yaksma (consumption), this disease is being explained after Raktapitta. The four types of aetiology mentioned here are the distant causes of this disease by knowing which the treatment can be planned accordingly. Natural urges in this context, are fart, urine and faeces and not all those yawning etc., mentioned in Navegandhara- ṇiyādhyaya (7th chapter of Caraka Saṃhitā Sūtrasthāna). Caraka enumerates Vāta (fart), Mutra (urine) and Purisa (faecal matter) as the urges by suppressing which, Yakṣma (consumption) occurs. Kṣyā is emaciation of the body due to over indulgence in sexual act, not taking food, being envious and poisoning etc. Over doing the daring things without considering one's own strength. Irregular eating habits, as Rājakṣma-kṣṭakṣīnanidāna against to the twelve regulations of food consumption, mentioned by Suśruta. In short, taking smaller quantities of food or untimely eating habits are considered as Visamasana (irregular eating). It is said in Caraka, ''By consuming various foods in an irregular manner, the Dosas become irregular (vitiated) and cause serious illnesses. Dosa's block the channels due to vitiation of Dhatus (tissues) and cause diseases while they also do not replenish the Dhatus which results in depletion of the body.'' (Ca. ci. 8). Yakṣmā (consumption) is caused by Tridoṣas (all the three Dosas) as one. It is not many due to many causative factors, as said by Susruta, Sosa (emaciation/consumption) is only one as all the three Dosas involve in its pathogenesis. Due to predominance of each of the Dosas there will be variation in the symptomatology from individual to individual (Su. u. 41). As such Vāta aggravates due to suppression of natural urges. Then how come the consumption caused by suppression of natural urges has three Doşas involved in it? It is said that due to aggravation of Vata, agni (the digestive fire) is vitiated which in turn aggravates Pitta and Kapha also. By saying Hetucatuṣṭaya, the reason quartrad, it is implied that all other reasons are classified into these four only. This disease is called by various names like Soşa etc.; as it dries up the chyle etc. tissues, it is styled as Sosa; as it diminishes the activity of the individual, it is named as Ksaya; this disease afflicted the king, the moon and hence the name, Rājayakṣma (kingly consumption). (Su. u. 41). Vāgbhaṭa defines that it is called Rājayakṣmā as it is the Rājā (king) of all diseases. Pathogenesis of Rājayakṣmā When the Rasa (chyle) channels are blocked by Dosas, with Kapha in pre- dominance and also due over indulgence in sexual act, when the semen is depleted in the body, the other Dhatus (tissue) are diminished and ultimately an individual gets emaciated
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana, Chapter 10, verse 2.
context: मधुकोश: राजयक्ष्मरूपेषु पित्ताद्रक्तस्य चागम इति वचनाद्रक्तपित्तानन्तरं यक्ष्मनिदानम् । चिकित्सोपयोगिविप्रकृष्टकारणं चतुर्विधमाह-वेगरोधादित्यादि वेगोऽत्र वातमूत्रपुरीषाणां, नतु नवेगान्यारणीयोक्तानां जृम्भादीनां सर्वेषाम् । यदुक्त चरके—‘हीमत्त्वाद्वा घृणित्वाद्वा भयाद्वा वेगमागतम् । वातमूत्रपुरीषाणां निगृह्वाति यदा नरः’ (च. चि. ८) इत्यादि । क्षयादिति, क्षीयते अनेनेति क्षयः, तेनातिव्यवायानशनेर्ष्याविषादादयो धातुक्षयहेतवो गृह्यन्ते । साहसादिति, साहसं बलवद्विग्रहादिरुरःक्षतहेतुत्वेन कारणम् । विषमाशनादिति, सुश्रुतोक्तद्वादशाशनप्रविचारव्यतिरेकेणोपयोगः, तस्य शीघ्र स्रोतोरोधकत्वात् उक्त हि चरके, – ‘विविधान्यन्नपानानि वैषम्येण समश्नताम् । जनयन्त्यामयान् घोरान् विषमा मारुतादयः । रुद्ध्वा स्रोतांसि धातूनां वैषम्याद्विषमं गताः । दोषा रोगा कल्पन्ते पुष्यन्ति न च धातव:’ (च. चि. ८) इति । त्रिदोष इति, मिलितत्रिदोषज एक एव, नतु कारणभेदादनेक: । यदाह सुश्रतः— ‘एक एव मतः शोषः संनिपातात्मको यतः । उद्रेकात्तत्र लिङ्गानि दोषाणां निपतन्ति हि’ (सू. उ. ४१) इति । ननु, वेगरोधादयो वात प्रकोपयन्ति, तज्जनितो यक्ष्मा कथं त्रिदोषज इति चेत् ? उच्यते, वातप्रकोपादेवाग्निदुष्ट्या कफपित्तयोरपि प्रकोप इत्याहु: । हेतुचतुष्टयादित्यनेनासंख्येया अपि हेतव उक्तचतुष्टयेऽन्तर्भवन्तीति दर्शयति । शोषादिनानाशब्दवाच्यत्वेन चौस्य सुश्रुतान्वयमकार्षीत् । यथा—‘संशोषणाद्रसादीनां शोष इत्यभिधीयते । क्रियाक्षयकरत्वाच्च क्षय इत्युच्यते बुधै: ।। राज्ञश्चन्द्रमसो यस्मादभूदेष किलामयः । तस्मात्तं राजयक्ष्मेति केचिदाहुर्मनीषिण:' (सु. उ. ४१) इति । वाग्भटे तु—‘यक्ष्मणां राजा राजयक्ष्मा’—इत्युक्तम् । ‘राजदन्तादिषु परम्’ इति उपसर्जनस्य यक्ष्मशब्दस्य परनिपातः ।।[१]। ‘संज्ञां स्वयमेवाकार्षीत सश्रुत:’ इति पा. । २. वाग्भटे तु ‘नक्षत्राणां द्विजानां च राज्ञोऽभूद्यदयं पुरा । यच्च राजा च यक्ष्मा च राजयक्ष्मा ततो मत:’ इति पठ्यते (वा. नि. ५) कफप्रधानैदोंषैस्तु रसवर्त्मसु । रुद्धेषु अतिव्यवायिनो वाऽपि क्षीणे रेतस्यनन्तरा: । क्षीयन्ते धातवः सर्वे ततः शुष्यति मानवः ।। २।।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Charaka Samhita (Chikitsasthana, Chapter 1, verse 58):

यथोक्तगुणानामामलकानां सहस्रं पिष्टस्वेदनविधिना पयस ऊष्मणा सुस्विन्नमनातपशुष्कमनस्थि चूर्णयेत् । तदामलकसहस्रस्वरसपरिपीतस्थिरापुनर्नवाजीवन्तीनागबलाब्रह्मसुवर्चलामण्डूकपर्णीशतावरीशङ्खपुष्पीपिप्पलीवचाविडङ्गस्वयंगुप्तामृताचन्दनागुरुमधुकमधुकपुष्पोत्पलपद्ममालतीयुवतीयूथिकाचूर्णाष्टभागसंयुक्तं पुनर्नागबलासहस्रपलस्वरसपरिपीतमनातपशुष्कं द्विगुणितसर्पिषा क्षौद्रसर्पिषा वा क्षुद्रगुडावति कृत्वा शुचौ दृढे, घृतभाविते कुम्भे, भस्मराशेरधः स्थापयेदन्तर्भूमैः पक्षं कृतरक्षाविधानमथर्ववेदविदा, पक्षात्यये चोद्धृत्य कनकरजतताम्रप्रवालकालायसचूर्णाष्टभागसंयुक्तमर्धकर्षवृद्ध्या यथोक्तेन विधिना प्रातः प्रातः प्रयुञ्जानोऽग्निबलमभिसमीक्ष्य, जीर्णे च षष्टिकं पयसा ससर्पिष्कमुपसेवमानो यथोक्तान् गुणान् समश्नुत इति ॥ ५८ ॥
answer_text: The fruits of amalaki having the above qualities are taken in the number of 1000 and are steamed on the vapour of milk like the flour-paste. When they are well-steamed, they are taken out, dried in shade and are powdered after removing the seeds. This is impregnated with the juice of one thousand fresh fruits of amalaki and added with the powder of śālaparṇī, punarnavā, jīvantī, nāgabalā, brahmasuvarcalā, maṇḍūkaparṇī, śatāvarī, śaṅkhapuṣpī, pippalī, vacā, viḍaṅga, svayaṅguptā, amṛtā, candana, aguru, madhuka, flowers of madhuka, utpala, padma, mālatī, yuvatī and yūthikā in the quantity one eighth of the āmalakī powder. This is again impregnated with the juice of nāgabalā in the quantity of 40 kg, and dried in shade. Then in double quantity, ghee or ghee-honey, mixed, are added to it and is made in the shape of small boluses. This is kept in a clean and strong vessel uncted with ghee and is stored underground/within the heap of ashes for a fortnight after having performed the protective rites through the knowers of Atharvaveda. After the fortnight is over, this should be taken out and added with the powder (bhasma) of gold, silver, copper, coral and iron in one-eighth quantity. This should be taken regularly in the dose of 5 gms, gradually increasing with the same by the said method in every morning taking into consideration the power of digestion. After the drug is digested, sastika rice alongwith milk added with ghee should be taken. Thus one attains the results mentioned above. (Thus is said the Brahma rasayana)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Chikitsasthana, Chapter 1, verse 58.

( च. चि. ५ ) मधुकोश: वातिकमाह—रूक्षेत्यादि । विषमातिमात्रमित्यन्नपानविशेषणम् । विचेष्टनं विरुद्धचेष्टाः बलवद्दियहादि । अतिमलक्ष्यो विरेकादिना । निरन्नता निराहारता । विकल्पशब्दः स्थानादिभिः प्रत्येक योज्यः । स्थानविकल्पो यथा—कदाचित्राभो, कदाचित्यार्श्वयोः, कदाचिद्वस्तावित्यादिस्थानान्तरगमनम् । संस्थानविकल्पो यथा—कदाचिदल्पः, कदचिन्महान्, वृत्तो, दीघों वेति । रुजाविकल्पो यथा—कदाचिन्महती, तोदरूपा, भेदरूपा, अनेकरूपा वेति । न च तत्रोपश्रेते न सुखयति ।।६-८.11 कट्वम्लतीक्ष्णोष्णविदाहिरूक्षक्रोधातिमद्यार्कहताशसेवा आमाभिधातो रुधिरं च दुष्ट पैत्तस्य गुल्मस्य निमित्तमुक्तम् ।। ९ !!
answer_text: Dry food, continuous irregular eating habits and improper behaviour, suppres¬ sion of natural urges, grief, exposure to injury, excessive loss of impurities (exces- sive purgation therapy) and lack of food are the reasons of Vāta type of Gulma. This has the place of origin, shape and nature of pain as per the Vata Dosa and also constipation of faecus and flatus, dryness in the throat and mouth, blackish red col¬ our in the body, cold-fever, pain in the heart, stomach, flanks, scapular region and head, aggravation on digestion of food and palliation (of the symptoms) on indigestion of food are the features of Vata Gulma and it aggravates also on consuming dry, astringent, bitter and pungent foods. 6, 7, 8 (Ca. ci. 5) Gulmanidānam Irregular behaviour includes forcible deeds like wrestling with more powerful people etc. Vikalpa applies to Sthāna (place of origin), Saṃsthāna (shape) and Rujā (nature of pain). Place of origin of Vāta Gulma is some times, the navel, some times the flanks and sometimes, the bladder and so on. The shape of Vata Gulma keeps changing some times small, some times big circular or longitudinal etc. The pain also is fluctuating from less, more or piercing etc. Pitta type of Gulma
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana, Chapter 28, verse 9.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 20):

कफजमाह सम्पूरणेरित्यादि । मन्दविचेष्टितस्य आयासशन्यस्य । सम्पूरणै- भेजिनादिभिः कफो दुष्ट इति सम्बन्धः । सोष्मा सपितः । कफेनापि क्रियमाण उन्मादोऽवश्यं सपित्तेन क्रियते व्याधिमहिम्ना यथा मूर्च्छा । अन्ये त्वाहः केवलकफेनापि क्रियते सोष्मपदेन तु द्वन्द्वजोऽपि भवतीति सूच्यते । अन्ये त्वाहुः ऊष्मशब्देन शक्तिरुच्यते तेनोत्कृष्टशक्तिकः कफ इत्यर्थः । मर्मणीति हदये । विकारमुन्मादम् । वागित्यादि नारी- विविक्तप्रियतेति नारीप्रियता विज्ञाप्रियता च । वर्ल च भुक्ते इति व्याघेः इति शेषः । नखादीत्यादिशब्देन त्वङ्मूत्र-नेत्रादीनां ग्रहणम् ॥॥ यः सन्निपातप्रभवोऽतिघोरः सर्वैः समस्तैः स च हेतुभिः स्यात् । सर्वाणिक रूपाणिक बिभर्ति कताक्रिवरुद्धभैषज्यविधिर्विवर्ज्यः ॥१३॥
answer_text: The term sampuranaih signifies something 'due to replenishing foods’. It should be combined with the sentence ‘kapha gets aggravated’. The role of pitta is always implied in unmada caused by the kapha. By the term sosmā even the unmādā caused by syncope is implied here. Some scholars opine that it suggests dual dosa (that is kapha and pitta) vitiation and cause of the disease. Others suggest that the term marmani signifies something existing in the heart. The term nakhadi suggests the nails, skin, urine, and eyes. Sannipāta type of unmāda (CS. Ci. S. 9.15) Sannipataja unmada is generated by morbid increase in all the three dosas together by their respective causes. The features of all the dosas are seen in the patient and the medicines as well as the methods of management (for each type) being mutually contradictory this discase becomes unmanageable. 13
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 20.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 306):

शालपर्णी पृश्रिपर्णी वार्त्ताकी कण्टकारिका । गोक्षुरः पञ्चभिश्रैतैः कनिष्ठ पञ्चमूलकम् ।।४७।। पञ्चमूलं लघु स्वादु बल्यं पित्तानिलापहम् । नात्युष्णं ब्रेंहणं ग्राहि ज्वरश्वासाश्मरीप्रणुत् ।।४८.।। उभाभ्यां पञ्चमूलाभ्यां दशमूलमुदाहृतम् । दशमूलं त्रिदोषघ्नं श्वासकासशिरोरुजः । तन्द्राशोथज्वरानाहपार्श्वपीडाऽरुचीहरित् । । ४.९ । ।
answer_text: Urinary disease: The infusion prepared from fruits is effective Mūtrala (Diuretic) useful in Mūtraghāta (Retention of urine), Mūtrakṛchra (Dysuria) etc. External uses: The extracted leaf juice is applied externally over Mukhapāka (Stomatitis), Vrna (Wounds) etc. Mātrā (Dosage): Phala cūrna: 3-6 gms, Kwātha: 50-100ml. LAGUPAÑCAMÜLA Sālparṇī, Pṛsniparṇī, Bṛhatī, Kanṭakāri and Gōkṣurā all togetherly known as Laghu Pañchamūla. These are Laghu (Light for digestion), Swādu (Palatable), Bala Karaka (Strength promoters), subsides Vāṭa and Pitta doṣa, Nati usna (Not excessive hot in potency) Bṛhmaṇa (Stoutning) and Grāhī (Absorbents). it cures Jvara (Fever), Swāsa (Dysponea)and Aśmari (Renal calculi). Bṛhat and Lagu pañcamūla togetherly known as Daśamūla. It is useful in diseases of Tridoshaja origin, Swāsa (Dysponea), Kāsa (Cough), Udaraśūla (Head ache), Tandrā (Delerium), Sotha (Inflammation), Jvara (Fever), Ānāha (Flatulence), Pāśva śūla (Pain in flanks) and Aruchi (Aneroxia)
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 306
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 306.
context: शालपर्णी पृश्रिपर्णी वार्त्ताकी कण्टकारिका । गोक्षुरः पञ्चभिश्रैतैः कनिष्ठ पञ्चमूलकम् ।।४७।। पञ्चमूलं लघु स्वादु बल्यं पित्तानिलापहम् । नात्युष्णं ब्रेंहणं ग्राहि ज्वरश्वासाश्मरीप्रणुत् ।।४८.।। उभाभ्यां पञ्चमूलाभ्यां दशमूलमुदाहृतम् । दशमूलं त्रिदोषघ्नं श्वासकासशिरोरुजः । तन्द्राशोथज्वरानाहपार्श्वपीडाऽरुचीहरित् । । ४.९ । ।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Charaka Samhita (Chikitsasthana, Chapter 3, verse 128-131):

ते पूर्व केवलाः पश्चान्निजैर्व्यामिश्रलक्षणाः ॥ १२८ ॥ हेत्वौषधविहाराश्च भवन्त्यागन्तवो ज्वराः । संश्लिष्टाः सन्निपतिताः पृथग्वा कुपिता मलाः ॥ १२९ ॥ रसार्ख्यं धातुमन्वेत्य पक्तिं स्थानान्निरस्य च । स्वेन तेनोष्मणा चैव कृत्वा देहौष्मणो बलम् ॥ १३० ॥ स्रोतांसि बद्ध्वा संप्राप्ताः केवलं देहमुल्वणाः । संतापमधिकं देहे जनयन्ति नरस्य च ॥ १३१ ॥ भवत्युत्युष्णसर्वाङ्गो ज्वरितस्तेन चोच्यते ।
answer_text: The exogenous fevers are at first unstinted but later on get symptoms combined with those of innate factors. They are also specific in respect of etiology, and therapeutics. The vitiated dosas, duals, aggregated or single, associate them with rasa dhatu while expelling the agni from its place and adding to the body-heat with their own heat and the heat of (displaced) agni, also blocking the channels spread all over the body with aggravation and thus produce pyrexia. The patient gets his entire body heated and thus is said as suffering from fever
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Chikitsasthana, Chapter 3, verse 128-131.

Diseases of Ear: In case of Karnasula (Earace), extract leaves juice of radish is used as ear drops. Menstural disorders: In case if Anarthava (Ammonorrhoea) it’s seeds are used internally. GRÑJANAM Latin: Daucas carota var. sativa DC. Fam: Apiaceae Hin: Gajar ng: Carrot Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Gājara and Nāraṅgavarṇaka. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Gājara is Madhura (Sweet) and Tikta (Bitter), Tīkṣṇā (Penetrating), Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), Dīpana (Appetizer), Laghu (Light for digestion) and Sangrāhī (Absorbent). It cures Raktapitta (Haemorrages), Arśas (Piles), Grahaṇi (Sprue), Cures diseases of Kapha and Vāta. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Cultivated all over india, usually durning cold weather. Swarūpa (Botanical description): Annul to biennial herb grows 1-4ft. with tuberous root. Leaves 2-3 pinnate, lobed, narrow linear lanceolate. Flowers are arranged in compound umbel & white. Fruit 0.5 cm., bristy white. Seeds 1.5 cm dorsally compressed. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Mūla (Roots), Bīja (Seeds). question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 12):

सम्राप्तिमाहयदेत्यादि । स्रोतांसीति हिक्कानिर्विष्ट्राणीदानवहानि । कफः पूर्व प्रधान यस्य स तथा । तेनैव कफेन रुद्धो विमार्गगतिर्विमार्गगत्वेन विष्वाव्रजति विष्वगञ्वतीति विष्वक् सर्वत इत्यर्थः नरः । उद्धयमानवातों कायः कशब्दवदुदःखितों क उच्चैः श्वसिति संरुद्धो मत्तर्षभ इवानिशम् ॥१ ॥ विभ्रान्तलोचनः । प्रनष्टज्ञान-विज्ञानस्तथा बद्धमूत्र-वर्चा विवृताक्ष्याननो - दीनः प्रश्नसितं चास्य दूराद्विज्ञायते भूशम् । क्षिप्रमेव में कार विपद्यते ।। महाश्वासोपसृष्टस्तु - - -
answer_text: The passage starting from yada describes the pathogenesis of the disease śvāsa. The channels involved in breathing are prāṇavaha- srotas and udānavahasrotas. As opined in different texts, the channels involved in this disease are Prāṇavaha or the one carrying vāta, Annavaha (carrying food) and Udakavaha (carrying liquid), identical to those involved in condition of the hikka. The ensuing ‘kapha’ suggests the significance of this dosa in dyspnea. The term visvak connotes completeness and the capability of the vāyu to move every here and there. Mahāśvāsa (Great dyspnoea) (CS. Ci. S. 17.46- 48) Vata, having vitiated greatly, moves upward constantly with heavy sound and pain, like that of a powerful bull tied firmly to a peg. He loses his senses, has terrified looks with wide opened eyes and mouth, suffers from constipation and retention of urine, and speaks in feeble voice. He is depressed and his breathing can be heard from a distance. The patients undergoing such conditions are known to be suffering from mahāśvāsa; he might pass away within a short period. 18-20

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 58):

मधुकोशः अतः परमपरान् विकारान् प्रवृद्धाः प्रतिश्यायाः कुर्वन्ति; तानाह-बाधियंमित्यादि। घोरान्नयनामयनित्यभि- धानादेवान्ध्ये लब्धे विशेषेण तत्करत्वप्रतिपादनार्थमान्ध्यग्रहणम्। अग्रत्वमिति न जिघ्रतीत्यघस्तस्य भावोऽघ्रत्वम्। ‘घ्रा’ गन्धोपादाने इत्यस्मात् ‘सुपि’ स्थः’ इत्यत्र योगविभागात् कप्रत्ययः॥ ७॥ अर्बुदं सप्तधा शोथाश्चत्वारोऽर्शश्चतुर्विधम्। चतुर्विधं रक्तपित्तमुक्तं घ्राणेऽपि तद्विदुः॥ २८॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने नासारोगानिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ५८॥ मधुकोशः सुश्चते नासारोगा एकत्रिंशदुक्ताः अत्राप्यपीनसमारभ्य प्रतिश्यायपर्यन्तेन पञ्चदशोक्ताः, शेषसंख्यापूरणाया- परान् षोडश नासारोगानाह-अर्बुद सप्तथेत्यादि। एकैकदोषरक्तमांसमेदःसंभवत्वेन षडर्बुदानि, शालाक्यसिद्धान्तेन सन्निपातजमधिकं, एवं सप्त। तथा च विदेहः-‘सर्वलिङ्ग’ रुजायुक्तमर्बुद् विद्धि सर्वजम्’ इति। शोथाश्यत्वारो वातपित्तकफसन्निपातजभेदात्, एवमशोंऽपि चतुर्विधं, रक्तपत्ति चतुर्विधमपि रक्तपित्तत्वसामान्यादेकत्वेन गणनीयं, तेन न संख्यातिरेकः । अर्बुदादीनों तत्र तत्रोक्तानामत्राभिधानं शालाक्योक्तसंख्यापूरणार्थमाश्रयप्रभावेणा- तिरिक्तलिङ्गादिख्यापनार्थं च॥ २८॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां नासारोगनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ५८॥
answer_text: Now, the diseases that are caused by aggravated Pratisyayas are mentioned. Though blindness is included in mentioning "the severe eye-diseases", it is given seperately to indicate the special role of chronic pratisyaya in causing blindness. Aghratvam means not being able to distinguish the odours. The remaining nasal disorders-arbuda etc. Arbuda is of seven varieties, Šotha (oedema) is of four types, Arśas (piles) is of four types and so is Raktapitta (Haemorrhagic disease) as envisaged earlier. These diseases occuring in the nasal cavity are to be understood as having the same fea¬ tures. 28. Thus ends the chapter on diagnosis of Nasaroga (diseases of the nose) in the Mādhava’s book of diagnosis. 58. Nāsā Roga Nidāna In Susruta nasal disorders are mentioned as thirty one in number. Here also, starting from Apīnasa upto Pratiśyāya, fifteen diseases are mentioned. In order to complete the number, further sixteen diseases are being given in the above stanza. In fact arbuda is of six types only viz., vātaja, pittaja, kaphaja, raktaja, māṃsaja and medoja. As per the Śālakya subject, Sannipātaja is also considered which is the sev¬ enth. And also Videha says, "The Sarvaja (Sannipātaja) type of arbuda has the charecteristic of all the arbudas.” Sotha’s are four types viz., vātaja, pittaja, kaphaja, and sannipātaja. In the same way, Arías are four; though raktapitta is of four types, it is considered as one which makes the total number as thirty one. The arbuda etc., diseases mentioned here and there are to be included here to complete the num¬ ber and also make understand their extra features, as per the place of occurance. 28. Thus ends the diagnosis of nasal disorders in the Madhukośa commentary written by Srikantha datta. 58. **** 17 M.N. Pt-II'
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 58.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 22):

मांस-मेदोगतवातलक्षणमाह- युर्वित्यादि । श्रमितं श्रान्तं निःसहमित्यर्थः । मांस- मेदोगतवायोरेकलिङ्गत्वमदूरान्तरेण प्रत्यासत्तेराश्रयाभेदात् एवं मज्जास्थिकृपितेऽपि वाच्यम् क्षिप्रंध मुञ्चति बध्नाति शुक्रंध गर्भमथापि वा । विक्रतिं जनयेच्चापि शुक्रस्थः कुपितोऽनिलः ॥१ ॥ - - - -
answer_text: The passage starting from ruja mentions features of the vata disease that has got located in the mamsa-medogata dhatu. The term śramitam refers to the situation when one is dead tired or is not in a position to perform laborious tasks. Due to the proximity of muscle and fat tis- sues (māmsa-medas), the symptoms of the disease in context appears identical to the condition of the vata occupying either of these two. The same observation is applicable in the case of marrow and bone. Features of vitiated vāta when it reaches śukra (Semen) (CS. Ci. S. 28. 34) If the vitiated vata affects the reproductive elements (śukra) there could be either premature or delayed expulsion of semen and foetus or abnormalities in the embryo. 19
