question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 842):

प्रायः शाकानि सर्वाणि विष्टम्भीनि गुरूणि च । रूक्षाणि बहुवर्चांसि सृष्टविण्मारुतानि च।।२।। शाकं भिनत्ति वपुरस्थि निहन्ति नेत्रं, वर्णं विनाशयति रक्तमथापि शुक्रम् । प्रज्ञाक्षयं च कुरुते पलितं च नूनं, हन्ति स्मृति गतिमिति प्रवदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः ।। ३ ।। शाकेषु सर्वेषु वसन्ति रोगास्ते हेतवो देहविनाशनाय । तस्माद् बुधः शाकविवर्जनं तु कुर्यात्तथाऽम्लेषु स एव दोषः ।।४।। वास्तूक वास्तुकं च स्यात्क्षारपत्रं च शाकराट् । तदेव तु बृहत्पत्रं रक्तं स्याद् गौडवास्तुकम् ।।५।। प्रायशो यवमध्ये स्याद्यवशाकमतः स्मूतम् । वास्तूकद्वितयं स्वादु क्षारं पाके कटूदितम् ।।६।। दीपनं पाचनं रुच्यं लघु शुक्रबलप्रदम् । सरं प्लीहास्त्रपित्तार्शः कृमिदोषत्रयापहम् । । ७ । ।
answer_text: In Usually all Pot herbs /Vegetables are Vişṭambika (Causes constipation), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Rūkṣa (Drying), Excreated excessive Stools and Urine and flatus. As per scholars Śāka weakens the bones, diminishes the vision, it destroys blood, seman, Intellect, steady gait and untimely greying of hairs. All Śāka possess diseases, similar diseases destroy the body. So wise person should not consume Śāka and sour substances, which leads to negative impact on body. VĀSTŪKA DVAYAM Latin: Chenopódium album Linn. Fam: Chenopodiaceae Hin: Bathuā Eng: Lambs quarters Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Vāstuka, Kṣāra patra and Śākarāṭ. Vāstuka which having larger leaves and red in colour is know as Gouda vāstuka. Most of these are grown in the feild of barely so it is also know as Yāva Śāka. Guna Karma (Properties and indications): Both the varieties are Swadu (Palatable), Kṣāra (Alkaline), Kaṭu vīpaka (Pungent in post digestive), Dīpana (Appetizers), Pācana (Digestives), Rucya (Promotes taste), Laghu (Light for digestion), Ŝukrapradā (Increases seman), Sāra (Laxative). It cures Plīha (Diseases of spleen), Diseases of Rakta, Arśas (Piles), Kṛmi (Worm infestations) and Diseases of Tridoṣa. Note: There is another species named Sugandhā vāstuka (C. ambrosioides L.). It grows mainly in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu. It is used for the treatment of Kṛmi (Worm infestations), Atisarā (Diarrhea), Jwara (Fever) and Ajīrṇa (Indigestion). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is common in temperate regions, growing almost everywhere in soils rich in nitrogen, especially on wasteland. Botanical description (Swarūpa): It is a fast-growing, upright, weedy annual leaf grows heights of 30-80 cm. Leaves are simple, oblong, entire or toothed. Flowers are tiny small gray to green, 10-40 cm long, grow in small cymes. Seed round, very small, flattened, black in colour. Chemical constituents: Carbohydrate, Fats, Protein, Fibres, Iron, Calcium, Phosphorous and Vit C

explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 842.

answer_text: This passage suggests the major causes of indigestion. They include holding of the force of nature like urge of defection and urination. Another factor to cause indigestion is the daytime sleeping. The term Api in ‘Laghu Capi’ has been used to describe that food ftems that are even little oily and warm are not easily digestible and hence, they produce indigestion. Moreover, psychological attitudes like envy, fear, anger etc. are also among the causative factors of indigestion SS. Su. 46.501). Symptomatology of Afirna The features of āmajīrṇa include heaviness of the abdomen and/or of the whole body, nausea, swelling of the cheeks and eyes, belching occurring soon after meals. 10, The symptoms of vidagdhajirna include giddiness, thirst, fainting, sour, and warm belching, perspiration, burning sensation inside and other symptoms of the provoked pit: a. 11 A. S., Sū. Sthā., Ch. 11.55, 57, 56, 60.1) The vistabdhajirna manifests with pain in the abdomen, tympanitis, non-movement of flatus and delusion and other features of vāta. In the case of rasājīrṇa, aversion to food, bad belching and heaviness of the abdomen are seen. 12

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 74):

मधुकोशः जलस्रावपर्यायस्य पित्तस्रावस्य लक्षणमाह-हरिद्राभमित्यादि। हरिद्राभं - पीतलोहितं बोद्धव्यं, परतः पीतमित्यस्योक्तैः ( जलाभमिति जलवत् स्वच्छम्। उष्णमिति सर्वत्रैव संबध्यते। केचित् ‘पीतम्’ इत्यस्य स्थाने 'नीलम्' इति पठन्ति। 'यत्तु' 'जलाभम्' इत्यस्य स्थाने 'जलं वा' इति तदसंगतं, सुश्रुतेनोईशावसरे जलस्त्रावनामतयाऽस्योद्देशातु, तद्धि नाम जलवदास्त्रावोऽस्येति योगतः समावेशितम्। यदा तु ‘जलं वा’ इति पाठः स्यात्तदा कदाचिजलाभंता स्यादिति न सर्वत्र योगव्याप्तिरिति ) सन्धिमध्यादित्यविशेषोक्तेः सर्वसन्धिमध्यादिति बोद्धव्यम्। ननु, वातजस्त्रावः कुतो नोक्तः, वातेन स्त्रावाभावदिति चेतु; नैवं, वाताभिष्यन्दे शिशिराश्रते त्युक्तेर्वातजोऽपि स्रावो दर्शितः। उच्यते, विशिष्टेऽक्षिप्रदेशे केवलवायोः स्रावजनकत्वं संबन्धितव्यमभिधानात्। विदेहऽपि चत्वार एवोक्ताः, ‘सन्निपातात्’ कफाद्रक्तात्’ पित्तात्’ स्रावोऽक्षिसन्धिषु’ इति॥ ७३ ॥ ताम्रतन्वी दाहशूलोपपन्ना रक्ताज्ञेया पर्वणी वृत्तशोधा। जाता सन्धौ कृष्णशुक्ले- ( सु. उ. २) मधुकोशः तदेवमसाध्यनां चतुर्णां स्त्रावणां लक्षणमभिधाय पर्वणीलक्षणमाह-ताम्रेत्यारभ्य कृष्णशुक्ल इत्यन्तेन। इयं रक्तजा कफानिलजा च, रक्तजत्वमत्र सुश्रुते दर्शितमाधिक्येन॥ ऽलजी स्यात्तस्मिन्नेव ख्यापिता पूर्वलिङ्गैः॥ ७४॥ ( सु. उ. २ )
answer_text: Haridrabham like turmeric in colour-yellowish red; pitta indicates the domina¬ tion of yellow colour. Jalābhaṃ means clear like water. uṣṇa warm related to all the terms i.e, Haridrābha-uṣṇa, pīta-uṣṇa; jalābha uṣṇa-yellowish red and warm; yellow and warm; watery and warm. Some read nīla-blue-in the place of pīta-yellow. But reading jalam va in the place of jalābha does not suit here, because Suśruta wanted to make clear that this looks like clear liquid which may be in any colour but pure water discharge can not be taken as crieteria in this condition. Using the term sandhimadhyāt is applicable to any sandhi in the eye. Vātaja srāva is not mentioned here. Is it because vāta does not produce any discharge? It is not so; because in vātābhiṣyanda there is a feature, śiśirāśruta (cold-tears); hence pure vāta also will be able to cause discharge in specific part of the body. (In fact, this text should be asrāva janakatva in the place of srāvajankatva which is seen in some texts). In Videha also discharges are mentioned as four, "Due to sannipata, kapha, rakta and pitta, there will be discharge in the sandhis”. 73. Parvanī (Phlyctenular Conjunctivitis) In the Krsna-sukla sandhi (limbus) a round inflamation caused by rakta, coppery in colour, thin and associated with burning sensation and pain is known as. parvaṇī (Su.u, 2) Netra Roga Nidāna 28 1 After describing the four incurable discharges, parvani is being explained. This is caused by rakta and also kapha-vata. Susruta, considers raktaja srava as the excess type. Alañ Alajī is caused in the same sandhi with the same symptoms. 74. (Su.u.2)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 74.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2):

अथैपां लक्षणान्याहसप्ताहमित्यादि । एते विकल्पा यथाक्रमं वात-पित्त-कफोल्व- णत्वेन जेयाः । यथोक्तम्पित्तकफानिलवृद्ध्या दशदिवस-द्वादशाह-सप्ताहात् । हन्ति विमुझति वाऽऽशु त्रिदोपजो धातुमलपाकात् ॥ इति । अयं च सन्ततस्त्रिदोषज एव द्वादशा- श्रयत्वेन । यदुक्तं चरकेणयथा धातूंस्तथा मूत्रं पुरीषं चानिलादयः । युगपच्चानुपद्यन्ते नियमात् सन्तते ज्वरे ।। च०चि० इति । सन्तत्या अविच्छेदेन सप्ताहादीन् व्याप्य अविसर्गी अपरित्यागी अत्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया । ननु यद्येवं कथमस्य विषमज्वरे पाठः मुक्तानुबन्धित्वं विषमत्वं तच्चात्र नास्ति । नैवम् अस्यापि तथाभावात् । तथा च तल्लक्षणे चरकःविसर्गं द्वादशे कृत्वा दिवसेऽव्यक्तलक्षणः । दुर्लभोपशमः कालं दीर्घमप्यनुवर्ति ।। च०चि० इति । यत्तूक्त खरनादेन चत्वारः सन्ततं हित्वा ज्ञेयास्ते विषमज्वराः ।। इति तत् सन्ततं मुक्तानुबन्धित्वस्यैकदाभावि त्वेनाल्पत्वान्न तद्व्यपदेशः एकतण्डुलाभ्यवहारेऽनशनशब्दस्य व्यपदेशवत न हि तृतीय- कादिवदावृत्त्या मुक्तानुबन्धित्वमस्येत्यभिप्रायेण द्रष्टव्यम् । अथवा विषमज्वरोल्लेखेन या चिकित्सोक्ता सा सन्ततवर्जं सततादिष् कार्येति प्रतिपादनार्थम् । हरिचन्द्रेणापि किल कर्म साधारणं जह्यात्तृतीयकचतुर्थकौ । च०चि० इति चरकवचनाद्विषमज्वरोक्त- चिकित्सा तृतीयकचतुर्थकयोरेव अन्येष् दोषप्रत्यनीकचिकित्साकार्येत्यभिव्याख्यातम् । अस्यां हरिचन्द्रव्याख्यायां कर्म साधारणं सर्वत्रैव विषमज्वरे कार्यं विशेषेण तृतीयकचतुर्थकयोरिति द्रष्टव्यम् अन्यथोक्ततन्त्रान्तरविरोधः । अहोरात्रे सततको द्वी कालावनुवर्तत इति अह्नि द्वी कालो रात्रो कालों वा अह्नि एककालं रात्रावेककालमेवं वा ट्वै कालौइतीशानदेवः नियमानभि धानात्तथा दर्शनाच्च । अनुवर्तते वेगं करोति । तृतीयेऽहि तृतीयक इति वेगदिनापेक्षया तृतीयेऽहि यो भवति स तृतीयको भवति एवं चतुर्थकेऽपि वाच्यम् ।।-।। मा०नि०- केचिन्द्रताभिषङ्गोत्थं बुवते विषमज्वरम् ॥३ ॥ - - - - - -
answer_text: This passage is meant to detail features of the Santata and the like jvaras in the category of the so-named Visama Jvara. These types of fevers vary as per the pre-dominance of the vitiated dosas involved. As it has been suggested in the condition of the dhātupāka this type of tridosaja fever proves to be fatal within ten days (if pitta dosa is prominently vitiated in the given case), it turns fatal within twelve days (if kapha dosa is prominently vitiated in the given case) while it appears fatal within seven days (if vāta doṣa has been prominently vitiated in the given case). However, in the condition of the malapaka this type of tridosaja fever could be treated. One could infer the concerned passage in the sense that a fever is controlled within 7, 10 and 12 days respectively if the case is related to malapāka and if there is involvement of vāta, pitta and kapha doṣas respectively. However, if within the stipulated period there occurs the situation of dhātupāka, this disease might turn fatal. At times, the disease would continue for a long time. In this situation the physician should take into account the dosas involved. Thus, the differentiation of duration in the various sorts of Santata fever is due to the predominance of three dosas. As suggested by Caraka, the Dhātus are involved in the santata fever along with the waste (mala) like the mūtra (urine), purīṣa (stool) as well as the vāta and other dosas simultaneously (CS. Ci. 3). Thus, the vāta, pitta and kapha dosas do not free the patient of visama fever for 7, 10 and 12 days respectively. Nonetheless, now, the objection could be raised as to when muktānubandhitva (relief and affliction) is the criterion for irregular or vişama fever, how come Santata fever that remains active without break has been counted under this category? It may be noted that Caraka has suggested that even though the patient of visama fever gets relieved on twelfth day, the ailment continues to be there with feeble symptoms and the regular signs of relief from fever (like feeling of lightness in the body) do not manifest. If the feeble symptoms of the disease are not cured, the disease may continue further for a longer period (CS. Ci. 3.59). The commentator Kharanāda states, ‘Out of the five Santata and other fevers counted by me, the four ones excepting Santata are visama jvaras (irregular fevers). It seems that due to absence of ‘affliction after relief’ in Santata, this indisposition has not been counted among the Vişama jvaras. The core symptom of irregular fever does not exclude it from the irregular fevers, as eating one grain of rice does not rule out fasting. It should not be viewed as in the Truyaka fever where the cycle of fever repeats with a series of ‘relief and affliction’. Or else, Kharanada might have proposed the common treatment to all the irregular fevers excepting the Santata fever. Haricandra also opines that the treatment of visama jvara should be done as suggested by Caraka in whose opinion the common treat¬ ment is to be adopted for Triīyaka (tertian) and Caturthaka (quartan) fevers (CS. Ci. 3. 291) while in the case of others i.e. Santata, Satata, and Anyedyuşka the management has to be in the line of the doṣapratyaṇīka system. As suggested by Ḥaricandra the treatment should be common to all irregular fevers, particularly the tertian and quartan fevers. A treatment following other line would appear oppo¬ site to the instruction of other treatises. The sentence that Salalaka afflicts twice in day and night means it afflicts twice in the day and twice in the night; or it can also be taken as - it afflicts once in the day and once in the night. The commentator Iśānadeva opines that twice’ is the right choice. Finally, the types of fever named Trityaka (tertian) and Caturthaka (quartan) have been defined. The Trityaka fever is the one that appears after the third day of the first bout of fever. The caturthaka fever is the one that appears after the fourth day of the first bout. (SS. Ut. 39. 68/2) Some scholars opine that viṣama jvaras or the intermittent fevers are due to bhūtābhiṣaṅga. Note- The term bhūtābhiṣaṅga has been taken to mean bacterial infection by some modern scholars and translators. 36

answer_text: The premonitory symptoms of Apasmāra (epilepsy) are described in detail. These early signs may include aura, unusual sensations, or behavioral changes that precede the epileptic episode. answer_text: The passage starting from hyllasa refers to the prodromal character¬ istics of chardi. There is udgāra rodha that is cession of belching. Moreover, there is lavanalva that is the salty taste in the saliva as the side effect of the disease caused by either cructation from the stom¬ ach or over-burning of kapha. H Vāta type of chardi (CS. Ci. S. 20.8-9) In a case of vataja emesis or chardi there is pain in the region of the heart and flanks; dryness of mouth, discomfort in head and umbility cus, cough and hoarseness of voice, production of great sound during belching; interrupted bouts of vomiting. Moreover, the patient brings out frothy, scanty, blackish, thin, astringent materials and that too with great effort accompanied with pain all over the body. 6
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 15.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 69, verse 21-24):

मधुकोशः विषलिप्रशस्त्रहतस्य लिङ्गमाह-सद्य इत्यादि। पच्यते चाप्यभीक्ष्णमिति सद्यस्तावत् पच्यते पश्चादपि पुनः-पुनः पाकमेति॥ १३–१४॥ सपीतं गृहधूमाभं पुरीषं योऽतिसार्यते। फेनमुद्वमते चापि विषपीतं तमादिशेत्॥ १५॥ वातपित्तकफात्मानो भोगिमण्डलिराजिलाः । यथाक्रमं समाख्याता, द्वयन्तरा द्वन्द्वरूपिणाः ॥ १६ ॥ मधुकोशः स्थावरमभिधाय जङ्गमेष्वतितीक्ष्णत्वेन सर्पविषे वाच्ये तदाश्रयान् सर्पानाह वातपित्तकफात्मान इत्यादि । भोगी फणी, मण्डली मण्डलवद्रथाङ्गलाङ्गलादिरूपमण्डलयुक्तः राजिलश्चित्रदीर्घरेखावान् एते यथाक्रमं वाताद्यात्मानो वातादिप्रकृतयः । व्यतिकरजान् सर्पान् दर्शयति-द्वयन्तरा द्वन्द्वरूपिण इति। द्वयोरन्तर विशेषो येष् ते तथा। यथा-फणिना मण्डलिन्यां गोनसा जाताः, मण्डलिना गोनसेन च फणिन्यां कृष्णसर्पाः, एवमन्येऽपि जातिसंकरा ऊह्याः । व्यन्तरा इति पाठे स एवार्थः, विशब्दस्य द्वयर्थत्वात्; तथा 'विभवान्महानाकाशः' इत्यत्र व्याख्यातं, विभवादिति द्विभावात् द्विभावश्य सर्वभूर्तद्रव्यैः संयोगः सर्वत्रोपलम्भश्रेति। द्वन्द्वरूपिण इति द्वयोः फणिमण्डलिनोर्वातपित्तप्रकृत्योर्यत् प्रकृतित्वं तन्मिलितप्रकृतित्वमेषामित्यर्थः, वातपित्तप्रकृत्योरथवा द्वयोर्यद्दोषयो रूपं तद्रूपमित्यर्थः ॥ १६ ॥ दंशो भोगिकृतः कृष्णः सर्ववातविकारकृत्। पीतो मण्डलिजः शोथो मृदुः पित्तविकारवान्॥ १७॥ राजिलोत्थो भवेद्दंशः स्थिरशोथश्च पिच्छिलः । पाण्डुः स्निग्धोऽतिसान्द्रासृक् सर्वश्लेष्मविकारकृत्॥ १८॥ मधुकोशः भोगिप्रभृतिकृतदंशेषु वातादीनां लिङ्गमाह-दंशो भोगिकृत इत्यादि। संर्ववातविकारकृदित्यनेनैव कृष्णत्वे सिद्धे तदुक्तिरवश्यंभावित्वख्यापनार्थं, एवमुत्तरत्रापि पीताद्यभिधानम्॥ १७–१८ ॥ अश्वत्थदेवायतनश्मशानवल्मीकसन्ध्यासु' चतुष्पथेषु । याम्ये च दष्टाः परिवर्जनीया ऋक्षे सिरामर्मसु ये च दष्टाः॥ १९॥ मधुकोशः विशिष्टदेशादिदष्टस्यासाध्यत्वमाह-अश्वत्थेत्यादिं। याम्ये चेति भरण्याम् । ऋक्षे नक्षत्रे । मर्मस्विति आशुघातिषु। याम्ये चेति चकारेणाईश्लेषामधामूलकृत्तिकानां ग्रहणम्। यदुक्तम्। यदुक्तमन्यत्र-'चैत्यायनतन- वल्मीकश्मशानेषु चतुष्पथे। आर्द्राश्लेषामधामूलकृत्तिकाभरणीषु च॥ पञ्चभ्यां सन्ध्ययोर्दशे मर्मस्वाशुहरेषु च। दष्टाः कष्टेन जीवन्ति यदि दूतादिसंपदः॥’ इति॥१९॥ दर्वीकराणां विषमाशुघाति सर्वाणि चोष्णे द्विगुणीभवन्ति । मधुकोशः दर्वीत्यादि। दर्वीकराणां विषमाशु हन्ति अश्वत्थादौ विशेषेण दर्वीकराणामाशुमारकं, दर्वीकराः फणिनः। सर्वाणि चोष्णे द्विगुणीभवन्तीति उष्णसंयोगे सति सर्वाणि विषाणि स्वरूपतो द्वैगुण्यं भजन्ते; ‘सर्वाणि चोक्तानि यथाक्रमेण’ इति पाठान्तरे अयमर्थः-सर्वाणि भोगिमण्डलिराजिलविषाणि यथाक्रमेण यथोद्दिष्टक्रमेणोक्तान्यश्चत्था- दिष्वाशुघातीनि। दर्वीकरविषस्य पृथगुपादानं विशेषार्थम्। 1 अजीर्णपित्तातपपीडितेषु बालेषु वृद्धेषु बुभुक्षितेषु॥ २०॥ क्षीणक्षते मेहिनि कुष्ठयुक्ते रूक्षेऽबले गर्भवतीषु चापि। ( सु. क. ३) मधुकोशः एवमपरेष्वप्याशुघातित्वं संभवति, तानाह-अजीर्णेत्यादि। अजीर्णपित्तातपपीडितेष्विति अजीर्णिनि दोषत्रयप्रकोपात् पित्तातपपीडितयो रौक्ष्यात्, बालवृद्धयोरसंपूर्णक्षीणधातुत्वेन विषवेगासहत्वात्, ब्रभुक्षितेष्विति पित्तवृद्धयोष्णदेहत्वात्, क्षीणक्षत इति क्षतक्षीणे बहुलवातदुष्टेः, मेहिनि दोषत्रयप्रकोपात्, कुष्ठयुक्ते रक्तादिदोषात रूक्षे वातकोपात्, अबले क्लेशासहत्वात्,गर्भवतीषु गर्भेणोत्क्षिप्तदोषत्वात्, एषु विष माधुघतीति॥ २०॥ शस्त्रक्षते यस्य न रक्तमेति राज्यो लताभिश्च न संभवन्ति॥ २१॥ शीताभिरद्दिश्च न रोमहर्षो विषाभिभूतं परिवर्जयेत्तम्। जिह्मं मुखं यस्य च केशशातो नासावसादश्च सकण्ठभङ्कः॥ २२॥ कृष्णः सरक्तः श्वयथुश्व दंशे हन्वोः स्थिरत्वं च विवर्जनीयः। वर्तिर्घना यस्य निरेति वक्ताद्रक्तं स्त्रवेदूर्ध्वमधश्च यस्य॥ २३॥ दंष्ट्रानिपाताश्चतुरश्च यस्य तं चापि वैद्यः परिवर्जयेच्च। उन्मत्तमत्यर्थमुपद्रुतं वा हीनस्वरं वाऽप्यथवा विवर्णम्॥ २४॥ सारिष्टमत्यर्थमवेगिनं च ज्ञात्वा नरं कर्म न तत्र कुर्यातु। ( सु. क. ३)
answer_text: Pacyate cabhiksnam means once it is ripened initially, the ripening continues fast further causing severe damage to the body. 13-14. Mādhavanidānaṃ Viṣa þīta (Signs and symptoms of the individual who drinks poison) If an individual keeps passing stools in yellowish and smoky colour and vom¬ its froath from the mouth, it should be known that he has drunk the poison. 15. (Su.ka 3) The types of serpants and the doshic ralationship The Bhogī type of snakes are of vāta temperament, manḍali ones are of pitta temperament and rajila are of kapha temperament. By mixture of the quantities of two of these varieties the duyantara types of snakes are seen which have the temparament of both the corresponding dosas. 16. After mentioning about Sthavara visa, the jangamavisa is being told out of which, due to fastness, the sarpavisa (snake-poison) is explained and as a source of it, the snakes are first classified as per doşa. Bhogī means the snakes that have hood, mandali variety are those which have wide spots on the body and Rājila are those with typical stripes on the body.These have the temperaments of Vata, pitta and kapha. other types of snakes are indicated by “dvyantarā…….” i.e., new breeds having features of two of the above e.g., Gonosa type have the features of both phannini and mandali snakes having born to these two. Mandali and gonesa when cross with phanini krşna sarpa (black cobra) are resulted. In the same way other sub types have to be imagined. Dvandvarūpa means having feature of two of the three or temperament of two of the three dosas. 16. The features of Various Snake bites Visa Roga Nidāna The bite of bhogi type of snake is black in colour and causes all vata-disorders. The bite caused by mandali is in yellow colour and has soft oedema and also associated with pitta disorders. The bite of Rajila is stable, swollen, with sticky exudation, pale in colour, oily for touch, has thick blood coming out of bite-area and associated with all the Śleṣmā- disorders. 17-18. When it is mentioned sarvavatakrt causing all the Vata disorders the blackness of the bite is implied but mentioning it seperately is to emphasise the particular symptoms. In the same way pitatva (yellow colour) etc., are to be understood. The particular place where the snake bites and the part of the body of snake-bite which indicate the incurability (fatal nature) If the snake-bite takes place under a pipul tree, in a temple, in the grave-yard, near the ant-hill, during the dawn and dusk times, in the cross roads, on the days when bharani, ārdrā etc., deadly stars are present and also on the veins and vital parts of the body-that situation is incurable (lethal). 19. Yamye means in a day when the star, bharani exists. Rkse means in that star. Marmasu means in the vital point that kill immediately. By using the word, Ca in yamye ca it is to be included the stars Ardrā, Aśleṣā, Maghā, Mūlā and kṛattikā. In other texts, it is said, “Sacred places, ant-hills, grave-yards and cross roads; on the days when the stars ārdrā, āsleṣā, maghā, mūla and kṛttika exist and also on the fifth day of ascending or descending moon and during the dawn and dusk - if the snake bites, that individual can live with difficulty that if equipped with proper messen¬ ger etc.". 19. Mādhavanidānaṃ The lethality of snake poison The hooded snake-poison kills instantaneously. The effect of the poison of all other snakes becomes double folded if the bite takes place during summer. The poison of hooded snakes that too in the places mentioned in the above stanza, kill instantaneously. During the warm time (summer or midday or in a place where warmth is more) the poisonous effect of other snakes become double folded. As per the different text, "Sarvani coktani yatha kramena" the meaning is - the poison of bhogi, mandala and rājila, as per the order of merit, become lethal instantaneously, as per the place of bite also. The seperate mentioning of hooded snakes is to make clear its severe lethal nature. State of the individual at the time of snake that leads to incurability If the individual, at the time of snake bite, in one of these conditions, it becomes difficult for cure- indigestion, pitta affliction, suffering from hot-Sun, earlyage, old-age, hunger sticken, emaciated due to injury, suffering with delusion, suffering with skin disease, dryness of the body weakened and in pregnancy. 20, (Su.Ka.3) The faster killing of the snake poison is caused in indigestion-due to Tridosa aggravation, suffering from pitta affliction and hot sun-due to dryness of the body, in early age-due to incomplete tissue structure, in old age-due to emaciated tissue Visa Roga Nidāna status, (in both these conditions the body can not withstand the snake poison), in hunger sticken stage-due to increase of the pitta. There will be more warmth in th e body, in emaciated stage caused by injury due to aggravated Vāta., in meha-due to tridosa aggravation, in skin disease due to vitiation of blood, in dryness due to aggravation of vāta, in weakness due to not being able to with stand any suffering and in pregnancy due to aggravated dosas. 20. The other condition that are incurable When an snake-bitten individual does not bleed on being cut with weapon, does not show any signs on tying tightly with vines and ropes and does not get skintillation by the touch of cold water, he should not be taken for treatment. When the face becomes curved, the hair keeps falling, there is depression of the brim of the nose, suffers from neck problem (not being able to hold the neck straight), the bite area becomes redish black with inflammation and when there is lock-jaw, such patient also should be discarded from treating. If salivation gets so¬ lidified and comes out in the form of a wick and blood comes out from the mouth nose and anus and has four marks of snake bite, such an individual also should be left without treating. When the snake - bitten individual becomes insane or gets many compliations, the voice becomes very weak, the body becomes discoloured, there are many fatal complications and the natural urges are not passed or be¬ comes very slow-such a person also should not be treated. 21-24. (Su. ka. 3)

‘सर्वाणि चोक्तानि यथाक्रमेण’ इति पाठान्तरे अयमर्थः-सर्वाणि भोगिमण्डलिराजिलविषाणि यथाक्रमेण यथोद्दिष्टक्रमेणोक्तान्यश्चत्था- दिष्वाशुघातीनि। दर्वीकरविषस्य पृथगुपादानं विशेषार्थम्। 1 अजीर्णपित्तातपपीडितेषु बालेषु वृद्धेषु बुभुक्षितेषु॥ २०॥ क्षीणक्षते मेहिनि कुष्ठयुक्ते रूक्षेऽबले गर्भवतीषु चापि। ( सु. क. ३) मधुकोशः एवमपरेष्वप्याशुघातित्वं संभवति, तानाह-अजीर्णेत्यादि। अजीर्णपित्तातपपीडितेष्विति अजीर्णिनि दोषत्रयप्रकोपात् पित्तातपपीडितयो रौक्ष्यात्, बालवृद्धयोरसंपूर्णक्षीणधातुत्वेन विषवेगासहत्वात्, ब्रभुक्षितेष्विति पित्तवृद्धयोष्णदेहत्वात्, क्षीणक्षत इति क्षतक्षीणे बहुलवातदुष्टेः, मेहिनि दोषत्रयप्रकोपात्, कुष्ठयुक्ते रक्तादिदोषात रूक्षे वातकोपात्, अबले क्लेशासहत्वात्,गर्भवतीषु गर्भेणोत्क्षिप्तदोषत्वात्, एषु विष माधुघतीति॥ २०॥ शस्त्रक्षते यस्य न रक्तमेति राज्यो लताभिश्च न संभवन्ति॥ २१॥ शीताभिरद्दिश्च न रोमहर्षो विषाभिभूतं परिवर्जयेत्तम्। जिह्मं मुखं यस्य च केशशातो नासावसादश्च सकण्ठभङ्कः॥ २२॥ कृष्णः सरक्तः श्वयथुश्व दंशे हन्वोः स्थिरत्वं च विवर्जनीयः। वर्तिर्घना यस्य निरेति वक्ताद्रक्तं स्त्रवेदूर्ध्वमधश्च यस्य॥ २३॥ दंष्ट्रानिपाताश्चतुरश्च यस्य तं चापि वैद्यः परिवर्जयेच्च। उन्मत्तमत्यर्थमुपद्रुतं वा हीनस्वरं वाऽप्यथवा विवर्णम्॥ २४॥ सारिष्टमत्यर्थमवेगिनं च ज्ञात्वा नरं कर्म न तत्र कुर्यातु। ( सु. क. ३)

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 312):

अष्टवर्गः सयष्टीको जीवन्ती मुद्गपर्णिका । माषपर्णी गणोऽयं तु जीवनीय इति स्मृतः ।।५७।। जीवनो मधुरश्रापि नामा स परिकीर्तितः । जीवनीयगणः प्रोक्तः शुक्रकृद् बृंहणो हिमः ।।५८।। गुरुर्गर्भप्रदः स्तन्यकफकृत्पित्तरक्तहत् । तृष्णां शोष ज्वरं दाह रक्तपित्तं व्यपोहति ।।५९।।
answer_text: The Drug's belonging to Astavarga along with Yastīka, Jīvantī, Mudga parṇī and Māṣa parnī togetherly known as Jīvanīya gana. It is also known by names Jīvana and Madhura. It is Sukrajanaka (Increases seman), Bṛhmaṇa (Stoutning), Sīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Gurus (Heavy for digestion) Garbhapradā (Helpful in concive), Stanyajanana (Galactogogue), increases Kapha doşa, Subsides Pitta and Rakta. It cures Tṛṣṇā (Thrist), Soṣa (Emaciation), Jvara (Fever), Dāha (Burning sensation) and Raktapitta (Haemorrages)
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 312
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 312.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 118):

नाकुली सुरसा नागसुगन्धा गन्धनाकुली । नकुलेष्टा भुजङ्ग़ाक्षी सर्पाङ्गी विषनाशिनी ।।१६५।। नाकुली तुवरा तिक्ता कटुकोष्णा विनाशयेत् । भोगिलूतावृश्चिकाखुविषज्वरकृमिव्रणान् ।। १६६।।
answer_text: Latin: Rauwolfia serpentina Benth.Ex.Kurz. Fam: Apocynaceae. Hin: Nakulakandha. Eng: Snake dog-eared bane, Small moon plant. Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Surasā, Nāgsugandhā, Gandhnākulī, Nakulēṣṭā, Bhujañgāṣī, Sarpāñgī, and Visanāśinī. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): It is Kaṣāya (Astringent), Tiktā (Bitter) and Kaṭu (Pungent) in taste, Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), it destroys Posionous ill effects of Sarpa, Lutā and Vrścikā and Mūśika, cures Jwara (Fever), Krmi (Worm infestations) and Vṛṇa (Wounds). Note: There was a contraversy regarding correct identity of Nākulī. Some scholars has equated this with Aristolochiaceae indica Linn. and Rawolfia serpentine Benth. Ex. Kurz. Caraka has not taken in notice the term or disease ãmãtisãra and has suggested that visũcikã is the symptom of discharge of uncooked and stomached materials from the mouth as well as through rectum. question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 20):

answer_text: According to Cakrapāṇi, the term alpasattva is the personality of one with lesser Sattva guņa, the most desirable mental characteristic. In the opinion of Jejjata, it is the mind itself. Alpatva, lesser attitude, applies to the discriminative capability. Mala refers to the vāta and other dosas. By stating that the Hrdaya is the abode of buddhi of intellect, it has been suggested here that the vitiation of intellect can also take place. Manovāhaśrotas are the ten dhamanīs attached to the heart, which are spread all over the body according to Caraka. Common symptomatology of unmāda (Insanity) (CS. Ci. S. 9.6) The common specific features of unmada include a confused intellect and fickleness of mind, in-coordination of gaze, incoherent speech, and mental vacuum and similar features. 6
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 20.

answer_text: In view of the commonality of swelling (between śūpada and vidradhi ) vidradhi is being explained (after śūpada ). (Ca. ci. 17) āta type of vidradhi The colour of the Vidradhi will be either black or red; irregular in size, has severe pain and has typical on set and ripening - in the case of Vata predominance in Vidradhi. 4. (Su. Ni. 9). Visama bhrsam means some times small and some time big. Typicality in onset and ripening of this disease is due the irregular nature of vāta. 4. (Su. Ni. 9)

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 101):

ऋद्धिवृद्धिश्व कन्दौ द्वौ भवतः कोशलेऽचले । श्वेतलोमान्वितः कन्दो लताजातः सरन्थ्रकः ।।१३८।। स एव ऋद्धिर्वृद्धिश्च भेदमप्येतयोब्रुवे । तूलयग्रन्थिसमा ऋद्धिर्वमावर्त्तफला चसा ।।१३९।। वृद्धिस्तु दक्षिणावर्तफला प्रोक्ता महर्षिभिः । ऋद्धियोग्यं सिद्धिलक्ष्म्यौ वृद्धेरप्याह्वया इमे ।।१४०।। ऋद्विबल्या त्रिदोषघ्नी शुक्रला मधुरा गुरुः । प्राणैश्वर्यकरी मूर्च्छारक्तपित्तविनाशिनी ।।१४१।। वृद्धिगभेप्रदा शीता बृंहणी मधुरा स्मृता । वृष्या पित्तास्त्रशमनी क्षतकासक्षयापहा ।।१४२।। राज्ञामप्यष्टवर्गस्तु यतोऽयमतिदुर्लभः । तस्मादस्य प्रतिनिधि गृह्हीयात्तद्गुणं भिषक् ।।१४३।।
answer_text: Riddhi and Vrddhi found in Koshala hills. Both are having similar morphological features and Kandha (Tubers) are fibrous white in colour. Riddhi resembles those of ‘Tūlagranthi’ (Knott’s of cotton plant) and its fruits has a left twist and Vrddhi has takes right twist. Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Both have commonly named as Yogya, Siddhi and Lakshmi. Guna karma (Properties and indications): Riddhi is Balya (Strength promoters), Subsides all tridosas, Sukrala (Increses seman), Madhurā rasa (Sweet) in taste, Guru (Heavy for digestion), Aishwarya janaka (One which brings wealth & progeny), Pranaprada (Life saving), it cures Murcha (Vertigo)and Raktapitta hara (Useful in intrinsic haemorrage). Vrddhi is Garbhaprada (One which gives progeny), Sītavīrya (Cold potency), Bṛmhaṇa (Stoutning), Madhurā (Sweet) in taste, Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac), and Raktapittahara (Cures intrinsic haemorrage). It cures Kṣatakāsa (manifestation of cough due to injured lung) and Kṣaya (Emaciation). The above said Astavarga group of drugs are very rare in occurance, it is very difficult to found even for the kings in olden days. So it's the duty of vaidyas to look for such subsitutes which having similar properties & actions
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 101
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 101.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 22):

स्वास्थ्यं पीडालाघवं, भारापगमे सुखित्वव्यपदेशवत् ।। जिह्वानिर्लेखनाच्छुष्कभक्षणादभिघाततः हनुमूलस्थः स्त्रंसयित्वाऽनिलो हनुमू ॥49॥ दिवास्वप्नेत्यादि । एवेति वातः ॥51॥
answer_text: The passage starting from kṣīṇasya refers to the characteristics of the incurable variety of the disease ardita. In this situation, the patient is not able to close the eye as signified by the term animiṣākṣa. The term prasaktāvyaktabhāṣiṇ signifies the one having hindered speech. Term avyaktabhāsin signifies the one having unclear speech or having difficulty in speaking. Some scholars opine that the term prasakta suggests the one who speaks continuously. It seems to be incorrect, as stated in the text of Caraka, the tongue of the Ardita- patient is flaccid and it remains hidden inside the buckle cavity and it is no longer active when there is a need for speaking (CS. Ci. 28.41). The term Trivarṣa signifies the completion of three years of duration after onset of the disease. The term may also mean the discharge (varṣā) from the three (tri) of the limbs: mouth, nose, and cyes. Note: The disease and its description broadly match to the symplom identified as Bell’s palsy in the modern medicine. It is a unilateral facial paralysis of sudden onset. The paralysis involves both the up¬ per and lower halves of the face. It has been differentiated from the facial strokes in terms of the fact that the stroke in question affects the muscles of mouth more than those of the eye or forehead do. The Bell's palsy is generally caused by activation of herpes simplex vi¬ rus. The temporary relief in convulsions (Periodicity and remission) (AH. Ni. 15.28/2) In all types of convulsive disorders (ākṣepakas) described above, the patient is considered as have regained when the episodes of attack pass off. 48 In terms of signifying a svastha or healthy person, it is suggested here that there is decrease in the pain and a feeling of comfort by an individual as if he has taken off the weight he has been carrying. Note: As regards convulsion, the modern science has accepted that it appears due to certain other disorders like epilepsy, eclampsia, meningitis, heat cramps, brain lesions, tetanus, uremia, and hyper- tension. In children, convulsion could also appear due to fever. Hanugraha (Lock-jaw) (Dislocation of jaw) (AH. Ni. 15.29-30) Indulgence in putting out the tongue too much for long periods, eating dry foods and also due to trauma, the vāyu situated at the temporomandibular joint of the jaw turns vitiated and dislocates the mandible making the mouth either remain open or closed. The condition is called hanugraha (dislocation of the jaw) and it causes inability to masticate and to utter voice. 49-50

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 445):

काकमाची ध्वाङ्क्षमाची काकाह्वा चैव वायसी । काकमाची त्रिदोषघ्नी स्निग्धोष्णा स्वरशुक्रदा ।।२४६।। तिक्ता रसायनी शोथकुष्ठाशोज्वरमेहजित् । कटुर्नेत्रहिता हिक्काच्छर्दिहद्रोगनाशिनी ।। २४७ ।।
answer_text: Roots are Recaka (Purgative), useful in Yakṛt roga (Liver diseases) and Prameha (Diabetes). The paste of the murva root is applied externally over Twak vikaras (Skin diseases). Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrṇa: 3-6gms., Kwātha: 50-100ml. KĀKAMĀCĪ Latin: Solanum nigrum Linn. Fam: Solanaceae Hin: Makoya Eng: Black nightshade Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Dhvāmkṣaṃācī, Kākāhvā and Vāyasī. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Kākamācī is Katu (Pungent) and Tikta (Bitter) in taste, subsides Tri doşas, Snigdha (oilyness), Uşna virya (Hot in potency), Swarya (Promotes good voice), Sukrala (Increases seman), and Rāsayana (Reguvenator). It cures Sotha (Inflammation), Kuşta (Leprosy), Arśas (Piles), Jvara (Fever), Prameha (Diabeties), Netrahita (Good for eyes), Hikkā (Hicough), Chardi (Vomiting) and Hrdroga (Cardiac diseases). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is found in Western Himalayan regions at the elevation of 8000ft. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is diffuse much branched annual herb reaches upto 1-2ft. Stem erect, glabrous. Leaves 10cm long and 5cm wide, ovate- lanceolate, with serrated margins. Flowers small white arranged in Umbellate cymes. Fruit is berry, 6mm. across, black when ripe. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Pañcānga (Fruit), Phala (Fruits). Chemical constituents: Alkaloid- Solanin and Saphonins
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 445
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 445.
context: काकमाची ध्वाङ्क्षमाची काकाह्वा चैव वायसी । काकमाची त्रिदोषघ्नी स्निग्धोष्णा स्वरशुक्रदा ।।२४६।। तिक्ता रसायनी शोथकुष्ठाशोज्वरमेहजित् । कटुर्नेत्रहिता हिक्काच्छर्दिहद्रोगनाशिनी ।। २४७ ।।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 11):

क्षयजकासमाह विषमेत्यादि । घृषिनां शोचतां चाहाराभावात् कुपितेन वायुनाऽग्ने- रुपप्लवाद्दोषत्रयप्रकोप इति । क्षयजमिति श्रक्रादिधातक्षयजं न त राजयक्ष्मजम् । त्रिदोषजंऽपि राजयक्ष्मणि कासः कफेनैव क्रियते । यद्रक्त कासः कण्ठस्य चोद्ध्वसो विज्ञेयः कफ- कोपतः । इति क्षयजकासस्तु विदोषज इति । नन कासादेव क्षयों जायते तत् कथं क्षयजः कास इति उक्त हिकासात् संझायते क्षयः च०नि० इति । उच्यते दृष्टो हि परस्परं व्यक्तिभेदेन कार्यकारणभावो बहुशः यथाऽतीसाराशोंऽम्निमान्यादविंति । ननु स गात्रशूलेत्यादिश्लोकार्धस्य क्षयजकासमध्ये पर्वोड्यक्तः प्रतिभाति सुश्रते स्क्षतजकासे पठितत्वात् क्षयकासश्चात्र चरक-सुश्चत्रवाक्ये मेलयित्वा माधवकरेण लिखितः उच्यते स गात्रशूलेत्याद्यन-तरं क्षयकासः सुध्रतेन पठितः तेन स मात्रशूल इत्यादिश्लोकार्धस्य परेण सम्बन्धात् क्षयकासलिङ्गत्वमिति माधवकरस्याभिप्रायः एतच्चान्ये नानुमन्यन्ते यतः क्षत- कासस्यावस्थायामसाध्यत्वख्यापनपरमेतद्व्याख्यातं जेज्जटेन गयदासेनापि क्षतजकास- रूपत्वेनेति - देहनाशनः । क्षयजः कासः क्षीणानां इत्येष - साध्यो बलवतां वा स्याद्याप्यस्त्वेवं क्षतोत्थितः ॥ ॥ कदाचित्सिध्येतामपिक स्थापादगुणान्वितौ । नवौ स्थविराणां जराकासः सर्वो याप्यः प्रकीर्तितः । त्रीन् पूर्वान् साध्ययेत् साध्यान् पथ्यैर्याप्यांस्त्र यापयेत् ॥१ ॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने कासनिदाने समाप्तम् ॥ ॥ - - -
answer_text: The passage starting from visama refers to the kṣayaja type of kasa. The deterioration of digestive fire occurs to those who suffer from aversion towards food and who remain concerned about their own well-being, as they could not consume food in such a situation. Cough is caused by kṣaya i.e. depletion of tissues and not by consumption. The kasa that is produced as implication of the tridoṣaja rājayakṣmā is also generated due to the vitiated kapha. The hoarseness of voice and choking in the throat are also caused due to the vitiated kapha. Nonetheless, the kṣayaja kāṣa is generated by vitiation of all the three dosas. As such, cough leads to emaciation, as supported by Caraka, who is of the opinion that kasa is the reason due to which kṣaya occurs ( CS. Ci. 8.19). Then how can kṣaya cause kāsa? It is considered that the interchange of the cause and effect in their roles has been noticed in various instances, such as the diarrhoea, piles and weak digestion keep causing each other. The passage starting from sa gatrasiila refers to the ksayaja variety of kāsa while Suśruta suggested these features (as mentioned in the passage starting from sa gātraśūla) in the context of the kṣataja variety of kasa. Probably the author Madhavakara has mixed the narratives relating to both the varieties of the kāsa. This mixing has not found favour on the part of the commentators like Jejjaṭa and Gayadāsa. Curability and incurability of kāsa (Cough) (CS. Ci. S. 18.29-31: 1) Cough is curable if it is affecting persons who are strong. It is also curable if it is of a recent onset (at the time of the beginning of treatment). The prolonged cases of kūsa could be cured with suitable foods and medicines. The first three varieties are easily curable; the chronic cases of kāsa are to be controlled with suitable eatables and the like. The first three types of cough are curable and they are to be treated. 14-15
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 11.

answer_text: This condition is caused by the śleṣmā which is lodged in the first and second layers of the eye. In the next line it is said that "in three of the layers". Tani means the objectives. By saying, "The dosa lodged in three of the layers in smaller amount.....". It is indicated the positivity towards vision during day time. If the dosa is heavily accumulated, there would not be vision during day time also. Dosa, here is kapha because it is only occupying here. This condition is Naktandhya (night blindness). Mādhavanidānaṃ Dhūmadarśi (Smoky vision) If the vision of an individual is affected by grief, fever, strain, warmth of the head, everything appears as clusters of smoke. question:

बहुवारस्तु शीतः स्यादुद्दालो बहुवारकः । शेलुः श्लेष्मातकश्चापि पिच्छिलो भूतवृक्षकः ।।१०५।। बहुवारो विषस्फोटव्रणवीसर्पकुष्ठनुत् । मधुरस्तुवरस्तिक्तः केश्यश्र कफपित्तहृत् ।।१०६।। फलमामन्तु विष्टम्भि रूक्षं पित्तकफास्त्रजित् । तत्पकं मधुरं स्निग्यं श्लेष्मलं शीतलं गुरु ।।१०७।।
answer_text: Digestive diseases: Dadima phalā twak is predominant of Kaṣāya (Astringent) taste, valuable in Ātisarā (Diarrhoea) and advanced stages of Atisarā (Dysentery). It is usually administered in decoction prepared by alone phala twak or along with Lavanga or Twak. The fresh root bark is a reliable remedy for the expulsion of Kṛmi (Worms) especially tenia or tape worm. A kwātha is prepared from Phalā twak is used to cure Raktārśas (Bleeding piles). Respiratory diseases: The flowers buds powder given in appopriate dosage cures Swasānalikaśotha (Chronic Bronchitis) etc. Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrṇa: 1-2 gm. BAHUVÃRA Fam: Boraginaceae Latin: Cordia myxa Roxb. Hin: Bhairala Eng: Sebesten Plum Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Śīta, Uddāla, Śelu, Ślesmātaka, Pichcila and Bhūtavṛkṣaka. Guna karma (Properties and indications): Bahuvāra cures Viṣa (Posions), Vispoṭa (Boils), Vṛṇa (Wounds), Visarpa (Herpes), Kuṣṭa (Leprosy) and diseases of Kapha and Pitta. It acts as Kesya (Good for hairs), Madhura (Sweet), Kaşāya (Astringent) and Tiktā (Bitter) in taste. It’s unripen fruits are Viṣṭambi (Causes constipation), Rūkṣā (Drying), cures diseases of Pitta, Kapha and Rakta. Its ripen fruits are Madhura (Sweet) in taste, Snigdha (Oilyness), Increases Kapha, Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency) and Guru (Heavy for digestion). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): it is grown throughout the warmer and drier parts of India. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a moderate-sized deciduous tree. Bark is grey or brown rough, with longitudinal wrinkles and furrows. Leaves are simple, 6-10 cm. long, 4-7 cm. ovate- elliptical, alternately arranged, round base, obtuse apex and entire margins. Flowers are arranged in corymbs cymes, white in colour. Fruit-drupe, cylindrical, pink or black when ripe. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Patra (Leaves), Twak (Bark), Puṣpā (Flowers), Phalā majja (Fruit pulp). Chemical constituents: Fruits contain sugar, gum, β-sitosterol, palmitic, stearic and oleic acids. Bark contains tannins

मधुकोशः शोथस्योपद्रवत्वेनोक्तत्वात्तदनन्तरं शोथनिदानम्। उदरे संप्राप्तिमाहरक्तपित्तकफानित्यादि। तस्य रक्तपित्तकफान् स्वहेतुभिः दुष्टान् कुपितान्, दुष्टः स्वहेतकुपितो वायुर्बहिःसिरा बाह्या अगम्भीराः सिरा नीत्वा गमयित्वा, तै रक्तपित्तकफै रुद्धगतिरावृतमार्गो वायुरुत्सेधमुच्छायं कुर्यादिति योजना। बहिःसिराशब्देनात्रा- गम्भीरतयोक्तानां स्रोतसामपि ग्रहणम्। त्वड्सांससंश्रयमित्यनेन व्रणशोथाद् भेदं दर्शयति, अष्टसु व्रणवास्तुषु व्रणशोथस्य संभवात्। यदुक्तं सुश्रुतेन-'त्वड्मांससिरास्नाय्वस्थिसन्धिकोष्ठमर्माणीत्यष्टौ व्रणवास्तूनि भवन्ति' सु.सू.स्था. २२) इति। संहतं संहतात्मकमित्यत आह—निचयादत इति। अतोऽस्मात् पूर्वोक्ताद्रक्तसहितदोषत्रय– समुदायात्; एतेन रक्तसहितत्रिदोषजन्यत्वमस्योक्त भवति। सर्वमित्यादि। सर्वामिति पूर्वेण संबध्यते, सर्वमुत्सेधं शोथमाहुरित्यर्थः। हेतुविशेषैरिति दोषत्रयाभिधातप्रभूतिभिः कारणभेदैर्यो रूपभेदस्तस्मात् सर्व नवात्मकमाहुरिति पूर्वक्रियया संबन्धः । ' सर्वहेतुविशेषैः ' इति पाठान्तरे सर्वेषां हेतुविशेषैरित्यर्थः । द्वयैरिति द्वन्दैः, सर्वेस्त्रिभिः ॥ १–२ ॥ तत्पूर्वरूपं दवथुः सिरायामोऽङ्गौरवम्॥ ३॥ ( वा.नि. १३ ) मधुकोशः पूर्वरूपमाह-तदित्यादि। दवथुरुपतापः। सिरायामः सिराप्रसरणवत् पीडा॥ ३॥ शुद्ध्यामयाभुक्तकृशाबलानां क्षाराम्लतीक्ष्णोष्णगुरूपसेवा। दध्याममृच्छाकविरोधिदुष्टगरोपसृष्टान्ननिषेवणं च॥ ४॥ अर्शांस्यचेष्टा न च देहशुद्धिर्मर्मोपघातो विषमा प्रसूतिः । मिथ्योपचारः प्रतिकर्मणां च निजस्य हेतुः श्वयथोः प्रदिष्टः॥ ५॥ मधुकोशः पूर्वरूपानन्तरं कामचारान्निदानमाह-शुन्द्र्यामयेत्यादि। शुन्द्रिवर्वमनविरेचनादिः, आमया ज्वरादयः, अभुक्तम- भोजन विगुणं च भोजनं, तैः कृशानामबलानां च क्षारादिसेवा निजस्य श्वयथोहेंतः । दध्यादयः स्वतन्त्रा एव हेतवः, आममपक्क, दुष्ट दोषजनक मन्दकनवोदकादि, गरं संयोगज विषम्। अचेष्टा निष्क्रियत्वम्। न च देहशुद्धिरिति शोधनाहेंऽपि दोषे देहाशुद्धिः। मर्मोपघात इह दोषकृत एव ज़ेयः, बाह्यहेतुजस्तु मर्मोपघात आगन्तुशोथहेतुरेव। विषमा प्रसूतिरामगर्भपतनादिका। मिथ्योपचारोऽसम्यक्करणमसम्यगुपचारः। प्रतिकर्मणां वमनादीनाम्॥ ४–५॥ सगौरवं स्यादनवस्थितत्वं सोत्सेधमूष्माऽथ सिरातनुत्वम् । सलोमहर्षश्च विवर्णता च सामान्यलिङ्ग श्वयथोः प्रदिष्टम्॥ ६॥
answer_text: Since śotha is mentioned as a complication in udara chapter, it is now being explained (in full fledged manner) after udara roga. The vāia agravated by its own reasons, brings the rakta, pitta, and kapha which are individually vitiated by their own aetiological factors, to the external veins which are not so deeply situated and having obstructed by rakta, pitta and kapha, causes oedema. By saying superficial Mādhavanidānaṃ viens, the not so deep srotas (channel) should also be taken into consideration here. To differentiate this oedema from the inflammation caused by wound, skin and muscle are only said to be involved here. Susruta said, regarding the involvement of the material in the wound, “Skin, muscle, veins, ligaments, bone, joints, alimentary canal and vital points, are the eight things involved in the wound (These are called vraṇa vastu (material for wound)”. (Su. Sū. 22). Samhatam means brought together to one place. Why is it samhata? The an¬ swer is given in the word "nicayadatah". The origination of sotha involves tridosas along with rakta. All swellings are to be known as śothas. Hetuviśeṣaiḥ means, due to three dosas, etc., whatever differentiation in the symptomatology occurs, by that appearance sotha is of nine types. According to the different text, "sarvahetuvisesaih", means-due to different aetiological factors. "dvayoh" - due to dosa duo. sarviah due to - dosa - triad. Premonitory symptoms of Sotha The premonitory symptoms of śotha are - burning sensation, stretching pain in the veins and heaviness in the limbs. 3 (Davathu means light burning sensation. According to Caraka, severe burn¬ ing sensation in the eyes etc.). (Vā. Ni. 13). Davathu - slight burning sensation. Sirayama means stretching pain in the veins. Aetiology of Sotha Consumption of little amount of incompatible food by the individuals who have under gone cleansing therapy or afflicted by diseases, consumption of alkali foods, sour, fast, warm and heavy food by those who observe fasting or weakened after cleansing therapy or due to affliction of diseases: consumption of curds, wet mud, uncooked vegetables, incompatible food combination, putrified foods and Sotha Nidāna foods that are afflicted by poisons that originate due to typical combinations: suffering from piles, not indulging in any activity, not following the body cleansing measures, trauma to the vital parts, irregular child delivery and improper regimen after cleansing therapies, are the aetiological factors for the natural type of Sotha. (oedema caused by intrisic factors) 4, 5. (Ca. Ci. 12). As before, the nidana (aetiology) is being explained after the premonitary symptoms. Suddhi - the cleansing measures - are emesis, purgation etc., āmayā means diseases like fever etc; abhukta not eating or irregular eating; those who are emaciated due to these factors or weakened, when they consume alkali foods etc., w it becomes aetiological factors (without even any other condition if one indulges in consumption of curds etc., he gets śotha). Ama means unripe or uncooked. I Duşta means harmful foods, mandaka (incompletely formed alcohol) new waters etc., gara means poison formed by typical combinations of incompatible foods. Acestā means not indulging in any activity. Not adopting any body-cleansing means even when it is needed, such measures are neglected. Marmapaghāta, here, should be taken as caused by intrinsic factors. The external stimuli that is causing marnapaghāta (trauma to the vital parts) is causative factor of āgantu śotha (Sudden on set of oedema). Visama prasuti means delivery of incompletely formed foetus (abortion) etc., improper treatment - (mithyopcāra) improper procedures with improper apparatus, pratikarma means vamana (Emesis) etc. 4, 5. Common symptomatology of Sotha Unstableness, feeling of heaviness, swelling, warmth on the skin, thinning of the veins, horippulation, and discolouration of the skin are the common signs and symptoms of Sotha. 6. (Ca. Ci-12)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 36, verse 6.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Nidanasthana, Chapter 2, verse 75):

अस्फुटध्वनि:’ इति पा. I स्वेदो लघुत्व शिरसः कण्ड्: पाको मुखस्य च । क्षवथुश्रान्नलिप्सा च ज्वरमुक्तस्य लक्षणमु ।।७५।।
answer_text: Kujana is making unclear sounds, Caraka says, ‘‘When the fever relieves, the individual makes unclear sounds and vomits. (Ca. ci. 3). Vāgbhaṭa also says that the Dosa, while detaching from the Dhatu, becomes strong and irritates them and the individual breathes vigorously, sweats, makes unclear sounds and vomits. (Vā. ni. 2). Actually the relief of a disease is characterised by weakened Dosa; then how can a weak Dosa cause these symptoms? It is said that certain things, though they are weak, before they get destroyed, show up intensity as the wick burns bright just before extinguishing. The Dosa afflicted tissues get irritated when the Dosa re¬ lieves them and causes burning sensation etc., as the tender branches of a tree are shaken when the monkey leaves the tree. Signs and symptoms on relief of fever Thus ends the diagnosis of fever in the Madhavanidana written by Srīmādhavakara
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana, Chapter 2, verse 75.
context: अस्फुटध्वनि:’ इति पा. I स्वेदो लघुत्व शिरसः कण्ड्: पाको मुखस्य च । क्षवथुश्रान्नलिप्सा च ज्वरमुक्तस्य लक्षणमु ।।७५।।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59):

मधुकोशः रागोऽरुणो मारुतज इत्यादिसूत्र पूर्वोक्त विवृणोति-अरुणं मण्डलं वातादित्यादि। पित्तान्मण्डलमानीलमिति आनीलमीषन्नीलं पीतमेव, तेन रक्तसंबन्धे सति कांस्याभम्। पीतमेव चेति रससंबन्धे पीतमेव, कांस्याभमा- पाण्डुपीतमित्यर्थः। केचिदत्र कफर्जे पठन्ति, 'संकुचत्यातपेऽत्यर्थं छायायां विस्तृतो भवेत्' इति। शोणितजे प्रवालेत्यादौ प्रवाल स्वनामख्यातं तदाभं, पद्मपत्राभं च रक्तपद्मपुष्पदलाभम्। त्रिदोषजे चित्र इत्यत्र यथास्वं वातादिवर्णविभेदेन चित्रत्वं बोद्धव्यं, यथास्वमित्यस्य वक्ष्यमाणस्यात्रापि संबन्धात्; तेनायमर्थः-यथायथं वातादीनां वर्णभेदेन चित्रवर्णो भवति, उद्देशोक्तवर्णचित्रत्वे साक्षादेतादूशविवरणाभाव इति विशेषः। यथास्वं दोषलिङ्गानीत्यस्याभिधानं न्यायसिद्धस्यैवार्थस्य द्योतनार्थम्। दोषलिङ्गानि वातादीनां क्रमेणारुणादिलिङ्गान्युक्तेषु ज्ञातव्यानि ॥ ५१–५४ ॥ षड् लिङ्गनाशाः षडिमे च रोगा दृष्ट्याश्रयाः षट् च षडेव वाच्याः। ( सु.उ. ७) मधुकोशः अतः परमुक्तवश्यमामविकारयोः संख्याभिधानार्थमाह-षडित्यादि। षड्लिङ्गनाशा इत्युक्तानुवादोऽयम्। षडिमे च रोगा इति पित्तविदग्धदृष्ट्यादयो वक्ष्यमाणाः। ननु, उक्तानुवादो युक्तः, वक्ष्यमाणानां, पुनः किमथी संख्योक्तिः ? नैवं पित्तकफविदग्धदृष्ट्यवस्थान्तराभ्यां दिवान्धरात्र्यन्धाभ्यां संख्याधिक्यनिरासार्थम्, अत एव षडेवेत्यवधारणं कृतं, षट् च षडेवेति मिलित्वा द्वादश, अमुं च ग्रन्थं केचिदत्र संग्रहे न पठन्येव॥ पित्तेन दुष्टेन सदा तु दूष्टिः पीता भवेद्यस्य नरस्य किञ्चितु॥ ५५॥ पीतानि रूपाणि च तेन पश्येत् स वै नरः पित्तविदग्धदृष्टिः। प्राप्ते तृतीयं पटलं तु दोषे दिवा न पश्येन्निशि चेक्षते सः॥ ५६॥ रात्रौ च शीतानुगृहीतदृष्टिः पित्ताल्पभवादपि तानि पश्येत्। ( सु.उ. ७ )
answer_text: The previous aphorism, "The colour of the Vata predominent disease is aruna (red) etc, is being explained here. Anila means slightly bluish but yellow colour only, by which the bronze like colour is established in spite of the associa¬ tion of blood. Yellow only indicates the relationship of blood. Kāṃsyābha-like bronze means mild yellow some read, "The cornea constricts on exposure to sun¬ light while it dilates in shade" in kapha symptoms. Pravala is coral beed. Lotus petal, here, is red lotus petal. Citra raga means the typicality of the colours which can not be explained. Dosa linga means - apart from the said aruna (red) etc., of Vāta etc., doṣas. The enumeration of the diseases of drstimandala There are six types of linganāsa which are already explained - six more other diseases originate in the drstimanadala. (Su.u.7) The six vaieties of Linganasa " relates to the Linganasas which are already explained. “Şadime…..” means the six more diseases- pitta vidaghda dṛṣṭi etc., which are going to be explained. But why the enumeration of the diseases which are yet be explained? It is to rule out excession in number with day blindness and night blindness which fall with in pittavadagdba dṛṣṭi and kaphavidagdha dṛṣṭi. That is why “only six” is mentioned. The “Six and” “Sadeva” only six, together become twelve. Pittavidagdhadrsti (Refractive error) The drsti mandala become yellow by the aggravation of pitta and the indi¬ vidual perceives every thing to be in yellow colour - this condition is known as pittavidagdhadṛṣṭi. When the pitta dosa gets lodged in the third layer, the individual cannot have visual perception during day time and can see at night time. context: मधुकोशः रागोऽरुणो मारुतज इत्यादिसूत्र पूर्वोक्त विवृणोति-अरुणं मण्डलं वातादित्यादि। पित्तान्मण्डलमानीलमिति आनीलमीषन्नीलं पीतमेव, तेन रक्तसंबन्धे सति कांस्याभम्। पीतमेव चेति रससंबन्धे पीतमेव, कांस्याभमा- पाण्डुपीतमित्यर्थः। केचिदत्र कफर्जे पठन्ति, 'संकुचत्यातपेऽत्यर्थं छायायां विस्तृतो भवेत्' इति। शोणितजे प्रवालेत्यादौ प्रवाल स्वनामख्यातं तदाभं, पद्मपत्राभं च रक्तपद्मपुष्पदलाभम्। त्रिदोषजे चित्र इत्यत्र यथास्वं वातादिवर्णविभेदेन चित्रत्वं बोद्धव्यं, यथास्वमित्यस्य वक्ष्यमाणस्यात्रापि संबन्धात्; तेनायमर्थः-यथायथं वातादीनां वर्णभेदेन चित्रवर्णो भवति, उद्देशोक्तवर्णचित्रत्वे साक्षादेतादूशविवरणाभाव इति विशेषः। यथास्वं दोषलिङ्गानीत्यस्याभिधानं न्यायसिद्धस्यैवार्थस्य द्योतनार्थम्। दोषलिङ्गानि वातादीनां क्रमेणारुणादिलिङ्गान्युक्तेषु ज्ञातव्यानि ॥ ५१–५४ ॥ षड् लिङ्गनाशाः षडिमे च रोगा दृष्ट्याश्रयाः षट् च षडेव वाच्याः। ( सु.उ. ७) मधुकोशः अतः परमुक्तवश्यमामविकारयोः संख्याभिधानार्थमाह-षडित्यादि। षड्लिङ्गनाशा इत्युक्तानुवादोऽयम्। षडिमे च रोगा इति पित्तविदग्धदृष्ट्यादयो वक्ष्यमाणाः। ननु, उक्तानुवादो युक्तः, वक्ष्यमाणानां, पुनः किमथी संख्योक्तिः ? नैवं पित्तकफविदग्धदृष्ट्यवस्थान्तराभ्यां दिवान्धरात्र्यन्धाभ्यां संख्याधिक्यनिरासार्थम्, अत एव षडेवेत्यवधारणं कृतं, षट् च षडेवेति मिलित्वा द्वादश, अमुं च ग्रन्थं केचिदत्र संग्रहे न पठन्येव॥ पित्तेन दुष्टेन सदा तु दूष्टिः पीता भवेद्यस्य नरस्य किञ्चितु॥ ५५॥ पीतानि रूपाणि च तेन पश्येत् स वै नरः पित्तविदग्धदृष्टिः। प्राप्ते तृतीयं पटलं तु दोषे दिवा न पश्येन्निशि चेक्षते सः॥ ५६॥ रात्रौ च शीतानुगृहीतदृष्टिः पित्ताल्पभवादपि तानि पश्येत्। ( सु.उ. ७ )

answer_text: The above passage starting from the term ciram etc., describes features of the disease mūtrāfīla. The term mehamānasya refers to the urine of the person that is urinating (at the given time). The term has been replaced with the term mehanasya in some text. Meaning of the both is similar. Mūtrajaṭhara (Distended bladder) (SS. Ut. 58.13-14) The cause of udāvarta is the suppression of the urge of urination. The condition, in which the apāna vāta gets disturbed, begins to move upwards, accumulates in the stomach, and causes distension of the stomach below the umbilicus and produces severe pain and blockage in the urinary bladder, has been known as mutrajaṭhara. 8-9

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Vatadi Varga, Chapter 5, verse 551):

काकोदम्बरिका फल्गुर्मलयूजघनेफला । मलयुः स्तम्भकृत्तिका शीतला तुवस जयेत् । कफपित्तव्रणश्चित्रकुष्ठपाण्ड्वर्शकामलाः ।।१०।।
answer_text: Digestive disease: The twak, patra and apakwa phala is used externally and internally in Pravāhikā (Dysentery). Haemorrages: In Rakta pitta (Haemorrages), extracted juice of tender leaves along with Sugar candy taken regularly. Menstural disorders: In Pradara (Meno-Metroghia), juice of the fruits is taken along with Madhu and Sarkarā. External uses: A bath made of the Phalā and Twak is used to cure Kuṣṭa (Leprosy). A bark paste is apply externally in Vispoṭa (Blisters), Yavānpidika (Pimples) Vyanga (Freckles) and Dagdha (Burns) and Kīṭaviṣa (Posionious bites). Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrṇa: 3-6 g, Kaṣaya: 50-100 ml, Kṣīrā: 10-20 drops. KĀKODUMBARIKĀ Latin: Ficus hispida Linn Fam: Moraceae Hin: Gobla ng: Wild fig, Devil fig. Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Phalgu, Malayū and Jaghanephalā. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Malayū is Stambaka (Stops the flow of the fluid), Sītavīrya (Cold in potency) and Kaṣāya (Astringent) in taste. It cures diseases of Kapha, Pitta, Vṛṇa (Wounds), Switra (Vitiligo), Kuṣṭa (Leprosy), Pāṇḍu (Anemia), Arśas (Piles) and Kāmala (Jaundice). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is found in outer Himalayan ranges ascending to 3500ft. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is shrub or small tree. Leaves are ovateoblong, oppositely arranged, 10-25 cm long and 5-10 cm wide, thickly papery, covered with coarse hairs, accuminate apex, base round and entire margin. Fruits are figs, hairy, clustered directly on the main stem, become yellow when ripe. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Twak (Bark), Phala (Fruit), Kṣīrā (Latex). Chemical constituents: Bark contains tannin, wax, caoutchouc, glucoside principle. phenanthroindolizidine alkaloids and oleanolic acid
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Vatadi Varga, Chapter 5, verse 551
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Vatadi Varga, Chapter 5, verse 551.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 1):

उपशयमाह हेतुव्याधीत्यादि । हेतुर्वाह्य आभ्यन्तरश्च व्याधिर्ज्वरादिः एतयोहेतुव्या- ध्योर्व्यस्तसमस्तयोर्विपर्यस्ता विपरीताः एतयोरेव व्यस्तसमस्तयोर्विपर्यस्तार्थकारिणो निदान- समानधर्मिणोडपि प्रभावाद्रोगप्रशमकारिणः एवंविधा ये औषधात्रविहारा भेषजाहाराचारास्तेषा- मुपयोगमाचरणें सुखावहं सुखकरमुपशयं विद्यादुपशयाख्यं जानीयादव्याधेः । तस्य पयाय- माह सा हि सात्म्यमिति स्मृत इति । चरकेऽप्युक्तं सातम्यार्थो ह्यपशर्यार्थः इति च०वि० । हिशव्दः पादपूरणे । सुखावहमिति सुखं रोगनिवृत्तिलक्षण यथा व्यपदिशन्ति लोके भारापगमे सुखिनः संवृत्ताः स्म इति तत् सुखमावहति सम्यगा- यत्याडनुबन्धेन च करोतीति सुखावहम् । एतेन सदाहतृष्णानवज्वरिणः शीतलजलपान तदात्वसुखकरमपि नोपशय इति तात्पर्यार्थः । अग्र ऑपधात्रविहाराणामित्युपलक्षण तन देशकालावपि बोद्धव्यो । अत एव वृद्धवाग्भटेन व्याध्यादिविपरीतमभिधाय एतेन देश- कालावपि व्याख्याती अ०सं०नि० इत्याख्यातम् । सुदान्तसेनोंडप्याहसुखानु- बन्धो यो हेतुव्याध्यादिविपरीतकः । देशादिकश्चोपशयो जेयोऽनुपशयोऽन्यथा ॥ इति । सङ्क्षेपतस्तु लक्षणम् आपधादिजनितः सुखानुवन्ध उपशयः इति । स्रक्चन्दनवनितादि- जनितसुखनिवृत्त्यभ्रमोषधादिपदम् अनुवन्धशब्दश्चापथ्यजनिततदात्वसुखव्यवच्छेदाथः । एतदप्युदाहरणदर्शनपरं न तु लक्षणम औषधादीनां हेतुविपरीतादीनां च परस्परव्यभिचारण लक्षणत्वायोगात् । तस्मात् सम्यग्व्याधिजदुःखोपशमहेतुरुपशयः सात्म्यमुपशयः इति वा लक्षणम् ऑपधजनितः सुखानुवन्ध उपशयः इति वा लक्षण चरके आहाराचारदेशकाल- लङ्वनादीनां द्रव्याद्रव्यभूतानामीपधत्वेनाभिधानात् । अथैषामुदाहरणानि तत्र हेतुविपरीतानि । ओषधं यथाशीतज्वरे शुण्ठ्याद्वष्णं धेषजम् । यदुक्तं शीतेनोष्यकृतात्रोगान् शमयन्ति भिषग्वराः । ये तु शीतकृता रोगास्तेषामुष्णं भिष्मितम् ॥ इति च०वि० । अन्न यथाश्रमानिलजे ज्वरे रसौदनः । विहारो यथादिवास्वप्नोत्थे कफे रात्री जायरणमिति । अथ व्याधिविपरीतानि । औषधं यथा अतिसारे स्तम्भनं पाठादि तथा शिरीषो विष्ट हन्ति खदिरः कुष्ठं हरिद्रा प्रमेहमिति नैते दोषमपेक्षन्ते प्रभावाद्रोगप्रशमकारिण इति । वाप्यचन्द्रस्त्वाह ज्वरादिव्याधिहरं यदद्रव्यं तदपि दोषप्रत्यनीक किन्तु दोषप्रत्यनीकादस्थायं भेदः यद्दोषप्रत्यनीकं तन्नावश्यं व्याधिहरं यथावमनलङ्गने कफहरे न कफगुल्म हरतः उक्त हिकफे लङ्गनसाध्ये तु कर्तरि ज्वरगुल्मयोः । तुल्येऽपि देशकालादी लङ्कने न च सम्मतम् । इति तथान वामयेत्तैमिरिकं न गुल्मिन न चापि पाण्डूदररोगपीडितम् इति सु०वि० यत्त व्याधिहरं तदवश्यं दोषहरं तद्व्याधिं शमयेत्तदारम्भकदोषमपि शमयतीति अन्यथा स रोगो जित एव न स्यात् कारणस्य तादवस्थ्यात् इति । तव्रातिसङ्कतमित्यन्ये यतो दोषस्तत्र समवायी निमित्तं वा न च समवायिनिमित्ताभावप्रयुक्तो नियमेन कार्यभावः किन्त्वसमवायिकारणभावप्रयुक्तोऽपि यथाकपालमालसंयोगस्यासमवायिकारणस्य विनाशादपि घटाभावः तथारोगेऽपि सम्प्रप्तिलक्षणस्य संयोगस्य विनाशाद्रोपस्यापि विनाशः दोषस्तु स्वतः क्रियान्तरेण वा निवर्तत यदि व्याधिप्रत्यनीकमवृश्यं दोष निक्तर्येदित स्वीक्रियते तदोभयप्रत्यनीकाद्वेदो दुरुपपादः स्यादिति । ननु यदि निमितकारणं दोषस्तत्कथं तदाख्यविकारे वमनादिना दोषहरणं विधीयते नहि दण्डकुलालाद्युच्छेदे घटोच्छेद इति । उच्यते यत्र यावत्रिमित्तकारणस्थायि कार्य तत्र निमित्तकारणोच्छेदादपि कार्यनाशः यथा वर्तितैलनाशादपि प्रदीपनाशः तथाभूताश्च दोषाः प्रायश इति । अन्नं यथा अतिसरे स्तम्भन मसूसदि विहारो यथा उदावतें प्रवाहरणं मन्त्रीषधिधारणबल्युपहारनियम-प्रायश्चितहोमगुरुदेवशुध्रूषादयोऽपि याधिविपरीता विहारा इति वाप्यचन्द्रः । अथ हेतुव्याधिविपरीतानि । ओषधं यथावातशोथे दशमूलं वातहरं शोथहरं च । युदक्त चरके पड्विरेचनशताश्रितीयेंडध्यायेपाटला इत्यादि यावत्दशेमानि शोथ- हराणि इति च०सू० अन्नं यथावातकफग्रहण्यां तक्रं शीतवातोत्थे ज्वरे पेया सा ह्रुष्णवीर्यत्वाद्रातं हन्ति प्रभावाज्जरं च । युद्कं चरके ज्वरघ्नो ज्वरसाम्यत्वात् इति चचि । सुश्रुतेऽपिज्वरे चैवातिसारे चैवागूः सर्वदा हिता । इति सु०्ड० । विहारो यथा स्निम्धदिवास्वप्नप्रजातायां तन्द्रायां रूक्ष तन्द्राविपरीतं रात्रिजागरणमिति । अथ हेतुविपरीतार्थकारीणि । ओषधं यथापितप्रधाने व्रणशोथे पित्तकर उष्ण उपनाहः । अन्ने यथा पव्यमाने व्रणसोथेडन्ने विदाहि । विहारो यथा वातोन्मादे त्रासनमिति । अथ व्याधिविपरीतार्थकारीणि । ओषधं यथाछद्यां वमनकारके मदनफलादि । अन्ने यथाअतिसारे विरेचने क्षीरम् । विहारो यथाछर्चां वमनाथं प्रवाहणमिति । अथ हेतुव्याधिविपरीतार्थकारीणि । औषधं यथाअग्निप्लुष्टे उष्णोऽगुर्वादिलेपः विषे वा विषम् । अन्न यथा मद्यपानोत्थे मदात्यये मदकारकं मद्यम् । विहारो यथा व्यायामजनितसम्मूढवाते जलप्रतरणरूपो व्यायाम इति । ननु छर्द्यां बहुश्लेष्मजायां वमनयोग्यायां यदि वमनं न क्रियते तदा चिरानुवर्ती रोगोऽनुच्छेद्यो वा स्यात् ततश्च वमनं प्रयुक्त दोषप्रत्यनीकमेव भवति यदुक्तं सुश्रुते छर्दिषु बहुदोषासु वमनं हितमुच्यते । सु०उ० इति यथा आमातिसारे क्षीरस्य विरेकित्वेनामनिःसरणाद्धेतुप्रत्यनीकमेव भवति एवमग्निप्लुष्टेडप्युष्णक्रियया रक्तस्य विलयनेन स्थानान्तरगमनाद्वेतुप्रत्यनीकतैव अन्यथा दाहप्रकुपितं रक्त तत्रस्थं पाकमारभेतु यदुर्क्त सुश्रुतेअग्निना कोपितं रक्तं भृशं जन्तोः प्रकुप्यति । ततस्तेनैव वेगेन पित्त मस्याप्युदीयते ॥ इति सु०सू० शीतक्रिया च तत्र निषिद्धा रक्तस्य स्त्या- नत्वहेतुत्वात् यदाह सुश्रुतःप्रकृत्या ह्युदकं शीतं स्कन्दयत्यति शोणितम् । तस्मात् सुखयति ह्युष्णं न तु शीतं कथञ्चन ।। इति सु०सू० । स्कन्दयति स्त्यानीकरोति तथा जङ्गमविषे ऊर्ध्वगस्वरूपे मोलविषमधोगस्वरूपं हेतुविपरीतमेव यदुर्क्त चरके विष विषघ्नमुर्क्त यत् प्रभावस्तत्र कारणम् । ऊर्ध्वानुलोमिकं यच्च तत् प्रभावप्रभावितम् ।। इति च०सू० अस्यायमर्थः विषत्वाविशेषेऽपि कृतो गतिभेद इत्यत उक्तं तत् प्रभावप्रभावितमिति तथा मद्यकृते मदात्यये यन्मद्यं तदपि मातुलुङ्गचुक्रादियुतं सुश्रुता- दिभिविहितं केवलाच्च द्रव्यान्तरसंयुक्तमन्यदेव अथवा वातमदात्यये रूक्षमाध्वीकादिना जनिते स्निग्धपैष्टिकादिमद्यं प्रयुज्यमानं हेतुविपरीतमेव यच्चोक्तं सुश्रुतेयथा नरेन्द्रोपहतस्य कस्यचिद्दवेत् प्रसादस्तत एवं नान्यतः । ध्रुवं तथा मद्यहतस्य देहिनो भवेत् प्रसादस्तत एव नान्यतः ।। इति सु०उ० तन्मद्यजातीयाभिप्रायेणैव यच्चोरुस्तम्भे जलप्रतरणं तत्रापि जलस्य शैत्येन बहिरगच्छन् देहोष्मा कुम्भकारपवनन्यायेनान्तःपिण्डितौ मेदःश्लेष्माणौ विलाययति व्यायामश्च तौ शोषयति ततस्तु निरावरणो वायुः स्वमार्गप्रतिपत्रो भवतीति हेतुप्रत्यनीकतैव अनेन न्यायेन सर्वमेव तदर्थकारि यथासम्भवं हेतुप्रत्यनीकादवेवान्त- र्भवतीति । उच्यते यद्यप्येवं तथाऽप्यवान्तरवैधर्म्यप्रतिपादनार्थमाचायेंः पृथम्दशितम् । तथा चरकेऽप्युक्तम् उपशयः पुनर्हेतुव्याधिविपरीतानां विपरीतार्थकारिणां चीषधाहारविहाराणा- मुपयोगः सुखानुवन्धः । इति च०नि० । वेधर्म्यं च हेतुसमानधर्मकत्वेऽपि रोग- प्रशमकत्वमिति मा ० नि० - विपरीतोऽनुपशयोयाध्यसात्म्याभिसंज्ञितः विपरीतोऽनुपशय इति औषधादीनां दुःखकर उपयोगोऽनुपशय इत्यर्थः । तत्पर्याय- माहव्याध्यसात्म्यमिति स्मृत इति । व्याधिग्रहणेन दोषोऽपि बोध्यः । ननु अनुपशयः किं व्याधिविशेषं बोधयति नो वा नेति चेत् निदाने तदुपन्यासो व्यर्थः प्रतिपादयतीति चेत् विज्ञानं रोगाणां पञ्चधा स्मृतम् इति व्याहन्यते तस्य षष्ठत्वापत्तेः । नैवं प्रतिपादयत्येव यदाह चरकः गूढलिङ्गं व्याधिमुपशयानुपशयाभ्यां परीक्षेत । इति च०वि० । किन्तु निदाने तस्यान्तर्भावः दोषस्य रोगस्य वा वर्धकत्वात् इत्यनुपशयस्य निदानेऽन्तर्भावान्न षष्ठत्वापत्तिः वक्ष्यति चनिदानोक्तानुपशयः इति । इत्युपशयलक्षणम् ।।।। दुष्टेन के दोषेण के यथा के चानुविसर्पता । यथा निर्वृत्तिरामयस्यासौं का प्राप्तिर्जातिरामतिः ॥१ ॥ - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
