answer_text: Pañca Nidana Lakṣaṇam Discussion The Madhukośa has discussed about the description of upaśaya with the present passage starting from the terms Hetuvyādhī etc. The causative factor or hetu of a disease includes two different types of factors i.e. the external ( bāhya) and internal ( ābhyantara ). The term vyādhi refers to the diseases like jvara. Vyādhi, individually and collectively, is also known as Viparita (opposite or antagonistic). Though the Auşadha (medicine), Anna (food) and Vihara (behaviour) are similar to the etiological factors of the disease, they nullify the disease by way of their Prabhāva (special effect). Such usages, which mitigate diseases, are considered to be bringing about sukha (happiness). As implied in the term Vikāroduhkhameva ca, the duhkha or sorrow is a disease and elimination of the same. It would thus, naturally imply the curc from disease. It is also called Updsaya Pañca Nidāna Lakṣanam positive trial). Upasaya is also known as Satmya (compatibility). Caraka opines that something that gives happiness or positive result is homologous or capable to check the situation (CS. Vi. 1.17: sātmyārtho hyupaśayārtha iti). The term hi in the given passage has been used to complete the meter in question ( pāda-pūraṇa ). (Nonetheless, scholars argue that the system of pāda-pūraṇa is used in cases of poetry and not in case of prose.) As in the popular usage, it is stated that removal of a head-load is the factor of happiness, the removal of a disease is also tantamount to happiness. Happiness is the criterion of mitigation of the disease. Nevertheless, temporary happiness attained by taking cold water in a just erupted fever, in which burning sensation and thirst are salient features, should not be considered as upasaya as the problem is aggravated latter by taking such measures. Vrddha Vāgbhaṭa advises to add desa (place) and kāla (time) as additional factor to the three other factors i. e. medicine, food and behavioural regimen (AS. Ni.1.12). The commentator Sudānta Sen has stressed the term Sukhānubandha (continuous happiness) (that is actualized by auṣadha or medicine etc.) as identical to upaśaya. He has suggested that a major characteristic of upaśaya is that it should be based on the ingredients or measures that are opposite to the factors that produce diseases. In addition, the paraphernalia of upaśaya should also include positive correspondence of the factors like locality, season, etc. In other words, the medicines and the regimen of the concerned patient should be compatible to the treatment of the disease. Rest of the factors that do not contribute to the healing of disease should be known as anupasaya that is non-upasaya. The gamut of upasaya excludes such items as happiness caused by application of fragrant unguent like paste of candana and by having the company of women. The word anubandha (continuous) has been used to exclude the temporary happiness caused by apathya (harmful foods etc.). This explanation serves as an example but it does not outline the definitions or quality of upaśaya, as auṣadha and hetu etc. will not be able to produce any symptom in the absence of the other. Caraka considered material and non-material things like acara (behaviour), desa (place), kāla (time) etc. as part of the medicine itself. The example for Upasaya through Ausadha (positive trial with medicine) which is opposite to hetu (the causative factor) could be referred to in terms of using the drug of hot potency like the Sunthī (dry ginger) in the cases of śīta jvara (cold fever). This is based on the Caraka’s statement to the effect that the disease caused by uşna (hot) are treated with śīta (cold) drugs and vice versa. (CS. Vi. 3.41) It may be noted that certain practices act as upasaya while in other cases the same practices produce counter effects. For example, the use of cold water being the one capable to aggravate vala is generally harmful in vāta related ailments but in the cases of urustambha or paralysis, it is beneficial to swim in the cold water (CS. Vi. 3.41). Thus, to qualify a particular measure as upasaya might not make sense all the time. Therefore, the measure that indeed eliminates ailments as such is only fit to be termed as upaśaya. The same factor is also true regarding the term sātmya (compatible). The term auṣadhādi janita sukhānubandha upaśaya has stressed the medicine, etc. The definition of upasaya could be made plain by stating that the factor that nullifies the unhappiness caused by a disease is to be known as upaśaya or the factor that causes sātmya (compatibility) is upaśaya. The sustained happiness caused by auṣadha is also known as upaśaya. Here, auṣadha (medicine) should be taken as to include food and behavioural aspect too as suggested by Caraka above. A hetuviparīta food (anna) is one that is opposite to the causative factor of the disease. For example, in fever caused by exertion and vāta aggravation, the meat soup and cooked rice are to be served as a hetuviparīta item. (See CS. Ci. 3.191) One of the examples of hetuviparīta in terms of vihāra or the behavioural regimen (as part of the daily routine) is the waking during the nights while suffering through kapha-accumulation caused by daysleep. (See CS. Su. 21.49) As regards the hetuviparita in terms of auşadha or medicine, it may include administration of the astringent drugs like patha in atisara (diarrhoea), śirıṣa in poisoning, khadira in skin disorders and haridra (turmeric) in prameha (urinary anomalies). These drugs need not be considered for their anti-dosa action but because of their Pañca Nidāna Lakṣanam special effect (prabhāva) they are capable to alleviate the paticular diseases. The commentator Vāpyacandra argues that the drug that is antagonistic to a particular dosa and that cures the jvara need not necessarily be antagonistic to all the diseases caused by that dosa. The kapha gulma (vāta oppression caused by kapha) would not be cured by vamana (emesis) and langhana which by nature serve as anti-kapha. It is also said that even though desa (place), kāla (time), etc. permit the practice of langhana (fasting), it should not be opted in jvara (fever) and gulma (vāta oppression) even when the both are produced by kapha. Moreover, the individuals suffering from timira, gulma, pāṇḍu (anemia) and udara (abdominal disorder) should not be subjected to vamana (emesis) (Su. Ci. 33.14). Whichever factor is instrumental in curing disease is also capable to alleviate the dosa concerned. When the disease is pacified, the causative dosa is also actuated. Otherwise, the disease would not have been cured as the causes naturally cease to exist when the effect is eliminated. The above theory does not appeal to some authorities. They would argue that since the dosa is either inherent or incidental cause of the disease, therefore, elimination of these causes is essential for elimi¬ nation of the disease. Nonetheless, as per the author of Madhukosa, this objection is overruled. In his opinion, the above condition should be qualified with addition to the reality that it is only the elimination of inherent causes that eliminates the disease. When the inherent and incidental causes cease to exist, the effect also ceases but it also ceases when the non-inherent cause is destroyed. As an earthenware (ghaṭa) is automatically destroyed when both of its sections (the one called kapāla and the base) are destroyed. It may be recalled that an earthen pot consists of an upper portion and a base. Separately they are like large bowls and when united they form shape of an earthen pot. Similarly, the existence of a disease could be compared with the unity of the non-inherent causes like prākṛta-vaikṛta generated vitia- tion (ghata) and the vitiated dhātu, etc. (e.g. paṭa). Thus, treatment of any one of them could mean elimination of the disease. Thus, the conditionality of treating both of them does not make a sense. This assumption is also supported by Caraka (Su. 16.28). As per the Nyāya system of thought, the causes of disease are three: l. Samavāyī factors like the vāta and doṣas, etc. 2. Asamavāyī factors, that is combination of the doṣas and the dūsyas or the vitators and the vitiated, and 3. Mithyā (also called Nimitta), it includes use of food and regimen that are opposite to the nature of the individual, locality and the season in context. (In modern medicine, too, there is emphasis on the Agent, Host, and Environment factors.) Thus, the measures of treatments to be followed are also three: l. Administration of Hetu-viparīta factors, also called Hetu- pratyanīka factors. These measures are to be opted when the samavāyī factors are dominant in the given case. 2. Administration of Kyādhi- viparīta factors. These measures are to be opted when the asamavāyī factors are dominant in the given ase. 3. Administration of Hetuyyadhi-viparita factors, also called Ubhaya-pratyamka factors. These measures are to be opted when the mithyā or nimitta factors are dominant in the given case. Now the nature of dosa is debated. Some authorities consider the doşa as relating to the nimitta factor. Then the issue surfaces that if it is so then why could the removal of dosa through emesis and purgation actualize the treatment of a disease! It has been observed that destruction of the baton, wheel and potter and the like does not mean the destruction of the pot. This issue is addressed with the theory that the dosa when it becomes instrumental in causing disease in a fashion of the nimilla factor then its elimination would be tantamount to the cure of disease. As the destruction of wick, oil etc. means destruction of the lamp the climination of dosa would mean elimination of the disease. The above assimilation of doya with the nimilia factors in accordance with the Nyaya system of thought, however, is not compatible with the principles of Ayurveda. Both Caraka and Suśruta have instructed that dosas relate only to the samavayī factors and in no case, they could be considered as the nimitta factor. (Susruta: Su. 25.8) Pañca Nidāna Lakṣanam The commentator further discusses the Vyadhi-Viparita factors. Vyādhi-Viparīta cereals: A major example of Vyādhi-Viparīta cereal is lentil that is profitably used to control the cases of diarrhoea. Vyādhi-Viparīta regimen: An example of Vyādhi-Viparīta Vihāra (or behavioural regimen that is antagonistic to the disease) is Prava¬ hanam (applying internal pressure) in udāvarta (flatulence) (SS. Ut. 55.19). The commentator Vāpyacandra has included among Vyādhi- Viparīta Vihāra measures like chanting of mantra (the sacred terms), Ausadhi-dharana (holding the medicinal herbs at the wrist, neck, loin etc.), Bali (sacrificing animals), Niyama (adhering to traditional norms and regulations), Prāyaścita (repentance) Homa (performing the rituals of sacred pyres) and Gurudevasuśrusā (serving the teachers and Gods and the like) etc. as well. This discussion is followed by the description of the Hetuvyadhi- viparītakārī factors (that are antagonistic to both the cause and the disease): Auṣadha (medicine) – A brilliant example of Hetuvyādhiviparītakārī medicine is administration of the plant dasamula (the ten roots involving plants such as Bilva etc.) in the cases of vāta related śotha. Decoction of the dasamula herbs checks the vata dosa that is one of the causes of the ailment. It also controls the disease śotha (CS. Sī. 4.16). Thus, being opposite to both the disease and the cause of disease the daśamūla herbs are known as Hetuvyādhiviparītakārī Upasaya. As regards the example of Hetuvyādhiviparītakārī Anna or food one could note the consumption of takra (butter-milk) in the cases of grahaṇī (sprue) caused by vāta or kapha. Use of Peyā (gruel) in the cases of fever caused by śīta-vāta is another example. Peyā is hot by nature usnavīrya and as such, it nullifies vāta while its prabhāva (special effect) cures the fever. Caraka has also suggested that peya (gruel) etc., are antagonistic to fever because they remain homologous in fever (CS. Ci. 3.153). Susruta has opined that in the cases of fever and diarrhoea, intake of yavāgīī (porridge) is always helpful (SS. Ut. 40.158). As regards the example of Hetuvyādhiviparītakārī Vihāra (behavioural aspects and the like), it may be noted that the disease tandrā that is drowsiness could be checked by use of the snigdha or oily items as well as through measures such as waking during the night. As far as the Hetuvyādhiviparītakārī factors are concerned, the following points could be considered: In terms of Hetuvyādhiviparītakārī medicine, applying hot poultice in the case of pitta-induced inflammatory wound is helpful. The poultice in fact ripens the wound and thus, climinates the same. In fact, pitta is one of the causes of the ailment and the application of hot poultice is also pro-pitta in effect. (SS. Su. 17.7) Yet it acts as treatment of the disease as pitta is suppurated by its use (and there is a sort of supernova effect). In terms of food items, it may be noted that serving the foods that cause burning sensation in an inflammatory wound when it is in the ripening stage, is an example of Hetuvyādhiviparītakārī food. As regards Hetuvyādhiviparītakārī Vihāra or behavioural regimen, etc., threatening the patient in insanity caused by vala is an example (CS. Ci. 3.115). Now the examples for Wyādhi Viparīfārīhākārī (factors that are antagonistic to the disease). In terms of medicine, administering madana-phala (Randia dumatorum, the emetic nut) in the cases of chardi (nausea and vomiting) serves as the vyādhi viparīlārīhakārī factors. In terms of food, serving laxatives like milk in the cases of diarrhoea is an example of vyādhi viparīlārīhakārī factor. In terms of behavioural activities, attempting to vomit by intake of internal pressure in the cases of nausea and vomiting is an example of Vyādhi Viparītārthakārī factor. Now, the examples for Heluvyādhiviparīlakārī (factors that are opposite to both the cause and disease). In terms of medicine, applying hot-natured aguru (the plant Aquillaria agallocha) etc., lepa (external application) in the cases of burn wounds is an example of Hetryyūdhiviparītārīhakārī factor. In addition, application of poison in the cases of poisoning is another example of Hetuvyadhiviparttarthakari factor. Pañca Nidāna Laksanam In terms of food, serving alcohol in intoxication caused by consumption of alcohol is an example of Hetuvyadhiviparitarthakari factor. In terms of behaviour etc., doing regular exercise in the form of swimming in the ailment of the sammidhavala (immobility of the limbs) caused by excessive bodily exercise is an example of Hetuvyādhiviparītārthakārī factor. Now the issue arises as to what would be the result if a patient is eligible for emesis and if he is suffering from nausea and vomiting due to over accumulation of kapha. If he is not given emetic, will the discase continue for a long time and will not be alleviated? Then, at this juncture, emesis to be considered only as dosapratyanika (antagonistic to dosa). Sustuta also supports this – In vomiting caused by multiple dosas (impurities), vamana (emisis) is advisable.’ (Su.ut. 49.16). Likewise, expelling ama (undigested foodstuffs) with help of laxative caused by serving milk in the cases of amalisara (Diarrhoea due to undigested foods) could mean that the cause of the disease has been mitigated. This measure serves as an example of the hetupratyamka upaśaya. In the same way, it is also considered as hetupratyanika when cauterization is done in the case of burn wound where the blood either rushes to the other place or dissolves without getting accumulated at the site of the burn. Susruta states – ‘The blood, when afflicted by heat (burning), gets aggravated fast and with the same pace, it vitiates pitta' (Su. Su. 12.17). Cold therapy is also to be avoided as it facilitates coagulation of blood. In support of this view Suśruta says, ‘By nature, the cold water application coagulates the blood while hot application is comforting at this stage. The cold applications are not advisable’ (Su. Sii. 12.21). Likewise, in the cases of poisoning caused by the poisonous material of living sources (snakes etc.), doses of the poison of herbal roots make a sense. The poison of the living being like snake, etc. moves upward in the body while the poisons obtained from the herbal roots move downward. Thus, in terms of their respective especial effects prabhava), both these poisons control each other. Caraka while accepting that not all the poisons check poisons has admitted that the poisons check each other if their effects are dissimilar or in other words they move inside the body in directions opposite to each other (CS. Sī. 26.69). Thus, application of static poison obtained from roots etc. is to be considered antagonistic to the cause of the disease. This is an example of the application of measures and material that e. g. poison, here) are category-wise identical in terms of cause (hetu) of the disease and its treatment (ausadha), yet they are opposite to each other. Another example relates to the excessive alcoholic intoxication. It is well known fact that the disease madūtyaya is caused by intake of madya (alcohol) only. Yet alcohoi itself is given as its antidote. Nonetheless, the type of alcohol used as antidote is different from the alcohol that produces the disease. The antidote variety is not the same alcohol but the one prepared with mātulunga (the plant Citrus medica) etc. as explained in Suśruta. In the intoxication caused by vāta the dry type of alcohol or the drink called mādhvīka (prepared with plant Madhuca indica) could be served. Application of oily pista (flour) etc. could also be included in this category of treatments. These are the examples of Hetuviparīta Upaśaya. In support of this theory, Suśruta has cited the example of the punishment and reward by a similar agency that is the royalty. As the individual punished by the king has to be consoled by none other than the king himself, in the same way one who is diseased by alcoholic intoxication has to be rescued through use of alcohol and nothing else.” (Su.Ut. 47.48). Caraka is of the same view (CS.Ci. 24. 209). However, it must be noted that the alcohol that is served as antidote to the disease madātyaya is different from the alcohol that produces the disease. In addition, the support of Caraka and Susruta in this connection should be viewed in the light of the application of a different sort of liquor. Swimming exercise in urustambha (gripping in the things) is another example of Hetuviparīta Upaśaya. It so happens that the coldness of water does not allow the heat of the body to be released from the body. Thus, the heat of the body does not spread outside the body and it spreads only within the body. As such, there is melting of the kapha and medas (fat) inside the body. It may be noted that accumulation of these two matters is instrumental in generating the urustambha. On the other hand, the bodily exertion caused by swimming dries the kapha and medas up and consequently relieving the vāta accumula- tion actuates it, thereby providing relief in the disease. This process also comes under hetupratyanīka upaśaya. To make the issue plain, the logical similarity contained in the term Kumbhakāra-pavana Nyaya has been quoted here. It may be noted that the potter (Kum- bhakāra) seals with coat of soil the kiln of the unbaked or raw pots so that the heat of kiln does not spread out. It dries up the water contents in the pot and thoroughly bakes the pots in making. The above passage suggests that the basic purpose of the suggested measure is to turn the vitiated vata into normalcy. Thus, it appears to be an example of the hetuviparita upaśaya only. Likewise, all the tadarthakārī illustrations come under hetuviparīta category only. Then, what is the justification of accepting a separate tadarthakārī hetuviparīta category. It is told that this is to propose the subtle difference between the effects of hew and auṣadha or the material used. Though in nature and category, the hetu and ausadha some¬ times appear identical yet by incident ( tadartha ) they serve different purposes. Probably that is why the authorities of Ayurveda has indicated a separate group of tadarthakarī medicines, foods and behavioural regimen. This separation has been supported by (Nidāna, 1.8). 119 II (AH. Ni. 1. 7) The opposite of upasaya is anupasaya (that increasing the discom- fort) or asatmya (incompatible) to the disease. 9 The above description suggests that what is opposite to upasaya in terms of medicine, food and measures and the like is named Amupasaya. It is the negative trial where the experimentations fail and consequently the disease remains uncured. It is also known as Asatmya (non-homologous state) to the disease (diseased person). The term Vyadhi (disease) also implies the dosa involved. Appli- cation of the Anupasaya factors adds to the aggravation of diseases as they fail to check even the initial features of disease. It is argued that the Anupasaya factors are also useful in locating the disease. Otherwise, it was not necessary to mention this factor separately. However, if it is to be included the number of diagnostic factors mentioned by Mādhavakāra the same should be raised from five to six. It may be noted that Mādhavakara has used the term pañca or five to indicate the factors that are useful in exploring the diseases. However, Anupasaya has been taken note of by Caraka who opines that the inexplicit picture of the disease is to be examined with the help of upaśaya (positive trial) and anupaśaya (negative trial) (CS.Vi. 4.15). Thus, it is plain that Anupaśaya is one of the means to know the disease. The exclusion of Anupasaya from the group of five etiological factors of Mādhavakara has been justified from two points of view: l. The factors naturally form part of the Nidāna. The 58th passage of the chapter on Jvara in the present book has categorically suggested that Nidānaoktānūpaśaya, that is, the behaviour and regimens that are instrumental in producing the diseases are called anupasaya of the same disease. And those factors that act as opposite to them are termed as upasaya. Secondly, in accordance with the commentator Vijayaraksita, it may be argued that since anupasaya is opposite to the upaśaya, it naturally forms the part of upaśaya, hence, its saperate counting is not required like that. Samprāpti (The pathogenesis) The samprapti, jati or agati are the terms that denote the process of appearance of the disease by the provoked dosas which are circulating all over the body. 10
chapter_title: Pañca Nidāna Lakṣaṇam – Five Means of Diagnosis
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 1.
context: उपशयमाह हेतुव्याधीत्यादि । हेतुर्वाह्य आभ्यन्तरश्च व्याधिर्ज्वरादिः एतयोहेतुव्या- ध्योर्व्यस्तसमस्तयोर्विपर्यस्ता विपरीताः एतयोरेव व्यस्तसमस्तयोर्विपर्यस्तार्थकारिणो निदान- समानधर्मिणोडपि प्रभावाद्रोगप्रशमकारिणः एवंविधा ये औषधात्रविहारा भेषजाहाराचारास्तेषा- मुपयोगमाचरणें सुखावहं सुखकरमुपशयं विद्यादुपशयाख्यं जानीयादव्याधेः । तस्य पयाय- माह सा हि सात्म्यमिति स्मृत इति । चरकेऽप्युक्तं सातम्यार्थो ह्यपशर्यार्थः इति च०वि० । हिशव्दः पादपूरणे । सुखावहमिति सुखं रोगनिवृत्तिलक्षण यथा व्यपदिशन्ति लोके भारापगमे सुखिनः संवृत्ताः स्म इति तत् सुखमावहति सम्यगा- यत्याडनुबन्धेन च करोतीति सुखावहम् । एतेन सदाहतृष्णानवज्वरिणः शीतलजलपान तदात्वसुखकरमपि नोपशय इति तात्पर्यार्थः । अग्र ऑपधात्रविहाराणामित्युपलक्षण तन देशकालावपि बोद्धव्यो । अत एव वृद्धवाग्भटेन व्याध्यादिविपरीतमभिधाय एतेन देश- कालावपि व्याख्याती अ०सं०नि० इत्याख्यातम् । सुदान्तसेनोंडप्याहसुखानु- बन्धो यो हेतुव्याध्यादिविपरीतकः । देशादिकश्चोपशयो जेयोऽनुपशयोऽन्यथा ॥ इति । सङ्क्षेपतस्तु लक्षणम् आपधादिजनितः सुखानुवन्ध उपशयः इति । स्रक्चन्दनवनितादि- जनितसुखनिवृत्त्यभ्रमोषधादिपदम् अनुवन्धशब्दश्चापथ्यजनिततदात्वसुखव्यवच्छेदाथः । एतदप्युदाहरणदर्शनपरं न तु लक्षणम औषधादीनां हेतुविपरीतादीनां च परस्परव्यभिचारण लक्षणत्वायोगात् । तस्मात् सम्यग्व्याधिजदुःखोपशमहेतुरुपशयः सात्म्यमुपशयः इति वा लक्षणम् ऑपधजनितः सुखानुवन्ध उपशयः इति वा लक्षण चरके आहाराचारदेशकाल- लङ्वनादीनां द्रव्याद्रव्यभूतानामीपधत्वेनाभिधानात् । अथैषामुदाहरणानि तत्र हेतुविपरीतानि । ओषधं यथाशीतज्वरे शुण्ठ्याद्वष्णं धेषजम् । यदुक्तं शीतेनोष्यकृतात्रोगान् शमयन्ति भिषग्वराः । ये तु शीतकृता रोगास्तेषामुष्णं भिष्मितम् ॥ इति च०वि० । अन्न यथाश्रमानिलजे ज्वरे रसौदनः । विहारो यथादिवास्वप्नोत्थे कफे रात्री जायरणमिति । अथ व्याधिविपरीतानि । औषधं यथा अतिसारे स्तम्भनं पाठादि तथा शिरीषो विष्ट हन्ति खदिरः कुष्ठं हरिद्रा प्रमेहमिति नैते दोषमपेक्षन्ते प्रभावाद्रोगप्रशमकारिण इति । वाप्यचन्द्रस्त्वाह ज्वरादिव्याधिहरं यदद्रव्यं तदपि दोषप्रत्यनीक किन्तु दोषप्रत्यनीकादस्थायं भेदः यद्दोषप्रत्यनीकं तन्नावश्यं व्याधिहरं यथावमनलङ्गने कफहरे न कफगुल्म हरतः उक्त हिकफे लङ्गनसाध्ये तु कर्तरि ज्वरगुल्मयोः । तुल्येऽपि देशकालादी लङ्कने न च सम्मतम् । इति तथान वामयेत्तैमिरिकं न गुल्मिन न चापि पाण्डूदररोगपीडितम् इति सु०वि० यत्त व्याधिहरं तदवश्यं दोषहरं तद्व्याधिं शमयेत्तदारम्भकदोषमपि शमयतीति अन्यथा स रोगो जित एव न स्यात् कारणस्य तादवस्थ्यात् इति । तव्रातिसङ्कतमित्यन्ये यतो दोषस्तत्र समवायी निमित्तं वा न च समवायिनिमित्ताभावप्रयुक्तो नियमेन कार्यभावः किन्त्वसमवायिकारणभावप्रयुक्तोऽपि स्वीक्रियते तदोभयप्रत्यनीकाद्वेदो दुरुपपादः स्यादिति । ननु यदि निमितकारणं दोषस्तत्कथं तदाख्यविकारे वमनादिना दोषहरणं विधीयते नहि दण्डकुलालाद्युच्छेदे घटोच्छेद इति । उच्यते यत्र यावत्रिमित्तकारणस्थायि कार्य तत्र निमित्तकारणोच्छेदादपि कार्यनाशः यथा वर्तितैलनाशादपि प्रदीपनाशः तथाभूताश्च दोषाः प्रायश इति । अन्नं यथा अतिसरे स्तम्भन मसूसदि विहारो यथा उदावतें प्रवाहरणं मन्त्रीषधिधारणबल्युपहारनियम-प्रायश्चितहोमगुरुदेवशुध्रूषादयोऽपि याधिविपरीता विहारा इति वाप्यचन्द्रः । अथ हेतुव्याधिविपरीतानि । ओषधं यथावातशोथे दशमूलं वातहरं शोथहरं च । युदक्त चरके पड्विरेचनशताश्रितीयेंडध्यायेपाटला इत्यादि यावत्दशेमानि शोथ- हराणि इति च०सू० अन्नं यथावातकफग्रहण्यां तक्रं शीतवातोत्थे ज्वरे पेया सा ह्रुष्णवीर्यत्वाद्रातं हन्ति प्रभावाज्जरं च । युद्कं चरके ज्वरघ्नो ज्वरसाम्यत्वात् इति चचि । सुश्रुतेऽपिज्वरे चैवातिसारे चैवागूः सर्वदा हिता । इति सु०्ड० । विहारो यथा स्निम्धदिवास्वप्नप्रजातायां तन्द्रायां रूक्ष तन्द्राविपरीतं रात्रिजागरणमिति । अथ हेतुविपरीतार्थकारीणि । ओषधं यथापितप्रधाने व्रणशोथे पित्तकर उष्ण उपनाहः । अन्ने यथा पव्यमाने व्रणसोथेडन्ने विदाहि । विहारो यथा वातोन्मादे त्रासनमिति । अथ व्याधिविपरीतार्थकारीणि । ओषधं यथाछद्यां वमनकारके मदनफलादि । अन्ने यथाअतिसारे विरेचने क्षीरम् । विहारो यथाछर्चां वमनाथं प्रवाहणमिति । अथ हेतुव्याधिविपरीतार्थकारीणि । औषधं यथाअग्निप्लुष्टे उष्णोऽगुर्वादिलेपः विषे वा विषम् । अन्न यथा मद्यपानोत्थे मदात्यये मदकारकं मद्यम् । विहारो यथा व्यायामजनितसम्मूढवाते जलप्रतरणरूपो व्यायाम इति । ननु छर्द्यां बहुश्लेष्मजायां वमनयोग्यायां यदि वमनं न क्रियते तदा चिरानुवर्ती रोगोऽनुच्छेद्यो वा स्यात् ततश्च वमनं प्रयुक्त दोषप्रत्यनीकमेव भवति यदुक्तं सुश्रुते छर्दिषु बहुदोषासु वमनं हितमुच्यते । सु०उ० इति यथा आमातिसारे क्षीरस्य विरेकित्वेनामनिःसरणाद्धेतुप्रत्यनीकमेव भवति एवमग्निप्लुष्टेडप्युष्णक्रियया रक्तस्य विलयनेन स्थानान्तरगमनाद्वेतुप्रत्यनीकतैव अन्यथा दाहप्रकुपितं रक्त तत्रस्थं पाकमारभेतु यदुर्क्त सुश्रुतेअग्निना कोपितं रक्तं भृशं जन्तोः प्रकुप्यति । ततस्तेनैव वेगेन पित्त मस्याप्युदीयते ॥ इति सु०सू० शीतक्रिया च तत्र निषिद्धा रक्तस्य स्त्या- नत्वहेतुत्वात् यदाह सुश्रुतःप्रकृत्या ह्युदकं शीतं स्कन्दयत्यति शोणितम् । तस्मात् सुखयति ह्युष्णं न तु शीतं कथञ्चन ।। इति सु०सू० । स्कन्दयति स्त्यानीकरोति तथा जङ्गमविषे ऊर्ध्वगस्वरूपे मोलविषमधोगस्वरूपं हेतुविपरीतमेव यदुर्क्त चरके विष विषघ्नमुर्क्त यत् प्रभावस्तत्र कारणम् । ऊर्ध्वानुलोमिकं यच्च तत् प्रभावप्रभावितम् ।। इति च०सू० अस्यायमर्थः विषत्वाविशेषेऽपि कृतो गतिभेद इत्यत उक्तं तत् प्रभावप्रभावितमिति तथा मद्यकृते मदात्यये यन्मद्यं तदपि मातुलुङ्गचुक्रादियुतं सुश्रुता- दिभिविहितं केवलाच्च द्रव्यान्तरसंयुक्तमन्यदेव अथवा वातमदात्यये रूक्षमाध्वीकादिना जनिते स्निग्धपैष्टिकादिमद्यं प्रयुज्यमानं हेतुविपरीतमेव यच्चोक्तं सुश्रुतेयथा नरेन्द्रोपहतस्य कस्यचिद्दवेत् प्रसादस्तत एवं नान्यतः । ध्रुवं तथा मद्यहतस्य देहिनो भवेत् प्रसादस्तत एव नान्यतः ।। इति सु०उ० तन्मद्यजातीयाभिप्रायेणैव यच्चोरुस्तम्भे जलप्रतरणं तत्रापि जलस्य शैत्येन बहिरगच्छन् देहोष्मा कुम्भकारपवनन्यायेनान्तःपिण्डितौ मेदःश्लेष्माणौ विलाययति व्यायामश्च तौ शोषयति ततस्तु निरावरणो वायुः स्वमार्गप्रतिपत्रो भवतीति हेतुप्रत्यनीकतैव अनेन न्यायेन सर्वमेव तदर्थकारि यथासम्भवं हेतुप्रत्यनीकादवेवान्त- र्भवतीति । उच्यते यद्यप्येवं तथाऽप्यवान्तरवैधर्म्यप्रतिपादनार्थमाचायेंः पृथम्दशितम् । तथा चरकेऽप्युक्तम् उपशयः पुनर्हेतुव्याधिविपरीतानां विपरीतार्थकारिणां चीषधाहारविहाराणा- मुपयोगः सुखानुवन्धः । इति च०नि० । वेधर्म्यं च हेतुसमानधर्मकत्वेऽपि रोग- प्रशमकत्वमिति मा ० नि० - विपरीतोऽनुपशयोयाध्यसात्म्याभिसंज्ञितः विपरीतोऽनुपशय इति औषधादीनां दुःखकर उपयोगोऽनुपशय इत्यर्थः । तत्पर्याय- माहव्याध्यसात्म्यमिति स्मृत इति । व्याधिग्रहणेन दोषोऽपि बोध्यः । ननु अनुपशयः किं व्याधिविशेषं बोधयति नो वा नेति चेत् निदाने तदुपन्यासो व्यर्थः प्रतिपादयतीति चेत् विज्ञानं रोगाणां पञ्चधा स्मृतम् इति व्याहन्यते तस्य षष्ठत्वापत्तेः । नैवं प्रतिपादयत्येव यदाह चरकः गूढलिङ्गं व्याधिमुपशयानुपशयाभ्यां परीक्षेत । इति च०वि० । किन्तु निदाने तस्यान्तर्भावः दोषस्य रोगस्य वा वर्धकत्वात् इत्यनुपशयस्य निदानेऽन्तर्भावान्न षष्ठत्वापत्तिः वक्ष्यति चनिदानोक्तानुपशयः इति । इत्युपशयलक्षणम् ।।।। दुष्टेन के दोषेण के यथा के चानुविसर्पता । यथा निर्वृत्तिरामयस्यासौं का प्राप्तिर्जातिरामतिः ॥१ ॥ - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 16):

असाध्यानां लक्षणमाह सर्वास्त्वित्यादि । सर्वा वातजादयः अंतिप्रसक्ता अतिप्रवृद्धाः । घोरोपद्रवयुक्ता मुखशोपादिभिर्बलवद्दिरुपद्रवैः समन्विता इति जेज्जटः ।।।। इति श्रीविजयरक्षितकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां तृष्णानिदानं समाप्तम् ने का प्रति के ल -
answer_text: The passage starting from sarvāstu describes features of the incurable variety of the disease. Actually, all types of thirst are incurable if they have advanced and have got accompanied by several complications as described above. This view has been supported by Jejjaṭa. Thus concludes the Chapter on Thirst. MODERN PERSPECTIVES ON MORBID THIRST In modern medical parlance, this sign is known as polydipsia or dyspepsia. The term pepsia might be connected to the Sanskrit term pipāsā; thus, the polydipsia is excessive (poly) thirst while dyspepsia is disordered (dys) thirst. Either is believed to appear due to endocrine disorders and certain drugs. It might reflect decreased fluid intake, increased urine output, or excessive loss of water and salt. A patient of dyspepsia should be examined through the blood pressure and pulse in supine and standing positions. A decrease of 10 Hg in systolic pressure and a pulse rate increase of 10 beats/minute from the supine to standing positions might demonstrate hypovo¬ lemia. If these changes are detected the patient should be asked about the recent weight loss. The physician should detect the symptoms of dehydration in terms of dry mucuous membranes and decreased skin turgor. The patient should be infused with IV substitute fluids if needed. Polydipsia might appear as an auxiliary sign also due to medical conditions such as Diabetes insipidus, Diabetes mellitus, Hyperca¬ lacmia, Hypokalemia, Psychgenic polydipsia, Chronic renal disor- ders, Sheehan’s syndrome, Sickle cell anemia and Thyrotoxicoisis. Moreover, diuretics and demeclocycline might generate polydipsia. Besides, phenothiazines and anticholinergics can produce dry mouth, making the patient so thirsty that he tends to drink water compulsively. In this disease, the physician should monitor the patient's fluid balance by monitoring his total intake and output. However, it might be noted that the thirst is normally the body’s way of compensating for water loss; the patient of excessive thirst might be given ample liquids. It might also be noted that some children develop habitual polydipsia that is unconnected to any disease
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 16.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 18):

तृतीयमदमाहगच्छेदित्यादि । ननु चरके द्वितीय-तृतीययोर्मध्ये मदान्तरं पठितं यदाहमध्यमं मदमुक्रम्य मदमप्राप्य चोत्तमम् । न किश्चिदशुभं कुर्युर्नरा राजसतामसाः ।। को मदं तादृशं गच्छेदुन्मादमिव चापरम् । च०चि० इति तत् कुतोऽत्र न पठितम् उच्यतेद्वितीयमदान्ते तृतीयमदस्य पूर्वावस्थैवातिनिन्दनीया सुतरां तृतीयो मद इति प्रतिपादनार्थं तत्पठितं न तु तयोः परमार्थतोऽन्तराले पृथङ्मदान्तरमस्ति यथाकुम्भ- मीनर्क्षयोर्मध्ये यदा चरति चन्द्रमाः । नाहरेतृण-काष्ठानि न गच्छेद्दक्षिणां दिशम् ।। इति । अत्र हि कुम्भस्य शेषांशो मीनस्य प्रथमांश एतद्वयं मध्यशब्देनोच्यत इत्याहुर्जेज्जटादयः हरिचन्द्र- व्याख्यानं तु विस्तरत्वान्न लिखितम् । अगम्यान् गुरुदारादीन् दुष्टयानादींश्च । नष्टसंज्ञ इति संज्ञा नामोल्लेखेन ज्ञानं तन्न्टं यस्य स तथा । गुह्यानि गोप्यानि । अस्वतन्त्रो मदपरवशः ।।।। चतुर्थे होतु होमदेव मूढो हो भग्नदार्विव होनिष्क्रियः । कार्याकार्यविभागज्ञो का मृतादप्यपरोधार्मिक मृतः ॥ ॥ को में में के तादृशंक गच्छेदुन्मादमिक ने चापरमू । बहुदोषमिवामूढः - कान्तारंक स्ववशः - कृती ॥१ ॥ - - -
answer_text: The passage starting from gacchet refers to the peculiar characteris¬ tics of the third or ultimate level of intoxication. It could be recalled here that the Caraka Text refers to a middle level of intoxication (CS. Ci. 24.46). This state is allegedly severe, too. Then why this level of intoxication has been denied a discussion here by the author? This issue could be addressed through the fact that the last stage of the secondary or the second level of intoxication is very dangerous and so is the first stage of the third or ultimate level of intoxication. Therefore, the description of the second level of intoxication could be automatically materialized through description of the first and third levels of intoxication. Jejjata has explained this through the example of the constellatory movements of the moon and the star mina where the last and first stages of their movement are not treated exclusively. The narrative of Haricandra is likewise explanatory (but due to fear of being too claborate, the same is being avoided here). The term agamyān signifies ones who are not fit for copulation like the teacher’s wife (or a pious woman) and it also signifies travelling by improper vehicles and ways. The term nastasanjya implies losing sense or ability of discrimination. The term asvatantra connotes dependence on or total dominance by intoxication. Caturtha mada (Fourth stage of intoxication) In the fourth and final stage of intoxication, the person falls to the ground unconscious like a tree cut down. He becomes incapable like a dead body. He no longer remains able to determine what to do and what not to do. Who would like to reach to the stage that is like another variety of dementia? No sensible, self-controlled, and knowledgeable person would like to go to a jungle full of adversi¬ ties. 10-11

context: तृतीयमदमाहगच्छेदित्यादि । ननु चरके द्वितीय-तृतीययोर्मध्ये मदान्तरं पठितं यदाहमध्यमं मदमुक्रम्य मदमप्राप्य चोत्तमम् । न किश्चिदशुभं कुर्युर्नरा राजसतामसाः ।। को मदं तादृशं गच्छेदुन्मादमिव चापरम् । च०चि० इति तत् कुतोऽत्र न पठितम् उच्यतेद्वितीयमदान्ते तृतीयमदस्य पूर्वावस्थैवातिनिन्दनीया सुतरां तृतीयो मद इति प्रतिपादनार्थं तत्पठितं न तु तयोः परमार्थतोऽन्तराले पृथङ्मदान्तरमस्ति यथाकुम्भ- मीनर्क्षयोर्मध्ये यदा चरति चन्द्रमाः । नाहरेतृण-काष्ठानि न गच्छेद्दक्षिणां दिशम् ।। इति । अत्र हि कुम्भस्य शेषांशो मीनस्य प्रथमांश एतद्वयं मध्यशब्देनोच्यत इत्याहुर्जेज्जटादयः हरिचन्द्र- व्याख्यानं तु विस्तरत्वान्न लिखितम् । अगम्यान् गुरुदारादीन् दुष्टयानादींश्च । नष्टसंज्ञ इति संज्ञा नामोल्लेखेन ज्ञानं तन्न्टं यस्य स तथा । गुह्यानि गोप्यानि । अस्वतन्त्रो मदपरवशः ।।।। चतुर्थे होतु होमदेव मूढो हो भग्नदार्विव होनिष्क्रियः । कार्याकार्यविभागज्ञो का मृतादप्यपरोधार्मिक मृतः ॥ ॥ को में में के तादृशंक गच्छेदुन्मादमिक ने चापरमू । बहुदोषमिवामूढः - कान्तारंक स्ववशः - कृती ॥१ ॥ - - -

question:

असुग्गतवातलक्षणमाहरुज इत्यादि । अरूंषि न्रणाः । भुक्तस्य स्तम्भो भुक्तवतो गात्रस्तम्भः सन्तर्पणेन रक्तस्य वृद्धेः । अन्ये त्वसृग्गतवातलक्षणं न पठन्ति वातरक्तेन सहा- भेदात् तन्न अंत्र दुष्टो वायू रक्तेनावृतः कुप्यति वातरक्ते तु स्वकारणादुभावपि हस्त्या- दिगमनकुपितौ विशिष्टसम्प्राप्त्या हस्तपादगतावेव वातरक्ताक्ष्यं विकारं जनयत इति ।।।। तुद्यतेऽत्यर्थं का दण्डमुष्टिहतं का स्था यथा । गुर्वङ्ग र मांस-मेदोगतेऽनिले ॥१ ॥ श्रमितमत्यर्थं सरुक् भेदोऽस्थिपर्वणां का सन्धिशूलं का मांस-बलक्षयः । अस्वप्नः सन्तता रुक् च मज्जास्थिकुपितेऽनिले ॥१ ८॥ - -
answer_text: The passage starting from ruja discusses the features of the vāta disease that has got located in the raktagata dhatu. The term arumsi signifies wounds. The passage bhuktasya stambha indicates the rigidity in the body that develops after consuming food, as eating produces increase in blood. Other scholars do not mention this condition. As some opine, asṛggatavāta is not different from vāta-rakta, but this view is apparently incorrect. In this condition, the vāta and rakta or blood vitiate due to their own reasons as when riding an elephant etc. and in the process of specific pathogenesis, they reach the hands and legs of the patient and subsequently produce vālarakta or gout. Signs and symptoms which occur when vāta reaches māṁsa and medas; majjā and asthi (CS. Ci. S. 28.32) If the vitiated vata gets in the mamsa and meda (muscles and fat) it generates feeling of heaviness of the body parts associated with severe pain as though one is being beaten by a stick or by fist and there is a feeling of extreme exhaustion. 17 (CS. Ci. S. 28.33) When vitiated vāyu gets located in the bone and bone marrow there may occur splitting pain in the bones and the small joints of the hands and the feet, severe pain in the big joints, wasting of muscles and depletion of strength, insomnia and persistent pain across the body. 18

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 20):

संस्वेदीत्यादि ।।।। हष्टात्मा पुलिन-वनान्तरोपसेवी स्वाचारः प्रियपरिगीत-गन्ध-माल्यः । नृत्यन् वै प्रहसति चारु चाल्पशब्दं गन्धर्वग्रहपरिपीडितो मनुष्यः ॥20॥
answer_text: In the above passage starting from the term santuṣṭa, etc., the symp- toms of the unmada or insanity that has been produced by the posses- sion of benevolent celestial elements (deva) have been presented. The term deva should be meant here to involve the celestial mothers (gaṇā mātṛka) as well. The narrative of Videha also corresponds to b the above narrative. He has suggested that the patient possessed by the celestial mothers (gana mātṛka) turns quarrelsome and attains a high temper. There is continuous discharge of saliva from his mouth. He would ever appear as sleepy. He remains silent. He trembles, too. These are the symptoms of the patient possessed by the celestial mothers (gaṇa māṭṛka). Afflication caused by devaśatrus Enemies of God i.e. demons) (SS. Ut. 60.9) The person who gets profuse perspiration, speaks lowly of the Brahmins, preceptors and gods, gazes with a frown, is afraid of none. looks towards an unrighteous path, does not get satisfied in spite of plenty of food and drinks and has an impious disposition should be considered to be afflicted with the visitation by the enemies of gods (asura graha). 19 In the above passage starting from the term samsvedi etc., features of the insanity produced by the malevolent celestial elements (deva- satru or demons) have been presented. Afflication caused by Gandharvagrahas (SS. Ut. 60.10) The features of the person possessed by gandharvagraha include contentment; desire to roam about on riverbanks, gardens and the like. He is also seen indulging in virtuous deeds and remains fond of suitable company, songs, scents, and garlands. He would remain dancing, laughing and speaking merrily, even without a purpose or sense. 20
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 20.
context: संस्वेदीत्यादि ।।।। हष्टात्मा पुलिन-वनान्तरोपसेवी स्वाचारः प्रियपरिगीत-गन्ध-माल्यः । नृत्यन् वै प्रहसति चारु चाल्पशब्दं गन्धर्वग्रहपरिपीडितो मनुष्यः ॥20॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 681):

अमृतफल लघु वृष्यं सुस्वादु त्रीन् हरेद्दोषान् । देशेषु मुद्रलानां बहुलं तल्लभ्यते लोकैः ।।१७।।
answer_text: Latin: Pyrus communis Linn. Fam: Rosaceae Hin: Naspati Guna karma (Properties and indications): Amrta Phalā is Laghu (Light for digestion), Vrṣya (Aphrodisiac), Suswādu (Palatable), subsides all Tridoṣas. It is abundantly grown in Mughal desa. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Distributed in the temperate regions of Europe and West Asia grown in Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Kashmir. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a small-medium sized tree reaches upto 10m. Leaves are orbicular- ovate, alternately arranged, accuminate apex, glossy dark green and toothed margins. Flowers, white in clusters, 1.5-2 cm. across, arranged in corymbs. Fruit subglobose, fleshy, contains 4-6 seeds. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Patra (Leaves), Phala (Fruits). Chemical constituents: Fruit contains Beta carotene, Amino acids (Glycine, arginine, alanine), isoleucine, leucine and threonine. Leaves- pyroside and Bark- Friedelin and epifriede'inol
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 681
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 681.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 5):

रक्तार्शोलक्षणमाह रक्तेल्बणा इत्यादि । गुदेकीलाः कीलवत् कीलाः अर्शांसि हलदन्तात् सप्तम्याः संज्ञायाम् पा०अ० पा० सू० इत्यलुक्समासः पित्ताकृति समन्विताः पैत्तिकार्शोलक्षणयुक्ताः । विद्रमसन्निभाः प्रवालमणिवल्लोहिता इत्यर्थः । ते गाढविट्कप्रपीडिताः कठिनपुरीषयन्त्रिताः दुष्टम् आविलम् उष्णं च रक्तं स्नवन्ति । तस्येति रक्तस्य अतिप्रवृत्तितः अतिक्षयात् भेकाभः प्रावृषेण्यवर्षाभ्वाभः पीतच्छविः पुरुषः इति शेषः । दुःखैः रोगैः । शोणितक्षयसम्भवैरिति त्वक्पारुष्याम्लशीतप्रार्थनासिराशैथिल्यैः सु०सू० सुश्रुतोक्तैः । वलं स्थौल्यम् उत्साहो हर्षः । हतौजाः हतशक्तिः । कलुषेन्द्रिय आविलचक्षुः व्याकुलसर्वेन्द्रियो वा ।।- तत्रानुबन्धो द्विविधः श्लेष्मणो मारुतस्य च । विट् श्यावं कठिनं रूक्षमधोवायुर्न वर्तते ॥॥ तनु चारुणवर्ण चारु फेनिलं चारुगर्शस्ताम् । कट्यूरु-गुदशूलं च दौर्वल्यं यदि चाधिकम् ॥ ॥ त्रानुवन्धो वातस्य हेतुर्यंदि च रूक्षणम् । शिथिलं श्रेतपीतं च विद् रिनार्ध गुरु शीतलम् यद्यर्शसां घनं चासृक् तन्तुमत् पाण्डु पिच्छिलम् । ग्रदं सपिच्छं स्तिमितं ग्रुरु स्निग्धं च कारणम् । श्लेष्मानुबन्धो विज्ञेयस्तत्र रक्तार्शंसां बुधेः - - - - - - - -
answer_text: This passage is meant to explain features of the raktaja arsa or the piles produced by the vitiated blood. The piles in such case look like nails and that is why they are called as kildka’s (nails’) variety. The term pittākṛtisamanvitā refers to the fact that the blood-induced piles are similar in form to the ones produced by pitta. The term vidruma- sannibha refers to the reddish colour of the sprouts. The term Bhe- kābha means looking yellow-green like the frog (bheka) in the rainy season. The disease also produces the complications that are caused due to deficiency of blood including dryness of skin, loss of strength, zeal, and weakness of all the sense organs (SS. S7. 15.9). Association of vāta and kapha in Bleeding piles Raktārsa may have associations of two dosas as well, the vata and kapha. If the faeces are blackish, hard and dry, the flatus is passed (easily) and thin, red-coloured frothy blood is passed associated with colicky pain in the waist, thighs and perianal regions along with extreme weakness and if these are due to the substances which produce dryness in the body the secondary involvement should be considered to be that of vāyu. In the case of kapha association, faeces could be broken (semi-solid), whitish yellow in colour, frothy, heavy, and cold. The pile mass exudes thick, sticky and whitish yellow blood that resembles piece of thread in shape. It could be smooth, immovable, heavy, and slippery to touch. 27-30
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 5.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 52):

मधुकोशः अम्लपित्तसंभवच्छर्देर्वेगाविधारणाद्रक्तदुष्टौ सत्यां विसर्पोत्पत्तेर्हेतुसाम्यात्तदनन्तरं विसर्पनिदानम्। छर्दिवेग- विघातस्य रक्तद्वषकत्वे चरकवचनं यथा,-‘छर्दिंवेगप्रतीघातात् कालेचानवसेचनात्। शरत्कालप्रभावाच्य शोणितं संप्रदृष्यति' (च.सू. २४) इति। तस्य निदानपूर्विकां संख्यां निरुक्ति चाह-लवणाम्लेत्यादि। ‘विसर्पो न ह्यसंसृष्टो रक्तपित्तेन लक्ष्यते’ इति वचनात् लवणाम्लादिकं विशेषेण रक्तपित्तनिदानमुक्तम्। संसेवया सततसेवया दोषकोपः संसेवादोषकोपस्ततः । अत्र आदिग्रहणाच्चरकोक्तानां हरितशाकशिण्डाकीप्रभृतीनां ग्रहणम् । सप्तधेति उल्वणैकैक- दोषजास्त्रयः, सन्निपातज एकः, त्रयो द्वन्द्वजाः, इति सप्तप्रकारत्वमुक्तम्। सर्वतः परिसर्पणादिति सर्वतः परिसर्पणात् परिसर्पः, विविधं सर्पणाद्विसर्पः। यदुक्तं चरके, 'विविधं सर्पति यतो' विसर्पस्तेन स स्मृतः। परिसर्पोऽथवा नाम्ना सर्वतः परिसर्पणात्’ (च.चि. २१) इति॥ १–३॥ रक्तं लसीका त्वड्मांसं दूष्यं दोषास्त्रयो मलाः ॥ ४॥ विसर्पाणां समुत्पत्तौ विज्ञेयाः सप्त धातवः । तत्र वातात् स वीसर्पो वातञ्वरसमव्यथः ॥ ५ ॥ ( च.चि. ११ ) शोथस्फुरणनिस्तोदभेदायासार्तिहर्षवान्। पित्तादुद्रतगतिः पित्तच्वरलिङ्वोऽतिलोहितः॥ ६॥ कफात् कण्ड्रयुतः स्निग्धः कफज्वरसमानरुक्। सन्निपातसमुत्थश्च सर्वलिङ्गसमन्वितः॥ ७॥ ( वा.नि. १३ ) मधुकोशः सर्वेषामेव रक्तादिद्रुष्यचतुष्टयदोषत्रयजन्यत्वमाह-रक्तमित्यादि। विसर्पस्य समानसमामग्रीकत्वेऽपि कुष्ठाद्वेदः कुष्ठाध्याये एव निरूपितः । दोषशब्देनैव वातादिग्रहणे सिद्धे मला इति यत् कुतं,तदत्यर्थद्ष्ट्या शरीरमलिनीकरणत्वं दोषाणां प्रतिपादयित्म्। सन्निपातजेऽसाध्यत्वमपि ‘सर्वात्मकः क्षतकृतक्ष न सिद्धिमेति’ ( सु.नि.१०) इति वचनात् । तेन विकृतिविषमसमवेतत्वमस्य। चरके त्वन्तर्जबहिर्जभदेन विसर्पः पठितः । यदाह-'मर्मोपघातात्र संमोहादयनानां विघटुनात् । तृष्णातियोगाद्वेगानां विषमं च प्रवर्तनात् ॥ विद्याद्विसर्पमत्तर्जमाशु चाग्निबलक्षयात् । अतो विपर्ययाद्वाह्यमन्यं विद्यात् स्वलक्षणैः ' ( च.चि. २१ ) इति ॥ ४-७॥ वातपित्ताजवरच्छर्दिमूर्च्छातीसारतृड्भमैः । ग्रन्थिभेदाग्निसदनतमकारोचकैर्युः तः ॥ ८ ॥ करोति सर्वमड़ुं च दीप्ताङ्गारावकीर्णवत्। यं यं देशं विसर्पश्च विसर्पति भवेत् स सः॥ ९॥ शान्ताङ्वारासितो नीलो रक्तो वाऽऽशु च चीयते। अग्निदग्ध इव स्फोटैः श्रीघ्रगत्वाद्दुतं च सः॥ १०॥ मर्मानुसारी वीसर्पः स्याद्वातोऽतिबलस्ततः। व्यथतेऽङ्गं हरेत्संज्ञां निद्रां च श्वासमीरयेत्॥ ११॥ हिक्कां च स गतोऽवस्थामीदृशीं लभते न ना। क्रचिच्छर्मारतिग्रस्तो भूमिशय्यासनादिषु॥ १२॥ चेष्टामानस्ततः क्लिष्टो मनोदेहप्रमोहवान्। दुष्प्रबोधोऽश्नुते निद्रां सोऽग्निवीसर्प उच्यते ॥ १३ ॥ ( वा.नि.१३ ) मधुकोशः आग्नेयविसर्पमाह-वांतपित्तदित्यादि। दीप्ताङ्कारावकीर्णवदिति ज्वलदङ्कारेणैव व्याप्तमङ्कं मन्यते । शान्ताङ्गारासित इति निर्वाणाङ्गारवत् कृष्णवर्णः स देशो भवति। नीलो रक्तो वेति स देशः स्निग्धनीलो रक्तोव ा भवति। अग्निदग्ध इवेति अग्निदग्धदेश इव। शीघ्रगत्वादिति शीघ्रकारित्वात्। मर्मानुसारी हृदयाद्यनुसारी। व्यथतेऽङ्गमित्यत्रान्तर्भावितो ण्यर्थंः, तेन व्यथयतीत्यर्थः। निद्रां चेत्यत्र हरेदिति संबध्यते। शर्म सुखम्। दुष्प्रबोधोऽश्नते निद्रामिति निद्रां मरणरूपां प्राप्नोति॥ ८-१३॥ कफेन रुद्धः पवनो भित्त्वा तं बहुधा कफम्। रक्त वा वृद्धरक्तस्य त्वक्सिरास्नायुमांसगम्॥ १४॥ दूषयित्वा तु दीर्घाणुवृत्तस्थूलखरात्मनाम्। ग्रन्थीनां कुरुते मालां सरक्तां तीव्ररुग्ज्वराम्॥ १५॥ श्वासकासातिसारास्यशोषहिक्कावभिभ्रमैः । मोहवैवर्ण्यमूर्च्छाङ्गभङ्गाग्निसदनैर्युताम्॥ १६ ॥ इत्ययं ग्रन्थिवीसर्पः कफमारुतकोपजः। ( वा.नि. १३ ) मधुकोशः ग्रन्थिविसर्पमाह-कफेन रुद्ध इत्यादि। कफेनेति स्वहेतुकुपितेन, पवनः स्वहेतुकुपितः, तेन कफमारुत- जत्वमस्योपपन्न भवति। भित्त्वा तं बहुधा कफमिति कफं विस्तार्य। रक्तं वेति दूषयित्वेत्यनेन वक्ष्यमाणेन संबध्यते। दीर्घाणुवृत्तस्थूलखरा त्मनामिति वृत्तं वर्तुलं, स्थूलमुच्छूनं, खरं कठिनं, एवंरूपाणां ग्रन्थीनां मालां करोति, अयं च ग्रन्थिविसर्प, सुश्रुतेऽपचीसंज्ञया पठ्यते ॥ १४–१६ ॥ कफपित्ताज्ज्वरः स्तम्भो निद्रा तन्द्रा शिरोरुजा॥ १७॥ अङ्गावसादविक्षेपौ प्रलेपारोचकभ्रमाः । मूर्च्छांग्निहानिर्भेदोऽस्थ्नां पिपासेन्द्रियगौरवम्॥ १८॥ आमोपवेशनं लेपः स्रोतसां स च सर्पति। प्रायेणामाशयं गृहणन्रेकदेशं न चातिरुक् ॥ १९ ॥ पिडकैरवकीर्णोऽतिपीतलोहितपाण्डुरैः। स्निग्धोऽसितो मेचकाभो मलिनः शोथवान् गुरुः॥ २०॥ गम्भीरपाकः प्राज्योष्मा स्पृष्टः क्लिन्नोऽवदीर्यते। पङ्कवच्छीर्णमांसश्च स्पष्टस्नायुसिरागणः॥ २१॥ शवगन्धी च वीसर्पः कर्दमाख्यमुशन्ति तम् । ( वा.नि. १३ ) मधुकोशः कर्दमविसर्पमाह-कफपित्तादित्यादि। स्तम्भ इति गात्रस्य स्तब्धता, आमोपवेशनमामस्य वर्चसंस्त्यजनम्। स च सर्पति प्रायेणार्मशयं गृह्णन्नेकदेशमिति कफपित्तयोरामाशयस्थत्वात् प्रायेणामाशये भवन्नेकदेशव्यापी भवतीत्यर्थः । पिडकैरिति पिडकाभिः, मलिन इति मलदिग्धः । गम्भीरपाक इत्यन्तः पाकः, प्राज्योष्मा प्रचुरोष्मा। स्पष्टस्नायुसिरागण इति पूतिमांसगलनेन स्राय्वादीनां स्पष्टता। कर्दमाख्यमुशन्ति तमिति तं कर्दमसारूप्यात् कर्दमाख्यमिच्छन्ति॥ १७–२१ ॥ बाह्यहेतोः क्षतात् क्रुन्द्रः सरक्त पित्तमीरयन्॥ २२॥ ( वा.नि. १३ ) वीसर्पं मारुतः कुर्यात्कुलत्थसदृशैश्चितम्। स्फोटैः शोथज्वररुजादाहाढयं श्यावशोणितम्॥ २३॥ ज्वरातिसारी वमथुस्त्वड्मांसदरणं क्लमः । अरोचकाविपाकौर्च विसर्पाणामुपद्रवाः ॥ २४॥ ( सु.नि. १० ) मधुकोशः क्षतविसर्पमाह-बाह्यहेतोरित्यादि। अयं च पित्तजे विसर्पेऽन्तर्भावनीयः, तेन न संख्याधिक्यम्। तथाच भोजः– शस्त्रप्रहारेस्तैस्तैस्तु व्याडदत्तनखैरपि। क्षते वाऽप्यथवा भग्ने बहुदोषस्य देहिनः। रक्त पित्तं च कुपितं व्रणमाशु प्रपद्यते। कुरुतस्ते समेते तु व्रणशोथं सुदारुणम्। आचितं तनुविस्फोटैः कृष्णेः पीतकसन्निभैः। पित्तवीसर्पवलिङ् तस्य शेषं 'विनिर्दिशेत्' इति ॥ २२-२४॥ सिध्यन्ति वातकफपित्तकृता विसर्पाः सर्वात्मकः क्षतकृतश्च न सिद्धिमेति। पित्तात्मकोऽअनवपुश्च भवेदसाध्यः कृच्छाश्च मर्मसु भवन्ति हि सर्व एव॥ २५ ॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने विसर्पनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ५२॥ मधुकोशः साध्यत्वदिकमाह-सिध्यन्तीत्यादि। पित्तात्मकोऽञनवपुरिति अत्यन्तमुद्रिक्तपित्तोऽञनसमवर्णतनुः, अग्नि- विसर्पाख्यो न साध्य इति व्याख्यानयन्ति। कृच्छाश्च मर्मेस्विति असाध्यत्वेन कृच्छत्वं बोद्धव्यम्। यदाह। भोजः- वर्ज्यस्तु क्षतजस्तेषां सन्निपातातु यो भवेत्। भिषजा जानता त्याज्याः सर्व एव तु मर्मजाः' इति॥ २५॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां विसर्पनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥ ५२ ॥
answer_text: Due to suppression of the emission caused by Amlapitta, the vitiation of Rakta takes place which is also a cause for visarpa. Therefore, in view of this similarity, Visarpa is explained after Amlapitta. Due to suppression of the bout of vomitting, Rakta gets vitiated as per the statment of Caraka, “Due to suppression of the bout of Mādhavanidānaṃ vamana (emesis), not inducing the vamana in suitable time and also due to the effect of Saratkāla (moonlight season), the blood gets vitiated.” (Ca. Sū. 24). The individual visarpa is akin to Rakta pitta. That is why the Rakta pitta aetiology-consumption of salty, sour foods - is mentioned here. Samsevaya means to consume continuously.The word ādi (etc., ) in......kaṭūṣṇādi indicates the inclusion of green vegetables, śiṇdākī (fermented beverage) etc., are also mentioned by Caraka. 7 types means 3 from three dosa individually, 1 from three dosas together and 3 from dual combination of three doşas. Since it spreads all over the body, it is known as parisarpa (sarvatah parisarpanat); vividham parisarpanat —Since it spreads differently also, it is known as Visarpa. As said in Caraka, “As it spreads differently in the body, it is known as Visarpa. It is also called as parisarpa as it spreads all over the body". 1-3. (Ca.Ci. 21). The involvement of Dosa-dusya; Symptomatology of single dosa and Tridosa visarpa Rakta (blood), Lasīkā (water), Tvak (Skin)and māṃṣa (muscle tissue) are the dūṣya (vitiated factors) and the tridoṣas are the turbid factor (that vitiate other). All these seven important factors takes part in the origination of the disease, visarpa. ( Ca. Ci-21 ). In vata-dominated Visarpa, there will be suffering as that of Vata jvara (Vata dominated fever). There will also be oedema, pulsation, pinning sensation, break¬ ing sensation, fatigue, pain, and horrippulation. The spreading is fast in pitta dominated Visarpa red in colour and the symptomatology is like that of pitta-jvara. Due to kapha there will be itching sensation, oiliness in the skin and the suffering is as that of kapha juara (Kapha-dominated fever). (Vā. Ni. 13) In the sannipata type where all three of the dosas are equally involved, there will be mixed symptomatology of all three of the dosas together. 4-7. Visarpa Nidāna In all the visarpas, , Rakta etc., four dusyas and Tridosa involvement is ex¬ plained here. Though the factors involved in kustha and visarpa are common, the difference of Visarpa from kustha is established in kustha tself. When the Vata etc., three dosas are indicated by the word dosa itself, usage of the term mala is to show the over vitiation and the capacity of these dosas causing more turbidity in the body. The incurability of Sannipātaja is as per the statement of Suśruta- “The one in which all doşas (three) are involved and the one caused by external injury sarvatmaka and ksatakṛta) are incurable. Hence irregular and improper combina¬ tion of the morbid factors is present in this disease (Vikrtivisama samaveta). In Caraka, two varieties of visarpa by name Antarja and Bahirja are mentioned — Due to injury in the vital parts, by willfully causing injury to the orifices due to ignorance, due to over thirst, by exerting the natural urges in an irregular manner Antarja visarpa is produced which is to be considered very fast as it depletes the digestion power and bodily strength. The one which is different from this type of visarpa is Bahyaja (bahirja) to be known by the symptomatology manifested”. 4-7. (Ca. Ci. 21). Agni visarpa Due to predominance of Vāta and Pitta in visarpa, there are fever, vomitting, syncope, diarrhoea, thirst, giddiness, tumours, breaking pain in the joints, loss'of appetite, darkening before the eyes or severe dyspnoea (Tamaka) anorexia, feel¬ ing as if covered by burning coal; wherever this types of visarpa manifests in the body, that place becomes black like extinguished coal or blue or red, there will be blisters resembling those caused by burning that spread fast. It affects mostly the Mādhavanidānaṃ, vital parts. Due to the influence of Vata there will be severe pain, loss of conscious¬ ness, sleeplessness, severe dyspnoea and hiccup. Such patient will never get relief in any posture. He keeps sitting, lying down again and again to find relief; He goes into difficult position mentally and physically and may get into sleep from which he can never wake up. This condition is called agni ufarpa. 8-13. (Vā. Ni. 13). Diptangaravakirnavat" -means feeling as if the body is amidst burning coal. Santangarasita" means - that place becomes black like the extinguished coal. Nilo raktovā means - that place becomes smooth blue or red. Agnidagdhaiva means - as if burnt by fire; Sīghragatitvāt means - due to its nature of fast spreading; marmānusarī spreading to vital parts like heart etc., pierces the organs means - causes piercing pain in the organs; Nidram ca - sleep also is to be connected to haret- destroys; sarmarelief. Dusprabodha asnute nidram; gets into the sleep which has no awakeningmeans gets into death form of sleep. 8-13. Granthi Visarpa Vata that is obstructed by kapha, breaks that kapha into various forms, or the rakta which is accumulated in the skin, veins, tendons and muscle tissue and on vitiating them causes long, small, round, big and hard tumours in series which are red in colour, severely painful, associated withfever, dyspnoea, cough, diarrhoea, dryness in the mouth, hiccup, vomitting, giddiness, delusion, discolouration, syn¬ cope, breaking sensation in the body and loss of appetite. This condition is called granthi visarpa caused by aggravated kapha and vāta. 14-16. (Vā. Ni. 13). Visarpa Nidāna Kaphena - by kapha which has aggravated by its own reasons; pavana - văta aggravated due to its own reasons; therefore, this disease being caused by kapha and Vāta is established. Breaking that kapha in different forms - means having spread the kapha. Raktam va or the blood is connected to the for the coming dūṣayitvā —having vitiated. vrittam means round, sthūlam - elevated/swollen; kharaṃ - hard; causes such type of tumours in series which is called granthivīsarpa which is read as apaci in Susruta. 14-16. Kardama visarpa Due to kapha and pitta, there is fever, rigidity in the limbs, excessive sleep, tiredness of the hands and legs, feeling of stickiness, anorexia, giddiness, syncope, loss of appetite, breaking sensation in the bones, thirst, heaviness in the senseorgans, passing stool with more of āma (undigested stuff), sticky feeling, moving in the channels it taken shelter in the āmāsaya and is not much painful. The vesicles that arise are in clusters-yellow in colour, red and pale, oily, blackish like the col¬ lyrium, turbid, swollen and heavy, they get ripened internally with lot of warmth and wetness, they wither away even by touch; the muscle looks like mud/black clay, withers out exposing the ligaments and veins with necrosed smell. Such vasarpa is called kardama vīsarpa. 17-21. (Vā. Ni. 13 ). Stambha -rigidity-means rigidity of the body. Amopavésana means passing āma 152. Mādhavanidānaṃ in the stool. Since the seat of kapha and pitta is amasaya, the disease also gets con¬ centrated in one place.i.e., amāśaya; pidakaih means by vesicles; malinah means full of turbidity. Gambhīra pāka means getting ripened internally; prajyoṣmā means intense warmth. The exposure of ligaments, veins etc., is due to withering ot the putrified muscle-tissue, these will be seen out; kardama means turbid mud; since the site of affected area in this disease looks like mud, it is styled thus. 17-21. Ksata visarpa and complications of visarpa Due to external stimuli when an injury occurs, Vāta causes visarpa in which it aggravates the pitta along with rakta causing innumerable vesicles of horse-gram - size in blackish-red colour. There will be inflammation, fever, pain and severe burning sensation in this condition. (This is known as kṣataja visarpa). 22, 23. (Vā. Ni. 13). The complications of visarpa are fever, diarrhoea, vomitting, breaking and withering of skin and muscle-tissue, fatigue, distaste and indigestion. 24. (Su. Ni. 10) Ksata visarpa should be taken as part of pittaja visarpa by which there can not be extra enumeration. Bhoja also says, “Due to blow of various weapons and of teeth, fangs and nails of wild animals, there occur injury or fracture in an indi¬ vidual who has aggravation dosas. The rakta and pitta get vitiated and causes wound and due to accumulation of all these morbidities, vrana sotha (oedematous wound) forms which is severe, full of small papules which are black and yellow which is similar to pitta vīsarpa in other respects”. 22-24. Curability of Visarpa Visarpa Nidāna Visarpas caused by individual vata, pitta and kapha are curable. Tridosaja variety (caused by all three of the doşas) and kşataja (caused by injury) are not curable. The one dominated by pitta and where the body becomes like collyrium is also incurable. The visarpa originating on the vital parts are difficult for cure. 25. (Su. Ni. 10) Thus ends the diagnosis of visarpa (erysipelas) in Madhava's book of diagno¬ sis written by Śrīmādhavakara Pittatmakanjana vapuh " means the body becomes black like collyrium in highly aggravated state of pitta which is seen in Agni vīsarpa. This is incurable. The visarpa originating on vital parts in is also incurable, thus declared as difficult for i cure - is to be known. As said by Bhoja, “The kṣataja variety and Sannipata variety of visarpa are to be left without treating. The physician when identifies that visarpa is caused on vital parts, such condition should also be discarded". 25. Thus ends diagnosis of visarpa (erysipelas) in the Madhukosa commentary written by Śrikaṇṭhadatta. 52. ****.225

context: मधुकोशः अम्लपित्तसंभवच्छर्देर्वेगाविधारणाद्रक्तदुष्टौ सत्यां विसर्पोत्पत्तेर्हेतुसाम्यात्तदनन्तरं विसर्पनिदानम्। छर्दिवेग- विघातस्य रक्तद्वषकत्वे चरकवचनं यथा,-‘छर्दिंवेगप्रतीघातात् कालेचानवसेचनात्। शरत्कालप्रभावाच्य शोणितं संप्रदृष्यति' (च.सू. २४) इति। तस्य निदानपूर्विकां संख्यां निरुक्ति चाह-लवणाम्लेत्यादि। ‘विसर्पो न ह्यसंसृष्टो रक्तपित्तेन लक्ष्यते’ इति वचनात् लवणाम्लादिकं विशेषेण रक्तपित्तनिदानमुक्तम्। संसेवया सततसेवया दोषकोपः संसेवादोषकोपस्ततः । अत्र आदिग्रहणाच्चरकोक्तानां हरितशाकशिण्डाकीप्रभृतीनां ग्रहणम् । सप्तधेति उल्वणैकैक- दोषजास्त्रयः, सन्निपातज एकः, त्रयो द्वन्द्वजाः, इति सप्तप्रकारत्वमुक्तम्। सर्वतः परिसर्पणादिति सर्वतः परिसर्पणात् परिसर्पः, विविधं सर्पणाद्विसर्पः। यदुक्तं चरके, 'विविधं सर्पति यतो' विसर्पस्तेन स स्मृतः। परिसर्पोऽथवा नाम्ना सर्वतः परिसर्पणात्’ (च.चि. २१) इति॥ १–३॥ रक्तं लसीका त्वड्मांसं दूष्यं दोषास्त्रयो मलाः ॥ ४॥ विसर्पाणां समुत्पत्तौ विज्ञेयाः सप्त धातवः । तत्र वातात् स वीसर्पो वातञ्वरसमव्यथः ॥ ५ ॥ ( च.चि. ११ ) शोथस्फुरणनिस्तोदभेदायासार्तिहर्षवान्। पित्तादुद्रतगतिः पित्तच्वरलिङ्वोऽतिलोहितः॥ ६॥ कफात् कण्ड्रयुतः स्निग्धः कफज्वरसमानरुक्। सन्निपातसमुत्थश्च सर्वलिङ्गसमन्वितः॥ ७॥ ( वा.नि. १३ ) मधुकोशः सर्वेषामेव रक्तादिद्रुष्यचतुष्टयदोषत्रयजन्यत्वमाह-रक्तमित्यादि। विसर्पस्य समानसमामग्रीकत्वेऽपि कुष्ठाद्वेदः कुष्ठाध्याये एव निरूपितः । दोषशब्देनैव वातादिग्रहणे सिद्धे मला इति यत् कुतं,तदत्यर्थद्ष्ट्या शरीरमलिनीकरणत्वं दोषाणां प्रतिपादयित्म्। सन्निपातजेऽसाध्यत्वमपि ‘सर्वात्मकः क्षतकृतक्ष न सिद्धिमेति’ ( सु.नि.१०) इति वचनात् । तेन विकृतिविषमसमवेतत्वमस्य। चरके त्वन्तर्जबहिर्जभदेन विसर्पः पठितः । यदाह-'मर्मोपघातात्र संमोहादयनानां विघटुनात् । तृष्णातियोगाद्वेगानां विषमं च प्रवर्तनात् ॥ विद्याद्विसर्पमत्तर्जमाशु चाग्निबलक्षयात् । अतो विपर्ययाद्वाह्यमन्यं विद्यात् स्वलक्षणैः ' ( च.चि. २१ ) इति ॥ ४-७॥ वातपित्ताजवरच्छर्दिमूर्च्छातीसारतृड्भमैः । ग्रन्थिभेदाग्निसदनतमकारोचकैर्युः तः ॥ ८ ॥ करोति सर्वमड़ुं च दीप्ताङ्गारावकीर्णवत्। यं यं देशं विसर्पश्च विसर्पति भवेत् स सः॥ ९॥ शान्ताङ्वारासितो नीलो रक्तो वाऽऽशु च चीयते। अग्निदग्ध इव स्फोटैः श्रीघ्रगत्वाद्दुतं च सः॥ १०॥ मर्मानुसारी वीसर्पः स्याद्वातोऽतिबलस्ततः। व्यथतेऽङ्गं हरेत्संज्ञां निद्रां च श्वासमीरयेत्॥ ११॥ हिक्कां च स गतोऽवस्थामीदृशीं लभते न ना। क्रचिच्छर्मारतिग्रस्तो भूमिशय्यासनादिषु॥ १२॥ चेष्टामानस्ततः क्लिष्टो मनोदेहप्रमोहवान्। दुष्प्रबोधोऽश्नुते निद्रां सोऽग्निवीसर्प उच्यते ॥ १३ ॥ ( वा.नि.१३ ) मधुकोशः आग्नेयविसर्पमाह-वांतपित्तदित्यादि। दीप्ताङ्कारावकीर्णवदिति ज्वलदङ्कारेणैव व्याप्तमङ्कं मन्यते । शान्ताङ्गारासित इति निर्वाणाङ्गारवत् कृष्णवर्णः स देशो भवति। नीलो रक्तो वेति स देशः स्निग्धनीलो रक्तोव ा भवति। अग्निदग्ध इवेति अग्निदग्धदेश इव। शीघ्रगत्वादिति शीघ्रकारित्वात्। मर्मानुसारी हृदयाद्यनुसारी। व्यथतेऽङ्गमित्यत्रान्तर्भावितो ण्यर्थंः, तेन व्यथयतीत्यर्थः। निद्रां चेत्यत्र हरेदिति संबध्यते। शर्म सुखम्। दुष्प्रबोधोऽश्नते निद्रामिति निद्रां मरणरूपां प्राप्नोति॥ ८-१३॥ कफेन रुद्धः पवनो भित्त्वा तं बहुधा कफम्। रक्त वा वृद्धरक्तस्य त्वक्सिरास्नायुमांसगम्॥ १४॥ दूषयित्वा तु दीर्घाणुवृत्तस्थूलखरात्मनाम्। ग्रन्थीनां कुरुते मालां सरक्तां तीव्ररुग्ज्वराम्॥ १५॥ श्वासकासातिसारास्यशोषहिक्कावभिभ्रमैः । मोहवैवर्ण्यमूर्च्छाङ्गभङ्गाग्निसदनैर्युताम्॥ १६ ॥ इत्ययं ग्रन्थिवीसर्पः कफमारुतकोपजः। ( वा.नि. १३ ) मधुकोशः ग्रन्थिविसर्पमाह-कफेन रुद्ध इत्यादि। कफेनेति स्वहेतुकुपितेन, पवनः स्वहेतुकुपितः, तेन कफमारुत- जत्वमस्योपपन्न भवति। भित्त्वा तं बहुधा कफमिति कफं विस्तार्य। रक्तं वेति दूषयित्वेत्यनेन वक्ष्यमाणेन संबध्यते। दीर्घाणुवृत्तस्थूलखरा त्मनामिति वृत्तं वर्तुलं, स्थूलमुच्छूनं, खरं कठिनं, एवंरूपाणां ग्रन्थीनां मालां करोति, अयं च ग्रन्थिविसर्प, सुश्रुतेऽपचीसंज्ञया पठ्यते ॥ १४–१६ ॥ कफपित्ताज्ज्वरः स्तम्भो निद्रा तन्द्रा शिरोरुजा॥ १७॥ अङ्गावसादविक्षेपौ प्रलेपारोचकभ्रमाः । मूर्च्छांग्निहानिर्भेदोऽस्थ्नां पिपासेन्द्रियगौरवम्॥ १८॥ आमोपवेशनं लेपः स्रोतसां स च सर्पति। प्रायेणामाशयं गृहणन्रेकदेशं न चातिरुक् ॥ १९ ॥ पिडकैरवकीर्णोऽतिपीतलोहितपाण्डुरैः। स्निग्धोऽसितो मेचकाभो मलिनः शोथवान् गुरुः॥ २०॥ गम्भीरपाकः प्राज्योष्मा स्पृष्टः क्लिन्नोऽवदीर्यते। पङ्कवच्छीर्णमांसश्च स्पष्टस्नायुसिरागणः॥ २१॥ शवगन्धी च वीसर्पः कर्दमाख्यमुशन्ति तम् । ( वा.नि. १३ ) मधुकोशः कर्दमविसर्पमाह-कफपित्तादित्यादि। स्तम्भ इति गात्रस्य स्तब्धता, आमोपवेशनमामस्य वर्चसंस्त्यजनम्। स च सर्पति प्रायेणार्मशयं गृह्णन्नेकदेशमिति कफपित्तयोरामाशयस्थत्वात् प्रायेणामाशये भवन्नेकदेशव्यापी भवतीत्यर्थः । पिडकैरिति पिडकाभिः, मलिन इति मलदिग्धः । गम्भीरपाक इत्यन्तः पाकः, प्राज्योष्मा प्रचुरोष्मा। स्पष्टस्नायुसिरागण इति पूतिमांसगलनेन स्राय्वादीनां स्पष्टता। कर्दमाख्यमुशन्ति तमिति तं कर्दमसारूप्यात् कर्दमाख्यमिच्छन्ति॥ १७–२१ ॥ बाह्यहेतोः क्षतात् क्रुन्द्रः सरक्त पित्तमीरयन्॥ २२॥ ( वा.नि. १३ ) वीसर्पं मारुतः कुर्यात्कुलत्थसदृशैश्चितम्। स्फोटैः शोथज्वररुजादाहाढयं श्यावशोणितम्॥ २३॥ ज्वरातिसारी वमथुस्त्वड्मांसदरणं क्लमः । अरोचकाविपाकौर्च विसर्पाणामुपद्रवाः ॥ २४॥ ( सु.नि. १० ) मधुकोशः क्षतविसर्पमाह-बाह्यहेतोरित्यादि। अयं च पित्तजे विसर्पेऽन्तर्भावनीयः, तेन न संख्याधिक्यम्। तथाच भोजः– शस्त्रप्रहारेस्तैस्तैस्तु व्याडदत्तनखैरपि। क्षते वाऽप्यथवा भग्ने बहुदोषस्य देहिनः। रक्त पित्तं च कुपितं व्रणमाशु प्रपद्यते। कुरुतस्ते समेते तु व्रणशोथं सुदारुणम्। आचितं तनुविस्फोटैः कृष्णेः पीतकसन्निभैः। पित्तवीसर्पवलिङ् तस्य शेषं 'विनिर्दिशेत्' इति ॥ २२-२४॥ सिध्यन्ति वातकफपित्तकृता विसर्पाः सर्वात्मकः क्षतकृतश्च न सिद्धिमेति। पित्तात्मकोऽअनवपुश्च भवेदसाध्यः कृच्छाश्च मर्मसु भवन्ति हि सर्व एव॥ २५ ॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने विसर्पनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ५२॥ मधुकोशः साध्यत्वदिकमाह-सिध्यन्तीत्यादि। पित्तात्मकोऽञनवपुरिति अत्यन्तमुद्रिक्तपित्तोऽञनसमवर्णतनुः, अग्नि- विसर्पाख्यो न साध्य इति व्याख्यानयन्ति। कृच्छाश्च मर्मेस्विति असाध्यत्वेन कृच्छत्वं बोद्धव्यम्। यदाह। भोजः- वर्ज्यस्तु क्षतजस्तेषां सन्निपातातु यो भवेत्। भिषजा जानता त्याज्याः सर्व एव तु मर्मजाः' इति॥ २५॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां विसर्पनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥ ५२ ॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 14):

वातिकलक्षणमाह परीत्यादि । परिहष्टदन्त इति अम्लभक्षणेनेव ।। ।। कट्वम्लमुष्णं विरसं च पूति पित्तेन विद्यात्-- पैत्तिकलक्षणमाहकट्वित्यादि । कटुशब्दोऽत्र तिक्तवाची । यदाह विदेहःपित्तेन तिक्तास्य-विदाहकृत् स्यात् स्वाद्वास्य-हल्लासकरः कफेन । इति । - -
answer_text: In the above passage starting from the term pari etc., the symptom of the vātaja variety of arocaka has been described. The symptom parihrsta danta indicates a morbid feeling of sour taste. This symptom has been identified as the disease dantaharsa. Pitta type of arocaka n - (CS. Ci. S. 26.125) Bitter and sour taste, warmth and bad smell is there in the mouth in the pittaja type. In the above passage starting from the term katu etc., the symptom of the pittaja variety of arocaka has been described. The term kaṭu indicates the morbid feeling of bitter taste. As suggested by Videha there is the feeling of bitter taste in the mouth due to vitiation of pitta while the taste of mouth appears sweet and there is a vomiting- tendency in case there is vitiation of kapha
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 14.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 69, verse 28):

मधुकोशः गुणहीनतामेव कार्येण दर्शयति-वीर्याल्पभावादित्यादि। न निपातयेदिति न मारयति सद्यश्चिरेण वा । कफान्वितमिति कफान्वितं सत् मन्दीभूतौष्ण्यादिगुणं न मारयति। वर्षगणानुबन्धीति अपाकाच्चिरस्थायि। तेनार्दितो भिन्नपुरीषवर्ण इति तेन दूषीविषेणार्दितो भिन्नशब्दोऽत्र पुरीषवर्णाभ्यां प्रत्येकमभिसंबध्यते, भिन्नवर्णो विवर्णः । वैगन्ध्यवैरस्ययुत इति विरुद्धगन्धमुखवैरस्ययुत इति विरुद्धगन्धमुखवैरस्ययुक्तः । विचेष्टमानो विरुद्धां चेष्टा कुर्वन्, अरतिमसुखं लभते॥ २६–२७॥ आमाशयस्थे कफवांतरोगी पक्राशयस्थेऽनिलपित्तरोगी। भवेत् 'समुद्ध्वस्तशिरोरुहाड़ो विलूनपक्षस्तु' यथा विहङ्गः॥ २८॥ ( सु., क., २ )
answer_text: Na nipatayet means does not kill immediately or in due course of time. kaphānvita having associated with kapha - implies the reduction in the qualities of uṣṇa (heat) etc., by which also it does not kill. Varṣagaṇānubandhi means due to not being digested, it stays in the body. Bhinna purisavarana - diarrhoea and discolouration. Bhinna, here, relates to purīṣa (faecal matter) and varṇa (colour of the body). Vaigandhya vairasyayuta means has different smell and perceives the food in different tastes. Vicestamano doing unnatural body activity; arati restlessness-displeasure. 26, 27. The effect of dūṣiviṣa as per its locus standi When dūṣiviṣa is seated in the āmāśaya (stomach), it makes the individual suffer from kapha-vata disorders and when it takes shelterin the pakvasaya (intes¬ tines) it causes vāta pitta diseases and the hairs fall down from head and body due to which the individual looks like a bird that has withered wings. 28. (Su.Ka. 2)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 69, verse 28.

question:

दक्षं प्रजापतिं स्वस्थमश्विनौ वाक्यमूचतुः । कुतो हरीतकी जाता तस्यास्तु कति जातयः ।।१।। रसाः कति समाख्याताः कति चोपरसाः स्मृताः । नामानि कति चोक्तानि किं वा तासां च लक्षणम् ।।२।। के च वर्णा गुणाः के च का च कुत्र प्रयुज्यते । केन द्रव्येण संयुक्ता कांश्च रोगान्व्यपोहति ।।३।। प्रश्नमेतद्यथापृष्टं भगवन्वक्तुमर्हसि । अश्विनोर्वचनं श्रुत्वा दक्षो वचनमब्रवीत् ।।४।। पपात बिन्दुर्मेदिन्यां शक्रस्य पिबतोऽमृतम् । ततो दिव्यात्समुत्पन्ना सप्तजातिर्हरीतकी ।।५।।
answer_text: Some time in the distant past Aśvini Kumar’s physician of the dieties processed towards Lord Dakṣa prajapati and mentioned about Harītakī in the following way, what is the source of Harītakī? What number of name are there? How many primary tastes are existing in it? How many are the Sub-ordinante taste? What are the different qualities of them? What are the different colours? What are the different kinds of Harītakī and which type should utilized in illness? Associate with which other drug, it have the potential to cure which illness?: By heard these above question patiently Lord Dakşa answered, When master indra was drinking Amṛṭā, one drop had tumbled from his mouth on the earth from this one drop of Amṛṭā seven kinds of Harītakī appeared

explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 10.

answer_text: Speech disorders: Musk along with equal parts of Elā, Lavaṅga, Tvak and Kharjura and made into linctus with madhu indicated in Swarabheda (Horaseness of voice) and Mookatwa (speechless). Mental illness: Musk is prescribed in spasmodic diseases such as Apatantraka (Hysteria), Apasmāra (Epilepsy) and Jalasantrāsa (Hydrophobia), predominantly in the form of tincture or powders along with other drinks. Sexual dysfunction: As an Vrsya (Aphrodisiac), it is given in combination with other Vrsya (Aphrodisiac) drugs in Sukradourbalya (Seminal weakness) and Vandhyatva (Impotency). Mental illness: It is used as an nervine sedative in Apasmāra (Epilepsy), Unmadā (Insanity) in childrens. Matra (Dosage): Cūrna: 125- 500mg., Tincture: 10-30 drops. LATĀ KAȘTŪRĪ Latin: Hibiscus abelmoschus Linn. Fam: Malvaceae Hin: Lal Kasturi, Musk dana ng: Musk mallow A STATE AND A STATE BHĀVAPRAKĀŠA NIGHANTU AND A STATE AND A STATE Guna karma (Properties and indications): It is Tikta (Bitter) and Madhura (Sweet) in taste, Laghu (Light for digestion), Sītavīrya (Cold in polency), Chakṣuṣyā (Good for eyes), Chedana (cutting in nature), cures diseases of Kapha, Tṛṣṇā (Thrist), Basti roga ( Bladder diseases) and Mukha roga (Diseases of oral cavity). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is most common in hotter parts of India. Botanical description (Swarūpa): A small shrub grows upto 60-90 cm in height. Leaves are cordate, plamate 3 to 7 lobed, crenate-serrate or serrated margins and hairy on both surfaces. Flowers solitary, 7.5-10 cm across, yellow in colour. Fruits are capsule 6 to 7.5 cm long, hairy, oblong-lanceolate. Seeds flat & blackish exists odour like Kasturi. Prayojya anga (Part used): Patra (Leaves) Mūla (Roots) Chemical constituents: Resin, Crystalline substance, Gums, Albumin and Volatile oils

answer_text: Cardiac aliments: The powder of the root is efficacious. Respiratory diseases: The powder of the root of choraka is given with Madhu to treat Kāsa (Cough) and Swāsa (Dysponea). External uses: Choraka is applied externally over skin diseases like Dadru (Eczema), Kaṇḍū (Itching) etc. The root powder is used as an antitode in Sarpaviṣa (Snake bite), Vṛśchikaviṣa (Scorpion posion) etc., insect bites both externally and Internally. Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrna: 1-6 gms. TĀLĪSA PATRAM Latin: Abies webbiana Linn. Fam: Pinaceae Hin: Talispatra Eng: Himalayan silver, Silver fir Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Patradhya and Dhātrīpatra. Guna karma (Properties and indications): Tālīsa patra is Laghu (Light for digestion), Tīkṣṇa (Penetrating) and Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), It cures Swāsa (Dysponea), Kāsa (Cough), Diseases of Kapha and Vāta, Aruchi (Aneroxia), Gulma (Abdominal tumors), Ama (Undigested food), Agnimāndya (Dyspepsia) and Kṣaya roga (Wasting diseases). Note: The leaf of various drugs has claimed as Tālīsapatrm, according to their different habitats by several different scholars. Abies webbenia is the most commonly used as Tālīsapatra. S.no Leaf of various drugs Different habitats by the scholars Flacourtia cataphracta Roxb. Accepted by ancient scholars. Cinnamomum tamal Nees & Eberum, Southern part of india. Taxus baccata Linn. Uttra pradesh, Maharastra, Gujrat etc. Abies webbiana Lindl. Bengal etc. Rhododendron anthopogon D. Don. 1. Nepal, Punjab, etc. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Found in Himalayas from Kashmir to Assam at altitude of 1600-4500 m. Swarūpa (Botanical description): A tall evergreen tree attain at the height of 150 ft with long horizantally spreading branches. Bark brownish, rough, young shoots are clothed with short brown hairs. Leaves 1-2 inch long, distichous arranged (Phyllotaxy ½ or 2 ranked), upper surface of the leaf is rusty brown, while it is mealy white on under surface. Fruit are in cones, male cones arranged spirally in bunches, while female in short axis many small thin dry brownish scales. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Patra. Chemical Constituents: Essential oils, alkaloids

सौभाग्य टङ्कण क्षार धातुद्रावकमुच्यते । टङ्कण वह्निकृद्दृक्षं कफहद्वातपित्तकृत् ।। २५.६ ।।
answer_text: Respiratory diseases: In case of Swāsa (Dysponea), Swasānalikaśotha (Bronchitis) and Kāsa (Cough) etc., Inhalation of fumes of Potassium nitrate gives great relief External uses: It is applied in the form of cold and agreeable loation in case of Headace associated with Jvara (Fever)and Tandrā (Delirium). In Amavāta (Rheumatic ace's), a strong suspention of Potassium nitrate applied externally to swollen and painful joints. Mātrā (Dosage): 250 mg - 1gm. Note: It has become contraversial identity, some identifies it as Potassi nitras, while some has equated with Karpūra śilājatu. As per Bhāvamiśra calls it is a variety of Svarjikā and also has similar properties. Inhalation of fumes with caution, it may prove too irritating. TANKANA KSĀRA Latin: Sodii Biros. Hin: Sohag Eng: Borax, Sodium borate Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Soubhāgya and Dhatudrāvaka. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Tankaṇa is Dīpana (Appetizers), Rūkṣā (Drying), Subsides Kapha doṣa and Increses Vāta and Pitta, Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Hilly region of Himalayas, Kashmir, Srilanka especially Tibet. It is also obtained in the mud of lakes surrounded by the hills in Nepal. Qualties: Resemble like spaika, shiny, transparent, white odorless, crystalline solid, salty in taste, watery part evapoured on exposure to intence heat leaves behind dry crystalline molted substance

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 33, verse 26):

मधुकोशः उपेक्षया हि पित्तकफाजानामपि मधुमेहत्वं प्रर्वशयितुमाह-सर्व एवेत्यादि। धातुक्षयावरणाभ्यां कुपितवातेन मधुमेहसंभवमाह-मधुमेह 'इत्यादि। मधुसममिति। 'मूत्रम्' इति शेषः । स इति मधुमेहः सावरणालिङ्गमाह-आवृत इत्यादि। आवृत इति। आवृतवातकृतः। दोषलिङ्ग़नीति। येन पित्तादिना आवृतस्तस्य वातस्य च लिङ्ग़नि प्रदर्शयति। अनिमित्तमकस्मात्। क्षणात् क्षणात्पूर्ण इति। आवरणेन पुनः पूर्णो भवन् कृच्छ्साध्यो भवति। तथा च-चरकः-‘स मारुतस्य पित्तस्य कफस्य च मुहुर्मुहुः। दर्शयत्याकृतिं गत्वा क्षयमाप्याय्यते पुनः॥’ (च. सू. अ. १७) इति। धातुक्षयकुपितवातजस्य तु केवलवातजमेव लिङ्कम्। गदाधरस्त्वाह-'मधुमेहः सावरणवायुनैव क्रियते।’ यदाह-चरकः-‘तैरावृतगतिर्वायुरोज आदाय गच्छति। यदा बस्ति तदा कृच्छो मधुमेहः प्रवर्तते।’ (च. सू. अ. १७) इति। केवलवातजेष् तु कषायादिवमनाद्यतियोगादिकृतेष् धातुक्षयजेष् वायोरावरणं नास्तीति भेदः। मधुमेह शब्दप्रवृत्तिमाह-मधुरं यच्च मेहेष्वित्यादि॥ २३-२६॥ मधुरं यच्च मेहेषु प्रायो मध्विव मेहति। सर्वेऽपि मधुमेहाख्या माधुर्याच्च तनोरतः॥ २६॥ ( वा. नि. १० )
answer_text: To make it clear that leaving without treating the pitta and kapha pramehas make them also madhumeha - this stanza, “sarva eva pramehāstu….” is mentioned here. Madhumeha occurs due to aggravated vata either by emaciation of tissues or by obstruction or covering caused by other dosa or dhatus. The adjective madhu samaṃ (eqreal to or like honey) is applicable to the urine. It manifests the Vāta symptoms and also those of the covering dosa - pitta or kapha; without any reason - means suddenly. At one moment the manifestation of vāṭa is weakness and at another moment is full which makes the situation incurable. In Caraka also, it is mentioned, “The pitta and kapha- signs along with those of vāta are exposed fully and t disappear momentarily” (Ca.Sū. 17). The vātaja madhumeha caused by emaciation of tissues will have only vāta signs. Gadādhara holds that madhumeha is caused by only - āvṛtavāta (vāta that is covered or obstructed by other doṣas). As said by Carak, Vayu, when obstructed by the other dosas (and dusyas) carries the ojas - the essential immunity factor of the body and when brought to the urinary bladder, madhumeha, the incurable disease is manifested”. (Ca. Sū. 17). In the disease caused by the vata, aggravated due to excessive purifactory measures and emaciation of the tissues, there is no obstruction or covering of Vata by the other factors. 23-25. Reason for nomenclature of prameha as madhumeha Generally in all pramehas the individual passes urine that is sweet in taste and looks like honey and his body also gets sweetened, hence the name madhumeha is given to all these pramehas. 26. (Vā. Ni. 10)
