question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 56):

मधुकोशः सान्निपातिकलक्षणमाह-सकृदित्यादि। सकृदिति कदाचिद्विकृतिवशादेवं भवति अनेकापिडिकाचिताविति वातादिवेदनान्वितबहुपिण्डकौ, अनेकवर्णपिडकाचितावित्यन्ये; अनेकाश्च वर्णा वातादीना कृष्णपीतश्चेता; अत्र पक्षे सकृत्कृष्णावित्यादिपिडकातोऽन्यत्र कल्पनीयम्॥ ५॥ खर्जूरफलवर्णाभिः पिडकाभिर्निपीडितौ । रक्तोपसृष्टौ रुधिरं स्त्रवतः शोणितप्रभौ ॥ ६ ॥ ( सु.नि. १६ ) मधुकोशः रक्तजमाह-खर्जरेत्यादि। खर्जूरफलवर्णाभिरित्येनेन वर्णमात्रेणैवसाधर्म्य प्रतिपाद्यते, यदि तु सर्वात्मना साधर्म्यमभीष्ट स्यात्, तदा ‘खर्जूरफलतुल्याभिः’ इत्येवोच्येत। रक्तोपसृष्टाविति रक्तदूषितौ ॥ ६ ॥ गुरू स्थूलौ मांसदुष्टौ मांसपिण्डवदुहतौ। जन्तवश्चात्र मूर्च्छन्ति नरस्योभयतो मुखात्॥ ७॥ ( सु.नि. १६ ) मधुकोशः मांसजमाह-गुरू स्थूलावित्यादि। जन्तवश्चात्र मूर्च्छन्तीति क्रिमयोऽप्यत्र उच्छिता भवन्ति। उभयतो मुखा- दिति। मुखविवरमपेक्ष्योभयभागयोः, सुक्कणीप्रदेशयोरिति यावत्। मुखादिति ल्यब्लोपे पञ्चमी। ‘उभयतोमुखा’ इति पाठान्तरे उभयसृक्कणीभागो मुखमाश्रयो येषां ते तथा। द्विमुखा इत्यन्ये॥ ७॥ सर्पिर्मण्डप्रतीकाशौं मेदसा कण्डुरौ गुरू। अच्छं स्फटिकसंकाशमास्त्रावं स्त्रवतो भूशम्॥ ८॥ तयोब्रणो न संरोहेन्मृदुत्वं च न गच्छति। ( सु.नि. १६ ) मधुकोशः मेदोजमाह-सर्पिर्मण्डप्रतीकाशवित्यादि। सर्पिर्मण्डप्रतीकाशाविति सर्पिर्मण्डो घृतस्योपरितनः स्वच्छभागः, तत्प्रतीकाशौ तत्सदूशौं। तयोरिति तादृदशयोः॥ ८॥ क्षतजाभौ विदीर्येते पाट्येते चाभिघाततः॥ ९॥ ग्रथितौ च तथा स्यातामोष्ठौ कण्डूसमन्वितौ। ( सु.नि. १६ ) मधुकोशः अमिघातजमाह-क्षतजाभावित्यादिना। अत्र कफरक्तयोरप्यनुबन्धो बोद्धव्यः। यद्क्त भोजे, 'क्षतावभिहतौ वापि रक्तावोष्ठौ सवेदनौ। भवतः सपरिस्रावौ कफरक्तप्रदूषितौ’–इति। वायुरप्यत्राभिघाताल्लभ्यते, अयं चाभिघातजशोथाद्यथोक्तलक्षणकारणभेदेन तथा वातिकौष्ठप्रकोपादपि कफरक्तरूपहेतुभेदयोगाद्विद्यते॥ ९॥ शोणितं दन्तवेष्टेभ्यो यस्याकस्मात्प्रवर्तते। दुर्गन्धीनि सकृष्णानि प्रक्लेदीनि मृदूनि च॥ १०॥ दन्तमांसानि शीर्यन्ते पचन्ति च परस्परम्। शीतादो नाम स व्याधिः कफशोणितसंभवः॥ ११॥
answer_text: Sakrt means - sometimes it occurs (as per the dosa-predominance). Aneka Mukha Roga Nidāna pidakācitau - full of papules of various types means - full of papules of vāta etc., natured pain etc.. Some interpret as full of papules of different colours. The different colour of vāta etc., are black, yellow and white and in this case it can be inter¬ preted that both lips are filled with black papules or yellow papules or some times white papules. 5 Raktaja type of lip-disease Both the lips when afflicted by vitiated blood, become painful due to vesicles of palm- date colour; there will be blood oozing from them and there will be lustre in this lips like that of blood. 6. (Su. Ni. 16). Here the comparison of lips to palm-dates is with regards to the colour only. If it is to compare the complete shape, size etc., the statement would have been Kharjuraphalatulyabhih" meaning "equal to the palm-dates". Raktopasrsta means vitiated by blood. 6. Māmsaja type of lip-disease Both lips become heavy, thick, swollen and look like big pieces of muscle/ meat due to vitiation of māṃsa dhāṭu. There will be worms on both ends of the mouth. 7. (Su. Ni. 16). There will be worms on both sides/ends of the mouth which are called Sṛkkaṇī. Some say, “from both mouths” (dvimukhā). 7. Medoja type of lip-disease Mādhavanidānaṃ When there is vitiation of medas, the lips have the lustre like that of superna¬ tant part of ghee and with itching sensation. There will be profuse exudation that is crystal clear and the ulcers on the lips do not heal and even they do not become soft. 8. (Su. Ni. 16). The sarpimanda is the supernatant clear part of the stored ghee. Tayoh means that look like. 8. Abhighātaja type of lip-diseases Due to injury, both the lips are cut apart and the injured area becomes hard and knotty with itching sensation. 9. (Su. Ni. 16). The association of kapha and rakta in this context also is to be understood. As said by Bhojā, “Both the lips when cut or inujured, become red, painful and there is discharge due to vitiation of kapha and rakta”. Vāta involvement is already there that props up due to injury. This condition is different from Abhighātajā śotha and also vātika type of lip disease - due to involvement of kapha and rakta in aetiology and symptomatology. 9. Diseases of the root of the teeth Śītāda When there is sudden oozing of blood from the gums and they become black, bad odoured, discharging and spongy; the gums become thin by withering and ulceration takes place, such condition is called Sītāda caused due to vitiation of kapha and rakta 10, 11. (Su. Ni. 16)

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Mamsa Varga, Chapter 10, verse 915):

कालकण्ङ्गकहारीतकपोत शतपत्रकाः । पारावतः खझरीटः पिकाद्याः प्रतुदाः स्मृताः । प्रतुद्य भक्षयन्त्येते तुण्डेन प्रतुदास्ततः ।। २३.। प्रतुदा मधुराः पित्तकफघ्नास्तुवरा हिमाः । लघवो बद्धवर्चस्काः किश्चिद्वातकराः स्मृताः ।।१४।। काको गृध्र उलूकश्च चिल्लश्च शशघातकः । चाषो भासश्च कुरर इत्याद्याः प्रसहाः स्मृताः ।।२५।। प्रसहाः कीत्तिता एते प्रसह्याच्छिद्य भक्षणात् । । २६ । । प्रसहाः खलु वीर्योष्णास्तन्मास भक्षयन्ति ये । ते शोषभस्मकोन्मादशुक्रक्षीणा भवन्ति हि ।।१७।।
answer_text: Pratuda are the birds which takes food with the help of beaks. They are Kālakanṭhaka, Hārīṭa, Kapōṭa, Saṭapaṭraka, Pārāvāṭa, Khañījarīṭa, Pīka etc. Guna karma (Properties and indications): Pratuda meat is Madhura (Sweet) in taste, subsides Pitta and kapha, Kaṣāya (Astringent), Ṣīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Laghu (Light for digestion), Bhaddavarchaka (Causes constipation) and slightly increases vāta. Prasaha (Animals which takes food by attacking and snatching). Prasaha are birds which take food by attacking and snatching. It includes Kāka, Ulūka, Cilla, Sasaghātaka, Cāṣa, Bhāsa, Kurara etc. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Prasaha meat is Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), those who consume, they become Soşa (Emaciated), suffer from Bhasmaka roga (Bulimia), Unmadā (Insanity) and Sukrakṣaya (Decreases seman)
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Mamsa Varga, Chapter 10, verse 915
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Mamsa Varga, Chapter 10, verse 915.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 13):

वातिकमाह वातेनेत्यादि । कृष्णत्वं मूत्रादिषु स्वरभेदारम्भकदोषस्य सर्वङ्ग- व्यापकत्वात् अर्शोवत् । भिन्नं भिन्नस्वरं तदेवाह गर्दभवत् खरमिति खरं निष्ठाम् उद्वेजकमिति यावत् ।। पित्तेन पीतनयनानन-मूत्र-वर्चा ब्रूयाद्गलेन दाहसमन्वितेन ॥॥ - -
answer_text: The passage starting from vatena refers to the characteristics of the disease as originating through the vāta. In condition of this disease, there appears blackness in the urine of the patient. This is due to the disease-initiating dosa, i.e. vata that prevails in the whole body as in the case of the arsa or piles. It makes the voice sound very dry and irritating, something akin to a donkey’s voice. Pitta type of svarabheda (SS. Ut. 53.4) In the paittika type of hoarseness, the patient’s eyes, face, urine and stool turn yellowish. Moreover, while speaking he gets a burning sensation in the throat. 2

question:
Transliterate and give the contextual import of the following line from Sharangadhara Samhita — Uttarakhanda, Chapter 12, verse 12.5:

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 611):

आध्रातकः पीतनश्च मर्कटाप्रः कपीतनः । आध्रातमम्ल वातघन गुरूष्णा रुचिकृत्सरम् ।।१९।। पक्कनु तुवर स्वादु रसे पाके हिम स्मृतम् । तर्पणं श्लेष्मलं स्निग्थं वृष्यं विष्टम्भि बुंहणम ।। गुरु बल्य मरुत्पित्तक्षतदाहक्षयास्त्रजित् । । २० । ।
answer_text: Digestive disease: In Atisarā (Diarrhoea) a decoction of the kernel is given alone or in combination with Bilwa and Sunthī. Decoction of Amra and Jambu added with honey alleviates all types of Chardi (Vomiting) and Trsnā (Thrist). Menustral diseases and Vaginal discharges: A Infusion of the bark is used in Pradara (Meno-Metroghia), Sveta Pradara (Leucorrhoea). Respiratory disease: Smoke of the burning leaves is useful in Galaroga (Diseases of thoat) and Hikkā (Hiccup). Haemorrhages: In case of Pupusa Raktasträva (Lung haemorrhage) and Antragata raktastrava (Intestinal bleeding) the juice of the fresh bark administered with egg yolk or Ahiphena. Mātrā (Dosage): Swarasa: 10 - 20 ml, Kwātha: 50 - 100 ml, Bīja cūrna: 3 - 6 g. ĀMRĀTAKA Fam: Anacardiaceae Latin: Spondias pinnata Kurz. Eng: Indian hog plum Hin: Ambada Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Pūtanā, Markaṭāmra and Kapītana. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Āmrāta is Amla (Sour) in taste, subsides vāta, Guru (Heavy for digestion), Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), Rucya (Promotes taste) and Sāra (Laxative). Pakwa phalā is Kaṣāya (Astringent) and Madhurā (Sweet in taste), Madhurā vipāka (Sweet in post digestive), Sīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Santarpaṇa (Nourishing), Increas-U es Kapha, Snigdha (Oilyness), Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac), Viṣṭambi (Causes constipation), Brhmaṇa (Stoutning), Guru (Heavy for digestion) and Balya (Promotes strength). It cures diseases of Vāta, Pitta, Kṣhata (Injury), Dāha (Burning sensation), Kṣaya (Emaciation) and Diseases of Rakta. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is found throughout india. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a small tree reaches upto 10-15 m. Leaves are compound 30-40 cm long, leaflets 5-11 oppositely arranged ovate-oblong to elliptic-oblong, 7-12 cm long, 4-5 cm wide, papery. Leaf tapering apex, base is wedge- rounded, margin toothed or entire. Flowers are small, sessile, white, borne in panicles at the end of branches, 25-35 cm long. Fruit- Drupe, ellipsoid to elliptic-ovoid, yellowish orange at maturity, Seeds 1-3. Prayojya anga (Part used): Apakwa phala (Unripened fruit). Chemical constituents: β -sitosterol, β-amyrins, lignoceric acid, L-arabinose, D-galactose and galacturonic acid
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 611
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 611.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 23):

पादयोजातमप्रतिक्रियमाण देशान्तरं व्याप्नोति पादवद्वस्तयोरपि भवतीति दर्शयन्नाह पादयोरित्यादि । आखोर्विषमित्यनेन मन्दविसर्पितां दर्शितवान एतद्वातरक्ते चरकेण द्विविध- मुक्तम् । यदाह उत्तानमथ गम्भीरं द्विविधं वातशोणितम् । त्वङ्र्मासाश्रयमुत्तानं गम्भीरं त्वन्तराश्रयम् ।। व०चि० इति । सुश्रुतेन तु कुष्ठवदुत्पत्ती उत्तानस्योत्तरकाल गम्भीरत्वमुक्तमिति मतभेद इव आजानु स्फुटितं यच्च प्रभिन्नं प्रस्नुतं च यत् । यज्जुष्टं का प्राण-मांसक्षयादिभिः ॥१ ॥ उपद्रवैश्व वातरक्तमसाध्यं का स्याद्याप्यं का संवत्सरोत्थितम् । -
answer_text: To show the slow spreading nature it is compared to ākhuviṣa or rat’s poison. Caraka classified this disease into two, as he states, vātarākta is of two types, i.e 1. Uttāna that is rooted in the skin and muscle tissues and 2. Gambhira is the type that originates from the deeper strata of the body. (CS. Ci. 29.19). Suśruta on other hand, states that the initial stage of this disease is to be called Uttāna (as in the case of kustha). According to the seer, the gambhīra is to be considered as the advanced stage. Thus, in his opinion the terms uttāna and gambhīra signify different stages of the same disease while Caraka takes them as indicative of two different diseases. Prognosis of vātarakta SS. Ni. 1. 49) That case of vātarakta is difficult to cure in which the skin is cracked up to the knee, skin is cut off and there is exudation associated with complication, like emaciation of energy and muscle tissue. This cdondition is incurable while the case that has completed one year of duration is yapya (It can be prolonged).14
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 23.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 1):

उक्तनिदानपञ्चकस्य का रोगनिवृत्तिलक्षणसिद्धिहेतृत्वेनावश्यंका का ज्ञातव्यतामाह तस्मादित्यादि । उद्धतां बुद्धविषयत्वेन महतीम । विनिष्टयो निदानमिति । अथ वक्ष्यमाण- विकारेष् प्रकृतिसमसमवायविकृतिविपमसमवायादिज्ञानाथं चरकोक्ता वातादिगुणा लिख्यन्ते रूक्षः शीतो लघुः सुक्ष्मध्यलोऽथविशदः खरः । विपरीतपणेद्रव्येमर्कतः सम्प्रशाम्यति सस्नेहमुष्णं तीक्ष्यं च द्रवमम्लं सर्र कट्ट । विपरीतमर्णीः पित्त द्रव्येराशु प्रशाम्यति ग्रुशीतमुद्दस्निग्धमध्रस्थिरपिच्छिलाः । श्लेष्मणः प्रशर्म यान्ति विपरीतमुणेरुणाः इति च०सू० इति श्रीविजयरक्षितकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां पञ्चनिदानलक्षणं समाप्तम् ॥१ ॥ - - -
answer_text: ( ) = The above passage is by nature a summary of what has been stated in the present chapter. It emphasizes the importance of knowing the diagnosis of the diseases in alleviating the diseases. In order to achieve that purpose, one should know the diagnosis of the diseases, going to be dealt with in this book. This erudite observation of the present text is significant as it embodies the nidana paficaka including the factors relating to roga laksana as well as the roga nivrii which allow one to actualize the treatment. Viniscaya is Pañca Nidāna Lakṣanam nothing but the nidāna (diagnosis) only. For the sake of additional knowledge and the additional types of vitiations including the so¬ named Prakṛti samasamavāya (compatible) and Vikṛtiviṣamasama- vaya (incompatible) qualities, one could refer to Caraka which details the qualities and the incompatibility of vāta, pitta and kapha (Ca. Sii. 1.58-60).. In brief it is mentioned there that the väta is dry, cool, light (in weight), subtle, mobile, vivid and rough; it is pacified by things possessing qualities that are antagonistic to these features. As regards the pitta, it is said to be oily, hot, fast, liquid, sour, mobile, and pungent; it is pacified by use of the drugs possessing opposite qualities. Similarly, the kapha is alleged to be heavy, cool, soft, smooth, sweet, static and sticky, it is brought down by drugs and foods which have opposite qualities. (Ca. Sū. 1.58-60) Thus concludes the first Chapter named Pañcanidāna Lakṣaṇaṃ

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 4):

पेत्तिकग्रहण्या निदानसम्प्राप्तिपूर्वकं रूपमाह कट्वित्यादि । विदाहि विदाहजनकं वंशकरीरादि । क्षारोऽपामार्गादिकृतः तथा क्षारो यवक्षारादिः तथा सक्षारं च द्रव्यं क्षारोदक- साधित हि व्यज्जनमश्नन्ति कामरूपार्दी । आद्यप्रहणल्लवणतीक्ष्णोष्णानां ग्रहणं तैर्वृद्धं पित्तम नलमाप्लावयदभिभवत्तं हन्ति । ननु पित्तमाग्नेयमग्निरेव वा ततश्व वृद्धिमेवाप्लोति कथं हन्त्यत आहजलं तप्तमिवानलमिति । यथोष्णयुणयुक्तमपि जलमनलं हन्ति तथा द्रवांशेन परिवृद्धं पितमूष्मरूपमग्नि हन्त्येवेति । स पीताभः पुरुषः सार्यते वर्चः इत्यनुवर्तते ॥-॥ गुर्वतिस्निग्ध-शीतादिभोजनादतिभोजनात् भुक्तमात्रस्य च स्वप्नाद्वन्त्यग्निं कुपितः कफः ॥ ॥ तस्यान्नं पच्यते दुःखं हल्लास-च्छर्द्यरोचकाः । आस्योपदेह-माधुर्यंकास-ष्ठीवन-पीनसाः मन्यते हैं स्त्यानमुदरंश स्त्रिमितंश स्त्यागुरु । हदयं मधुर का उद्गारः सदनं स्त्रीष्वहर्षणम् ॥१ ॥ दृष्टो भिन्नामश्लेष्मसंसुष्टगुरुवर्चःप्रवर्तनम् अक्रशस्यापि दौर्बल्यमालस्यंक चार कफात्मके ॥ ॥ - - - - -
answer_text: This passage is meant to suggest the symptoms, pathogen, and characteristics of the disease grahanī. The term vidahi means the substances that cause a burning sensation. Such substances include the plant vamśakarīra and the like. The term kṣāra refers to the alkali prepared with the plant Apāmarga and Yavakṣāra (potassium bicarbonate) and the food that is prepared with alkalis. Such dishes are used in the region called Kāmarūpa or Assam. Application of the term ‘Adi’ (etc.), has been done here to include the very salty, fast and very warm foods among the items that produce the disease grahanī. This type of foodstuffs provokes the pitta that in turn overshadows the digestive fire and diminishes the same., Now the question arises as to when pitta itself is fiery, how can it eliminate or diminish the digestive fire? The situation could be visualized in terms of the reality that the consumption of the above types of foodstuff provokes only the liquid part of pitta and though it is warm in quality the liquid has the capacity of extinguishing the fire that comes in its contact. It may be remembered that even warm water could extinguish the fire. Kapha type of Grahanīroga 111 4 11 (CS. Ci. 15.67-70) The kapha which is increased by heavy, very oily and very cold foods and by over-eating and sleeping immediately after eating. This habit destroys the digestive fire. Consequently individual’s diet is digested with difficulty; he has nausea, vomiting, distaste, sticky sensation and sweetness in the mouth, cough, salivation, coryza, gripping sensation in the heart, heaviness and stability in the abdomen, sweet and stinking belching. There is, moreover, loss of appetite and the individual has no desire for the company of women. He defecates in fragments accompanied with phlegm and his stool remains heavy in nature. He gets debilitated though not emaciated and he remains non¬ enthusiastic. These features are seen in the kapha type of graham- roga. 13-16

answer_text: Fam: Verbenaceae. Latin: Angelica glauca Edgw. Hin: Bhateur. Eng: Angelica. Paryāyanāma (Synonymes): Niśacara, Dhanahara, Kitara, Gaṇahāsaka, Saṅkita, Canda, Duspatra, Ksēmaka and Ripu. Guna karma (Properties and indications): Choraka is Madhura (Sweet), Tikta (Bitter) and Kaṭu (Pungent) in taste, Kaṭu in vipaka (Pungent in post digestion), Laghu (Light for digestion), Tīkṣṇa (Penetrating), Hṛdya (Beneficial for heart) and Sīta vīrya (Cold in potency). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Extending form Western Himalayas from Kashmir to Shimla at an altitude of 8000-10, 000 ft. Swarūpa (Botanical description): A glabrous herb reaches upto 1-3m. Leaves usually large 1-3 pinnate, leaflets often in three, ovate-lanceolate, sharply toothed margins, upper surface dark green, lower glaucous. question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Visa-Upavisa Varga, Chapter 7, verse 728):

तारमाक्षिकमन्यत्तु तद्धवेद् रजतोपमम् । किश्चिद्रजतसाहित्यात्तारमाक्षिकमीरितम् अनुकल्पतया तस्य ततो हीनगुणाः स्मृताः । न केवलं रूप्यगुणा यतः स्यात्तारमाक्षिकम् ।।६३।। स्वादु पाके रसे किश्चित्तिक्तं वृष्यं रसायनम । चक्ष्मष्यं वस्तिरुक्कुष्ठपाण्डुमेहविषोदरान् । अर्शः १ शोथं क्षयङ्कण्डूं त्रिदोषमपि नाशयेत् ।।६४।। मन्दानलत्वं बलहानिम्मयां विष्टाम्भितां नेत्रगदान्सकृष्ठान् । तथैव मालां व्रणपूर्विकाञ्ठ करोति तापीजमिदञ्ठ तद्वत्। । ६ ५ । ।
answer_text: lt is also know as Rupyamākṣika. It contain silver in little ratio hence it is called Tāmramākṣika. It doesn’t exhibit only silver like properties, it has also got properties of other metals in major amount. Guṇa karma (Properties and indication): Tāmramākṣika is Madhura (Sweet) and Tiktā (Bitter) in taste, Madhura vipāka (Sweet in post digestive), Vṛṣyaʾ (Aphrodisiac), Rāsayana (Rejuvenators) and Cakṣuṣya (Good for eyes).It cures Basti roga (Diseases of bladder), Kuṣṭa (Leprosy), Pāṇḍu (Anemia), Prameha (Diabeties), Viṣa (Posionous manifestations), Arśas (Piles), Sotha (Inflammation), Kṣaya (Wasting disease), Kaṇḍū (Itching) and Diseases of Tridosas. Aushuddha Tāmramākṣika doṣa (Diseases leads to consumption of Impure Iron pyrite): Consumption of impure Tāmramākṣika leads to Agnimāndya (Dyspepsia), Balahina ARTING DHÄTU-UPADHÄTU-RATNA-UPARANTA-VIŞA-UPAVIŞA VARGA (Loss of weight), Vistambī (Constipation), Netraroga (Eye diseases), Kuṣṭa (Leprosy), Kantmala (Lymphedinitits) etc
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Visa-Upavisa Varga, Chapter 7, verse 728
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Visa-Upavisa Varga, Chapter 7, verse 728.
context: तारमाक्षिकमन्यत्तु तद्धवेद् रजतोपमम् । किश्चिद्रजतसाहित्यात्तारमाक्षिकमीरितम् अनुकल्पतया तस्य ततो हीनगुणाः स्मृताः । न केवलं रूप्यगुणा यतः स्यात्तारमाक्षिकम् ।।६३।। स्वादु पाके रसे किश्चित्तिक्तं वृष्यं रसायनम । चक्ष्मष्यं वस्तिरुक्कुष्ठपाण्डुमेहविषोदरान् । अर्शः १ शोथं क्षयङ्कण्डूं त्रिदोषमपि नाशयेत् ।।६४।। मन्दानलत्वं बलहानिम्मयां विष्टाम्भितां नेत्रगदान्सकृष्ठान् । तथैव मालां व्रणपूर्विकाञ्ठ करोति तापीजमिदञ्ठ तद्वत्। । ६ ५ । ।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 69, verse 34):

मधुकोशः तदेव नानाप्रकारं यद्यत्करोति तत्तदाह-उन्मादमन्यदित्यादि। क्षपयेच्च शुक्रमिति षाण्ढ्यं करोतीत्यर्थः । तांस्तानिति विसर्पविस्फोटकादीन् ॥ ३२॥ दूषितं देशकालान्नदिवास्वप्नैरभीक्ष्णशः । यस्मात् संदूषयेद्वातूँस्तस्माद् दूषीविषं स्मृतम्॥ ३३॥ साध्यमात्मवतः सद्यो याप्यं संवत्सरोत्थितम्। दूषीविषमसाध्यं स्यात् क्षीणस्याहितसेविनः॥ ३४॥ ( सु.क. २ )
answer_text: Kṣapayecca śukram means causes impotency. Tāṃstān-certain others means erysipelas, breaking of skin etc.. 32. question:

दिवास्वप्नादतिक्रोधाद् व्यायामादतिमैथुनात्। क्षताच्च नखदन्ताद्यैर्वाताद्याः कुपिता यदा ॥ १॥ पूयशोणितसंकाशं निकुचाकृतिसंनिभम्। जनयन्ति यदा योनौ नाम्ना कन्दः स योनिजः॥ २॥ ( सु.उ. ८ ) मधुकोशः योन्याश्रयत्वाद्योनिकन्दनिदानमाह-दिवास्वप्नादित्यादि। नखद्न्ताद्यैरित्यत्रादि शब्दात् कण्टकादिपरिग्रहः। वाताद्याः कुपिता इति यथानिदानं प्रत्येकं वातादयः कुपिताः। निकुंचाकृतिसंनिभमिति वर्तुलमित्यर्थः; अस्यानन्तरंगुडकमिति द्रष्टव्यं तेन नुपंसकलिङ्गता सङ्गता भवति। कन्दः प्रायेण जरन्नारीयोनिगतो निकुचाकारो रोगः ॥ १– २ ॥ रूक्षं विवर्ण ' स्फुटितं वातिकं तं विनिर्दिशेत्। दाहरागज्वरयुतं विद्यात् पित्तात्मकं तु तम्॥ ३॥ नीलपुष्पप्रतीकाशं कण्डूमन्तं कफात्मकम्। सर्वलिङ्गसमायुक्तं सन्निपातात्मकं विदुः ॥ ४॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने योनिकन्दनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ६३॥ मधुकोशः वातजादिभेदेन रूपमाह-रूक्षमित्यादि। नीलपुष्पप्रतीकाशमिति अतसी कुसुमवर्णम्। कफजेऽपि नीलता व्याधिप्रभावादेव; अन्ये तु पैत्तिकलक्षण एव सम्बध्नान्ति, योग्यत्वात् ॥ ३–४॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां योनिकन्दनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ६३॥
answer_text: Due to sleeping in day time, excessive anger, strenuous extcercise, excessive coitus, injury by nails and teeth the vāta etc., doṣas get aggravated and cause a round shaped abcess in the yoni (vagina) which resemble the shade of pus and blood, is called yonikanda. 1, 2. In continuation of the diseases of yoni, yonikanda nidana is explained. In saying nails and teeth etc., indicates thorns etc; also “vāta etc., on aggravation” means vāta etc. doṣas on being aggravated by their own reasons. Nikucākṛti means round shaped. Kanda is a round shaped growth in the vagina generally seen in aged women. Symptomatology of Yonikanda based on Tridosa Vata type of yonikanda is dry, discoloured and in broken condition. When there is burning sensation, redness and fever it should be known as paittika yonikanda. The kaphaja variety is in blue colour and associated with itching sensation. In sannipata variety, all the above symptoms are present. Mādhavanidānaṃ Thus ends the chapter on diagnosis of yonikanda in the Madhava's book of diagnosis written by Śrīmādhavakara. 63. Nīla puṣpapratīkāśaṃ means in the shade of a flower of atasī (Linum usitatissimum). The bluish colour even in kaphaja yonikanda is due to the nature of the disease. Others relate this symptoms to pittaja type of yonikanda as it suits the con¬ text. 3, 4. Thus ends the diagnosis of Yonikanda in Madhukosa commentary written by Srikanthadatta, 63. ＊＊＊＊
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 63.

क्रिमयश्च द्विधा प्रोक्ता बाह्याभ्यन्तरभेदतः । बहिर्मल-कफासृग्विड्जन्मभेदाच्चतुर्विधाः नामतो विंशतिविधा
answer_text: 111 II (AH, Sū. 14.42: 2, 43: 1, 43: 2) Krmis or worms are of two varieties, namely, the bahya (external) and ābhyantara (internal). question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Charaka Samhita (Chikitsasthana, Chapter 21, verse 33-34):

पित्तमुष्णोपचारेण विदाह्यम्छाशनैश्वितम् । दृष्यान् संदृष्य धमनीः पूरयन् वै विसर्पति ॥ ३१ ॥ तस्य रूपाणि ज्वरस्तुष्णा मूर्च्छा मोहइछर्दिररोचकोऽङ्गभेदः स्वेदोऽतिमाघमन्तद्वीहः प्रलापः शिरोहक चक्रषोराकुलत्वमस्वप्रमरतिश्रेमः शीतवातवारितर्षोऽतिमात्रं हरितहारिद्वनैत्रमूत्रवर्वर्वस्त्वं हरित- हारिद्ररूपदर्शनं च, यसिमध्यावकारी विसर्पोऽनुसपति सोऽवकाशस्ताम्रहरितहारिद्रनीळकृष्णरक्तानां वर्णा- नामन्यतमं पुष्यति, सोल्सेवैधातिमात्रं दाहसंभेदनपरीतैः स्फोटकैरुपचीयते तुल्यवर्णास्नावैरचिरपाकैश्व, निद्।नोकानि चास्य नोपशेरते विपरीतानि चोपशेरत इति पित्तविसर्पः॥ ३२ ॥ स्वाह्रम्छलवणजिग्धगुर्वन्नसंचितः । कफः संदूषयन् दृष्यान् छच्छ्मङ्गे विसर्पति ॥ ३३ ॥ तस्य रूपाणि – शीतकः शीतज्वरो – गौरवं निद्रा तन्द्राऽरोचको – मधुरास्यत्वमास्योपलैपो – निष्टीविका छर्दिराछस्य स्तैमित्यमझिनाशो दौर्बल्यं च, अयरिमध्यावकाशे विसर्पोऽचुसर्पति सोऽवकाशः श्वयथमान् पाण्डुर्नातिरक्तः ख्रेइस्तिस्तम्भगौरवैरन्वितोऽल्पवेदनःका क्रच्छपाकैश्चिरकारिभिवेहुळत्वगुपलेपैः स्फोटैः श्वेतपाण्ड्रभिरतबध्यते, प्रभिन्नस्तु श्वेतं पिच्छिर्छं तन्तुमद्धनमनुबद्ध खिग्धमास्रावं स्नवति, ऊर्ध्वेत्व गुरुभिः स्थिरैर्जाछावतत्तः - ख़िम्पैर्डइछत्वगुप्लेपैर्वणेरनुबध्यतेऽनुषङ्गी | चराभवति, | इवेतनख़नथनवदनत्वङ्मूष्ठ- वर्चस्त्वं, निदानोक्तानि चास्य नोपशेरते विपरीतानि चोपशेरत इति श्लेष्मविसर्पः॥ ३४॥
answer_text: Pitta aggravated by hot regimens and intake of burning and sour foods effects the dusyas and while filling up vessels spreads. It has the following symptoms fever, thirst, fainting, confusion, vomiting, anorexia, breaking pain in limbs, excessive sweating, internal heat, .delirium, head¬ ache, congestion of eyes, sleeplessness, restlessness, giddiness, intense desire for cold air and water, deep green and yellow colour in eyes, urine and stool, and vision of green and yellow objects. The part where the disorder spreads has any of the coppery, green, yellow, blue, black and red colours; is filled with raised eruptions having intense burning sensation and tearing pain, suppurating quickly and dis¬ charging fluid of similar colour. The etiological factors do not suit and the con¬ trary ones suit the patient. - This is paittika visarpa. - Kapha vitiated by intake of sweet, sour, salty, fatty and heavy food affects the It exhibits the following symptoms—feeling—of—cold, cold, fever—( fever—with shivering ), heaviness, sleep, drowsiness, anorexia, sweetness of mouth, sliminess in mouth, spitting, vomiting, lassitude, feeling of wetness, loss of digestive power and debility. The part where the disease spreads becomes swollen, pale and reddish, associated with unctuousness, numbness, stiffness, heaviness, and, slight, pain... It, is also attended by eruptions which suppurate hardly, continue for long, have copious smearing on skin and are white-pale, when burst they discharge white, slimy, thready, viscous, continuous and unctuous fluid. Later on big, stable, membranous, unctuous wounds with copious smearing on skin appear and re-appear. There is also whiteness in nails, eyes, face, skin, urine and stool. The etiological factors do not suit while those contrary to them suit the patient. In This is kaphaja visar pa
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Chikitsasthana, Chapter 21, verse 33-34.
context: पित्तमुष्णोपचारेण विदाह्यम्छाशनैश्वितम् । दृष्यान् संदृष्य धमनीः पूरयन् वै विसर्पति ॥ ३१ ॥ तस्य रूपाणि ज्वरस्तुष्णा मूर्च्छा मोहइछर्दिररोचकोऽङ्गभेदः स्वेदोऽतिमाघमन्तद्वीहः प्रलापः शिरोहक चक्रषोराकुलत्वमस्वप्रमरतिश्रेमः शीतवातवारितर्षोऽतिमात्रं हरितहारिद्वनैत्रमूत्रवर्वर्वस्त्वं हरित- हारिद्ररूपदर्शनं च, यसिमध्यावकारी विसर्पोऽनुसपति सोऽवकाशस्ताम्रहरितहारिद्रनीळकृष्णरक्तानां वर्णा- नामन्यतमं पुष्यति, सोल्सेवैधातिमात्रं दाहसंभेदनपरीतैः स्फोटकैरुपचीयते तुल्यवर्णास्नावैरचिरपाकैश्व, निद्।नोकानि चास्य नोपशेरते विपरीतानि चोपशेरत इति पित्तविसर्पः॥ ३२ ॥ स्वाह्रम्छलवणजिग्धगुर्वन्नसंचितः । कफः संदूषयन् दृष्यान् छच्छ्मङ्गे विसर्पति ॥ ३३ ॥ तस्य रूपाणि – शीतकः शीतज्वरो – गौरवं निद्रा तन्द्राऽरोचको – मधुरास्यत्वमास्योपलैपो – निष्टीविका छर्दिराछस्य स्तैमित्यमझिनाशो दौर्बल्यं च, अयरिमध्यावकाशे विसर्पोऽचुसर्पति सोऽवकाशः श्वयथमान् पाण्डुर्नातिरक्तः ख्रेइस्तिस्तम्भगौरवैरन्वितोऽल्पवेदनःका क्रच्छपाकैश्चिरकारिभिवेहुळत्वगुपलेपैः स्फोटैः श्वेतपाण्ड्रभिरतबध्यते, प्रभिन्नस्तु श्वेतं पिच्छिर्छं तन्तुमद्धनमनुबद्ध खिग्धमास्रावं स्नवति, ऊर्ध्वेत्व गुरुभिः स्थिरैर्जाछावतत्तः - ख़िम्पैर्डइछत्वगुप्लेपैर्वणेरनुबध्यतेऽनुषङ्गी | चराभवति, | इवेतनख़नथनवदनत्वङ्मूष्ठ- वर्चस्त्वं, निदानोक्तानि चास्य नोपशेरते विपरीतानि चोपशेरत इति श्लेष्मविसर्पः॥ ३४॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 22):

अंसेत्यादि । अंसेत्यादिना श्लोकार्धेनांसशोषः केवलवातज उच्यते । अंसबन्धनकारकः श्लेष्मा अंसबन्धनः एतदनन्तरं अंसशोषं जनयेत् इति शेष इति कार्तिकः ।। जनयेदवबाहुकम् । सिराश्चाकुष्ट्य तत्रस्थो
answer_text: The half verse starting from amsa refers to the fact that the disease amsaśoṣa is produced only through the vātaśoṣa. The kapha that binds the amsa or shoulders is called amsabandhana, The factor that binds the scapula is signified through the term amsabandhan i.e. śleṣmā or synovial fluid. In the opinion of Kārtika, the above passage should be added with the part amsasosam janayet. It would complete the passage in the context, states Kārtika. Amsasosa (SS. Ni. 1.82/2) Amsaśoṣa is similarly a condition that emerges due to contraction of the tendons/nerves of that amsadeśa (the shoulder region)
chapter_title: Vātavyādhi Nidānam – Diagnosis of Neurological Diseases
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 22.

तेषां विस्नरतो लिङ्गमेक्रैंकस्य च मेपजम् । यथावत्संप्रवक्ष्यामि सिद्धान् वस्तींध्र यापनान् ॥ १३ ॥ तत्रोच्चैर्माष्यातिभाष्यास्यां, शिरस्तापशाङ्ककर्णनिस्तोदश्रोत्रोपरोधमुखतालुकण्डशोषतैमिर्यपिपासा- ज्वरतमकहनुय्रहमन्यास्तम्भनिष्टीवनोरःपाईर्वशुलस्वरमेदहिकाश्वासादयः स्युः ( १ ); रथक्षोभात् (संधिपर्वशैथिल्यहनुनासाकर्णशिरःशूलतोदकुश्निक्षोभाटोपान्त्रकूजनाःमानहदयेन्द्रियोप- रोधस्फिकपाईवेंश्लणब्रषणकटीपृष्ठवेदनासंधिस्कन्धश्रीवादौर्वल्याङ्गाभितापपाद्शोफप्रस्वापहर्षणाद्यः (२); अतिचङ्कमणात् पादजह्नोरुजानुवङ्क्षणश्रोणीपृष्ठशूलसक्थिसादनिस्तोदपिण्डिकोद्वेप्टनाङ्कमर्द्वेसा- भितापसिराधमनीहषश्वासकासादयः ( ३ ); थत्यासनाद्रथक्षोभजाः स्फिक्पाइवेवङ्गणत्रषणकटीपृष्ठवेदनादयः ( ४ ); अजीणध्यिशनाभ्यां तु मुखशोषाध्मानशुळनिस्तोदपिपासागात्रसादच्छर्चतीसारमूच्छर्छर्ज्वरप्रवाहणा- मविषादयः ( ५ ); विषमाहिताशनाभ्यामनन्नाभिलाषदौर्बल्यवैवर्ण्यकण्डूपामागात्रावसादा वातादिप्रकोपजाथ्य प्रहण्यर्गो- विकाराद्यः ( ६ ); दिवास्वप्नादरोचकाविपाकास्निनाशस्तैमित्यपाण्डत्वकण्डूपामादाइच्छर्येक्नमदेंहत्स्तम्भजाब्यतन्द्रा- निद्राप्रसङ्ग्रन्थिजन्मदीबेल्यरक्तमूत्राक्षितातालुलेपाः ( ७ ); व्यवायादाशुबलनाशोरुसादशिरोबस्तिगुदमेढ़बंक्षणोरुजानुजह्वापादशुलहदयस्पन्दननेत्रपीडाक्न- रोथिल्यशुक्रमार्गशोणित।गमनकासश्वासशोणितष्टीवनस्वरावसादकटीदीवस्यैकाङ्ग - सर्वाङ्गरोगमुष्कश्वयथु- वातवर्चोमूत्रसङ्ग्रकविसर्गजाड्यवेपथुबाधिर्यविषादादयः स्युः; अवलुप्यतः इव गुव्ः, ताड्यतः इव मेढ़म्, अवसीद्तीव मनो, वेपते हृद्यं, पीड्यन्ते सन्धयः, तमः प्रवेष्यतः इवाचा ( ८८);io इत्येवमेभिरप्टभिरपचारैंरेते प्रादुर्भवन्त्यु पद्रवाः ॥ १४ ॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 3, verse 8):

शुक्लमित्यादि । शुक्लमित्यादिना हृष्टरोमा इत्यन्तेन श्लैष्मिकः । विस्रमामगन्धि वराहस्नेह-मांसाम्बुसदृशं सर्वरूपिणम् । कृच्छुसाध्यमतीसारं विद्याद्दोषत्रयोद्धवम् ॥८॥
answer_text: The passage in context explains the features of diarrhoea caused by Sleşmā. The term visra signifies something having the smell of raw or uncooked flesh. Diarrhoea of dosa-triad Elimination of faeces resembling the fat of a wild boar or resembling, the colour of the water in which mutton has been washed and the patient having the characteristics of all the three doşas are seen in the atisāra that has been caused due to the morbid increase of all the three dosas together. This is difficult to cure. – Diarrhoea caused by tridosas has the faecal matter that looks like the fat of the pig (varahasneha) and/or meat-washed water (mamsambu). The disease is associated with the signs and symptoms of all the three dosas (sarvarūpinam) and it is difficult for cure. 8
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 3, verse 8.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Charaka Samhita (Chikitsasthana, Chapter 29, verse 127-132):

मचन्ति, चात्रनाथ सलिक्का व्यापदो योनेः सनिदानचिकित्सताः ॥ १२७ ॥ उक्ता विस्तरतः सम्प्यङ्मुनिना तस्वदर्शिना । पुनरेवास्निवेशस्तु पप्रच्छ मिषजा वरमू ॥ १२८ ॥ आत्रियमुपसङ्गम्य तेषा हितु भिषकथेष्ट ! दुष्पदुष्पद्धतिम ! चिकित्सतं च कात्स्येन हेव्यं यच चतर्दिघम ॥१३०॥ उपद्रवेष्ट योनीनों प्रदरो यथ्य कीर्तितः । तेपां, निदानं, लिङ्कं, च चिकित्सां चैव तत्वतः ॥ १३१ ॥ समासव्यासमेदेन प्रद्रहि सिपजों वर ! । तस्मेर
answer_text: The disorders of female genital track along with symptoms, causes and treatment have been said properly in detail by the sage, the secr of reality. Agnivesa again approached Atreya, the best among physicians, and queried him—O sinless | Bight defects of the semen of man have been mentioned by Lyou in the chapter on ( enumeration of ) diseases. Now O best among physicians! tell me, in brief as well as in detail, their etiology, symptoms, of Unormal, and abnormal and treatment and also the fourfold impotency. Tell me also about the cause, symptoms and treatment of pradara (menorrhagia) mentioned as one of the compli¬ cations of female genital disorders. On this the foremost among sages, said, to thim who was eager to listen
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Chikitsasthana, Chapter 29, verse 127-132.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2):

वातपित्तज्वरलक्षणमाह तृष्णेत्यादि । प्रदाणि भिद्यन्त इव वेदना पर्वभेदः । एतानि च लिङ्गानि विकृतिविषमसमावायारब्धस्य वोद्धव्यानि । विकृतिविषमसमवायारब्धत्वं चैषां केवलवातिकपैतिकज्वरलक्षणानां मध्ये केषाञ्टिदेव नियमेन पाठातदतिरिक्तलक्षणपाठाच्व वोद्धव्यम् । यथाअत्रैव वातपैत्तिकेऽरुचिरोमहर्षो वक्ष्यमाणवातश्लैष्मिके स्वेदः सन्तापश्च एवं कफर्पेत्तिके अनवस्थितशीतदाहौ एवं सन्निपातजे सास्नकलुषादिनेत्रत्वशिरोलोटनादि । प्रकृतिसमवायारव्ये तु वातजादिज्वरलिङ्गन्येव समस्तानि कतिपयानि वा भवन्ति । अत एव चिकित्सते चरको विकृतिविषमसमवायारव्यानां हन्दसन्निपातज्वराणां लक्षणानि साक्षात् पठित्वा निदानस्थानोक्तवातादिज्वरलिङ्गातिदेशेन प्रकृतिसमसमवेतानां द्वन्द्वसन्निपातज्वराणां लक्षण- मुक्तवान् । यदाह निवाने त्रिविधा प्रोक्ता या पृथग्जज्वराकृतिः । संसर्गसत्रिपातानों तया चोर्क्त स्वलक्षणम् चचि इति । एवं वक्ष्यमाण द्वन्द्वसन्निपातलक्षण व्याख्येयम् । प्रकृतिसमसमवायविकृतिविषमसमवाययोधायमर्थः प्रकृत्या हेतुभूतया समः कारणानुरूपः समवायः कार्यकारणभावसम्बन्धः प्रकृतिसमसमवायः कारणानुरूप कार्य- मित्यर्थः यथाशुक्लतन्तुसमवायाख्यस्य पटस्य शुक्लत्वम् । विकृत्या हेतुभूतया विषमः कारणाननुरूपः समवायो विकृतिविषमसमवायः यथा हरिद्राचूर्णसंयोगजं लौहित्य- मिति स्तैमित्यं पर्वणां भेदो निद्रा गौरवमेव च ॥ ॥ कासः स्वेदाप्रवर्तनम् । प्रतिश्यायःः शिरोग्रहः वातश्लेष्मज्वराकृतिः ॥१ ॥ मध्यवेगश्च सन्तापो - - - -
answer_text: Till now, the fever caused by individual dosas like the vata, pitta and kapha were being discussed. Now, one could discuss the fever that occurs due to vitiation of two dosas in combination. Such diseases are generally named as dvandaja diseases. Here are described the detailed symptoms of vātapitta fever. It has the symptoms such as the parvabheda. The term parvabheda refers to a severe pain in the joints. It appears as if the joints would break. These symptoms are known as Vikrti- viṣamasamavāya. This term refers to irrelevance of the symptoms to the apparent cause. It refers to a situation where there are only a few symptoms of the vitiated vāta and pitta, there is no other signs and yet there are a few signs that relate neither to the symptoms cited in the case of vāta jvara nor that of pitta jvara. For example, there is horripilation and loss of taste in eating. Both of these symptoms relate neither to the vata jvara nor to pitta jvara. Likewise, there occur, in the vatakapha jvara and pittakapha jvara, such symptoms as sweating and heat sensation ( santāpa ) (in vātakapha jvara), symptoms of unstable cold and burning sensation (in kaphapitta jvara) and such symptoms as filling of tears in the eyes, timidity, disoriented movement of head and its rolling (in sannipata jvara). It does not sound proper to accept that all these and the like symptoms occur due to combined effects of pathological conditions identified. That is why Caraka has explained these situations under the category Vikrtivişamasamavāya defined above. There has been referred another category named Prakrisamasamavaya. In the cases of the dvandaja jvara or the fever caused by Prakrtisamasamavāya factors there is found a combination of all or a few of the symptoms of the vitiation of the individual dosas involved. That is why Caraka, in the Cikitsā Sthāna section of his text has described the signs and symptoms irrelevant to the cause regarding the fevers caused by dual dosas and the dosa triad after which are given in Nidāna Slhāna. The features of three types of fever (vala, pitta and kapha) and the dual and dosa triad fevers have also been detailed in Nidāna Sthāna. As suggested above the signs and symptoms of diseases caused due to dual and triad of the dosas are to be understood as the combination of those detailed individually (CS, Ci.3.110). In this manner, the Dvandva and Samipāta types of fevers are to be analysed in the forthcoming passages of the present work. The relationship of similarity between the qualities of cause and effect is known as ‘Praketisamasamavāya’. This could be visualized with the example of production of white cloth with white threads. The dissimilarity between the qualities of cause and effect is called Vikrtivişamasamavaya’, as in the case of white coloured lime and yellow coloured turmeric when mixed produce red like liquid. It may be noted that either of the two elements do not have red colour. Signs and symptoms of Vāta-Sleṣmā type of fever (SS. context: वातपित्तज्वरलक्षणमाह तृष्णेत्यादि । प्रदाणि भिद्यन्त इव वेदना पर्वभेदः । एतानि च लिङ्गानि विकृतिविषमसमावायारब्धस्य वोद्धव्यानि । विकृतिविषमसमवायारब्धत्वं चैषां केवलवातिकपैतिकज्वरलक्षणानां मध्ये केषाञ्टिदेव नियमेन पाठातदतिरिक्तलक्षणपाठाच्व वोद्धव्यम् । यथाअत्रैव वातपैत्तिकेऽरुचिरोमहर्षो वक्ष्यमाणवातश्लैष्मिके स्वेदः सन्तापश्च एवं कफर्पेत्तिके अनवस्थितशीतदाहौ एवं सन्निपातजे सास्नकलुषादिनेत्रत्वशिरोलोटनादि । प्रकृतिसमवायारव्ये तु वातजादिज्वरलिङ्गन्येव समस्तानि कतिपयानि वा भवन्ति । अत एव चिकित्सते चरको विकृतिविषमसमवायारव्यानां हन्दसन्निपातज्वराणां लक्षणानि साक्षात् पठित्वा निदानस्थानोक्तवातादिज्वरलिङ्गातिदेशेन प्रकृतिसमसमवेतानां द्वन्द्वसन्निपातज्वराणां लक्षण- मुक्तवान् । यदाह निवाने त्रिविधा प्रोक्ता या पृथग्जज्वराकृतिः । संसर्गसत्रिपातानों तया चोर्क्त स्वलक्षणम् चचि इति । एवं वक्ष्यमाण द्वन्द्वसन्निपातलक्षण व्याख्येयम् । प्रकृतिसमसमवायविकृतिविषमसमवाययोधायमर्थः प्रकृत्या हेतुभूतया समः कारणानुरूपः समवायः कार्यकारणभावसम्बन्धः प्रकृतिसमसमवायः कारणानुरूप कार्य- मित्यर्थः यथाशुक्लतन्तुसमवायाख्यस्य पटस्य शुक्लत्वम् । विकृत्या हेतुभूतया विषमः कारणाननुरूपः समवायो विकृतिविषमसमवायः यथा हरिद्राचूर्णसंयोगजं लौहित्य- मिति स्तैमित्यं पर्वणां भेदो निद्रा गौरवमेव च ॥ ॥ कासः स्वेदाप्रवर्तनम् । प्रतिश्यायःः शिरोग्रहः वातश्लेष्मज्वराकृतिः ॥१ ॥ मध्यवेगश्च सन्तापो - - - -

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 20):

हरीतकी पञ्चरसाऽलवणा तुवरा परम् । रूक्षोष्णा दीपनी मेध्या स्वादुपाका रसायनी ।।१९।। चक्षुष्या लघुरायुष्या बृंहणी चानुलोमिनी । श्वासकासप्रमेहार्शः कुष्ठशोथोदरक्रिमीन ।।२०।। वैस्वर्यग्रहणीरोगविबन्धविषमज्वरान् गुल्माध्मानतृषाछर्दिहिक्काकण्ड्रहृदामयान् ।।२१।। कामला शूलमानाहं प्लीहानञ्च यकृत्तथा । अश्मरी मूत्रकृच्छुञ्च मूत्राघातञ्च नाशयेत् ।।२२।। स्वादुतिक्तकषायत्वात्पित्तहत्कफहत्त् सा । कटुतिक्तकषायत्वादम्लत्वाद्वातहृच्छिवा ।। २ ३ ।। पित्तकृत्कदुकाम्लत्वाद्वातकृन्न कथं शिवा ।।२४।। प्रभावाद्दोषहन्तृत्व सिद्ध यत्तत्रकाश्यते । हेतुभिः शिष्यबोधार्थं नापूर्वं क्रियतेऽधुना ।।२५ ।। कमन्यित्व गुणैः साम्य दृष्टमाश्रयभेदतः । यतस्ततो नेति चिन्यं धात्रीलकुचयोर्यथा ।। २६ ।। पथ्याया मज्जनि स्वादुः स्नाय्वामम्लो व्यवस्थितः । वृन्ते तिक्तस्त्वचि कटुरस्थिस्याजुवरो रसः ।।२७।।
answer_text: Haritaki has five rasas, Kaṣāya (Astringent) pradana, Alavaṇa (Deviod of Salt), Rūkṣā (Dry in action), Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), Dīpana (Appetizer), Mēdhya (Brain tonic), Madhura vipāka (Sweet in post digestive) & Rāsayana (Rejuvenators) Netrahita (Benficial for the eyes), Lagu Pācana (Easy for digestion), Ayuvardaka (Increases the life span), Brmhana (Promotes nourishment) and Anulomana (Carminative). It cures Swāsa (Dyspnoea), Kāsa (Cough), Premaha (Diabeties), Kuṣṭa (Leprosy), Sotha (Inflammation), Kṛmi (Worm Infestations), Swarabheda (Hoarseness of voice), Grahaṇī (Spure), Vibandha (Constipation), Viṣama jwara (Malaria), Gulma (Abdominal tumors), Ādmāna (Flatulence), Tṛṣṇā (Thrist), Chardi (Vomiting), Hīkkā (Hicough), Udardaha (Urticaria), Hrudroga (Cardiac diseases), Kāmala (Jaundice), Śūla (Abdominal pain), Anāha (Bloating) Plīhāroga (Spleen disorders), Yakṛt roga (Liver diseases), Aśmari (Urinary stones) Mūtrakṛcchra (Dysuria) and Mutrāghāta (Retention of urine). Madhura (Sweet), Tikta (Bitter), Kaṣāya (Astringent) rasa subsides Pitta and Kapha, It subsides Vāta by Kaṭu (Pungent), Kaṣāya (Astringent) and Amla (Sour) tastes. Usually Kaṭu and the Amala rasa of dravya Increases Vāta and Pitta, Why it is not in case of Harītakī?, it is tridoṣa śāmaka, the action of Haritaki is based on Prabhava. The pathology of doşas by the action of rasas is mentioned above is for enlighten the disciples. Sometime the rasa of the dravya does not exhibits structural related actions, so as in the example of Dhātri and Lakuca. The rind of Harītakī is Madhura (Sweet), Fibers are Amala (Sour), Peduncle isTikta (Bitter), Seed coat is Kaṭu (Pungent) and the Seed is Kaṣāya (Astringent)
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 20
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 20.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 4, verse 4):

कला धात्वाशयान्तरमर्यादा, पक्वामाशयमध्यस्था पच्यमानाशयरूपेत्यर्थः ।।- पूर्वरूपं तस्येदं तृष्णाऽऽलस्यं बलक्षयः । विदाहोऽन्नस्य पाकश्च चिरात् कायस्य गौरवम ॥4॥
answer_text: The term murcchitaih refers to one that has got highly aggravated. The reference is to suggest that through the vitiation of the dosas the undigested or digested stuff is expelled by the grahanī (It may be noted that this term signifies a part of the body, duodenum, to be precise, as well as the disease that is apparently produced due to improper functioning of the same). The term ‘eva’ is used to denote both the digested and undigested foodstuff. The term pūti or putrid refers something with bad odour. When vata is predominant one would pass the stool that is hard in consistency while one would pass loose stool in the case he is suffering from predominance of pitta. Grahanī is the seat of digestive fire. As suggested by Caraka, it is the seat of agni, the digestive fire. It is called grahaṇī as it receives the food. It is situated above the umbilicus. It receives the undigested stuff and processes the same for digestion. After digestion, it passes the stuff downwards (CS. Ci. 15.55). Suśruta has also opined that the sixth membrane in the body has been named as Pittādharā that is the one which holds pitta, the digestive fire. It is located between the pakvāśaya (intestines) and āmāśaya (stomach) and is known as Grahaṇī (SS. Ut. 40). The term kalā is the threshold between the dhātu (tissue) and the āśaya that is the organ or seat of a particular factor. Pacyamānāśaya (organ for processing of ingested food) is the name of this limb of body. Pūrvarūpa (prodromal features) of Grahaṇī (CS. Ci. 15) Thirst, lassitude, weakness, improper digestion, delayed digestion, and heaviness in the body are the premonitory symptoms of this disease. 4
chapter_title: Grahaṇī Roga Nidānam – Diagnosis of Duodenal Disorders
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 4, verse 4.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 68, verse 2):

वातदुष्ट शिशुः स्तन्यं पिबन् वातगदातुरः । क्षामस्वरः कृशाङ्गः स्याद्वद्धविण्मूत्रमारुतः ॥ १॥ स्विन्नो भिन्नोमलो बालः कामलापित्तरोगवान्। तृष्णालुरुष्णसर्वाङ्गः पित्तदुष्ट पयः पिबन्॥ २॥ कफदुष्ट पिबन् क्षीरं लालालुः श्लेष्मरोगवान्। निद्रान्वितो जडः शूनवक्त्राक्षश्छर्दनः शिश्र्ः ॥ ३॥ द्वन्द्वजे द्वन्द्वजं रूपं सर्वजे सर्वलक्षणम्। मधुकोशः बालरोगाणां दुष्टस्तन्येन संभवात्तदनन्तरं तानाह-वातदुष्टमित्यादि। वातगदातुर इति वक्ष्यमाणक्षामस्वरादि- युक्तः। तृष्णालुरिति तृष्णावान्। लालालुरिति लाला स्रावयुक्तः। छर्दन इति स्तन्यवान्तिकरः॥ १–३॥ शिशोस्तीव्रामतीव्रां च रोदनालक्षयेद्रजम् ॥ ४॥ स यं स्पृशेद् भूशं देशं यत्र च स्पर्शनाक्षमः । तत्र विद्याद्वजं मूर्ध्नि रुजं चाक्षिनिमीलनात् ॥ ५ ॥ कोष्ठे विबन्धवमथुस्तनदंशान्त्रकूजनैः । आध्मानपृष्ठनमनजठरोन्नमनैरपि॥ ६ ॥ बस्तौ गुह्ये च विण्मूत्रसंगत्रासदिगीक्षणैः । स्त्रोतांस्यङ्गानि सन्धींश्च पश्येद्यत्नान्मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ ७॥ मधुकोशः शिशोर्वक्तमक्षमस्यान्तर्गतवेदनाज्ञानोपायमाह-शिशोरित्यादि। तीव्रां रुजं बहुरोदनात्, अतीव्रामल्परोदना- लक्ष्येत् ॥ ४–७ ॥ कुकूणकः क्षीरदोषाच्छिशूनामक्षिवर्त्मनि। जायते तेन तन्नेत्रं कण्डूरं च स्रवेन्मुहः॥ ८॥ शिशुः कुर्याल्ललाटाक्षिकूटनासावघर्षणम्। शक्तो नार्कप्रभां द्रेष्ट न वर्त्मोन्मीलनक्षमः॥ ९॥ मधुकोशः बालानामेव दुष्टस्तन्यपानाद्वत्मरोगमाह-कुकूणक 'इत्यादि। कुकूणकः 'कोथ' इति ख्यातः। स्त्रवेन्मुहुरिति पिच्चिटस्नुतियुक्त भवतीत्यर्थः। न वर्त्मोन्मीलनक्षम इति न वर्त्मचालनपटुः॥ ८–९॥ मातुः कुमारो गर्भिण्याः स्तन्यं प्रायः पिबन्नपि। कासाग्निसादवमथुतन्द्राकार्श्यारुचिभ्रमैंः॥ १०॥ युज्यते कोष्ठवृद्ध्या च तमाहुः पारिगर्भिकम्। रोगं परिभवाख्यं च युज्यात्तत्राग्निदीपनम्॥ ११॥ मधुकोशः पारिगर्भिकमाह-मातुरित्यादि। पिबन्नपीति अपिशब्दादपिबन्नपि तमाहुः, पारिगर्भिकमिति पारिगर्भिकोऽ-प हिण्डीति ख्यातः; तस्यैव परिभवाख्य इति नामान्तरं बालं परिभवतीति परिभवः, स एव आख्या यस्य तम्। उपशयेनापि तस्ज्ञानमाह- युअ्यादित्यादि॥ १०–११ ॥ तालुमांसे कफः क्रुन्द्वः कुरुते तालुकण्टकम्। तेन तालुप्रदेशस्य निम्नता मूर्धिन जायते॥ १२॥ तालुपातः स्तनद्वेषः कृच्छात् पानं शकृद्ववम्। तृडक्षिकण्ठास्यरुजा ग्रीवादुर्धरता वमिः ॥ १३ ॥ मधुकोशः तालुकण्टकमाह-तालुमांस इत्यादि । अस्यैव लक्षणं तालुपात इत्यादि । तालुपात इत्यभ्यन्तरे तालुनोऽधःपातः। कृच्छ्रात् पानमित्यत्र 'स्तन्यस्य' इति शेषः। शकृद्द्रवं भिन्नपुरीषता। ग्रीवाया दुःखेन धारणम्। वमिः स्तन्यस्य वान्तिः ॥ १२–१३ ॥ विसर्पस्तत शिशोः प्राणनाशनो बस्तिशीर्षजः। पद्मवर्णो महापद्मनामा दोषत्रयोद्दवः॥ १४॥ शङ्वाभ्यां हृदयं याति हृदयाद्वा गुर्द व्रजेत्। मधुकोशः - महापद्मनामानं विसर्पमाह-विसर्पस्त्वित्यादि। बस्तिशीर्षज इति बस्तिजः शीर्षजश्र, शीर्ष शिरः। पद्मवर्ण इति लोहितपद्मवर्णः । शङ्वाभ्यां हृदयं यातीति शीर्षजः । पद्मपत्रतुल्यवर्णतां मुखतालुनि बहिर्देशे वेति वदन्ति। हृदयाद् गुदं यातीति बस्तिजः, ऊध्वी हृदयं गत्वा गुदं यातीत्यर्थः। अत्र पद्मसवर्णता बस्तिदेशे गुदे च। वाशब्दश्रात्र व्यवस्थित-विकल्पवचनः ॥ १४ ॥ क्षुद्ररोगे कथिते त्वगजल्ल्यहिपूतने॥ १५॥ मधुकोशः अन्यौ द्वौ विकारौ बालाना, भवतस्तावाह-क्षुद्रेत्यादि। स्निग्धा सवर्णेत्यादिनाऽजगलिका, कण्ड्रयनादि- त्यादिनाऽहिपूतना॥ १५ ॥ ज्वराद्या व्याधयः सर्वे महतां ये पुरेरिताः। बालदेहेऽपि ते तद्वद्विज्ञेयाः कुशलैः सदा॥ १६॥ मधुकोशः अन्येऽपि विकारा बालानां संभवन्तीत्यतिदेशेन तानाह-ज्वराद्या इत्यादि। पुरेरिता इति पूर्वोक्ताः। ते तद्वंदिति ते ज्वरादयस्तादृशा ज्ञेयाः । कुशलैरिति विज्ञेः ॥ १६ ॥ क्षणादुद्विजते बालः क्षणात्रस्यति रोदिति। नखैर्दन्तैर्दारयति धात्रीमात्मानमेव वा॥ १७॥ ऊर्ध्वं निरीक्षते दन्तान् खादेत् कूजति जृम्भते। भ्रवौ क्षिपति दन्तौष्ठ फेनं वमति चासकत्॥ १८॥ क्षामोऽति निशि जागर्ति शूनाक्षो भिन्नविट्स्वरः । मासंशोणितगन्धिश्च न चाश्नाति यथा पुरा ॥ १९ ॥ सामान्यं ग्रहजुष्टानां लक्षणं समुदाहतम्। मधुकोशः प्रायेण शौचभ्रंशादिना स्कन्दग्रहादयो नव बालेष्वावेशं कुर्वन्यतस्तत्परिज्ञानाय सामान्यलक्षणमाह- क्षणादुद्विजते बाल इत्यादि। एते ग्रहाः पूजार्थं बालान् हिंसन्ति। यदुक्तं सुश्रते-‘धात्रीमात्रोः प्राक प्रदिष्टापचाराच्छौचभ्रष्टान् मङ्गलाचारहीनान्। त्रस्तान् हष्टांस्तर्जितान् क्रन्दितान् वा पूजाहेतोर्हिस्युरेते कुमारान्॥' (सु.ड. २७) इति। उद्विजत इत्युद्विग्नो भवति; उद्विग्नो विह्वलः, नोतु विभेतीत्यर्थः, त्रस्यतीत्यनेन पौनरुक्त्य प्रसङ्गात्। कूजत्यार्तनादं करोति। भुवौ क्षिपतीति भ्रूभङ्गं रचयति। दन्तौष्ठमित्यत्र क्षिपतीति संबध्यते। क्षिपति खादति, धातूनामनेकार्थत्वात्। भिन्नविट् भिन्नशकृत्, भिन्नस्वरः स्वरभेदवान्। मांसशोणितगन्धिरिति विस्रगन्धि। न चाश्राति यथा पुरेति पूर्ववन्न भक्षयतीत्यर्थः ॥ १७–१९ ॥ एकनेत्रस्य गात्रस्य स्त्रावः स्पन्दनकम्पनम्॥ २०॥ ऊर्ध्वं दूष्ट्या निरीक्षेत वक्रास्यो रक्तगन्धिकः। दन्तान् खादति वित्रस्तः स्तन्यं नैवाभिनन्दति॥ २१॥ स्कन्दग्रहगृहीताना रोदनं चाल्पमेव च। मधुकोशः सामान्यलिङ्गमभिधाय विशेषग्रहलिङ्गमाह-एकनेत्रस्येत्यादि। एकनेत्रस्य वामस्य दक्षिणस्य वा स्रावोऽश्रु- स्नुतिः प्रभावात्, गात्रस्य स्रावो घर्मयुक्तगात्रतेत्यर्थः। स्पन्दनकम्पनमिति स्पन्दनं चलनं, कम्पनं महता वेगेन वेपनं; स्पन्दन कम्पन वा भवतीत्यर्थः । वक्रास्यो वक्रमुखः । रक्तगन्धिक इत्येतत् सामान्यलक्षणलब्धमप्यतिशयार्थमुक्तम्; एवमन्यत्रापि समान्यलक्षणे पुनरुक्ते व्याख्येयम्॥ २०–२१ ॥ नष्टसंज्ञो वमेत् फेनं संज्ञावानतिरोदिति। पूयशोणितगन्धित्वं स्कन्दापस्मारलक्षणम्॥ २२॥ मधुकोशः स्कन्दापस्मारलक्षणमाह-नष्टेत्यादि। नष्टसंज्ञो मधुकोशः शकुनीलक्षणमाह-स्रस्ताड्म इत्यादि। स्रस्ताड्म इति अङ्गस्रंसवद्व्यथावान्। भयचकित इति भयहेतुर्भयं भयानकमुच्यते, ततश्चकितः, असति भयहेतौ त्रस्यतीत्यर्थः। विहङ्गगंन्धिरिति विहङ्गस्येव गन्धो यस्य स तथा, उपमानाच्चेति समासान्त इत्यप्रत्ययः। विहङ्कशब्देन जलचरा मांसादाश्च पक्षिणो गृह्यन्ते, विस्रगन्धित्वात्। हिरण्याक्षेऽप्युक्त ‘संस्रावदाहपाकाद्यैश्चितः स्फोटैर्भयान्वितः। स्रस्ताङ्गो विस्रगन्धिः स्याच्छकुन्या पीडितः शिशुः ॥’ इति। सास्रावव्रणपरिपीडित इति स्फोटैरेव विदीर्णैर्वणरूपमापन्नैः परिपीडितः स्फोटैश्व प्रचिततनुरिति नवनवैः स्फोटैव्याप्ततनुः । क्षत इत्याभिभूतः ॥ २३ ॥ व्रणैः स्फोटैश्चितं स्त्रवेदसुगिति गात्रमिति कर्तृपदें, पड्ढगन्धं शटितकर्दमगन्धं, समासविधेरनित्यत्वादिप्रत्ययो न भवति पूतनालक्षणमाह-अतीसार इत्यादि। ग्रस्त इति गृहीत इत्यर्थः॥ २४-३०॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां answer_text: When the child is fed with breast-milk that is vitiated by vata, he suffers from vāta-disorders. His voice becomes weak and the body, emaciated. The faeces and urine will stop passing (freely). On being fed with breast-milk that is vitiatiated by pitta, the child suffers from over sweating, diarrhoea, jaundice and other pitta diseases. He has more thirst and the body feels warm; and on feeding with the breast-b milk which is vitiated by kapha, there is dribbling of saliva and it suffers from kaphadiseases. He keeps sleeping, motion-less and has swollen face and eyes and keeps vomitting. When the breast-milk is afflicted by two of the tridosa. Those two particular related symptoms are seen in the child and when it is tridosa-affected milk, the child suffers from all the symptomatology of all three of the dosas. 1-3. After describing the vitiated breast-milk (in the previous chapter), The dis¬ eases caused by consuming such breast-milk are being explained here. Vata dis¬ eases means the shrill voice etc., that will be mentioned (in the next line of the stanza). Tṛṣṇāluḥ-the one suffering from thirst. Lālāluḥ - The one suffering from continuous dribbling of saliva. Chardana means vomitting the consumed breast¬ milk. 1-3. The method of knowing the internal pain of the child Mādhavanidānaṃ The severity of the pain the child experiences is known by the intensity of its cry. The particular place of the body repeatedly touched by the child is to be known as the site of pain and also the place where the child can not withstand the touch (or pressure) is also to be recogonised as site of pain. If the child keeps its eyes closed, it should be known that it is suffering from head-ache. On seeing the symptoms of constipation, vomittings, biting the nipples of the mother, noise in the intestines, bloating of the abdomen, bending the back and raising the stom¬ ach, it should be understood as the child is suffering from some abdominal disorder.The problem in the bladder and genitals is understood by constipation of faeces and urine, getting terrified without any reason and staring hither and thither. The channels, parts of the body and joints are to be examined time and again (to, know about any disorder). 4-7. The method of knowing the suffering of the child since it is not in a position to speak out - is being explained. By crying more it should be known that the child has more pain and by seeing crying with lower intensity, it is to be understood that the pain is less. 4-7. Kukūnaka Due to intake of vitiated breast-milk, the child is afflicted by a disease called Kukūnaka in the eye-lids. By this, there is repeated itching sensation and discharge in that particular eye. The child keeps rubbing the fore-head, eye-sac and the nose and it cannot bear the sight of sun-light and cannot lift the eye-lid. 8-9. Kukunaka is a disease popular by name Kotha Sravenmukuh discharges repeatedly - means eye will be full of sticky substance; Na Vartmonmīlana kṣama not capable of lifting the eye-lid-means not being able to move the eye-lid. 8-9. Bālaroga Nidāna Pārigarbhika By drinking the breast-milk of a pregnant woman, the child gets a disease inse called, Parigarbhika which is charecterised by-cough, depleted digestive fire, vomitting, dizziness, emaciation, anorexia, giddiness and bloating of the abdo¬ men. This disease is also called as paribhava in which the the drugs and food that increase digestive fire are advised. 10-11. By the word api in pibannapi, it implies that it may occur to a child who does not consume such breast milk. Pārigarbhika is popular by name, “ahiṇḍī”. Since it insults (troubles) the child, it is called Paribhava. To show that this can also be correctly diagnosed by upasaya (positive trial) it is suggested to use the drugs that kindle the digestive fire. 10-11. Tālukaṇṭaka When kapha accumulated in the palate gets aggravated, it causes Tālukaṇṭaka due to which depression of the Tālu pradeshe takes place. There will be protrusion of palate, aversion towards breast, drinking with difficully, loose mo¬ tions, thirst, pain in eye, throat and mouth and not being able to straighten the neck. 12, 13. Tālupāta means loosening or bulging down of internal palate. “Drinking with difficulty” is to be added with - “of the breast-milk”. Śakṛddravaṃ -is looseness inthe faeces. Gnvadurdharata not being able to keep the neck straight. Vamih vomitting of breast-milk. 12, 13. 23 M.N. Pt-II Mādhavanidānaṃ Mahāpadma The visarpa (erysipelas) occuring in children in the bladder and head region is considered as a lethal disease. Since it is of the lotus (red)colour, it is named as mahāpadma. This is caused by tridosa. This spreads from the temples to the heart region or from heart region to the anus. 14. Vastisirsajah means it occurs in the vasti - bladder region and sirsa- head region. Padmavama means in the colour of red lotus. That spreads from temples to the heart - is the one which is originated on the head. It is said that the lotus colour in the mouth and palate or outside. That spreads form heart region to anus- is the one which is originated on the bladder. It goes upto the heart and comes down to the anus. The lotus colour in this (second) case is seen in the bladder-region and anus. vā is used to show the alternative nature of this condition. 14. Ajagallikā and Ahipūtanā Ajagallikā and ahipūtana are desrcribed in kṣudra roga (minor-diseases) chapter. 15. Other two diseases occuring in children are being mentioned. Ajagallikā is mentioned to have the symptoms of oiliness, skin colour-etc., and ahiputanā scratch etc., symptoms (in the kṣudra roga chapter). 15. Jvara etc., diseases occuring in children. The experts should know the fever etc., disease occuring children, in the same manner as they are seen in the elders. 16. Bālaroga Nidāna Pureritāh means told earlier. Te tadvat means the jvara etc., should be known in the same manner; kusalaih by the experts. 16. Common symptomatology of démonic affliction The common symptomatology of the children who are afflicted by the graha - demons is as follows - At every moment, the child gets, agitated, gets terrified, weeps repeatedly, scratches itself or the mother, looks upwards, bites the teeth, makes typical sóunds, keeps yawning, keeps constricting the eye- brows, teeth and lips, brings out froathing saliva from the mouth. It becomes, emaciated, remains awakene during nights. Its eyes get swollen; suffers from diarrhoea and shrillness in the voice; stinks like meat and blood and does not eat as earlier (to this affliction). 17, 18, 19. Generally due to lack of cleanliness the nine skandagraha etc., demons take hold of the children. To know about such affliction, common symptomatology is being explained here. These grahas, inorder to get worshipped, trouble the chil¬ dren. As said in Susruta, "Due to unclean practices of the mother or the feeding woman and absence of cleansing and pious habits, the children are made to get terrified, over pleasured or wept by the demons for getting worshipped". Udvijale means becomes helpless/agitated; it does not mean gets terrified because the word trasyate comes next which means gets terrified. Kujayati means makes a cry of agony. Bhruvau ksipati means constricts the eye-brows. Ksipati also means “bites” which can relate to teeth and lips. Bhinna vit means loose defecation. Bhinna swarah means having broken voice; mamsa śoņita gandhi means foul smell. Na cāśnāti yathā purā means does not eat as earlier. 17-19. Symptomatology of the child on being afflicted by skandagraha One of the eye has discharge and on one sided the body keeps pulsating and shaking in the child. It looks upwards as if awaiting for some body, keeps the face curved, its body stinks like blood, bites the teeth, fears, does not like the breast feeding and weeps mildly when the skandagraha takes hold of the child. 20, 21. After furnishing the common symptomatology of the children afflicted by grahas, the specific graha- afflicted signs and symptoms are being mentioned. Dis¬ charge from one eye is of either on the left or right. Gatra srava means the body becoming warm. Spandana means mild movements, kaṃpana is shaking with force; it means that there will be either mild movement or shake. Vakrāsyaḥ means curved face/mouth. Raktagandha smelling like the blood- though mentioned in the com¬ mon symptomatology, is to indicate the intensity of stinking. Other symptoms which are mentioned taking from the common symptoms are to be under stood in the same way. 20, 21. Skandāpasmāra The child gets unconscious and vomits froathy saliva, weeps loudly on getting back to senses, and its body stinks like pus and blood - this condition is called Skandāpasmāra". 22. Bālaroga Nidāna On being unconscious, the child vomits froathy saliva and on getting back to senses, it weeps loudly. 22. Sakunīgraha - Symptomatology All the bodily limbs become loosened, it gets terrified, stinks like a bird, the whole body is full of wounds with discharge. The body is full of opened vesicles with ulceration and burning sensation when the child is gripped by Śakunīgraha. Srastāṅga suffering as if the limbs have fallen down. Bhayacakita - gets terrified without any season. Vihangagandha smelling like a bird. Vihanga means the bird that lives on eating the amphibious. In Hiranyākṣa also, it is said, “The body is full of broken vesicles that are opened, have burning sensation and ulceration. The limbs can not be held in position and hence they are loosely kept and the body stinks when the child is gripped by Sakunī graha. Sasrāva vraṇa paripīditaḥ suffers from the wounds that keep oozing. The sphota vesicles on getting broken become wounds and new vesicles keep generating. Kṣataḥ means gripped. 23. Revatīgraha, pūtanā, Andhapūtanā śītapūtana mukhamaṇḍikā and vargameșa graha and curability Mādhavanidānaṃ The body of a child becomes dirty with full of wounds and bullae; Blood oozes with stinking smell that is similar to mud; it has diarrhoea, fever and burning sensation, when the Revatigraha holds that particular child. Diarrhoea, fever, thirst, cross looks, intense weeping, lack of sleep and agitation are seen in the child when it is gripped by putana graha. Vomitting, cough, fever thirst, stinking like fat, intense weeping, disliking the breast-milk and diarrohea are the signs and symp¬ toms of the child gripped by andhapūtanā. When the child is held by Sītapūtanā, there will be trembling of the body, cough, emaciation, eye-problems, unnatural smell in the body, vomitting and diarrohea. The child afflicted by mukhamandikā has pleasant face with good colour, the body is full of veins (swollen veins); it stinks like urine and the child eats more. There will be vomitting, mild tremors of the body, drying of throat and mouth, syncope, unnatural smell, looking upwards and biting of teeth when the child is gripped by Naigamesa graha. When a child has staring looks, has aversion towards breast-milk, gets syn¬ cope repeatedly and has all the symptoms of holding by a particular graha he will be killed with that problem within a short-time. 24-30. (Diagnosis of Diseases caused by poisons) Type of poisons The Poison is basically categorised into two types viz., Sthavara (static) and Jangama (mobile). The first one is (obtained from) roots of plants etc., while the second, originates in snakes etc. 1.. Since it is remaining, (in mentioning) the diagnosis of visaroga (poisonous diseases or diseases caused by poisons) are mentioned. Visa is the name of that substance which · causes Visada (agony or sadness). It is of two types (by source) viz., Sthavara from static sources and jangama from mobile sources. Muladyatmakam means the first one is static (from static sources)which is again divided into ten types; as said in Susruta - "Roots, leaves, fruits, flowers, flowers, bark, latex, pith-part, gum-resin, metal and rhizomes”. (Su.ka. 2) Mādhavanidānaṃ, The Klītaka, Aśvamāra, Guñjā, Su gandha, gargara, karaghāṭa, vidyutchikhā (gloriosa superba?) and anantā- these eight are mūla viṣa (which have poisonous roots); Viṣapatrikā, laṃbā, sudāru, karaṃbha and mahākaraṃbha are the five patravisa (the leaves of these plants are poisonous); Kumudvati, Renuka, karambha, mahākaraṃbha, karkoṭaka, Reṇuka, khadyotaka Carmari, bhagandhā, sarpaghāti, Nandana and Sārapāka -these twelve are phala viṣa (the furits of these plants are poisonous). Vetra, kādaṃba, valīya, karaṃbha and mahākaraṃbha are the five flower-poisons (The flowers of these plants are poisonous). Antrapācaka, kartarīya, Sailaya, karaṃbha, nandana, Karaghāṭa and Varāṭa these seven are bark poisons and gum-resin poisons and also pith poisons (the bark, gum-resin and pith parts of these plants are poisonous); kumudaghni, Snuhi and Jalaksin these three are latex - poisons (the latex of these plants is poisonous). Phenāśma (vitreous arsenic) and incenerated Haritāla (orpiment) are the metallic poisons; kālakūṭa, vatsanābha (Aconitum ferox), sarṣapa, kapāla, kardamaka, vairāṭaka, Mustaka, Mahāviṣa, prapounḍarīka, mūlaka, Halāhala, śrīīgi and markaṭaka these thirteen are rhizome-poisons. These are lethal poisons. Thus fifty five static poisons are recognised. (karambha comes into four groups, mahakarambha is taken into three groups, Nandana is taken into two groups, thus making total number of drugs to 55-6=49) These are recognised, identified and collected with the help of hunters and aborigins those live in forests and mountains. The other (second) type is sourced from mobile-living creatures like snakes etc.. param the other vari¬ ety i.e. jangama which is of 16 types viz, dṛṣṭi (sight), Niśvāsa (exhalation) daṃṣṭrā (fangs), Nakha (nails), mutra (urine), purīṣa (faecal matter), śukra (semen) Lālāsrāva (Saliva), mukha saṃdaṃśa (biting with mouth), pardita (Stamping), gudāsthi (anus bone), pitta (bile), śūka (hair) and śava (dead-body). Pardita is done by the anus. Among these, the mobile creature which have poison in their sight and exhalation are divine serpants. The ones which live on earth have poison in their fangs. The cat, crocodile, tiger etc., have poison in fangs and nails, piccata, kaundinya etc., have poison in the urine and faecal matter.The mice have poison in the semen; scorpion, wasp and uccitinga etc. have poison in the particular sack that has sharp injecting end. Spider has poison in its saliva, feaces, urine, semen and bite or licking of the mouth, citrasirsa, sata dāruka, sārika etc have poision in mouth, bite or licking, fangs, stamping, anus and faecal matter. Poison striken bone and the bone of a fish etc., are having poisonous effect in the bone; śakulī fish has poison its bile The beetles with small pointed beak etc., have poison in the Suka the stinging part that protrudes on the face. Some insects and the snakes Viṣa Roga Nidāna which are dead are dead-body poisons. These are to be vividly seen in kalpasthana of Suśruta saṁhitā. 1. context: वातदुष्ट शिशुः स्तन्यं पिबन् वातगदातुरः । क्षामस्वरः कृशाङ्गः स्याद्वद्धविण्मूत्रमारुतः ॥ १॥ स्विन्नो भिन्नोमलो बालः कामलापित्तरोगवान्। तृष्णालुरुष्णसर्वाङ्गः पित्तदुष्ट पयः पिबन्॥ २॥ कफदुष्ट पिबन् क्षीरं लालालुः श्लेष्मरोगवान्। निद्रान्वितो जडः शूनवक्त्राक्षश्छर्दनः शिश्र्ः ॥ ३॥ द्वन्द्वजे द्वन्द्वजं रूपं सर्वजे सर्वलक्षणम्। मधुकोशः बालरोगाणां दुष्टस्तन्येन संभवात्तदनन्तरं तानाह-वातदुष्टमित्यादि। वातगदातुर इति वक्ष्यमाणक्षामस्वरादि- युक्तः। तृष्णालुरिति तृष्णावान्। लालालुरिति लाला स्रावयुक्तः। छर्दन इति स्तन्यवान्तिकरः॥ १–३॥ शिशोस्तीव्रामतीव्रां च रोदनालक्षयेद्रजम् ॥ ४॥ स यं स्पृशेद् भूशं देशं यत्र च स्पर्शनाक्षमः । तत्र विद्याद्वजं मूर्ध्नि रुजं चाक्षिनिमीलनात् ॥ ५ ॥ कोष्ठे विबन्धवमथुस्तनदंशान्त्रकूजनैः । आध्मानपृष्ठनमनजठरोन्नमनैरपि॥ ६ ॥ बस्तौ गुह्ये च विण्मूत्रसंगत्रासदिगीक्षणैः । स्त्रोतांस्यङ्गानि सन्धींश्च पश्येद्यत्नान्मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ ७॥ मधुकोशः शिशोर्वक्तमक्षमस्यान्तर्गतवेदनाज्ञानोपायमाह-शिशोरित्यादि। तीव्रां रुजं बहुरोदनात्, अतीव्रामल्परोदना- लक्ष्येत् ॥ ४–७ ॥ कुकूणकः क्षीरदोषाच्छिशूनामक्षिवर्त्मनि। जायते तेन तन्नेत्रं कण्डूरं च स्रवेन्मुहः॥ ८॥ शिशुः कुर्याल्ललाटाक्षिकूटनासावघर्षणम्। शक्तो नार्कप्रभां द्रेष्ट न वर्त्मोन्मीलनक्षमः॥ ९॥ मधुकोशः बालानामेव दुष्टस्तन्यपानाद्वत्मरोगमाह-कुकूणक 'इत्यादि। कुकूणकः 'कोथ' इति ख्यातः। स्त्रवेन्मुहुरिति पिच्चिटस्नुतियुक्त भवतीत्यर्थः। न वर्त्मोन्मीलनक्षम इति न वर्त्मचालनपटुः॥ ८–९॥ मातुः कुमारो गर्भिण्याः स्तन्यं प्रायः पिबन्नपि। कासाग्निसादवमथुतन्द्राकार्श्यारुचिभ्रमैंः॥ १०॥ युज्यते कोष्ठवृद्ध्या च तमाहुः पारिगर्भिकम्। रोगं परिभवाख्यं च युज्यात्तत्राग्निदीपनम्॥ ११॥ मधुकोशः पारिगर्भिकमाह-मातुरित्यादि। पिबन्नपीति अपिशब्दादपिबन्नपि तमाहुः, पारिगर्भिकमिति पारिगर्भिकोऽ-प हिण्डीति ख्यातः; तस्यैव परिभवाख्य इति नामान्तरं बालं परिभवतीति परिभवः, स एव आख्या यस्य तम्। उपशयेनापि तस्ज्ञानमाह- युअ्यादित्यादि॥ १०–११ ॥ तालुमांसे कफः क्रुन्द्वः कुरुते तालुकण्टकम्। तेन तालुप्रदेशस्य निम्नता मूर्धिन जायते॥ १२॥ तालुपातः स्तनद्वेषः कृच्छात् पानं शकृद्ववम्। तृडक्षिकण्ठास्यरुजा ग्रीवादुर्धरता वमिः ॥ १३ ॥ मधुकोशः तालुकण्टकमाह-तालुमांस इत्यादि । अस्यैव लक्षणं तालुपात इत्यादि । तालुपात इत्यभ्यन्तरे तालुनोऽधःपातः। कृच्छ्रात् पानमित्यत्र 'स्तन्यस्य' इति शेषः। शकृद्द्रवं भिन्नपुरीषता। ग्रीवाया दुःखेन धारणम्। वमिः स्तन्यस्य वान्तिः ॥ १२–१३ ॥ विसर्पस्तत शिशोः प्राणनाशनो बस्तिशीर्षजः। पद्मवर्णो महापद्मनामा दोषत्रयोद्दवः॥ १४॥ शङ्वाभ्यां हृदयं याति हृदयाद्वा गुर्द व्रजेत्। मधुकोशः - महापद्मनामानं विसर्पमाह-विसर्पस्त्वित्यादि। बस्तिशीर्षज इति बस्तिजः शीर्षजश्र, शीर्ष शिरः। पद्मवर्ण इति लोहितपद्मवर्णः । शङ्वाभ्यां हृदयं यातीति शीर्षजः । पद्मपत्रतुल्यवर्णतां मुखतालुनि बहिर्देशे वेति वदन्ति। हृदयाद् गुदं यातीति बस्तिजः, ऊध्वी हृदयं गत्वा गुदं यातीत्यर्थः। अत्र पद्मसवर्णता बस्तिदेशे गुदे च। वाशब्दश्रात्र व्यवस्थित-विकल्पवचनः ॥ १४ ॥ क्षुद्ररोगे कथिते त्वगजल्ल्यहिपूतने॥ १५॥ मधुकोशः अन्यौ द्वौ विकारौ बालाना, भवतस्तावाह-क्षुद्रेत्यादि। स्निग्धा सवर्णेत्यादिनाऽजगलिका, कण्ड्रयनादि- त्यादिनाऽहिपूतना॥ १५ ॥ ज्वराद्या व्याधयः सर्वे महतां ये पुरेरिताः। बालदेहेऽपि ते तद्वद्विज्ञेयाः कुशलैः सदा॥ १६॥ मधुकोशः अन्येऽपि विकारा बालानां संभवन्तीत्यतिदेशेन तानाह-ज्वराद्या इत्यादि। पुरेरिता इति पूर्वोक्ताः। ते तद्वंदिति ते ज्वरादयस्तादृशा ज्ञेयाः । कुशलैरिति विज्ञेः ॥ १६ ॥ क्षणादुद्विजते बालः क्षणात्रस्यति रोदिति। नखैर्दन्तैर्दारयति धात्रीमात्मानमेव वा॥ १७॥ ऊर्ध्वं निरीक्षते दन्तान् खादेत् कूजति जृम्भते। भ्रवौ क्षिपति दन्तौष्ठ फेनं वमति चासकत्॥ १८॥ क्षामोऽति निशि जागर्ति शूनाक्षो भिन्नविट्स्वरः । मासंशोणितगन्धिश्च न चाश्नाति यथा पुरा ॥ १९ ॥ सामान्यं ग्रहजुष्टानां लक्षणं समुदाहतम्। मधुकोशः प्रायेण शौचभ्रंशादिना स्कन्दग्रहादयो नव बालेष्वावेशं कुर्वन्यतस्तत्परिज्ञानाय सामान्यलक्षणमाह- क्षणादुद्विजते बाल इत्यादि। एते ग्रहाः पूजार्थं बालान् हिंसन्ति। यदुक्तं सुश्रते-‘धात्रीमात्रोः प्राक प्रदिष्टापचाराच्छौचभ्रष्टान् मङ्गलाचारहीनान्। त्रस्तान् हष्टांस्तर्जितान् क्रन्दितान् वा पूजाहेतोर्हिस्युरेते कुमारान्॥' (सु.ड. २७) इति। उद्विजत इत्युद्विग्नो भवति; उद्विग्नो विह्वलः, नोतु विभेतीत्यर्थः, त्रस्यतीत्यनेन पौनरुक्त्य प्रसङ्गात्। कूजत्यार्तनादं करोति। भुवौ क्षिपतीति भ्रूभङ्गं रचयति। दन्तौष्ठमित्यत्र क्षिपतीति संबध्यते। क्षिपति खादति, धातूनामनेकार्थत्वात्। भिन्नविट् भिन्नशकृत्, भिन्नस्वरः स्वरभेदवान्। मांसशोणितगन्धिरिति विस्रगन्धि। न चाश्राति यथा पुरेति पूर्ववन्न भक्षयतीत्यर्थः ॥ १७–१९ ॥ एकनेत्रस्य गात्रस्य स्त्रावः स्पन्दनकम्पनम्॥ २०॥ ऊर्ध्वं दूष्ट्या निरीक्षेत वक्रास्यो रक्तगन्धिकः। दन्तान् खादति वित्रस्तः स्तन्यं नैवाभिनन्दति॥ २१॥ स्कन्दग्रहगृहीताना रोदनं चाल्पमेव च। मधुकोशः सामान्यलिङ्गमभिधाय विशेषग्रहलिङ्गमाह-एकनेत्रस्येत्यादि। एकनेत्रस्य वामस्य दक्षिणस्य वा स्रावोऽश्रु- स्नुतिः प्रभावात्, गात्रस्य स्रावो घर्मयुक्तगात्रतेत्यर्थः। स्पन्दनकम्पनमिति स्पन्दनं चलनं, कम्पनं महता वेगेन वेपनं; स्पन्दन कम्पन वा भवतीत्यर्थः । वक्रास्यो वक्रमुखः । रक्तगन्धिक इत्येतत् सामान्यलक्षणलब्धमप्यतिशयार्थमुक्तम्; एवमन्यत्रापि समान्यलक्षणे पुनरुक्ते व्याख्येयम्॥ २०–२१ ॥ नष्टसंज्ञो वमेत् फेनं संज्ञावानतिरोदिति। पूयशोणितगन्धित्वं स्कन्दापस्मारलक्षणम्॥ २२॥ मधुकोशः स्कन्दापस्मारलक्षणमाह-नष्टेत्यादि। नष्टसंज्ञो मूर्च्छितः सन् फेनं वमति, तथा संज्ञावान् सन्नतिरोदिति॥ २२॥ स्त्रस्ताड्गो भयचकितो विहङ्गन्धिः सास्त्रावव्रणपरिपीडितः समन्तात्। स्फोटैश्च प्रचिततनुः सदाहपाकै विंज्ञेयो भवति शिशुः क्षतः शकुन्या॥ २३॥ मधुकोशः शकुनीलक्षणमाह-स्रस्ताड्म इत्यादि। स्रस्ताड्म इति अङ्गस्रंसवद्व्यथावान्। भयचकित इति भयहेतुर्भयं भयानकमुच्यते, ततश्चकितः, असति भयहेतौ त्रस्यतीत्यर्थः। विहङ्गगंन्धिरिति विहङ्गस्येव गन्धो यस्य स तथा, उपमानाच्चेति समासान्त इत्यप्रत्ययः। विहङ्कशब्देन जलचरा मांसादाश्च पक्षिणो गृह्यन्ते, विस्रगन्धित्वात्। हिरण्याक्षेऽप्युक्त ‘संस्रावदाहपाकाद्यैश्चितः स्फोटैर्भयान्वितः। स्रस्ताङ्गो विस्रगन्धिः स्याच्छकुन्या पीडितः शिशुः ॥’ इति। सास्रावव्रणपरिपीडित इति स्फोटैरेव विदीर्णैर्वणरूपमापन्नैः परिपीडितः स्फोटैश्व प्रचिततनुरिति नवनवैः स्फोटैव्याप्ततनुः । क्षत इत्याभिभूतः ॥ २३ ॥ व्रणैः स्फोटैश्चितं गात्रं पड्कगन्धं स्त्रवेदसुक्। भिन्नवर्चा ज्वरी दाही रेवतीग्रहलक्षणम्॥ २४॥ अतीसारो ज्वरस्तृष्णा तिर्यक्प्रेक्षणरोदनम्। नष्टनिव्रस्तथोद्विग्रो ग्रस्तः पूतनया शिशुः ॥ २५ ॥ छर्दिः कासो ज्वरस्तृष्णा वसागन्धोऽतिरोदनम्। स्तन्यद्वेषोऽतिसारश्चर अन्धपूतनया भवेत्॥२६॥ वेपतो कासते क्षीणे नेत्ररोगो विगन्धिता। छर्द्यतीसारयुक्तश्च शीतपूतनया शिशुः ॥ २७॥ प्रसन्नवर्णवद्नः सिराभिरभिसंवृतः । मूत्रगन्धी च बह्वाशी मुखमण्डिकया भवेत्॥ २८॥ छर्दिंस्प( स्य )न्दनकण्ठास्यशोषमूर्च्छांविगन्धिताः । ऊर्ध्वं पश्येद्दशेद्दन्तान् नैगमेषग्रहं वदेत् ॥ २९ ॥ प्रस्तब्धाक्षः स्तनद्वेषी मुह्यते चानिशं मुहुः। तं बालमचिराद्धन्ति ग्रहः संपूर्णलक्षणः॥ ३०॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने बालरोगनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ६८॥ मधुकोशः रेवतीग्रहलक्षणमाह-व्रणैरित्यादि। व्रणैः पुराणैः, स्फोटैरविदीर्णैर्नूतनै, चितं व्याप्तम्। गात्रं पङ्कुगन्धं स्त्रवेदसुगिति गात्रमिति कर्तृपदें, पड्ढगन्धं शटितकर्दमगन्धं, समासविधेरनित्यत्वादिप्रत्ययो न भवति पूतनालक्षणमाह-अतीसार इत्यादि। ग्रस्त इति गृहीत इत्यर्थः॥ २४-३०॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां बालरोगनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥ ६८ ॥ स्थावरं जङ्गमं चैव द्विविधं विषमुच्यते। मूलाद्यात्मकमाद्यं स्यात् परं सर्पादिसंभवम्॥ १॥ मधुकोशः पारिशेष्याद्विषरोगनिदानमुच्यंते-स्थावरमित्यादि। विषादजनकत्वाद्विषं, तच्च द्विविधं स्थावरं जङ्गमं च। मूलाद्यत्मकमिति आद्य स्थावरं मूलादिरूपं दशविधं, यदुक्तं सुश्रुते-‘मूलं पत्रं फलं पुष्पं त्वक् क्षीरं सार एव च। निर्यासो धातवश्चैव कन्दश्च दशमः स्मृतः ' (सु.क. २) इति तत्र क्लीतकाश्चमारकगुझासुगन्धगर्गर्गर्गर्गर्गर्गर्ग विद्युच्छिखानन्ताविजयानीत्यष्टौ मूलविषाणि विषपत्रिकालम्बासुरदारुकरम्भमहाकरम्भाणि पञ्च पत्रविषाणि, कुमुद्वतीरेणुकाकरम्भमहाकरम्भकर्कोटकरेणुकखद्योतकचर्मरीभगन्धासर्पघातिनन्दनसारपाकानि द्वादश फल- विषाणि, वेत्रकादम्बवल्लीज करम्भमहाकरम्भाणि पञ्च पुष्पविषाणि, अन्त्रपाचककर्तरीयशैलेयकरम्भनन्दन- करघाटवाराटकानि सप्त त्वड्निर्याससारविषाणि, कुमुदघ्नीस्नुहीजालक्षीरीणि त्रीणि क्षीरविषाणि, फेनाश्म भस्म- हरितालं च द्वे धातुविषे, कालकूटवत्सनाभसर्षपकपालकर्दमक वैराटकमुस्तकमाहविषप्रपौण्डरीकमूलकहालाहल शृङ्गिमर्कटकानि त्रयोदश कन्दविषाणि, एतानि प्राणहराणि, एव पञ्चपञ्चाशत् स्थावराणि विषाणि भवन्ति। एषां च व्याधपुलिन्दादिभ्यो व्यक्तिज्ञानं कर्तव्यम्। परं सर्पादिसम्भवमिति परं जङ्गमं, तच्च षोडशाभिधानं- दृष्टिनिःश्वासविषा दिव्याः सर्पाः, भौमाः सर्पा दंष्टाविषाः, मार्जारमकरव्याघ्रादयो दंष्टानखविषाः, विश्चिट- कौण्डिन्यादयो मूत्रपुरीषविषाः, मूषिकाःशुक्रविषाः, वृश्चिकवरट्युच्चिटिङ्गादय आरविषाः, लूता लालातंव- विण्मूत्रशुक्रमुखसंदंशविषाः, चित्रशीर्षकशतदारुकशारिकादयो मुखसन्दंशदंष्टापर्दितगुदपुरीषविषाः, विषहता- स्थिमत्स्यास्थिप्रभूतयोऽस्थिविषाः, शकुलीमत्स्यादयः पित्तविषाः, सूक्ष्मतुण्डभ्रमरादयः शूकविषाः, कीटसर्पदेहा गतासवः शवविषाः । एषां च सुश्रुतस्य कल्पस्थाने विस्तरो द्रष्टव्यः ॥ १ ॥ निद्रां तन्द्रां क्लमं दाहमपाकं लोमहर्षणम्। शोथं चैवातिसारं च जङ्कमं कुरुते, विषम्॥ २॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59):

मधुकोशः बिसवर्त्मलक्षणमाह-त्रयो दोषा इत्यादि। बहिःशोथमिति बहिरुच्छूनत्वं यथा भवति तथा वर्त्मनोश्छिद्राणि दोषास्त्रयः कुर्युरित्यर्थः । तानि छिद्राणि अन्तर्मुखान्येव, यदाह-प्रस्त्रवन्त्यन्तरुदकमिति। छिद्राणीति बहुवचन- निर्देशाद्वहुमुखानि, अत्रापि दोषाः कुर्युरिति संबन्धः । अत एव बिसवन्मृणालवत्, तच्चानेकच्छिद्रयुक्तं भवति तद्वत्। अत्रैव चन्द्रिकाकारः सुश्रुते पठति-‘शूनं यद्वर्त्म बहुभिः श्लेक्ष्णेश्छिद्रैः समन्वित्। वर्त्मान्तरे विसमिव विसवर्त्मेति तत् स्मृतम्॥’ इति। सात्यकिरप्याह-‘बिसस्योपचितस्येव बहुमांससिरामुखम्। बिसवत्मेंति जानीयाद् दुश्चिकित्स्यं त्रिदोषजम्’ इति॥ ९५ ॥ वाताद्या वर्त्मसंकोचं जनयन्ति मला यदा। तदा द्रुष्ट न शक्रोति कुञ्चनं नाम तद्विदुः॥ ९६॥ ( सु.उ. ३ ) मधुकोशः कुञ्चनलक्षणमाह-वाताद्या इत्यादि। मला इत्यस्याभिधानं दुष्टत्वप्रतिपादनार्थं, यतो ‘मलिनीकरणान्मला’ इत्युच्यन्ते। कुश्चनं च कस्यापि तन्त्रस्य माधवकरेण लिखितं न सौश्रुतं, तेन सुश्रुतोक्तषट्सप्तिसंख्य न हीयते, एवं वक्ष्यमाणेऽपि पक्ष्मशाते बोद्धव्यम्॥ ९६॥ प्रचालितानि वातेन पक्ष्माण्यक्षि विशन्ति हि। घृष्यन्यक्षि मुहस्तानि संरम्भं जनयन्ति च॥ १७॥ असिते सितभागे च मूलकोषात् पतन्त्यपि। पक्ष्मकोपः स विज्ञेयो व्याधिः परमदारुणः ॥ ९८ ॥ ( सु.उ. २ ) मधुकोशः पक्ष्मकोपलक्षणमाह-प्रचालितानीत्यादि। प्रचालितानि प्रकर्षेण चालितानि, प्रतीपीकृतानीत्यर्थः। पक्ष्माणि वर्त्मरोमाणि वातचालितानि सन्ति नेत्रं प्रविशन्ति अन्तर्मुखानि वर्त्मन इत्यर्थः । तान्यसिते कृष्णमण्डले, सितभागे शक्लमण्डले वा अक्षिं घृष्यन्ति घर्षयन्तीत्यर्थः। अत एव संरम्भ श्रोथं जनयन्ति। मूलकोषात्, पक्ष्मेकोषात् पतन्त्यपीति ‘पक्ष्माणि’ इति शेषः, अपिशब्दान्न पतन्ति च। त्रिदोषजश्रायं, प्रचालने वातमात्रकारणत्वमुक्त; तथा च चन्द्रिकाकारः पाठान्तर पठति-‘पक्षमाशयगता दोषास्तीक्ष्णाग्रणि खराणि च। निर्वतंयन्ति पक्षमाणि तैर्घृष्ट चाक्षि दृष्यते॥ उद्धतैरुद्धतैः शान्तिः पक्ष्मभिश्रोपजायते।’ इति। अतः पक्ष्माशयों वर्त्म। विदेहोऽप्याह-‘यस्य वात- संबन्धेन दोषाः प्रकुपितास्त्रयः’ इत्यादिनेति। कल्याणविनिश्चये उपपक्ष्म पठ्यते-‘पक्ष्मोपरोधो वातेन कोठोऽन्तर्मुखरोगवान्। रोमैरन्तर्मुखैरन्यैरुपपक्ष्ममलैस्त्रिभिः॥' इति। उपपक्ष्मणि यादृशो पूर्वसिद्धा तादृश्य- पराऽन्तर्मुखी पक्ष्मपिड्क्तरिति भेदः, अस्य पक्ष्मोपरोधविशेषत्वात् समानचिकित्स्यत्वाच्य पृथगिहानभि- धानम्॥ ९७–९८ ॥ वर्त्मपक्ष्माशयगतं पित्तं रोमाणि शातयेत्। कण्डूं दाहं च कुरुते पक्ष्मशातं तमादिशेत्॥ ९९॥ नव सन्ध्याश्रयास्तेषु वर्त्मजास्त्वेककविंशतिः । शुक्लभागे दशैकश्र चत्वारः कृष्णभागजाः॥ १॥ः सर्वाश्रयाः सप्तदश दृष्टिजा द्वादशैव तु। बाह्यजौ द्वौ समाख्यातौ रोगो परमदारुणौ॥ २॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने नेत्ररोगनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥ ५९॥ मधुकोशः पक्ष्मशातलक्षणमाह-वर्मेत्यादि। पक्ष्माशयोऽत्र पक्ष्ममूलं, शातयेदुन्मूलयेदित्यर्थः। अयं च कफपैत्तिकः, कण्ड्रदाहवत्त्वात् । अत्र कृच्छ्रोन्मीलनं वाग्भटः पठति-‘रोगान् कुर्याच्चलस्तत्र प्राप्य वर्त्माश्रयाः सिराः । सुप्रोत्थितस्य कुरुते वर्त्मस्तम्भं सवेदनम्॥ पांशपूर्णाभनेत्रत्वं कृच्छ्रोन्मीलनमश्रू च। विमर्दनात् स्याच्य शमः कृच्छ्रोन्मीलं वदन्ति तम्' (वा.उ. ८) इति। अस्य चकारेण संग्रहः। पक्ष्मणां वर्त्माश्रयत्वादयमपि वर्त्मरोग एव। इति वर्त्मगता एकविंशतिर्व्याधयः समाप्ताः॥ ९९॥ इतिवर्त्मगताः॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां नेत्ररोगनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ५९॥
answer_text: When there is inflammation on the outer side of the eye-lid, the three dosas cause holes in it. These holes have opening towards in side only; as said- “they exude water inwardly". Chidrani - many holes-hence the similarity with the transeverse section of the stalk of a lotus flower. The author of candrikā reads the text of Suśruta as, “The eye-lid is swollen and has many small openings in side that look like the cut stalk of a lotus which is called bisavartma. (Su.u.3) Sātyaki also says", Like the cut stalk of a lotus, there will be many openings (in side the eye-lid) of muscle and veins this is called bisavartma; caused by tridosa and is difficult for cure". 95. Kuñcana Vāta etc; turbid factors cause constriction of the eye-lids, the individual will not be able to see anything. This condition is called kuñcana. 96. The term used for vāta etc., is malāḥ (the turbid factors) which denotes their nature of causing turbidity. This kancana has been taken from some book by Mādhavakara and it is not related to Suśruta by which there will be no change in number of diseases of the eye of Suśruta. Same is applicable to the Pakṣmaśāta which will be explained further. Paksmakopa (Trichiasis) The eye-lashes, disturbed by vata grow towards the eye-ball, there by cause friction and irritation repeatedly on the black and white part of the eye-ball and they also fall from the follicles. This serious condition is called Pakṣmakopa. 97, 98. (Su. u. 2). Mādhavanidānaṃ Pracalitani means - shaken extensively. When the eye-lashes are shaken by vāta, they grow in opposite direction towards the eye-ball and cause friction to the black and white parts of the eye and thereby irritate the eye. They may also fall down, as understood by the word api. This disease is of tridosa nature but the role of vāta is to disturb the direction of the eye-lashes. The author of Candrikā gives different text “the dosas that take shelter in the follicles of eye-lashes facilitate sharp and rough lashes by which the eye is bruised and irritated." Su.u.3 Paksmāśaya is the eye-lid. Videha also said, “The three doṣas take shelter in the eye lids……” In Kalyān aviniścaya, it is read, “Pakṣmāparodha takes place by vātā by which they grow inwardly causing upapaksma (Secondary growth of eye lashes).This condition is caused by trimala (Tridoşa)”. Upa pakşma is the secondary inward growth of eye-lashes. This being charecterised by paksmoparodha and can be treated in the same manner, is not seperately mentioned. 97-98. Paksmaśāta (Madarosis) The Pitta, seated in the eye lid and the base of eye-lash follicles, makes the lashes fall and cause itching and burning sensation. This condition is called pakṣmaśāta. 99. (Nine, in the joints of the eye, eleven in the eye lids, eleven in the white part, four in the black part, seventeen that affect the complete eye, Twelve in the sightarea and two externally are the total diseases affecting the eye. Thus ends the chapter on the diseases of eye in the Madhava's book on diagnosis written by Srīmādhavakara. Netra Roga Nidāna Pakṣmāśaya means the root of eye-lashes; Ṣātayet means roots out. This is kapha paittika disease as there is itching and burning sensation. Vagbhaṭa adds Kṛcchrormīlana opening with difficulty to this stanza. He says, “The doṣas reach the veins located in the vartma and cause numbness, rigidity and pain there (in the eye lids). The eyes are felt like filled with sand, they open with difficulty and this condition is (temproarily) pacified by rubbing which is called krcchronnilana” The twenty one diseases are completed with this. Thus end the diseases of eye-lids. 99. Thus ends the chapter on eye-disease in the Madhukosa commentary written by Srikanthadatta. 59. ＊＊＊＊
