question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2):

विषमज्वरविशेषानाहविदग्ध इत्यादि । विदग्धेऽन्नरसे दुष्टे आहाररसे तथा दुष्टे श्लेष्मणि पित्ते दुष्टे देहे व्यवस्थिते भवतः तेन हेतुना देहमधं शीतलं कफेनाधं चोष्णं पित्तेन प्रजायते । अर्धत्वं चार्धनारीश्वराकारेण नरसिंहाकारेण वा यथादोषं व्यवस्थानियमहेतोर- भावादिति । काय इत्यादि । काये अन्तरग्नौ कोष्ठे इति यावत् । अन्ते हस्तपादयोंः । उक्तार्थस्य विपर्ययेण जवरान्तरमाहकाये श्लेष्मेत्यादि । त्वक्स्थावित्यादि । त्वक्शब्देन त्वक्स्थो रस डच्यते तत्स्थस्य तुदुपचारेणेति गदाधरः जेज्जटस्तु त्वचमेवाह । एतदभिप्रायेणेव चरकेण ज्वरेऽभ्यङ्गाथं तैलादीन्यभिधायोक्तःतैराशु प्रशमं याति बहिर्मार्गगतो ज्वरः ॥ चचि इति । तयोः श्लेष्मानिलयोः । प्रशान्तयोरिति प्रशान्तवेगयोरित्यर्थः नहि विषमेषु दोषस्य प्रशान्तिर्भवति पुनर्वेगागमात् । यदाह सुश्रुतः स चापि विषमो देहं न कदाचिद्विमुद्वति । ग्लानिगौरवकार्श्येध्यः स यस्मान्न प्रमुच्यते ॥ वेगे तु समतिक्रान्ते गतोऽयमिति लक्ष्यते । धात्वन्तरस्थो लीनत्वात् सीक्ष्यान्नैवोपलभ्यते ॥ सु०उ० - इति । इतरी वातकफी । दाहशीतादीति एक्रो दाहादिः अपरः शीतादिः । ननु एतयोः सम्प्राप्तौ त्रिदोषजत्वमुक्त तत् कथं संसर्गजावित्युक्तं संसर्गो हि द्वयोभवति त्रयाणां सन्निपात इति स्थितिः । उच्यते संसर्थः सम्बन्धः स च हयोवहूनां च भवति अत्र त्रयाणामुक्तः न चैवं सर्वत्र अथवा संसर्गः सोम्यानेयदोषकोटिद्वयमेलापः । तत्र शीतादों ज्वरे पित्तमनुवन्यः दाहादी वातकफावनुवन्यै अनुवन्ध्य प्राधान्येन चिकित्स्योऽनुबन्धा- विरोधेनेति प्रयोजनमेतस्य । तयोदाहशीतादिज्वरयोर्मध्ये दाहपूर्वो दाहादिः कष्ट इति दुःखप्रदः । दाहादेः कष्टसाध्यत्वामिधानेन शीतदेरर्थतोऽकथ्वमिति । उक्तविषमज्वराणामुपलक्षण- व्वादन्येऽपि विपमज्वरा रात्रिज्वरादयो वोद्धव्या इति जेज्जटः । उक्तं च तन्त्रान्तरे समो वातकफी यस्य क्षीणपितस्य देहिनः । प्रायो रात्री ज्वरात्रास्य दिवा हीनकफस्य तु ॥ इति । सर्वेपु च विषमज्वरेप्ववश्यम्भावी वायुः । यदाह कुछपुष्ट्रतः नर्तंडनिलाद्वै विषमज्वरः समुपजायते । कफपित्ते हि निश्चेष्ट चेष्टयत्यनिलः सदा ।। इति । तथा विदेहेऽपिपवनो गतिवैषम्याद्विषमज्वरकारणम् ।। इति । एषां च ज्वराणामृत्वादिहेत्वन्तरलाभादन्यथाभावोऽपि दृश्यते । तद्यथा सन्ततः स्वरूपं त्यक्त्वा सततादीनामन्यतमत्वं प्रतिपद्यते तथा चतुर्थकस्तृतीयकादिरूपत्वम् । यदाह चरकः ऋत्वहोरात्रदोषाणां मनसश्च वलाबलात् । कालमर्थवशाच्चैव ज्वरस्तं तं प्रपद्यते ॥ च०चि० इति । अस्यार्थःबलावलादिति ऋत्वादिमनोन्तेन सम्बध्यते वलं चाबलं च बलाबलम् । अर्थशव्दोऽत्र प्राक्तनकर्मवाची । ते ते कालं सततकाद्युक्त ज्वरः प्रतिपद्यत इति योजना । उदाहरणं च ऋत्वहोरात्रबलाबलाद्यथायदा निदाघोत्पन्नो वातप्रधानश्चतुर्थको वर्षासमयमाप्नोति तदा तेनर्तुनाऽऽप्यायितबलस्तृतीयकान्तानां सततकादीनामन्यतमत्वं प्राप्नोत्युत्कर्षात् । एवं वर्षात्समुत्पन्नः सन्ततः शरदं प्राप्यापकृष्टवलः सततादीनामन्यतमत्वमेत्यपकर्षात् । एवं पित्तकफयोरप्युत्कर्षापकर्षावृतुकृतौं व्याख्येयौं । अहोरात्रशब्देन कतिपयान्यहोरात्राणि गृह्यन्ते नह्येकस्मिन्नहोरात्रे सततादीनामुत्कर्षापकर्षाभ्या- मन्यथाभाव उपपद्यते किन्तु कतिपयैरेव । यदा वर्षा-शरद्वसन्तप्रारम्भे वातादयो ज्वरं चतुर्थक- मारभन्ते तदा मध्यानि कतिपयदिनान्यवाप्य स एव तृतीयकपूर्वत्वेन विपरिणमते उत्कर्षात् अपकर्षात्तु यदाऽन्त्यानि दिनान्याप्नोति तदा सन्ततो वातारब्धः प्रावृषः पित्तारब्धः शारदो वसन्तस्य च श्लेष्मारव्यः प्रतनुकत्वादोषस्य सततादीनामन्यतमत्वेन विपरिणमत इति । दोषबलाबलाद्यथायदा सततादीनामन्यतमकारी दोषः श्लेष्मा मधुरस्निग्धादीन् दिवास्वप्ना दीश्च हेतूनाप्नोति तदा सन्ततकादीन् करोति । एवं वातपित्तयोरप्यूह्यम् । मनोबलाबलाद्यथा यदा सन्ततज्वरी सत्त्वगुणोद्रेकात् प्रहर्षावष्टम्भवहुलो भवति तदा सततादीनामन्यतमत्वं प्राप्नोति यदा चतुर्थकज्वरी प्राज्ञापरा धाद्देवादीनभिभूयाहितान्याचरति तदा तृतीयकपूर्वेषामन्यतमत्वमाप्नोति यदा तु शुद्धसत्वो- स त्कर्षाद्विवेकिन्या बुध्या युक्तः स्यात्तदा श्रुभानि देवताराधनेष्टिबल्युपहारादीन्याचरति तदा सन्ततज्वरी से सेततादीनामन्यतमत्वं से प्राप्नोति । अर्थवशाद्यथा सेन्ततज्वरिणोंऽपि यदि चतुर्थकवेदनीयं कर्म स्यात्तदा सन्ततोऽपि चतुर्थकत्वेन विपरिणमते अथ चतुर्थकज्वराविष्टस्य यदि तत्कालपरिपाकि कर्म बलीयो चास्योपजायते ॥॥ - - - - - - -
answer_text: The passage relates to the descriptions of the various types of irregular or visama fevers. In this context, two types of body positions have been mentioned, the position of Ardhanāriśvara and the position of Narasimha. The first position suggests a situation when half of the body remains cold while the other half is warm. The second position signifies a condition when the lower half of the body remains warm whiles the other half remains cold or vice versa. The heat is due to pitta while kapha is the causative factor for the cool touch. As there is no certainty of the vitiation of these dosas the exact locations of the cold and warm portions of the body could not be defined as such. However, an attempt has been made to explain the situations as below: When there is vitiated pitta in the so-named kosthapradesa (that is the stomach, pancreas, duodenum, urinary tract, heart, unduka and lungs) then the whole body gets fever. When there is vitiated kapha lodged in the arms and the legs then these limbs remain cold. When the vitiated kapha lodges above the kosthapradesa then the torso of the patient remains cold. Similarly, when there is vitiated pitta in the arms and the legs then these limbs remain warm. Gadādhara opines that ‘the dosas seated in the skin’ implies that those are seated in the rasa (chyle) existing in the skin because the treatment would be aimed at the rasa only. Jejjata feels that it is the skin only that provides room to the dosas. Caraka states that application of oil on the skin gives faster relief from fever (CS. Ci. 3.175). Hence, the involvement of skin is confirmed. The narrative 'when the starting dosa pacifies' should not be taken as indicating a complete pacification as the irregular fever related dosas only shift their seat from one tissue or the limb to the other and during this transition, the bout of temperature comes down but only temporarily. It gives room for a feeling that the dosa was pacified. However, the vitiated dosa hardly leaves the body. At the time of temporary relief, there is the feeling of heaviness, lack of zeal and emaciation (SS. Ut. 39.63-64). However, even after the bouts of fever are over the dosa remains there seated inside the rasa (chyle) and like dhātus. As it is quite minor, the patient or physician generally do not realize its presence. The term itarau signifies the vāla and kapha. The term dahasitadi suggests that one of the dosas is capable to produce heat while the other is capable to produce coldness. Someone could raise the objection on the inclusion of the disease among the samsargaja fevers, for this ailment has been included among the tridoṣaja fevers and the saṁsargaja fevers are those that are produced by only two of the dosas. Nevertheless, it is said that Samsarga has two meanings; it could indicate relationship, which might be of two or more factors or dosas, now; it could also mean the association of the Saumya (soft cool) and Agneya (fiery or heating) factors or doṣas. It is to be noted that in Sītādi (starting with coldness) fever, there is added relation or Anubandha of pitta while in Dahadi (starting with heat and burning sensation) sort of fever there is added relation of the vāta and kapha doṣas. Thus, the term saṁsargaja has been highlighted to plan the treatment without disturbing the Anubandhya (the principal) doṣɑ. It has been indicated that the dāhapūrva jvara is severe and difficult for cure while the śītapūrva jvara is not so severe and is easily curable. The commentator Jejjaṭa has suggested inclusion among the viṣama jvaras those types of fever also that occur only during the nightly hours. It has been also said in some other treatises that when one has his vāta and kapha doṣas equally strengthened while his pitta contents remain mild, the individual has fever during nights that is called rūtri jvara and if his kapha dosa is mild fever occurs during the daytime (divā jvara). Moreover, it is to be noted that vāyu is an essential factor in all the irregular fevers. As supported by Vrddha Susruta, without the involvement of anila (vata), visama jvara (irregular fever) does not occur. The inert kapha and pitta are activated by vāta.’ (SS. Ut. 39). (Note: though the work Madhu Kośa has quoted the name of Vṛddha Suśruta, the available copies of Suśruta Saṁhitā do not contain the quoted passage as reported by Śrī Brahmānanda Tripāthi). The text composed by Videha also states that viṣama jvara occurs due to the irregular activity of vāta. With the help of factors like rtu (season) etc., the above mentioned visama jvara, change their nature. And apart from the features described above they manifest symptoms that are opposite to the above description. For example, the santata fever frees itself from the features described above and turns itself into one of the satata fevers like the so-named trtiyaka or caturthaka. Caraka has also stated that ‘based on the strength and weakness of season day, night, doṣa, manas, time, fate and like factors, fevers transform their nature.’ (CS. Ci. 3.74). Example for this trans- 122. formation is the vāta-predominant caturthaka or tertian fever, which when occurring in the summer season gets strengthened in rainy season and transforms itself into one of the Satata, Anyedyuşka and Trüyaka fevers. The other factors are also to be understood in the same way. Likewise, the santata jvara occurring in the rainy seasons is weakened during the winters and consequently it turns into one of the satata fevers. The term ahorātra referred here involves a few days and not a period of 24 hours. In fact, fluctuation in physical condition is not possible within the limited period of one day as far as the different varieties of viṣama jvaras are concerned. When the vāta etc. produce the caturthaka jvara in the rainy season, winter season, and the spring, this fever is strengthened and promotes itself into the trifyaka type of fever. However, these dosas are weakened during the final days of the above seasons. Sub¬ sequently, the vāta dominant santata type of fever originating in the rainy season, the pitta -dominant santata type of fever originating in the winter season, and the kapha-dominant santata type of fever originating in the rainy season, turn into satata etc. like viṣama jvaras in due course of time. The other examples of the shifting nature of the visama jvara could be presented as below: Example of the impact of the strength of dosas: The kapha induced satata fever is strengthened due to intake of sweet, oily items and by sleeping during daytime, etc. Then the satata fever turns into santataka fever. Example of the impact of the strength of manas: The patient of santata fever transfers his disease to satata fever when he comes to stabilize his mind by the increased quality of sattvaguṇɑ. Likewise, the patient of caturthaka fever turns into a patient of tṛtīyaka fever if his mind becomes obsessed by tamoguna through sorrow and the like factors. It may be noted that sorrow is one of the significant factors to impact on one’s health. Caraka has also emphasized it (CS. Str. 25.39). Example of the impact of strength of buddhi: The patient of caturthaka fever converts his disease to trifyaka fever when he comes to knowingly commit misdemeanor against the deities, teachers and the priests. In that case, the patient should engage himself in such acts as the worship of deities, organization of sacrifice, offering ceremony and making donations. Such acts help the patient transfer the tṛtīyaka fever into satata fever. Example of the impact of the strength of the deeds of past lives: It is believed that if the deeds of the past lives of a patient were worth or capable to produce caturthaka jvara then the santata jvara of the patient would turn into the caturthaka jvara only. If the deeds of the patient are otherwise, his Caturthaka jvara could also convert into santata jvara. Likewise, the relationship of the season, timing, and strength or weaknesses of the doşas all are interlinked. These topics have been detailed at relevant places as well. Dhātu (tissue) based fevers If the jvara (fever) is lodged in the blood plasma (rasadhātu), it manifests with a feeling of heaviness in the body, nausea, debility, vomiting, loss of appetite and a feeling of helplessness. 48

चार्धनारीश्वराकारेण नरसिंहाकारेण वा यथादोषं व्यवस्थानियमहेतोर- भावादिति । काय इत्यादि । काये अन्तरग्नौ कोष्ठे इति यावत् । अन्ते हस्तपादयोंः । उक्तार्थस्य विपर्ययेण जवरान्तरमाहकाये श्लेष्मेत्यादि । त्वक्स्थावित्यादि । त्वक्शब्देन त्वक्स्थो रस डच्यते तत्स्थस्य तुदुपचारेणेति गदाधरः जेज्जटस्तु त्वचमेवाह । एतदभिप्रायेणेव चरकेण ज्वरेऽभ्यङ्गाथं तैलादीन्यभिधायोक्तःतैराशु प्रशमं याति बहिर्मार्गगतो ज्वरः ॥ चचि इति । तयोः श्लेष्मानिलयोः । प्रशान्तयोरिति प्रशान्तवेगयोरित्यर्थः नहि विषमेषु दोषस्य प्रशान्तिर्भवति पुनर्वेगागमात् । यदाह सुश्रुतः स चापि विषमो देहं न कदाचिद्विमुद्वति । ग्लानिगौरवकार्श्येध्यः स यस्मान्न प्रमुच्यते ॥ वेगे तु समतिक्रान्ते गतोऽयमिति लक्ष्यते । धात्वन्तरस्थो लीनत्वात् सीक्ष्यान्नैवोपलभ्यते ॥ सु०उ० - इति । इतरी वातकफी । दाहशीतादीति एक्रो दाहादिः अपरः शीतादिः । ननु एतयोः सम्प्राप्तौ त्रिदोषजत्वमुक्त तत् कथं संसर्गजावित्युक्तं संसर्गो हि द्वयोभवति त्रयाणां सन्निपात इति स्थितिः । उच्यते संसर्थः सम्बन्धः स च हयोवहूनां च भवति अत्र त्रयाणामुक्तः न चैवं सर्वत्र अथवा संसर्गः सोम्यानेयदोषकोटिद्वयमेलापः । तत्र शीतादों ज्वरे पित्तमनुवन्यः दाहादी वातकफावनुवन्यै अनुवन्ध्य प्राधान्येन चिकित्स्योऽनुबन्धा- विरोधेनेति प्रयोजनमेतस्य । तयोदाहशीतादिज्वरयोर्मध्ये दाहपूर्वो दाहादिः कष्ट इति दुःखप्रदः । दाहादेः कष्टसाध्यत्वामिधानेन शीतदेरर्थतोऽकथ्वमिति । उक्तविषमज्वराणामुपलक्षण- व्वादन्येऽपि विपमज्वरा रात्रिज्वरादयो वोद्धव्या इति जेज्जटः । उक्तं च तन्त्रान्तरे समो वातकफी यस्य क्षीणपितस्य देहिनः । प्रायो रात्री ज्वरात्रास्य दिवा हीनकफस्य तु ॥ इति । सर्वेपु च विषमज्वरेप्ववश्यम्भावी वायुः । यदाह कुछपुष्ट्रतः नर्तंडनिलाद्वै विषमज्वरः समुपजायते । कफपित्ते हि निश्चेष्ट चेष्टयत्यनिलः सदा ।। इति । तथा विदेहेऽपिपवनो गतिवैषम्याद्विषमज्वरकारणम् ।। इति । एषां च ज्वराणामृत्वादिहेत्वन्तरलाभादन्यथाभावोऽपि दृश्यते । तद्यथा सन्ततः स्वरूपं त्यक्त्वा सततादीनामन्यतमत्वं प्रतिपद्यते तथा चतुर्थकस्तृतीयकादिरूपत्वम् । यदाह चरकः ऋत्वहोरात्रदोषाणां मनसश्च वलाबलात् । कालमर्थवशाच्चैव ज्वरस्तं तं प्रपद्यते ॥ च०चि० इति । अस्यार्थःबलावलादिति ऋत्वादिमनोन्तेन सम्बध्यते वलं चाबलं च बलाबलम् । अर्थशव्दोऽत्र प्राक्तनकर्मवाची । ते ते कालं सततकाद्युक्त ज्वरः प्रतिपद्यत इति योजना । उदाहरणं च ऋत्वहोरात्रबलाबलाद्यथायदा निदाघोत्पन्नो वातप्रधानश्चतुर्थको वर्षासमयमाप्नोति तदा तेनर्तुनाऽऽप्यायितबलस्तृतीयकान्तानां सततकादीनामन्यतमत्वं प्राप्नोत्युत्कर्षात् । एवं वर्षात्समुत्पन्नः सन्ततः शरदं प्राप्यापकृष्टवलः सततादीनामन्यतमत्वमेत्यपकर्षात् । एवं पित्तकफयोरप्युत्कर्षापकर्षावृतुकृतौं व्याख्येयौं । अहोरात्रशब्देन कतिपयान्यहोरात्राणि गृह्यन्ते नह्येकस्मिन्नहोरात्रे सततादीनामुत्कर्षापकर्षाभ्या- मन्यथाभाव उपपद्यते किन्तु कतिपयैरेव । यदा वर्षा-शरद्वसन्तप्रारम्भे वातादयो ज्वरं चतुर्थक- मारभन्ते तदा मध्यानि कतिपयदिनान्यवाप्य स एव तृतीयकपूर्वत्वेन विपरिणमते उत्कर्षात् अपकर्षात्तु यदाऽन्त्यानि दिनान्याप्नोति तदा सन्ततो वातारब्धः प्रावृषः पित्तारब्धः शारदो वसन्तस्य च श्लेष्मारव्यः प्रतनुकत्वादोषस्य सततादीनामन्यतमत्वेन विपरिणमत इति । दोषबलाबलाद्यथायदा सततादीनामन्यतमकारी दोषः श्लेष्मा मधुरस्निग्धादीन् दिवास्वप्ना दीश्च हेतूनाप्नोति तदा सन्ततकादीन् करोति । एवं वातपित्तयोरप्यूह्यम् । मनोबलाबलाद्यथा यदा सन्ततज्वरी सत्त्वगुणोद्रेकात् प्रहर्षावष्टम्भवहुलो भवति तदा सततादीनामन्यतमत्वं प्राप्नोति यदा चतुर्थकज्वरी तमोगुणभूयिष्ठत्वाद्विषादादभिभूयते तदा तृतीयकादीनामन्यतमो भवति विषादो रोगवर्धनानाम् च०सू० इत्यागमात्। अन्ये तु मनःशब्देन बुद्धि व्याख्यानयन्ति कारणे कार्योपचारात् । तस्याश्च बलाबल यथायदा चतुर्थकज्वरी प्राज्ञापरा धाद्देवादीनभिभूयाहितान्याचरति तदा तृतीयकपूर्वेषामन्यतमत्वमाप्नोति यदा तु शुद्धसत्वो- स त्कर्षाद्विवेकिन्या बुध्या युक्तः स्यात्तदा श्रुभानि देवताराधनेष्टिबल्युपहारादीन्याचरति तदा सन्ततज्वरी से सेततादीनामन्यतमत्वं से प्राप्नोति । अर्थवशाद्यथा सेन्ततज्वरिणोंऽपि यदि चतुर्थकवेदनीयं कर्म स्यात्तदा सन्ततोऽपि चतुर्थकत्वेन विपरिणमते अथ चतुर्थकज्वराविष्टस्य यदि तत्कालपरिपाकि कर्म बलीयो question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Takra Varga, Chapter 15, verse 1021):

घोल तु मथित तक्रमुदश्चिच्छाच्छिकाऽपि च । ससर निर्जल घोल मथित त्वसरोदकम् ।।१।। तक्रं पादजलं प्रोक्तमुदश्चित्वर्द्धवारिकमु । छच्छिका सारहीना स्यात्स्वच्छा प्रचुरवारिका । घोलं तु शर्करायुक्त गुणैल्लेयं रसालवत् ।।२११ घोलं तु शर्करायुक्त गुणैज़यं रसालवत् । वातपित्तहरं ह्रादि मथितं कफपित्तनुत् ।।३।। तक्र ग्राहि कषायाम्ल स्वादु पाकरस लघु । वीर्योष्ण दीपन वृष्य प्रीणन वातनाशनम् ।।४।। ग्रहण्यादिमता पथ्यं भवेत्सड्याहि लाघवात् । किञ्च स्वादुविपाकित्वान्न च पित्तप्रकोपणम् ।।।५।। अम्लोष्ण दीपन वृष्य प्रीणन वातनाशनम् । कषायोष्णविकाशित्वाद्रौक्ष्याच्चापि कफापहम् ।।।६।। न तक्रसेवी व्यथते कदाचिन्न तक्रदग्याः प्रभवन्ति रोगाः । यथा सुराणाममृत सुखाय तथा नराणा भुवि तक्रमाहुः ।।७।। उदश्चित् कफकृद् बल्यमामध्यं परमं मतमू । छच्छिका श्रीतला लघ्वी पित्तश्रमतृषाहरी । वातनुत् कफकृत् सा तु दीपनी लवणान्विता ।।८।। समुद्धृतघृतं तक्रं पथ्यं लघु विशेषतः ।।’९।। स्तोकोद्धतघृत तस्माद् गुरु वृष्य कफापहम् । अनुद्धतघृत सान्द्र गुरु पुष्टिकफप्रदम् ।।१०।। वातेऽम्लं शस्यते तक्रं शुण्ङ्गीसैन्यवसंयुतम् । पित्ते स्वादु सितायुक्तं व्योषक्षारयुतं कफे ।।११।। हिङ्गजीरयुतं घोलं सैन्यवेन च संयुतम् । भवेदतीव वातघ्नमर्शोऽतीसारहृत्परम् ।।१२।। रुचिद पुष्टिद बल्य वस्तिशूलविनाशनम् । मूत्रकृच्छे तु सगुडं पाण्डुरोगे सचित्रकम् ।।१३।।
answer_text: Based on their properties and differ in water proportion different names has been given - Ghola, Mathita, Takra, Udachita and Chachikā. Different names are given according to different properties and preparation methods of Takra- they are Ghola, Mathita, Takra, Udaśvit and Chacchikā. S.no Different types Method of preparation of Takras. Ghola Prepared by churning curd without removing fat and adding water. Mathita Prepared by churning curd by removing supernated fat and without adding water. Takra Prepared by churning curd by adding four parts of water. Udaśvit Prepared by churning curd by adding half part of water. Chacchikā Prepared by churning curd removing supernated fat and repeat n the content of churning by adding sufficient quantity of water. If sarkara is added into the Ghola, its properties are equavalent to Rasala. It subsides Vāta, Pitta doṣa and Aālladhajanaka (Pleasent to body and mind). Mathita subsides Kapha and Pitta doṣa. Takra is Kaṣāya (Astringent), Amla (Sour) and Madhura (Sweet) in taste, Madhura vīpaka (Sweet in post digestive), Grahī (Absorbent), Laghu (Light for digestion), Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency), Dīpana (Appetizer), Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac), Prinanam (Satisfying) and subsides Vāta. In Grahani (Spure) etc., diseases Takra is a ideal drink, being Laghu (Light for digestion) it acts as Grahī (Absorbent), Madhura vīpaka (Pungent in post digestion) and doesn’t aggravates Pitta. Being amla rasa (Sour), Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency), Dīpana (Appetizer), Vrṣya (Aphrodisiac) and Pinana (Satisfying), it aggravates Vāta. Being as Kaşāya (Astringent), Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency), Vīkasi (immuno suppressant) and Rūṣka (Drying), it subsides Kapha. Person who consumes the Takra regularly as diet never becomes ill, diseases cured by takra do not recurved, just as amrta (divine nector) is for the gods, takra is to humans. Udaśvit increases Kapha, Balya (Promotes strength), relieves excessive Ama (Undigested food). Chacchikā is Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Laghu (Light for digestion), Subsides Vāta, increases Kapha. It cures Srama (Fatigue) and Tṛṣṇā (Thrist). If it is taken along with Sindhava lavana, acts as Dīpana (Appetizer). Takra which is deviod of Ghṛta is acts as Pathya (Ideal diet) and Laghu (Light for digestion). if Ghṛta is partly removed is Guru (Heavy for digestion), Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac) and subsides Kapha and Vāta. If Ghṛta is not removed is Guru (Heavy for digestion), Pustikara (Nutrient) and Increases Kapha dosa. Usage of Takra as per Dosa andVyadhi: In case of aggravated Vāta, Amla (Sour) butter milk along with Suṇṭhī and Saiṇḍhava lavaṇa is ideal. In case of aggravated Pitta, Madhura (Sweet) butter milk along with sugar is ideal. In case of Increased Kapha, Takra along with Sunṭhi, Marica, Pippali and Yava kṣara is best. If Ghola is taken along with Hingu, Jīraka, and Saindhava lavaņa, it will increases Vāta, cures Arśas (Haemorrhoids), Atisāra (Diarrhoea), Rucya (Promotes taste), Puṣṭikara (Nutrient), Balya (Promotes strength) and Basti śūla nāṣaka (Cures bladder colic). Ghola along with guda is beneficial in Mūtrakṛcchra (Dysuria) and along with Chitraka it is good in Pāṇḍu (Anemia)

explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Takra Varga, Chapter 15, verse 1021.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 5, verse 1):

यत्र तु स्वकारणात् त्रयोऽपि कुपितास्तत्र त्रिदोषव्यपदेश इति सिद्धान्तः; एवं सर्वत्र ॥१॥
answer_text: If the etiology and symptoms of any two of the three dosas are seen combined in a particular patient of piles, it is to be understood that he is suffering from 'dvandva' (dual dosa) affliction. If all the etiological factors of all of the three dosas have become instrumental in producing the disease, it is called Tridosa Arsa or piles caused by all the three dosas. The symptoms of this condition are, however, identical to that of the Sahaja Arsa (congenital piles). Etiolgy of piles of three dosa afflictions (CS. Ci. 14.20/2) All types of etiological factors may be roughly identical in the types; features of the hereditary piles are also similar. 9 If the individual etiological factors mentioned in the context of the piles based on the three varieties of dosas are combined, they become the causative factors for what is called Sannipata or iridosaja piles. The symptoms of Sahaja or congenital variety of piles are similar to that of Sannipāta (having the involvement of three dosas). In the sahaja variety of piles, according to Susruta, the piles are unshapely, rough, and pale, reddish in colour has cuts and are inverted inside. One who suffers from such pile gets emaciated, cats low quantity of food, has bulged veins, has few offsprings, produces less quantity of semen, has a weak voice, gets angry frequently and has mild digestive fire. The patient also suffers from diseases of nose, head, eye, and ear; his intestines make sounds; he has bloated abdomen; he feels that his heart is covered with something and he has distaste. (SS. Ni. 2.15). Caraka has also elaborated the features of piles on the same line ( CS. Ci.14.6 ). Now the question arises as to when all the diseases are considered to be caused by none other than the tridosas why is there a separate enumeration by the name Tridosaja Arsa. It has been also said elsewhere that there is no drug of one single and exclusive taste (there is indeed more than one rasas in every substance) nor there is any disease of one single dosa (there is indeed instrumentality of more than one dosa in every disease) and that is being so, there is need to indicate the major rasa or the major dosa. However, as per the statement of Caraka, vala, pilla and Slesma move all over the body and hence, if one of the dhatus were vitiated by one dosa, the other two dosas would participate in the act of Vitia- tion due to the inherent relationship of the vitiated and the vitiator (CS. Su. 20.8). The vata dosa is aggravated due to its own reasons but it gets some amount of coldness from kapha and lightness from pilla and thus becomes aggravated. Pina also, due to its pungency, gets some support from vata and the liquidity from kapha. Likewise, kapha also turns powerful by taking cold quality from vala and If- quidity from pitta. That is why it is considered that there is no disease of single dosa vitiation. With the same view, it is considered that one vitiated dosa would subsequently vitiate all others. Wherever the efi- ology of vitiation due to all the three of the dosas exists, from the very beginning the situation is identified as the tridosa-induced ail- ment. Everywhere this theory has to be applied. Symptomatology of vāta type of piles ll 1 3 li (A H, Ni. 7.28/2-34/1) The features of vātaja Arṣa are the following: The muscular sprouts in the anus affected by piles caused by provoked vata are dry, with pricking sensation, thin in consistency, blackish red, rigid, with no exudation, harsh, coarse, irregular in shape and size, bent, poignant, and cracked at the ends. They look like the fruits of bimbī (the plant Cephelendra indica), kharjūra (date palm), karkandhū (the plant Zizyphus ceroplia), kārpāsa (cotton), kadamba flower (having several sprouts) and some like mustard seeds (very small in size). The patient eliminates faeces which is scrabulous, scanty, associated with noise, straining and painful; frothy and semi¬ solid in consistence and has skin, nails, faeces, urine, eyes and face becomes black in colour. Gulma (abdominal tumor), plihā (splenic enlargements), udara (enlargement of abdomen) and asthila (enlargement of prostate) may appear as its implication. 10-15

question:

answer_text: This passage underlines the severe consequences of overeating. Anatmavanta are the individuals with indecent mind and a lust for temporary satisfaction and greed. The use of the term atma here is very significant. It highlights the fact that ātmā or one’s soul is pure and knowledgeable. Characteristics like greed are not compatible with one’s soul. That is why the greed to consume more food has been accepted as un-soulful or anatma type of conduct. Disregard to the factors denoting the consumable and non-consumable is tanta¬ mount to the habit of an animal. That is why the senseless eater has been compared with an animal. Finally, it has been suggested that indigestion produces innumerable diseases like visuci (gastro-enteri- tis) and alasaka, and vilambika. (SS. Ut. 56.3) hills 1999), fixe Amājīrṇa, vidagdha, and viṣṭabdha are the three types of indigestion which produce diseases named visūcikā, alasaka and vilambikā respectively. 15

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 20, verse 17):

— अवाश्यीत्यादि अवाश्यी अधोमुखः, उदश्ची ऊर्घ्वमुखः, अत एवान्ये अवाङ्मुखस्तुन्मुखो वा इति पठन्ति । जागरूकोऽनिद्रः अमर्त्यवाग्विक्रम-वीर्यंचेष्टो उन्मादकालोऽनियतश्च का तस्या को भूतोत्थमुन्मादमुदाहरेत्तम् ॥१७॥
answer_text: Through the passage starting from avāncī, the features of incurable insanity is being discussed. The term avañcī refers to the one holding his head down while the term udafici refers to one that is holding his head upwards. The term jāgarūka here indicates the one who is not able to sleep. MODERN PERSPECTIVES ON INSANITY The unmāda has not been described by the modern medicine as any particular ailment. Unmāda as it appears through Ayurvedic literature may relate delirium, psychosis, depression, dementia, and certain effects of medications. As regards dementia, it has been known as a progressive, irreversible decline in mental function. Dementia could signify deficits in reasoning, judgment, abstract thought, registration, task execution, and use of language. It could also signify a mild to severe agitation that results from many common syndromes, such as Alzheimer’s disease and Huntington’s chorea. The patient can display a decrease in memory, attention span, disorder-solving ability, and alertness. Hypo-activity, wandering behaviour, hallucinations, aphasia, and insomnia can also occur. Unmāda caused by supernatural powers (CS. Ci. S. 9.17) A patient of insanity having majestic powers of speech, valour, strength and activities, as well as knowledge, scientific erudition, power, etc. and in whom fits of insanity manifest at unpredictable intervals should be regarded as suffering from bhūtonmāda. Vi The term amartya refers to someone with superhuman qualities. Jñāna is knowledge while the term Vijñāna denotes its practical implications. The term adi suggests memory etc. Aniyata significs the irregular as opposed to the regular or normal situations. As the yāta and other varieties of doṣas appear after digestion of improper food, the bout of insanity appears in an unexpected manner. The term bhūla suggests the superhuman powers like those possessed by devagraha etc., which have been discussed below. Unmāda caused by deva (God) (SS. Ut. 60.85) The individual afflicted by Gods (devagraha) always looks con¬ tented, keeps himself tidy, wears divine garlands and unguents, has no sleep, speaks only truth and refined language, looks bright, has stable looks, and keeps giving boons to everybody. 18

Iong, Leaflets 12-20 pairs, 1/2 inch. long, sessile and oblique. Flower heads globose pink in colour. Fruits Pods 1inch long. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Pañcāṅga (Whole plant). question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Purvārdḍha, Chapter 5, verse 10):

रक्तार्शसां लक्षणं विस्तरेणोक्तम् ।।१०।।
answer_text: The signs and symptoms of Raktarśas (bleeding piles) are described. This condition involves bleeding from the rectal masses, often associated with Pitta vitiation, and requires specific treatment to address both the bleeding and the underlying Doṣa imbalance. Arsonidānaṃ Whatever individual aetiological factors mentioned for the three types of Dosa based piles, are causative factors for Sannipāta or Tridoṣaja piles when occur combinedly. The symptomatology of Sahaja types of piles (congenital) is similar to that of Sannipāta (having the involvement of three Doṣas). The features of Sahaja type of piles, according Sufruta, ''The piles are awkward, rough, pale reddish in colour having cuts and inverted inside. The one who suffers with such pile is emaciated, eats low quantity of food, his body is seen with bulged veins, has a few children, less quantity of semen, has weak voice, gets angry frequently, has mild digestive fire, he also suffers from diseases of nose, head, eye and ear, his intestines make sounds, he has bloated abdomen, he feels that the heart is covered by something and he has distaste. (Su. ni. 2). Caraka said ''Some are small.........'' (Ca. ci. 14). When all the diseases are considered to be caused.by all the Tridosas there need not be seperate enumeration by name Tridoşaja Arśa etc., as said elsewhere, ''There is no drug of one single taste neither there is disease of one single Dosa and which ever of these factors is predominant, that label is given to the drug and disease''; It is not so; as per the statement of Caraka, Vāta, Pitta and Śleṣmā move all over the body, if one of the Dhātus is vitiated by one Doṣa, the other two Doṣas also participate in the act of vitiation due to the relationship of vitiated and vitiator. The Vata t aggravated due to its own reasons gets some amount of the cóld quality from Kapha f and lightness from Pitta and gets more power. Pitta also, due to its pungency, gets some support from Vāta and the liquid from Kapha. Like-wise, Kapha also becomes powerful by taking cold quality from Vata and liquid from Pitta. That is why it is said that there is no disease of a single Dosa vitiation. With the same view, it is said that one vitiated Dosa vitiates all others. Wherever the aetiology of vitiating all three of the Dosas exists there is vitiation of Tridosa simultaneously. This theory has to be applied everywhere. Symptomatology of Vāta type of piles Even if the food is taken in time, which is homologous and light for digestion, Agnimāndyadhinidānaṃ it will not be digested by taking more water, irregular eating, suppressing natural urges and reversal sleeping habits (sleeping in the day-time and waking in the nights). It will also not be digested properly due to envy, fear, anger, greed, pain, agony and hatred. 7, 8 (Su. sū. 46) Even if the food is consumed in limited quantity and in consumable form it will not be digested due to over thinking, grief, anger, fear, agony, oversleep and awakening during nights. 9 (Ca. vi. 2) By the word Api in ''Laghu Capi'', it is implied that the foods of oily and warm nature alongwith lightness for digestion psychological disturbances like envy etc., are causative factors for indigestion of psychological disturbance. Symptomatology of Ajīrṇa
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Purvārdḍha, Chapter 5, verse 10.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 55, verse 22-24):

मधुकोशः चिप्पमाह-नखेत्यादि। तं व्याधि चिप्पमिति चिप्पमङ्गलिवेष्टकमिति ख्यातम्। चरके त्वक्षतनामाये विकारः । यदुक्तं, 'रोगोऽक्षश्चर्मनखान्तरे स्यान्मांसास्त्रदोषी भृशदाहपाकः' (च.चि. १२) इति॥ १८–१९॥ गम्भीरामल्पसंरम्भां सवर्णामुपरिस्थितामु। पादस्यानुशयीं तां तु विद्यादन्तःप्रपाकिनीम्॥ २०॥ मधुकोशः अनुशयीलक्षणमाह-गम्भीरामित्यादि । गम्भीरामित्यन्तः पाकेन । अल्पसंरम्भा मित्यल्पशोथाम् ॥ २० ॥ विदारीकन्दवद् वृत्ता कक्षावड्क्षणसन्धिष् मधुकोशः विदारीलक्षणमाह-विदारीत्यादि। विदारिका भवेद्रक्ता सर्वजा सर्वलंक्षणेत्यत्र केचिदसर्वजा, असर्वलक्षणेति उभयत्रापि नञः प्रयोगमिच्छन्ति, तेनासर्वजा इति सर्वदोषैः सन्निपतितैर्न भवति, असर्वलक्षणेति सन्निपातलक्षण- रहितेत्यर्थः । तेन प्रत्येकदोषद्वन्द्वजत्वेन षड्विधा सन्निपातमात्रेण न भवतीति वाक्यार्थः । किन्त्वयं पक्षो यद्यभिमतः स्यादाचार्यस्य, तदा व्यक्तयर्थं ‘षड्विधा द्वयेकदोषजा’ इति पदं कृतं स्यात्। किञ्च बहुप्रपञ्चत्वेन क्षुद्रत्वासङ्गतिश्च। अपरे ‘असर्वजा सर्वलक्षणा’ इति पठन्ति; तदपि न संगतं, सर्वेदोर्षैन भवत्यथ सर्वदोषलक्षणा भवति हन्त तर्हि लिङ्गिनमन्तरेण लिङ्गप्रादुर्भावप्रसङ्ग । अन्ये तूत्तरपद एव नञः प्रयोगात् ‘सर्वजाऽसर्वलक्षणा’ इति वदन्ति; तत्र यदि सर्वेषां लक्षणानि' सर्वलक्षणानि तान्यविद्यमानानियस्यामिति, तदा कथं लिङ्गमन्तरेण लिङ्गिनः परोक्षस्य परिच्छेदोदयः। अथ सर्वाणि च तानि ल्रक्षणान्यविद्यमानानि यस्यामिति, सन्निपातजत्वेऽप्यसंपूर्णलक्षणेत्यर्थः। एतदपि न सङ्गतम्, यद्ययं पक्षोऽसर्वलक्षणेति न वक्तव्यमत्र स्यात्, सर्वत्र न्यायस्यास्य समानत्वात्; हेत्वनुरूपकोप- बलेन हि सर्वत्र सर्वाधाल्पलिङ्गसङ्गतिः। असंपूर्णलक्षणत्वेन दोषाणां हीनबलत्वं समवृद्दानामनारम्भकत्वं वा शक्यमेवास्मिन् पक्षे वक्तुं, किन्तु तन्नाद्रियन्ते; ततश्चोभयत्रापि नञः प्रयोगं विना सर्वजा सर्वलक्षणेति पाठो युक्तः सर्वजेत्यभिधायापि सर्वलक्षणेति वचनमिरिवेल्निकायामिव प्रकृतिसमसमवायजन्यवातादिलक्षणदर्शनाथं, तेन विकृतिविषमसमवायजन्यासाध्यत्वादिलक्षणानि न भवन्ति। अस्मिन्नपि पाठे सर्वजा सर्वेरिकादिप्रकारैर्वातादि- भिर्जन्यते, एवं सर्वलक्षणेति वक्तुं पार्यते, किन्तु क्षुद्ररोगत्वाद्दोषभेदेन गणना न युक्ता। चरके त्वियं कफमारुतजा पठ्यते। यदुक्तं-‘ज्वरान्विता वड्क्षणकक्षसन्धौ वर्तिर्निरर्तिः कठिना मता या। विदारिका सा कफमारुताभ्याम्’ ( च.चि.१२) इति। तेनात्राप्यल्पपित्तयुक्तकफवातजत्वेन सर्वजत्वं ज्ञेयम्। यथा-ज्वरयोगेनाल्पपित्तत्वम्। यदुक्तम्- कष्मा पित्तादृते नास्ति ज्वरो नास्त्यूष्मणा विना' (वा.चि. १) इति। 'विदारीमिति तां विद्यात् सर्वजां सर्वलक्षणाम्' इति पाठान्तरे न कश्चिद्व्याख्यानप्रपञ्चः ॥ २१ ॥ प्राप्य मांससिरास्नायूः श्लेष्मा मेदस्तथाऽनिलः । ग्रन्थिं करोत्यसौ भिन्नौ मधुसर्पिर्वसानिभम्॥ २२॥ स्त्रवत्यास्त्रावमनिलस्तत्र वृद्धि गतः पुनः। मांसं संशोष्य ग्रथितां शर्करां जनयेत्ततः॥ २३॥ दुर्गन्धि क्लिन्नमत्यर्थं नानावर्णं ततः सिराः। स्त्रवन्ति रक्तं सहसा तं विद्याच्छर्करार्बुदम्॥ २४॥ ( सु.नि. १३ )
answer_text: Cippa is also famous by name angulivestaka. This disease is named in Caraka as akṣata. As said, “The disease akṣata originates in between nail and skin. The flesh and the blood are vitiated and lead to severe burning sensation and ulceration". 18, 19. (Ca. Ci. 12). Anuśayī The abscess that originates deeply in the foot with less inflammation, is skin coloured and ripens inside is known as anusayi. 20. (Su.Ni. B). Kṣudraroga Nidāna Gambhīra-means deep rooted and getting ripened inside. Alpa samrambhā means less inflammed. 20. Vidārikā The abscess that is originated in the axilla and groin looking like vidarikanda (Rhizome-Puraria tuberosa), red in colour, caused by all three of the dosas, with complete symptomatology is called, vidārikā. 21. (Su. Ni. 13). Some read “asarvajā” and “asarvalakṣaṇa” in the place of ‘sarvaja’ and ‘sarva lakṣaṇā’ which is understood as not by the combination of all doṣas and not having complete array of the symptomatology of all the dosas. So the disease occurs as 6 types i.e., - 3 due to individual dosas and 3 due to dual combination of the three dosas. If this is the opinion of the author, he would have mentioned this “ Sadvidhādvyeka doṣaja”- This is of six types - 3 due to single doṣas and 3 due to dual dosa. Then it would not be included in minor diseases due to over description. Mādhavanidānaṃ Some read this as asarvajā and sarvalakṣaṇā - which also does not stand good because when all the dosas are not involved in the origination of the disease how can there be complete symptomatology of all dosas. Some others take it as “Sarvajā asarva lakṣana”-caused by all doṣas, but not having complete symptomatology.This is also not correct because, when there is involvement of all the dosas in origination of this disease, there should also be the manifestion of all the signs and symptoms of all the dosas. The incomplete manifestation indicates the weakness of dosas which is doubtful in the very origination of the disease. Therefore sarvaja sarvalakṣaṇā is the correct text. After saying “sarvajā” (caused by all doṣas) men¬ tioned “sarvalakṣṇā” (with complete symptomatology of all the doṣas) is to indicate the positive signs and symptoms of Vata etc., dosas which does not show any incurability of the disease Sarvaja, here may indicate at this disease being differentiated by doşa variation. But in kşudra roga such classification is not seen. In Caraka, this is considered as originated of aggravated kapha and vāta. As said by him, “Hard growth in the groin and axilla, associated with fever, caused by kapha and vata is called vidārikā”. (Ca. Ci. 12). That is why here the involvement of pitta of low profile is seen to call it as sarvaja; fever is due to alpa pitta. As said, "There is no heat without pitta and there no fever without heat". (Va. ci. 1). According to different text, the statement is, “Vidarīmiti tām vidyāt sarvajāṃ sarvalakṣanāṃ” which need not be detailed. 21. Sarkarārbuda Kapha, medas and vāta take shelter in māṃsa (muscle) sirā (veins) and snāyu (tendons) and cause a tumour, on breaking of which there will be discharge that looks like honey, ghee and fat. Due to emaciation of these tissues, vata increases and dries up the, mamsa and makes (breaks) it into granule form. It will have stinking smell, is very wet with discharge, the veins discharge discoloured blood. This condition is called Sarkarābuda. 22-24. (Su. Ni. 13)

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 4):

मारुतः कुपितो वह्निं सञ्छाद्य कुरुते गदान् । तस्यान्नं पच्यतेदुःखं शुक्तपाकं खराइता ॥6॥ कण्ठास्यशोषोऽक्षुत्तष्णा तिमिरं कर्णयोः स्वनः । पार्श्वोरु-वङ्क्षण-ग्रीवारुगभीक्ष्णंविस्रचिका परिकर्तिका । हृत्पीडा-कार्श्य-दौर्बल्यंवैरस्यं, गृद्धिः सर्वरसानां मनसः सदनं तथा ॥৪॥
answer_text: 17 II 119 H 111 O II (CS. Ci. 15.59-64) Regular indulgence in pungent, bitter, astringent, dry, contaminated food items and taking scanty or no food at all; too much of walking, suppression of natural urges and excess sexual activities result in provoked vāta which subsequently destroys the digestive activity and produces the disease identified as vataja grahamroga. In the case of this ailment the food is digested with difficulty and it under- goes fermentation. Moreover, there occur the following symptoms: hardness of the body parts, dryness of the throat and mouth, absence of hunger, feeling of thirst, darkness before the eyes, noise in the ears, constant pain in the flanks, thighs, groins and the neck; vomiting, diarrhoea, pain in the region of the heart, emaciation. weakness, bad taste in the mouth, cutting pain in the rectum, desire for eatables of all the tastes, mental depression, distension of the abdomen during the period of digestion and feeling of comfort on taking eatables. The features are very much identical with those of the re are and the state of abdominal tumor (vātagulma), disease of the heart (hṛdroga) and splenic disorder (pliha), thus causing difficulty in diagnosis. The patient voids faeces after a long time, it is watery or dry, thin, frothy, improperly processed and is accompanied with pain and noise; he has cough and an increased or difficult respiration as well. 5–10 The term Samdusta means incompatible and the like foodstuff. The term has been replaced elsewhere through the term situall. It refers to the intake of the cold and the like foodstuff. Pramita is very limited; some commentators read this as Pramṛta that refers to untimely and delayed intake of food as a habit. The term anasana refers to skipping the regular meals or remaining on fast. Thus, the causative factors of the disease has been referred to through the terms samduşta or sitadi, pramita or pramrta and anasana with their diverse connotations. The term sañcādya refers to the condition of having vitiated. Vata dries the oily contents of the skin causing rigidity in the body. The term timira significs loss of vision. The term ruk refers to pain, which is in the present context, the pain in stomach, heart region, and throat, etc. The term visucika refers to the expulsion of undigested food in stomach through mouth and through anus. The term vairasya refers to a situation when the patient is, unable to correctly appreciate the rasa or taste. For example, he can feel the taste of tamarind when in fact he is consuming a ripe mango. The term parikartikā refers to the cutting pain (in the anal region, in the present context). The desire of cating foods of varied taste is called grddhih which is produced by either vala or it is due to the effect of the disease. There are also signs of ādhmāna (formation of wind due to improper digestion) and mental depression (manasah sadana). question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Vatadi Varga, Chapter 5, verse 581):

तमाल उक्तस्तापिच्छः कालस्कन्योऽमितहुमः । लोकस्कन्यो नीलध्वजो नीलतालश्च स स्मृतः ।। तमालः शालवद्वेद्यो दाहविस्फोटहृत् पुनः ।।४४۱۱
answer_text: Digestive diseases: The bark decoction is also given in Tṛṣṇā (Thrist) and Ātisarā (Diarrhoea). Diseases of oral cavity: Decoction of the bark is used as Gargle in Gala roga (Sore thoat), Dantasūla (Toothache) etc. External uses: The extracted oil of the bark is applied externally over Vrna (Wounds). TAMALĀ Latin: Garcinia morella. Desr. Fam: Guttiferae Hin: Tamal Eng: Indian Gambose, Gamboge Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Tāpichca, Kālaskandha, Amitadruma, Lōkaskandha, Nīladhwaja and Nīlatāla. Guna karma (Properties and indications): It's properties and indication are similar to the Sāla. It particularly relieves Dāha (Burning sensation) and Vispoṭa (Blisters). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Khasia hills, Bengal and evergreen forests of South india. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is small to medium sized evergreen tree growing upto 18 m. Bark is smooth, dark brown; blaze white. Leaves are simple, 6.5-15 cm.long and 3.5-8 cm. wide, elliptical- oblong, accuminate apex, tapering at base, leathery or subleathery, crowded at the end of the branchs. Flowers are dioecious, male flowers pinkish white in fasciles, female flowers axillary and solitary. Fruit- Berry, globose, smooth, 4-seeded. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Niryāsa (Gum). Chemical constituents: Morellinol, Morellaflavone glucoside, Dihydromorelloflavone, Morellic acid and Forbesione
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Vatadi Varga, Chapter 5, verse 581
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Vatadi Varga, Chapter 5, verse 581.

Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Karpuradi Varga, Chapter 2, verse 224):

जातीफलं जातिकोशं मालतीफलमित्यपि । जातिफलं रसे तिक्त तीक्ष्णोष्णं रोचन लघु । कट्टर्क दीपन ग्राहि स्वर्यं श्लेष्मानिलापहम् ।।५४११ निहन्ति मुखवैरस्यं मलदौर्गन्ध्यकृष्णताः कृमिकासवमिश्वासशोषपीनसहहहुजः १११५ ५११ जातीफलस्य त्वक् प्रोक्ता जातीपत्री भिषग्वरैः ।।५६।। जातीपत्री लघुः स्वादुः कटुष्णा रुचिवर्णकृत् । कफकासवमिश्वासतृष्णाकृमिविषापहा ।।५७।।
answer_text: Respiratory disease: It is good respiratory stimulant expectorant useful in Kāsa (cough) etc. diseases. In Swāsa (Dyspnoea), a medicated smoke of Shilarasa, Guggulu and Padmaka should be used. External uses: It is valuable remedy for skin diseases, mixed with Olive oil and apply locally in Dadru (Ringworm), Kanḍū (Itching), Pāmā (Scabies) etc. Mātrā (Dosage): 1-2 gms. JĀTĪPHALA Family: Myristicaceae Latin: Myristica fragrance Houtt. ng: Nutmeg Hin: Jayphala 18 JA-413 AVAPRAKĀŚA NIGHAN Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Jātī Kośa and Mālatīphala. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Jatiphala is Tikta (Bitter), Tīkṣṇa (Penetrating), Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), Recana (Purgative), Laghu (Light for digestion), Kaṭu (Pungent) in taste, Dīpana (Appetizers), Grāhī (Absorbent) and Swarya (Good for voice). It cures diseases of Kapha and Vāta, Mukhadourgandya (Relieves bad breath), Maladourgandya (Relieves bad odour of faceas), Feacal discoloration, Kṛmi (Worm infestations), Kāsa (Cough), Chardi (Vomiting), Swāsa (Dyspnoea), Soṣa (Emaciation), Pīnasa (Running nose) and Hṛdya roga ( Cardiac Diseases). Note: Myristicin malbarica a source plant is a common adulterant and substitute. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is a native of East Moluccas and cultivated in many parts if Southern India. Swarūpa (Botanical description): An everygreen tree with spreading branches grows upto 25 ft. Bark is greyish brown smooth. Leaves 2-5 inch long, elliptical-ovate, accuminate apex, obtuse base and pale under side. Flower are small pale yellow in color, usually single sexed in axillary racemose. Fruit ovid or pyriform, 1-2 inches across develop into yellow fleshy fruit, the ripen fruit splits to exposea. Seed single, purple brown nut, enclosed by an aril. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Bīja (Seed), Koṣa- Jātīpatri. Chemical Constituents: Nutmeg has volatile oil contains Myristicin, Myristic acid, Engenol & Iso engenol it also contains Nutmeg butter, Fatty acids, Aromatic blasams, Starch and Fibrous substance etc. Digestive disease: The essential oil is Uttejaka (Stimulant) and Anulomaka (Carminative) and is administered in Atisāra (Diarrhoea), Pravahīkā (Dysentery) and Śūla (Abdominal pain). It’s Infusion is said to be useful in quenching the Tṛṣṇā (Thrist) of Visūcikā (Cholrea) patients. External uses: The extracted oil is used externally in various painful conditions like chronic Āmavāta (Rheumatism), Sandhiśūla (Joint inflammation), sprain, spasm, Dantasūla (Tooth ache ) etc., painful conditions. The oil prepared with seeds is applied to male genitals for promoting erectability. In case of Vipadika (Cracks in feet), a paste prepared from Jātiphala is applied externally. In Vyanga (Freckles), the paste of the aril of the Jātīphala applied externally. Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrṇa: 1-3 gms., Taila: 1 to 5 drops. JĀTĪPATRĪ Latin: Myristica fragrance Houtt. Fam: Myristicaceae Hin: Javitri ng: Mace The name jatiphala has very popular in Vedas. It is an unrippen seeds enclosed by fleshy red net like skin covering is called as aril or javitri. Guna karma (Properties and indications): It is Laghu (Light for digestion), Madhura (Sweet) and Katu (Pungent) in taste, Uṣṇa virya (Hot in potency), Rucya (Promotes taste) and Vranakṛt (Promotes complexion). It cures Diseases of Kapha doṣa, Kāsa (Cough), Chardi (Vomiting), Swāsa (Dyspnoea), Tṛṣṇā (Thrist), Kṛmi (Worm infestations) and Viṣa Posionous manifestations). Chemical composition: Volatile oils, Gums, Resins, Fats, Sugar etc. Properties and indications: Almost similar to that of Jātīphala. Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrna: 1-3gm
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Karpuradi Varga, Chapter 2, verse 224
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Karpuradi Varga, Chapter 2, verse 224.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 693):

अम्लिका चुक्रिकाऽम्ली च चुक्रा दन्तशङ्गापि च । अम्ला च चिश्चिका चिश्चा तिन्तिंडीका च तिन्तिंडी ।।१४२।। अमिलकाऽम्ला गुरुर्वातहरा पित्तकफास्रकृत् । पक्का तु दीपनी रूक्षा सरोष्णा कफवातनुत् ।।१४३।।
answer_text: Digestive disease: Fruit juice is employed in the treatment of Sūla (Abdominal colic), Chardi (Vomiting), Medoroga (Obesity) etc. Galactagogue action: Fruits are efficacious. Menstural disorders: It's fruits in larger dose can acts as Arthavajanana (Emmenogogue) and Garbhapada (Aboeficient). External uses: Grated fruits, with a little salt added, are applied on the face to treat Yavānpidika a (Acne vulgaris). Leaf and shoot applied externally in Dadru (Ringworm), Pāmā (Scabies), Laghu masūrikā (Chickenpox), Kaṇḍū (Itching), Vispoṭa (Blisters), Kiṭaviṣa (Inscets bites) etc. AMLIKĀ Latin: Tamarindus indica Linn. Fam: Leguminosae Hin: Imli Eng: Tamarind Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Cukrikā, Amlī, Cukrā, Dantaśaṭhā, Aṃ, Cincinnati, Tintidīkā and Tintidī. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Amlikā is Amla (Sour in taste), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Subsides Vāta, Increases Pitta, Kapha and Rakta. Ripen fruit is Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), Rūkṣā (Drying), Dīpana (Appetizers), Sāra (Laxative), subsides Kapha and Vāta. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Indigenous to Southern india is Cultivated throughout India and Burma. Swarūpa (Botanical description): A large tree with spreading glabrous branches reaches upto 20-30m. Leaves paripinnate compound, leaflets 20-34, opposite, sessile, 1.5-4 long and 0.4-1.3 cm, oblong, base unequal, apex obtuse, margin entire and glabrous. Flowers in lax raceme yellow with pink strips. Fruits are Pods 10-15 cm. long and 1-2 cm. wide oblong, fruit wall crustaceous, mesocarp pulpy, endocarp septate, leathery and indehiscent. Seeds 3-12, obovate-oblong, smooth, brown in colour. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Bīja (Fruit seed) Patra (Leaves), Puṣpa (Flowers), Phala (Fruits). Chemical constituents: Citric acid, Tartaric acid, Potassium bitartrate and Sucrose
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 693
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 693.

तूणी तुन्नक आपीनस्तुणिकः कच्छकस्तथा । कुङ्गेरकः कान्तलको नन्दीवृक्षश्च नन्दकः ।।४५.।। तूणी रक्तः कटुः पाके कषायो मधुरो लघुः । तिक्तो याही हिमो वृष्यो व्रणकुष्ठास्रपित्तजित् ।।४६।।
answer_text: Digestive disease: Fruits are sliced and dried under sunlight to preserve it for long time, it is used in treating Pravāhikā (Dysentery). It is Recaka (Purgative), used to expell to Krmi (Worm) from intestines. The fruit is hailed as an excellent remedy in Medoroga (Obesity). External uses: It may applied externally over Vrna (Wounds). Mātrā (Dosage): Niryāsa: 50-125mg. TÜNI Latin: Cedrela toona Roxb. Fam: Meliaceae Hin: Tuni ng: The toon Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Tunnaka, Āpīna, Tunika, Kachcaka, Kuṭheraka, Kānṭalaka, Nandivrksa and Nandaka. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Tūṇī is Red in colour, Kaṣāya (Astringent), Madhurā (Sweet) and Tiktā (Bitter) in taste, Kaṭu vipāka (Püngent in post digestive), Laghu (Light for digestion), Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Grāhī (Absorbent) and Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac). It cures Vrna (Wounds), Kusta (Leprosy) and Raktapitta (Haemorrages). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Tropical Himalayas, from the Indus east wards acending to 1000m. also throughout the hills of central and Southern India. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a large tree reaches upto 40 m. Leaves Imparipinnate, leaflets, opposite- alternately arranged, ovate-lanceolate, 4-13 cm long, long point at the tip, unequal at the base. Flowers are arranged in panicles, fragrant, orange- red in colour. Fruits capsule, 2cm.long, seeds-1, membranous wings at each end. Prayogya aṅga (Part used): Twak (Bark), Puṣpā (Flowers). Chemical constituents: Tetranortriterpenoids, toonacilin, coumarin, geranylgernalol and its fatty esters
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Vatadi Varga, Chapter 5, verse 582
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Vatadi Varga, Chapter 5, verse 582.

Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 490):

मयूराह्वशिखा प्रोक्ता सहस्राहिर्मधुच्छदा । नीलकण्ङ्गशिखा लघ्वी पित्तश्लेष्मातिसारजित् ।।३०९।।
answer_text: It is Useful in Jvara (Fever), Pāṇḍuroga (Anemia), Switra (Vitiligo), Krmi (Worm infestation), Karnaśūla (Earache), Sotha (Inflammation) etc. Mātrā (Dosage): Swarasa: 10-20ml. MAYŪRA ŚIKHĀ Latin: Actinopteris dichotoma Bedd. Fam: Actinopteridaceae Hin: Mayurashikha Eng: Peacock’s tail Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Sahasrāhi, Madhuchcadā and Nīlakanṭha śikhā. Guna karma (Properties and indications): It is Lagu (Light for digestion), cures diseases of Pitta and Kapha and Atisāra (Diarrhoea). Note: The word Mayūra means peacock and śikhā means a crest on his head. The plant which may resemble the feathers of peacock may be called as Mayūra śikhā. Amongest Actiniopteris dichotoma Bedd.is genrally used in the name of Mayūra śikhā. Source plants Actiniopteris dichotoma Bedd Actunopteridaceae, Celsoia argentea Linn. Amaranthaceae Adiantum caudatum Linn. Elephantopus scaber Linn. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Throughout India in moist places. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is an annual fern reaches upto 0.2m. Ferns fan like densely tufted, consist of innumerable dichotomous fragments grows up to 5-15cm. across, veins less, and sub- lateral with ill-defined mid-rib, the fragments of the stipes larger than those of barren one. Part used: Pañcānga (Whole plant). Chemical constituents: Rutin, Sistosterol D and Hentriacontane. Prayoga (Therapeutic uses): It is useful in Krmi roga (Worm infestations), Kuşta (Leprosy), Atisāra (Diarrhoea), Raktaja vyadies (Bleeding disorders) and Jwara (Fever). Mātrā (Dosage): 10-20ml. 39 JA-413
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 490
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 490.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 117):

रास्ना युक्तरसा रस्या सुवहा रसना रसा । एलापणी च सुरसा सुगन्धा श्रेयसी तथा ।।१६२।। रास्नाऽऽमपाचिनी तिक्ता गुरूष्णा कफवातजित् ।।१६ः३३।। शोथश्वाससमीरास्रवातशूलोदरापहा । कासज्वरविषाशीतिवातिकामयसिध्महत् ।। १६४।।
answer_text: Emetic action: Madana is repuated as best Vamaka (Emetic drug), it is very safe doesn’t cause any complications. The rind and pulp of the fruit are genrally used to produce Vamana (Vomiting). The pulp may be removed, dried and powered and kept ready for use and used in the dose of 1-4gms. for Vamana (Emetic) and 0.5-1gm. for Hrilasa (Nausea) and Kaphagna (Expectorant). The pulp of 2 or 3 fruits are soaked in 30 ml of water and ground and given, in about 10 min the vamana will occure for more bouts of vamana warm water is given, some time one pulp of fruits of sufficient and effective. Respiratory disease: The dried cürna of Madanaphala, Arka mula, and Yaştīmadhu taken in equal quantity to cure Swāsa (Dyspnoea). Digestive disease: It is used Internally in Ātisarā (Diarrhoea), Raktātisāra (Blood stools), Pravāhika (Dysentery), Jwara (Fever) etc. The pulp of Madana also has Recaka (Purgative) and Krmiaghna ( useful in worm infestations). Use in childrens to relieve Krmi (Worm infestations). Mental illness: The powder of Madana and Pingītaka seeds pounded with water alleviates Apasmāra (Epilepsy). External uses: Make paste of the fruit with vinegar and apply externally around naval to relieve Sūla (Abdominal colic). The tree bark is applied externally to relieve Sotha (Inflammation), Amavāta (Rheumatism), Vrna (Wounds) etc pain ful conditions. Leaves are used as poutice in Dusta vrna (Non- healings ulcers). Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrṇa: 3-5 gms. For vamana karma., and for other 1-2 gm. RĀSNĀ Paruāyanāma (Synomyms): Yuktarasā, Rasyā, Suvahā; Rasanā, Rasā, Elāparnī, Surasā, Sugandhā nad Sreyasī. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Rasanā is Amapācana (Digestive), Tiktā (Bitter) in taste, Guru (Heavy for digestion), Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency), and subsides Kapha and Vāta doṣa. It cures Śotha (Inflammation), Swasā (Dysponea), Vātarakta (Gout), Vātaśūla (Abdominal colic with Vāta predominance), Udarroga (Abdominal diseases), Kāsa (Cough), Jwara (Fever), Viṣa (Posionous manifestations), All eighty types of Vātaja rogas and sidma (type of skin disease). Note: In India Rasanā is yet a highly contraversial drug. There have many plants which are currently being identified and used as Rasanā in different regions of India. However, at present it is very difficult to identify which one the genuine plant drug is considered to be Rasanā. although the Plucea lancealata oliver and Hiern. is accpected as an ideal source in most parts of north India. The different source plants are currently being identified and used as Rasanā in different regions. Pluchea lanceeolate. C.B.Clarke. (Compositae).: It is accepted as 'Patra rasana' leaves of this plant is being used as Rasana’. Aplina galanga. Swartz. (Scitaminaceae): It is taken as ‘Mūla rasana’ Rhizome of this plant are used as Rasana. Vanda roxburghii R.Br. (Orchidaceae): It is used as 'Trṇa rasana' Inula racemosa Hook. f. (Compositae). It is equated with Puskarmūla more suitable than with Rāsnā

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2, verse 30):

भूताभिषङ्गादिति भूता देव- ग्रहादय उन्मादनिदाने वक्ष्यमाणाः, तेषामभिषङ्गः सम्बन्धः । उद्वेग उद्विग्नचित्तता - काम-शोक-भयाद्वायुः, क्रोधात् पित्तं, त्रयो मलाः ॥३०॥
answer_text: and abhiśāpas (micro-organisms?) generate āgantu jvara. Even in such fevers, the features of dosas have to be recognised. The agantu jvara (fever due to external factors) is caused by such factors as injury, witchcraft, wrath of pious people and affliction of the evil. Basing on the signs and symptoms, such fevers can be classified as per the dosa classifications. In agantu jvara generated by poison, bluish discolouration of the mouth, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, thirst, pain and fainting are seen; in fever generated by smell of plants (pollen of flowers and the like), fainting, headache, vomiting and sneezing are seen. In käma jvara that is the fever caused by insatiable lust, such symptoms as instability of mind, drowsiness, laziness, distaste to food, pain in the heart and emaciation of the body are seen. Delirium occurs in fevers caused by fear and grief. Trembling is seen in fever caused by anger. Fever caused by witchcraft and wrath of pious people features delusion and thirst while in fever that is resulted by affliction of evil spirits, the patient could be highly emotional and could indulge in non-sense laughing, weeping and shivering, 26-29 This passage relates to the detailed description of the so-named Abhighātaja jvara or fever caused due to injury factors. The term abhighāta refers to the injury caused by weapons, stones, fist and sticks. Abhicāraja jvara is the fever that has been caused through the malevolent efforts to harm the foes. Such malevolent efforts include performance of sacrifice and fire rituals involving use of mustard, etc. and chanting of malevolent spells or mantras. The so-named Abhiṣaṅga Jvara is caused by lust, grief, fear, and anger and by evil spirits (CS. Ci. 3.114). The term Abhisapa refers to the incurring the wrath of Brahmins, gurus, the elderly and the seers. This Agantu- jvara (fever caused by external factors out of sudden) has to be approached as classified into divisions pertaining to the dosa invol- ved. The reality that vāyu is provoked by such factors as unfulfilled sexual desire, grief and fear has been admitted by (Cikitsā. 3. 115). In the Agantujvara this doṣa context, appear at latter stage and not at the onset of the disease. This case has been discussed earlier in the context of Samprāpti. The term śyāva refers to whitish black colour. Some people read it as śyāma that is bluish black colour. The diarrhoea that is caused by consumption of herbal poison in the fever is caused by the downward movement of the poison that is its natural movement. The inhalation of pollen grains of flowers and strong odour of some other herbs produces a fever that is called auṣadhigandhaja jvara. The Trnapuspa type of fever described by Vrddha Suśruta comes under the category of auşadhigandhaja jvara (SS. U. 39). (It may be noted that the related passage is not available today in the present text of Suśruta Saṁhitā). The Kāmaja type of fever is caused by unfulfilled sexual desire. The term Cittavibhramsa refers to mental derange¬ ment and giddiness etc., as described by Vāgbhaṭa. In fact there appear traits like lack of shame, sleep, bravery and intelligence apart from giddiness, distaste, burning sensation, etc. in the situation of the Kāmajvara' (AH. Ni. 2.42). Apart from the kāmaja fever there is also a type of fever supposed to occur through fear (bhayāt). Delirium in grief-stricken fever is due to vata; as suggested by Caraka vayu is aggravated by lust, grief, and fear while pitta is supposed to get aggravated by anger (CS. Ci. 3.115). Now the question arises as to why be vepathu (that is trembling) present there in anger-stricken fever, for trembling is supposed to occur by vitiated vāta while anger is allegedly produced by pitta doṣa. One could expect, in anger-induced fever such symptoms as burning sensation, morbid thirst, etc. instead. In response to this objection, Jettaṭa opines that vitiation of vāla aggravates all other doṣas as well. Thus, it is to be understood that trembling is the manifestation of vāla that is prompted by aggravated pitta. Trembling is generally seen in an angry individual. This is the direct evidence of this truism. The anger aggravates pitta as well as as vāta. The commentator Videha has suggested that anger and grief both aggravate väta, rakta, as well as pitta. By including ‘ca’ in the phrase kopaca used here, headache is also to be included as one of the symptoms of the krodhaja jvara. Vagbhaṭa has also suggested that anger generates trembling as well as headache while the fevers caused by grief and fear produce delirium (AH. Ni. 2.42). Though all these sorts of fever come under the category of mānasa or psychological variety, the especial narrative of fevers related to fear etc. has been presented here to trace the causative factor and the differentiation that helps in managing the treatment of the concerned disease. In the context of Abhicara related fever the term 'ca' has been used ('Trsna ca'). It implies burning sensation etc. As suggested by Vāgbhaṭa, at first the mind of the person who is targeted is subjected to a burning sensation as an effect of the chanting of the sacrificial mantras; latter the fever spreads to the body and subsequently it increases day by day ( AH. Ni. 2.44-45). The term Bhūtābhiṣaṅgaja refers to the affliction caused by malevolent celestial elements including planets etc. Details of the same have been explained under the section of ‘diagnosis of insanity’ in this work ahead. The term udvega refers to the mental tension. The dosa relation in the Agantu jvara (accidental fevers) (CS. Ci. 3. 115/2, 116/2). Lust, grief, and fear excite vāta while anger provokes pitta. Similarly, possession by evil spirits excites all the three dosas. Moreover, other symptoms and features also occur in these cases as per the specific dosa involved. 30
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2, verse 30.

question:

answer_text: The Sahaja or congenital variety of piles could also be identified with its Tridosa variety. The term sarvaih refers to the vāta, pitta and kapha. All these dosas are instrumental in producing the sannipātaja piles and thus the signs and symptoms of this disease is similar to those of tridosaja variety of piles. (A H, Ni. 7.43-45) In the case of hemorrhoids or bleeding piles ( raktarsas ), most of the symptoms are identical to those of the pittaja arsas. The sprouts of this pile look like the tender twigs of banyan tree, guijā (abrus seed) and vidruma (coral bead). They exudate vitiated and warm blood on being pressurised by hard stool. Due to excessive loss of blood, the individual looks like a frog and suffers from the diseases that are caused due to diminished blood. The lustre of his body, his strength and aptitude and his ojas, that are the essential immunity factor in the body, are lost and his organs become feeble. 24-26

वासाणं चूर्ण निश्वर्यं किलासं नामनिर्मितम् । विरेच्यं विस्रुतं रक्तं विदोष्यं प्रायशस्तथा ॥ १६२ ॥ दोषे रक्तक्षिते रक्तं तादृशं मांसमाक्षिपेत् । स्वेदने मर्दनेन क्षुरं तद्वा नखलोमरुम् ॥ १६३ ॥ यत् परुत्तममिन्नं बहु यद्रक्तलोचनम् । यश्च वर्षाकलोत्पन्नं तद्वैद्यं नैव सिध्यति ॥ १६४ ॥ अरुक्क्लाम तनु यत्तु पाण्डु नातिचिरोत्थितम् । मध्यकायगतं चोच्छ्रूनं श्वित्रं तत्साध्यमुच्यते ॥ १६५ ॥
answer_text: By evacuation, blood-letting, roughening and intake of parched grain powder, the leucoderma is got rid off in rare cases where the sin is attenuated. Kilāsa is mostly tridoṣaja and is of three types—dāruṇa aruṇa, and świtra. The diseased spot is red, coppery, and white and the morbidity is located in blood, flesh and fat respectively. Their severity is in successive order. The leucoderma ( spot ) which is undemarcated mutually, extensive, having red hairs and arisen since many years is not curable. That leucoderma is curable which has no red hairs, is thin, pale, not so old and raised upwards in the middle
chapter_title: Raktapitta Chikitsita – Treatment of Internal Haemorrhage
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Chikitsasthana, Chapter 4, verse 162-165.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 5):

असाध्यो हि द्विविधो याप्यप्रत्याख्येयभेदात् तत्र यद्यायुःशेषोऽस्ति चतुष्पादसम्पत्तिश्च तदा याप्यत्वमन्यथा प्रत्याख्येयत्वमित्याह शेपत्वादित्यादि । चतुष्पादसमन्विते अशेसिंगिण इति शेषः । समन्वित इति भावे क्तः तेन चतृष्यद्समन्वये सति इति चक्रः ।। पादे मुखे नाभ्यां गुदे वृषणयोस्तथा । हस्ते शोथो हत्पार्श्वशूलं च यस्यासाध्योडर्शसो हि सः ॥३ ॥ हत्पार्श्वशूलंक का सम्मोहश्छर्दिरङुस्य का स रुग्ज्वरः । तृष्णा का गुदस्य का पाकश्च का निहन्युर्गुदजातुरम् ॥॥ तृष्णारोचक-शूलार्तमतिप्रस्त्रुतशोणितम् शोथातिसारसंयुक्तमर्शांसिक में क्षपयन्तिक में हिं - - -
answer_text: This passage describes the difference between the stages identified as yāpya and pratyākhyeya. The first stage is indicative of the availability of all the four factors or resources of life as well as to the patient’s life left as per the destiny. The term pratyākhyeya relates to the situation opposite to that of the yapya. The great commentator Cakrapāṇi has put stress on the availability of all the four pillars of treatment to confirm the position of yāpya (CS. Ci. 14.29). Complications of the piles-disease (CS. Ci. 14.26) The patients of piles who have oedema in the hands, feet, face and the umbilical, anal and scrotal regions, as well as who have colicky pain in the pericardium and sides are incurable. The following symptoms are also indicative of a fatal variety of arśas: pain in the region of the heart and flanks. 39 (CS. Ci. 14.27) If a patient of piles is having such symptoms as pain in heart, flanks, delusion, vomiting, pain all over the body, fever, thirst, anal suppuration, heavy bleeding from the pile mass, he might soon head to the death. 40 (SS. Sū. 33.10) The patient of piles having such additional symptoms as thirst, anorexia, colic pain, profuse bleeding, oedema as well as diarrhoea is to be understood to have reached a fatal stage. 41

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 872):

अगस्तिकुसुमं श्रीतं चातुर्थिकनिवारणम् । नक्तान्थ्यनाशनं तिक्त कषायं कटुपाकि च । पीनसश्लेष्मपित्तघनं वातघनं मुनिभिर्मतम् ।।४८।। कदल्याः कुसुमं स्निग्धं मधुरं तुवरं गुरु । वातपित्तहरं शीतं रक्तपित्तक्षयप्रणुत् ।।४९।। शिग्रोः पुष्पं तु कटुकं तीक्ष्णोष्णं स्नायुशोथनुत् । कृमिहत्कफवातघन विद्रधिप्लीहगुल्मजित् । मधु शिग्रोस्त्वक्षिहित्व रक्तपित्तप्रसादनम् ।।५०।। शाल्मलीपुष्पशाक तु घृतसैन्धवसाधितम् । प्रदरं नाशयत्येव दुःसाध्यं च न संशयः ।।५१।। रसे पाके च मधुरं कषायं शीतलं गुरु । कफपित्तास्त्रजिद् ग्राहि वातलं च प्रकीर्तितम् ।।५२।।
answer_text: Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Agasti flowers is Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Cāturtihikanivāraṇa (Cures tertian fever), Tikta (Bitter) and Kaṣāya (Astringent) in taste, Kaṭu vipaka (Pungent in post digestive), it cures Naktandya (Night-blindness), Pīnasa (Common cold), Diseases of Kapha, Pitta and Vāta. Note: Details about Agasti puṣpa explained in Puṣpā varga. PRAKĀŚA NIGHAN KADALI PUSPĀ Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Kadalī Puṣpā is Madhura (Sweet) and Kaşāya (Astringent) in taste, Guru (Heavy for digestion), Snigdha (Oilyness), subsides Vāta and Pitta, cures Raktāpitta (Haemorrages) and Kṣaya (Emaciation). Note: For further details refer Phalā varga. sigru madhu sighru Guna karma (Properties and indications): The flowers of Sigru are Katu (Pungent) in taste, Tīkṣṇa (Penetrating) and Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency) It cures Snayu śothanut (Relieves inflammation of Tendons), Kṛmi (Worms infestations), Diseases of Kapha and Vāta, Vidradi (Abcess), Plīha roga (Spleen disorders) and Gulma (Abdominal tumors). Flowers of Madhuśigru are spefically useful in Aksihita (Good for eyes) and Ráktāpitta (Haemorrages). Note: For further details refer Gudūcyādi varga. ŚĀLMALĪ PUṢPAM Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Śālmalī flowers are made by adding Ghee and Rock salt, surely it cures Pradara (Meno-Metroghia) even though it is incurable. It is Madhura vīpaka (Sweet in post digestive), Kaṣāya (Astringent) in taste, Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Grāhī (Absorbent) and Increases Vatā. It cures diseases of Kapha Pitta and Rakta, Note: Details about Sālmalī puṣpā explained in Vaṭādi varga

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Nidanasthana, Chapter 2, verse 40):

(च. चि. ३) मधुकोशः चतुर्थकविपर्ययमाह—विषमेत्यादि । अन्न तन्त्रान्तरम्—‘अस्थिमज्जोभयगते चतुर्थकविपर्ययः । स मध्ये ज्वरयत्यह्वी ह्यादावन्ते च मुञ्चति' । इति । आदावेकदिनं मुक्त्वा, मध्ये दिनद्वयं भूत्वा, अन्ते एकदिनं न भवतीति व्याचक्षते जेज्जटादय: । अस्थिमज्जोभयगते चतुर्थकविपर्ययः । त्र्यहाद्र ' द्व्यहं ज्वरयत्यादावने च मुझ्ठति—इति पराशरवचनस्यापि स एवार्थः; त्यहादिति त्यहस्यादिदिनं विमुझ्ठति, दिनद्वयं ज्वरयति, त्यहस्याने चतुर्थदिनं-मुञ्चतीति तात्पर्यार्थं व्याचक्षते । हरिचन्द्रस्त्वाह—द्वे अहनी निरन्तरं ज्वरयित्वा उपरम्यैकमहः पुनर्ज्वरयतीत्येवं चतुर्थकविपर्यय इति । आदिदिनाभावश्रोत्तरपातिदिवसेष्ववधार्यः । चतुर्थकविपर्ययस्योपलक्षणत्वेन तृतीय- कादिविपर्ययोऽप्यूह्य इत्याहुः । तद्यथा—मध्ये एकदिनं ज्वरयति, आद्यन्तयोमुञ्ठतीति तृतीयकविपर्ययः; एककाल विमुच्य सर्वमहोरात्र व्याप्नोतीत्यन्येद्युष्कविपर्ययः; (कालद्वये मुञ्चति, सर्वमहोरात्र ज्वरयतीति सततविर्ययः ' ।) अत्र दोषविकृतिरेव नानाविधा हेतुरिति । ‘कफस्थानेषु वा निष्ठन् दोषो द्वित्रिचतुर्षु च । विपर्ययाख्यान् कुरुते विषमान् कृच्छ्रसाधनान्’ (सु. उ. अ. ३९) इति वृद्धसुश्रतवाक्यं व्याचक्षाणो जेज्जटोऽन्येद्युष्कतृतीयकचतुर्थकमात्रस्य विपर्ययमुदाहरति । यद्यथा—आमाशयहृदयस्थदोषेण यथोदाहृत एवान्येद्युष्कविपर्ययः; आमाशयहृदयकण्ठस्थितेन तृतीयकविपर्ययः, तट्रैकस्मिन् दिने हृदयस्थो दोष आमाशयमागत्य तत्स्थेन सहज्वरयति तहिने कण्ठस्थितक्ष हृदयमायाति, अपरदिने सोऽप्यामाशयमागत्य ज्वरयति, एवं दिनद्वयं भूत्वा पश्चादेकदिनं न भवतीति तृतीयकविपर्ययः, आमाशयहहदयकण्ठशिरःस्थेन दोषेण चतुर्थकविपर्यय इति तत्र यस्मिन् दिने हृदयस्थो दोष आमाशयमागत्य ज्वरयति तस्मिन् दिने कण्ठस्थो हृदयं शिरस्थश्च कण्ठमायाति; अपरदिने हृदयस्थ आमाशयमागत्य ज्वरयति कण्ठस्थितश्च हृदयमायाति, अपरदिने हृदिस्थ एवामाशयमागत्य ज्वरयति, एवं दिनत्रये भूत्वा पश्चादेकदिनं न भवतीति चतुर्थकविपर्यय इति । एते च सर्व एव ज्वरा न विरुद्धाः, सर्वेषामेव मुनिप्रणीतत्वात् । यथोक्त स्मृतिशाख्रे—‘स्मृतिद्वैधं तु यत्र स्यात्तत्र धर्मावुभौ मतौ’ (म. स्मृ. अ. २ श्लोक १४) इति । दृश्यन्ते च नानाविधा एष विषमज्वराः, एष.एव न्यायश्चरकसुश्चतयोः कुष्ठवैषम्ये वाप्यचन्द्रेण दर्शितः; न वा चिकित्साभेदोऽप्येषामुक्तः; यैव तृतीयकादौ चिकित्सा सैव तद्विपर्ययेऽपीति ।।३९.।। २, अयं पाठ: क-ख पुस्तकयोनोपलभ्यते । व्यहाद द्वयहं ज्वरयति’ आतङ्कदर्पणसंमतः पाठः । नित्यं मन्दज्वरो रूक्षः शूनकस्तेन सीदति । स्तब्धाङ्गः श्लेष्मभूयिष्ठो नरो वातबलासकी । । ४ ० ! । ( अ. सं. नि. अ. २) मधुकोशः उक्तसंगत्या प्रलेपकादनूपद्रवत्वेन तत्सधर्मिणी वातबलासके वाच्ये प्रतिलोमतन्त्रयुक्त्या वातबलासकमेवाह- नित्यमित्यादि । वातबलासकाख्यो ज्वरोऽयास्तीति वातबलासकी नरः, तेन ज्वरेण, शूनकः शोथी, सीदति अवसन्नो भवति; शोधिन: स उपद्रव इत्यर्थ: । शून: कृच्छ्रेण सिध्यति इति पाठात्तरे तेन इति शेष:। वातबलासमेके कुम्भाह्वयापाण्डुरोगविषयमाह्व-रिति गदाधर: ' । वातबलासकारब्यत्वद्वातबलासकः; बलासकः श्लेष्मा, पित्तमत्र बोद्धव्यम् । यदुक्कं तन्त्रान्तरे—वायुः प्रकुपितो दोषावुदीयोभौ विधावति । स शिरस्थः शिरःशूलम्’— ‘भवेद् वातबलासकी’ इति पाठान्तरम् । २. ‘ग़यदास’ इति ग । ‘मन्दज्वरत्वं’ के ख । इत्यादि । यच्चोक्त सुश्रतेन—‘‘प्रलेपक वातबलासक वा कफाधिकत्वात् प्रवदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः’ (सु. उ. अ. ३९) इति । तत्त श्लेष्मणो नित्यानुषक्तत्वेनेति जेज्जट: । रूक्षत्वं चास्य वातपित्ताभिभूतत्वात् कफस्नेहस्य, व्याधिप्रभावाद्वेति ।।४० | |
answer_text: There is another variety of Visamajvara called ''Caturthaka Viparyaya'' in which fever grips for two days with relief on predecessive and successive days to the two days (on which fever manifests). 39 (Ca. ci. 3). In some other treatise it is mentioned that the fever afflicting bone and marrow is Caturthaka Viparyaya which relives on the first day, manifests for the next two days and again relieves on the fourth day. This is supported by Parasara also. *Tryahat' means on the first of the three days it relieves, grips (causes fever) on the last two days at the end of third day, i.e., on the fourth day it relieves again. According to Haricandra, after having caused fever (bout of temperature) for two days, it pacifies on third day and again causes fever on the fourth day and fifth and sixth days. In the same way the Santata Viparyaya etc. have to be imagined. The actual time of affliction of Doşa that causes fever of the irregular fevers is reversed here i.e. the relief period of the normal irregular fever is the fever period of reversal irregular fever and vice versa. Here, the reason is attributed to and hence the name Viparyaya (reversal) to the vitiated Dosa. While commenting on Susruta's state¬ ment, ‘‘while lodging in the Kapha sthana (the places of Kapha), Doşa gives rise to fever on second, third and fourth days called the reversal (irregular) fever which is difficult to cure'', Jejjata mentions about the Anyedyuska, trtiyaka and Caturthaka fevers only, viz. When the Dosa is lodged in the Amasaya and Hrdaya it causes reversal Anyedyuşka. When it is in the Amāśaya (stomach), Hṛdaya (heart-chest) and Kantha (throat), reversal Trtīyaka is caused here, on one day. The Doṣa which is lodged in the heart comes to the stomach and causes fever on the same day. The Dosa which is in the throat comes to the heart and reaches stomach on the next day and causes fever. Thus there is fever for two days continuously with a gap on the third day in the the reversal Trtiiyaka fever. As the Dosa gets seated in Amasaya, Hrdaya, Kantha and Sira it causes Caturthaka Viparyaya, the reversal quartan fever. On the day when the Dosa which is located in Hrdaya comes to Amasaya and causes fever, the Doşa of Kantha (throat) comes to the Hrdaya and reaches Amāśaya on the next day and that also causes fever. On the same day Dosa of Sira comes to Kantha and that of Kantha reaches Hrdaya and ultimately this reaches Amāśaya on the next day and causes fever. Thus fever grips continuously for three days and relieves on the fourth day. This explanation, though seems to be controvertial, is not so because it came from sages as said in Smrti śāstra, ‘‘When there is dual testimony, both can be adopted’’ (Manu Smṛti 2/24). Thus there are many types of irregular fevers. The same theory is given by Vapyacandra in understanding the controversy of Kustha (skin diseases) between the statements of Caraka and Susruta. And also there is no variation of treatment to these reversal irregular fevers. Which ever management is indicated in the irregular fevers, the same is to be adopted here also. ātabalāsaka fever The individual afflicted by Vātabalāsa fever, has continuous mild fever, dryness in the body, oedema, depression, rigidity in the limbs and profuse Slesma. 40 (A. sa. ni. 2)
