context: (च. चि. ३) मधुकोशः चतुर्थकविपर्ययमाह—विषमेत्यादि । अन्न तन्त्रान्तरम्—‘अस्थिमज्जोभयगते चतुर्थकविपर्ययः । स मध्ये ज्वरयत्यह्वी ह्यादावन्ते च मुञ्चति' । इति । आदावेकदिनं मुक्त्वा, मध्ये दिनद्वयं भूत्वा, अन्ते एकदिनं न भवतीति व्याचक्षते जेज्जटादय: । अस्थिमज्जोभयगते चतुर्थकविपर्ययः । त्र्यहाद्र ' द्व्यहं ज्वरयत्यादावने च मुझ्ठति—इति पराशरवचनस्यापि स एवार्थः; त्यहादिति त्यहस्यादिदिनं विमुझ्ठति, दिनद्वयं ज्वरयति, त्यहस्याने चतुर्थदिनं-मुञ्चतीति तात्पर्यार्थं व्याचक्षते । हरिचन्द्रस्त्वाह—द्वे अहनी निरन्तरं ज्वरयित्वा उपरम्यैकमहः पुनर्ज्वरयतीत्येवं चतुर्थकविपर्यय इति । आदिदिनाभावश्रोत्तरपातिदिवसेष्ववधार्यः । चतुर्थकविपर्ययस्योपलक्षणत्वेन तृतीय- कादिविपर्ययोऽप्यूह्य इत्याहुः । तद्यथा—मध्ये एकदिनं ज्वरयति, आद्यन्तयोमुञ्ठतीति तृतीयकविपर्ययः; एककाल विमुच्य सर्वमहोरात्र व्याप्नोतीत्यन्येद्युष्कविपर्ययः; (कालद्वये मुञ्चति, सर्वमहोरात्र ज्वरयतीति सततविर्ययः ' ।) अत्र दोषविकृतिरेव नानाविधा हेतुरिति । ‘कफस्थानेषु वा निष्ठन् दोषो द्वित्रिचतुर्षु च । विपर्ययाख्यान् कुरुते विषमान् कृच्छ्रसाधनान्’ (सु. उ. अ. ३९) इति वृद्धसुश्रतवाक्यं व्याचक्षाणो जेज्जटोऽन्येद्युष्कतृतीयकचतुर्थकमात्रस्य विपर्ययमुदाहरति । यद्यथा—आमाशयहृदयस्थदोषेण यथोदाहृत एवान्येद्युष्कविपर्ययः; आमाशयहृदयकण्ठस्थितेन तृतीयकविपर्ययः, तट्रैकस्मिन् दिने हृदयस्थो दोष आमाशयमागत्य तत्स्थेन सहज्वरयति तहिने कण्ठस्थितक्ष हृदयमायाति, अपरदिने सोऽप्यामाशयमागत्य ज्वरयति, एवं दिनद्वयं भूत्वा पश्चादेकदिनं न भवतीति तृतीयकविपर्ययः, आमाशयहहदयकण्ठशिरःस्थेन दोषेण चतुर्थकविपर्यय इति तत्र यस्मिन् दिने हृदयस्थो दोष आमाशयमागत्य ज्वरयति तस्मिन् दिने कण्ठस्थो हृदयं शिरस्थश्च कण्ठमायाति; अपरदिने हृदयस्थ आमाशयमागत्य ज्वरयति कण्ठस्थितश्च हृदयमायाति, अपरदिने हृदिस्थ एवामाशयमागत्य ज्वरयति, एवं दिनत्रये भूत्वा पश्चादेकदिनं न भवतीति चतुर्थकविपर्यय इति । एते च सर्व एव ज्वरा न विरुद्धाः, सर्वेषामेव मुनिप्रणीतत्वात् । यथोक्त स्मृतिशाख्रे—‘स्मृतिद्वैधं तु यत्र स्यात्तत्र धर्मावुभौ मतौ’ (म. स्मृ. अ. २ श्लोक १४) इति । दृश्यन्ते च नानाविधा एष विषमज्वराः, एष.एव न्यायश्चरकसुश्चतयोः कुष्ठवैषम्ये वाप्यचन्द्रेण दर्शितः; न वा चिकित्साभेदोऽप्येषामुक्तः; यैव तृतीयकादौ चिकित्सा सैव तद्विपर्ययेऽपीति ।।३९.।। २, अयं पाठ: क-ख पुस्तकयोनोपलभ्यते । व्यहाद द्वयहं ज्वरयति’ आतङ्कदर्पणसंमतः पाठः । नित्यं मन्दज्वरो रूक्षः शूनकस्तेन सीदति । स्तब्धाङ्गः श्लेष्मभूयिष्ठो नरो वातबलासकी । । ४ ० ! । ( अ. सं. नि. अ. २) मधुकोशः उक्तसंगत्या प्रलेपकादनूपद्रवत्वेन तत्सधर्मिणी वातबलासके वाच्ये प्रतिलोमतन्त्रयुक्त्या वातबलासकमेवाह- नित्यमित्यादि । वातबलासकाख्यो ज्वरोऽयास्तीति वातबलासकी नरः, तेन ज्वरेण, शूनकः शोथी, सीदति अवसन्नो भवति; शोधिन: स उपद्रव इत्यर्थ: । शून: कृच्छ्रेण सिध्यति इति पाठात्तरे तेन इति शेष:। वातबलासमेके कुम्भाह्वयापाण्डुरोगविषयमाह्व-रिति गदाधर: ' । वातबलासकारब्यत्वद्वातबलासकः; बलासकः श्लेष्मा, पित्तमत्र बोद्धव्यम् । यदुक्कं तन्त्रान्तरे—वायुः प्रकुपितो दोषावुदीयोभौ विधावति । स शिरस्थः शिरःशूलम्’— ‘भवेद् वातबलासकी’ इति पाठान्तरम् । २. ‘ग़यदास’ इति ग । ‘मन्दज्वरत्वं’ के ख । इत्यादि । यच्चोक्त सुश्रतेन—‘‘प्रलेपक वातबलासक वा कफाधिकत्वात् प्रवदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः’ (सु. उ. अ. ३९) इति । तत्त श्लेष्मणो नित्यानुषक्तत्वेनेति जेज्जट: । रूक्षत्वं चास्य वातपित्ताभिभूतत्वात् कफस्नेहस्य, व्याधिप्रभावाद्वेति ।।४० | |

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Dugdha Varga, Chapter 13, verse 1007):

सन्तानिका गुरुः शीता वृष्या पित्तास्रवातनुत् । तर्पणी बृंहणी स्निग्धा बलासबलशुक्रला ।।३५।। खण्डेन सहितं दुग्धं कफकृत्पवनापहम् । सितासितोपलायुक्त शुक्रलं त्रिमलापहम् । सगुडं मूत्रकृच्छुघ्र पित्तश्लेष्मकरं परम् ।।३६।। रात्रौ चन्द्रगुणाधिक्याद्वयायामाकरणात्तथा । प्राभातिक पयः प्रायः प्रादोषाद् गुरु शीतलम् ।।३७।। दिवाकरकराघाताद्वयायामानलसेवनात् । प्राभातिकात्तु प्रादोष लघु वातकफापहम् ।।३८।। वृष्यं बृहणमग्निदीपनकरं पूर्वाहण्काले पयो, मध्याहे तु बलावहं कफहरं पित्तापहं दीपनम् । बाले वृद्धिकरं क्षयेऽक्षयकरं वृद्धेष रेतोवहं, रात्रौ पथ्यमनेकदोषशमनं चक्षुहितं संस्मृतम् ।।३९।। वदन्ति पेयं निशि केवलं पयो भोज्यं न तेनेह सदौदनादिकम् । भवत्यजीर्णं न शयीत शर्वरीं क्षीरस्य पीतस्य च शेषमुत्सृजेत् ।।४०।। विदाहीन्यन्नपानानि दिवा भुड्क्ते हि यन्नरः । तद्विदाहप्रशान्यर्थ रात्रौ क्षीरं सदा पिबेत् ।।४१।। दीप्तानले कृश्ने पुंसि बाले वृद्धे पयःप्रिये । मतं हितमतं दुग्धं सद्यःशुक्रकरं यतः ।।४२।।
answer_text: Cream which form on the upper part of the milk is Guru (Heavy for digestion), Śītavīrya (Cold in potency), Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac), cures diseases of Pitta, Rakta and Vāta, Tarpaṇa (Nourshing), Bṛhmaṇa (Stoutning), Snigdha (Oilyness), Increases Kapha, and Sukrala (Improves seman). If milk is mixed with sugar Increases Kapha and subsides Vāta. If it is added with sugar candy, it is Sukrala (Improves seman) and Subsides all tridoşas. If it is added with Jaggery cures Mūtrakrcchra (Dysuria) and increases Pitta and Kapha doṣas. Benefits of milk specifically to time: Because of predominance of qualities of moon and lack of physical activities, milk from the animals durning day is more guru (Heavy for digestion) and Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency). Where as in the evening, due to exposure to sun, fresh air and excessive physical activities, it makes the milk more Laghu (Light for digestion) and also subsides Vāta and Kapha. Benefits of milk according to times and phases of life phases: Consumption of milk durning morning hours is Vrsya (Aphrodisiac), Brhmana (Stoutning), it stimulates the digestive fire, Durning afternoon, it is Balya (Promotes strength), Subsides Kapha and Pitta and Dīpana (Appetizer). Intake of milk durning child, hood increases bodly tissues, relieves Kaṣāya (Emaciation) and milk consumption durning old age protects seman. In women’s it acts as good pathya (ideal diet), subsides all Tridosas and Chakṣuṣyahita (Good for eyes). Acharya has opinion that, during night consumption of milk is ideal, along with this rice should not be take which may lead Ajīraṇa (Indigestion) and it also promotes good sleep. Milk should not left in the vessel, should be taken as per necessity and should not be waste. To counter the ill effects of Vidāhi aahara (Irritant food) etc., one should consume milk at night. Those who having good digestive capacity, emaciated, childrens, old people and those who like milk, in such person milk is ideal, it stimulate breast milk and improves seman

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Charaka Samhita (Siddhisthana, Chapter 9, verse 111-115):

अजीर्णे मोजने भुक्ते तोये पीतेऽथ उर्विने । प्रतिष्याये नवे खाते खेइपानैऽजुवासने ॥ १११ ॥ नायमं स्नेइनं रोगान करोति स्रैष्मिकान् बहुन् । तत्र एलेप्महरः सर्वस्तीक्ष्णोष्णादिविंधिहितः ॥११२॥ कामे विरेखिते गर्मे व्यायायायिदते वृषि । वातो रूक्षेण नस्येन कुछः स्वाखनयेद्रदान् ॥ ११३ ॥ तम बातहर: सर्वो विधिः स्नेइनर्ष्ट्रणः । स्वेदादिः, स्याद्रघूते क्षीर्र गर्मिण्यास्तु विशेषतः ॥ ११४॥ व्यरशोकातितप्राना तिमिरं मधपस्य तु । रूसी: शीताअनेलेपैः पुटपार्केश साधयेत् ॥ ११५ ॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59):

answer_text: Vihvalati means - reapeatedly the actual vision is perceived and fictitious ob¬ jects are seen or implies the individual gets terrified by the sight of flies etc. Jūlakāni means cob-web; maricini means the rays. Pariplavān - the leaping animals other and as the frog objects seen everywhere. Pariplavan vividhan is considered as, multicoloured things seen leaping in the water by some people. Gocaravibhrama means disturbance of sight perception. Sucipasam na pasyati- the individual can¬ not perceive Sūcīpāśam - the eye of a needle; Pāśam also means the tip of a needle. 30-32, The symptomatology when the dosas get lodged in the third layer When the dosas are located in the third layer, the individual will be able to see the things which are above the level and not the objects in the lower side. The bigger objects are perceived as if covered by a cloth. The living beings (including humans) are perceived as if they are devoid of ears, nose and eye and in deshaped form. And as per the predominance of the afflicting dosa, the colour of the vision keeps changing. 33, 34. (Su.u.7)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Charaka Samhita (Chikitsasthana, Chapter 3, verse 210-215):

बृहती, वत्सकं, मुस्तं, देवदारु, महौषधम् । चव्यं च योगोऽयं संनिपातज्वरापहः ॥ २१० ॥ शटी पुष्करमूले च व्याघ्री शृङ्गी दुरालभा । गुडूची नागरं पाठा किरातं कटुरोहिणी ॥ २११ ॥ बृहत्यौ पौष्करं, भार्गी शटी शृङ्गी दुरालभा । वत्सकस्य च बीजानि पटोलं कटुरोहिणी ॥ २१३ ॥ बृहत्यादिर्गणः प्रोक्तः सन्निपातज्वरापहः । कासादिषु च श्वासेषु दद्यात् सोपद्रवेषु च ॥ २१४ ॥ कषायाश्च यथौवश्यं पिपासाज्वरनाशनाः । निर्दिष्टा भेषजाध्याये भिषगानपि योजयेत् ॥ २१५ ॥
answer_text: Bṛhatī, vatsaka, musta, devadāru, śuṇṭhī and cavya—this formulation is efficacious in sannipātaja fever. Śaṭī, puṣkaramūla, vyāghrī, śṛṅgī, durālabhā, guḍūcī, nāgara, pāṭhā, kirāta and kaṭurohiṇī. Bṛhatī, puṣkaramūla, bhārgī, śaṭī, śṛṅgī, durālabhā, vatsaka seeds, paṭola and kaṭurohiṇī—this Bṛhatyādi group is said to alleviate sannipātaja fever and should be given in cough, dyspnoea, and other complications. The physician may also apply the extracts and gruels prepared from the drugs of thirst-alleviating and antipyretic groups mentioned in the chapter of drugs (Sū. 4)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Chikitsasthana, Chapter 3, verse 210-215.
context: बृहती, वत्सकं, मुस्तं, देवदारु, महौषधम् । चव्यं च योगोऽयं संनिपातज्वरापहः ॥ २१० ॥ शटी पुष्करमूले च व्याघ्री शृङ्गी दुरालभा । गुडूची नागरं पाठा किरातं कटुरोहिणी ॥ २११ ॥ बृहत्यौ पौष्करं, भार्गी शटी शृङ्गी दुरालभा । वत्सकस्य च बीजानि पटोलं कटुरोहिणी ॥ २१३ ॥ बृहत्यादिर्गणः प्रोक्तः सन्निपातज्वरापहः । कासादिषु च श्वासेषु दद्यात् सोपद्रवेषु च ॥ २१४ ॥ कषायाश्च यथौवश्यं पिपासाज्वरनाशनाः । निर्दिष्टा भेषजाध्याये भिषगानपि योजयेत् ॥ २१५ ॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 23):

स्वेदोऽत्यर्थं वा काष्ण्यं स्पर्शाज़त्वं क्षतेऽतिरुक् । सन्धिशैथिल्यमालस्यं सदनं पिडकोद्गमः ॥5॥ जान-जज्ञोर-कट्यस-हस्त-पादाङ्रसन्धिषु निस्तोदः स्फ़रणं भेदो म़क़त्वे सुप्तिरेव च ॥6॥ कण्ड्रः सन्धिषु रुग्भूत्वा भूत्वा नश्यति चासकृत् वैवर्ण्यं मण्डलोत्पत्तिर्वातासुक्पूर्वलक्षणम् ॥7॥
answer_text: The passage starting from hastyasostraih refers to the pathogenesis of the disease vātarakta. Causes of aggravation of vāta include riding on elephant. It makes the blood thinner and thus it forces the blood to accumulate in the lower extremities of the body. Vidahi or over-burnt food also causes accumulation of blood. Excessive walking is also considered an etiological factor of the ailment. Due to domination of vāta that itself is a doṣa and that plays an important role in vitiating other factors the disease vātarakta (and not raktavāta) is produced though both the rakta and vāta are vitiated in the vātarakta. Pūrvarūpa (Premonitory symptoms) (CS. Ci. S. 29.16-18) The prodromal features of the vātarakta include the following features: excessive or no perspiration, blackish discolouration, loss of tactile sensation, severe pain even on slight hurting, lack of firm- ness in the joints, lassitude, depression, appearance of blisters on the skin; pricking sensation, pulsation, breaking sensation, heaviness, numbness and itching sensation in the knees, calf muscle, thighs, pelvis, scapular region, hands, legs and joints. The pain in joints persists and disappears alternatively. There could also manifest discolouring and patches on the body. 5-7
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 23.
context: स्वेदोऽत्यर्थं वा काष्ण्यं स्पर्शाज़त्वं क्षतेऽतिरुक् । सन्धिशैथिल्यमालस्यं सदनं पिडकोद्गमः ॥5॥ जान-जज्ञोर-कट्यस-हस्त-पादाङ्रसन्धिषु निस्तोदः स्फ़रणं भेदो म़क़त्वे सुप्तिरेव च ॥6॥ कण्ड्रः सन्धिषु रुग्भूत्वा भूत्वा नश्यति चासकृत् वैवर्ण्यं मण्डलोत्पत्तिर्वातासुक्पूर्वलक्षणम् ॥7॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 8):

पाण्डुरोगावस्थायां कामलामाहपाण्डुरोगीत्यादि । दग्ध्वा सन्दूष्य । रोगाय कामलारूपाय । भेकवर्णः प्रावृषेण्यभेकवर्णः । कोष्ठ-शाखाश्रयेति एका कोष्ठाश्रया अपरा शाखाश्रया शाखा रक्तादयो धातवः । स्वतन्त्राऽपि कामला भवति यथा राजयक्ष्मा स्वतन्त्र उपेक्षितेष्वपि कासेषु भवतीत्याहुः - कालान्तरात् खरीभूता कृच्छा स्यात् कुम्भकामला । - -
answer_text: One who takes pitta-provoking food is vulnerable to be afflicted with the kāmalā disease in which the pitta vitiates the flesh and blood of the patient. As cough when unattended degenerates into tuberculosis so does the pāṇḍu disease when neglected turns into kāmālā. Kumbha Kāmalā (Advanced stage of jaundice) (CS. Ci. S. 16.37: 1) If left untreated the above situation makes the organs hard and subsequently turns into a difficult disease called Kumbhakamala
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 8.
context: पाण्डुरोगावस्थायां कामलामाहपाण्डुरोगीत्यादि । दग्ध्वा सन्दूष्य । रोगाय कामलारूपाय । भेकवर्णः प्रावृषेण्यभेकवर्णः । कोष्ठ-शाखाश्रयेति एका कोष्ठाश्रया अपरा शाखाश्रया शाखा रक्तादयो धातवः । स्वतन्त्राऽपि कामला भवति यथा राजयक्ष्मा स्वतन्त्र उपेक्षितेष्वपि कासेषु भवतीत्याहुः - कालान्तरात् खरीभूता कृच्छा स्यात् कुम्भकामला । - -

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 6):

अलसकमाह कुक्षिरित्यादि । आनह्यते आध्मायते मलविष्टम्भस्य वक्ष्यमाणत्वात् । प्रताम्येत् मुह्यति पुरुषः परिकूजति आर्तनादं करोति । निरुद्ध इत्यजीर्णेनाधः प्रतिरुद्धगतिः कुक्षी वा तेनोपरि धावति ऊध्वं हृदयकण्ठादिकं गच्छति। अलसक इति दोषस्थिरत्वनिमिता संज्ञा । यदुक्त तन्त्रान्तरे प्रयाति नोध्व नाधस्तादाहारो न विपच्यते । आमाशयेऽलसीभूतस्तेन सोऽलसकः स्मृतः ।। इति ।।- दुष्ट तु भुक्तं कफ-मारुताभ्यां प्रवर्तते नोर्ध्वमधश्च यस्य । विलम्बिकां तां भृशदुश्चिकित्स्यामाचक्षते शास्त्रविदः पुराणाः ॥ ॥ - - -
answer_text: The passage in context details the implications of alasaka that could develop due to indigestion. Constipation causes bloated stomach. In this state, the downward movement of the vala is obstructed and it moves upwards towards the heart and throat. The condition where in there is a lack of movement of dosas is termed as alasaka (lassitude of doşas as there is no apparent expulsion of the digested food, either upwards or downwards). As stated elsewhere, The food settles in the stomach without going upwards or downwards and it does not get digested even. Such condition is called Alasaka or immobility of food. The term parikijati has been explained differently. Vijaya- raksita, the author of Madhukośa, has suggested that it refers to the moaning of the patient who is in severe pain due to non-movement of the food in the intestines. Some other scholars opine that the term kūjati signifies not moaning but the sound produced by the blocked intestines. It may be noted that the term parikujati denotes the pecu- liar voice produced by the pigeons. Vilambikā (SS. Ut. 56.9) The ingested food, when vitiated by kapha and vāta, does not move upwards or downwards. Such symptoms have been identified as vila¬ mbikā that is very tough to manage according to the learned ones. 21
chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 6.
context: अलसकमाह कुक्षिरित्यादि । आनह्यते आध्मायते मलविष्टम्भस्य वक्ष्यमाणत्वात् । प्रताम्येत् मुह्यति पुरुषः परिकूजति आर्तनादं करोति । निरुद्ध इत्यजीर्णेनाधः प्रतिरुद्धगतिः कुक्षी वा तेनोपरि धावति ऊध्वं हृदयकण्ठादिकं गच्छति। अलसक इति दोषस्थिरत्वनिमिता संज्ञा । यदुक्त तन्त्रान्तरे प्रयाति नोध्व नाधस्तादाहारो न विपच्यते । आमाशयेऽलसीभूतस्तेन सोऽलसकः स्मृतः ।। इति ।।- दुष्ट तु भुक्तं कफ-मारुताभ्यां प्रवर्तते नोर्ध्वमधश्च यस्य । विलम्बिकां तां भृशदुश्चिकित्स्यामाचक्षते शास्त्रविदः पुराणाः ॥ ॥ - - -

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 55):

मधुकोशः अहिपूतनसमानहेतुलिङ्गतया गुदाश्रयं गुदभ्रंशमुल्लङ्वयानन्तरं वृषणकच्छूमाहस्नानोत्सादनहीनस्येत्यादि। एषा च निदानविशेषात् प्रायो वृषणभावित्वाद्विशिष्टचिकित्सोपयोगित्वाच्च कुष्ठोक्तकच्छुतो भेदेन पठ्यते ॥ ५२–५३ ॥ प्रवाहणातीसाराभ्यां निर्गच्छति गुदं बहिः। रूक्षदुर्बलदेहस्य गुदभ्रंशं तमादिशेत्॥ ५४॥ मधुकोशः गुदभ्रंशलिङ्गमाह-प्रवाहणेत्यादि। प्रवाहणं प्रकर्षेण कुन्थनम्। ‘वाह प्रयत्ने’ इत्यस्य रूपम्। प्रवाहणे- नातिवेगोदीरणेन वातकोपः, अतीसारेण तु धातुक्षयात्; यदि वा प्रवाहणेनातीसारेण चाधोगतमारुतत्वेन गुदनिर्गमो रूक्षादिदेहस्य॥ ५४॥ सदाहो रक्तपर्यन्तस्त्वक्पाकी तीव्रवेदनः । कण्ड्रमाञ् ज्वरकारी च स स्याच्छूकरदंष्टूकः ॥ ५५ ॥ ( सु.नि. १३ ) इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने क्षुद्ररोगनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ५५॥ मधुकोशः वराहदंष्ट्रलिङ्गमाह-सदाह इत्यादि। अयं ‘वराहदाढ’ इति लोके प्रसिद्धः॥ ५५॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां क्षुद्ररोगनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥ ५५ ॥
answer_text: Since there is similarity in the aetiology and symptomatology Vṛṣɑṇɑ kɑcchū is being explained after ahiputana; skipping Gudabhramsa (prolapse of the anus) (which also occurs in the anus as ahiputana). Due to typical aetiology and perhaps occuring only in the testes and also haivng a specific line of treatment, this condi¬ tion is read seperately from the Kacchū mentioned in Kuṣṭha (skin-diseases). 52, 53. Gudabhraṃśa Due to forceful evacuation of stools and also due to severe diarrhoea, in dry and weak indivduals the anus comes out of its place (prolapses out) which is called Gudabhraṃśa (prolapse of the ani). Mādhavanidānaṃ Pravahana - forceful endeavour to pass motion (moaning with effort); vahmaking effort. In atisara, due to loss of essential fluids (dhatus), again vata aggravates. Otherwise it can be implied that due to applying pressure and also due to diarrhoea, in a dry and weak individual, the anus prolapses out. 54. Sūkara damstraka/Varāha damstraka A condition where there is burning sensation, bleeding, ulceration severe pain, itching sensation and fever is called Sukaradamstra. Thus ends the chapter on Ksudra roga (minor disease) in Madhava's book of diagnosis, written by Srimādhavakara 55. This disease is popular by the name Varahadadh. Thus ends the chapter on Ksudra roga (minor diseases) in the Madhukosacommentary in Madhava's book of diagnosis. 55. ＊＊＊＊
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 55.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 5):

पूर्वरूपमाह विष्टम्भ इत्यादि । विष्टम्भोऽन्नस्येति विष्टभ्यान्नस्य जीर्णतागमनमु आहारो विष्टव्य आमाशय एवावतिष्ठते वातवैगुण्यात् । दौर्बल्यं हीनशक्तिता । विष्टम्भोऽङ्गस्य इति पाठान्तरे विष्टम्भो मलस्य अङ्गस्य दौर्बल्यम् । यद्यपि निदानानन्तरं पूर्वरूपं वक्तव्यं भवति तथाऽपि निदानलक्षणानन्तरमत्र पूर्वरूपं निदानलिङ्गयोश्चिकित्साङ्गतमत्वप्रतिपादनाथं तयोः पूर्वमभिधानम् अथवाऽवश्यवक्तव्यानां कामचारादभिधानमिति । एवमन्यत्रापि व्यतिक्रमे द्रष्टव्यम् । कुक्षेराटोपो गुडगुडाशब्दः इति चक्रः तनतनी इति गुणाकरः रुजापूर्वकः क्षोभः इति गदाधरः पुरीषवृद्धिलक्षणे च आटोपम् आध्मानम् इति विवृतवान् एतच्च न सर्वत्र ग़ुल्मपूर्वरूपे आटोपाध्मानयोरुभयोरपि पाठात् । उद्गरबाहुल्यमधीनिरुद्धस्य वायोरूध्व- गमनात । संक्थिसादो जङ्गावसादः । ग्रहणीदोषपाण्ड्वर्तेः ग्रहणीदोषयुक्तपाण्ड्रोगस्य उदास्य चाशङ्गा तेषां लक्षणदर्शनात् । ग्रहणीदोषपाण्ड्वर्तिः इति पाठान्तरे ग्रहणीदोषस्य पाण्डोः पाण्डुरोगस्य चार्तिः पीडा स्यात् । अभिवृद्धये उत्पत्यर्थमिति ।।- पञ्चात्मा मारुतः पित्तं कफो गुदवलित्रयम् । सर्व एवं प्रकुप्यन्ति गुदजानां समुद्भवे ॥३३॥ तस्मादशांसि दुःखानि बहव्याधिकराणि च । सर्वदेहोपतापीनिधि प्रायः - कृच्छूतमानिधि चे ॥॥ ननु गुददेशदुष्ट्या गुदजस्योत्पादात् कथं सर्वर्देहे कृशत्व-कृष्णत्वादिरूपा दृष्टिरित्यत आहपञ्चात्मेत्यादि । पञ्चात्मा पञ्चस्वरूपः प्राणापानसमानोदानव्यानभेदात् हदि प्राणो गुदेऽपानः समानो नाभिसंस्थितः । उदानः कण्ठदेशे स्याद् व्यानः सर्वशरीरगः ॥ इति तेषां स्थानानि । एवं लिङ्गविपरिणामात् पश्चात्मकत्वं पित्तेऽपि योज्यं पित्तं ह्यालोचक-रञ्जक- साधक-पाचक-भ्राजकभेदाद्दित्रम् । आलोचकं नेत्रयोः रञ्नकं यकृत्प्लीहोः साधर्क हृदि पाचक पक्वामाशययोर्मध्ये भ्राजकं त्वचीति। एवं कफोऽपि पञ्चात्मा हृदयामाशयजिह्नाशिरः सन्धिषु क्रमेणावलम्बक-क्लेदक-बोधक-तर्पक-श्लेष्मकभेदात् । यदाह गोतमः श्लेष्मा तु पञ्चघोरस्थः क्लेदकादिस्वकर्मणा । कफधाम्ना च सर्वेषा यत् करोत्यवलम्बनम् ।। अतोऽवलम्बकः श्लेष्मा यस्त्वामाशयसंश्रितः । क्लेदकः सोऽन्त्रसङ्वातक्लेदनाद् रसबोऽ नात् । बोधको रसनास्थस्तु शिरःसंस्थोऽक्षितर्पणात् । तर्पकः श्लेष्मकः सम्यक् श्लेषणात् सन्धिपु स्थितः ॥ इति । गुदवलित्रयस्य च प्रकोपो विकृतत्वं प्रवाहणादिस्वकार्याकर्तृत्वं च । गुदवलित्रये इति पाठान्तरं न युक्तं तत्र प्राणोदानयोः सन्निधानस्याप्यभावात् वलिदुष्टर- प्राप्तेश्व । सर्व एवेति उक्तमारुतादय एवेति । तस्मादित्यादि । बहुव्याधिकराणीति जठराग्नि- मान्द्याद्यपद्रवकराणि । प्रायः कृच्छ्रतमानीति प्रायोग्रहणादसाध्यानि सुखसाध्यान्यपि ।।-।। बाह्यायां तु वलौ जातान्येकदोषोल्बणानि च अर्शांसि सुखसाध्यानि न चिरोत्पतितानि च ॥ ॥ द्वन्द्वजानि द्वितीयायां वलौ यान्याश्रितानि च । कच्छसाध्यानि तान्याहः परिसंवत्सराणि चं॥॥ सहजानि त्रिदोषाणि यानि चाभ्यन्तरां वलिम् । जायन्तेऽर्शांसि संश्रित्य तान्यसाध्यानि निर्दिशेत् ॥३७॥ - answer_text: This passage is meant to describe the prodromal features of the piles. The disturbed vala causes vistambha (halted digestion of the food taken). In this situation, the food taken remains in the stomach for a stretched time and subsequently the vata dosa gets provoked. In the opinion of some scholars, the first term should be read as ‘Viṣṭambhoaṅgasya’; in that case, it would mean ‘non-movement of excreta and weakness of the body’. Normally, prodromal description of a disease is presented before the discussion on the pathogenesis. Here, this order has been reversed. However, it may be noted that both the prodromal features as well as the pathogenesis are significant from the point of view of the treatment. It is the discretion of author to decide the order of the narrative. The readers should be cautious regarding the order preferred by the author in context. The commentator Cakrapāṇi has taken the term kukṣeraṭopa to mean the sound of gurgling. The term has been accepted to mean tension in the stomach by the commentator Gunakara while Gadadhara would. Arsa Nidanam take the same term to mean movement in the stomach. Mādhvakara has accepted the term āṭopa to mean the disease ādhmānā. Nevertheless, it should be remembered that the terms adhmana and ātopa have been used differently in the context of the prodromal features of the disease gulma. Over-belching is due to restriction of the downward movement of vāta. This has been signified by the term udgārabāhulya. This also means the reversal of the direction of the fart. The term sakthisāda means loss of strength in the thighs. The term grahaṇīdoṣapāṇḍvarte or grahaṇīdoṣapāṇḍvarti refers to the pain produced by the ailment that is similar to the one generated by the diseases grahanī as well as pāṇḍιι. Among the prodromal features of the piles all the above signs are noticed. The role of piles in troubling the whole body (CS. Ci. 14.24, 25) All the five divisions of each of the vāta, pitta and kapha doṣas invade all the three folds of the rectum to generate arsas. Thus, arsa is a very painful disease. It affects the whole body, is difficult for treatment, and gives rise to several other diseases also. 33-34 It is only because of the vitiation of the anus (and not any other part of the body) that piles are formed there. Then how do they produce the same variety of symptoms like, emaciation, blackishness etc. that relates to the entire body? This aspect is explained in the preceding lines. The five types of vata situated in the anus include the Prana or the respiratory element which is situated in the Hṛdaya or heart, Apāna (force for excretion) situated in the anus, Samana (force that kindles the digestive fire) situated in the naval region, Udāna (the speech element) situated in the throat and Vyāna (the circulatory element) which moves about in the whole body. Likewise, pitta is also of five varieties: the Alocaka (sight element) that is situated in the eyes, Bhrajaka (factor responsible for skin colour and absorption of unguents) that is situated in the skin; Rañjaka that is situated in the liver and spleen, Sādhaka that is located in the heart and finally the Pācaka pitta that is seated in between the stomach and intestines (duodenum). Similarly, there are five categories of kapha also. They are situated in the Hrdaya (breast), Amāṣaya (stomach), Jihvāʿ (tongue), Sira (head), and the Sandhi (joints). They have been named respectively as Avalambaka, Kledaka, Bodhaka, Tarpaka and Sleşaka. The seer Gautama has stated that ślesmā which exists in the chest is of five types. As it is related to the chest, it is named Avalambaka. The one that is found in the stomach provides wetness to the food stuff, hence, it is called Kledaka. One is called Bodhaka as it is located in the tongue and the taste is identified by this. The Tarpaka variety of kapha is located in the brain while the one which exists in the joints is called Śleṣaka as it provides proper lubrication there. The term gudayalitraya refers to the vitiation of the three rings of the anus and their deformation. They no longer remain capable to carry out their function of expelling the stool. Various diseases or complications are caused by piles such as Agnimandya (lost or weakened appetite) etc. and these are generally difficult ones. In this, the term probably (Prūyah) suggests that piles are both difficult and easy to cure according to their location and style. Prognosis of the disease of piles (CS. Ci. 14.31) The pile mass located in the external fold of the rectum, that has emerged out of the provocation of only one dosa and which has only recently appeared is easy to cure. 35 (CS. Ci. 14.30) The pile mass generated by vitiation of two dosas together, located in the middle fold of the rectum and existing for more than one year is difficult to cure. 36 (CS. Ci. 14.28) The pile mass that is hereditary, born out of all the three dosas provoked together, that has been located in the innermost fold of the rectum is impossible to cure. 37

कृच्छूतमानिधि चे ॥॥ ननु गुददेशदुष्ट्या गुदजस्योत्पादात् कथं सर्वर्देहे कृशत्व-कृष्णत्वादिरूपा दृष्टिरित्यत आहपञ्चात्मेत्यादि । पञ्चात्मा पञ्चस्वरूपः प्राणापानसमानोदानव्यानभेदात् हदि प्राणो गुदेऽपानः समानो नाभिसंस्थितः । उदानः कण्ठदेशे स्याद् व्यानः सर्वशरीरगः ॥ इति तेषां स्थानानि । एवं लिङ्गविपरिणामात् पश्चात्मकत्वं पित्तेऽपि योज्यं पित्तं ह्यालोचक-रञ्जक- साधक-पाचक-भ्राजकभेदाद्दित्रम् । आलोचकं नेत्रयोः रञ्नकं यकृत्प्लीहोः साधर्क हृदि पाचक पक्वामाशययोर्मध्ये भ्राजकं त्वचीति। एवं कफोऽपि पञ्चात्मा हृदयामाशयजिह्नाशिरः सन्धिषु क्रमेणावलम्बक-क्लेदक-बोधक-तर्पक-श्लेष्मकभेदात् । यदाह गोतमः श्लेष्मा तु पञ्चघोरस्थः क्लेदकादिस्वकर्मणा । कफधाम्ना च सर्वेषा यत् करोत्यवलम्बनम् ।। अतोऽवलम्बकः श्लेष्मा यस्त्वामाशयसंश्रितः । क्लेदकः सोऽन्त्रसङ्वातक्लेदनाद् रसबोऽ नात् । बोधको रसनास्थस्तु शिरःसंस्थोऽक्षितर्पणात् । तर्पकः श्लेष्मकः सम्यक् श्लेषणात् सन्धिपु स्थितः ॥ इति । गुदवलित्रयस्य च प्रकोपो विकृतत्वं प्रवाहणादिस्वकार्याकर्तृत्वं च । गुदवलित्रये इति पाठान्तरं न युक्तं तत्र प्राणोदानयोः सन्निधानस्याप्यभावात् वलिदुष्टर- प्राप्तेश्व । सर्व एवेति उक्तमारुतादय एवेति । तस्मादित्यादि । बहुव्याधिकराणीति जठराग्नि- मान्द्याद्यपद्रवकराणि । प्रायः कृच्छ्रतमानीति प्रायोग्रहणादसाध्यानि सुखसाध्यान्यपि ।।-।। बाह्यायां तु वलौ जातान्येकदोषोल्बणानि च अर्शांसि सुखसाध्यानि न चिरोत्पतितानि च ॥ ॥ द्वन्द्वजानि द्वितीयायां वलौ यान्याश्रितानि च । कच्छसाध्यानि तान्याहः परिसंवत्सराणि चं॥॥ सहजानि त्रिदोषाणि यानि चाभ्यन्तरां वलिम् । जायन्तेऽर्शांसि संश्रित्य तान्यसाध्यानि निर्दिशेत् ॥३७॥ - answer_text: Eranḍa taila Tīkṣaṇa (Penetrating), Dīpana (Appetizer), Picchala (Sticky), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac), Tvacya (Good for skin), Vayastapana (Antiagening), Mēdhya (Brain tonic), Kanti (Lustre), Balya (Promotes strength), Kaṣāya (Astringent) in secondary taste, Sukṣma (Minute), Yoniśhodaka (Clears female genitals), Śukraśhodaka (Purifies seman), Vistram (Foul smelling), Madhura (Sweet), Tikta (Bitter) and Katu (Pungent) in taste Madhura vīpaka (Pungent in post digestion) and Sāra (Laxative). It cures Vişama jvara (Malaria), Hrdroga (Cardiac diseases), Pruştagudaśūla (Pain in back and anal region), Disease of Vāta, Udararoga (Abdominal diseases), Gūlma (Abdominal tumors), Aṣṭilā (Diseases of Prostate), Katigraha (Stiffness in waist regions), Vātarakta (Gout), Malabadha (Constipation), Brandha (Hernia), Sotha (Inflammation), Āma (Undigested food) and Vīdradi (Abcess). The fatal disease Āmavāta (Rheumatism) is roaming throughout the body as like an elephant in the forest, which can be controlled by the action of Eranda taila, like a loin, the majesty of wild animals. question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2):

अथ विषमज्वरसम्प्राप्तिमाहदोषोऽल्प इत्यादि । अल्प इत्यनेनाबलत्वात् काल- विशेषमवाप्य लव्धबलो ज्वरयति यस्तु बलवान् स नित्यज्वरमेव करोति । अहितसम्भूत इति अहिताहाराचारादिसम्भूतो वृद्धः । ज्वरोत्सृष्टस्य सहसा निवृत्त-ज्वरस्य । वाशब्देन प्रथमतोऽपि विषमज्वरो भवतीति दर्शयति । यदुक्त आरम्भाद्विषमो यस्तु इत्यादि । धातुमन्यतमें रस- रक्तादिकम् । विषमज्वरं तृतीयकादिकम् । विषमज्वरसामान्यलक्षणं च भालुकिना पठितं यः स्यादनियतात् कालाच्छीतोष्णाभ्यां तथैव च । वेगतश्रापि विषमो ज्वरः स विषमः स्मृतः सन्ततं रसरक्तस्थः सोऽन्येद्युः पिशिताश्रितः ॥३ ॥ मेदोगतस्तृतीयेऽह्नि त्वस्थिमज्जगतः पुनः । कुर्याच्चतुर्थकं का प्रघोरमन्तकं का परोगसङ्करम् ॥३३॥ - - - - -
answer_text: This passage is meant to signify the pathological features of the disease named Viṣama Jvara. The term alpa bala means something that has least strength. The something here is none but the dosa that has been aggravated but has no capability to cause fever in the beginning. Nonetheless, the same weak dosa after having positive circumstantial conditions gains strength in due course of time and produces irregular fever or Visama Jvara. If the vitiated dosa had been strong enough it could have caused natural fever only. The term 'Ahitasambhūta' used there means something developed for strengthened by adopting non-homologous foods etc. The dosa of a person who has been just recovered from fever can also produce fever by adopting non-homologous foods and the like habits etc. By using the term va it has been stressed that even without having relieved from fever, adopting non homologous foods and the like habits etc. could cause fever in a person who has been indulging in these habits. It has been suggested that such habits may provoke the dosas to enter one of the dhatus (rasa, rakta etc.) to subsequently produce vişama jvara or irregular fever like tertian fever etc. The commentator Bhaluki presents the common features of an irregular fever in the following term: There will be no regulation or correspondence with time, atmosphere, and bout of temperature in irregular fever and hence, it is named so. Dhātu-relationship of irregular fevers (SS. Ut. 39. 67, 68/1) Among the fevers referred to above, the santata jvara involves rasa and rakta dhātus, anyedyuṣka jvara involves māṁṣadhātu. The tritiyaka jvara involves medas. The caturthaka jvara involves asthi and majjā dhātus, which is a dreadful and fatal symptom. 32-33
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 411):

शतावरी बहुसुता भीरुरिन्दीवरी वरी । नारायणी शतपदी शतवीर्या च पीवरी ।।१८४।। महाशतावरी चान्या शतमूल्यूर्ध्वकण्टिका । सहस्रवीर्या हेतुश्च ऋष्यप्रोक्ता महोदरी ।।१८५।। शतावरी गुरुः शीता तिक्ता स्वाद्वी रसायनी । मेधाऽग्निपुष्टिदा स्निग्धा नेत्र्या गुल्मातिसारजित् ।।१८६।। शुक्रस्तन्यकरी बल्या वातपित्तास्रशोथजित् । महाशतावरी मेध्या हृद्या वृष्या रसायनी ।।१८७।। शीतवीर्या निहन्त्यश्रोंग्रहणीनयनामयान् । तदङ्करस्त्रिदोषघ्न लघुरर्शःक्षयापहा ।।१८८।।
answer_text: External uses: The roots of Musali are rubbed with goats milk and applied over Vyanga (Feekles). Mātrā (Dosage): Mūla cūrṇa: 3 - 6 gm. ŚATĀVARĪ AND MAHĀŚATĀVARĪ Latin: Asparagus racemosa Willd. Fam: Liliaceae Hin: Satavare, Satamuli Eng: Buttermilk root Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Bahusutā, Bhīru, Indīvarī, Varī, Nārāyanī, Śatavīryā and pīvarī and that of Māha Saṭāvarī are Saṭamūlī, Urdhavakaṇṭakā, Sahasravīryā, Hētu, Rṣyaprōktā and Mahodarī. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Śatāvarī is Guru (Heavy for digestion), Sita vīrya (Cold in potency), Tikta (Bitter) and Madhura (Sweet) in taste, Rasāyana (Rejuvenator), Mēdhya (Brain tonic), Agnivardaka (Appetizers), Puṣṭidā (Nutritious), Snigdha (Oilyness), Netrahita (Good for eyes), Sukravardaka (Promotes seman), Stanyajanana (Galactagogue), Balya (Strength promoters). It cures Gulma (Abdominal tumours), Atisāra (Diarrhoea), Diseases of Vāta, Pitta, Rakta and Sotha (Inflammation). Māhāśaṭāvarī is a Mēdhya (Brain tonic), Hṛdya (Useful in cardiac diseases), Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac), Rasāyana (Rejuvenator) and Śitā vīrya (Cold in potency). It cures Arśas (Piles), Grahaṇī (Spure) and Netraroga (Eye diseases). It’s young shoots are Laghu (Light for digestion), Increases tridoṣas and cures Arśas (Piles) and Kṣaya (Emaciation). Note: Māhāśatāvarī (Asparagus sarmentosus Linn.) Habitat of south India, Bigger climber, Root stalk have more number of tubers. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Throughout tropical and Subtropical India. Swarūpa (Botanical description): A tuberous, branched, climber with straight or recurved spines. The branches are modified into leaflets called Cladodes 1/2-1inch long. Flowers in racemes or fascicles, fragnant small, white in colour. Fruits berry 0.4-0.6cm. long, are in the purple- black when ripe consist of 1-2 seeds. Prayojya anga (Part used): Kanda (Root tubers). Chemical constituents: Furostanolic sponins, Sitosterol, B- sitosterol, Favonoids, Glycosides, Sugars
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 411
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 411.

द्विविधं हि रोगस्य कारणंविप्रकृष्ट सन्निकृष्ट च तत्र विप्रकृष्ट विरुद्धाहारादि सन्निकृष्ट वातादि तस्य वातादेः सर्वरोगेष्वव्यभिचरितकारणत्वमाहसर्वेपामित्यादि । यदुक्तं सुथ्रुत नास्ति रोगो विना दोपैर्यस्मात्तस्माद्विचक्षणः । अनुक्तमपि दोपाणां लिङ्गैव्याधिमुपाचरेत् । इति सु०सू० । आगन्तुव्याधिपु यद्यप्युत्पत्ती दोषकोपो नास्ति तथाऽप्युत्पत्यनन्तर- मवश्यम्भावी उत्पन्नद्रव्ये गुणयोगवत् । यदुक्तं चरकेआगन्तुर्हि व्यथापूर्वसमुत्पन्नो जघन्यं वातपित्तश्लेष्मणां वैषम्यमापा-दयति इति च०सू० निदानं कारणम् । मला दोषाः मलिनीकरणात् । ननु वातादीनां किमिदं दोषत्वम् अत्राहुरेके स्वातन्त्येण दूषकत्वं दोषत्वं रसादिदूष्य-व्यवच्छेदार्थं स्वातन्त्र्येण इति पदं ते हि वातादिदुष्टाः सन्तो दूष्यान्तर- द्षकाः । अत्राहुरन्येकिमिद स्वातन्त्र्यं किं दोषान्तरनिरपेक्षत्वं हेत्वन्तरनिरपेक्षत्वं वा आद्ये वातस्येव दोषत्व स्यात् न तु वातसापेक्षयोः कफपित्तयोः यदुक्तं पित्तं पङ्गुः कफः पड्गुः पड्गवो मलधातवः । वायुना यत्र नीयन्ते तत्र गच्छन्ति मेघवत् ।। इति द्वितीये वातस्यापि न दोषत्वं कफपित्तयोरिव निदानसापेक्षस्यैव तस्य दूषकत्वात् तस्मात् प्रकृत्यारम्भकत्वे दुष्टिकर्तृत्व दोषत्वम् इति लक्षणम् । रसरक्तादिनिवृत्यथं प्रकृत्यारम्भ- कत्वम् इति विशेषणम् । नहि वातादिप्रकृतिवच्छास्त्रे रसरक्तादिप्रकृतिरुक्ता वातादिप्रकृतित्वं च शरीस्य वातादिदूषित-शुक्रशोणितारब्धत्वम् । यदाह चरकःदोषानुशायिता होषां देहप्रकृतिरुच्यते । तथा वातलाद्याः सदाऽऽतुराः । इति च०सू० । सुश्रुतेनापि प्रकृतिलक्षणे वातप्रकृतिः स्फुटितकर- चरणो जागरूकोऽनवस्थितचितः सु०शा० इत्याद्युक्तम् । प्रकृतिरोगयोश्चायं भेदःप्रकृतिरपथ्यसेवया नात्यन्तं बाधते । यदुक्तंविषजातो यथा कीटो विषेण न विपद्यते । तद्वत् प्रकृतिभिर्देहस्तज्जातत्वान्न वाध्यते ।। सु०शा० इति सङ्क्षेपः । विस्तरस्तु सुश्रुतश्लोकवार्तिके प्रश्नविधानाख्ये टीकासु च द्रष्टव्यः । ननु प्रकृत्यारम्भकत्वे दोषत्वम् इत्येवास्तु । सत्यं विपक्षाद्व्यावृत्तिर्भवत्येव किन्तु दोषस्वरूपं नोक्त स्यादिति । सुश्रुतादिभिर्वातादेरिव चिकित्साविशेषाणामभिधानाद्रक्तस्यापिक दोषत्वं - पूर्वटीकाकारैराषाढवर्मस्वामिदासादिभिः स्वीकृतं तदप्येतेन व्यवच्छिन्नम् अधुनातनैरस्वीक्रियमाणत्वात् । ननु दोषाश्चेत् कारणं तर्हि तेषां सर्वदा देहे सद्भावातु सर्वदा रोगोत्पादकत्वप्रसङ्ग इत्यत आहकुपिता इति विकृतिमापत्राः । ननु तत्प्रकोपः स्वभावात् कारणान्तराद्वा नाद्यः पूर्ववत्प्रसङ्गात् अथ कारणान्तरादिति किं तदित्याह विविधाहितसेवनमिति । विविधस्य नानाविधस्य अहितस्य असात्म्येन्द्रियार्थ- संयोग-प्रज्ञापराध-परिणाम-लक्षणस्य सेवनमिति ।। मा०नि०-७ निदानार्थकरो रोगो रोगस्याप्युपजायते ॥ ॥ - answer_text: The reason (hetu) for diseases are of two types Sannikṛṣṭa (proximal) and Viprakrṣṭa (distant). The Viprakṛṣṭa (distant) reasons include factors like indulging in consumption of incompatible foods. The Sannikrsta (proximal) reasons include factors like vata and other dosas. These factors have a major impact on the genesis of a disease. lt has been told in Suśruta that there is no disease without involvement of dosas and even if the particular dosa’s involvement is not detected, the wise physician should treat the disease through the signs and symptoms (SS. Sū. 35.19). Though there is no involvement of dosa-aggravation in the onset of disease, it could take place after the disease is manifested. Though in the case of Agantu (suddenly occurring due to extrinsic causes) diseases, the instrumentality of doşa is not that apparent, in terms of the practical realities, but once the disease is unfolded it is manifested through the vitiation of dosa only. Thus, it is certain that the vitiation of doşa would take place even when its genesis is due to āgantuja causes. Caraka has also supported this view (CS. Sīī. 20.6). It could be clear through this example: A disease called injury (kṣata) is produced by injury to the body. Nevertheless, immediately after that the injury produces swelling, burning sensation, supperation and pus. These implications are possible through none but the different dosas. In this case the dosas involved include pitta (swelling, burning sensation and suppuration) and kapha (pus). Nidāna implies the doṣas as instrumental in causing disease. The doşas are termed as malas as they vitiate the body. But how can vāta etc. be called as doṣas (vitiators)? Authorities say that the factor that individually vitiate is a dosa. The word has been used here individually/independent to avoid the inclusion of rasa etc. which are in fact the dusyas (the ones to be vitiated). These (Rasa etc. dhatus) get vitiated by vata etc. and subsequently vitiate other factors. Other authorities argue as to what is that individuality? Is it the factor not depending upon other doşa or not depending upon another reason in the process of pitta and kapha. It is claimed that pitta is lame, kapha is lame, and the excreta (impurities) and other dhātus (tissues) are lame as well. All these are moved from one place to other by vāta as the clouds move with the force of wind. Yet some authorities maintain that vāta has also no vitiating property like kapha and pitta. They all get vitiated or aggravated by the etiological factors. That is why they are termed as dosas. The dosas are also formed in the body in the very beginning, i. e. at the time of the formation of the zygote, which is also known as onset of Prakṛti (the bodily constitution). To exclude Rasa (chyle) and Rakta (blood) etc., the word Prakṛtyarambhakatva (cause of the onset of Prakṛtī) has been used. The body has been classified as per the vāta and other doșa constitution. Such classification has not been mentioned regarding Rasa (chyle), Rakta (blood) etc. The formation of Prakyti of the body takes place with doṣas. Caraka has said that the bodily constitution is based upon dosas and those who are dominated by vāta are always prone to diseases. (CS. Pañca Nidāna Lakṣanam Sī. 7.39). Regarding the qualities of Prakṛti, it is also said by Suśruta, that the individual of vāta Prakṛti has ticking sounds in the hands and legs while walking and working, he remains always waking and he has a fickle mind. (SS. Śā. 4.64). The Prakṛti is associated with the doṣas and the rogas or diseases are also associated with the dosas. Then what is the difference between the two? The difference between Prakṛti (the bodily constitution) and roga is that the Prakṛti does not give much trouble to the body inspite of taking incompatible foods and indulging in unhealthy habits. If an individual having the vāta dominated natural constitution (Prakṛti) he would not face much trouble if he indulges in the vāta promoting food and regimens. On the other hand, if a patient of vāta indulges in vāta promoting food and regimens he would face dire consequences. As stated by Susruta, the poisonous insect is not disturbed by its own poison like-wise the Prakṛti of a body is not disturbed by the dosa from which it has been originated. SS'. Sā. 4.79). This aspect has been detailed in the Commentary, 'Prasna Vidhana' written on the Suśruta Saṁhitā and in the text Suśruta Sloka Vārtika. (As reported by Dr Brahmānanda Tripāthi, both of these texts is neither available nor reported through an old text except the present Madhukośa). Thus, origin of the Prakṛti is the criterion of doṣa. Yet admitting this would not be sufficient for an inquisitive physician. He should also try to know the impact of dosa on parts of body such as the rakta and other dhatus. Moreover, the detailed form of the dosa is also to be ascertained. The time of aggravation, its extension to other places, diseases caused, symptomatology and management of rakta (blood) etc. have also been explained by Suśruta in the particular contexts of the vāta, pitta and kapha. This description was acceptable to the old commentators like Aṣāḍha, Dharma, Svāmidāsa and others. However the new generation scholars are not accepting this. They do not accept Rakta as dhatu. The debate on rakta is a long one. Generally it has been accepted as none but one of the seven dhātus. The three great authorities Caraka, Susruta and Vāgbhata have repeatedly laid stress on the three doṣas only: the vāta, pitta and kapha. The references that create confusion regarding rakta as one of the dosas are not many and are ambiguous. They could be dismissed as exceptions. References from Caraka that are quoted in this context include: Sī. 24.18, Ci. 5.27. References from Suśruta that are quoted in this context include: Sī. 21.3; 14. 44. Finally, the question arises that if the doṣas like vāta, pitta and kapha are ever present in the body how come they do not produce diseases all the time? This question is countered with the fact that the dosas produce diseases only when they get vitiated (either singly or in a joint way). Then it could be asked whether the doşas get vitiated by nature or by any other cause? The answer is that the dosas that are naturally present do not produce ailments but when they get vitiated through factors such as intake of harmful foods and regimen (the parināma), harmful use of the sense organs (asātmyendriyārtha samyoga) and offence commited against social conducts and regula¬ tions (the prañjyāparādha). Sometimes some diseases acting as etiological agents, might be instrumental in producing other diseases. 15

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 33):

मधुकोशः चन्द्रोदयप्रणयपीवरदुग्धसिन्धुपूरभ्रमं वहति यद्गुणकीर्तिगुच्छः॥ तेन व्यधायि गुरुणा विजयेन शिष्यप्रेम्णाऽश्मरीरुगवधेर्मधुकोषबन्धः॥ १ ॥ १ ॥ श्रीकण्ठद्तभिषजा गुरुभक्तिलेशादारभ्यते प्रभृति संप्रति मेहरोगात्॥ सूक्तीर्विचिन्त्य मधुशीकरमुद्गिरन्तीष्टीकाकृतः कतिपयस्य तदीयशेषः ॥ २ ॥ अश्मीरीरोगानन्तरं बस्तिविकृतिसाम्यात्रमेहनिदानमुच्यते—आस्यासुखमित्यादि। आस्या उपविष्टस्य चेष्टोपरमः, तेन कृतं सुखमास्यासुखम्, एवं स्वप्नसुखमिति द्रष्टव्यम्। तेनासनादिदोषादास्यादुःखं स्वप्नदुःख वा न प्रमेहहेतुः । गुडवैकृतमिति गुडविकाराः शर्करादयस्तथा गुडकृताश्च भक्ष्याः । प्रमेहहेतुः कफकृच्य सर्वमित्यनुक्त- हेतुसंग्रहार्थमुक्तम्। एष साधारणो हेतुः प्रमेहस्यः, विशेषहेतुस्तु चरके निदानस्थाने,-‘हायनकोद्दालक’—इत्यादिना कफजस्य, ‘उष्णाम्ललवण’—इत्यादिना पित्तजस्य, ‘कटुतिक्तकषाय’ (च. नि. ,अ. ४) इत्यादिना वातस्याभि- हितः। एतेन सामान्यहेतुसहितो विशिष्टहेतुः कफजादि प्रमेहस्य। किंच कफजानिदानप्येतदास्यासुखादि- बोद्धव्यम्॥ १.॥ मेदश्च मांसं च शरीरजं च क्लेदं कफो बस्तिगतः प्रदूष्य। करोति मेहान् समुदीर्णमुष्णैस्तानेव पित्तं परिदूष्य चापि॥ २॥ क्षीणेषु दोषेष्ववकृष्य धातून् संदूष्य मेहान् कुरुतेजनिलश्च। साध्याः कफोत्था दश, पित्तजाःषड् याप्या, न साध्यः पवनाच्चतुष्कः॥ समक्रियत्वाद्विषमक्रियत्वान्महात्ययत्वाच्च यथाक्रमं ते॥ ३॥ ( च. चि. ६ )
answer_text: Madhukosa: The Guru Vijayaraksita who has bright fame has built the honeycomb like commentary upto the disease Aśmanī. Thē disciple. Srikanṭhadatta has taken up the task of completing the work from meha rogas, supported by reverance to his guru. After expounding on urinary calculus, the prameha, (turbid and excessive urination) is being detailed since there is similarity in terms of the locus standi of the diseases i.e the bladder. 'Pleasure derived out of doing nothing while sitting is Asyasukham. Pleasure of sleep is also to be understood in the same manner. This means that sitting with difficulty or sleeping with difficulty are not considered as aeteological factors of prameha. With out specification, all that increases kapha has been given as common reason for this disease. The specific reason is given in Caraka nidāna - hāyanaka, uddālaka etc. for kapha type of prameha; where sour and salty foods for pitta type and kaṭu, tikia and kaṣāya tasted foods for vātaja prameha. (Ca. Ni. 4). Thus it is implied that the common and specific aeteological factors casue prameha of kaphaja type etc., or else, it can be understood that the Asya sukham etc. should be taken as factors causing kaphaja prameha. Atanka darpana - Curds means curds of any source. Gramya means meat of animals like sheep etc. Audaka means - fish, tortoises etc. Anūpa means flesh of swan, duck, Cakrāvāka etc. Pānāni means - water of fresh rain. Pathogenesis of prameha Medas (fat), māṃsa (muscle tissue) and the wetness of the body are vitiated by the kapha situated in the urinary bladder and cause urinary flux. (This is in the case of kaphaja prameha). The same factors when vitiated by aggravated pitta due to foods and drugs of hot nature, pittaja prameha is resulted. In depleted state of dosa and etc., vāta again brings down the tissues to the bladder and causes vātaja prameha. But of these, ten caused by kapha are curable due to samakriyatva (i.e the treatment to the aggravated kapha and vitiated factors is common) while the six caused by pitta are only manageable because of visama kriyatva (i.e the treatment of aggravated pitta further vitiates the vitiated factor and hence it is not congenial to Prameha-Prameha Pidakā Nidāna body) and the four caused by vāta are incurable due to the acuteness in the manifestation. 2, 3. (Ca. Ci. 6)

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 69):

मधुकोशः अर्जुनलक्षणमाह-एक इत्यादि। एक एव सन् यः शशरुधिरवल्लेहितोबिन्दुरूपश्च विकारस्तमर्जुनं वदन्तीत्यर्थः । उक्तं च कल्याणविनिश्चये-‘शक्रगोपनिभं शुक्लेऽर्जुनं रक्तपकोपतः’ इति। एतेन बिन्दुरूपत्वे नियमो नास्तीति ज्ञेयम्। अत एव रविगुसे-'कृष्णेभागे सितं बिन्दु शुक्ल विद्यात्कफात्मकम्। रक्त च शुक्लभागस्थमर्जुन शोणितोद्धवम्॥’ इति॥ ६७॥ श्लेष्ममारुतकोपेन शुक्ले पिष्ट समुन्नतम्। पिष्टवत् पिष्टकं विद्धि मलाक्तादर्शसन्निभम्॥ ६८॥ मधुकोशः पिष्टकलक्षणमाह-श्लेष्ममारुतकोपेनेत्यादि। पिष्टमिति लक्षणपदम्। पिष्टवदिति आलेपनपिष्टतुल्यं श्रेतत्वेन। पिष्टकमिति लक्ष्यपदम्। समुत्रतमुच्छूनम्। मलाक्तादर्शसन्निभमिति धूल्यादिम्रक्षितदर्पणतुल्यम्। अयं पुनः कफवातजः, अतः कफेनाच्छतया, वातेन किंचिच्छ्यावतया मलाक्तदर्पणनिभत्वमस्येत्यर्थः ॥ ६८ ॥ जालाभः कठिनसिरो महान् सरक्तः संतानः स्मृत इह जालसंज्ञितस्तु। मधुकोशः सिराजाललक्षणमाह-जालाभ इत्यादि । अनुलोमविलोमसिरानिचयरचित निरन्तरविवरगवाक्षीभावात् जालस्येव आभा आकृतिर्यस्य स तथा। कठिनसिर इत्येनन सिराणामेव संतानोऽयं विकार इति दर्शयति। सरक्त ईषल्रोहितः। संतनेति आछादयतीति संतानः, बहुलवचनात् कर्तरि घञ्। अत्र बिन्दुशब्दोऽनुवर्तनीयः, स सर्वत्र विशेष्यः। जालसंज्ञित इत्यत्र ‘सिरापूर्व’ इति शेषः, तेन सिराजालसंज्ञित इत्यर्थंः। अयं च रक्तजः॥ शुक्लस्थाः सितपिडकाः सिरावृता यास्ता ब्रूयादसितसमीपजाः सिराजाः ॥ मधुकोशः सिराजापिडकालक्षणमाह-शुक्लस्था इत्यादि। सितपिडका इति सितवर्णाः पिडकाः। सिरावृताः सिराव्याप्ताः । असितसमीपजा इति कृष्णभागाभ्यर्णशुक्लज़ाः । सिरापरिवृतत्वात्सिराजाः, नतु साक्षात्सिराजाता इति गदाधरः । अयं च त्रिदोषजः, त्रिदोषजसाध्यप्रकरणे सुश्रुतेन पठितत्वात् ॥ कांस्याभोऽमूदुरथ वारिबिन्दुकल्पो विज्ञेयो नयनसिते बलाससंज्ञः ॥ ६९ ॥ ( सु.उ. ४) मधुकोशः बलासप्रधितलक्षणमाह-कांस्याभ इत्यादि। कांस्यस्येवाभा दीप्तिर्यस्य स तथा सित इत्यर्थः, वारिबिन्दुरिवोच्छूनत्वात्। अमृदुः कठिनः, कफानिलजत्वात्। तथा च विदेहः-‘मारुतोत्पीडितः श्लेष्मा शुक्लभागे व्यवस्थितः । जलबिन्दुरिवोच्छूनो ह्यमृदुः कफसम्भवः ॥ बलासग्रथितं नाम तं शोथं वृत्तमादिशेत् ।’ इति । (‘कोषाभ’) इति कश्चित् पठति, कोषो मांसकुङ्मलं तदाभस्तदाकारः; एवावताऽत्यर्थमुच्छूनत्वं प्रतिपाद्यते। वारिबिन्दुकल्प इति चेषदुच्छूनताऽपि, नयनसिते शुक्लेभागे इत्यर्थः। बलाससंज्ञ इत्यत्र ग्रथितशब्दलोपः, तेन बलासग्रथित इति संज्ञा। अत्र सिरोत्पातसिराहर्षौं वाग्भटेन पठितौं। तथा हि-‘रक्तराजीनिभं शुक्ले उष्यतेऽपि सवेदनम्। अशोधाश्रूपदेहं च शिरोत्पातः सशोणितम्॥ उपेक्षितः सिरोत्पातो राजीस्ता एव वर्धयन्। कुर्यात् सास्त्रं सिराहर्षं तेनाक्ष्युद्वीक्षणाक्षमम्॥’ (वा.उ. १०) इति॥ ६९॥
answer_text: The substance is that - the only singular spot that is of red colour-like the blood of a rabbit is called arjuna. It is mentioned in Kalyana viniscaya, “Due to aggravation of blood there will be discolouration in the Śuklamanḍala” which is called arjuna. By this explanation, the spot like appearance is not a pre-condition (to call this as arjuna). That is why in Ravigupta, "The white spot in the kṛṣṇamaṇḍala” is known as śukla caused by kapha and the red coloured spot in śukla mandala which is caused by rakta is called arjuna. 67. Piṣṭaka (Pinguncula) A paste like thick coating in the śuklamaṇḍala caused by śleṣma and vāta is called pistaka. It is so styled because the coating looks like paste similar to a mirror afflicted by dust. 68. Netra Roga Nidāna Pista-paste is adjective, since it looks as if a paste is applied on the śuklamaṇḍala; piṣtaka paste here, is the name of the disease; samunnata swollen up. Malāklādarśa sannibhaṃ means - like a mirror covered by dust. This is caused by kaphaύāta. The coating is whitish due to kapha and slightly bluish due to vāta. 68 Sirājāla (Circumcilliary Congestion) A layer that looks like net fabricated by hardened veins, big in size and red in colour - is called jāla (sirājāla). (Su.u.4) A cris-cross fabrication with sieve like appearance of veins is compared to a net. By saying, Kaṭhina sirā - hardened veins, it is shown that this is a layer formed by siras. Sarakia means - slightly reddish. Santana is a layer - that which covers is termed as Santāna. Jāla implies sirājāla. This is a condition caused by rakta. Sirājapiḍakā (Scleritis) The white vesicles encircled by veins existing in the white part (śuklamaṇḍala) near the kṛṣṇamaṇadala are known as Sirāja piḍakā. (Su.u.4). Sitapidakah - white coloured vesicles. Siravriah - occupied by veins. Asitasamipaja - born in the white part near the black part. Since these are encircled by Sira (veins) the name Siraja is given and not that they are from the Sira, according to Gadadhara. This is a Tridosa disease as described in the chapter of curable tridosa diseases. Mādhavanidānaṃ Balāṣagrathita (Episcleritis) A water-drop like formation hard in nature and bronze coloured on the white part of the eye is termed as balāsagrathita. 69. (Su.u.4) Kamsyabha- like bronze - means in the glistening whitish colour of bronze, because it is swollen like a drop of water. Amrdu means hard-due to the predominence of kapha and Vāta. Also, Videha says, “śleṣmā that is dried up by vāta takes shelter on the Suklamandala looks as a drop of water, round, hard and swol¬ len. This is caused by kapha. This swelling is called Balasagrathita." Some read koşābha in the place of kāmsyābha which means bullae of muscle and indicates more inflammation. Water-drop-like appearance indicates more inflammation of a lesser grade. Nayana site - in the white part of the eye. In the stanza only balāsa is used but should be understood as bālāsa grathita. In this connection, Sirotpata and Siraharsa are given by vagbhata “The red stripe like formation on the white part with burning sensation and pain; there will be no swelling and the eye is afflicted by tears - this condition is called Siraharsa where there is further aggravation of rakta resulting in loss of vision". 69. (Vā.u.10)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 69.
context: मधुकोशः अर्जुनलक्षणमाह-एक इत्यादि। एक एव सन् यः शशरुधिरवल्लेहितोबिन्दुरूपश्च विकारस्तमर्जुनं वदन्तीत्यर्थः । उक्तं च कल्याणविनिश्चये-‘शक्रगोपनिभं शुक्लेऽर्जुनं रक्तपकोपतः’ इति। एतेन बिन्दुरूपत्वे नियमो नास्तीति ज्ञेयम्। अत एव रविगुसे-'कृष्णेभागे सितं बिन्दु शुक्ल विद्यात्कफात्मकम्। रक्त च शुक्लभागस्थमर्जुन शोणितोद्धवम्॥’ इति॥ ६७॥ श्लेष्ममारुतकोपेन शुक्ले पिष्ट समुन्नतम्। पिष्टवत् पिष्टकं विद्धि मलाक्तादर्शसन्निभम्॥ ६८॥ मधुकोशः पिष्टकलक्षणमाह-श्लेष्ममारुतकोपेनेत्यादि। पिष्टमिति लक्षणपदम्। पिष्टवदिति आलेपनपिष्टतुल्यं श्रेतत्वेन। पिष्टकमिति लक्ष्यपदम्। समुत्रतमुच्छूनम्। मलाक्तादर्शसन्निभमिति धूल्यादिम्रक्षितदर्पणतुल्यम्। अयं पुनः कफवातजः, अतः कफेनाच्छतया, वातेन किंचिच्छ्यावतया मलाक्तदर्पणनिभत्वमस्येत्यर्थः ॥ ६८ ॥ जालाभः कठिनसिरो महान् सरक्तः संतानः स्मृत इह जालसंज्ञितस्तु। मधुकोशः सिराजाललक्षणमाह-जालाभ इत्यादि । अनुलोमविलोमसिरानिचयरचित निरन्तरविवरगवाक्षीभावात् जालस्येव आभा आकृतिर्यस्य स तथा। कठिनसिर इत्येनन सिराणामेव संतानोऽयं विकार इति दर्शयति। सरक्त ईषल्रोहितः। संतनेति आछादयतीति संतानः, बहुलवचनात् कर्तरि घञ्। अत्र बिन्दुशब्दोऽनुवर्तनीयः, स सर्वत्र विशेष्यः। जालसंज्ञित इत्यत्र ‘सिरापूर्व’ इति शेषः, तेन सिराजालसंज्ञित इत्यर्थंः। अयं च रक्तजः॥ शुक्लस्थाः सितपिडकाः सिरावृता यास्ता ब्रूयादसितसमीपजाः सिराजाः ॥ मधुकोशः सिराजापिडकालक्षणमाह-शुक्लस्था इत्यादि। सितपिडका इति सितवर्णाः पिडकाः। सिरावृताः सिराव्याप्ताः । असितसमीपजा इति कृष्णभागाभ्यर्णशुक्लज़ाः । सिरापरिवृतत्वात्सिराजाः, नतु साक्षात्सिराजाता इति गदाधरः । अयं च त्रिदोषजः, त्रिदोषजसाध्यप्रकरणे सुश्रुतेन पठितत्वात् ॥ कांस्याभोऽमूदुरथ वारिबिन्दुकल्पो विज्ञेयो नयनसिते बलाससंज्ञः ॥ ६९ ॥ ( सु.उ. ४) मधुकोशः बलासप्रधितलक्षणमाह-कांस्याभ इत्यादि। कांस्यस्येवाभा दीप्तिर्यस्य स तथा सित इत्यर्थः, वारिबिन्दुरिवोच्छूनत्वात्। अमृदुः कठिनः, कफानिलजत्वात्। तथा च विदेहः-‘मारुतोत्पीडितः श्लेष्मा शुक्लभागे व्यवस्थितः । जलबिन्दुरिवोच्छूनो ह्यमृदुः कफसम्भवः ॥ बलासग्रथितं नाम तं शोथं वृत्तमादिशेत् ।’ इति । (‘कोषाभ’) इति कश्चित् पठति, कोषो मांसकुङ्मलं तदाभस्तदाकारः; एवावताऽत्यर्थमुच्छूनत्वं प्रतिपाद्यते। वारिबिन्दुकल्प इति चेषदुच्छूनताऽपि, नयनसिते शुक्लेभागे इत्यर्थः। बलाससंज्ञ इत्यत्र ग्रथितशब्दलोपः, तेन बलासग्रथित इति संज्ञा। अत्र सिरोत्पातसिराहर्षौं वाग्भटेन पठितौं। तथा हि-‘रक्तराजीनिभं शुक्ले उष्यतेऽपि सवेदनम्। अशोधाश्रूपदेहं च शिरोत्पातः सशोणितम्॥ उपेक्षितः सिरोत्पातो राजीस्ता एव वर्धयन्। कुर्यात् सास्त्रं सिराहर्षं तेनाक्ष्युद्वीक्षणाक्षमम्॥’ (वा.उ. १०) इति॥ ६९॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2):

कालेऽपि दोपविशेषस्य लक्षणमित्याहकाल इत्यादि । यथास्वं काले यस्य वातादेयः प्रकोपकालस्तत्र तज्जन्यज्वरस्य प्रवृत्तिरत्पादो वद्धिर्वा भवति अथवा प्रवृत्तिनित्यज्वरस्य वृद्धिर्विपमज्वरस्येति ॥ विपरीतोपशायिता ॥ ॥ निदानोक्तानुपशयो यथा कालो दोषविशेषस्य लक्षणं तथोपशयानुपशयावपि लक्षणमित्याहनिदाने- त्यादि । निदानत्वेन ये उक्ता आहाराचारादयस्तौरनुपशयो दुःखं निदानोक्तानुपशयः । विपरीतै- र्दोषादिविपरीताहाराचारैरुपशायिता सुखजननशोलत्वं विपरीतोपशायितेति श्वसनंत्र भ्रमः अन्तर्दाहोऽधिकस्तृष्णा प्रलापः दोष-वर्चोविनिग्रहः ॥ ॥ सन्ध्यस्थिशूलमस्वेदो अन्तर्वेगस्य लिङ्गानि ज्वरस्यैतानि लक्षयेत् । सन्तापो ह्यधिको बाह्यस्तृष्णादीनां च मार्दवम् ॥॥ बहिर्वेगस्य लिङ्गानि सुखसाध्यत्वमेव च । - - - -
answer_text: This passage has been presented here to stress that the fever induced by different dosas appear only during the period of aggravation of vata, etc. as suggested by the classical texts. It has been suggested that the timing of the vitiation of dosas is well defined in terms of its relation to the vāta, pitta and kapha. In details, it may be noted that the vāta doṣa gets vitiated during the rainy scason. The pitta doṣa is vitiated during the winter season. Likewise, the kapha doşa is naturally vitiated during the spring season. On a shorter term, it is considered that the kapha dosa gets provoked during the morning hours and during the early hours of night and at the time of taking foods. It also remains powerful during the childhood. Likewise, the pitta doşa gets provoked during the afternoon hours and during the middle of the night and at the time of digesting the foods. It also remains powerful during the youthful ages. The vata dosa gets provoked during the late hours of the day as well as the night and after the foods taken are digested. It also remains powerful during the old ages. The above pattern has been suggested through the passage beginning from the term kāle etc. The passage starting from the pravṛtirvṛddhireva vā lays stress on the theory that if a vāta fever has started in the summer it may turn powerful during the rainy season. Similarly, the kaphaja and pittaja fevers could turn powerful in the seasons when they are naturally strengthened. This format of becoming powerful or turning weak alternatively is applicable on short-term basis as well as described above. In that case, the age of patient, the time of day and status of the food digestion are of significant import. (AH, Ni. 2.23.2), Similarly, such factors that tend to promote the particular dosa also bring about increase of fever, whereas the opposites of it actuate the fever. 58 This passage is meant to narrate the significance of the upasaya and amupšaya in terms of diagnostics. As the factors like kala have a significant impact on the various dosas the upasaya and anupsaya also play significant role in addressing the diseases. The passage quoted by Mādhavakara refers to the anupśaya that has been mentioned in the case of effects of the unjustitied intake of meals, etc. and opting irregular and harmful regimen and activities. In brief, it could be understood that the use of the food and regimen that provoke vāta and other dosas are bound to produce troubles while the use of the food and regimen that actuate the dosas ever generate happiness. This measure is called upasaya. (The same topic has been detailed above in the treatment of the five limbs of Nidāna incıuding upaśaya and anupśaya). Internal and external fevers (CS. Ci. 3.3.39/2, 40, 41) Fever is considered antarvega when manifesting inside the body predominantly it demonstrate the following features: feeling of burning sensation inside, too much of thirst, delirium, difficult respiration, giddiness, pain in the joints and bones, absence of perspiration and non-elimination of dosas and faeces. On the other hand, when the fever is manifesting with very high temperature externally, but thirst and other features are mild, this situation is considered bahirvega (residing and manifesting externally). This situation is easy to cure. 59-60

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2):

आगन्तुज्वरेष्वपि प्रतिनियतदोषानबन्धदर्शनार्थमाह कामशोकेत्यादि । त्रयो मला भूताभिषज्ञात् कुप्यन्तीति भूतप्रभावात् । यच्च चरकेण निदानस्थाने अभिषज्ञजः पुनर्वातपित्ताध्यो च०नि० इत्युक्त तत् प्रायिकं मन्तव्यमिति जेज्जटः चक्र- स्त्वाहअभिषङ्गज इत्यनेन कामाद्यभिषङ्गज उच्यते न तु भूताभिषङ्गजः । इति । भूत- सामान्यलक्षणा इति यस्य भूतस्य देवग्रहादेरभिषङ्गात् कुप्यन्ति तस्य यल्लक्षणं रोदनादि तेन सह सामान्य लक्षणं येषां ते तथा इति व्याचक्षते जेज्जटादयः दोषलक्षणानि भूतलक्षणानि च भवन्तीत्यर्थः दोषोऽल्पोऽहितसम्भूतो । ज्वरोत्सृष्टस्य पवा । पुनः ॥३१॥ करोति पर विषमज्वरम् । धातुमन्यतमं का प्राप्य --
answer_text: This passage is meant to distinguish the various types of fever within the category of āgantuja fever. It has been accepted that the instrumentality of the bhūtas (malevolent celestial elements) in producing fever is reflected through vitiation of all the three doşas. Caraka has categorically stated in Nidāna Sthāna that Bhūta-afflic- tion aggravates vāta and pitta (CS. Ni. 1.23). This statement has been accepted in general according to the commentator Jejjaṭa. Cakrapāṇi, in this context, however, suggests that the affliction produced by abhişanga etc. relates to such mental indisposition as unfulfilled lust and not to any malevolent celestial elements. Commentator Jejjata has opined that apart from the symptoms of vitiated dosas there is also other symptoms (like weeping) of the affliction of bhūtas. Onset of vişama jvara (irregular fever) (SS. Ut. 39. 66) The doşas that have undergone only a slight increase due to unsuitable eatables and activities, get lodged in other tissues (dhātus) and generate vişama jvara that is irregular or intermittent fever. 31
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2.

answer_text: 14 M.N. Pt-II Mādhavanidānaṃ The lips are full of painful vesicles, with burning sensation, ulceration and yellowish discolouration due to pitta - aggravation. The pain in the lips, here - is due to pitta. If so, why is it again mentioned that the vesicles are associated with burning sensation and ulceration, when already the meaning is conveyed? This need not to be taken as repetition. It is mentioned to give another meaning that - some times the lips are full of pain that is caused by pitta and some times they are full of vesicles associated with burning sensation and ulceration. Others opine that since there is no much differentiation and inexplicity in the words (in the first line), and to indicate the extreme burning - sensation and ulceration, the pidakā is repeated here 3. Kapha type of lip-disease Both the lips are full of - skin coloured and painless vesicles due to kapha aggravation. They are sticky, cold and heavy. 4. (Su. Ni. 16)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 56, verse 4.

ज्वरमुक्तिलक्षणमाह स्वेद इत्यादि । स्वेदो घर्मागमनं स्रोतसां स्फुटत्वात् । लघुत्व गात्रस्ये । शिरसः कण्डूरिति सर्वो हि ज्वरस्तेजसः विरोधिव्यपममात् सौम्यः श्लेष्मा लव्यवलः संच्छिरसि स्वस्थानेऽसाधारणात्मलक्षणं कण्डूं करोति व्याधिमहिम्ना नान्यत्र कफस्थाने इति वदन्ति । पार्को मुखस्येति ज्वरोष्मकोपितपित्तात् यत्तु पूर्वी नाकार्पीदन्यत्र वा तदप व्याधिमहिम्नेव । एतच्च दाहमारभ्य लक्षणं द्रिदोषषेऽन्तर्वंगे ज्वरे भवति न तु सर्वत्र । तथा चैतदनन्तरं भालुकिः प्राहत्रिदोषजे ज्वरे ह्येतदन्तवंगि च धातुगे । लक्षणं मोक्षकाल स्यादन्यरिमन् स्वेददर्शनम् ।। इति । नमु ज्वस्य प्रत्यक्षत्वात्तस्याभावोऽपि प्रत्यक्षः तत् कि तल्लक्षणपाठेन तथाऽपि वा पठितव्यं तर्हि सर्वविकारेषु पठ्यताम् उच्यते विषमज्वरशङ्कानिरासार्थं विषमज्वरो निवृत्तोऽपि। पुनरायाति दोषाणां धातुलीनत्वातु एतल्लक्षणे तु निःशेषदोषनिवृत्त्या न पुनरागमः । यत्र चैवंविधा शङ्का तट्रैव लक्षणं पठति न सर्वत्र यथा प्रमेहातीसारादिष्विति सर्वं सुस्थम् ।।७५।। इति श्रीविजयरक्षितकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां ज्वरनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥॥
answer_text: Jvara Nidanam This passage is meant to clarify different symptoms that signify the elimination of fever. The sweating appears due to clarity in the channels. In addition, there is a feeling of lightness in the body. The fever is considered associated with the pitta dosa. As this dosa is actuated, the kapha doşa that is antagonistic to the pitta turns strong and it causes itching sensation on the head, which is the specific effect of this disease, and not that kapha situated in the head. In the morbidity, there appears the symptom of mukhapāka because of the heat of pilla that remains prominent in all types of fever. Still there is no such symptom in the fever in context. This could be the unique feature of the disease. As regards the symptoms like burning sensation, it appears only in the antarvega or gambhīra type of sannipata and not in all types of fevers. Bhaluki has also stated that during the subsidence of the sannipāta, antarvega and dhātugata types of fever there is burning sensation while in other types of fever there is sweating during their subsidence. One could argue that the onset as well as the relief from fever is apparent then why the features of its relief have been presented here; then there should also be presentation of relief from all the diseases. To address the above objection one could submit that the relief from fever has been detailed here in order to remove confusion regarding the appearance of Visama Jvara. The lack of temperature does not mean relief of fever because the dosa may remain in some tissue and there is a chance of relapse as it happens in Visama Jvara. Nevertheless, the above are the features of complete relief from dosas (Nissesadosa) and their complete removal from the body. Such picture is given in Jvara, Atisära, Prameha and not everywhere, as there could be no chance of relapse in cases of other diseases. Thus concludes the Chapter on Jvaras
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2.

Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Puspa Varga, Chapter 4, verse 527):

answer_text: Digestive disease: The fruits are useful in Atisarā (Diarrhoea) etc. gastric diseases. Urinary disease: Root decoction is administered for treatment of Mūtrakṛcchra (Dysuria). JAPĀPUSPAM Latin: Hibiscus rosasinensis Linn. Fam: Malvaceae. Hin: Jasut. Eng: China rose. Oḍhra puṣpam is know as Japā. Both red and white flowers varieties is know as Trisandhyā. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Japā is Grāhī (Absorbent), Keṣya (Good for hairs) and Trisandhyā cures diseases of Vāta, Pitta and Laghu (Light for digestion). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is commonly grown as garden plant. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a large shrub or small tree grows upto 15ft high. Leaves simple, ovate, alternately arranged, bright green with serrated margins. Flowers solitary, red in colour, axillary, bell shaped, 10-15cm, in diameter. Fruits are capsule, rounded contains many seeds. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Puṣpā (Flowers), Mūlatwak (Root bark). Chemical constituents: Flower mainly contains anthocyanins and flavonoids
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Puspa Varga, Chapter 4, verse 527
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Puspa Varga, Chapter 4, verse 527.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 22):

अधः प्रतिहतो वायुः श्लेष्मणा मारुतेन वा । करोत्युद्गारबाहल्यमूर्ध्ववातः का समाच उच्यते ॥ ॥ खल्लीत्यादि । खल्ली सिरावमोट्टन इति लोके । अधः प्रतिहतो वायुः श्लेष्मणा मारुतेन च । करोत्युद्वारबाहुल्यमूर्ध्ववातं प्रचक्षते ।। इत्यत्राधिकं केचित् पठन्ति ।।।। स्थाननामानुरूपैश्च लिङ्गैः शेषान् विनिर्दिशेत् । सर्वेप्वेतेपुर - ि संसर्ग पित्ताद्येरुपलक्ष्येत् ॥७ ॥ हनुस्तम्भार्दिताक्षेप-पक्षाघातापतानकाः कालेन महता वाता यत्नात् सिध्यन्ति वातान वा ॥॥ बलवतस्त्वेतान् साधयेन्निरुपद्रवान् । नरान् अनुक्तवातरोगसङ्ग्रहार्थमाहस्थानेत्यादि । नखभेद इत्यादि । नामानुरूपैर्लिङ्गैर्यथा शूलमित्युक्ते कीलनिखातवट्टेदनाविशेष एव बोध्यते तथा भेदतोदादिभिरपि पीडाविशेष एव गम्यते । वाता इति वातविकाराः कार्यकारणयोर- भेदोपचारात् । वातादिति पाठे तु वाताद्ये पक्षवधादय इति योज्यम् ।।।। विसर्प-दाह-रुक्सङ्ग-मूर्च्छारुच्यग्निमार्दवैः क्षीणमांसबलं वाता घ्नन्ति पक्षवधादयः । कम्पाध्माननिपीडितम् । सुप्तत्वचं भग्नं वातव्याधिर्विनाशयेत् रुजार्तिमन्तंत का चाहत नरंग का - - - - - - - - -
answer_text: The vata being obstructed in its downward movement either by kapha or by itself begins to move upwards and generates severe belching. This condition has been identified as ūrdhvavāta. 75 The above passage starting from the term khallī etc., presents the symptoms of the different varieties of khallī. In the common lan¬ guage, the term siramotana is used for this disease. The term motana refers to the act of press-squeezing. In addition, as the wet piece of cloths is press-squeezed the vitiated vāyu sqeezes different veins in this disease. The term pracakṣate has been also read as ucyate. How- ever, the meaning of both the terms is identical. As noted by Brahmanand Tripathi, the term motanī has been used to denote the shifting nature of the disease by the text Atankadarpana. In fact, the patient of khalli feels that his veins are shifting from one place to another. Knowing the remaining vata disorders (CS. Ci. S. 28.58) Features of the varieties of vata related diseases (vyadhis) that has not been discussed above are to be diagnosed considering their site of affliction and name, as well as their association with vata, pitta and other dosas. 76 Curability and incurability of certain vāta-disorders (CS. Ci. S. 28.74) Lock jaw (hanustambha), facial paralysis (ardita), convulsive disor- ders (ākṣepaka), hemiplegia (pakṣāghāta) and apatānaka (tetanus?) and other vātika diseases may be managed only after a careful man¬ agement. Even then, they may not be cured. Hence, patients with good general condition and no complications should only be taken up by the wise physicians. 77 The above passage starting from the term sthāna, etc. indicates the other type of vāta diseases that might have been left un-described through the above narratives. In this context, the nomenclature of different diseases and the specific terminology employed may help to have an idea of the ailment as indicated by the term namanu- rūpairlingayathā. The terms like kukṣiśūla and nakhabheda are self- explanatory indeed. Likewise, the term vatadi refers to various vata disorders like hemiplegia, etc. Upadrava (complications) of vāta disorders 117 8 117 8 11 The vata disorders such as paksavadha could turn fatal if the patient also develops such symptoms as visarpa (erysipelas), burning sensation, severe pain, non-elimination of flatus, faeces, urine and the like, fainting, anorexia, poor digestive capacity, wasting of muscles and loss of strength. 78 (SS. Sü. 33.7) Swetling of the body, loss of tactile sensation, fractures of joints, tremors, flatulence, or severe pain found in valavyadhis are also to be considered as fatal conditions. 79

context: अधः प्रतिहतो वायुः श्लेष्मणा मारुतेन वा । करोत्युद्गारबाहल्यमूर्ध्ववातः का समाच उच्यते ॥ ॥ खल्लीत्यादि । खल्ली सिरावमोट्टन इति लोके । अधः प्रतिहतो वायुः श्लेष्मणा मारुतेन च । करोत्युद्वारबाहुल्यमूर्ध्ववातं प्रचक्षते ।। इत्यत्राधिकं केचित् पठन्ति ।।।। स्थाननामानुरूपैश्च लिङ्गैः शेषान् विनिर्दिशेत् । सर्वेप्वेतेपुर - ि संसर्ग पित्ताद्येरुपलक्ष्येत् ॥७ ॥ हनुस्तम्भार्दिताक्षेप-पक्षाघातापतानकाः कालेन महता वाता यत्नात् सिध्यन्ति वातान वा ॥॥ बलवतस्त्वेतान् साधयेन्निरुपद्रवान् । नरान् अनुक्तवातरोगसङ्ग्रहार्थमाहस्थानेत्यादि । नखभेद इत्यादि । नामानुरूपैर्लिङ्गैर्यथा शूलमित्युक्ते कीलनिखातवट्टेदनाविशेष एव बोध्यते तथा भेदतोदादिभिरपि पीडाविशेष एव गम्यते । वाता इति वातविकाराः कार्यकारणयोर- भेदोपचारात् । वातादिति पाठे तु वाताद्ये पक्षवधादय इति योज्यम् ।।।। विसर्प-दाह-रुक्सङ्ग-मूर्च्छारुच्यग्निमार्दवैः क्षीणमांसबलं वाता घ्नन्ति पक्षवधादयः । कम्पाध्माननिपीडितम् । सुप्तत्वचं भग्नं वातव्याधिर्विनाशयेत् रुजार्तिमन्तंत का चाहत नरंग का - - - - - - - - -

Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 481):

विज्ञेया नागदमनी बलामोटा विषापहा । नागपुष्पी नागपत्रा महायोगेश्वरीति च ।।२९९।। बलामोटा कटुस्तिक्ता लघुः पित्तकफापहा । मूत्रकृच्छुव्नणान् रक्षो नाशयेज्जालगर्दभम् ।।३००।। सर्व्रग्रहप्रशमनी निःशेषविषनाशिनी । जयं सर्वत्र कुरुते धनदायुर्मतिप्रदा ।।३०१।।
answer_text: Respiratory diseases: A decoction is used in the treatment of Pīnasa (Common cold), lung, thoat and other chest infections. External uses: The leaf powder or Ash applied external over Mūkhapāka (Stomatitis). The leaf powder is dusted over Vṛṇa (Wounds). Mātrā (Dosage): Swarasa: 10-20ml, Cūrṇa: 1-3gms. NĀGADAMANĪ Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Balāmōṭā, Viṣāpahā, Nāgapuṣpī, Nāgapaṭrā and Mahāyogeśvarī. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Nāgadamanī is Kaṭu (Pungent) and Tikta (Bitter) in taste, Lagu (Light for digestion), cures diseases of Pitta and Kapha, Mūtrakrcchra Dysuria), Vrna (Wounds), Rakṣhonāśa (Evil sprits), Jālagardabha (Glandular swellings), Grahabādhā (Avoids away associated evils), Eradicates Posionous manifestations and brings success, welth and intelligence. Note: The correct source plant has not been identified. As per Balvantsinghji it can taken as Pupalia lappaceae Moq
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 481
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 481.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 69, verse 29):

मधुकोशः तेन स्थानविशेषेण विशिष्टलिङ्गमाह-आमाशयस्थ इत्यादि। कफावृतत्वेन वातकोप आमशये, कफवातरोगीत्युक्तम्। अनिलपित्तरोगीति पक्राशये दुष्टवातसंबन्धेन प्रत्यासन्नस्याशयस्थस्य पित्तस्य कोपः। भवेत् समुद्धवस्तशिरोरुहाङ्गः इति अत्राङ्गशब्दात् परं रुहशब्दो द्रष्टव्यः, तेनायमर्थः-समुद्धवस्तशिरोरुहाङ्गः, शिरोरुहा केशाः, अड़रुंह लोम, तदुक्तमालम्बायने-सीदन्ति केशलोमानि तस्मिन् पक्रवाशयं गते’ इत्यादि। विलूनपक्षस्तु यथा विहङ्ग इति मुण्डितपक्षशकुनिसदृशः, एतत् पक्वाशयगतस्यैव लिङ्गम्॥ २८॥ स्थितं रसादिष्वथवा यथोक्तान् करोति धातुप्रभवान् विकारान्। कोपं च शीतानिलदुर्दिनेषु यात्याशु, पूर्व शृणु तस्य रूपम्॥ २९॥ ( सु.क. २ )
answer_text: 24 M.N. Pt-II Mādhavanidānaṃ In the āmāśaya, vāta aggravates due to covering of kapha by which kaphavāta diseases occur. In the pakvāśaya due to contact of aggravated vāta, the pitta which is in near vicinity also gets aggravated and hence there arise vāta-pitta disorders. The word ruha is to be applied to Sira (head) and anga (body) which means-hair on the head and that on the body. In Alambāyana it is said, “ The hair on head and body fall off when the dūṣīviṣa is seated in pakvāśaya”. Vilūnapakṣastu yathā vihaṅga”. means like a bird that is removed off its quills. This is the symptom found in the case when Dūṣivisa takes shelter in the pakvāśaya. 28. The symptomatology when the dūṣīviṣa is seated in the dhātus When Dūṣīvisa gets seated in dhātus (Rasa etc.), it causes symptoms-aversion to food, anorexia etc., (mentioned by Susruta in Su. Su. Na) There will be aggravation on exposure to cold winds and on a cloudy day. The premonitary symptoms are being explained further. 29. (Su.ka.2)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 69, verse 29.
context: मधुकोशः तेन स्थानविशेषेण विशिष्टलिङ्गमाह-आमाशयस्थ इत्यादि। कफावृतत्वेन वातकोप आमशये, कफवातरोगीत्युक्तम्। अनिलपित्तरोगीति पक्राशये दुष्टवातसंबन्धेन प्रत्यासन्नस्याशयस्थस्य पित्तस्य कोपः। भवेत् समुद्धवस्तशिरोरुहाङ्गः इति अत्राङ्गशब्दात् परं रुहशब्दो द्रष्टव्यः, तेनायमर्थः-समुद्धवस्तशिरोरुहाङ्गः, शिरोरुहा केशाः, अड़रुंह लोम, तदुक्तमालम्बायने-सीदन्ति केशलोमानि तस्मिन् पक्रवाशयं गते’ इत्यादि। विलूनपक्षस्तु यथा विहङ्ग इति मुण्डितपक्षशकुनिसदृशः, एतत् पक्वाशयगतस्यैव लिङ्गम्॥ २८॥ स्थितं रसादिष्वथवा यथोक्तान् करोति धातुप्रभवान् विकारान्। कोपं च शीतानिलदुर्दिनेषु यात्याशु, पूर्व शृणु तस्य रूपम्॥ २९॥ ( सु.क. २ )

Its Fruits subsides Kapha- Vāta doṣa, cures Prameha (Diabeties), Arśas (Piles), Krmi (Worm infestations) and Kuşta (Leprosy). The properties of both Karañja and Ghṛta karañja are similar. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is grown throughout India. Swarūpa (Botanical description): A medium sized tree which attains the height of about 50–60 ft. It has a straight or crooked trunk with smooth grey-brown coloured, vertically fissured bark. Leaves are compound imparipinnate of the three, 20-35cm long, ovate or oblong, accuminate apex, rounded or cuneate at the base, even margins, alternately arranged and short-stalked, Flowers in small clusters of white, purple, and pink arranged in raceme. Fruits pods are thick-walled, flattened and elliptical, contains one or two bean-like brownish-red seeds. The seeds are about 1.5–2.5 cm. round, smooth or wrinkled.
