question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 895):

मूलकं द्विविधं प्रोक्तं तत्रैकं लघुमूलकम् । शालामर्कटकं विस्रं शालेयं मरुसम्भवम् ।।१९।। चाणक्यमूलकं तीक्ष्णं तथा मूलकपोतिका । नेपालमूलकं चान्यत्तद्ववेद्रजदन्तवत् ।।१००।। लघुमूलं कटूष्णं स्याद्वच्यं लघु च पाचनम् । दोषत्रयहरं स्वर्यं ज्वरश्वासविनाशनम् ।।१.०१।। नासिकाकण्ङ्गरोगघ्नं नयनामयनाशनम् ।।१०२ ? । महत्तदेव रूक्षोष्णा गुरु दोषत्रयप्रदम् । स्नेहसिद्धं तदेव स्याद् दोषत्रयविनाशनम् ।।१०३।।
answer_text: Fam: Cruciferae Latin: Raphanus sativus Linn Eng: Radish Hin: Mauli Mūlaka is of two types Laghu mūlaka and Sthūla mūlaka. Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Śālāmarkaṭaka, Visra, Śāleya, Marusambhava, Cāṇakyamūlaka Tīkṣṇā and Mūlakapotikā. The second type which resembles like tooth of elephant is know as Nepala mūlaka. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Laghu mūlaka is Kaṭu (Pungent in taste), Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency), Rucya (Promotes taste), Laghu (Light for digestion), Pācana (Digestive), subsides all Tridoṣas and Swarya (Promotes good voice). It cures Jwara (Fever), Swāsa (Dyspnoea) and Diseases of Nasa (Nose), Kanṭa (Thoat) and Nayana (Netra). Sthūla mūlaka is Rūkṣa (Drying), Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Increases all Tridoşas and if it is fried in oil it subsides Tridoşas. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is cultivated throughout india. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is an erect herb. Leaves are in rosette, radical, lyrate and lobed. Flowers are arranged in racemes white pink or purple. Fruits -Pods, 2.5- 5cm. long, cylindrical, gibbous at base, consist of many round, mustard size seeds. Chemical constituents: Sufloraphene, Sitostreol, Stearic acid, Castasterone, Brassinolide P-Coumaric, Ferulic and Caffeic acids

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 48, verse 5):

मधुकोशः सर्षपिकामाह-गौरेत्यादि। शूकदुर्भुग्नहेतुकेति दुर्भुग्नशूकहेतुकेत्यर्थः। पिडकादिषु उभयवचनमिति ( ? ) परनिपातः। दुर्भुग्नो दुरवचारितः। ‘शूकदुर्भगहेतुका’ इति पाठान्तरे शूकनिमित्ता दुष्टयोनिनिमित्ता चेत्यर्थः॥ २॥ कठिना विषमैर्भग्नैर्वायुनाऽष्ठीलिका भवेत्। मधुकोशः अष्ठीलिकामाह-कठिनेत्यादि । विषमैर्भूग्रैरिति वक्ष्यमाणशूकैरित्यनेन संबध्यते । विषमैरित्यप्रशस्तैः । अष्ठीलिका लोहकारस्य भाण्डीविशेषः, तत्तुल्यत्वादष्ठीलिका। शूकैर्यत् पूरितं शश्वद् ग्रथितं नाम तत् कफात्॥ ३॥ मधुकोशः ग्रथितमाह-शूकैरित्यादि। शूकैर्यत् पूरितं शश्चद्ग्रथितमिति शूकैः सर्वदा पूरितं लिङ्गं यद् ग्रन्थिलं तद् ग्रथितमित्यर्थः, ग्रन्थितुल्यत्वाद् ग्रथितसंज्ञा॥ ३ ॥ कुम्भिका रक्तपित्तोत्था जाम्बवास्थिनिभाऽशुभा। मधुकोशः कुम्भिकामाह-कुम्भिकेत्यादि। कुम्भी कुम्भीडुलता, तस्याः फलं कुम्भी; तद्वितस्य लुक; इवे प्रतिकृतौ इति कन्, कुम्भीफलवत् कुम्भिका। अशुभेति शुभं शुक्लं तद्विरोधे नञ्, कृष्णेत्यर्थः। ‘आशुजा’ इति पाठान्तरम्॥ तुल्यजां त्वलजीं विद्याद्यथाप्रोक्तां विचक्षणः॥ ४॥ मधुकोशः अलजीमाह-तुल्यजामित्यादि। तुल्यजामिति प्रमेहपिडिका अलजी तत्तुल्यसंभवा सा च रक्ताऽसिता। तुल्यत्वमेव विवृणिति-यथाप्रोक्तामिति, अलजी यथा प्रोक्ता यादुशलक्षणा तथेयमपीत्यर्थः। एषा च कारमचिकित्साभेदात् प्रमेहं विना लिङ्ग एव संभवाच्च ततः पृथग्भूता ज़ेया॥ ४॥ मुदितं पीडितं यच्च संरब्धं वातकोपतः । मधुकोशः मृदितमाह-मृदितमित्यादि। पीडितमिति अधिकृतत्वात् शूकपातानन्तरं पीडितमिति अधिकृतत्वात् शूकपातानन्तरं पीडितमिति ज्ञेयं, पीडितं ‘लिङ्गम्’ इति श्ञेषः, संरब्धं सशोथम्। पाणिभ्यां भृशसंमूढे संमूढपिडका भवेत् ॥ ५ ॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 45):

मधुकोशः पित्तजामाह-पित्तादित्यादि। अधिकमुष्णमहःसु चेति दिवा औष्ण्येन पित्तकोपात्॥ ३॥ ज़ेया कफाद्वहघनार्ज़ुनपिच्छिलास्त्रा स्तब्धा सकण्डुररुजा रजनीप्रवृद्धा। मधुकोशः कफजामाह-ज्ञेयेत्यादि। बहुधनार्जुनपिच्छिलास्ट्रेति। अत्राजुनः श्वेतः, घनः सान्द्रः आस्वशब्द आस्ववशब्दैक- देशपाठः, पदेऽपि पदैकदेसप्रयोगात्। यथा ‘जे प्रोष्ठपदानाम्’-इत्यत्र जे इत्यनेनैव जात इत्युच्यते। पिच्छिलास्त्रिति पाठेऽप्ययमेवार्थः। आस्त्रुशब्दः संपदादिषु पाठात् क्रिबन्त्ः; तुगभावस्त्वागमनित्यत्वात्॥ दाहज्वरश्वसनमूर्च्छनवक्त्रशोषा यस्यां भवन्त्यभिहितानि च लक्षणानि॥ ४॥ तामादिशेत्पवनपित्तकफप्रकोपाद्घोरामसुक्षयकरीमिव कालरात्रिम्। मधुकोशः त्रिदोषजामाह- दाहेत्यादि। अभिहितानीति प्रत्येकं वातादिजनाडीकथितानि। असुक्षयकरीमिति मारणात्मिकां, कालरात्रि मरणकारिणीं यमभगिनीमिव । ‘गतिं त्वसुहराम्’ इति पाठान्तरम् ॥ ४॥ नष्ट कथंचिदनुमार्गमुदीरितेषु स्थानेषु शल्यमचिरेण गतिं करोति॥ ५ ॥ सा फेनिलं मथितमुष्णमसृग्विमिश्रं स्त्रावं करोति सहसा सरूजा च नित्यम्। मधुकोशः शल्यनिमित्तामाह- नष्टमित्यादि। नष्टमदृश्यमानमु। कथंचिदित वेगक्षयादिकारणानामनियमार्थमुक्तमु। अनुमार्ग मार्ग लक्ष्मीकृत्य। केचित् ‘अणुमार्गम्’ इति पठित्वा शल्यविशेषणतया योजयन्ति। किंत्वस्मिन् पक्षेऽणुमार्गत्वेनैव शल्यस्यादर्शने प्रयुक्ते कथंचिदिति निरर्थकं स्यात्। उद्दीरितेष्विति त्वगादिषु। फेनिलं फेनवन्तम्। मथितमुन्मथितम्। उष्णमुष्णस्पर्शम्। एते च धर्माः प्रसारणाकुञ्चनादौ चलता शल्येन मांसादिक्षोभेण भवन्ति॥ ५॥ नाडी त्रिदोषप्रभवा न सिध्ये च्छेषाश्चतस्त्रः खलु यलसाध्यः॥ ६॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते मादवनिदाने नाडीव्रणनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ४५॥ मधुकोशः असाध्यत्वादिकमाह–नाडीत्यादि। ननु, नाडी त्रिदोषप्रभवा न सिध्येदिति पुनरुक्त असुक्षयकरीमित्यनेनै– वासाध्यत्वस्योक्तत्वात्। नैवम्, अयं ग्रन्थः सुश्रुतेन निदानस्थानोक्तमेव त्रिदोषनाड्या असाध्यत्वमन्द्य तदन्यासा शेषत्वनिश्चयेन यलसाध्यत्वप्रतिपादनाय चिकित्सिते पठितः, स एवात्र माधवकरेण लिखित इत्यदोषः॥ ६॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तविरचितायां मधुक्रोशव्याख्यायां नाडीव्रणनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ४५ ॥
answer_text: Due to heat in the day time, there will be aggravation of pitta and the exudation is warm and more in that time. Kaphaja type of Nāḍī Vraṇa There will be exudation in kapha type of Nādī vraṇa which is excessive, thick white in colour and sticky in nature. (Su. Ni. 10). Arjuna means white in colour, Ghana is dense, Asra means exudation. Tridosaja type of Nādī Vrana Apart from the individual symptoms of all the three dosas, there will be more burning sensation, fever, dyspnoea, swooning and dryness of the mouth in the Tridosaja type of Nadi vrana which is serious and causes death like a kalaratri (the sister of death-god). (Su. Ni. 10) Abhihitani" those signs and symptoms described in the case of Nada Vranas caused individually by the three dosas. Asuksyakari the one which causes death. Kālarātri is the sister of death god. “Gatim tvasuharāṃ” is another text which means that leads to death. Nādīvraṇa Nidāna Sinus wound caused by the foreign body The foreign body that enters by any means (injury etc., ) into one of the eight locations of vrana (wound) and gets concealed in the place, makes way causing a sinus wound in a short period. There is sudden exudation from such wound mixed with blood, warm and which is like churned curds in consistency and that wound is always associated with pain. 5. (Su. Ni. 10). Naştam means that which is not visible. Kathañchit (by any means) word - is used here to indicate the irregularity in the fluctuation of bout of pain etc. Anumārgaṃ means making - way. Some read this as Aṇumārgaṃ to denote the subtleness of the foriegn body. But in such case the usage of “Kathancit” has no place because the invisibility of the foreign body is made clear by the use of the word subtleness. Udīriteṣu means in the skin etc. Phenilam means - with froath. Mathitam means churned (curds that is churned); usnam means warm in touch. 5. Curability of Nādīvraṇa The tridosa type of sinus wound is incurable while the remaining four are curable when proper steps are taken. 6. (Su. Ci. 17). Thus ends the diagnosis of Naḍī vraṇa (sinus wound) in the Mūdhava’s book of diagnosis written by Srīmādhavakara. 45 Since it is already mentioned in the context of the Tridosaja type of Nāḍī Mādhavanidānaṃ vrana about its incurability, does it not amount to repeatetion? Not so. That text (stanza) was written in the Nīdāna sthāna of Śusruta samhita estimating the incurability of Tridosaja variety of sinus wound. To propose the curability with ef¬ forts, of the other types which was not made made clear in that chapter, this is mentioned in the cikitsā sthāna of There is nothing wrong if Mādhavakara writes it here. Thus ends the diagnosis of Nadi vrana (Sinus wound) in the Madhukosa commentary written by Śrīkanṭhadatta. ****
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 45.
context: मधुकोशः पित्तजामाह-पित्तादित्यादि। अधिकमुष्णमहःसु चेति दिवा औष्ण्येन पित्तकोपात्॥ ३॥ ज़ेया कफाद्वहघनार्ज़ुनपिच्छिलास्त्रा स्तब्धा सकण्डुररुजा रजनीप्रवृद्धा। मधुकोशः कफजामाह-ज्ञेयेत्यादि। बहुधनार्जुनपिच्छिलास्ट्रेति। अत्राजुनः श्वेतः, घनः सान्द्रः आस्वशब्द आस्ववशब्दैक- देशपाठः, पदेऽपि पदैकदेसप्रयोगात्। यथा ‘जे प्रोष्ठपदानाम्’-इत्यत्र जे इत्यनेनैव जात इत्युच्यते। पिच्छिलास्त्रिति पाठेऽप्ययमेवार्थः। आस्त्रुशब्दः संपदादिषु पाठात् क्रिबन्त्ः; तुगभावस्त्वागमनित्यत्वात्॥ दाहज्वरश्वसनमूर्च्छनवक्त्रशोषा यस्यां भवन्त्यभिहितानि च लक्षणानि॥ ४॥ तामादिशेत्पवनपित्तकफप्रकोपाद्घोरामसुक्षयकरीमिव कालरात्रिम्। मधुकोशः त्रिदोषजामाह- दाहेत्यादि। अभिहितानीति प्रत्येकं वातादिजनाडीकथितानि। असुक्षयकरीमिति मारणात्मिकां, कालरात्रि मरणकारिणीं यमभगिनीमिव । ‘गतिं त्वसुहराम्’ इति पाठान्तरम् ॥ ४॥ नष्ट कथंचिदनुमार्गमुदीरितेषु स्थानेषु शल्यमचिरेण गतिं करोति॥ ५ ॥ सा फेनिलं मथितमुष्णमसृग्विमिश्रं स्त्रावं करोति सहसा सरूजा च नित्यम्। मधुकोशः शल्यनिमित्तामाह- नष्टमित्यादि। नष्टमदृश्यमानमु। कथंचिदित वेगक्षयादिकारणानामनियमार्थमुक्तमु। अनुमार्ग मार्ग लक्ष्मीकृत्य। केचित् ‘अणुमार्गम्’ इति पठित्वा शल्यविशेषणतया योजयन्ति। किंत्वस्मिन् पक्षेऽणुमार्गत्वेनैव शल्यस्यादर्शने प्रयुक्ते कथंचिदिति निरर्थकं स्यात्। उद्दीरितेष्विति त्वगादिषु। फेनिलं फेनवन्तम्। मथितमुन्मथितम्। उष्णमुष्णस्पर्शम्। एते च धर्माः प्रसारणाकुञ्चनादौ चलता शल्येन मांसादिक्षोभेण भवन्ति॥ ५॥ नाडी त्रिदोषप्रभवा न सिध्ये च्छेषाश्चतस्त्रः खलु यलसाध्यः॥ ६॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते मादवनिदाने नाडीव्रणनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ४५॥ मधुकोशः असाध्यत्वादिकमाह–नाडीत्यादि। ननु, नाडी त्रिदोषप्रभवा न सिध्येदिति पुनरुक्त असुक्षयकरीमित्यनेनै– वासाध्यत्वस्योक्तत्वात्। नैवम्, अयं ग्रन्थः सुश्रुतेन निदानस्थानोक्तमेव त्रिदोषनाड्या असाध्यत्वमन्द्य तदन्यासा शेषत्वनिश्चयेन यलसाध्यत्वप्रतिपादनाय चिकित्सिते पठितः, स एवात्र माधवकरेण लिखित इत्यदोषः॥ ६॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तविरचितायां मधुक्रोशव्याख्यायां नाडीव्रणनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ४५ ॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 38, verse 12):

मधुकोशः अनन्तरमपचीगुडकतुल्यतया ग्रन्थिमाह-वातादय इत्यादि। वातपित्तकफाः प्रत्येक दुष्टाः; दुष्टिश्चात्र वृद्धिरेव न क्षयः क्षीणानां विकारकरणाक्षमत्वात्। यद्येवं तर्हि कथं वातादिक्षये मन्दचेष्टादयः? उच्यते, तत्क्षये विरोधिदोषकोपात्; यथा-मधुरस्निग्धादिभिर्वाते क्षीणे तत्समानत्वाच्छ्लेष्मा प्रकुप्यति। वचनं हि, ‘वृद्धिश्चापि विरोधिनाम्' इति। संदूष्य मेदश्च मांसमसुक् सिराश्चेत्यनेन मेदोजः, कफसंबन्धाद्यो भवति तथा सिराजोऽपि वायुना सिरादृष्ट्या यो जन्यते स उच्यते। एवं पञ्च ग्रन्थयः। तथेति संदूष्य मांसमसुगिति। अत्रासृजः क्रमोलङ्डनेन पाठोऽप्राधान्यसूचकं निवेश्य ‘असुक् च’ इति पाठः। चरके तु ग्रन्थिग्रंथितकफज एव ग्रन्थिविसर्प–शब्देनोक्तः। वृत्तोन्नतमिति वृत्तं वर्तुलम् उन्नतमुच्छूनम्। विग्रथितं कठिनं, कर्कश वा; विग्रथितत्वादेव ग्रन्थिरिति संज्ञा॥११॥ आयम्यते वृश्चयति तुद्यते च प्रत्यस्यते मथ्यति भिद्यते च । कृष्णो मृदुर्बस्तिरिवाततश्च भिन्नः स्त्रवेच्चानिलजोऽस्त्रमच्छम्॥ १२॥ ( सु.नि ११ )
answer_text: Further granthi is explained due to its similarity with apaci. Vatadayah means vāta etc., all three doṣas that are vitiated individually. Here the vitiation means after increase in their quantity and not decrease since the depleted can not cause dis¬ ease. If it is so. How come dullness - inactivity comes when vāta is depleted? It is said that the antagonistic dosa, kapha is on increase which is why dullness, inactivity takes place when vāta is depleted? It is said that the antagonistic doṣa, kapha is on increase which is why dullness and inactivity takes place. When vata is depleted due to over intake of sweet, oily etc., food, śleṣmā repletes which has those sweet, oily etc., qualities. As said "the replete may take place in the antagonistic factors also” The medoja type of granthi that has association of kapha and siraja type in which vata disturbs the siras are also enumerated here, thus making the number of granthis as five. In the word māṃsamasṛjah, asṛk (blood)is mentioned after māṃsa muscle) to show its unimportance. In the disease visarpa, blood is important fac¬ tor. That is why, according to different text, “asykca” is read in which the usage of Ca (also) indicates the secondary place of blood. In Caraka, granthi is described as caused by solidified kapha and called as granthi visarpa. Vrtta is round in shape, unnata means swollen/high-risen. Vigrathita is hard or rough (hardened). Vigrathitat granthih." Since it is hardened, the swelling is called "granthi", 11. Vātaja granthi There is stretching, cutting and pinning sensation in the tumour in vatic Mādhavanidānāṃ granthi. The patient feels as if he is thrown out, squeezed and broken. The tumour is black in colour soft and blown like bladder and on opening, it exudes clear liquid. 12. (Su. Ni. 11)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 38, verse 12.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 73):

मधुकोशः श्लेष्मोपनाहलक्षणमाह-ग्रन्थिरित्यादि। नाल्प इति महान्। अपाक ईषत्याकः अत एव सुश्रुतेऽल्पस्रावः पठितः । दृष्टिसन्धाविति कृष्णदूष्टिमण्डलयोः सन्धावित्यर्थः । कण्डूप्रायः कफप्राबल्यात् । नीरुजोऽल्यरुज इत्यर्थः । तथाच विदेहः-'वायुः श्लेष्माणमादाय दृष्टिसन्धौ व्यवस्थितः । अरुणं कठिनं ग्रन्थिं जनयेदल्पवेदनम् ॥ श्लेष्मप्राबल्यात् श्लेष्मोपनाहव्यपदेशः । आश्रयप्रभावादरुणत्वमत्र ॥ ७० ॥ गत्वा सन्धीनश्रुमार्गेण दोषाः कुर्युः स्त्रावाँलक्षणैः स्वैरुपेतान्। तं हि स्रावं नेत्रनाडीति चैके तस्या लिड़ुं कीर्त्तयिष्ये चतुर्धा॥ ७१ ॥ ( सु.उ. २ ) मधुकोशः चतुणाँ स्त्रावाणाँ संप्राप्तिमाह-गत्वा सन्धीनित्यादि। सन्धीनिति बहुवचननिर्देशात्सर्वनेत्रान्तर्गताश्चत्वारः सन्धयो गृह्यन्ते। अश्रमार्गेणेति अश्रवाहिन्यौ धमन्यौ अश्रमार्गः 'द्वे चाश्रवाहिन्यौ' (सु.शा. ९) इति सुश्रुतः, अश्रुवहधमनीभ्यामित्यर्थः। ननु, यद्यश्रुवहधमनीभ्यां गत्वा दोषाः स्त्रावानापादयन्ति, तत्कथं 'सिरानुसारिभिदोषैः' इत्याद्युक्ता संप्राप्तिन् व्याहन्यते, सिराधमन्योरन्यत्वात्। उच्यते-सामान्यविशोषत्वात् संप्राप्तयभिधानद्वयस्य; पूर्वा संप्रातिः सामान्यम्, इतरा च विशेष इति न विरोधः। अथवा 'सिराधमनील्रोतसामविभागः' (सु.शा. ९) इति परकीयमतेन सिराधमन्योरैक्यादविरोधः। अस्मिन्नर्थें संप्राप्युक्त एवार्थो निष्पन्नीक्रियते। नेत्रनाडीति चैंक इति वदन्तीति शेषः, अनिषेधादनुमतमिदम् ( दोषाः सन्निपातश्लेष्मरक्तपित्तात्मकाः। लक्षणेदोषलक्षणैः। उपेतान् परीतानिति। गदाधेरेण ‘लक्षणैरित्यर्थविशोषादधिगन्तव्यम्। चतुर्धेति सान्निपातिककफजरक्तजपित्तजत्वभेदात्; वातजस्तु' स्त्रावो नास्त्येव, व्याधिस्वभावत्; पित्तजगलगण्डवत्')॥ ७१ ॥ पाकात् सन्धौ संस्त्रवेद्यस्तु पूयं पूयास्त्रावोऽसौ गदः सर्वजस्तु। ( सु. उ. २) मधुकोशः चतुर्विधस्त्रावमध्ये पूयास्त्रावलक्षणमाह-पाकादित्यादि। सर्वजस्त्रिदोषज इत्यर्थः । अस्य प्रत्याखयेयत्वादग्रे- भिधानं, यद्यप्यन्येऽपि स्त्रावा असाध्यत्वेनोक्तास्तथाऽपि याप्या बोद्धव्याः। ‘पाकः’ इति पाठे पाकः संस्रवेत् पाकवान् शोथः स्त्रवेदित्यर्थः, उपचारात्, पाकस्य क्रियामात्रत्वात्॥ श्वेतं सान्द्रं पिच्छिलं यः स्त्रवेत्तु श्लेष्मस्त्रावोऽसौ विकारो मतस्तु॥ ७२ ॥ ( सु.उ. २ ) मधुकोशः श्लेष्मस्त्रावलक्षणमाह-श्वेतमित्यादि सान्द्रं घनम्॥ ७२ ॥ रक्तस्रावः शोणितोत्थो विकारः स्त्रवेद् दुष्टं तत्र रक्तं प्रभूतम्। ( सु. उ. २ ) मधुकोशः रक्तस्रावलक्षणमाह-रक्तस्राव इत्यादि। रक्तकृतः स्रावो रक्तस्रावः ( रक्तस्राव इत्यनेनैव स्रवेदित्यस्य लब्धत्वात्तदुक्तिर्निरन्तरस्रावप्रतिपादनार्थमिति कार्तिकः। न चैतत् प्रभूतमित्यनेन गतार्थम्, अनिरन्तरतयाऽपि प्रभूतस्रावसंभवात् )। रक्तस्राव इत्यनेनैव रक्तजत्वे सिद्धे शोणितजो विकार यदुच्यते तदत्यन्तकुपित रक्तजत्वप्रतिपादनार्थम्। कार्तिकस्त्वाह-पित्तलिङ्गपरिग्रहार्थं, पित्तेन सह तुल्यत्वाद्रक्तस्य। तथा क्वचित् पाठः- रक्तस्त्रावः पित्तलिड़ौरुपेतः ।' इति ॥ हरिद्राभं पीतमुष्णं जलाभं पित्तात्त्रावः संस्रवेत् सन्धिमध्यात् ॥ ७३ ॥ ( सु. उ. २)
answer_text: Nālpa - not a small one - means a big one. Apāka not ripening means slightly ripening, that is why Susruta mentions the symptom slightly oozing. Drstisandhau means in the junction of kṛṣṇα and dṛṣṭi sandhi and as a result, there arises red and hard tumour which has least pain. This condition is called śleṣmoþanāha. Though caused by both vāta and śleṣmā, it is termed so, due to predominance of śleṣmā. The aruṇa varṇa (red colour) is due to the place of origin. 70 Four types of Śrāva (discharges) Mādhavanidānaṃ The-dosas reach the sandhi (junction/conjoining place) through the chan¬ nels that transport the tears and produce (in the sandhi area) discharges with their own symptoms; such condition is called srāva and netranāḍi as some call it. The four types of Srāva will be explained further. 71. (Su.u. 2). By using the plural number Sandhin it is implied as all four sandhis in the eye. Aśrimārgeṇa through the dhamani’s that carry tears. As said by Suśruta, “Two dhamanīs are meant for carrying/transporting tears”. (Su.ṣā.9). When the doṣas are said to be entering the sandhis through the dhamani and causing srava (discharge), the pathogenesis described, in which the śirās help the doṣas in getting to Sandhis is contradicted, as sirā and dhamanī are two different entities. It is said that the first one, is a specific one and thus it is not a contradiction. It is also said that there is no difference among sirā, dhamanī and srotas (Su. śā. 9). Vadanti - some say - is to be added to netranālīti; netranālī is the name given to this condition. Doṣaḥ means sannipāta, śleṣmā, raktā and pitta. Lakṣanaiḥ with the symptoms. Upetān mixed with Gadādhara used the term sarvaiaḥ in the place of lakṣanaiḥ. “The doṣa with their own symptomatology, are manifested” is the substance. Caturdha - in four types means with the differentiation of sānnipātika, kaphaja, raktaja and pittaja. The vātaja srāva does not occur at all by nature of disease as in the case of pillaja galagaṇḍa. 71. Pūyasrāva Due to ulceration in the sandhi there will be discharge of pus in that place - this condition is called puyasrava caused by all the dosas - (sannipata). (Su.v.2) Netra Roga Nidāna Sarvaja means caused by all dosas. Since this is a pratyākhyeya (difficult disease for cure) it is mentioned first. Though others are labelled as difficult for cure asadhya), they should be known as yapya (prolongable). Paka means the inflam¬ mation gets ripened and results in ulceration by therapeutic intervention. Slesma srāva The discharge which is white, dense and sticky is called slesma srava. 72. (Su.u.2) Sāndra means solid (dense). 72. Raktasrāva Raktasrava is originated due to(aggravated) rakta There will be profuse dis¬ charge of vitialed rakta in this condition. (Su. u. 2) Discharge of blood is rakta srāva. By the word raktasrava itself the discharge of blood is indicated; using the word, sravet is to emphasise the continuous flow¬ according to Kartika. This is again indicated by the word prabhuta (copious) but prabhūta also means continuous and copious. Again, the origination of this disease is indicated by the word raktasrāva. But using the word śoṇitottha (caused by blood) is to make clear, the high degree of vitiation of Rakta. Kārtika says, take the role of pitta here, “Since rakta is similar to pitta……”. Some read this as, “Rakta srāvaḥ pitta..... ". Which means-Discharge of blood with the symptoms of pitta. context: मधुकोशः श्लेष्मोपनाहलक्षणमाह-ग्रन्थिरित्यादि। नाल्प इति महान्। अपाक ईषत्याकः अत एव सुश्रुतेऽल्पस्रावः पठितः । दृष्टिसन्धाविति कृष्णदूष्टिमण्डलयोः सन्धावित्यर्थः । कण्डूप्रायः कफप्राबल्यात् । नीरुजोऽल्यरुज इत्यर्थः । तथाच विदेहः-'वायुः श्लेष्माणमादाय दृष्टिसन्धौ व्यवस्थितः । अरुणं कठिनं ग्रन्थिं जनयेदल्पवेदनम् ॥ श्लेष्मप्राबल्यात् श्लेष्मोपनाहव्यपदेशः । आश्रयप्रभावादरुणत्वमत्र ॥ ७० ॥ गत्वा सन्धीनश्रुमार्गेण दोषाः कुर्युः स्त्रावाँलक्षणैः स्वैरुपेतान्। तं हि स्रावं नेत्रनाडीति चैके तस्या लिड़ुं कीर्त्तयिष्ये चतुर्धा॥ ७१ ॥ ( सु.उ. २ ) मधुकोशः चतुणाँ स्त्रावाणाँ संप्राप्तिमाह-गत्वा सन्धीनित्यादि। सन्धीनिति बहुवचननिर्देशात्सर्वनेत्रान्तर्गताश्चत्वारः सन्धयो गृह्यन्ते। अश्रमार्गेणेति अश्रवाहिन्यौ धमन्यौ अश्रमार्गः 'द्वे चाश्रवाहिन्यौ' (सु.शा. ९) इति सुश्रुतः, अश्रुवहधमनीभ्यामित्यर्थः। ननु, यद्यश्रुवहधमनीभ्यां गत्वा दोषाः स्त्रावानापादयन्ति, तत्कथं 'सिरानुसारिभिदोषैः' इत्याद्युक्ता संप्राप्तिन् व्याहन्यते, सिराधमन्योरन्यत्वात्। उच्यते-सामान्यविशोषत्वात् संप्राप्तयभिधानद्वयस्य; पूर्वा संप्रातिः सामान्यम्, इतरा च विशेष इति न विरोधः। अथवा 'सिराधमनील्रोतसामविभागः' (सु.शा. ९) इति परकीयमतेन सिराधमन्योरैक्यादविरोधः। अस्मिन्नर्थें संप्राप्युक्त एवार्थो निष्पन्नीक्रियते। नेत्रनाडीति चैंक इति वदन्तीति शेषः, अनिषेधादनुमतमिदम् ( दोषाः सन्निपातश्लेष्मरक्तपित्तात्मकाः। लक्षणेदोषलक्षणैः। उपेतान् परीतानिति। गदाधेरेण ‘लक्षणैरित्यर्थविशोषादधिगन्तव्यम्। चतुर्धेति सान्निपातिककफजरक्तजपित्तजत्वभेदात्; वातजस्तु' स्त्रावो नास्त्येव, व्याधिस्वभावत्; पित्तजगलगण्डवत्')॥ ७१ ॥ पाकात् सन्धौ संस्त्रवेद्यस्तु पूयं पूयास्त्रावोऽसौ गदः सर्वजस्तु। ( सु. उ. २) मधुकोशः चतुर्विधस्त्रावमध्ये पूयास्त्रावलक्षणमाह-पाकादित्यादि। सर्वजस्त्रिदोषज इत्यर्थः । अस्य प्रत्याखयेयत्वादग्रे- भिधानं, यद्यप्यन्येऽपि स्त्रावा असाध्यत्वेनोक्तास्तथाऽपि याप्या बोद्धव्याः। ‘पाकः’ इति पाठे पाकः संस्रवेत् पाकवान् शोथः स्त्रवेदित्यर्थः, उपचारात्, पाकस्य क्रियामात्रत्वात्॥ श्वेतं सान्द्रं पिच्छिलं यः स्त्रवेत्तु श्लेष्मस्त्रावोऽसौ विकारो मतस्तु॥ ७२ ॥ ( सु.उ. २ ) मधुकोशः श्लेष्मस्त्रावलक्षणमाह-श्वेतमित्यादि सान्द्रं घनम्॥ ७२ ॥ रक्तस्रावः शोणितोत्थो विकारः स्त्रवेद् दुष्टं तत्र रक्तं प्रभूतम्। ( सु. उ. २ ) मधुकोशः रक्तस्रावलक्षणमाह-रक्तस्राव इत्यादि। रक्तकृतः स्रावो रक्तस्रावः ( रक्तस्राव इत्यनेनैव स्रवेदित्यस्य लब्धत्वात्तदुक्तिर्निरन्तरस्रावप्रतिपादनार्थमिति कार्तिकः। न चैतत् प्रभूतमित्यनेन गतार्थम्, अनिरन्तरतयाऽपि प्रभूतस्रावसंभवात् )। रक्तस्राव इत्यनेनैव रक्तजत्वे सिद्धे शोणितजो विकार यदुच्यते तदत्यन्तकुपित रक्तजत्वप्रतिपादनार्थम्। कार्तिकस्त्वाह-पित्तलिङ्गपरिग्रहार्थं, पित्तेन सह तुल्यत्वाद्रक्तस्य। तथा क्वचित् पाठः- रक्तस्त्रावः पित्तलिड़ौरुपेतः ।' इति ॥ हरिद्राभं पीतमुष्णं जलाभं पित्तात्त्रावः संस्रवेत् सन्धिमध्यात् ॥ ७३ ॥ ( सु. उ. २)

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 20):

त्रिविधं हि हिंसा-क्रीडा-पूजार्थं ग्रहा गृहन्ति । यदुक्तम्अशुचिं भिन्नमर्यादं क्षतं वा यदि वाऽक्षतम् । हिंस्युहिंसा-विहाराथं सत्कारार्थमथापि च ।। सु०उ० इति । तत्र हिंसार्थं गृहीतोऽसाध्यो भवति तस्य श्लोकार्धद्वयेन लक्षणमाहस्थूलाक्ष इत्यादि । स्थूलाक्षो विकृतनेत्र इति जेज्जटः । द्रुतमटनो द्रुतगतिः अत एव त्वरितगतिः इति जेज्जटेन पठितम् । यश्चेत्यादि । पर्वतादिपतितः सन् यो गृह्यते सोऽप्यसाध्यः नगो वृक्षः । सर्व एवोन्मादी त्रयोदशेऽब्दे देवतागृहीतोऽप्यसाध्यः । विदेहेऽधिकमप्यसाध्यलक्षणं पठ्यतेमेढ्रप्रवृत्त- क्षतजः सास्राक्षः स्रुतनासिकः । रूक्षजिह्नः पूतगर्भो हतवागतिदुर्बलः ।। इत्यादि ।।।। पौर्णमास्यामसुराः दवग्रहाः प्रायशोऽप्टम्यां यक्षाश्च प्रतिपद्यथ ॥ गन्धवाः पित्र्याः कृष्णक्षये हिंस्यः पञ्चम्यामपि चोरगाः । रक्षांसि रात्री पैशाचाश्चतुर्देश्यां विशन्ति हि ॥॥ - - - - - -
answer_text: As per the belief of Ayurveda, the grahas or celestial elements afflict individuals in three ways: 1. by injuring and 2. by playing with the individual or by 3. by forcing him to worship (the graha instrumental in seizure). Suśruta states, ‘The grahas overpower the untidy, one with abnormal conduct. They also seize the injured or unhurt individuals for troubling them, and for the selfish purpose of playing with them or getting worshipped by the same (SS. Ut. 60.5). The one who has been afflicted by the grahas and who has got injured as well would not be cured. According to Jejjata, the term sthulaksa implies terrifying eyes. Mountains, trees, buildings etc. are objects with higher levels. If they fall and if subsequently a graha seizes an individual he would not be curable. If one remains seized for as long as thirteen years, he could not be cured even if the seizure has involved a heavenly agency. Videha states that unmāda caused by over-activity and injury of the penis and with symptoms like blood-red eyes, running nose, dry tongue, weak belly, impaired speech, and over-emaciation, is also incurable. The time of affliction (SS. Ut. 60.17-18) The Deva Grahas afflict individuals during the full-moon day, the asura grahas or demons afflict during the dawn as well as the dusk. Gandharvas overpower the humans mostly on the eighth day of the each half of the month and the Yakṣas on the first of every fortnight. The Pitrgrahas afflict on the fortnight of the descending moon and the Nāgas, on the fifth day of the fortnight. The Rākṣasas afflict during night time while the Pisacas catch hold of human beings mainly on the fourteenth day of the fortnight. 27-28
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 20.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 22):

विमुक्तेत्यादि । तदेवेत्यनेन साटोपादित्वमति– दिशति । कफव्याकुलितानिलं कफावृतवातम् ।।–।। नाभेरधस्तात् सझातः सञ्चारी यदि वाऽचलः ॥७०॥
answer_text: (SS. Ni. 1.89) A The vitiated vāta associated with kapha causing the condition in the region of the stomach but away from the region of the heart and the flanks is known as the symptom of Pratyādhmāna. 69 The passage starting from sāṭopaṃ refers to the peculiar characteri- stics of the diseases ādhmāna and pratyādhmāna. According to Gayadāsa, the term ātopa is fickle movement in the abdomen while Kārtika states that it suggests a guḍa-guḍa sound in the abdomen. The term adhmatam suggests a stomach inflated like leather bag filled with air. The term udara has been used for abdomen. The āmāʿaya or stomach is the place where originates the Pratyādhmāna. Asthīlā (SS. Ni. 1.90) When a stony hard globular gland enlarges upwards significantly and produces a fixed or mobile swelling below the umbilicus this condition is identified as Vatasqhila; it produces obstruction in passing urine and faecal matter.70-71

question:

answer_text: Now is being discussed the symptoms of the fever caused by the combined effect of the vāta and kapha doṣas (vātakaphaja jvara). 1There is excessive sweat in this kind of fever. It is due to irrelevant relationship of cause and effect (Vikrtivisamasamavaya) factor as per the opinion of the commentator Kārtikakuṇḍa. This argument holds good as Hārīta has also included svedabhāva (production of sweat) among various features of this type of fever like severe headache and cough. Moreover, there is Madhyavega (medium bout of tempera- ture) in the fever that signifies a situation when there is neither too high nor too low bout of temperature. Features of signs and symptoms of Slesmā-pitta type of fever (SS. Ut. 39. 50) The features of Śleṣmā-pitta type of fever include sticky and bitter sensation in the mouth, drowsiness, delusion, cough, distaste, thirst, and alternative feeling of heat and cold in the body. 17
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2.

answer_text: The passage starting from sphikpurva refers to the features of the disease grdhrasī. The disease has been called sphikpurvā as it first attacks the sphik that is the buttocks. Two kinds of the disease have been noticed: one originating through vitiation of vāta as well as the kapha and the other produced by vitiation of only vāta. Features of both of them are identical but there is a feeling of heaviness and anorexia in the cases of the grdhrasi originating through vitiation of vata as well as the kapha. Viśvācī (Radio-ulnar paralysis) (SS. Ni. 1.75) Viśvãci or the brachial (related to the arm) neuralgia is affection of the dorsal aspect of the arm including tendons/nerves of the surface of the fingers, the arms and the shoulders. It results in the loss of function of the arm. 57

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Charaka Samhita (Chikitsasthana, Chapter 14, verse 234-242):

answer_text: Adhahpuspi, bala, daruharidra, prsniparni, goksura, leaf, buds, of nyagrodha, paste the following drugs are taken 10 gm. each -jivanti, katurohini, pippali, pipplimula, sunthi, devadaru, indrayava, salamali flowers, vira, candana, utpala, katphala, citraka, musta, priyangu, ativisa, salaparni, stamens of lotus vand water lily, prepared in water four prastha reduced to one-fourth, for this preparation 'prastha' [ CH. ] should be taken as of thirty two palas. (Thus water for decoction will be 5.12 litres and r the extract will the 1.28 litres) with this decoction and the juice of sunişannakanand ( cangeri two prastha (1.28 litres), ghee one prastha (640 gm.) should be cooked. This is free from complication and be used alone or mixed with various foods and drinks in piles, diarrhoea, tridosaja haemmorrhage, tenesmus, rectal prolapse, various slimy discharges, frequent urge for evacuation, swelling and pain, in anorectum, retention of urine, confounded vata, sluggishness of digestion, anorexia. It promotes strength, complexion and digestive power
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Chikitsasthana, Chapter 14, verse 234-242.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 7):

रक्तजानाहरक्तेत्यादि । रक्तवाहिसिरास्थानाश्च ते रक्तजाश्चेति रक्तवाहिसिरास्थान रक्तजाः अथवा रक्तवाहिसिरास्थानं यद्रक्त तज्जाः । नामभेदाते षद् तत्र केशादादयश्चत्वारः सह सौरसनाम-मातृनामभ्यां क्रिमिभ्यां वर्तन्त इति सहसौरसमातरः एवं षड् भवन्ति । कुष्ठेककर्माण इति कुष्ठमेवैक कार्यं येषां ते तथा कुष्ठजनका इति यावत् । उक्तं हि सुश्रुते सवाणि कुष्टानि सवातानि सपित्तानि सश्लेष्माणि सक्रिमीणि चोपदिश्यन्ते । इति सु०नि० जायन्तेऽधोविसर्पिणः । पुरीषोत्था पक्वाशये प्रवृद्धाः स्युर्भवेयुश्व ते यदाऽऽमाशयोन्मुखाः ॥१३॥ मा०नि०-१८ तदाऽऽस्योद्गार-निःश्वासा विड्गन्धानुविधायिनः । पृथुवृत्त-तनु-स्थूलाः ते पञ्च नाम्ना क्रिमयः केरूक-मकेरूकाः । सौसुरादाः सश्रूलाख्या लेलिहा जनयन्ति हि ॥१ ॥ विड़भेद-शुल-विष्टम्भ-कार्श्य-पारुष्य-पाण्डुताः । गुदकण्डूर्विमार्गगाः रोमहर्षाग्निसदनं इति माधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने क्रिमिनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥॥ - - - - - -
answer_text: 5: 6) 111-1211 The passage in context details the implications of the worms origi¬ nating in the blood. These worms exist in the blood flowing in the veins and that is why they are called raktavāhisirāsthānāh. In terms of their names, they are said to be six: keśāda, romavidhvaṁsa, ro- madvipa, udūmbara, saurasa and māṭr. Thus, the Keśāda and others are four in number while Saurasa and Māṭr are two. As the two live together, they are also referred as Sahasaurasamātṛ. The Kuṣṭha (leprosy or any otner skin disease) is caused by them. It is considered in Susruta that all skin diseases are caused by the involvement of vāta, pitta, śleṣmā as well as the krimi (worms) (SS. Ni. 5.6). Worms of purīṣa (faeces) origin (AH. Ni. 14.53-56) ) = The faecal worms originate in the intestines and when mature they have a tendency to travel downwards. However, when they increase, they instead move towards āmāṣaya (stomach) and produce the odour of faeces in the belch and in the respiration of the patient. They are big, round, thin or thick; blue, yellow, white or black. They are of five varieties, namely, Kakeruka, Makeruka, Sausurāda, Saśūla and Leliha. They generate diarrhoea, pain in the abdomen, constipation, emaciation, dryness, pallor (whitish-yellow discolouration), horripi¬ lations, poor digestion, and itching in the anus. They even move into organs nearby and create problems. 13-16

मधुकोशः दन्तहर्षलक्षणमाह-शीतेत्यादि। ‘शीतमुष्णं च दशनाः सहन्ते स्पर्शनं न च। यस्य तं दन्तहर्ष तु व्याधि विद्यात्, समीरणात्’ इति श्लोकान्तरं पठन्ति। तत्र दन्तहर्षस्य वातजत्वेऽप्युष्णासहत्वं व्याधिप्रभावात्, कफरक्तावृतत्वाद्वा बोद्धव्यम्॥ २५॥ मलो दन्तगतो यस्तु पित्तमारुतशोषितः। शर्करेव खरस्पर्शा सा ज्ञेया दन्तशर्करा॥ २६॥ ( सु. नि. १६ ) मधुकोशः दन्तशर्करालक्षणमाह-मल इत्यादि। ‘शर्करेव खरस्पर्शा’ इत्यस्य स्थाने ‘सा दन्तानां गुणहरी’ क्वचित् पठ्यते, दन्तानां गुणस्य शुक्लत्वदूढत्वादिकस्य हरणशीला॥ २६ ॥ कपालेष्विव दीर्यत्सु दन्तानां सैव शर्करा। कपालिकेति विज्ञेया सदा दन्तविनाशिनी॥ २७॥ ( सु.नि. १६ )
answer_text: Some read the verse in Suśruta as, “The teeth do not withstand cold and warm (foods and beverages) and even touch. This condition is known as Dantaharsha caused by vāta”. (Su. Ni. 16). Though this is caused by vāta not being able to with stand warmth, is to be understood as the specific feature of this disease or due to āvaraṇa (covering) of kapha'and rakta. 25. Danta śarkarā The foreign matter stuck up in between the teeth gets dried up due to aggra¬ vation of pitta and vāta and becomes like sand, with rough touch which is known as dantaśarkarā. 26. (Su. Ni. 16). In the palce of “śarkareva kharasparśā”, “sā dantānāṃ guṇahaṁ” is read by some which means - this condition snatches away the original qualities of teeth i.e white colour and strong nature. 26. Mukha Roga Nidāna Kapālikā The same sarkara, when it forms into big pieces - breaks the teeth and destroys them, is known as kapālikā. 26. (Su. Ni. 16)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 56, verse 26.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 6):

प्रतिलोमतन्त्रयुक्त्या तेपां रूपमाह विषम इत्यादि । वातजान् रोगानिति वातनानात्म- जानामशीतरन्यतमान् सामान्यजांध्य ज्वरातीसारादीन् एवं पित्तनानात्मजानामोषचोषादीना चत्वारिशतोऽन्यतमान् एवं कफनानात्मजाना विंशतेरालस्यादीनामन्यतमान् । एते एच विकाराधरके महारोगाध्याय च०सृ० एव द्रश्व्याः । समेत्यादि । समा उचिता मात्रा आहारस्य सम्याग्यस्य विपच्यते स समाग्निः । तीक्ष्याग्निरिति ते विद्यादिति छेदः । मात्राऽति- मात्रेत्युपलक्षणं तेनाजीर्णगुरुभोजनादिकमपि लक्षणीयम् । यदुक्तमन्यत्र अंतिमात्रमजीर्णंडपि गुरु चान्नमथाश्नतः । दिवाऽपि स्वपतो यस्य पच्यते सोऽग्निरुत्तमः ।। इति । तीक्ष्णग्रहणेन भस्मकस्यावरोधः अत्यन्ततीक्ष्णाग्निरेव भस्मक इत्युच्यते । यदुक्तं चरकेनरे क्षीणकफे पित्तं कुपितं मारुतानुगम् । स्वोष्मणा पावकस्थाने बलमग्नेः प्रयच्छति ।। तदा लब्धबलो देहं विरुजेत् सानिलोऽनलः । अभिभूय पचत्यन्नं तैक्ष्ण्यादाशु मुहुर्मुहुः ।। पक्त्वाऽन्नं स ततो धातून् शोणितादीन् पचत्यपि । ततो दौर्बल्यमातङ्कान् मृत्युं चोपनयेन्नरम् ।। भुक्तेऽन्ने लभते शान्तिं जीर्णमात्रे प्रताम्यति ।। तृट्-कास-दाह-मूर्च्छाद्या व्याधयोऽत्यग्निसम्भवाः ।। च०चि० - इति - आमं विदग्धं विष्टब्धं कफ-पित्तानिलैस्त्रिभिः । अजीर्णं केचिदिच्छन्ति चतुर्थं रसशेषतः ॥॥ अजीर्णं पञ्चमं केचिन्निर्दोषं दिनपाकित चा। वदन्ति - - -
answer_text: The passage in context has described the visama and other types of digestive fires. It may be noted that there are two types of diseases in terms of the causative factors: sāmānyaja and nānātmaja. The former type of diseases relates to more than one doṣa. The nānātmaja type of diseases is produced by a certain dosa. It may be noted that eighty diseases of vāta origin are caused by viṣaṁa agni, common diseases among them being the jvara (fever) and atisara (diarrhoea). Likewise, forty diseases of pitta origin are caused by visama agni. These diseases include such problems as osa (burning) and cosa (in- flammation). Similarly, twenty diseases of kapha origin are caused by mandagni, for example alasya (lassitude). All these diseases have been detailed in the text of Caraka (Sīī, 20; the Mahārogādhyāya). As regards the sama type of agni or digestive fire, it may be noted that it facilitates easy digestion of the proper meals taken in the proper quantity and in proper time. The tikṣṇāgni could be instrumental in digesting both the proper and improper types of the food taken. It could even digest the constipating and heavy food items consumed. That variety of digestive fire is considered to be best (ullama) which helps one to digest the heavy meals and digests the meals of an individual who sleeps during the day hours. As said elsewhere, ‘when the digestive fire metabolizes the eaten food and the food that is eaten without complete digestion of the previously eaten food and even if the individual sleeps during the day it is considered the best. Tiksuāgni is different from Bhasmaka which signifies a higher degree of strong and powerful digestive power. The text of Caraka narrates, ‘When kapha is decreased and pitta is aggravated, the latter takes the help of Maruta or vāta and with its own heat bestows enormous strength to the digestive fire. The digestive fire, then having accrued the energy accumulated, troubles the body. It digests the food in a speedier manner. When food is Adhuad An ingested, a person feels pacified and after complete digestion he or she feels severe weakness and suffers from disorders like thirst, cough, burning sensation and syncope that are caused by Bhasmaka or the excessively powerful digestive fire’ (it is also called the atyagni) (CS. Ci.15. 219-220). After having completed the digestion it even endeavors to digest tissues like blood and ultimately having destroyed the vital tissues it even proves fatal for the individuals. Varieties of indigestion (SS. Sū. 46. 499) There are three varieties of ajīrṇa (indigestion): āma, vidagdha and vistabdha. They are generated by kapha, pitta and vata dosas respectively. There is also a fourth type of indigestion that is called rasasesa. It relates to ahara rasa and its symptom is indigestion of the nutrient portion of the eatables. 5 Some others name a fifth type of indigestion. It is called dinapaki ajīrṇa. In this condition, the eatables are digested the next day without causing any problem. There are still other individuals who count a sixth sort of indigestion. It is called the prativāsara aftrṇa that is found every day normally immediately after taking eatables. 6
chapter_title: Agnimāndya, Ajīrṇa, Visūcikā, Alasaka, Vilambikā Nidānam
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 6.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 18):

उपद्रवानाहहिक्केत्यादि । एतैः कृच्छूसाध्यं भवति न त्वसाध्यमु असाध्य- लक्षणेभ्यः पृथक्पाठादिति जेज्जटः । ध्वंसक-विक्षेपकाख्यो मद्यविकारो चरके पृथक् पठितौ तद्यथाविच्छिन्नमद्यः सहसा योऽतिमद्यं निषेवते । ध्वंसो विक्षेपकश्चैव रोगस्तस्योपजायते ।। श्लेष्मप्रसेकः कण्ठास्यशोषः शब्दासहिष्णुता । तन्द्रा-निद्राभि-योगश्च ज्ञेयं ध्वंसकलक्षणम् ।। हत्कण्ठरोधः सम्मोहश्छर्दिरङ्गरुजा ज्वरः । तृष्णा कासः शिरःशूलमेतद्विक्षेपलक्षणम् ।। च०चि० - इति तो च सुश्रुतेन विच्छित्रमद्यः सहसा योऽतिमद्यं निषेवते । तस्य पानात्ययोद्दिष्टा विकाराः सम्भवन्ति हि ।। सु०उ० इत्यनेन सङ्गृहीतौ बोद्धव्यौ । न वा चिकित्साभेद-स्तयोरुक्तः यत्यरक एवोक्तवान् तयोः कर्म चिकित्सा च वातिके यन्मदात्यये । च०चि० इति ।।।। इति श्रीविजयरक्षितकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां पानात्यय-परमद- पानाजीर्ण-पानविभ्रमनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥१ ॥ -
answer_text: The passage starting from likka mentions the peculiar implications of the disease madatyaya. Through these implications, the disease turns to be difficult to cure. It does not turn to be impossible to cure. lifikka or hiccups etc. are the complications because of which intoxication, according to Jejjata, becomes difficult to cure but does not turn completely incurable; the features of incurability have been discussed separately. Two alcoholic disorders named dhvamsaka or destroyer and viksepaka that is the heat that makes one fall down have been enumerated by Caraka (CS. Ci. 24. 199-202). Dhvamsaka is characterized by dribbling of phlegm, dryness of throat and mouth, mability to endure noise, drowsiness and long sleeping hours. The symptoms of viksepaka are feeling of grip in the heart and throat, delusion, vomiting, pain in the body, fever, thirst, cough, and headache (ibidem). Suśruta states that excessive consumption of alcohol leads to diseases mentioned in Panatyaya (SS. Ut. 47.49). Caraka states that the two conditions mentioned above should have the same treatment as the vata variety of excessive intoxication. Thus concludes the Chapter on Madātyaya
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 18.

question:

वन्ध्याकर्कोटकी देवी कन्या योगीश्वरीति च । नागारिर्नक्रदमनी विषकण्टकिनी तथा ।। २८७।। वन्ध्याकर्कोटकी लघ्वी कफनुद् व्रणशोधिनी । सर्पदर्पहरी तीक्ष्णा विसर्पविषहारिणी ।।२८८।।
answer_text: Digestive diseases: It is useful Agnimāndya (Dyspepsia), Śūla (Abdominal colíc), Gulma (Abdominal tumors) and Krmi (Worm infestation). The powered seeds used internally for the expulsion of Round worms. Febrifuge action: A decoction of the root is used to treat Jwara (Fevers). Diseases of Ear: The juice of the leaves used as an ear drops in Karna sūla (Earache) and Karna strava (Ear discharge). External uses: The leaves are used as an external applicant for Vrna (Wounds) and Dustavrna (Indolent ulcers). The juice of the root is used to relieve Vrscikavisa (Scorpion stings). Māṭrā (Dosage): Bīja cūrṇa: 3-6gm., Patra swarasa: 10-20ml. VANDHYĀ KARKOTAKI Fam: Cucurbitaceae Latin: Momordica diocia Roxb. Eng: Small bitter gourd Hin: Vankakoda. Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Devī, Kanyā, Yogīsvarī, Nāgāri, Narkadamanī and Vishakantakini. Guna karma (Properties and indications): It is Laghu (Light for digestion), Subsides Kapha dosa, Vrna shodanī (Wound healing), Sarpadarpaharī (Relieves the Posionous manifestations of Snake), Tīkṣṇa (Penetrating), cures Visarpa (Herpes) and Viṣa (Posionous manifestations). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): All through India upto an altitude of 5000ft, in the Himalayas. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a perennial climber with tuberous roots and tendrils smooth. Leaves 4-8cm.long and 3-6 cm., broad, ovate, deeply 3-5-lobed, acute apex, base cordate, serrated margins, petiole 2.5 cm. Flowers dioecious, yellow in colour, 4-6 cm across, solitary on axillary stalks. Fruits 2.5-6.5cm., ovoid, densely covered with soft spines. Seeds 6-7 - 5-6 mm, many, ovoid, compressed and pale yellow. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Phala (Fruits). Chemical constituents: Alkaloids, Ascorbic acid
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 475
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 475.
context: वन्ध्याकर्कोटकी देवी कन्या योगीश्वरीति च । नागारिर्नक्रदमनी विषकण्टकिनी तथा ।। २८७।। वन्ध्याकर्कोटकी लघ्वी कफनुद् व्रणशोधिनी । सर्पदर्पहरी तीक्ष्णा विसर्पविषहारिणी ।।२८८।।

answer_text: The passage starting from muhurmuhu refers to the characteristics and etiology of the disease hikkā. The word Vāyu means Prāṇa (the one that is responsible for respiration) along with Udāna (the one that is responsible for speech). The passage Hinastyasūn iti Hikkā suggests that it is named so as this disease damages the pranas. question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 905):

पद्मादिकन्दः शालूक करहाटश्च कथ्यते ।।११४।। मृणालमूलं भिस्साण्डं जलालूकश्च कथ्यते । शालूकं शीतलं वृष्यं पित्तदाहास्रनुद् गुरू ।।११५।। दुर्जरं स्वादुपाकश्च स्तन्यानिलकफप्रदम् । संग्राहि मधुरं रूक्षं भिस्साण्डमपि तहुणम् ।।११६ ।। बालं ह्यनार्तवं जीर्णं व्याधितं कृमिभक्षितम् । कन्द विवर्जयेत्सर्वं यद्वाऽग्न्यादिविद्वितम् । अतिजीर्णमकालोत्यं रूक्षसिद्धमदेशजम् । । ११७ । । कर्कश कोमलं चातिशीतव्यालादिदूषितम् । संशुष्क सकलं शाक नाश्नीयान्मूलकं विना ।।११८।। उक्त संस्वेदजं शाकं भूमिच्छत्रं शिलीन्य्रकम् । क्षितिगोमयकाष्ठेषु वृक्षादिषु तदुद्धवेत् ।।११९।। सर्वे संस्वेदजाः शीता दोषलाः पिच्छिलाश्र ते । गुरवश्छर्द्यतीसारज्वरश्लेष्मामयप्रदाः ।।१२०।। श्चेताशुचिस्थलीकाष्ठवंशगोमयसम्भवाः । नातिदोषकरास्ते स्युः शेषास्तेभ्यो विगहिताः ।।१२१।।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 55, verse 33):

मधुकोशः पलितमाह–क्रोधेत्यादि। श्ररीरोष्मेति देहाग्निः। पित्तं चेति पित्तमपि श्रिरोगतं पलितहेतुः। ननु, पित्तमेवाग्निः, तव्र तत्र पित्तस्य पाचकत्वेनाभिधानात्; यदुक्तवान् सुश्रुतः-‘न पाकः पित्तादृते’ (स.सू. १७) इति, तथा-‘पित्ते तस्मिन् पाचकोऽग्निरिति संज्ञा' (सु.सू. २१) इति; तथा स एव-‘न खलु पित्तव्यातिरेकेणान्योऽग्निरुप- लभ्यते,आग्नेये तु पित्ते दहनपचनदारणादिष्वभिवर्तमानेऽग्निवदुपचारः क्रियते अन्तरग्निरिति, क्षीणे ह्यग्निगुणे तत्समानद्रव्योपयोगगदतिवुद्दे शीतक्रियोपयोगादागमाच्च पश्यामः न खलू पित्तव्यतिरेकेणान्योऽग्रिः' (सु.सू. २१) इति; चरकाचार्योऽप्याह-‘दर्शनं पक्तिरूष्मा च क्षुत्तृष्णा देहमार्दवम्। प्रभाप्रसादौ मेधा च पित्तकर्माविकारजम्’ च.सू. १८) इति; पाकस्यान्यथानुपपत्त्या चाग्नेरङ्गीकारः; किंच मन्देऽग्नौ पित्तकरमरीचादिद्रव्योपयोगादग्नेर्वेद्धिः, पित्तप्रतिकूल-शीतमधुरादिद्रव्योपयोगाश्चोपशम उपलभ्यते; यदि हि पित्ताद्विन्नोऽग्निः स्यात्तदा पित्तस्य वृद्धिहासानुविधानमस्यानुपपन्नं स्यात्, न हि तुहिनकरमण्डले हिमभाज्यहिमोपलम्भः, अतुहिनमण्डले अहिमभाजि भगवति भास्करेऽभिमतो हिमोपलम्भः, यद्यतो भिन्नं तत्ततो भेदेनोपलभ्यते, यथा सागरादजगरः, न चैवं पित्तादग्निः, तत्कुतः पित्तादग्नेः पृथगुपादानमिति? अत्र प्रत्यभिधीयते-न तावदन्तरग्निः पित्तादभिन्नः भेदेसाधकप्रमाणस्य भूयः सद्दावात्; तथाह्यभेदे ‘समदोषः समाग्निश्च,’ ( सु.सू. १५) इत्यत्र, ‘समप्रकोपौ दोषाणां सर्वेषामग्निसंश्रयौ’ इत्यत्र च दोषपदलब्धत्वादग्नेः पृथगुपादानमसङ्गतं; तीक्ष्णः पित्तेन चेति स्वात्मनि क्रियाविरोधादसङ्गतं; 'यत्युनः 'न 'खलु' पित्तव्यतिरेकेणान्योऽग्निः' इत्याद्युक्तः 'तद्भेदमेव' साधयति, उपचाराभिधानात्, न ह्यभेदे उपचारः संभवति। यदप्यग्नेः पित्तवृद्धिहासानुविधानमभिहितं तदप्रयोजकं, भेदेऽपि समानत्वेन तदुपपत्तेः । यथा कफवृद्धिहासकरसौम्याग्नेयद्रव्याभ्यां शुक्रस्य वृद्धिहासौ दृष्टौ, न च कफशुक्रयोरैक्यं; किंच घृतं पित्तशमनमग्नेश्व दीपनं, पितस्य सञ्चयादौ नाग्नेर्वृद्धिः, पेयादिकं चाग्निकरं, न पित्तकृत्; ततश्व पित्ताद्विलक्षणोऽन्तरग्निः । स च द्रवतेजःसमुदायात्मकस्य पित्तस्य तेजोभागो न बहिरनलवद्दस्माङ्गाराकारः, समुदायतश्च समुदायी अन्य एव करचरणादिभ्य इव शरीर; अत्यन्तभेदेन चाग्रहणं, तस्य नित्यसंश्लेष्णशालित्वात्। पित्तस्य तेजोंऽश एव पाच(व)कः, तदाह भोजः-'दृढमुष्णोचितं ह्येतत् पित्तोष्मा पचतीति यत्। मूर्च्छितो रसवीर्याभ्यां समानव्यानसंहितः’-इत्यारभ्य, ‘तस्मात् तेजोमयं पित्तं पित्तोष्मा यः स पक्तिमान्। स कायाग्निः स कायोष्मा स पक्ता स च जीवनः'-इति। पित्तैकदेशत्वात्तेजसि पित्तोपचारमाश्रित्य सुश्रतेनोक्तम्-'न पाकः पित्तादृते’–इति, तथा-‘न खलु पित्तव्यतिरेकेणान्योऽग्निः’–इति। एवमन्यदप्यग्नेरभेदसाधकं वचनं समाधेयम्। ननु, यदि तीक्ष्णः पित्तेनेत्युक्तम, तत् कथं पित्तेनैवाग्नेः प्रशमनमभिधीयते। यदुक्तंचरके–‘कट्वजीर्णविदाह्यम्लक्षाराद्चैः पित्तमुल्बणम्। आप्लावयद्वन्यनलं जलं तप्तमिवानलम्’ (च.चि.१५) इति उच्यते, यदा कटुकेन रूक्षोष्णेन पित्तं वुद्ध भवति, तदा तेजोभागरूपायाः पित्तस्यावस्थाया उल्वणत्वात्तीक्ष्णः पित्तेनेति सङ्गतं; यदाऽम्ललवणेन स्निग्धोष्णोन कफानुगमनभाजा वृद्ध पित्तं तदा पित्तस्य द्रवावस्थाया उद्रिक्तत्वान्निर्वापमग्नेरुक्तमिति। जतुकर्णेऽप्युक्तं–‘कुपितेन वायुना दीपस्येवाग्रेर्निर्वापणं, पित्तेनोष्णजलवत्, कफेनाम्बुवत्’ इति। ततश्च युक्तमग्नेः पुथगुपादानमिति। अग्निश्च पित्तगतत्वेन क्रोधकृतो भवत्येव, क्रोधेन पित्तकोपातु; शोकश्रमाभ्यां तु जनितवातेन शरीरोष्मणोऽपि विक्षेपणाच्छिरोगतत्वं, तेनानिलोऽपि लभ्यते, पित्तं च साक्षाद्पात्तं, चकारेण श्लेष्माऽपि केशशुक्लताकरो गृह्यते। एतेन दोषत्रयसहितशरीरोष्मा पलितहेतुरिति वाक्यार्थंश्वरकोक्तार्थेन सह संवादी भवति। यदाह-'तेजोऽनिलाद्यैः सह केशभूमिं दग्धवा तु कुर्यात् खलितिं नरस्य। किंचित्तु दग्ध्वा पलितानि कुर्याद्धरित्प्रभत्वं च शिरोरुहाणाम्’ (च.चि.२) इति। एतच्चाकालजपलितव्यापकं लक्षणम्। कालजे तु क्रोधादिग्रहणं कारणान्तरोपलक्षणं, तेन वयःपरिणामकृतश्रोष्मा दोषत्रययुक्तः कालजपलितहेतुः । अन्यथा कालजपलितस्य संग्रहो न स्यात्। किंवा कालजं स्वाभाविकत्वादेव नोच्यते। अन्ये तु पित्तगतश्चेच्छरीरोष्मा तत् किमुभयोरुपादाने- नेत्यभिधाय शरीरोष्मा पित्तं चेति कर्तुद्वयमाचक्षते; तेन नात्रैकस्मिन् विषये समुच्चयः, किं तर्हि विषयभेदात्। र्कतृद्वयं-तत्र शरीरोष्मा वैकृतं पलितं करोति, पित्तं च प्राकृतं पित्तप्रकृतेः पलितं करोति। यदुक्तं- पित्तप्रकृतिरकालजवलीपलितयुक्तश्च भवति' इति। एवं स्वाभाविकजरापलितमपि पित्तेनैवास्य हेतोः क्लूपत्वात् । न चोष्मकृतत्वेन पलितस्यादोषजत्व प्रसङ्गः, ऊष्मणः पित्तधर्मत्वेन पित्तेऽन्तर्भावात्॥ ३२॥ शाल्मलीकण्टकप्रख्याः कफमारुतरक्तजाः । युवानपिडका यूनां विज्ञेया मुखदूषिकाः ॥ ३३ ॥ ( सु.नि. १३)
answer_text: Sarīroṣma means the heat of the body. By saying “pittam ca”-pitta also - it means that pitta also which gets into the head, is a causative factor for greying of the hair. Pitta is considered as agni and is responsible for heating/boiling/baking/ripening, also as per the statements “without pitta there is no boiling”. (Su. Su. 17) and pitta is the heat factor that bakes/boils" (Su. Su. 21). Susruta only emphasizes, “Other than pitta there is no heat factor and due to this fiery pitta burning, boiling, craking etc., heating like procedures are taking place inside the body due to antaragni” the internal heat. When this function is dimnished, drugs are used to increase it - which have same qualities as that of pitta; and when it is increased, cold therapy is administered. Due to these experiences and also as per the verbal testimony of the seers, it is confirmed that - "there is no other heat factor other than pitta". (Su. Su. 21). Carak also said, "Visual perception, digestive heat, hunger, thirst, smoothness of the body, lustre, glow and intellect are the functions of un¬ disturbed pitta”. (Ca.Sù.18). Since there is nothing else that helps in pāka (boiling/ baking), agni should be taken as pitta. Also when agni is diminished, the pitta promoting drugs like marica (black pepper) are used to increase it and when it is increased, the anti-pitta drugs-like sweet tasted ones are adiminstered to bring it down. If agni is different from pitta, it should not have positively reacted to the Mādhavanidānaṃ accumulation and diminishing of pitta. In the domain of sun planet, the ice will not sustain and in other places the sun will not have effect on the ice. Which ever is different will be the cause of difference, as in the case of ocean and the ajagara, the big serpent. It is not so in the case of pitta and agni. Then how can one establish that agni and pitta are different from each other? It is said this juncture, that the antaragni (the internal fire) is not different from pitta. Also there are many epistemalogical evidences available to differentiate these two. In the referances, “Samadosa Samagnisca......” (Su. Su. 15) (equilibrium of dosa and equilibrium of agni) and “Sama prakopau doṣaṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ agni saṃśrayau” (The equilibrium and aggravation of dosas are always based on the state of agni). When the word dosa that includes pitta which is not different from agni, seperate mentioning of agni is not proper. This does not appear proper because tiksanatva (fastness) is part of pitta. Again, saying that there is no other agni other than pitta indicates the difference of these two factors only. Because the equality has been mentioned. When there is no difference, there need not be a seperate mentioning of quality. Even though mentioning that agni increases and decreases as and when pitta increases and decreases, it is useless because the same argument establishes the difference in these two; as in the case of - sukra (semen) responding positively to the growth and diminishing of kapha; but this will not establish oneness of kapha and sukra (semen). Also ghṛta is said to be palliative of pitta and promoter of agni; when pitta is accumulated there is no increase in agni; peya (gruel) etc, are said to increase the agni and not the pitta; because of such instances, autaragni is considered different from pitta. Agni is the fiery part (tejas), pitta which is constituted by drava (liquid), Tejas (fiery part) and not like the burning fire which is seen out side. The sub¬ stance is always different from its contents as the body is different from hands and legs. They are not taken as totally different because of the continuous co-existance. The fiery part of pitta alone is pavaka (agni) (pacaka, as per different text which means the digesting factor). Bhoja says, "Fortified by concerned rasa (taste), virya (potency) (of the foods and drugs induced) and kindled by samāna and vyāna, the warmth of pitta is responsible for baking/digesting. Therefore pitta is full of teja (the fiery part), that alone is the baking factor, it is called Kayagni (the internal digestive fire in the body), Kayosma (the heat of the body), Pakta (the digestive factor) and is Jivana (responsible for sustainance of life)." Susruta in view of the tejas being an integral part of pitta says, there is no paka (boiling/heating/digestion) without pitta.” and “There is no other agni factor without pitta; ” when Tikṣṇa (fastness) is due to pitta, how come the palliation of agni takes place by pitta by more intake of kaṭu (pungent), ajirṇa (improperly cooked or half cooked), vidāhi (over Kṣudraroga Nidāna burnt), amla (sour) kṣāra (alkaline) etc., foods. It drenches the agni (internal fire/ digestive fire) causing it to get extinguished - as the hot water extinguishes the out side fire." (Ca.Ci.15). It is said that - when pitta increases by the intake of kapu (pungent), ruksa (dry) and uṣṇa (warm) factors, then the fiery part (teja) is also increased leading to growth of agni (the internal fire). And when it (pitta) increases by intake of salt, smooth and warm foods that also increases kapha, the watery part of pitta is in¬ creased which extinguishes the internal fire. It is also said in jatūkarṇa that the agni is extinguished by aggravated vāta as the lamp due to wind; by aggravated pitta, it happens (extinguishing of agni)as the hot water does to the fire and by aggravated kapha, as the normal water does to the fire. Hence it is proper to say that pitta is different from agni. Due to anger, agni increases by increase in pitta. The bodily heat reaches to the head due to the vāta that is generated by śoka (grief) and śrama (strain).This is how the role of vata in greying of hair is postulated; pitta is directly involved; by using the word ca-slesma also is included here as there is whitening of the hair. Thus the bodily heat alongwith tridosas is the reason for greying of the hair. This supports the statement of Caraka. He said, “ Teja (heat) alongwith vāta etc., three dosas destroys (burns) the scalp and causes baldness and by destroying (burning) to a little extent, causes greying of hair destroying the lustre of the hair" (Ca. Ci. 2). This is applicable to untimely greying of the hair. As far as timely greying is considered, krodha (anger) etc., are subsidiary causative factors; the body heat that accumulates due to ageing alongwith three dosas is the case for greying in old age; otherwise there would not be greying of hair in old age; timely greying would not be told as naturally occuring. According to others, if bodily heat is a part of pitta, why these two are seperately named as causative factors, which do not give conclu¬ sion in either of the cases? Because the role is different. The two causative factors¬ bodily heat which is vitiated causes (untimely) greying of hair and pitta in natural state causes greying of hair in pitta natured (pitta prakṛti) individuals. It is said that the pitta-prakṛti individuals have untiṁely greying of hair. In the same way in the timely greying of hair also, pitta is the causative factor. The bodily heat-originated greying is also not devoid of pitta, as that heat is also a part of pitta. 32. Yuvāna piḍakā The papules that arise on the face of the youth, caused by kapha, vata and Mādhavanidānaṃ rakta, that look like the thorns on the trunk of Śalmaū (Bombax malabaricum) tree which deface the face are called yuvāna piḍaka (pimples) 33. (Su. Ni. 13)

context: मधुकोशः पलितमाह–क्रोधेत्यादि। श्ररीरोष्मेति देहाग्निः। पित्तं चेति पित्तमपि श्रिरोगतं पलितहेतुः। ननु, पित्तमेवाग्निः, तव्र तत्र पित्तस्य पाचकत्वेनाभिधानात्; यदुक्तवान् सुश्रुतः-‘न पाकः पित्तादृते’ (स.सू. १७) इति, तथा-‘पित्ते तस्मिन् पाचकोऽग्निरिति संज्ञा' (सु.सू. २१) इति; तथा स एव-‘न खलु पित्तव्यातिरेकेणान्योऽग्निरुप- लभ्यते,आग्नेये तु पित्ते दहनपचनदारणादिष्वभिवर्तमानेऽग्निवदुपचारः क्रियते अन्तरग्निरिति, क्षीणे ह्यग्निगुणे तत्समानद्रव्योपयोगगदतिवुद्दे शीतक्रियोपयोगादागमाच्च पश्यामः न खलू पित्तव्यतिरेकेणान्योऽग्रिः' (सु.सू. २१) इति; चरकाचार्योऽप्याह-‘दर्शनं पक्तिरूष्मा च क्षुत्तृष्णा देहमार्दवम्। प्रभाप्रसादौ मेधा च पित्तकर्माविकारजम्’ च.सू. १८) इति; पाकस्यान्यथानुपपत्त्या चाग्नेरङ्गीकारः; किंच मन्देऽग्नौ पित्तकरमरीचादिद्रव्योपयोगादग्नेर्वेद्धिः, पित्तप्रतिकूल-शीतमधुरादिद्रव्योपयोगाश्चोपशम उपलभ्यते; यदि हि पित्ताद्विन्नोऽग्निः स्यात्तदा पित्तस्य वृद्धिहासानुविधानमस्यानुपपन्नं स्यात्, न हि तुहिनकरमण्डले हिमभाज्यहिमोपलम्भः, अतुहिनमण्डले अहिमभाजि भगवति भास्करेऽभिमतो हिमोपलम्भः, यद्यतो भिन्नं तत्ततो भेदेनोपलभ्यते, यथा सागरादजगरः, न चैवं पित्तादग्निः, तत्कुतः पित्तादग्नेः पृथगुपादानमिति? अत्र प्रत्यभिधीयते-न तावदन्तरग्निः पित्तादभिन्नः भेदेसाधकप्रमाणस्य भूयः सद्दावात्; तथाह्यभेदे ‘समदोषः समाग्निश्च,’ ( सु.सू. १५) इत्यत्र, ‘समप्रकोपौ दोषाणां सर्वेषामग्निसंश्रयौ’ इत्यत्र च दोषपदलब्धत्वादग्नेः पृथगुपादानमसङ्गतं; तीक्ष्णः पित्तेन चेति स्वात्मनि क्रियाविरोधादसङ्गतं; 'यत्युनः 'न 'खलु' पित्तव्यतिरेकेणान्योऽग्निः' इत्याद्युक्तः 'तद्भेदमेव' साधयति, उपचाराभिधानात्, न ह्यभेदे उपचारः संभवति। यदप्यग्नेः पित्तवृद्धिहासानुविधानमभिहितं तदप्रयोजकं, भेदेऽपि समानत्वेन तदुपपत्तेः । यथा कफवृद्धिहासकरसौम्याग्नेयद्रव्याभ्यां शुक्रस्य वृद्धिहासौ दृष्टौ, न च कफशुक्रयोरैक्यं; किंच घृतं पित्तशमनमग्नेश्व दीपनं, पितस्य सञ्चयादौ नाग्नेर्वृद्धिः, पेयादिकं चाग्निकरं, न पित्तकृत्; ततश्व पित्ताद्विलक्षणोऽन्तरग्निः । स च द्रवतेजःसमुदायात्मकस्य पित्तस्य तेजोभागो न बहिरनलवद्दस्माङ्गाराकारः, समुदायतश्च समुदायी अन्य एव करचरणादिभ्य इव शरीर; अत्यन्तभेदेन चाग्रहणं, तस्य नित्यसंश्लेष्णशालित्वात्। पित्तस्य तेजोंऽश एव पाच(व)कः, तदाह भोजः-'दृढमुष्णोचितं ह्येतत् पित्तोष्मा पचतीति यत्। मूर्च्छितो रसवीर्याभ्यां समानव्यानसंहितः’-इत्यारभ्य, ‘तस्मात् तेजोमयं पित्तं पित्तोष्मा यः स पक्तिमान्। स कायाग्निः स कायोष्मा स पक्ता स च जीवनः'-इति। पित्तैकदेशत्वात्तेजसि पित्तोपचारमाश्रित्य सुश्रतेनोक्तम्-'न पाकः पित्तादृते’–इति, तथा-‘न खलु पित्तव्यतिरेकेणान्योऽग्निः’–इति। एवमन्यदप्यग्नेरभेदसाधकं वचनं समाधेयम्। ननु, यदि तीक्ष्णः पित्तेनेत्युक्तम, तत् कथं पित्तेनैवाग्नेः प्रशमनमभिधीयते। यदुक्तंचरके–‘कट्वजीर्णविदाह्यम्लक्षाराद्चैः पित्तमुल्बणम्। आप्लावयद्वन्यनलं जलं तप्तमिवानलम्’ (च.चि.१५) इति उच्यते, यदा कटुकेन रूक्षोष्णेन पित्तं वुद्ध भवति, तदा तेजोभागरूपायाः पित्तस्यावस्थाया उल्वणत्वात्तीक्ष्णः पित्तेनेति सङ्गतं; यदाऽम्ललवणेन स्निग्धोष्णोन कफानुगमनभाजा वृद्ध पित्तं तदा पित्तस्य द्रवावस्थाया उद्रिक्तत्वान्निर्वापमग्नेरुक्तमिति। जतुकर्णेऽप्युक्तं–‘कुपितेन वायुना दीपस्येवाग्रेर्निर्वापणं, पित्तेनोष्णजलवत्, कफेनाम्बुवत्’ इति। ततश्च युक्तमग्नेः पुथगुपादानमिति। अग्निश्च पित्तगतत्वेन क्रोधकृतो भवत्येव, क्रोधेन पित्तकोपातु; शोकश्रमाभ्यां तु जनितवातेन शरीरोष्मणोऽपि विक्षेपणाच्छिरोगतत्वं, तेनानिलोऽपि लभ्यते, पित्तं च साक्षाद्पात्तं, चकारेण श्लेष्माऽपि केशशुक्लताकरो गृह्यते। एतेन दोषत्रयसहितशरीरोष्मा पलितहेतुरिति वाक्यार्थंश्वरकोक्तार्थेन सह संवादी भवति। यदाह-'तेजोऽनिलाद्यैः सह केशभूमिं दग्धवा तु कुर्यात् खलितिं नरस्य। किंचित्तु दग्ध्वा पलितानि कुर्याद्धरित्प्रभत्वं च शिरोरुहाणाम्’ (च.चि.२) इति। एतच्चाकालजपलितव्यापकं लक्षणम्। कालजे तु क्रोधादिग्रहणं कारणान्तरोपलक्षणं, तेन वयःपरिणामकृतश्रोष्मा दोषत्रययुक्तः कालजपलितहेतुः । अन्यथा कालजपलितस्य संग्रहो न स्यात्। किंवा कालजं स्वाभाविकत्वादेव नोच्यते। अन्ये तु पित्तगतश्चेच्छरीरोष्मा तत् किमुभयोरुपादाने- नेत्यभिधाय शरीरोष्मा पित्तं चेति कर्तुद्वयमाचक्षते; तेन नात्रैकस्मिन् विषये समुच्चयः, किं तर्हि विषयभेदात्। र्कतृद्वयं-तत्र शरीरोष्मा वैकृतं पलितं करोति, पित्तं च प्राकृतं पित्तप्रकृतेः पलितं करोति। यदुक्तं- पित्तप्रकृतिरकालजवलीपलितयुक्तश्च भवति' इति। एवं स्वाभाविकजरापलितमपि पित्तेनैवास्य हेतोः क्लूपत्वात् । न चोष्मकृतत्वेन पलितस्यादोषजत्व प्रसङ्गः, ऊष्मणः पित्तधर्मत्वेन पित्तेऽन्तर्भावात्॥ ३२॥ शाल्मलीकण्टकप्रख्याः कफमारुतरक्तजाः । युवानपिडका यूनां विज्ञेया मुखदूषिकाः ॥ ३३ ॥ ( सु.नि. १३)

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 10):

शोकशोषिणो लक्षणमाहप्रध्यानेत्यादिना । शोकशोष्यपि तादृश इति शुक्रस्य क्षयलक्षणव्यतिरिक्तेन शुक्रशोषलिङ्गेन युक्तः यदुक्तं सुश्रुतेविना शुक्रक्षयकृतैर्विकारै- रुपलक्षितः सु०उ० इति मन्दवीर्य-बुन्द्वि-बलेन्द्रियः ॥१ ॥ जराशोषी है। कृशो भिन्नकांस्यपात्रहतस्वरः । कम्पनोऽरुचिमान् श्लेष्मणा के हीने के गौरवारतिपीडितः ॥ ॥ ष्ठीवति का प सम्प्रस्वुतास्य-नासाक्षिः शृष्क-रूक्ष-मल-च्छविः । वार्धक्यशोषिणो लक्षणमाहजरेत्यादि। कम्पनः कम्पयुक्तः । भिन्नस्य स्फुटितस्य कांस्यपात्रस्य हतस्य दण्डादिनेव स्वरो यस्य स तथा । ष्ठीवति श्लेष्मणा हीनमिति श्लेष्महरणाय यले कृतेऽपि न श्लेष्मनिःसरणम् । शुष्क-रूक्ष-मल-च्छविरिति शुष्क-रूक्षे यथाक्रमं मल- च्छवी यस्य स तथा - अध्वशोषी संचार स्वस्ताङ्गः सम्भृष्टपरुषच्छविः ॥१ ॥ प्रसुप्तगात्रावयवः अध्वशोषिणो लक्षणमाहअध्वेत्यादि । सम्भृष्टस्येव भर्जितस्येव छविः वर्णो यस्य स तथा । प्रसुप्तः स्पर्शानभिज्ञः । क्लोम पिपासास्थान हदये क्लोमस्थाने ताल्विति पाठान्तरम् व्यायामशोषी का भूयिष्ठमेभिरेव का समन्वितः । लिईकरःक्षतकृतैः - संयाकृष्ट - संक्षतंत्र - विना - - - - - - -
answer_text: The passage in context describes the symptoms of the patients suffer- ing from the consumption caused by grief. It could be noted that the symptoms reflected in this case are similar to those symptoms mani¬ festing in case of consumption due to excessive intercourse. The only difference between the symptoms of the two diseases is the fact that there is loss of semen in case of the former due to excessive inter- course while there is no loss of semen in case of consumption due to grief as suggested also by Suśruta (SS. Ut. 41.18). Consumption caused by senility (SS. Ut. 41.19, 20) The old age patients suffering from consumption manifest the fol- lowing symptoms: emaciation, low-potency, mental dullness, re- duced strength, and tremor. Such patients develop anorexia; their voice appears as if it is coming out of a broken bronze vessel. The patients spit small amounts of phlegm, suffer from heaviness, insta¬ bility, have exudation from mouth, nose, eyes, and they develop a dry, rough and pale complexion. 16-17 This passage defines the symptoms of the consumption with old age syndromes. The term kampana suggests that the patient regularly trembles. He passes the voice that is similar to the sound appearing out of a broken vessel. He spits without kapha content in it. Even after making efforts, he is unable to cough out the phlegm. He has a pale, dry, and deserted look. (SS. Ut. 41.21) Patients wasted due to constant and long distance walking manifest the following symptoms: weakness, hardness, and loss of sensation in body parts, dryness of kloma, throat and mouth. 18 The individual suffering from consumption caused by excessive walking has a shrunken body, complexion of over burnt and harsh nature. He suffers from numbness in the body and limbs and has dryness in the kloma (spleen), throat, and mouth (SS. Ut. 41). Note: The kloma has been defined by Caraka (CS, Vi, 5, 7) as well as by Suśruta (SS. Sā, 9. 12). Kloma is the seat of thirst that exists around the heart. In some texts, this term has been replaced by Talu that means, ‘palate’. That is again considered as the seat of thirst by Caraka (CS. Vi. 5.7). Consumption caused by strenuous exercise (SS. Ut. 41.22) Persons wasted due to excess physical exertion manifest the same symptoms as above. Moreover, he would also reflect features of injury to the chest without a lesion. 19
chapter_title: Rājayakṣmā, Kṣatakṣīṇa Nidānam – Diagnosis of Tuberculosis
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 10.

answer_text: The passage starting from arocaka refers to the peculiar characteris¬ tics of the āgantuja variety of the diseasc. As suggested by Suśruta, when śleṣmā gets vidagdha or over-burnt, its taste turns out to be very salty while pitta remains sour (SS. Su. 40.10). Vibaddha or hin¬ drance is the inability to swallow food; the term sambaddha con¬ notes association of kapha. The term ahrdyagandha refers to an unpleasant smell that irritates the nostrils. Natural taste is the simple, uncontaminated taste, quite unlike the case of vāta affliction where an astringent-like taste is felt. Agantu type of arocaka If the arocaka has developed due to such external factors such as grief, fear, greed, anger and other mental affections or it has devel- oped due to intake of bad food or repulsive smell, the patient will have a natural taste in mouth. Still, he would have an aversion to ood

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 26):

कट्वम्ल-सौवीर-सुराविकारैः प्रकुप्याशुर्म करोति कर्शुलम् । ग्राम्यातियोगादशनैर्विदग्धैः पित्तं संस्वेद-मूर्च्छा-भ्रम-चोषयुक्तम् ॥7॥ तृण्मोह-दाहार्तिकरं कुप्यति – चार्धरात्रे – विदाहकाले – जल्दात्यये – चे । मध्यन्दिने शीते – चार शीतेः – समुपैति – शान्ति – सुस्वादुशीतेरपि – भोजनैश्व ॥৪॥
answer_text: The above passage starting from the term vyayam, etc. indicates features of the vālaja variety of āmavāla. It may be noted that as vāta is vitiated due to excessive bodily exercises, the śūla is also produced by such exercises. This principle should also be applied in cases of pittaja and kaphaja varieties of śūla. However, apart from this supplement, the passage of commentary in context does not advance upon the presentation or argument of the original text. It simply explains the verbatim treatment of the MN passage we have already translated. Thus, for the English readers the commentary is not very useful. Pitta type of śūla The following things promote pitta and generate colic: 1. Over- indulgence in eatables that are alkaline, heat-producing, very warm; 2. Taking items that cause burning sensation during digestion; 3. Taking oils, cow-pea, oil cake, soup of horse gram; the eatables that are pungent and sour, fermented beverages like sauvīra, surā. The disease has been also seen as being produced through anger, exposure to fire, fatigue, and prolonged exposure to warm sun; sexual intercourse and irritating eatables. It is relieved during the cold season, by the use of cold objects as well as by eating delicious sweet and cold food. Thirst, delusion, burning sensation near the umbilicus, perspiration, fainting, giddiness, and localized burning sensation are some of the symptoms of the disease. Pain exacerbates during midday or midnight, during digestion of eatables and in rainy weather; it is reduced by cold comforts, cold and sweet eatables and drinks. 6-8
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 26.

Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 407):

तालमूली तु विद्वव्विर्मुशली परिकीर्त्तिता । मुशली मधुरा वृष्या वीर्योष्णा बृंहणी गुरुः । तिक्ता रसायनी हन्ति गुदजान्यनिलं तथा ।।१८३।।
answer_text: The root powder is Mrudu Virecaka (Mild purgative) useful in Vibanda (Constipation) and Stanyajanana (Galactogogue). It is useful to treat Yakṛṭplīhāvriddi (Enlargement of Liver and Spleen). In spermatorrhoea (Involuntary discharge of semen without orgasm), the extracte root is taken with jīraka and Sita. Mātrā (Dosage): Mula cūrna: 3-6 gm. RSNA MUŚALĪ Latin: Curculigo orchioides. Gaert'n. Fam: Amaryllidaceae in: Musalikand in Eng: Black Musale, Black Musalie Most scholars have an opinion that ‘Tālamūli’ is known as Musali. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): It is Madhura rasa (Sweet in taste), acts as Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac), Uṣṇavīrya (Hot in potency), Bṛhmaṇa (Stoutning), Guru vipaka (Madhura in post digestive), Tikta rasa (Bitter in taste) and Rasāyana (Rejuvenator). It cures Arśas (Piles) and Diseases of Vāta. Note: The genuine source of a Musali as per Bhāvamiśra is Curculigo orchioides Gaertn, popularly used as Krsna musalī. As per Ayurvedic classics mention two varieties of Muśalī viz. a. Kṛṣṇā muśalī Curculigo orchioides Gaerttu (Amaryllidaceae) b. Two plants are recognized as Sveta muśalī Asparagus adscendens Roxb (Liliaceae) and Chorophytum arundinaceum Baker. The word Musalī alone denotes the white variety, which is commonly used. Despite the fact that the black variety is supposed to be superior in properties, both the varities have pretty much comparable properties and utilized clinically. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It grows in moist and rich soil. Assam, Bihar, Bengal, Kumaon eastwards, ascending up to Khasi hills. Swarūpa (Botanical description): A small herb with tuberous root stock up to 30 cm high. Leaves are sessile sheathing bases, 15-45×1.2-2.5 cm. across, linear or linearlanceolate, glabrous or sparsely softly hairy. Flowers are bisexual, arranged in axillary racemes, bright yellow in colour.Fruit- capsule 1.5-2cm. long and 8mm. broad consist of 1-4 black, oblong, seeds. Prayojya anga (Part used): Kandha (Tubers). Chemical constituents: Mucilage, Alkaloid (Lycorine), Glycosides, Saponins, Fatty acids, Tannins, Resin, Potassium, Copper, Calcium
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 407
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 407.

शीतमारुतसंस्पर्शात्रदुष्टौ कफमारुतौ। पित्तेन सह सम्भूय बहिरन्तर्विसर्पतः॥ १॥ मधुकोशः त्वग्दुष्टिदोषत्रयजन्यत्वसामान्यात् कुष्ठानन्तरं शीतपित्तोदर्दादिनिदानम्। तस्य दोषत्रयजन्यत्वमाह- शीतमारुतसंस्पर्शादित्यादि। पित्तेन सह संभूयेति स्वहेतूपचितेन पित्तेन संभूय मिलित्वा। बहिरन्तरिति बहिस्त्वचि, अन्तः शोणितादौ, विसर्पतः प्रसरतः ॥ १ ॥ पिपासाऽरुचिह्न मधुकोशः पूर्वरूपमाह-पिपासेत्यादि। रक्तलोचनता प्रभावात्। पूर्वरूपस्य लक्षणमिति पूर्वरूपस्य स्वरूपमित्यर्थः; न तु लक्षणमंत्र लिङ्गं, पिपासादिव्यतिरिक्तस्य पूर्व रूपस्याभावात् ॥ २ ॥ वरटीदष्टसंस्थानः शोथः संजायते बहिः । सकण्डूस्तोदबहुलश्छर्दिज्वरविदाहवान्॥ ३॥ उदर्दमिति तं विद्याच्छीतपित्तमधापरे। वाताधिकं शीतपित्तमुदर्दस्तु कफाधिकः ॥ ४॥ मधुकोशः उदर्दलक्षणमाह-वरटीत्यादि। सकण्डूस्तोदबहुलश्छर्दिंज्वरविदाहवानिति अत्र कण्डूः कफात् तोदो वातातु, छर्दिच्चरविदाहः पित्तादिति दोषत्रयलिङ्गम्। अनयोः शीतपित्तोदर्दयोः समानसंस्थानत्वेऽपि वाताधिकं शीतपित्तं, कफाधिक उदर्दः॥ ३–४॥ सोत्सङ्गैश्च सरागैश्च कण्डूमद्भिश्च मण्डलैः। शैशिरः कफजो व्याधिरुदर्द इति कीर्तितः॥५॥ मधुकोशः उदर्दस्य धर्मान्तरमाह-सोत्सङ्गैरित्यादि। उत्सङ्गैर्मध्यनिप्नैः शैशिर इति शिशिरसंभवः। असम्यग्वमनोदीर्णपित्तश्लेष्मान्ननिग्रहैः। मण्डलानि सकण्डूनि रागवन्ति बहूनि च। उत्कोठः सानुबन्धश्च कोठ इत्यभिधीयते ॥ ६ ॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने श्रीतपित्तोदर्दकोठनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ५०॥ मधुकोशः त्वग्दुष्टिसाम्यादत्रैव कोठोऽभिधीयते-असम्यग्वमनेत्यादि। असम्यक्त्वं वमनस्यायोगमिथ्यायोगादिना, तथोदीर्णानां पित्तश्लेष्मान्नानां निग्रहो वेगविधारणं, तैर्मण्डलानि जायन्ते, स कोठः; अथवाऽयमर्थः-असम्यग्व- मनोदीर्णों पित्तश्लेष्माणों, तथाऽन्ननग्रह उपस्थितवेगस्यान्नस्य निग्रहश्छर्दिनिग्रह इति यावत्, तैर्देतुभिर्भवन्ति। वमनस्य चासम्यक्तवमयोगमिथ्यायोगाभ्यां ज्ञेयम् अतियोगस्य तु पित्तश्लेष्मकोठाकरत्वात् । एतेन हेतुलक्षणभेदाद्विन्नः कोठ उदर्दात्। कोठो निरनुबन्धः। तथा चोक्तं,-'क्षणिकोत्यादविनाशः कोठ इति निगद्यते तप्जैः’ इति। सानुबन्ध उत्कोठोऽभिधीयते। सानुबन्धता च पुनः पुनर्भवनेन॥ ६॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायां शीतपित्तोदर्दकोठनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ५०॥
answer_text: Due to continuous contact of cold winds, the kapha and vāyu get vitiated in the body and in association with pitta, spread inside and out side the body 1. Due to the similarity in vitiation of skin with three dosas, Sitapitta etc. are being explained after kuştha. The exposure to cold winds in given here as a causative factor. Pittena saha sambhūya means - gets mixed up with pitta which is increased because of its own reasons. Bahirantar - means bahi - outer side of the skin (on the skin), antaḥ in raktā etc., visarpataḥ spreading. Pūrvarūpa (pre-monitory symptoms). Thirst, distaste, nausea, tiredness of the body, heaviness in the limbs and redness in the eyes are the premonitory symptoms of the above diseases. 2. Reddening of the eyes is the specific effect (prabhāva) of the disease. Pūrvarūpasya lakṣaṇam means the feature of promonitory symptoms. The word lakṣaṇa should not be taken as symptomatology here because the pipāsa (thirst) etc., are told as only pūrvarupa (premonitory symptoms). 2 Symptomatology of Udarda and Śītapitta Mādhavanidānaṃ The patches look like those caused by sting of the wasp; there will be upward inflammation associated with itching, pinning sensation, vomitting, fever and burning sensation in udarda. The other one (with same features) is called Sitapitta. Sītapitta is vāta dominated while udarda is of kapha predominance. 3, 4. Kandu (itching) is due to kapha; Toda (pinning sensation), due to vāta and chardi (vomiting), Jvara (fever) and vidāha (severe burning sensation) are due to pitta; Thus the features of three dosa s are seen in this disease. Though the featrues of Sitapitta and udarda are similar to each other, there is more predominance of vata in sitapitta while udarda is dominated by kapha. Another feature of udarda The kapha dominant disease occuring in sisira rtu (winter), charecterised by urticarial patches that are elevated, reddish in colour and associated with itching sensation is called udarda. 5. Utsanga - elevated - implies having depression in the centre; saisira means occuring in śiśiraṛtu (winter season). 5. Aetiology and symptomatology of Kotha (Skin allergy) Due to incomplete or improper emesis and also by suppressing the vomitting of pitta, ślesma and food stuff, there arise plenty of patches with itching and redness in colour which is called kotha. The same, if occurs repeatedly, is called utkotha. 6. Thus ends the diagnosis of Sītapitta, udarda and koṭha in the Mādhava’s book on diagnosis written by Śrīmādhavakara. 50. Sītapitta Udarda Koṭha Nidāna Due to the similarity of vitiation of skin, kotha is also explained here. Asamyak vamana means the therapy of emesis not being carried out perfectly i.e., resulting in over emesis or insufficient emission etc., also suppression of nausea in which pitta and Slesma and food stuff which are ready for expulsion but are not vomitted out. This amounts to suppression of the natural bout of emesis; which ever skin¬ rashes occur due to above reasons, are called kotha. Otherwise it can be understood in this manner - emission of pitta and slesma which are not prepared for expulsion and suppresion of the vomitting of food stuffs cause kotha. Improper emesis should mean here as having no bout of vomitting are having irregular vomitting because over emesis of pitta and slesma does not cause kotha. Due to this difference in aetiology and symptomatogy, koṭha is different from udarda. Koṭha is not having continuity. As also mentioned “momentary occurance and getting cleared by itself immediataly - is the cardinal feature of kotha, according to specialists”. Sāmbandha, that which has continuity is called utkoṭha.The continuity is due to repeated occurance. 6. Thus ends the diagnosis of Sitapitta (urticaria), udarda (rashes) and kotha (skin allergy) in the Madhukośa commentary written by Śrīkanḍhātta. 50. ＊＊＊＊ 11 M.N. Pt-II
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 50.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 313):

शुक्ल एरण्ड आमण्डश्चित्रो गन्धर्वहस्तकः । पञ्चाङ्गलो वर्द्धमानो दीर्घदण्डो व्यडम्बकः ।।६०।। वातारिस्तरुणश्चापि रुबूकश्च निगद्यते । रक्तोऽपरो रुबूकः स्यादुरुबूको रुबुस्तथा ।।१६१।। व्याप्रपुच्छश्च वातरिश्चञ्चरुत्तानपत्रकः । एरण्डयुग्मं मधुरम्भष्णं गुरु विनाशयेत् ।।६१।। शूलशोथकटीबस्तिशिरःपीडोदरज्वरान् एरण्डपत्रं वातघ्नं कफक्रिमिविनाशनम् । मूत्रकृच्छ्हरं चापि पित्तरक्तप्रकोपणम् । वातार्यप्रदलं गुल्मबस्तिश्रूलहरं परम् ।।६४।। कफवातकृमीन्हन्ति वृद्धिं सप्तविधामपि । एरण्डफलमत्युव्णं गुल्मशूलानिलापहम् ।।६५।। यकृत्प्लीहोदराशोंघन कटुक दीपन परम् । तद्वन्मज्जा च विडभेदी वातश्लेष्मोदरापहः ।। ६ ६ । ।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Vatadi Varga, Chapter 5, verse 587):

कुत्सितः शाल्मलिः प्रोक्तो रोचनः कुटशाल्मलिः । कुटशाल्मलिकस्तिक्तः कटुकः कफवातनुत् ।।५८।। भेद्युष्णः प्लीहजङ्गरयकृद्गुल्मविषापहः । भूतानाहविबन्यास्रमेदःशूलकफापहः ।।५९।।
answer_text: Digestive disease: In case of Pravāhikā (Dysentery) a decoction of Bilwa phala in aja kṣīrā is taken along with mocā rasa and kutaj seeds. Haemorrages: In case of Adhoga raktapitta (Rectal bleeding), Milk boiled with mocā rasa is efficacious. Mātrā (Dosage): 1-3gm. KUTAŚĀLAMALI Fam: Bombacaceae Latin: Ceiba pentandra (Linn.) Gaertn. Eng: True kapok tree Hin: Safed semal Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Kutsiṭaśālmali and Kūṭaśālmalika. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Kūṭaśālmalika is Tiktā (Bitter) and Kaṭu (Pungent) in taste, Subsides Kapha and Vāta, Bhedana (Purgative) and Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency). It cures Pliha roga (Diseases of Spleen), Udararoga (Abdominal diseases), Yakrt roga (Liver disorders), Gulma (Abdominal tumors), Viṣa (Posionous manifestations), Bhūtagrha (Evil spirits), Anāha (Flatulence), Vibanda (Constipation), Diseases of Rakta, Medoroga (Obesity) and Sūla (Abdominal colic). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Temprate regions of Western and Southern India, Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is medium to large tree can reach upto 9ft. Leaves are palmately compound, 5-9 leaflets are 7-8 cm long and 1-4 cm wide, lanceolateelliptical, petioles are longer than the leaflets. Flower are about 2.5 cm long, creamy white or pale pink in color, arranged in clusters at the end of the branches. Fruit- capsule, 10-30 cm long, tapering at both ends, dehiscent. Seeds round black, embedded in cottony hairs. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Bīja (Seeds), Niryasā (Gum), Twak (Bark). Chemical constituents: Rhamnose, glucuronic acid, garabinose, arabinose, xylose and galactose
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Vatadi Varga, Chapter 5, verse 587
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Vatadi Varga, Chapter 5, verse 587.

answer_text: Saṅgraha Grahaṇī is caused by Amavāta and has the following symptomatology sounds in the intestines, lassitude, weakness, weak digestive fire and defaecation in liquid form-cold in touch solid, some times-oily with pain in low back region- unformed stool abundant-sticky-with sounds and mild pain. This disease repeats once in 15 days, 30 days, 10 days or once in a day. This aggravates during day time and pacifies in nights. It is very difficult to diagnose this disease and also difficult for cure. This afflicts the individuals for a long time. The Grahaṇīroga in which the patient sleeps always, feels pain in the flanks and makes the sound of water pouring out of a pot while defaecating, is called Ghatiyantra Grahaṇī which is incurable. Prognosis of Grahanīroga The Sāma (undigested) and Nirāma (digested) (–unformed and formed in other words) stages of the Dosas which is mentioned in Atīsāra is applicable in Grahaniroga also. Same is the case regarding incurability
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana, Chapter 4, verse 19.

answer_text: Urinary diseasae: The fruit is Mūtrala (Diuretic), being effective remedy in Sotha (Inflammation) and Asmari (Renal calculi). Worm infestations: The extracted seed oil used in the treatment of Krmi (Worm infestations) especially Tapeworms and Roundworms. KHARBŪJĀ Latin: Cucumis mello Linn. Fam: Cucurbitaceae Hin: Kharbuj Eng: Melon, Musk melon 49 JA-413 Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): The synonyms of Kharbūjam is Daśāñgulam. Guna karma (Properties and indications): It is Mūtrala (Diuretic), Balya (Promotes strength), Koşṭśhuddhikar (cleanses the digestive tract), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Snigdha (Oilyness), Swādutara (Promote staste), Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac) and Subsides Pitta and Vāta. It's fruit are Madhura (Sweet), Amla (Sour), Kṣāra (Alkaline) in taste, causes Raktapitta (Haemorrages) and Mūtrakṛcchra (Dysuria). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Cultivated in all warm countries. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a postate annuals. Leaves 8-15 cm.long, 3-7 lobed, obtuse, sub-orbicular, dentate margins, cordate base and hirsute. Flowers are monocious, yellow, 1.5 -2 cm.long. Fruit round, 20 cm. long, greenish-yellow and longitudinally striped or mottled. Seeds long and flat. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Mūla (Roots), Phalā majja (Fruit pulp) Bīja (Seeds), Phalā twak (Fruit bark). Chemical constituents: Fruit contains ferulic, catteic and chlorogenic acids and Vit A, B1, B2 and C. Seeds contain an edible fixed oil, protein and essential amino acids
