question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 22):

अष्टीलामाहनाभेरित्यादि। अष्टीला उत्तरापथे वर्तुलः पाषाणविशेष इति जेज्जट- मतानुवादी कार्तिकः चर्मकाराणां वर्तुला दीर्घा लोहभाण्डीति गयदासः । ऊर्ध्वमायत उपरि- दीर्घः । उन्नतस्तिर्यगुन्नतः । वातकृता अष्ठीला वाताष्ठीलेति स्वरूपपरं व्यावृत्यभावात् । बहिर्मार्गावरोधिनीं वात-मूत्र-पुरीषावरोधिनीम् । एतामित्यादि सैव जठरे तिर्यगुत्थिता तिर्यगायता प्रत्यष्ठीलेति भेदः । वात-विण्मूत्ररोधिनीमिति विशेषपरम् ।। ।। मारुतेऽनुगुणे बस्तौ मूत्रं सम्यक् प्रवर्तते । विकारा विविधाश्चात्र प्रतिलोमे भवन्ति च ॥॥ अष्ठीलाव्यतिरिक्तमपि वातविकृतिं मूत्ररोधिनीमाहमारुत इत्यादि । अनुगुणेऽनुलोमे । प्रतिलोमे मारुत इति सम्बन्धः । विकारा अश्मरी-मूत्र-कृच्छादयः ।। वायुर्वेपथुसंज्ञकः । सर्वाडुकम्पः शिरसो वेपथुवातविकारमाह सर्वेत्यादि । शिरसः कम्प इति सम्बन्धः शिर इत्यवय- वोपलक्षणं तेन हस्तादेरपि कम्पो वेपथुरित्यर्थः ॥ मा०नि०-३१ खल्ली पाद-जङ्गोरु-करमूलावमोटनी ॥ ॥ - - -
answer_text: The passage starting from nābheh explains the characteristics of the disease named Vātāṣṭhīlā. The aṣṭhīlā is a round stone that is found in the northern countries (uttarāpatha) as defined by Kārtika, the fol- lower of Jejjaṭa. According to Gayadāsa, it is a long-round iron ves- sel. It is wide on the top and elevated on the sides. Along with hin¬ drance in passing stool and urine as present in Aşṭhīla, there is also hindrance in passing even the fart in condition of pratyasthila. Hindrance of urination due to disturbance of vāta When the vāta has its normal downward movement called anuloma, it makes for proper elimination of urine from the urinary bladder. However, it generates a painful disorder if it moves in the upward direction called pratiloma. 73 The above passage starting from the term Maruta etc., presents the symptoms of the different varieties of asthila and other complica¬ tions. These complications include the asmarī (stone) and mūtra¬ kṛcchṛa (disuria). However, the passage of commentary in context does not advance upon the presentation or argument of the original text. It simply explains the verbatim treatment of the MN passage we have already translated. Thus, for the English readers the commen¬ tary is not very useful. Kampavāta (Shaking palsy) Vepathu is that condition generated by vāta in which all the parts of the body including the head have tremors. The above passage starting from the term sarvānga etc., stresses the complications of trembling of head in the diseases vepathu and other complications. Khallīvāta (CS. Ci. S. 28.57) Khallī is the condition in which there could be distortions of the legs, ء calves, thighs, chest, and arms. 74

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 22):

पित्त-कफावृतानां प्राणादीनामधर्धश्लोकेन लिङ्गान्याह--प्राण इत्यादि । गात्रहर्षो रोमाञ्चः । दण्डको दण्डवत् स्तम्भः । परस्परं च प्राणादीनामावरणानि विंशतिर्भवन्ति । यदक्तं चरके मारुतानां हि पञ्चानामन्योन्यावरणे शृणु । चचि इत्यादि । एषां च लक्षणं चरक एव द्रष्टव्यम् । विदेहे चैक एव वायुः स्थानकर्मभेदात् पञ्चेत्याहुः संसर्गि- द्रव्यत्वेनैकाश्रये जलवत्पृथगवस्थानानुपपत्तेः । ईशानोऽप्याहयर्थैको देवदत्तः स्थानभेदात् गृहस्थो वानप्रस्थः कर्मभेदात् कुम्भकारो मालाकार इत्युच्यते तथा वायुरपीति ।। यदा तु धमनीः सर्वाः कुपितोऽभ्येति मारुतः । तदाऽऽक्षिपत्याशुरा हो । मुहुर्मुहुर्देहं मुहुश्चरः ॥॥ मुहुमुंहुश्चाक्षेपणादाक्षेपक इति स्मृतः । -
answer_text: The passage starting from prāṇɑ refers to the peculiar characteristics of the situation when the prāṇavāyu is covered by the vitiation of pitta and kapha simultaneously. The term gātraharṣa refers to the sensation over the skin. The term dandaka implies becoming straight like a stick or danda. These are also included in the five varieties of vata, which makes a total of twenty (CS. Ci. 28.199). This descrip¬ tion is available only in the Caraka Text. Videha has mentioned that vāta is only one. However, due to different places and different actions, it could be classified into five types, just as water can be categorized into different types depending on its source. Iśānadeva also said that a single person (for example Devadatta) is called, due to difference of place, as landlord and hermit and due to difference of skill as pot maker and garland maker. Vayu should also be understood in the similar fashion. General feature of ākṣepaka (Convulsions) (SS. Ni. 1. 50- 51) When the vitiated vāta is localized in all the blood vessels (dhamanīs) of the body, it generates quick and frequent jerky movements of the body. This condition has been identified as the disease Aksepaka (convulsions). 27

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 18):

विधिनोपयुक्तस्य फलमाहविधिनेत्यादि । काल इति नित्यगे चावस्थिके च तद्यथा ग्रीष्मे शीतमधुरं माध्वीकादि शीते उष्णतीक्ष्णं गौडिकपैष्टिकादि तथा वाते स्निग्धादि एव वयस्युदाहार्यम् । हितेरत्रेरिति वक्ष्यमाणस्निग्धादिभिर्मद्वविपरीतगुणेः । स्निग्धेरित्युपलक्षण तेनान्यैरपि मद्यविपरीतगुणैरिति बोद्धव्यम् । यदुर्क्त सुश्रतेनमद्यमम्लं तथा तीक्ष्यं सूक्ष्म विशदमेव च । रूक्षमाशुकरं चैवं व्यवायि च विकाशि च ॥ सु०उ० इंति । अम्लरसत्वंध चास्योद्धूतरसत्वेनोक्तं यदुक्तमन्यत्रसर्वेषामम्लजातीनां मद्यं मूर्धि व्यवस्थितम् ।। इति । मूर्धिन व्यवस्थितमुक्कृष्टम् । अन्येऽप्यत्र रसाः सन्ति । यदाह भोजः मीरेयं मदिरा सीधु चतुर्थ मधु चोच्यते । एकैकं पड्रसं तत्र रसतो मद्यमीरितम् ॥ इति । अत्र- भक्ष्यशब्दयोरुपादानेन प्रायो लेहां द्रवान्तरपानं च मद्यपानोचितं न भवतीति दर्शयति । अन्न- भक्ष्याभ्यां लव्धेऽपि मांसे मांसग्रहणं विशेषेण हितत्वोपदर्शनार्थम् । वलं शक्तिः उपचयः स्थौ- ल्यम् । अपरमपि विधिसेवागुणमाहकाम्यतेत्यादि । काम्यता कमनीयमूर्तिता मनसस्तुष्टिः सन्तोषः । अथवा काम्यता मनस कमनीयवस्तुनि मनोवृत्तिः तुष्टिश्च मनस एवेंति योज्यम् । तेज उत्साहः । विक्रमः पराभिभवार्थं बलवती शरीरचेष्टा ।।-।। बुद्धि-स्मृति-प्रीतिकरः सम्पाठ-गीत-स्वरवर्धनश्च प्रोक्तोऽतिसम्यः प्रथमोऽमदोऽहि ॥॥
answer_text: The passage starting from vidhina refers to the implications of the methodical intake of liquor. The suitability of consuming Madya depends on season. In summer, intake of cold and sweet alcohol like the one prepared with honey is good. Likewise, in winter, warm and strong alcohol like the one prepared with jaggery and paste is useful. Those foods that have qualities antagonistic to madya are said to be compatible. As suggested by Suśruta, madya is sour, sharp, penetrating, subtle, and dry. It is quick acting. Moreover, it spreads all over the body even before it is digested and dislodges the joints and affects the essential immunity factors in the body. Sour taste is the most significant quality of madya. There are also other tastes in madya, as mentioned by Bhoja, ‘Maireya, Madirā, Sidhu and Madhu are the four varieties of madya and each of them possess all the six basic tastes. Only anna and bhakṣya are suggested for consumption during madyapāna or consumption of alcohol; this implies that lehya (linctus) and pāna (liquid) are to be avoided. Although māmsa or meat belongs to the anna and bhaksya group, they needed separate mentioning, as the both are serviceable during madyapana. Signs and symptoms of prathama mada (Primary intoxication) The first stage of drinking is considered to be very charming; it increases intelligence, memory, affection and happiness, induces further interest in drinking, eating, sleeping and sex. Moreover, it intensifies the power to recite, sing and the ability to speak loudly. 7

context: विधिनोपयुक्तस्य फलमाहविधिनेत्यादि । काल इति नित्यगे चावस्थिके च तद्यथा ग्रीष्मे शीतमधुरं माध्वीकादि शीते उष्णतीक्ष्णं गौडिकपैष्टिकादि तथा वाते स्निग्धादि एव वयस्युदाहार्यम् । हितेरत्रेरिति वक्ष्यमाणस्निग्धादिभिर्मद्वविपरीतगुणेः । स्निग्धेरित्युपलक्षण तेनान्यैरपि मद्यविपरीतगुणैरिति बोद्धव्यम् । यदुर्क्त सुश्रतेनमद्यमम्लं तथा तीक्ष्यं सूक्ष्म विशदमेव च । रूक्षमाशुकरं चैवं व्यवायि च विकाशि च ॥ सु०उ० इंति । अम्लरसत्वंध चास्योद्धूतरसत्वेनोक्तं यदुक्तमन्यत्रसर्वेषामम्लजातीनां मद्यं मूर्धि व्यवस्थितम् ।। इति । मूर्धिन व्यवस्थितमुक्कृष्टम् । अन्येऽप्यत्र रसाः सन्ति । यदाह भोजः मीरेयं मदिरा सीधु चतुर्थ मधु चोच्यते । एकैकं पड्रसं तत्र रसतो मद्यमीरितम् ॥ इति । अत्र- भक्ष्यशब्दयोरुपादानेन प्रायो लेहां द्रवान्तरपानं च मद्यपानोचितं न भवतीति दर्शयति । अन्न- भक्ष्याभ्यां लव्धेऽपि मांसे मांसग्रहणं विशेषेण हितत्वोपदर्शनार्थम् । वलं शक्तिः उपचयः स्थौ- ल्यम् । अपरमपि विधिसेवागुणमाहकाम्यतेत्यादि । काम्यता कमनीयमूर्तिता मनसस्तुष्टिः सन्तोषः । अथवा काम्यता मनस कमनीयवस्तुनि मनोवृत्तिः तुष्टिश्च मनस एवेंति योज्यम् । तेज उत्साहः । विक्रमः पराभिभवार्थं बलवती शरीरचेष्टा ।।-।। बुद्धि-स्मृति-प्रीतिकरः सम्पाठ-गीत-स्वरवर्धनश्च प्रोक्तोऽतिसम्यः प्रथमोऽमदोऽहि ॥॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 310):

माषपर्णी सूर्यपर्णी काम्बोजी हयपुच्छिका । पाण्डुलोमशपर्णी च कृष्णवृत्ता महासहा ।।५५।। माषपर्णी हिमा तिक्ता रूक्षा शुक्रबलासकृत् । मधुरा ग्राहिणी शोथवातपित्तज्वरास्त्रजित् ।।५६।।
answer_text: Febrifuge action: Whole plant is efficacious in Jvara (Fever). External uses: The paste prepared with roots and leaf applied over Vrna (Wounds) to promote early healing. Mātrā (Dosage): Bīja cūrna: 2-5gm. MĀSAPARNI Latin: Teramnus labialis Spreng. Fam: Leguminosae Hin- Vana Udad Eng: Vogel-Tephrosis Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Suryaparṇī, Kambojīka, Hayapucchikā, Pāṇḍura, Lomashaparnī, Krsnavrnta and Māhasahā. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Māśaparni is Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Tikta (Bitter) and Madhura (Sweet) in taste, Rūkṣā (Drying), Grahi (Absorbent), Sukrajanana (Increases seman) and Increases Kaphe doşa. It cures Sotha (Inflammation), Diseases of Vāta, Pitta and Raktaja origin and Jvara (Fever). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Throughout India, especially in deep forests. Swarūpa (Botanical description): A widely spreading twinning hairy herb. Leaves 3-foliolate; leaflets membranous and sub coriaceous 1.2-2.8 cm.in length, elliptic, ovate-oblong, lower surface is tomentosed.Flowers red, pink or purple arranged in lax, axillary racemes. Pod thin, linear, straight or recurved. Seeds 10-12, Red in fresh state, black on dry.. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Pañchāṅga (Whole plant), Mula (Roots) Chemical constituents: Glucoside and a complex hydrocarbon
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 310
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 310.

Guṇa karma (Properties and indication): Kansya is Kaṣāya (Astringent) and Tiktā (Bitter) in taste, Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), Lekhana (Scarping), Visāda (Sticky), Sāra (Laxative), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Netrahita (Good for eyes), Rūkṣā (Drying), subsides Kapha and pitta

explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Visa-Upavisa Varga, Chapter 7, verse 730.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 60):

मधुकोशः धूम ( म्र ) दर्शिनो लिङ्कमाह-श्रोकज्वरायासेत्यादि। श्रोकांदिभिः कारणैः कुपितेन पित्तेनाभ्याहता उपहता दृष्टिरिति प्रत्येतव्यम् अस्य सुश्रते रोगसंग्रहे पैत्तिकगणेऽभिधानात्। अयं च रोगो बाह्यपटलस्थेन दोषेण जन्यत इति गदाधरः, तृतीयपटलाश्रितदोषेणेति कार्तिकः । दिवा धूप्रान् पश्यति, न तु नक्त; तदा पित्तस्य क्षीणत्वादिति व्याख्यानयन्ति ॥ ५९ ॥ यो ह्रस्वजाड्यो दिवसेषु कृच्छाद्धस्वानि रूपाणि च तेन पश्येत् । मधुकोशः हस्वजाड्यलक्षणमाह-यो हस्वजाड्य इत्यादि। तेन हस्वजाड्येन हस्वानि रूपाणि दिवा यः पश्येत् स हुस्वजाड्य इति योजना। अत्र दोषो दृष्टिमध्यगतः। यदुर्क्त-'दृष्टिमध्यगते दोषे महद्धस्वं च पश्यति' इति। अयं पैत्तिकः ॥ विद्योतते यस्य नरस्य दृष्टिर्दोषाभिपन्ना नकुलस्य यद्वत्॥ ६०॥ चित्राणि रूपाणि दिवा स प्रश्येत् स वै विकारो नुकलान्ध्य संज्ञः।
answer_text: It should be understood that pitta having aggravated due to grief etc., afflicts the vision; in this case since this disease is enumerated in pitta group. According to Gadadhara this is caused due to the affliction of external layer but Kartika opines that this arises due to the dosa lodged in the third layer. It is explained that appearance of every thing as a cluster of smoke, is during day time only and not at nights because pitta is diminished in nights. 59. Hrasva jāḍya (Presbiopia) The individual suffering from Hrasvajāḍya will be able to see the small things with difficulty due to that disease. (Su. u. 7). Due to the Hrasvajadya the individual sees the small things (only) in day time. The dosa here is centrally located in the drstimandala. As it is said, "when the dosa is lodged” in the centre of drstimandala the bigger things are seen smaller”. This is a pitta related disease. Nakulāndhya (Lenticular opacity) Netra Roga Nidāna When the drstimandala is afflicted by the dosa, the eye of that particular individual looks like that of a mongoose (Nakula). During day time, he sees typically different objects. This condition is called Nakulandhya. 60. (Su.u 7)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 60.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 87):

मधुकोशः क्लिप्टवर्त्मलक्षणमाह-मृद्वल्पवेदनमित्यादि। रक्तजत्वेऽप्यस्यल्पवेदनत्वमधिककफदूषितत्वाद्रक्तस्य। वर्त्मेति विदेहदर्शनाद्वत्मद्वयं ग्राह्यम्, अत एव समं युगपदेवेत्यर्थः । अकस्मादित्यहेतोरनियमेनैवेत्यर्थः । ताम्रमित्यनेनोपात्तेऽपि लौहित्ये रक्तमित्युपादानं हेत्वनियमप्रयुक्तं कादाचित्कं लौहित्यमिति द्योतयति। अत्रैव विदेहः-‘श्लेष्मदुष्टेन रक्तेन क्लिष्ट मांसमिवोभयम्। बन्धुजीवनिभ वर्त्म क्लिष्टवर्त्म तदुच्यते॥’ इति। अन्ये सममनुच्छूनं यावदित्याचक्षते। अत्र पक्षे क्लिष्टत्वं वेदनातियोगादवगन्तव्यम् ॥ ८५ ॥ क्लिष्टं पुनः पित्तयुतं शोणितं विदहेद्यदा। ततः क्लिन्नत्वमापन्नमुच्यते वर्त्मकर्दमः॥ ८६॥ ( सु.उ. ३ ) मधुकोशः वर्त्मकर्दमलक्षणमाह–क्लिष्ट पुनरित्यादि। ( क्लिष्टमिति प्रागुक्तस्य कर्तृत्वेनायमर्थः–क्लिष्ट क्लिष्टवर्त्मेव पित्तलाभ्यासादधिकपित्तं सच्छोणितं विदहेद्विरुद्धदाहेन संयोजयेत्तदा क्लिष्ट( न्न )त्वमापादयति, यदा संक्लेदत्वमापन्नं वर्त्मकर्दमर उच्यत इति योज्यम्।) ‘ततः कृष्णत्वमापन्नम्’ इत्यन्ये पठन्ति। तत्र कृष्णत्वं शोणितविदाहेनैव। एवं च सति कृष्णत्वेन कर्दमसंज्ञासमावेशोऽपि घटत इति। कर्तिकस्त्वन्यथा व्याचष्टे- शोणितमिति कर्तृपदं, तेन शोणितं पित्तयुक्तं कर्तृभूतं, यदा पूर्वोक्तं विलष्टमेव विदहेदित्यादि सर्वमपरं समानं पूर्वेण। अस्य तु सुश्रते यत् सान्निपातिकत्वमुक्त तत् कफपित्तरक्तारब्धत्वात् वातकरणत्वस्याश्रुतेः ॥ ८६ ॥ यह्वत्म बाह्यतोऽन्तश्च श्यावं शूनंर सवेदनम्। तदाहः श्याववर्त्मेति वर्त्मरोगविशारदाः॥ ८७॥ ( सु.उ. ३ )
answer_text: Though this is caused by rakta, mild pain is due to rakta being vitiated by kapha profusely. Vartma in the view of Videha - both the eye lids which is why sama, both one time, is used. Akasmat means without any reason. When redness is under¬ stood by tāmra (coppery in colour), using rakta is to indicate turning that colour into into blood-red without any reason. Videha in this context, says, “ The both vartmas are afflicted by rakta which is vitiated by kapha and they look like bandhujīva - this condition is called klisṭavartma”. Others comment that sama means not swollen. As per this version, difficulty is due to severe pain. 85. Vartma Kardama (Blepharitis) The above condition (Klista vartma) further gets damaged when afflicted with the rakta that is vitiated by pitta (induced by pitta provocating foods etc.), becomes turbid (with discharge etc.), and such condition is called vartma kardama. 86. (Su.u.3) In the klista vartma condition when rakta gets over burnt by pitta that is aggravated by pitta-increasing foods and habits, the eye lids become turbid with discharges and such a condition is named as vartma kardama. In the Place of Tatah klinnatvamāpannaṃ, some read- “Tataḥ Kṛṣṇatvaamāpannaṃ” in which case the krsnatva-blackishness is due to over burning of rakta. Then also the use of the word kardama (dirt/mud) suits. Kārtika explains this differently; he says that rakta/śoṇita is the the main causative factor and that is why pitta afflicted rakta causes this condi¬ tion. When the previous klistvartma is to be considered as over burnt, the other features should have remained as usual. Categorising this into sannipata group by Suśruta is in consideration of kapha, pitta and rakta and not including vāta since vāta causing such condition is not heard anywhere. 86. Syava vartma (Traumatic lid) If the eye-lid becomes bluish, swollen and becomes painful out-wardly and in wardly, such a condition is called, Syāvavartma by the experts. 87. (Su.u.3)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 87.
context: मधुकोशः क्लिप्टवर्त्मलक्षणमाह-मृद्वल्पवेदनमित्यादि। रक्तजत्वेऽप्यस्यल्पवेदनत्वमधिककफदूषितत्वाद्रक्तस्य। वर्त्मेति विदेहदर्शनाद्वत्मद्वयं ग्राह्यम्, अत एव समं युगपदेवेत्यर्थः । अकस्मादित्यहेतोरनियमेनैवेत्यर्थः । ताम्रमित्यनेनोपात्तेऽपि लौहित्ये रक्तमित्युपादानं हेत्वनियमप्रयुक्तं कादाचित्कं लौहित्यमिति द्योतयति। अत्रैव विदेहः-‘श्लेष्मदुष्टेन रक्तेन क्लिष्ट मांसमिवोभयम्। बन्धुजीवनिभ वर्त्म क्लिष्टवर्त्म तदुच्यते॥’ इति। अन्ये सममनुच्छूनं यावदित्याचक्षते। अत्र पक्षे क्लिष्टत्वं वेदनातियोगादवगन्तव्यम् ॥ ८५ ॥ क्लिष्टं पुनः पित्तयुतं शोणितं विदहेद्यदा। ततः क्लिन्नत्वमापन्नमुच्यते वर्त्मकर्दमः॥ ८६॥ ( सु.उ. ३ ) मधुकोशः वर्त्मकर्दमलक्षणमाह–क्लिष्ट पुनरित्यादि। ( क्लिष्टमिति प्रागुक्तस्य कर्तृत्वेनायमर्थः–क्लिष्ट क्लिष्टवर्त्मेव पित्तलाभ्यासादधिकपित्तं सच्छोणितं विदहेद्विरुद्धदाहेन संयोजयेत्तदा क्लिष्ट( न्न )त्वमापादयति, यदा संक्लेदत्वमापन्नं वर्त्मकर्दमर उच्यत इति योज्यम्।) ‘ततः कृष्णत्वमापन्नम्’ इत्यन्ये पठन्ति। तत्र कृष्णत्वं शोणितविदाहेनैव। एवं च सति कृष्णत्वेन कर्दमसंज्ञासमावेशोऽपि घटत इति। कर्तिकस्त्वन्यथा व्याचष्टे- शोणितमिति कर्तृपदं, तेन शोणितं पित्तयुक्तं कर्तृभूतं, यदा पूर्वोक्तं विलष्टमेव विदहेदित्यादि सर्वमपरं समानं पूर्वेण। अस्य तु सुश्रते यत् सान्निपातिकत्वमुक्त तत् कफपित्तरक्तारब्धत्वात् वातकरणत्वस्याश्रुतेः ॥ ८६ ॥ यह्वत्म बाह्यतोऽन्तश्च श्यावं शूनंर सवेदनम्। तदाहः श्याववर्त्मेति वर्त्मरोगविशारदाः॥ ८७॥ ( सु.उ. ३ )

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 38, verse 11):

मधुकोशः मेदोजमाह-स्निग्ध इत्यादि। देहानुरूपक्षयवृद्धियुक्त इति देहक्षये क्षयं, देहवृद्धौ च वृद्धिं यातीत्यर्थः। गलेऽनुशब्दमिति अनुनादं करोति। ‘गले तु शब्दम्’–इति पाठान्तरं सुगमम्॥ ६॥ कृच्छ्राच्छ्वासन्तं मृदुसर्वगात्रं संवत्सरातीतमरोचकार्तम् ॥ ७॥ क्षीणं चं वैद्यो गलगण्डयुक्तं भिन्नस्वरं चापि विवर्जयेच्च। ( सु.नि. ११ ) मधुकोशः असाध्यतामाह-कृच्छ्राच्छ्वसन्तमित्यादि। कृच्छ्राच्छ्वसन्तं दुःखेन श्वास विमोक्षकारिणम्। भिन्नस्वरं स्वरभेदवन्तम् ॥ ७॥ कर्कन्धुकोलामलकप्रमाणैः कक्षांसमन्यागलवडक्षणेषु ॥ ८ ॥ मेदः कफाभ्यां चिरमन्दपाकैः स्याद्गण्डमाला बहुभिश्च गण्डैः । मधुकोशः स्थानंतुल्यतया गण्डमालामिहैवाह-कर्कन्धुकोलामलकप्रमाणैरित्यादि। कर्कन्धुः श्रृगालकोलिः, कोलं ब्रहद्वदरम्। मेदः कफाभ्यामिति मेदो दूष्यं, कफो दोषोऽत्रारम्भकः, मेदः कफौ प्राधान्येनोक्तौ; तेन वातपित्त- संबन्धोऽप्यत्र द्रष्टव्यः। यदाह भोजः, 'वातपित्तकफा वृद्धा मेदश्रापि समाचितम्। जङ्डयोः कण्डराः प्राप्य मत्स्याण्डसदृशान् बहून्॥ कुर्वन्ति ग्रथितांस्तेभ्यः पुनः प्रकुपितोऽनिलः। तान् दोषानूध्वंगो वक्षः- कक्षामन्या- गलाश्रितः ॥ नानाप्रकारान् कुरुते ग्रन्थीन् सा त्वपची स्मृता । तां तु मालाकृति विद्यात्कण्ठह्हद्दनुसन्धिषु ॥ गण्डमालां प विजानीयादपचीतुल्यलक्षणाम्’ इति । स्याद्गण्डमालेति मालातुल्यगण्डयोगाद्गण्डमाला। गलमात्र एव गण्डमाला चरके पठिता। यथा ‘मेदः कफाच्छोणितसंचयोत्थो गलस्य मध्ये गलगण्ड एकः । स्याद्रण्डमाला बहुभिश्च गण्डैः ’ ( च.चि.स्था. १२) इति ॥ ८ ॥ ते ग्रन्थयः केचिदवाप्तपाकाः स्त्रवन्ति नश्यन्ति भवन्ति चान्ये॥ ९॥ कालानुबन्धं चिरमादधाति सैवापचीति प्रवदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः। साध्याः स्मृताः पीनसपार्श्वशूलकासज्वरच्छर्दियुतास्त्वसाध्याः॥ १०॥ मधुकोशः गण्डमालातुल्यतयांऽपचीमाह–ते ग्रन्थय इत्यादि। ते इति गण्डमालारम्भक दोषदूष्यकृता ये ग्रन्थयस्त एवे– त्यर्थः। कालनुबन्धं चिरमिति चिरकालानुबन्धम्। सैवापचीति तादृशी अमालारूपा अपची भण्यते। सैवापचीति इतिशब्देनाभिहितत्वात् प्रवदन्तीति क्रियायोगेऽपि न द्वितीया। अपचीनिरुक्तिश्चापरापरोपचीयमानतया। अत एव 'चयप्रकर्षादपचीं वदन्ति' (सु.नि.स्था. ११) इति सुश्रुतः । चयप्रकर्षश्चा परापरभवनेनैव, साधुत्वं च नैरुक्तेन विधिना। यदुक्तम्-वर्णांगमो वर्णविपर्ययश्च द्वौ चापरौ वर्णविकारनाशौ। धातोस्तदर्थांतिशयेन योगस्तदुच्यते पञ्ठविधं निरुक्तम्’ इति। अत एवोक्त-नश्यन्ति भवन्ति चान्य इति। साध्याः स्मृता इति च्छेदः। पीनसादिभिरुप- द्रवैरसाध्याः अयं तु ग्रन्थिश्वरके गण्डमालायामस्ति; संग्रहकारेण तु गण्डमालया सह तुल्यत्वादपच्या अपच्यामेव पठितः ॥ ९–१० ॥ वातादयो मांसमसृक् प्रदुष्टाः संदूष्य मेदश्च तथा सिराश्च। ( सु.नि. ११) वृत्तोन्नतं विग्रथितं च शोथं कुर्वन्त्यतो ग्रन्थिरिति प्रदिष्टः ॥ ११ ॥
answer_text: In medoja galaganda, it is seen that the swelling increase when the body of the patient is repleted and it diseases when there is depletion in the patient. “gale tu sabdam” is different text which means sounds in the throat of the patient are heard. 6. Asādhyatā (incurability) of galaganda The physician should not take up the indiviual suffering from galaganda for treatment when he breathes with difficully, the whole body becomes soft, duration of the disease exceeds one year and he has a broken voice and emaciation. 7. (Su. Ni. 11) Galaganda-Gandamala Apaci-Granthy Arbuda Nidāna, 51 Kṛcchrāt śvɑsɑntɑṃ- those who breathe out with lot of difficulty. Bhinna svɑrɑm - Those who have disturbed or broken voice. 7. Picture of gandamālā Due to vitiated meda and kapha a number of gandas (morbid growths) occur in the arm pit, on the scapular region, neck, throat and the groin region in the size of karkandhu (small ziziphus furit) kola (ordinary ziziphus furit) and āmalakī (goose-berry) which ripen slowly after long time of onset, are called gandamala. 8. (Su. Ni. 11) Since the place of origin is same gandamāla is also explained here. Karkandhu is small variety of ziziphus fruit while kola is big variety of the same fruit. Meda (fat) is the dūṣya (vitiated) and kapha is the vitiator or the initiating factor. These two are said to be predominant factor. The role of vāta and pitta is also to be considered here. As said by Bhoja, “The increased vata, pitta and kapha and also the accumu¬ lated fat take shelter in the muscles of the groins and cause many knot-like forms that look like egg of fish. Vata which is aggravated by them, in turn-takes these morbid factors to chest, arm-pits and neck and causes various types of knots in those places which are called apacī. These look like garlands in joints of neck, heart/chest and jaw. In these places, they are called gandamālā.” Since they look like garland in the ganda (root of the cheeks) there called gandamala (cheek- garland). As per Caraka, gandamālā occurs only in the cheeks— “galaganda is one lump that occurs in the centre of the neck due to meda vitiated by kapha and accumulation of blood; and it is called gandamala when many lumps occur.". 8. (Ca. Ci. 12) Mādhavanidānaṃ Characteristics of Apaci Those tumour like swellings get ripened, exudate the slough and get supressed and some others originate in the near viscinity. In this way this disease continues to last long. This is called apaci according to the specialist plysicians, This disease is curable but it becomes incurable when associated with coryza, pain in the flanks, cough, fever and vomitting. 9, 10. Apac is detailed here after gandamala since there is similarity (in size?) among these two types of disease. Those - means those tumour like swellings which are caused by the same dosa and dūsya that give rise to gandamālā. Continuos means they keep rising, supressing and again rising continuously. It is called apaci because it keeps coming out or increasing one from another “aparāparopad̃yamānatayā” Suśruta, therfore, said, “Cayaprakarṣūdapacīm vadanti” it is called apacī because it keeps growing abundantly". (Su. ni. 11). Cayaprakarsa (abundantly increasing) is by arising one after another ( aparaparabhavana ) this nirukti is acceptable. As said, Varnāgama, varna viparyaya, varna vikāra, varna nāsa, Arthātiśayayoga are the five types of Nirukti (definition). That is why it is said that in appa the tumours get dessroyed and keep originating (Naśyanti bhavanti cānya). This disease becomes incurable when associated with complications like coryza etc, . This type of tumour is described in gaṇḍamāla in caraka. But here apaci is mentioned seperately. Charecteristics of granthi Galaganda-Gandamala Apaci-Granthy Arbuda Nidāna The aggravated Tridosas vitiate mamsa (muscle-tissue) Asrk (blood) meda (fat) and sirā (blood vessals-veins?) and cause swelling which is round in shape big in size and hard for touch that looks solidified which is why it is called granthi (tu¬ mour). 11. (Su. Ni. 11)

context: मधुकोशः मेदोजमाह-स्निग्ध इत्यादि। देहानुरूपक्षयवृद्धियुक्त इति देहक्षये क्षयं, देहवृद्धौ च वृद्धिं यातीत्यर्थः। गलेऽनुशब्दमिति अनुनादं करोति। ‘गले तु शब्दम्’–इति पाठान्तरं सुगमम्॥ ६॥ कृच्छ्राच्छ्वासन्तं मृदुसर्वगात्रं संवत्सरातीतमरोचकार्तम् ॥ ७॥ क्षीणं चं वैद्यो गलगण्डयुक्तं भिन्नस्वरं चापि विवर्जयेच्च। ( सु.नि. ११ ) मधुकोशः असाध्यतामाह-कृच्छ्राच्छ्वसन्तमित्यादि। कृच्छ्राच्छ्वसन्तं दुःखेन श्वास विमोक्षकारिणम्। भिन्नस्वरं स्वरभेदवन्तम् ॥ ७॥ कर्कन्धुकोलामलकप्रमाणैः कक्षांसमन्यागलवडक्षणेषु ॥ ८ ॥ मेदः कफाभ्यां चिरमन्दपाकैः स्याद्गण्डमाला बहुभिश्च गण्डैः । मधुकोशः स्थानंतुल्यतया गण्डमालामिहैवाह-कर्कन्धुकोलामलकप्रमाणैरित्यादि। कर्कन्धुः श्रृगालकोलिः, कोलं ब्रहद्वदरम्। मेदः कफाभ्यामिति मेदो दूष्यं, कफो दोषोऽत्रारम्भकः, मेदः कफौ प्राधान्येनोक्तौ; तेन वातपित्त- संबन्धोऽप्यत्र द्रष्टव्यः। यदाह भोजः, 'वातपित्तकफा वृद्धा मेदश्रापि समाचितम्। जङ्डयोः कण्डराः प्राप्य मत्स्याण्डसदृशान् बहून्॥ कुर्वन्ति ग्रथितांस्तेभ्यः पुनः प्रकुपितोऽनिलः। तान् दोषानूध्वंगो वक्षः- कक्षामन्या- गलाश्रितः ॥ नानाप्रकारान् कुरुते ग्रन्थीन् सा त्वपची स्मृता । तां तु मालाकृति विद्यात्कण्ठह्हद्दनुसन्धिषु ॥ गण्डमालां प विजानीयादपचीतुल्यलक्षणाम्’ इति । स्याद्गण्डमालेति मालातुल्यगण्डयोगाद्गण्डमाला। गलमात्र एव गण्डमाला चरके पठिता। यथा ‘मेदः कफाच्छोणितसंचयोत्थो गलस्य मध्ये गलगण्ड एकः । स्याद्रण्डमाला बहुभिश्च गण्डैः ’ ( च.चि.स्था. १२) इति ॥ ८ ॥ ते ग्रन्थयः केचिदवाप्तपाकाः स्त्रवन्ति नश्यन्ति भवन्ति चान्ये॥ ९॥ कालानुबन्धं चिरमादधाति सैवापचीति प्रवदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः। साध्याः स्मृताः पीनसपार्श्वशूलकासज्वरच्छर्दियुतास्त्वसाध्याः॥ १०॥ मधुकोशः गण्डमालातुल्यतयांऽपचीमाह–ते ग्रन्थय इत्यादि। ते इति गण्डमालारम्भक दोषदूष्यकृता ये ग्रन्थयस्त एवे– त्यर्थः। कालनुबन्धं चिरमिति चिरकालानुबन्धम्। सैवापचीति तादृशी अमालारूपा अपची भण्यते। सैवापचीति इतिशब्देनाभिहितत्वात् प्रवदन्तीति क्रियायोगेऽपि न द्वितीया। अपचीनिरुक्तिश्चापरापरोपचीयमानतया। अत एव 'चयप्रकर्षादपचीं वदन्ति' (सु.नि.स्था. ११) इति सुश्रुतः । चयप्रकर्षश्चा परापरभवनेनैव, साधुत्वं च नैरुक्तेन विधिना। यदुक्तम्-वर्णांगमो वर्णविपर्ययश्च द्वौ चापरौ वर्णविकारनाशौ। धातोस्तदर्थांतिशयेन योगस्तदुच्यते पञ्ठविधं निरुक्तम्’ इति। अत एवोक्त-नश्यन्ति भवन्ति चान्य इति। साध्याः स्मृता इति च्छेदः। पीनसादिभिरुप- द्रवैरसाध्याः अयं तु ग्रन्थिश्वरके गण्डमालायामस्ति; संग्रहकारेण तु गण्डमालया सह तुल्यत्वादपच्या अपच्यामेव पठितः ॥ ९–१० ॥ वातादयो मांसमसृक् प्रदुष्टाः संदूष्य मेदश्च तथा सिराश्च। ( सु.नि. ११) वृत्तोन्नतं विग्रथितं च शोथं कुर्वन्त्यतो ग्रन्थिरिति प्रदिष्टः ॥ ११ ॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 656):

पद्मबीज तु पद्माक्षं गालोड्यं पद्मकर्कटी । पद्मबीज हिम स्वादु कषायं तिक्तकं गुरु ।।८९।। विष्टम्भि वृष्यं रूक्ष्ठ गर्भसंस्थापकं परम् । कफवातकर बल्यं ग्राहि पित्तास्नदाहनुत् ।।९०।। मखान्न पद्मबीजाभं पानीयफलमित्यपि । मखान्नं पद्मबीजस्य गुणैस्तुल्यं विनिर्दिशेत् ।।९१।।
answer_text: Infusions of the bark, leaves and root are used to treat conditions such as Jwara (Fever) Atisarā (Diarrhoea) Sotha (Inflammation) and antitode in Sarpa viṣa (Snake bite) Mātrā (Dosage): Kwātha: 50-100ml, Swārasa: 10-20ml. PADMĀKSAM Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): The synonyms of Padmākṣam are Padmākam, Gālōdyam and Padmakarkatī. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Padmabīja is Swādu (Palatable), Kaṣāya (Astringent) and Tiktā (Bitter) in taste, Śīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Viṣṭambi (Causes constipation), Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac), Rūkṣā (Drying), Garbhastāpaka (Helps conception), Increases Kapha and Vāta, Balya (Promotes strength), Grāhī (Absorbent), cures diseases of Pitta, Rakta and Dāha (Burning sensation). Note: Padmākṣam are the seeds of Padma, seeds are hard, black, starchy and large. Detail description of which is made in Puṣpavarga. MAKHĀNNAM Latin: Euryale ferox Salisb. Fam: Nymphaeaceae Hin: Makhana ng: Fox nut Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Padmabījabham and Pānīyaphalam. Guna karma (Properties and indications): It is similar to Padmabija in properties. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Found in ponds of Northern, Central and Southern regions of India. and the control of the Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is spinous floating plant with large 4 to 5 feet across. Leaves, round, deeply veined, large obovate. Flowers large 5-8cm. in length red or voilet coloured. Fruit is a capsule containg 4-20 pea sized seeds. Processing of Makhānna: It develops into a spongy berry like fruit contains 30-40 pea size seeds and a mucilaginous aril. The thick aril keeps the organic product skimming for a couple of days. After this it at last settle down to the base. The sunken fruits are collected from the pond, these are cleaned, washed and sun-dried, water is sprinkled to keep the seeds fresh and stored. The seeds are warmed with constant mixing over flame for around 6 minutes followed by putting away them in open crates roughly for two days. These seeds are again heated in an open pan over fire. When a crackling sound is heard 5-7 seeds are taken and kept on a hard surface. These seeds are again warmed in an open container over fire. When a popping sound is heard 5-7 seeds are taken and kept on a hard surface. These are then hit with a wooden sledge. There is steam weight inside the seed, so hitting breaks the seed coat and the part flies out in extended from. Seed coats are then evacuated physically. These popped pieces are known as Makhana. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Bīja Chemical constituents: Seed contains proteins, essential aminoacids like cysteine
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 656
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 656.
context: पद्मबीज तु पद्माक्षं गालोड्यं पद्मकर्कटी । पद्मबीज हिम स्वादु कषायं तिक्तकं गुरु ।।८९।। विष्टम्भि वृष्यं रूक्ष्ठ गर्भसंस्थापकं परम् । कफवातकर बल्यं ग्राहि पित्तास्नदाहनुत् ।।९०।। मखान्न पद्मबीजाभं पानीयफलमित्यपि । मखान्नं पद्मबीजस्य गुणैस्तुल्यं विनिर्दिशेत् ।।९१।।

answer_text: Digestive disease: It is employed in appopriate dose in the form of cūrna and extract tincture, in conditions like Agnimāndya (Dyspepsia), Atisarā (Diarrhoea), Pravāhikā (Dysentery) and Kṛmi (Worm infestations) etc. The root bark ground into paste with lime juice and made into pills is used to cure Alasaka (Intestinal obstruction). Mental illness: It is also effective in Apatantraka (Hysteria), Jalasantrāsa (Hydrophobia) etc. Respiratory diseases: It is used as good Respiratory stimulant useful in various respiratory aliments like Swasānalikaśotha (Bronchitis), Rājayakṣma (Tuberculosis), Swāsa (Dysponea) etc. External uses: The leaves are applied as poultice in the treatment of Vrna (Wounds) and Dusta vrna (Non-healing ulcers). The seed paste of Kupilu is used in Mūṣaka viṣa (Rat posion). The oil obtained from the fresh seeds is used externally in Āmavāta (Rheumatism), Pakṣāghata (Paralysis) etc Vātavyadis. Mātrā (Dosage): Bīja cūrna: 50- 300 mg. RĀJĀJAMBU Fam: Myrtaceae Latin: Syzyzium cumini (L) skeels. ng: Java plum, Black plum Hin: Jamun Paryāyanama (Synonyms): The synonyms of Rāja jambū are Phalendra, Nandinī, Mahāphalā, Surabhipatrā and Maha jambū. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): The fruit is Swādu (Palatable), Viṣṭambi (Causes constipation), Guru (Heavy for digestion) and Rocana (Promotes taste). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is native to Indian subcontinent and adjoining parts of Southeast Asia. Swarūpa (Botanical description): An evergreen tree reaches upto 30m., with greyish brown thick bark. Leaves are ovate-lanceolate, oppositely arranged, 7.5-15cm long and 1-2cm wide, smooth and glossy. Flowers are very tiny, white colored, aromatic, 5mm in diameter, in dichotomous panniculate cymes. Fruit- berry, ovoid, green changes to pink and finally it changes to dark crimson after ripening, 1-seeded. Prayojya anga (Part used): Phala (Fruits), Bīja (Seeds), Patra (Leaves), Twak (Bark). Chemical constituents: Tannins, Glynoside, Jamboline, Ellagic acid, Gallic acid
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 639
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Amraphaladi Varga, Chapter 6, verse 639.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 892):

डोडिका विषमुष्टिश्च डोडीत्यपि समुष्टिका ।।८७।। डोडिका पुष्टिदा वृष्या रुच्या वह्निप्रदा लघुः । हन्तिपित्तकफार्शासि कृमिगुल्मविषामयान् ।।८८।। कण्टकारीफल तिक्त कटुक दीपन लघु । रूक्षोष्ण श्वासकासघ्न ज्वरानिलकफापहम् ।।८९।। तीक्ष्णोष्णं सार्षप नालं वातश्लेष्मव्रणापहम् । कण्ड्रूक्रमिहरं दहुकुष्ठघं रुचिकारकम् ।।९० ।। सूरणः कन्द ओलश्च कन्दलोऽशोंघन इत्यपि । सूरणो दीपनो रूक्षः कषायः कण्डुकृत् कटुः ।।९१।। विष्टम्भी विशदो रुच्यः कफार्शःकृन्तनो लघुः । विशेषादर्शसे पथ्यः प्लीहगुल्मविनाशनः ।।९२।। सर्वेषां कन्दशाकानां सूरणः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते । दहुणा कुष्ठिना रक्तपित्तिनां न हितो हि सः ।। सन्धानयोगं सम्प्राप्तः सूरणो गुणवत्तरः ।।९३।।
answer_text: Digestive diseases: Mucilaginous tubers those of the female plant used in the cases of Raktarśas (Bleeding piles) and Bowel affections. External uses: The juice of the leaves mixed with Nārikela, Maricha, Raktachandana made in the form of iontment applied externally in case of Sirasūla (Headace). Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Viṣamuṣṭi, Dōdi and Sumuṣṭikā. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Dōḍikā is Puṣṭidā (Nutrient), Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac), Rucya (Promotes taste), Agnipradā (Appetizer) and Laghu (Light for digestion). It cures diseases of Pitta and Kapha, Arśas (Piles), Kṛmi (Worm intestations) Gulma (Abdominal tumors), Vișa (Posionous manifestations). Note: It has become a Contraversial drug and It may be equated with Leptadinia reticulata. Detail description about the drug is explained in Guḍūcyādi varga varga. KANTAKĀRI PHALĀ Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Kaṇṭakari Phalā is Tikta (Bitter) and Kaṭu (Pungent) in taste, Dīpana (Appetizer), Laghu (Light for digestion), Rūkṣa (Drying) and Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency). It cures Swāsa (Dyspnoea), Kāsa (Cough), Jwara (fever), Diseases of Vāta and Kapha. Note: Details of drug Kantakāri is described in Guḍūcyādi varga varga. SARSAPANĀLA Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): The stems of Sarṣapā are Tīkṣṇā (Penetrating), Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency) and Ruchikar (Promotes taste). It cures Diseases of Vāta, Kapha, Vṛṇa (Wound), Kaṇḍū (Itching), Kṛmi (Worms infestations), Dadru (Ringworm) and Kusta (Leprosy). Note: Details of drug Sarṣapā is described in Śamī Dhānya varga. Kāṇda Saka (Tubers) used as Śāka (pot-herbs/vegetables): SÜRANAM Latin: Amorphophallus companulatus Blume. Fam: Araceae Hin: Sūran kandha Eng: Elephant Foot Yam Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Kāṇda, ola, Kandala and Arśōghna. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Sūraṇa is Dīpana (Appetizer), Rūkṣa (Drying), Kaṣāya (Astringent), Kaṭu (Pungent), causes Kaṇḍū (Itching) and Viṣṭambī (Constipation), Viśada (Clearness), Rucya (Promotes taste) and Laghu (Light for digestion). It cures Diseases of Kapha, Arśas (Piles), aspecially good diet in Arśas (Piles), diseases of Plīha (Spleen) and Gulma (Abdominal tumors). Amangest all Kāṇḍa Sāka Sūrana Kandha is considered to be the best. But it is not effective in diseases like Dadru (Ring worm), Kusta (Leprosy) and Raktapitta (Haemorrages). By undergoing fermentation process, it is made into pickles is more effective. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is found throughout India. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a perennial stemless herb reaches up to 30 cm. Leaves are large solitary 1 meter across, divided into many lobes, oblong-obovate, Spathe is sessile, dull-purplish the margins somewhat spreading or recurved. Spadix is longer than the spathe, appendage ovoid, depressed, up to 15 cm long.Fruits are cylindrical berries maturing green to bright red. Prayojya anga (Part used): Kānda (Rhizomes). Chemical constituents: Calcium oxalate, Protiens, Fats, Carbohydrates, Phrosphrous, Iron, Vit A and B1
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 892
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 892.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 11):

answer_text: Upadeha over - stickiness; Sitata cold touch in the eyes; picchila stickness or thickness applies to exudation. 242. Mādhavanidānaṃ Raktābhiṣyanda The tears have coppery colour and reddish eyes; with all the veins in the eye ball also bright red in colour, alongwith other symptomatology of Pittabhişyanda in the case of Raktābhiṣyanda. 8 (Su.u.6) Pittasya lingāni means the symptomatology of Pittābhiṣyanda. Abhisyanda being a cause of Adhimantha These abhisyandas get aggravated and when unattended cause Adhimantha resulting in severe pain in the eyes. 9. (Su.u. 6). All the four-vata-pittā-kapha-raktāja types of adhimantha have the common features of severe pain. Vedanā should be considered as only pain here by which the pinning sensation-like pain in vata type can be differentiated. Same should be applicable in the case of pitta, kapha and Raktaja types of Adhimantha. 9. Definition of Adhimantha (Glaucoma) Feeling of the eye being plucked out and half part of the head being churned are main features of adhimantha alongwith other doshik signs and symptoms of abhiṣyanda. 10. Netra Roga Nidāna The common feature of adhimantha is given here. The half of the head feels o like being plucked out and churned. The trouble afflicting half part of the head is the special effect of this disease. Svalakshnaih means the above said vāta etc., featrues of abhisyanda. That adhimantha has oozing nature. The time taken by adhimantha for destroying eye-sight as per dosa predominance The Slaişmika adhimantha destroys eye sight by seven nights while, raktaja and vātaja types take five and six nights respectively. But the pittaja abhiṣyanda causes blindness immediately after afflicition. 11. (Su.u. 6)

answer_text: The phrase ‘the mirror etc.’ also involves such items as water and oil among other objects. Now, the issue arises that if the celestial agencies enter the body of the patient how do they remain unseen while entering the body of the patient. Ut. 60.20) Observance of austerities, charity, vows, right conduct, rigid discipline, truth, adherence to the eight extra-ordinary verities, are the qualities found in the grahas. These qualities are there in a greater degree and larger quantity among the devagrahas and in lesser amount among the others. The same qualities and characteristics manifest in part or whole in the person afflicted as per the graha concerned. 31, (SS. Ut. 60.21, 22) ( ) = However, the grahas by themselves do not enter into the bodies of human beings. Those who say so have no knowledge of demonology. But there are thousands and millions of servants or retinue of the grahas, who are fond of blood and flesh. It is only they who are terrific and who roam about at nights and try to enter the human body and possess the human beings in the erratic ways. 32-33 Thus concludes the Chapter on Unmāda. MODERN PERSPECTIVES ON SEIZURES The modern science has identified two types of seizures: 1. A convulsion or other clinically detectable event caused by a sudden discharge of electrical activities in the brain; and 2. A sudden attack of pain, disease or specific symptoms. Absence seizures As described by the scientists, absence seizures are benign, generali¬ zed seizures thought to originate sub-cortically. These brief episodes of unconsciousness normally last 3 to 20 seconds and can occur 100 or more times a day, normally causing periods of inattention. The patient shows a blank facial expression that may be accompanied by movements such as repeated eye-blinking or lip-smacking and minor myoclonus of the upper extremities or the neck. Absence seizures normally start between the ages of 4 and 12. Their first symptom might be deteriorating school performance and behaviour. Their cause is unknown. Absence seizures occur without warning. The patient suddenly stops all purposeful activity and stares blankly ahead, as though day- dreaming. Absence seizures can generate automatisms, such as repetitive lip smacking or mild colonic or sub-colonic movements, including mild jerking of the eyelids. The patient can drop objects he is holding and muscle relaxation can generate him to drop his head or arms or to slump. After the attack, the patient resumes activity, typically unaware of the episode. Absence status, a rare form of absence seizure, occurs as a continued absence seizure or as repeated episodes of these seizures. Normally not life-threatening, it occurs most normally in patients who have previously experienced convulsion. If the physician suspects that a patient is having an absence seizure, one should examine its occurrence and duration by reciting a series of numbers and subsequently asking him to repeat them after the attack ends. If the patient has had an absence seizure, he would be unable to do this. Alternatively, if the seizures are occurring within minutes of each other, ask the patient to count for about 5 minutes. He might stop counting during a seizure and resume when it is over. One should remain alert for accompanying automatisms. One should explore if the family has noticed a change in behavior in home or at ork. The sign of this disease could develop also due to idiopathic epilepsy. Some forms of absence seizure are accompanied by learning disabilities. Seizures, simple partial Resulting from an irritable focus in the cerebral cortex, simple partial seizures typically last about 30 seconds and do not alter the patient’s level of consciousness (LOC). The type and pattern reflect the location of the irritable focus. Simple partial seizures might be categorized as motor (including both Jacksonian seizures and partials epilepsies) or somato-sensory (including visual and auditory seizures). A motor seizure is a series of unilateral colonic (muscle jerking) and tonic (muscle stiffening) movements of one part of the body. The patient’s head and eyes pointedly turn away from the hemispheric focus that is normally the frontal lobe near the motor strip. A tonic¬ colonic contraction of the trunk or extremities can follow. A Jacksonian minor seizure typically begins with a tonic contraction of a finger, the corner of the mouth or like. Colonic movements follow, spreading to other muscles on the same side of the body, moving up the arm or leg and eventually involving the whole side. Alternatively, colonic movements can spread to the opposite side, becoming generalized and subsequently leading to loss of conscious¬ ness. In the later phase, the patient can experience what has been called Todd’s paralysis in the affected limbs that normally resolves within 24 hours. A different kind of seizures manifest in twitching of one muscle group, normally in the face, arm or leg. Twitching occurs every few seconds and persists for hours, days or months without spreading to the distal arm and leg muscles more frequently than the proximal ones; in the face, they affect the corner of the mouth, one or both evelids and, on occasions, the neck or trunk muscles unilaterally. The somato-sensory seizure affects a localized body area on one side. Normally, this type of seizure initially causes numbness, tingling or crawling or "electric" sensations; on occasions, it causes pain or burning sensations in the lips, fingers or toes. A visual seizure involves sensations of darkness or of stationary or moving lights or spots, normally red at first, subsequently blue, green and yellow; it can affect either visual fields or the visual field on the side opposite the lesion. The irritable focus is in the occipital lobe. In contrast, the irritable focus in an auditory or olfactory seizure is in the temporal lobe. The sign of this disease could develop also due to following medical disorders: Brain abscess, brain tumor, cerebro-vascular accident (CVA), head trauma, multiple sclerosis, neurofibromatosis and sarcoidosis. Seizures, generalized tonic-colonic Like other types of seizures, generalized tonic-colonic seizures are generated by the paroxysmal, uncontrolled discharge of central nervous system (CNS) neurons, subsequently leading to neurologic dysfunction. Dissimilar to most other types of seizures, hyperactivity is not confined to the original focus or to a localized area but it spreads to the entire brain. A generalized tonic-colonic seizure spreads to the sub-cortical structures and the patient loses consciousness and falls to the ground. He can utter a loud cry that is precipitated by air rushing through the vocal cords. The body of patient stiffens and subsequently undergoes rapid synchronous muscle jerking motion. Tongue biting, incontinence, diaphoresis, profuse salivation, and symptoms of respiratory distress occur. The seizure normally lasts for 5 minutes. The patient subsequently regains consciousness but he might complain of headache, fatigue and arm and leg weakness. Generalized tonic-colonic seizure occurs singly. The patient can remain asleep, awake, and active. Possible complications that might accompany include respiratory arrest due to air from secretions. status epilepticus, head or spinal injuries and bruises. Patient might also suffer from Todd’s paralysis and on occasions, cardiac arrest Life-threatening epilepticus is marked by prolonged seizure. Generalized seizures might produce brain tumors, vascular trauma, infections, metabolic defects and alcohol withdrawal signs as well as genetic defects. Seizures, complex partial A complex partial seizure occurs when a focal seizure begins in the temporal lobe and causes a partial alteration of consciousness that is normally confusion. Psychomotor seizures can occur at any age, but incidence normally advances during adolescence and adulthood. Guna karma (Properties and indication): It is the variety of Kangu the properties of Cīnāka are similar to the Kangu. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is cultivated in dry ares of India. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is an erect herb grows upto 1.2-1.5 m tall. Stems are cylindric, delicately branched, with simple, alternately arranged hirsute leaves. question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Charaka Samhita (Chikitsasthana, Chapter 1, verse 62-75):

विल्वोऽस्निमन्थः श्योनाकः काश्मर्यः पाटलिर्बला । पर्ण्यश्चतस्रः पिप्पल्यः श्वदंष्ट्रा बृहतीद्वयम् ॥६२॥ शृङ्गी तामलकी द्राक्षा जीवन्ती पुष्करागुरु । अभया चामृता ऋद्धिर्जीवकर्षभकौ शटी ॥६३॥ मुस्तं चैला चन्दनोत्पलम् । विदारी वृषमूलानि काकोली काकनासिका ॥६४॥ एषां पलोन्मितान् भागान् शतान्यामलकस्य च । पञ्च दत्वा तदेकध्यं जलद्रोणे विपाचयेत् ॥६५॥ ज्ञात्वा गतरसान्येतान्योषधान्यथ तं रसम् । तच्चामलकपिण्डानि निष्कुलानि च तैळसर्पिषोः ॥६६॥ पलद्वादशके भृष्ट्वा दत्वा चार्धतुलां भिषक् । मत्स्यण्डिकायाः पूताया लेहवत्साधु साधयेत् ॥६७॥ षट्पले मधुना क्षौद्रं सिद्धशीते प्रदापयेत् । चतुष्पलं तुगाक्षीर्याः पिप्पलीद्विपलं तथा ॥६८॥ पलमेकं निदध्याच्च त्वगेलापत्रकेसरम् । इत्ययं च्यवनप्राशः परमुक्तो रसायनः ॥६९॥ कासश्वासहरश्चायं विशेषेणोपदिश्यते । क्षीणक्षतानां वृद्धानां बालानां चाङ्गवर्धनः ॥७०॥ स्वरक्षयोरोगं हृद्रोगं वातशोणितम् । पिपासां मूत्रशुक्रस्थान् दोषांश्चाप्यपकर्षति ॥७१॥ अस्य मात्रां प्रयुञ्जीत योपरुन्ध्यान्न भोजनम् । अस्य प्रयोगाच्च्यवनः सुवृद्धोऽभूत् पुनर्यूवा ॥७२॥ मेधां स्मृतिं कान्तिमनामयत्वमायुः प्रकर्षं बलमिन्द्रियाणाम् । स्त्रीषु प्रहर्षं परमां च वृद्धिं वर्णप्रसादं पवनानुलोम्यम् ॥७३॥ रसायनस्यास्य नरः प्रयोगाल्लभेत जीर्णोऽपि कुटीप्रवेशात् । हित्वा जराकृतं रूपमपास्य सर्वं बिभर्ति रूपं नवयौवनस्य ॥७४॥ ( इति च्यवनप्राशः ) अथामलकहरीतकीनामामलकबिभीतकानां पलाशित्वगवनद्धानां मृदाऽवलिप्तानां कुष्कुलस्विन्नानामकुलकानां पलाशसहस्रमूलखले संपोथ्य दधिघृतमधु-पिप्पलतैळशर्करासंयुक्तानां भक्षयेदनन्नमभ्यन्नोत्सादनं सर्पिषा यवचूर्णेन च । अयं च रसायनप्रयोगप्रकर्षो दिस्तावदग्निबलमभिसमीक्ष्य, प्रतिभोजनं यूषेण पयसा वा षष्टिकः ससर्पिष्कः, यतः परं यथासुखविहारः कामभक्ष्यः स्यात् । अनेन प्रयोगेणर्षयः रत्नैश्वर्यमहाबल ब्रह्मज्ञानिकवर्षशतजीविनो ह्यनिर्विकाराः परं निष्ठया तपः ॥७५॥ इति चतुर्थामलकरसायनम् ।
answer_text: Bilwa, agnimantha, śyonāka, kāśmarya, pāṭalā, balā, four leaved herbs (śālaparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, mudgaparṇī, māṣaparṇī), pippalī, gokṣura, bṛhatī, kaṇṭakārī, karkaṭaśṛṅgī, tāmalakī, drākṣā, jīvantī, puṣkaramūlā, agurū, harītakī, guḍūcī, ṛddhi, jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, śaṭī, musta, punarnavā, medā, elā, candana, utpala, vidārī, vāsā (roots), kākolī, and kākanāsā reach in quantity of 40 gms. and 500 fruits of āmalakī—all these together should be boiled in water measuring 100 litres 240 ml. till it is reduced to one-fourth. Then the decoction should be strained and the āmalakī fruits should be taken out and their seeds removed. Then they should be fried in 480 gms. of tila oil and ghee. Now it should be cooked in the above decoction adding to it 2 kg. of clean sugar candy and prepared into a linctus. When it is self-cooled, 240 gm. of honey should be added to it. In the end, 160 gm. twak, elā, patra and nāgakeśara (combined) should be added. This is the famous ‘cyavanaprāśa’, an excellent rasāyana. Particularly it alleviates cough and dyspnoea, is useful for the wasted, the injured and old people and promotes development of children. It alleviates hoarseness of voice, chest diseases, heart disease, vātarakta, thirst and disorders of urine and semen. It should be taken in the dose which does not interfere with food intake and digestion. By using this (rasāyana), the extremely old Cyavana regained youthful age. If this rasāyana is used by the indoor method, even the old attains intellect, memory, lustre, freedom from diseases, longevity, strength of senses, sexual vigour, increased agni (digestion and metabolism), fairness of complexion and carmination of wind. One, shedding the form of the old age, puts on that of the fresh youth. The fruits of amalaka and haritaki or amalaka and bibhitaka should be wrapped with the bark of palasa tree and after having been pasted with mud should be cooked on charcoal. ( When they are, well-cooked ) their seeds are removed and 40 kg. of this material should be pounded in a mortar, and added with curd, ghee, honey, sesamum paste, tila oil and sugar. This should be taken on empty stomach by the above method. After the course of treatment, one should be brought back to its normal state by intake of gruel etc. He should also be massaged and annointed with ghee and barley powder. This is the limit of the use of the rasayana. Keeping in view the power of digestion, he should be given diet consisting of sastika rice added with ghee along with soup or milk for the period double of the same for treatment. Thereafter he may move and eat according to pleasure. By this treatment, the sages regained youthfulness, and attained disease-free life of many hundreds of years, and endowed with the strength of physique, intellect and senses practised penance with utmost devotion
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Chikitsasthana, Chapter 1, verse 62-75.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Ashtanga Hridaya (Sutrasthana, Chapter 1):

तत्राद्या मारुतं घ्नन्ति त्रयः तिक्तादयः कफम् । कषाय तिक्त मधुराः पित्तमन्ये तु कुर्वते ॥
answer_text: In the list of tastes, the first three, i.e. Sweet, sour and salt mitigates Vata and increases Kapha. The last three, i.e. bitter, pungent and astringent tastes mitigates Kapha and increases Vata Astringent, bitter and sweet taste mitigates Pitta. Sour, salt and pungent tastes increase Pitta. Types of food substances: Shamana – Food that brings down the increased Dosha to normalcy Kopana – Food that increases the lowered Dosha to normalcy Swasthahita - Food that maintains the normalcy of Tridosha and health. Types of Potency (Veerya) Ushna veerya (Hot potency) -Some food items are hot in nature. For example pepper Sheeta veerya (cold potency) - Some food items are cold in nature. For example milk. These are the two types of potencies. Generally, substances that have Astringent, bitter and sweet tastes are coolant in nature and Sour, salt and pungent tastes are hot in nature. Three types of Vipaka Vipaka refers to conversion of taste after initial phase of digestion.  Madhura Vipaka (sweet) – Generally, Sweet, and salt tastes undergo this Vipaka.  Amla Vipaka (Sour) – Sour taste undergoes this Vipaka  Katu Vipaka – rest of the tastes – Bitter, astringent and pungent tastes undergo this Vipaka
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Sutrasthana, Chapter 1.
context: तत्राद्या मारुतं घ्नन्ति त्रयः तिक्तादयः कफम् । कषाय तिक्त मधुराः पित्तमन्ये तु कुर्वते ॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 8):

ज्वरारोचकेत्यादि । हतेन्द्रियः स्वविषयाग्राहकेन्द्रियः मलः । कप्यत्यन्यतमो मृत्तिकादनशीलस्य कफम् ॥८॥ पित्तमुषरा, मुध्यय कषाया मारुतं , मे रूक्ष्येत्र रोक्ष्यान्द्वक्त कोपयेन्मूद्रसादींश्च निरुणदध्यपि ॥9॥
answer_text: The passage above narrates the symptoms of sannipataja type of pāndu. As the disease is prakṛti samsaṁveta by constitution, it mani- fests the symptoms of all the three types of pandu (vataja, kaphaja and pittaja). Caraka (Ci. 16. 25) has also indicated that the persons who mindlessly consumes all kinds of eatables (or even) uneatables naturally invites affliction of the symptoms of pandu involving char- acteristics of all the three dosas that is vataja, kaphaja and pittaja. The same type of pandu has been described above. The term haten- driya indicates a condition in which a patient is no longer capable to use his sense organs or indriyas. The samprapti (pathogenesis) of the pāṇḍu caused by eating soil (CS. Ci. S. 16.27-29) At least one of the dosas of the individual who has a habit of eating habit the mud gets aggravated. The intake of astringent mud promotes vata; the the salty mud would provoke pitta while the intake of sweet mud generates kapha. Due to the dry nature of the soil, it also makes the ussues of the body dry. It will not be digested properly and as a result, it would block various channels. This retards the power of the sen- sory and motor organs and also the bodily lustre, potency and ojas, thereby producing anemia (pāṇḍu roga) which in turn destroys strength, colour, and digestion of the patient. 8-10
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 8.
context: ज्वरारोचकेत्यादि । हतेन्द्रियः स्वविषयाग्राहकेन्द्रियः मलः । कप्यत्यन्यतमो मृत्तिकादनशीलस्य कफम् ॥८॥ पित्तमुषरा, मुध्यय कषाया मारुतं , मे रूक्ष्येत्र रोक्ष्यान्द्वक्त कोपयेन्मूद्रसादींश्च निरुणदध्यपि ॥9॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Nidanasthana, Chapter 26, verse 6):

मधुकोश: वातिकमाह—व्यायामेत्यादि । शीतजलातिपानाच्छीतलजलस्य प्रभूतपानात् । आढकी तुवरी, कोरदूषः कोद्रवः, विरूढजान्नमङ्डरितधान्यकृतमन्ने, विरुढ़े क्षीरमत्स्यादिक, वल्लूरे शुष्कमांसम् । यद्यपि सवैरेव वातकोपनैर्वातशुल स्यात्तथाऽपि व्यायामादिपाठेनैतद्दर्शयति, व्यायामादयो यथा वातहेतवस्तथा शुलहेतवोऽपि; दोषव्याधिहेतव इत्यर्थः । एवं पित्तशुलादिषु द्रष्टव्यम् । जीर्णे इत्याहारे । घनागमे वर्षासु मेघोदये च । मुहुर्मुहरुपशमप्रकोपौ वायोश्चलत्वेन ।। २- ५ ।। क्षारातितीक्ष्णोष्णविदाहितैलनिष्पावपिण्याककुलत्थययषैः कट्वम्लसौवीरसुराविकारै: क्रोधानलायासरविप्रतापैः ।। ६ ।।।
answer_text: Due to excessive indulgence in physical excercise, travel, coitus, waking in the nights, over drinking of cold water, over consumption of lathyrus pulses, red-gram, green-gram, millets, very dry foods, over eating, on getting injured, eating foods of astringent and bitter taste, foods prepared out of seedling grains, incompatible com¬ bination of foods, dry meat, dry greens; supression of natural urges like faeces, semen, urine and fart; grief, fasting and due to over laughing and talking, Vata increases abundantly and causes Sūla (pain) in the heart, flanks, back, Sacrum and urinary bladder. The pain increases on digestion of food, evenings, cloudy day and in cold season. It repeatedly becomes aggressive and pacifies. There will be consti¬ pation of faeces and fart, pinning sensation and tearing pain in this disease. This pacifies by sudation therapy, oleation, massage and foods of oily and warm nature. 2, 3, 4, 5 Adhakī is red gram– Cajanus Cajana. Koradūṣa is millets. Virūdhaja anna is food prepared out of seedling grains/pulses. Viruddha is incompatible combination of foods like milk and fish etc. Vallura is dried meat. Though the Vata provoking aetiology causes Vata Sula, mentioning of Vyayama etc., here, denotes that as Vyayama (physical strain) etc., aggravate Vata and they also cause Sula, thus being the causative factors or aggravation of Dosa and the disease both. महाश्वासलक्षणमाहउद्धयमानेत्यादि। उद्धयमानवात इति उत् ऊध्वी धूयमानो नीयमानो वातो यस्य स तथा । शब्दवत् सशब्द यथो भवति । उच्चैर्दीर्घम् । संरुद्धो मत्तर्षभ इवेति स्वरविशेषज्ञापनार्थमयं दृष्टान्तः । ज्ञानं शाख़ं विज्ञानं तदर्थनिश्चयः । विभ्रान्तलोचनः चश्चलनेत्रः । विवृते स्तब्ये अक्ष्यानने यस्य स तथा नेत्रस्य विभ्रान्तस्तब्यत्वे कालभेदादिति जेज्जटः । विशीर्णवाक् वक्तमक्षमः मन्दवचनो वा । दीनः क्लान्तमनाः हीनमिति पाठान्तरमयुक्त दूराद्विज्ञायते भृशमित्यनुपपत्तेरित्याहुः - ऊर्ध्वंश श्र्वसिति यो दीर्घंशन च प्रत्याहरत्यधः । श्लेष्मावृतमुखस्रोताः क्रुन्द्वगन्धवहार्दितः ॥ ॥ ऊर्ध्वदृष्टिर्विपश्यंस्तु विभ्रान्ताक्ष का इतस्तितः । वेदनार्तश्च प्रमुह्यन् शुक्लास्योऽरतिपीडितः ॥ ॥ ऊर्ध्वश्वासे प्रकुपिते ह्यधःश्वासो निरुध्यते । मुह्यतस्ताम्यतश्चोर्ध्वं श्वासस्तस्यैव हन्त्यसून् - - -
answer_text: The passage starting from uddhūyamāna refers to the characteristics of the disease mahāśvāsa. The term uddhīyamānavāta has been used to note the situation when the patient feels as if his breathing is being hold in an upwardly direction. Other terms have been already explained above English translation. The term vibhrāntalocana has been accepted by Jejjaṭa to mean that the eyes get startled and remain open. Reading the term dīna and hīnam in place of the term visirnavak is not correct as it would not fit with the passage dūrātvijñāyate bhṛṣaṃ. Urdhva śvāsa (Upward dyspnoea) (CS. Ci. S. 17.48) Because of an accumulation of kapha the movement of air inside the upper part of the body is restricted and subsequently the air does not enter the lower tract of body even with difficulty. This is the condition of the prodromal features of ūrdhva śvāsa or rapid and shallow respiration. 21 (CS. Ci. S. 17.49-51) The following could be noted as features of the fatal stage of firdhva śvāsa: upward and agitated gaze, rolling eyeballs, distress, long expiration, the mouth turning white in complexion and an overall restlessness. 22-23

explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 12.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Dhanya Varga, Chapter 8, verse 837):

कोद्रवः कोरदूषः स्यादुद्दालो वनकोद्रवः । कोद्रवो वातलो ग्राही हिमः पित्तकफापहः ।। उद्दालस्तु भवेदुष्णो ग्राही वातकरो भृशम् ।।८०।।
answer_text: Latin: Paspalum scrobiculatum Linn. Fam: Gramineae ng: Koda millet Hin: Kodo dhan It is also know by name Koradūsa and Vanakodraka is know as Uddāla. Guṇa karma (Properties and indication): Kodrava Increases Vaṭa, Grāhī (Absorbent), Sitā vīrya (Cold in potency), Subsides Pitta and Kapha. Uddāla is Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), Grāhī (Absorbent) and Increases Vaṭa. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Throughout india and along roadsides, weedy places, often on damp soils. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a an annual grass grows upto 4ft. Leaves are 2 ranked stiff, light green upto 20- 40 cm in length. Flowers are delicate, arranged in 4-6 racemes. Seeds are very small and ellipsoidal, 1.5 mm in wide and 2 mm in length, light brown to a dark grey. Chemical constituents: Fibres, Carbohydrates, Protiens, Moisture

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 36):

रक्तपित्तकफान् वायुर्दुष्टो दुष्टान् बहिःसिराः । नीत्वा रुद्धगतिस्तैहिं कुर्यात्त्वड्मांससंश्रयम्॥ १॥ उत्सेधं संहतं शोथं तमाहुर्निचयादतः। सर्वं हेतुविशेषैस्तु रूपभेदान्नवात्मकम्॥ २॥ दोषैः पृथग्द्वयैः सर्वेरभिघाताद्विषादपि। वा.नि. १३ )
answer_text: The aggravated vayu brings the vitiated rakta, pitta and kapha to the outer veins which block the former resulting in the swelling due to deposition of the above in the skin and muscle tissue. This disease is considered as having the in¬ volvement of all three of the dosas. However basing on the difference of aetiology and symptomatology, Sotha is of nine types i.e. 3 due to three dosas individually, 3 due to combination of each two of the three dosas; 1 due to all three dosas together, 1 due to trauma, and 1 due to contact with poison 1, 2.
