question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Purvārdḍha, Chapter 1, verse 6):

उत्पित्सुरामयो दोषविशेषेणानधिष्ठित: । लिङ्गमव्यक्तमल्पत्वाद् व्याधीनां तद्यथायथम् ।।६।।
answer_text: In cases of specific Doṣa involvement, prodromal symptoms manifest with fragmentary intensity, indicating the particular Doṣa. The incomplete manifestation of symptoms allows the physician to identify the nature of the impending disease. The five principles which help in knowing the disease are mentioned here. These five are individually and collectively useful in getting the knowledge about the disease. Though anyone of these helps in diagnosing the disease, all of them are to be known specifically as they help differently in the diagnosis. If Nidana (aetiology) is not known, how can one avoid the aetiological factors while treating meaning—precisely the treatment is to avoid aetiological factors. In Pāṇḍu (anaemia) caused by eating mud, the habit of eating mud should, first, be avoided while treat- ing the disease. If one knows about the fact that eating mud causes anaemia then only, he will be able to ask the patient to stop that habit. This theory of one particu- lar aetiological factor causing one particular disease, does not apply in all cases. The aetiology of Jvara (fever), Gulma (upward oppression of vāta) etc, some dis- eases, is similar. As Caraka puts it-one aetiological factor causes many diseases and one causes one particular disease. In the same way, many aetiological factors cause one disease and many cause many diseases. Some times the immediate caus¬ ative factor may be hindered by a distant one in the form of accumulation of dis¬ eases and can cause a disease where the aetiology (immediate one) can not cause disease, Therefore, by knowing the Nidāna (aetiology) alone one can not get com- plete knowledge of the disease. Purvarupa is the premonitory symptom by learning about which one can avoid the manifestation of the disease. On seeing the premoni- tory symptoms of Jvara (fever) one has to adopt Langhana (fasting) or Apatarpana (depletive measures)–Ca-Ni-1. In the case of vāta type of fever, Ghrtapāna is advo- cated in the pūrvarūpa stage by which it does not lead to bad prognosis–Suśruta. It is also mentioned by Caraka (Ca. Ind. 5)— occurance of all the premonitory symp- toms in fever with high intensity or in any disease to that matter, leads to death. Without knowing the Pūrvarūpa, one can not also differentiate between Raktapitta (haemorrhagic disorder) and Prameha (urinary anomaly). If one passes urine in yellow colour and alongwith blood without having the premonitory symptoms of Raktapitta (haemorrhagic disorder)-Caraka. ci. 6. without knowing the Rupa (symptomalogy), the complete knowledge of a disease can never be attained and also, the prognosis can not be known. The premonitory symptoms become clear in the form of Rūpa when the disease is completely manifested. The prognosis can not also be decided without knowing the Rūpa (symptomology) of the diseases. Caraka says, ''In a disease, where the aetiology, prodromata and the symptomatology is weak or of low profile and where the Dosa that causes the disease and Dusya, the factor (tissue?) that undergoes the pathogenic changes are not equal in qualities and also where the temperament of the patient is not of equal quality of the Dosa which initially vitiates the body, the prognosis is positive.''-Caraka Regarding the bad prognosis, he says, ''When the Nidana (aetiology), Purvarupa (Prodromata) and Rūpa (signs and symptoms) are of medium intensity and have equal qualities to those of kāla (time of occurrence of disease) and Prakṛti (temperament/ constitution) and the Dūṣya (the factor that gets vitiated) is of the same qualities with the Doşa (the factor that vitiates e.g., Kapha Doşa is equal in qualities with those of Rasa and Medas. Pitta Dosa is similar to Rakta and Vāta Dōṣa’s qualities are akin to those of Asthi ), the prognosis is bad. He also says that the Sannipata Jvara manifesting with all the signs and symptoms is incurable (bad prognosis). In the light of above explanations it is clear that the knowledge of the Rupa (the signs and symptoms) becomes inevitable for the diagnosis. Diseases with equal symptomatology or inexplicit symptomatology will be known only with the help of Upaśaya, the positive trial treatment. In certain cases the symptomatology leads to confusion as to which disease it belongs. Such confusion is cleared by using a treatment indicated in one particular disease. If the disease responds positively i.e. if it gets cured, the disease is diagnosed as the one in which that particular treatment is indicated. This is known as Upasaya. If the disease is aggrevated, it is known as Anupasaya, the negative trial treatment. For example, if there is a confusion in dignosing the Urustambha (gripping in the thighs caused by Avrta Vata) and pure Vatavyadhi, the trial of applying medicated oil (Abhyanga) is done. If the disease is cured the disease is diagnosed as Vāta Vyādhi (neuro-muscular disorder caused by pure Vāta) and if it is aggravated, it is labelled as Urustambha. This trial is positive to Vāta Vyādhi hence called Upaśaya to Vāta Vyadhi and negative to Urustambha, hence the name Anupaśaya to this disease. Even after knowing about the Pūrvarūpa etc., if one does not get acquainted with Saṃprāpti (pathogenesis), it is not possible for him to estimate the strength of the Dosas and their gradation, time etc., which help in fixing correct treatment. Samprāpti is that aspect of the disease which elicits the pathological changes that take place in the body resulting in the manifestation of the disease. According to the theory–‘’Breaking of Samprāpti itself is treatment’’, it becomes essential to know about this aspect. Thus the knowledge of these five factors is necessary in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases. This book is called Nidāna of Mādhava’’. The word ‘Nidāna’ means that aspect which decides the disease. Hence Nidana covers all the above five factors of diagnosis. Adding to the above commentary of Madhukosa, these five aspects are to be known through three types of examination, i.e., Darsana (visual persception), Sparsana (touch) and Praśna (questioning). The aspects to be examined in the patients are Aṣṭaṣthānas (eight places) i.e., Nādī (pulse), Mūtra (urine), Mala (faeces), Jihvā (tongue), śabda (sound), Sparsa (touch), Drk (eye-sight) and Akrti (built of the body). The state of these aspects are known with the help of the Pramanas (epistemol- ogy or the instruments of knowledge), viz., pratyaksa (direct perception through sense- organs), Anumāna (analogy), upamāna (comparison), Aptopadeśa (verbal testimony of the seers and elders) yukti (considering various factors for sprouting of one result) etc. Nidāna (The aetiology) Nimitta, Hetu, Ayatana, Pratyaya, Utthāna and Kāraṇa are the synonyms of Nidana (aetiology or the causative factor). Nimitta is used to denote Sakuna (the omen). Hetu means the reason behind one project. Ayatana means the place of origin Pratyaya denotes the basic means of conversion of words as in ‘‘Lat’’ ‘‘Lut’’ etc. for various forms. Utthāna denotes the endeayour or begining of movement. Kāraṇa is the causative factor. These are used as synonyms of Nidana which means wherever these terms are used in this work, Nidāna is that factor which invariably causes a disease. Nidāna is classified in many varieties. This is of four types according to one classification- Sannikrsta (immediate cause), Viprakrṣṭa (a cause that gives raise to the disease after some time/distant cause), Vyabhicārī (a weak causative factor which may not produce a disease, Prādhānika (severe cause) as in the case of poisons. According to another classification, Nidana is of three varieties viz., Asatmyenrdriarthasamyoga (contact of incompatible objects with the sense organs); which is of three types again basing on the intensity of the contact-Hina (low), Madhya (medium) and Ati (excessive). Prajñāparādha (the wrong deeds of the individuals whose intellect and other mental abilities are derranged. Parinama the improper climate in the seasons), i.e. the seasonal qualities either become more as more cold in winter, which is termed as Atiyoga, or less cold, which is called Hina yoga and having rains or warmth in that season, that is called as Mithya yoga. Another Classification is- Dosa hetu-the seasonal variations causing natu- rally, the Sañcaya (accumulation), and Prakopa (aggrevation) to the Doşas. e.g. the Madhura rasa is more in Sisira (winter) which causes accumulation of Kapha inside the body and in Vasanta (spring) the Kapha is affected by sun-rays and becomes aggravated to cause Kapha-diseases inside the body. Vyadhihetu-such factors that cause a particular disease irrespective of the Dosa involved in it. E.g., eating mud causes anaemia. However, particular type of mud aggravates particular Dosa- astringent tasted aggravates Vata, that of non arable lands, Pitta and sweet tasted aggravates Kapha-the disease going to be occured is Pāṇḍu (anaemia). Ubhayahetu-that factor which, not only aggravates one particular Dosa but also causes a particular disease. e.g., riding on elephant, horse and camel and consuming foods that cause burning sensation cause vatarakta. The act of riding aggravates Vāta and eating such foods, the Rakta. Hence the treatment should aim at pacifying Vata and also curing the disease Vatarakta. Further, the Nidana is classified into two types, 1. Utpādaka (cause of initiation of disease) and Vyañjaka (cause that Sustains). Utpādaka-as in the cause of Madhura rasa causing Kapha accumulation and Vyañjaka as in the case of sun rays in the spring season that aggravate Kapha. Another classification says that Nidana is of two types, viz. Bahya and Abhyantara. Bahya is the external factor which includes food, behavioural aspects and time. Explaining this aspect, Tisata (cikitsa ka 29-31) gives the three aspects i.e. food, behaviour and time that act as external factors which cause aggrevation to Dosas. Abhyantara is the internal factor like Dosa and Dusya that exist inside the body. The Abhyantara factor invariably involves Dosa. This bodily factor, Dosa, when. Vitiated, is classified into various categories viz., Prakrta (natural), vaikrta (unnatu- ral) etc. Prākṛta is that kind of Dosa which naturally aggravates in particular season, as śleṣmā in Vasanta (spring season), pitta in śarat (moon-light season) and vāta in varşā (rainy season). That means these Doşas naturally attain, by external environ- ment and foods, the stage of aggravation. The treatment for such conditions is also easier because it is a natural course. Vaikrta is that Dosa which aggravates in the season other than the usual one, i.e., aggravation of Pitta or Vāta in Vasanta, Kapha or Pitta in Varşā, Kapha or Vāyu in Sarat. The treatment in such conditions is diffi- cult as it is unnatural for these Dosas to aggravate in these particular seasons. Hence, aggravation of Vāta in Varṣā, Pitta in Sarat and Kapha in Vasanta is natural and otherwise is unnatural. This knowledge helps in fixing the grade of curability of the diseases. Dosas are again classified as Anubandhya and Anubandha. Anubandhya is the factor which primarily causes a disease in the body and Anubandha is a Dosa or disease which follows the first one even when it exists. It can be called as Upadrava or a complication. When treating the first or main disease it should be kept in mind that the annexe or add on disease should not be aggravated. Caraka (ca. sū. 10) says that the Anubandha Automatically pacifies by treating main disease (ca. ci. 21) Pakrtivikrtitah is also one aspect of Dosa consideration in origination of a disease. A vata disease occuring to a Vata prakrti Individual can not be cured so easily while the Pitta prakrti and Kapha prakrti individuals with Vata disease will be cured easily. The Dosa-Dusya combination should also be not equal i.e. Kaphadosa- Rasadhātu, Pittadoṣa–Raktadhātu and Vātadoṣa-Asthidhātu combinations in the pathogenesis will also originate incurable diseases (ca. su. 10). Asayapakarsa is an¬ other consideration for the Dosas. The vāta, even if it is not more in quantity and if gets lodged in the place other than its main place of functioning, causes a disease. This theory applies to other Dosas also (Ca. su. 17). This helps in planning the management of the disease. When Vāyu and Śleṣma get depleted, pitta remains in its own quantitative status but gets displaced from its main place of functioning, reaches other places and causes pinning sensation and burning sensation leading to fatigue and weakness. (Ca. su. 17). In such condition, Vata has to be brought to its original status and Pitta is not be brought down. Those who do not know about this try to bring down Pitta and complicate the situation (Bhattaraharicandra). Accord- ing to some, Bhrājakapitta, which exists in the skin, becomes replete with the addi¬ tion of pitta coming from its asaya (locus standii) with the help of vata and the burning sensation thus caused should be attributed to excessive pitta and they opine that any Dosa in its original quantity will not be able to produce a disease. Bhattaraharicandra supports his statement by adding that, in the above situation, pitta is to be brought back to its locus standii, but it is viewed as Vrddhi (excession) of pitta, one may think of managing it by Virecana (purgation therapy) and thus brings down the pitta by doing so, leading to severe complications. Dosas should also be considered for their Gati. Caraka says that Gati (movement) of Dosa is of three types viz., Kṣaya (decrease), Sthāna (normalcy) and Vṛddhi. According to another classifi- cation, it is of three types namely. -Urdhva (upward), Adhah (downward) and Tiryak (sideward). He also says that Gati of Doşa may be classified in another way by their reach i.e. Koştha (alimentary canal), Śākhā (branch) and Marmāsthisandhi (vital points and bone-joints) (ca. su. 17). Dosas, when on increase, show their signs according to their intensity, they do not show their signs when on decrease and in normaly they perform the routine activity (ca. su. 17). Sudanta sena (one of the commentators of gives the complete picture of the activities of vāta, pitta and kapha. Each activity is also a quality of that particular Dosa. According to him, ''Flatulance, rigidity, roughness, breaking sensation, churning sensation, shaking sensation, trem¬ bling, pinning sensation, shrill voice, depression, fatigue, weeping, purging, pain, severe breaking sensation, hardness, sounds in the ear, irregular digestion, disturbed sight, delusion, feeling as if the body is thrown away and kicked, tiredness, insomnia, biting and squeezing sensation, bending forward and backward, mental agony, giddi¬ ness, falling down, yawning, skintillation, convulsions, emaciation, hollowness, cut¬ ting sensation, covering sensation, blackish or red colour in the body, feeling heavy thirst and lack of sleep are the activities produced in the body by vitiated or aggra¬ vated Vāta. The feeling of astringent taste is also felt in such conditions. Blisters on the skin, sour and smoky belching, delirium, over sweating, syncope, bad odour, braking of the skin, intoxication, quick digestion, un-easiness, thirst, giddiness, heat, not satisfying by foods and drinks, feeling of darkness, burning sensation, feeling of pungent, sour and bitter tastes, colour of the skin being other than anaemic and boil- ing sensation in the body are the activities of aggravated Pitta. Satiation, drowsiness, heaviness stability, hardness, excessive defaecation, oiliness, heaviness in the stom- ach, cold, itching sensation, dribbling of saliva, doing things at a low pace, swelling in the body, over sleep and feeling salt and sweet tastes. When two of these Dosas vitiate the situation is called Samsarga having the manifestation of the activities of those two particular Dosas and when all these activities pertaing to three Dosas are manifested, such condition is called Sannipāta. The knowledge of the above signs and symptoms help in planning the treatment. As put by Suśruta, the decreased Dosa are to be increased, the increased ones are to be decreased and the equilibrium should be maintained when the Dosas are in normal status. (Su. ci. 33). The upward, down- ward and sideward movement of Dosas also is to be known to manage the situation. In Rakta pitta heamorrhagic disease), the Dosa are to be treated by adopting the Pratimārgaharaṇa (nullifying Doṣas by changing the direction) (Ca. ni. 2). If one Pañcanidānalakṣana does not know this and aims at cleaning Pitta Dosa, by adopting purgation therapy a common treatment for that Doşa, in down-ward Rakta Pitta, he would be increas- ing the disease and there by endangering the life of the patient. In sideward move- ment of Dosas as in the case of Jvara, fever, the treatment should go according to t the situation. The increased Dosas, sometimes, reach the alimentary canal, some- times the branches and at times the vital points and bone-joints and cause diseases. As the reach of the Dosas in the vital points and bone-joints is considered to be causing severe disease which are curable with dificulty ( Krcchrasadhya ), these places are labelled as one place of reach of Dosas in vitiation. Kostha is the organs of alimentary canal, Sakhas are Rakta (blood) etc; tissues and also skin. This terminol- ogy is coined by Caraka himself. This also will be helpful in the treatment aspect. According to Caraka, ‘‘When Vata lodges in Amasaya (stomach) Sweda (perspira- tion therapy) without oleation is done and Kapha occupies the Pakvāśaya (intes- tines), Sweda (perspiration therapy) is to be performed following sneha (oleation). (Ca. su. 14). According to Suśruta, in irregular fevers, Santata is the one which lodges in Rasadhātu and Rakṭa dhātu. And the irregular fever which originates from Māmsadhātu is Anyedyu (Su. u. 39). Caraka says that Agnikarma (cauterisation) is not to be applied in Snāyu (ligament) based wounds and those raising in Marmas (vital points) (Ca. ci. 25). The Dosas are also to be understood in terms of Sāma (undigested) and Nirāma (digested) conditions. It is said by Vāgbhata (Va. sū. 13), ‘‘The first Dhatu (Rasa, the chyle, which is considerd as the first change undergone by the food after ingestion inside the body), is not digested, hence not formed com- pletely due to weak digestive fire vitiates and gets settled in the stomach. This is called Ama. The Doşa and Dūṣyas which get afflicted by this factor are called sāma (and when they get rid of Ama, they are called Nirama). The common diseases caused by such affliction are—obstruction in the channels, loss of energy, heaviness, immobility of Vāta, lethargy, indigestion, constant spitting, purging, distaste and fatigue. When there is no affliction, the above will be disappered. When particu¬ larly Vāyu is afflicted by Ama-constipation, indigestion, drowsiness, sounds in the intestines, pain, swelling and pricking sensation in the body are seen. After the affliction is nullified, vividity, dryness, laxation and less amount of pain are seen. The Ama-effect is countered by adopting opposite things to these conditions (Nirāma) and administering oily foods and drugs, when pitta is Sāma (associated with ama), there will be bad odour, greenish colour, blackish colour, sour taste, immobility, heaviness in it. It will be sour in taste and causes burning sensation in the throat and heart. Pitta will be coppery and yellowish in colour, very hot, bitter in taste and mobile when it gets rid of Ama. It is also devoid of bad odour and increases taste–perception, digestion and strength. When Kapha is afflicted by Ama (it is called Sāmā Kapha), it will be turbid, thready, immobile and gets lodged in the throat. It has bad odour and hinders appetite and causes belching. When it gets ripened (devoid of Ama), it becomes froathy, well formed, whitish in colour, loose in texture and lacks in odour. In this state, it gets dislodged easily and gets cleared from the throat. The benefit of this knowledge helps in adopting digestive measures in the Sāma-condition of Doṣas and palliative measures in Nirāma conditions. Per- mutation and combination of Dosas with variation in their intensity (Taratamabheda) is 62 in number. The details are given in Suśruta Saṃhitā (Su. u. 66), Pūrvarūpa (Premonitary Symptom)

question:

आरग्वधो राजवृक्षः शम्पाकश्चतुरङ्गलः । आरेवतो व्याधिघातः कृतमालः सुवर्णकः ।।१४८।। कर्णिकारो दीर्घफलः स्वर्णाङ्गः स्वर्णभूषणः । आरग्वधोगुरुः स्वादुः शीतलः स्रंसनोत्तमः ।।१४९।। ज्वरह्नद्रोगपित्तास्त्रवातोदावर्त्तशूलनुत् । तत्फलं स्रंसनं रुच्यं कुष्ठपित्तकफापहम् ।। ज्वरे तु सततं पथ्यं कोष्ठशुद्धिकरं परम् ।।१५०।।
answer_text: An oil processed with Kampillā applied externally over Vṛṇa (Wounds). Mātrā (Dosage): Phala raja cūrṇa: 2-8gms. ĀRAGVADHA Latin- Cassia fistula Linn. Fam: Leguminacae. Hin: Amaltas. Eng: Purging cassia or indain laburnum. Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Rājavṛkṣa, Śampāka, Caturañgula, Ārevāta, Vyādhighāṭa, Kṛtamalā, Suvarṇaka, Karṇikāra, Dīrghaphala, Svarṇañga and Svarṇabūṣaṇa. Guna karma (Properties and indications): Āragvadha is Guru (Heavy for digestion), Madhurā (Sweet) in taste, Śītavīrya (Cold in potency) and best Śamsrana (Laxative). It cures Jwara (Fever), Hṛdroga (Cardiac diseases), Raktapitta (Haemorrage), Diseases of Vāta, Udaravartha (Infrequent bowel movements) and Śūla (Abdominal colic). The Fruits is Recaka (Purgative) and Rucya (Promotes taste). It cures Kuşta (Leprosy), Diseases of pitta and kapha, most desireable in Jwara (Fever), it is one of best which alliviates abdominal toxins. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Common throughout India as wild or cultivated plant. Swarūpa (Botanical description): A medium sized much branched evergreen tree. Leaves 20-40 cm., long rachis, leaflet 8 pairs, 5-10 cm. long ovate, acuminate apex, entire margin. Flowers are arranged in lax pendulous recemes, golden yellow in colour. Fruits are indehicent pod 30-50 cm. long and 2.5cm. in diameter. dark brown in colour. Seeds flat embedded in soft black pulp. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Phalā majja (Fruit pulp), Mūla Twak (Root bark), Patra (Leaves). Chemical constituents: Mucilage, Pectin, Gucose, Hydroxymethyl-Anthraquinones, Essential oils etc

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Purvārdḍha, Chapter 2, verse 17):

आगन्तुज्वरस्य लक्षणं व्यथापूर्वो जायते ।।१७।।
answer_text: Āgantu (extrinsic) fever is characterized by pain appearing first, followed by the vitiation of Doṣas. This type of fever is caused by external factors such as trauma, poison, or supernatural influences. Immobility, severe pain in the joints, sleep, heaviness in the body, gripping sensation in the head, corryza, cough, excessive sweat, burning sensation and medium bouts of temperature are the features of Vātaśleṣma type of fever. 15, 16 (Su. u. 39) Excessive sweat in this context is due to irrelevant relationship of cause and effect according to Kārtika. This argument holds good as Hārīta also includes swedabhava (production of sweat) in this type of fever. Madhyavega (medium bout of temperature) is not too high or not too low bout of temperature. Features of signs and symptoms of Sleşma-Pitta type of fever Sticky and bitter sensation in the mouth, drowsiness, delusion, cough, distaste, thirst and repeated alternative feeling of warmth and cold in the body are the fea¬ tures of Slesma-pitta type of fever. 17 (Su. u. 39)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Purvārdḍha, Chapter 2, verse 17.
context: आगन्तुज्वरस्य लक्षणं व्यथापूर्वो जायते ।।१७।।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 451):

सोमवल्ली सोमलता सोमक्षीरी द्विजप्रिया । सोमवल्ली त्रिदोषघ्नी कटुस्तिक्ता रसायनी ।। १५७।। आकाशवल्ली तु बुधैः कथिताऽमरवल्लरी ।। २५८ ।। खवल्ली ग्राहिणी तिक्ता पिच्छिलाऽक्ष्मामयापहा । तुवराऽग्निकरी हृद्या पित्तश्लेष्मामनाशिनी ।।२५९।।
answer_text: It is used extensively in treatment of Jvara (Fevers), Kāsa (Cough), Diseases of Rakta, Kantaroga (Thoat diseases), Visarpa (Herpes) etc. Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrna: 1-3gms. SOMALATÃ Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Somavallī, Somakṣīrī and Dvijapriya Guna karma (Properties and indications): Somavallī subsides all three dosas, Kaṭu (Pungent) and Tikta (Bitter) in taste and Rāsayana (Reguvenator). Note: Soma was a sacred plant, the juice of which (Soma-Rasa) was considered as the divine drink offered to Gods, contemplated with medicinal efficacy, Acharya Sushruta has mentioned 24 varieties of Soma based on the differences in their habitat, name, shape and specific potencies etc. There has been a long search for the identity of the original Soma plant was and several plants have been proposed as representing it, amongest those few of them are as follows. mma brevistigma ĀKĀŚA VALLĪ Latin: Cuscuta reflexa Roxb. Fam: Convolvulaceae Hin: Amar Bel Eng: Dodder, Horse tail parasite Amaravallarī is the synonym of Ākāśavallī. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Ākāśavallī is Grāhī (Absorbent), Tikta (Bitter) and Kaşāya (Astringent) in taste, Picchala (Sticky), Netrala (Good for eyes), Agnivardaka (Appetizers), Hrdya (Good for heart) Cures disease of Pitta, Kapha and Āma (Undigested food). Note: The source plants used in the name of Ākāśavallī are Cuscuta reflexa Roxb. and Cassytha filiformis.Linn. These are parasitic plants. Because of their identical appearence causes contraversy both can be used with each other. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is commonly found throughout India to the hill tops up to a height of 8000ft. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is leafless parasitic twinner grows on bigger trees. Flowers are tiny, white, sessile arranged in short racemes. Fruit- Capsule 6-8mm. in diameter globose-conical. Seeds 3-3.5 mm long, black. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Pañcāṅga (Whole plant). Chemical constituents: Colouring agents- Cuscutin, Amarbelin. Glycoside- Luteolin, Phytosterol and Reducing sugars
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 451
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 451.
context: सोमवल्ली सोमलता सोमक्षीरी द्विजप्रिया । सोमवल्ली त्रिदोषघ्नी कटुस्तिक्ता रसायनी ।। १५७।। आकाशवल्ली तु बुधैः कथिताऽमरवल्लरी ।। २५८ ।। खवल्ली ग्राहिणी तिक्ता पिच्छिलाऽक्ष्मामयापहा । तुवराऽग्निकरी हृद्या पित्तश्लेष्मामनाशिनी ।।२५९।।

answer_text: Excessive or no perspiration, blackish discoulouration, loss of sense of touch, severe pain on injury, lack of firmness in the joints, lassitude, depression, appearance of blisters on the skin; pinning sensation, pulsation, breaking sensation, heaviness, numbness and itching sensation in the knees, calf muscle, thighs, pelvis, scapular region, hands, legs and joints. The pain in joints persists and disappears untimely. There will also be discolouration and patches on the body as prodromata of Vatarakta. 5, 6, 7 (Ca. ci. 29) Excessive or no perspiration results due to the special effect of the disease as in the case of leprosy. ‘‘Kṣateatiruk’’ severe pain on injury which occurs due to the vitiation of that region already caused by the disease. Symptomatology of Vātarakta, Doṣa - wise

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 51-54):

मधुकोशः वातादिभेदेन षड्विधं तिमिरमभिधाय रागैः षड्विधमाह-वक्ष्यामि षड्विधं रागैरित्यादि। सर्वानुगा तिमिरसंज्ञां विहाय लिङ्गनाशसंज्ञया कीर्तनं रागप्रकर्षप्राप्तेः ॥ ४८ ॥ रागोऽरुणो मारुतजः प्रदिष्टो म्लायीच नीलश्च तथैव पित्तात्। कफात् सितः शोणितजः सरक्तः समस्तदोषप्रभवो विचित्रः॥ ४९॥ ( सु.उ. ७ ) मधुकोशः वातादिरागोद्देशमाह-रागोऽरुण इत्यादि। म्लायी पीतनीलो वर्णः। ननु, शेषे परिम्लायि पठितं तत् कथमधुना वातरागानन्तरं तस्योक्तिः? नैवं, रागकाले वायुरप्यत्रांशेन व्याप्रियते इति प्रतिपादनार्थंमिति कार्तिकः । पैत्तिकरूपद्वयस्यैकत्राभिधानेन लाघवं स्यादिति युक्तं, यत्तु प्रागेव न कृतं तदेकविकारशङ्डानिरासार्थम्॥ ४९॥ अरुणं मण्डलं दृष्ट्यां स्थूलकाचारुणप्रभम्। ( सु.उ. ७ ) मधुकोशः उद्देशक्रमेण वातिकरागस्यैव विशिष्टलक्षणमाह-अरुणं मण्डलमित्यादि। अरुणं मण्डलं कीदृशं भवतीत्यत आह-स्थूलकाचारुणप्रभमिति। स्थूलकाचस्येव अरुणा प्रभा तत्तथा; एतेन बाहुल्यमरुणत्वं च प्रतिपाद्यते। काचोऽत्ररुणो विवक्षितः ॥ परिम्लायिनि रोगे स्यान्म्लायि नीलं च मण्डलम्॥ ५०॥ दोषक्षयात् स्यवं तत्र कदांचित् स्यात्तु दर्शनम्। ( सु.उ. ७ ) मधुकोशः परिम्लायिनो विशिष्टलिङ्गमाह-परिम्लायिनीत्यादि। अत्र गदाधरस्तु-‘रक्तजं मण्डलं दृष्ट्यां स्थूलकाचा- नलप्रभम्’ इति पठित्वा एतदपि परिम्लायिलक्षणमाह, व्याचष्ट च-बाहुल्येन स्थूलकाचस्येव वर्णतोऽनलस्येव प्रभा यस्य तत्तथेति, अनलप्रभत्वेन पीतं मण्डलं भवति पीतं चेषन्नीलं बोद्धव्यं, ‘म्लायि नीलं च मण्डलम्’ इत्यभिधानात्, 'तथा 'पित्तान्मण्डलमानीलं कांस्याभं पीतमेव च' इत्युक्तम, आनीलमीषत्रीलमित्यर्थः। म्लायीति म्लानमिति कार्तिकः । दोषक्षयादिति कर्मक्षयात् सत्यापि दोषरूपत्वे दर्शनसद्वावात्। ननु, किंग तहिं दोषरूपं तादूशमेवावतिष्ठते उत क्षीणं वा ? तत्र न तावदाद्यः पक्षः, दोषाणां कृतकार्याणां तथात्वे दर्शनस्यासंगतत्वातु; अध द्वितीयस्तदा दोषस्यैव क्षयादित्यापतितं किमिति कर्मक्षयादिति स्वीक्रियते? नैवं, विना दोषप्रतीकारं दर्शनोदयाद्विकारस्वभावादिति कार्तिकः । अन्ये तु कालवशाद्वातादिदोषस्यैव क्षयात् कदाचिद्दर्शनं स्यादित्याहुः, यतः कालादिजमपि विशेष क्रचिल्लक्षणत्वेन पठन्येव, दोषशब्देन च कर्मणोऽभिधानमप्रसिद्धं’ किंवा दोषक्षये एव कदाचित् कर्मक्षयो हेतुरिष्यतां, कर्मणश्च कदाचित् क्षयो वैचित्र्यात्। अथात्रैव कुत एवम्? उच्यते, अस्यैवविधकर्मजन्यत्वादिति। गदाधरपाठे रक्तजमित्यत्र रक्तमित्युपलक्षणं, तेन रक्तपित्तजम्॥ ५०॥ अरुणं मण्डलं वाताच्चञ्चलं परुषं तथा॥ ५१ ॥ पित्तान्मण्डलमानीलं कांस्याभं पीतमेव च। श्लेष्मणा बहुलं पीतं शङ्खकुन्देन्दुपाण्डुरम्॥५२॥ चलत्पद्मपलाशस्थः शुक्लो बिन्दुरिवाम्भसः । मृज्यमाने च नयने मण्डलं तद्विसर्पति॥ ५३॥ प्रवालपद्मपत्राभं मण्डलं शोणितात्मकम्। दृष्टिरागो भवेच्चित्रो लिङ्गनाशे त्रिदोषजे। यथास्वं दोषलिङ्गानि सर्वेष्वेव भवन्ति हि॥ ५४॥ ( सु.उ. ७ )
answer_text: After explaining six types of timira by vāta etc., doṣa-wise differentiation, the six types by colour differentiation will be explained further. This disease called hither to as Timira is named hereafter as linganāśa - having attained colour. 48. Varieties of Linganāśa as per colour Vata types of timira will be in red colour while the pitta dominated timira gets yellowish blue or blue colour, kapha dominated one becomes white, Rakta type gets blood-red colour, while the sannipāta type of timira will be of multicolours. 49. (Su. u. 7) Mlayi is yellowish blue. After previous classification of timira based on dosa determination, parimlāyi has been given. Why the term, mlāyi is used here after description of vāta-dominated colour? Not so, says Kārtika that during the time of attaining colour, the influence of vata is inevitable and to show this, it is men¬ tioned here. Generally the two varieties of diseases (of one organ) caused by one doşa (pitta) are to be described at one place. But mentioning at different places is to rule out the similarity. 49. The Specific symptom of Vāta - colour Due to vāta-aggravation, the sight area (cornea) becomes red which looks t like a thick-red glass. (Su. u. 7) The appearance of the cornea is compared with a thick red glass by which thickness and red colour are seen here. Mādhavanidānaṃ The specific symptom of Parimlāyi kāca In the disease Parimlayi, the cornea becomes turbid with blue colour. Some times when the dosa gets depleted the individual will be able to have visual perception, 50, (Su.u.7), Gadādhara, in this connection, says, “In Raktaja dṛṣṭimaṇḍala vyādhi (cornea afflicted by rakta)it becomes like a thick glass with a lustre of flame”. By its volume it is like thick glass and by colour-like a flame; flame that may be correlated to yellowish colour. This yellowishness should be understood as slightly bluish (because the flames are associated with bluish tint) and since it is also said, “Due to pitta, the mandala becomes (Anīla) slightly bluish and yellow like bronze”. Anīla, here, is taken as slightly bluish. Mlāyi means mlāna (faded) according to Kūrtika. Dosa ksayat means due to depletion of karma, because inspite of dosa being present there will be regaining of vision. Then, does the dosa remain unchanged or de¬ pleted? This is not the argument in the face of it, when the bad deeds lead to loss of vision. Then will the disease causing doşa be understood as depleted by the word Karmakṣayāt. Not so, because the vision is regained without taking any therapeutic measure (it cannot be taken so), according to Kārtika. Others say by the effects of time, when the vata etc., dosas are depleted, there will be regaining of vision since kāla is also attributed with the quality of affecting the doṣa. The word doṣa being termed as karma is not popular. Or, the Karmakṣaya takes place due to unknown (and typical) circumstances. Then why is it happpening so here? It is said it takes Netra Roga Nidāna place so because the situation is arisen by such karma. In the statement of Gadādhara, Raktaja should be taken as Raka pittaja. 50 The specific symptomatology of coloured dṛṣṭi maṇḍala as per dosa-predominance Due to Vāta predominance, the dṛṣṭimaṇḍala becomes red in colour, unstable and coarse/rough. Due to pitta predominance, it becomes bluish and yellow like bronze and in śleşmā predominance it becomes thick yellow like conch shell, moon-light and pale or white like a water drop that moves on the leaf of lotus and it also moves hither - thither when the eyes are rubbed. In Rakta predominance, the mandala turns into red colour like a coral beed or petal of a lotus flower. In tridosa-affliction, the dṛṣṭimaṇḍala becomes multi-coloured in a typical fashion and basing on the domination of a particular dosa, there will also be the symptoms related to that dosa. 51-54. (Su.u.7)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 51-54.

answer_text: Anorectal diseases: The mucilaginous tubers are used medicinally in case of Raktarsas (Bleeding piles) and small bowl affections. Posionious bites: The root of Karkoţaki along with Ghṛta alleviates all types of Visa (Posions manifestations). External uses: The expressed leaf juice added with Nārikela, Marica, Raktachandana applied tropically an ointment to relieve Siraśūla (Headache), Mātrā (Dosage): Mūla curna: 3-6gms. MARKANDKĀ Latin: Cassia angustifolia M.Vahl. Fam: Family: Caesalpiniaceae Hin: Bhuikhakhasa Eng: Tinnevelly Senna Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Bhūmivallī, Mārkandī, and Recanī. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): It cures Kuṣta (Leprosy), makes Śarīra Sodana by means of Vamana (Emesis) and Virecana (Purgation). It aso cures Vişa (Posions manifestations), Dourgandhya (Foul smelling), Kāsa (Cough), Gulma (Abdominal tumours) and Udararoga (Abdominal disorders). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is largely cultivated in Southern india. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a perennial shrub with spreading branches reaches upto 0.5-1m high. Leaves paripinnate 4 to 6 pairs, ovate- lanceolate, glabrescent, entire margin, sharp tip and yellow when dried. Flowers are borne in axillary raceme golden yellow in colour. Fruit is a pod 4-5cm. long, horned, broadly oblong, compressed and flat and contains 6 small, ovate, seeds. Prayojya anga (Part used): Patra (Leaves). Chemical constituents: Sennoside A and B, Rhein, Aloe-emodin, Kaempferol, Isormamnetin, Kaempferol, Myricylalcohol and Phytosterols

answer_text: Eye diseases: A varthi prepared with Matsyākṣī, Punarnavā, Bhṛṇgaraja used as añjana in diseases like Netrakaṇḍū (Eye itching), Netrabhiṣyandi (Conjunctivitis), Potakhī (Trachoma), Drṣṭimāndya (Diminished vision) etc. External uses: The oil processed with plant applied externally over Vrna (Wounds), Kanḍu (Itching) etc Skin conditions. Mātrā (Dosage): Swarasa: 10-20 ml, SARPĀKṢĪ GUDÜCYÄDI VARGA Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Gandālī and Nādīkalāpaka. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Sarpākṣī is Kaṭu (Pungent) and Tikta (Bitter) in taste, Usna vīrya (Hot in potency), Vrna ropaka (Promotes wound healing), Kṛmiagna (Useful in worm infestations), and useful in posionous bites like Scorpion string, Rats and Snakes. Note: Like Matsyākṣī it is also contraversial. The following two source plants are identified as Sarpākṣī. Source plants Ophiorrhiza mungos Linn. Polygonum plebejum R. Br. SAÑKHA PUŞPI Latin: Convolvulus Pluricaulis Chois.Fam: Convolvulaceae Hin: Sankhahul Eng: English speedwheel. Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Sańkhāhvā and Mańgalya Kusumā Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): It is Sāraka (Laxative), Mēdhya (Brain tonic), Vrsya (Aphrodisiac), Mānasrogaṛt (Cures psychological disorders), Rāsayana (Reguvenator), Kaṣāya rasa (Astringent) in taste and Uṣṇa virya (Hot in potency). It Promotes Smṛti (Memory power), Kānti (Lusture), Balā (Strength) and Agnivardaka (Appetizers), cures diseases of Tridoshaja origin, Apasmāra (Epilepsy), Bhūtagrha (Evil spirits), Eradicate poverty, Kuṣṭa (Leprosy), Kṛmi (Worm infestations) and Viṣa (Posionous manifestations). Note: The source plants are being used for Sankhapuspi. Convolvulus pluricaulis.Chois Evolvulus alsinoides Linn. Convolvulaceae Canscora decussata.Schult Gentinaceae Levendulla bipinnata O.Ketz. amiaceae In some texts Visnukrānta is correlated with Aprājita or either Saṅkhapuṣpī. Based on the colour of the flowers following source drugs are expected. Convolvulus pluricaulis.Chois

question:
Transliterate and give the contextual import of the following line from Charaka Samhita — Chikitsasthana, Chapter 13, verse 32-34:

अव्यायामदिवास्वप्रस्वाद्वतिक्रिग्धपिच्छलैः । द्धिदुग्धौद्कानूपमांसैथ्यप्यतिसेवितैः ॥ २९ ॥ कुद्देन श्रेष्मणा चोतःस्वावृतोऽनिलः । तमेव पीडयन् कुर्यादुवर्र बहिरन्त्रगः ॥ ३० ॥ तस्य रूपाणि — गौरवारोचकाविपाकाङ्गमद्दौः, स्त्तिः, पाणिपादमुष्कोबशोफः, उत्क्लेशनिद्राकासश्वासाः, शुक्रत्यं च नखनयनवद्नत्वङ्मू व्ववेसाम्; अपि चोद्रर्, शुक्रराजीसिरासंततं, गुरु, स्तिमितं, स्थिर, कठिनं च भवति; एतच्छूछैष्मीदरमिति विद्यात् ॥ ३१´॥ दुर्बळान्नेरपथ्यामविरोधिगुरुभोजनैः । ख्रीदत्तेथ्यामविरोरोमविण्मूत्रास्थिनखादिभिः ॥ ३२ ॥ विषेध मन्दैवीताद्याः कुपिताः संचयं त्रयः । शनैः कोष्ठे प्रकुर्वन्तो जनयन्त्युदरं जुणाम् ॥ ३३ ॥ तस्य रूपाणि—सर्वेषामेव दोषाणां समस्तानि छिङ्ग़न्युप्लभ्यन्ते, वर्णाश्य सर्वे नखादिषु, उदरमपि नानावर्णराजीसिरासंततं भवति; पतत् सन्निपातोदरमिति विद्यात् ॥ ३४॥१
answer_text: By lack of exercise, day-sleep, intake of sweet, too unctuous fand slimy food, excessive use of curd, milk, meat of aquatic and marshy animals kapha gets aggrav¬ ated and obstructs the passages, thus vayu having been blocked in its passage comes out of the intestines and produces ( kaphaja ) udara roga. The kaphaja type of udara roga has the following signs and symptoms-heav¬ iness, anorexia, indigestion, body-ache, numbness, swelling in hands, feet, scrotum and thighs, nausea, sleep, cough, dyspnoea, whiteness in nails, eyes, face, skin, urine and stool, prominence of white streaks and veins all over the 'abdomen; heavy, still immobile and hard abdomen. [ If one having poor digestion takes unwholesome, uncooked, antagonistic and heavy food, ( impure substances such (as ) menstrual blood, hairs, faeces, urine, bone, nail etc. administered by a woman, slow-acting poisons, the three dosas väta etc. get aggravated and accumulated gradually in belly and thus produce sannipattaja udararoga. It, exhibits, all, the, symptoms, of, all, the, dosas, all things in nails etc, and abdomen is also pervaded with variegated streaks and veins. This should be known as sannipātodara

Mātrā (Dosage): Swarasa: 10-20ml. GOJIVÃ Latin: Onosma bracteatum Wall. Fam: Boraginaceae Hin: Gaujaban ng: Frog Fruit Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Gojikā, Gobhī, Dārvika and Kharaparṇinī Guna karma (Properties and indications): It is Kasāya (Astringent), Tikta (Bitter) and Madhura (Sweet) in taste and Madhura vipaka (Sweet in post digestive), increases Vāta doṣa, Subsides Kapha and Pitta doṣa, Sīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Grāhī (AbsorVAPRAKĀŚA NIGHAN bent), Hrdya (Good for heart). (Boraginaceae) is commonly used in the name of Gojivha. ephantopus scaber accinia glauca Savi nosma bracteatum. Wall. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Found in Northwestern Himalayas from Kashmir, at an altitude of 3, 500-4, 500 meters. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is small hirsute perennial herb. Leaves are radical ovate- lanceolate, 12-30 cm long 1.5-3.5 cm broad, serrated and tomentosed on both the surfaces. Flowers head 5-7.5cm.in diameter, diocious, blue - purple, arranged in dense hairy, glomaerate clusters. Nutlets are ovoid, rough, grey, 4mm., rugose and tuberculate. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Patra (Leaves), Puṣpā (Leaves), Mūla (Roots). Chemical constituents: Rich quantity of mucilaginous matter, sodium, potassium, calcium, iron and magnesium salts

युदर्क्त कामशास्त्रे-‘शास्त्रस्य विषयस्तावद्यावन्मन्दरसा नराः। प्रवृत्ते रतिचक्रे तु न शास्त्रं नापि च क्रमः' (का.सू.सां.अ. २) इति। कलहादिवशाद्वा मेहेने नखदन्तपातः। अधावनादप्रक्षालनात्। रत्यतिसेवनादिति व्यवायस्यात्यन्तसेवनात्। योनिप्रदोषदिति दीर्घकर्कशरोमादियोगाद्योनिदुष्टेः । शिश्ने मेहने.। विविधापचौरैरिति अशुद्धसलिलप्रक्षालनब्रह्मचारिणीगमनादिभिः। उपदंशसंज्ञा च दंशनोपाधिमन्तरेणापि रूढा बोद्धव्या। यद्यप्यभिघातक्षते मेहने उपदंश आगन्तुः षष्ठः संभाव्यते, तथाऽपि तस्य दोषलिङ्गयुक्ततया दोषज एवान्तर्भावः ॥ १ ॥ सतोदभेदैः स्फुरणैः सकृष्णैः स्फोटैर्व्यवस्येत् पवनोपदंशम्। पीतैर्बहुक्लेदयुतैः सदाहैः पित्तेनरक्तात् पिशितावभासैः॥ २॥ स्फोटैः सकृष्णे रुधिरं स्त्रवन्तं रक्तात्मकं पित्तसमानलिङ्गम्। सकण्डुरैः शोथयुतैर्महद्दिः शुक्लैर्घनैः स्त्रावयुतैः कफेन॥ ३॥ नानाविधस्त्रावरुजोपपन्नमसाध्यमाहुस्त्रिमलोपदंशम्। मधुकोशः पैत्तिकमाह-पीतैरित्यादि। स्फोटैरित्यनुसंयोजनीयम्। एवमुत्तरत्रापि॥ रक्तजामाह-रक्तादित्यादि। रक्तात् पिशितावभासैरिति मांसवत्ताग्रैः स्फोटैः रक्ताच्छोणितादुपदंशं व्यवस्येत्। रक्तैः' इति पाठान्तरे रक्तैः शोणितैः ॥ २-३॥ सन्निपातजमाह-नानाविधेत्यादि। नानाविधस्त्रावरुजोपपन्नमिति प्रत्येकदोषोक्तस्त्राववेदनायुक्तम्। त्रिमलोप- दंशमिति त्रिदोषपदंशम्॥ विशीर्णमांसं कमिभिः प्रजग्धं मुष्कावशेषं परिवर्जयेच्च॥ ४॥ मधुकोशः असाध्यतामाह–विशीर्णेत्यादि। मुष्कावशेषमिति विशीर्णसमस्तमेहनमांसत्वेनावशिष्टफलकोषमात्रम्॥ ४॥ संजातमात्रे न करोति मूढः क्रियां नरो यो विषये प्रसक्तः। कालेन शोथक्रिमिदाहपाकैर्विशोर्णशिश्नो म्रियते स तेन॥ ५॥ मधुकोशः उपक्रमे चिकित्साकरणार्थमाह-संजातेत्यादि। विषये प्रसक्त इति अतिव्यवायरतः; कालेन चिरकालेन॥ ५॥ अड्डरैरिव सङ्गातैरुपर्युपरि संस्थितैः । क्रमेण जायते वर्तिस्ताम्रचूडशिखोपमा॥ ६॥ कोषस्याभ्यन्तरे सन्धौ सर्वसन्धिगताऽपि वा। ( सर्वेदना पिच्छिला च दृश्चिकित्स्या त्रिदोषजा। ) लिङ्गवर्तिरभिख्याता लिङ्गार्श इति चापरे ॥ ७॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने उपदंशनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ४७॥ मधुकोशः एकस्थानत्वेनात्र लिङ्ग़ार्श आह-अड्डरैरित्यादि। अड्डरैरड्डरसदृशैरीषद्दीर्धैः, संघातैमांसप्रतानैः, 'संजातै' इति पाठे ‘मांसेः’ इति शेषः। ताम्रचूडशिखोपमेति ताम्रचूडः कुक्कुट, तच्यूडातुल्या। सन्धाविति मेढ़रन्धसन्धौ, सर्वसन्धिगतेत्यनेन सर्वसन्धेरुक्तत्वात्। एषा त्रिदोषजाः, अत एव 'सवेदना पिच्छिला च दुश्चिकित्स्या त्रिदोषजा' इति क्वचित् पाठः। सुश्रते क्वचित् स्त्रीणामप्युपदंशः पठ्यते। यथा, 'मेढ़संथौ व्रणाः केचित् सर्वाश्रयास्तथा। कुलत्थाकृतयः केचित् केचित् पद्मदलोपमाः॥ रुजादाहर्तिबहुलाः कृष्णस्तोदसमन्विताः। शीघ्रां केचिद्विसर्पन्ति शनैः केचित्तथाऽपरे। स्त्रीणां पुंसां जायन्ते उपदशाः सुदारुणाः’ इति। किंतु 'समानतन्त्रेष्वदर्शनादेतदनार्षमाहुः इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायामुपदंशनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ४७॥
answer_text: There arise five types of syphilitic ulcers on the penis due to injury with hands, piercing with nails, biting with teeth, not cleaning it or over indulgence in sexual intercourse and also due to the vitiation/disease of the vagina where the sexual act - is performed and many other bad deeds. 1. Since this disease occurs in the proximity of the place where Bhagandara originates, upadamsa is being described here. Though the penis is not included in the parts where piercing with nails or biting with teeth are done during fore-play of the sex, it is done due to hyper-sexuality. This attitude is mentioned in Kama śāstra, viz. “The sexual instructions are applicable only as long as the inviduals are in a mild mood. Once the process of intercourse gets started there is no following of the text or any order." (Kāmasūtra-2). Piercing the penis with nails or biting with teeth may also occur due to fighting. Adhavanat- means by not cleaning. Ratyatisevanat means by over indulgence in sex. Disease of the vagina is the situa¬ tion where the pubic hairs of the particular vagina are long (unclean), rough etc., and many other unhygienic conditions. Many other bad deeds in this context in¬ clude washing with impure water, having intercourse with a woman who follows Upadaṃśa Nidāna celebacy etc., The term, ‘upadamsa’ is to be understood as applied here, since the place (penis) looks bitten - when afflicted with this disease. Though the injured penis also develops this disease, it need not be considered as sixth variety because the particular condition becomes comparable to the other infections caused by any one of the dosas. 1. Symptomatology of the five types of upadamśa The wounds in the vata type of upadamsa are associated with pinning sensation, breaking sensation and pulsations. They are black in colour. In pitta type they are yellowish in colour, associated with exudation and burning sensation. In case of the rakta type of upadaṃśa, the blister-wounds look like the muscle pieces, black in colour, oozing with blood and associated with itching sensation, inflammation bigger in size', white in colour, hard and exudating in kapha type. When the three doşas vitiate (hence the name, “Trimala”), there will be exudation of different t colours and consistencies, unbearable pain and such situation is considered as incurable. 2, 3. The word pita (yellow) is to be related to sphota (the blisters). In rakta (blood) - vitiation the blisters are coppery in colour. The variety in colour and consistency of the exudation in Sannipāta type is due to the combination of all three dosas in the vitiated satete. ‘Trimalopadamsa’ means syphilis of tridosa variety. Incurability of upadaṃśa When the penile musculature is destroyed, when it is eaten away by the worms and when the testes alone remain, such a case should be rejected for treat¬ ment. Muskavasesam means that - the complete musculature of the penis is eaten away and the testes only remain. 4 Complications of upadamśa due to negligence of treatment If an unwise individual does not take immediate treatment on the onset of upadamsa and continues to indulge in sextual activity, he will be affected by inflammation, worm-infestation, burning sensation and ripening and his penile muscula¬ ture gets withered due to which he meets his end. 5. In order to explain the necessity of providing treatment immediately after the onset of the disease, the complications are given here. Viṣaya prasaktāḥ - means the individual continuing to have sex. Kālena means - in due course of time. 5. Signs and symptoms of Lingārśa (Condyloma/Penile wart) When there is growth on the penis that looks like thick sprouting, one upon the other which - takes shape of a cock' crown gradually. This can occur in the junction of the orifice of the penis or any where inside the prepuce. This is caused by vitiation of tridosas and associated with pain and sticky exudation. This condition is difficult to cure and known by name Lingavarti. Some people call this as Lingārśa. 6, 7. Thus ends the chapter on diagnosis of Upadamsa in the Madhava's book of diagnosis written by Śrīmādhava kara. Upadamsa Nidāna II &-9 II Since this also occurs on the same place, Lingarsa is being deseribed here. Ankuraih means - like the sproutings of the seeds that look elongated. Sanghataih means - the dense growth of muscle tissue. Tamracuda means - the cock. The growth looks like the cock’s crown. Sandhau means - in the junction of the orifice of the penis. This occurs due to vitiation of tridosa. That is why it is told that it is associated with pain and stickiness, difficult for cure and caused by vitiation of tridosa. In Susruta, it is read by some that upadamsa is seen in women also; resembling “some ulcers seen in the junction of the orifice of the penis and some, any where on the penis; some look like horse-gram while some, like lotus petals. These are associated with severe pain, burning sensation, blackness and pinning sensa¬ tion. Some of these spread fast while some, in a slow pace. The upadamśa ulcers which are severe are seen in women and men as well. But such a description is not found in the contemporary text and also in other texts of Ayurveda and hence not considered as composed by the saintly Susruta. 6, 7. Thus ends the chapter on diagnosis of Upadamsa in the Madhukosa commentary written by Śrīkanṭhadatta. 47. ＊＊＊＊

question:
State whether the following statement based on Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) — Nidanasthana, Chapter 2, verse 67 is TRUE or FALSE.

Appetite, weakness, lightness of the body, less temperature, movement (outward movement) of Dosas (impurities) and (completion of) nine days are the features of Nirāma (digested) fever.
explanation: The original text states: "Appetite, weakness, lightness of the body, less temperature, movement (outward movement) of Dosas (impurities) and (completion of) eight days are the features of Nirāma (digested) fever." (number changed from 'eight' to 'nine').

State whether the following statement based on Sushruta Samhita — Nidāna-Sthāna, Chapter 5 is TRUE or FALSE.

Modes of Spread of Contagious Diseases: tāluśoṣa, fever, consumption, conjunctivitis and infectious diseases spread from human beings to human beings due to sexual intercourse, touching of the body, due to breath, eating together, and even sharing the same bed and by clothings, garlands and cosmetics.

answer_text: Bhaktam synonyms are Anna, Andra, Kūra, Odana (These are used in both masculine and neutral genders), Bissā (It is used in feminine gender) and Dīdivi (It is used in masculine gender). It is advisable to wash the rice before you cook it, after few minutes it should be boiled in five parts of water. Once it get softened, from this manda part is separated. Bhaktam is Agnipradā (Appetizer), Pathya (Diet), Tarpaṇa (Nourshing) and Rocana (Promotes taste). If same rice prepared without proper washing, separating manda portion, and cold, it is Guru (Heavy for digestion), causes Aruchi (Aneroxia) and Increases Kapha
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Krtanna Varga, Chapter 11, verse 960
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Krtanna Varga, Chapter 11, verse 960.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 55):

answer_text: After explaining the urine - hindering niruddha prakasa, the faeces-hindering sanniruddhaguda is being explained. Tasya means - of the anus. If it is read as mahat srota- it is meant as the orifice of the anus. As in niruddhaprakasa, here also constriction of skin causes sanniruddha guda. 48, 49. Ahipūtanaṃ When the child has passed stool and urine, after which these orifices are not washed properly or due to over sweat or not giving it a proper bath, kapha and rakta get aggravated and cause itching there. On scratching, there arise immediatly blisters and discharge. These small wounds come together causing a severe condition called ahipūtanaṃ. 50-51 (Su. Ni. 13) Kṣudraroga Nidāna Apane means - in the anus; svinne means - along with sweat; asnapyamane - means those who are not given bath. Ekibhutam means - the anus becoming one with the wounds (anus surrounded completely with wounds). Ahiputanam - occurs only in children. In Bhoja, it is read that this is caused also due to vitiated breastmilk. As he said, "Due to sucking vitiated breast-milk and not cleaning off the faeces properly there arise vesicles associated with itching, burning sensation and pain as per the dosas (kapha, pitta and vata respectively) which is known as Ahipūtanā.” 50-51. rṣaṇakacchū The dirt is accumulated around the testes of an individual who does not take bath and clean the area properly; when sweating causes wetness in the area, itch¬ ing arises. And on scratching, there arise blisters and oozing which is called Vrsanakacchu. This is caused by vitiation of slesma and rakta. 52, 53. (Su.Ni. 13)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 55.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Purvārdḍha, Chapter 1, verse 10):

यथा दुष्टेन दोषेण यथा चानुविसर्पता । निर्वृत्तिरामयस्यासौ संप्राप्तिजाँतिरागति: ।।१०।।
answer_text: Saṃprāpti (pathogenesis) is the process by which vitiated Doṣas extend in the body and cause disease. Jāti (genesis) and Āgati (occurrence) are synonyms of Saṃprāpti. Understanding Saṃprāpti helps in planning the management of the disease by breaking the pathological process. Hetu (causative factor) includes the two types of causative factors i.e. the ex¬ ternal and internal. Vyadhi (disease) means Jvara (fever) etc. The three factors which are antogonistic to Hetu and Vyadhi individually and collectively are known as Viparīta (opposing or antagonistic). Though the Auṣadha (medicine), Anna (food) and Vihāra (behaviour) are similar to the aetiological factors of the disease, they nullify the disease by way of their Prabhava (special effect). Such usage by which the disease is mitigated is considered to be bringing about Sukha (happiness) and is called Upasaya (positive trial). Upasaya is also known as Satmya (homologous). Caraka also says the one which gives happiness or positive result is only homolo- gous or suitable to the situation. (Caraka. ni. 1). Happiness is the criteria of mitiga¬ tion of the disease. But temporary happiness attained by taking cold water in just affected fever in which burning sensation and thirst are salient features should not be considered as Upasaya as the problem is aggravated later. Vrddha Vagbhata advises to add the Desa (place) and Kala (time) to the three factors-medicine, food and behavioural aspect (A. s. ni. 1). In short, Sukhanubandha (continuous happi- ness) that is occured by Ausadha (medicine) etc., is Upasaya. Here, the word Ausadha etc., is used to rule out the happiness caused by application of fragrant unguentum like Candana (sandal paste) and by having the company of women. The word Anubandha (continuous) is used to rule out the temporary happiness caused by Apathya (harmful foods etc.). This explanation serves as an example but it is not the definition or quality of Upasaya as Ausadha etc. and Hetu etc. will not be able to produce any symptom in the absence of each other. The definition of Upaśaya should be that the factor that nullifies the unhappiness caused by a disease is to be known as Upaśaya, or the one which is Sātmya (homologous) is Upaśaya, or the sustained happiness caused by Auşadha is Upaśaya. Here, Auşadha (medicine) should be taken as included with food and behavioural aspect also as Caraka considered material and non material things like Ahāra (food), Acāra (behaviour), Deśa (place), Kāla (time) etc. as medicines. The example for Upaśaya through Auṣadha (positive trial with medicine) which is opposite to Hetu (the causative factor), is-using Sunthi (dry ginger) the drug of hot potency in Sīta Jvara (cold fever). This is based on the Caraka's statement-The disease caused by Usna (hotness) are treated with Sita (cold) drugs and Vice Versa. (Caraka. vi. 3). The example for Hetuviparīta-Anna, food that is antagonistic to the causative factor of the disease (by which the disease is cured)-giving meat soup and cooked-rice in fever caused by excertion and aggrevation of Vāta. Vihāra or the behavioural aspect as Hetu Viparīta antagonistic to the causative factor of the disease-waking in the nights in kapha-accumulation caused by day-sleep. Now examples for Vyadhi Viparita, the factors which are antagonisic to the disease are being given-Ausadha-giving the astringent drugs, Patha (Cissamples periera) in Atisara (diarrhoea), Sirisa (Albezia lebbec) in poi¬ soning, Khadira (Acacia catechu) in skin disorders and Haridra (turmeric) in doşa action but because of their special effect (prabhāva) they are capable of allevi¬ ating the particular diseases. Vāpyacandra said that the drug that cures the Jvara etc., diseases is also antagonistic to the dosa that causes the disease. But a drug which is antagonistic to a particular doşa need not necessarily be antagonistic to the disease caused by that dosa. The Kapha gulma (vatic oppression caused by kapha) will not be cured by Vamana (emesis) and langhana which by nature, act as anti¬ kapha. It is also said that though Desa (place), Kala (time) etc., permit, langhana (fasting) should not be done in Jvara (fever) and Gulma (vatic oppression) both caused by Kapha. And also–the individuals suffering from Timira, Gulma, Pāndu (anaemia) and Udara (abdominal disorder) should not be subjected to Vamana (emis- sion). (Su. ci. 33). Which ever cures the disease also alleviates the Dosa. When the disease is pacified, the causative dosa is also pacified. Otherwise the disease would not have been cured as the cause siezes to exist when the effect siezes. This may not be so correct according to some; because the dosa is the either inherent or occasioning cause of the disease and not only when the inherent and occasioning causes sieze, the effect siezes but also it siezes when the non inherent cause siezes. As the kapālamāla the inherent cause when it is destroyed, Ghaṭa the effect, also siezes to exist. In the same manner, by the destruction of Samprapti (pathogenesis), the dis- ease also destroyed. Dosa is also pacified by itself or by some other means in this process. If one agrees that which ever is antagonistic to Vyadhi (disease) is also antagonistic to Dosa, then, there need not be another type of treatment which is called Ubhaya pratyanīka (Antagonistic to both Vyādhi and Doṣa). True, if Doṣa is the Nimitta Kāraṇa (occassioning reason), how is it mitigated by Vamana (emesis) etc., which are deployed to mitigate the disease caused by it? We are not seeing the siezure of the existance of the pot by the destruction of Danda (stick used to move the potter's wheel) and the Kulala (the potter). It is said that as long as the effect is at the stage of depending on the Nimitta kāraṇa (occassioning reason), the siezure of the that (occassioning) Kāraṇa (reason) results in the siezure of the kārya (ef- fect), as the light in the lamp extinguishes by destruction of wick and the oil. Same is the case with Dosa also. The example for Vyadhi Viparita Anna (food that is antagonistic to the disease) is giving bengal gram which is astringent in diarrhoea. The example for Vyadhi Viparita Vihara (behavioural aspect that is antagonistic to the disease) is Pravāhaṇaṃ (applying internal pressure) in Udāvarta (flatulance). Chanting of Mantra (the sacred verses), Auṣadhi dhāraṇa (tying of medicinal herbs to the wrist, neck, loin etc.), Bali (sacrificing the animals), Niyama (following cer¬ tain hard and fast regulations) Prāyaścitta (prostrating) Homa (performing sacred pyres) Gurudeva Susrusa (obedient-serving of master and Gods) etc., also come under vyādhi viparīta vihāra according to Vāpyacandra. Now, the Hetu Vyādhi Viparītkarī (factors that are antagonistic to both the cause and the disease)-Auṣadha (medicine)-giving Dasamula (ten roots-Bilva etc.) in Vata Sotha (inflammation caused by Vāta) which is anti inflammatory and also anti Vāta. Caraka coined Paṭalā (Steriospermum suaveolens) etc., ten drugs (the ten roots) as anti inflammatory- Ca. su 4. Anna (food, that is antagonistic to both cause and the disease)-giving Takra (butter-milk) in grahaṇī (sprue) caused by Vāta kapha, Peyā (gruel) in fever caused by Sītavāta which, by having uṣṇa vīrya, nullifies vāta and by prabhāva (special effect), cures fever. As said in Caraka, peya (gruel) etc., are antagonistic to fever because they are homologous in fever. Susruta also supports this-''In fever and diarrhoea, Yavāgū (porridge) is always good. Vihāra (behavioural aspect that is antagonistic to cause and the disease)—awakening (not sleeping) in nights which is dry in nature, in drowsiness caued by day sleep, which is Snigdha (oily) in nature. Now, the Hetuviparītarthakārī (that factor which looks like being similar to the cause of the disease, but does antagonistic action) medicine-Applying hot poultice in Pitta predominant inflammatory wound, food-giving foods that cause burning sensation in inflammatory wound when it is in a ripening stage (when pitta is ac¬ tive) and Vihāra, the behavioural aspect-threatening the patient in insanity caused by Vāta. The examples for Vyādhi viparītārthakāri (factors that are similar to the disease but antagonistic to the disease)-medicine-administering Madanaphala (Randia dumatorum, the emetic nut) in chardi (nausea and vomitting), food-giving milk which is laxative in diarrhoea. (Caraka also says in Pitta type of diarrhoea where many impurities are accumulated the patient should be given purgation therapy by giving milk. Ca. ci. 19) and regarding the behavioural aspect in this connection— attempting to vomit by applying internal pressure in nausea and vomitting. Now, the examples for Hetuvyadhiviparitarthakari (factors that are similar to the cause and the disease but mitigate same disease)-medicine-applying warm-natured Aguru (aquillaria agallocha) etc., lepa (external application) in burnt wounds. And also giving poison in the poisoning case, food-giving alcohol in the intoxication caused by consumption of alcohol and the example for behavioural aspect-advising excercise in the form of swimming in Saṃmūdhavāta (immobility of the bodily limbs) caused by bodily excercise. If a patient is eligible for emesis and suffering from nausea and vomitting due to over accumulation of kapha and in such condition if he is not given emetic, the disease will continue for a long time or the disease will not at all be alleviated. Then, the emision, at this juncture, is to be considered only as Dosa pratyanīka (antagonīstic to Doṣa). Suśruta also supports this— ''In vomittings caused by multiple Doşas (impurities), Vamana (emisis) is advisable''. (Su. u. 49). By expelling Ama (undigested food stuffs) with help of laxation caused by giving milk in Amātisara (Diarrhoea due to undigested foods) it is understood that the cause of the disease is mitigated. In the same way, it is considered as hetupratyanīka (an¬ tagonistic to the cause) when cauterisation is done in burnt wound where the blood either rushes to the other place or dissolves without getting accumulated at the site of the burn. Susruta says-''The blood, when afflicted by heat (burning), gets aggrevated fast and with the same pace, vitiates Pitta''. (Su. sū. 12). Cold therapy is also to be avoided as it facilitates Coagulation of blood. In support of this argument Suśruta says, ‘‘By nature, the cold water application coagulates the blood and warm applications are good at this stage. The cold applications are not at all advisable (Su. Su. 12) In poisoning caused by poisonous material of mobile sources (snakes etc.), giving static poison (roots etc.) is to be considered as only antagonistic to the cause (of the disease). It is said in Caraka–‘‘Poison acts as antidote to poison due to the Prabhava (special effect). Whatever upward or downward expulsion of impuri¬ ties, is also characterised by Prabhāva, the special effect. In alcoholic intoxication, the Madya (alcohol) which is to be given as antidote is not the same alcohol but the one which is prepared with Mātulunga (citrus medica) etc, as explained in Suśruta. Or, in the intoxication caused by dry type of alcohol like Mādhvīka (prepared with Madhuca indica), the alcohol prepared with oily Pista (flour) etc., are to be admin- istered. This is also considered as Hetuviparita (antagonistic to the cause, as the drugs are different in the therapeutic alcohol). As mentioned in Susruta, As the individual punished by the king, has to be consoled by none other than the king himself, in the same way the one who is fallen by alcoholic intoxication has to be rescued with only alcohol and nothing else.'' (Su. u. 47). In saying so Suśruta means Pañcanidānalaksana that even the therapeutic alcohol also belongs to the same alcoholic group. As re- gards to the suimming in Urustambha (gripping in the thighs—due to the cold qual- ity of water the bodily heat comes out and dissolves the solidified Medas (fat) and Slesma (in which form they generated the disease) and the bodily excertion caused by swimming dries them up, consequently relieving the Vātaaccumulation and there by relief of the disease take place. This process also comes under hetupratyanīka (antagonistic to the cause). In the light of this explanation all the tadarthakari¬ illustrations come under hetuviparita category only. It is told that to propose the subtle difference in the nature, the elders of Ayurveda had shown seperate group of tadarthakari medicine, food and behavioural aspect. The differentiation is, here, an- tagonistic to the disease but into the cause. Anupasaya is the negative trial where the above experimentations fail and consequently the disease is not cured. It is also known as Asātmya (non-homologous) to the disease (diseased person). By mentioning Vyādhi (disease), the doşa is also implied. Anupaśaya also is useful in knowing about the dis- ease. If not, it is not necessary to mention this factor. And if it has to be also included the number of diagnostic factors should have been mentioned as six and not as five. But it is also mentioned as an important factor to know the disease. Caraka says, the inexplicit picture of the disease is to be examined with the help of upasaya (positive trial) and Anupasaya (negative trial)(Ca. vi. 4). This factor can be included in the Nidana (aetiology) as it aggravates the disease of the dosa and thus, there is no question of considering anupaśaya as the sixth factor. In many places it is said that a disease will not be cured (has the Anupaśaya effect) when the incumbant is induced with the items mentioned in Nidana, the aetiology. This is about upasaya, the positive trial. Samprāpti- The pathogenesis

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2):

आमज्वरस्य लिङ्ग़ानि, दद्यात्तत्र भेषजम् । भेषजं - ह्यामदोषस्य - भूयो - ज्वलयति - ज्वरम् ॥63॥
answer_text: From the point of pathogenesis, the above types of fever have been described as being antarvega (internally motivated) and bahirvega (that is externally motivated). Features of both these types have been described here through various symptoms. First the term śvasana is to be noted. Generally, this term refers to the problem of breathing or dyspnea. In place of the term svasana some read sadana (myalgia or muscular rheumatism). However, this version is not acceptable to Jejjaṭa, the commentator. At one place, Suśruta has accepted the antarvega as a serious (gambhira) disease and has stated that savasana or 'dyspnea' is the predominant sign in this type of fever. The term vinigraha suggests the situation of hindrance in expulsion. It might relate to constipation or release of faccal matter and impurities. Thirst etc. means the features like the morbid thirst, delirium etc. The term Mardava signifies a lesser intensity of these symptoms. By saying that bahirvega fever is easily curable, it is implied that the former, the antarvega, is difficult to cure or it is incurable as also indicated by Suśruta, ‘The wise physician should leave a patient with serious and high-temperature fever without treating him as this is incurable. (SS. Ut.39.94). Āma (undigested), Pacyamāna (digesting) and Nirāma (digested) fevers Profuse production of the saliva, nausea, feeling of heaviness in the heart, drowsiness, lassitude, indigestion, distaste, heaviness in the body, loss of appetite, excessive urination, rigidity in the limbs and strong fever are the features of Ama Jvara that is the fever caused by dosas that have association of Ama (undigested food). One should not opt for medicine in such condition as the medicine itself could induce more fever. Temperature, excessive thirst, delirium, dyspnea, giddiness, passing of faces and vomiting sensation are the symptoms of Pacyamāna (digesting) fever. The features of Nirāma (digested) fever include such symptoms as agitated appetite, weakness, lightness of the body, less temperature, outward movement of the doṣas. 61-63
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2.

त्रिवृच्छ्यामाऽर्डचन्द्रा च पालिन्दी च सुषेणिका । मसूरविदला काली कैषिका कालमेषिका ।।१९५।। श्यामा त्रिवृत्ततो हीनगुणा तीव्रविरेचिनी । मूर्च्छादाहमदभ्रान्तिकण्ङ्गोत्कर्षणकारिणी ।।१९६।। लघुदन्ती विशल्या च स्यादुदुम्बरपण्यपि । तथैरण्डफला शीघ्रा श्येनघण्टा घुणप्रिया । १९७ । । वाराहाङ्गी च कथिता निकुम्भश्च मकूलकः । द्रवन्ती शम्बरी चित्रा प्रत्यक्पर्ण्याखुपर्ण्यपि ।।१९८ ।। उपचित्रा श्रुतश्रोणी न्यग्रोधी च तथा वृषा । दन्तीद्वयं सरं पाकं रसे च कटु दीपनम् ।।१९९।। गुदाङ्क्राश्मशूलास्रकण्डूकुष्ठविदाहनुत् । तीक्ष्णोष्णं हन्ति पित्तास्रकफशोथोदरक्रिमीन ।। २ ० ० ।। जयपालो दन्तिबीज विख्यात तिन्तिडीफलम् । जयपालो गुरुः स्निम्धो रेची पित्तकफापहः ।।२०२११

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Nidanasthana, Chapter 2, verse 55):

( सु. उ. ३९) रसरक्ताश्रितः साध्यो मांसमेदोगतश्र यः । अस्थिमज्जगतः कृच्छुः शुक्रस्थस्तु न सिध्यति ।।’१।।) ( च. चि. अ. ३) मधुकोश: उक्तवातादिज्वराणां धातुविशेषदूष्यतयाऽधिकलक्षणानि भवन्ति; यदुक्तः ‘वातपित्तकफोत्थानां ज्वराणां लक्षणं यथा । तथा तेषां भिषग्ब्रयाद्रसादिष्वपि बुद्धिमान्’ (सु. उ. अ. ३९) इति; एतदभिधानं च रसादिधात्वविरोधेन वातादिचिकित्साकरणार्थम्; अतस्तानाह—गुरुतेत्यादि । हृदयोत्क्लेशः हृदयस्थितदोषस्योपस्थितवमनत्वमिव, रसस्य हृदयस्थत्वात् । रसस्य इत्यनेन विशेषेणात्र रसो दूष्यः, सर्वेषामेव ज्वराणा रसानुगत्वात् दैन्य क्लान्त- चित्तत्वम् । पिण्डिकेत्यादि । पिण्डिका जान्वधो जङ्वामांसपिण्डः, तस्या उद्वेष्टनं दण्डादिना पीडनेनेव वेदना पिण्डिकोद्वेष्टनम्; एवमन्यत्रापि । सृष्टमूत्रपुरीषता प्रवर्तमानमूत्रपुरीषता र् । ऊष्मा बहिः, एतच्च विशेषपर, प्रायः सर्वज्वरेषु तथाभावात् । ‘ऊष्माऽन्तर्मोहविक्षेपौ’ इति पाठान्तरे ऊष्माऽन्तः अन्तर्दाह इत्यर्थः, विक्षेपो हस्तादिचालनम् । भृशं स्वेद इति घर्मस्य मेदोमलत्वात्; तद्विकृत्यैव दौर्गन्ध्यं गात्रे । असहिष्णुता वेदनाया असहत्वं, क्रोधनत्वमिति कार्तिक: । भेदोऽस्थ्नामिति भेद इव भेदः भङ्गवत्पीडेत्यर्थः, (परपदार्थेषु प्रयुज्यमानाः शब्दा वृत्ति (वृत्ति) मन्तरेणापि वृत्त्य (वृत्य)थ्र्षं गमयन्ति'') यथा—अग्निर्माणवकः । एवमन्यत्रापि भेदादौ द्रष्टव्यम् । कुजनं कुन्यनं; कुझनंम्' इति पाठान्तरेऽस्थ्नामेव संकोच इत्यर्थः । तम:प्रवेशनम् अन्यकारप्रविष्टस्येवासंवित्तिः । महाश्वासः श्वासाधिकारे वक्ष्यमाणलक्षणः । मर्मशब्देन हृदयमुच्यते, प्राधान्यादिति कार्तिक:; तस्य छेद इव मर्मच्छेद: । मरणमित्यादि शुक्रगतस्य । तत्रैतेषु रसादिधातुगतज्वरेषु मध्ये शुक्रस्थानगते मरणं प्रात्नुयादिति योज्यम् । शुक्रं च तत्स्थानं चेति शुक्रस्थानं; (न तु शुक्रस्य स्थानं शुक्रस्थानं ), शुक्रस्य सर्वदेहगत्वेन नियतस्थानासम्भवादिति कार्तिक: । यदुक्तं—‘यथा पयसि सर्पिस्तु गुडश्रेक्षुरसे’ यथा । शरीरेषु १. अस्याप्रे 'रोगप्रभावात्' इत्यधिकमातङ्कदर्पणे । २. अयं पाठ: ख पुस्तके नोपलभ्यते । ३. 'अस्फुटध्वनि:' इति पा. । ४. अयं पाठ: क ख पुस्तकयोनोपलभ्यते । ५. ‘गुणश्चेक्षो रसो’ इति पा. । तथा नृणां शुक्रं विद्याद्विषग्वर:'—(सु. शा. अ. ४ इति) विशेषत इति पदेन शुक्रस्य बाहुल्येन विसर्गः, अन्यस्यापि रक्तादेरिति वदन्ति ।।४८-५४।। वर्षाशरद्वसन्तेषु वाताद्यैः प्राकृतः क्रमात् । वैकृतोऽन्यः स दुःसाध्यः प्राकृतश्चानिलोद्धवः ।।५५।।
answer_text: Heaviness, nausea, exhaustion, vomitting, distaste and depression are the signs and symptoms when the fever is attached to the Rasa Dhatu (chyle). Dribbling of blood, burning sensation, delusion, vomitting, giddiness, irrelevant talk, bullae on the skin and thirst are seen when the fever is lodged in the Rakta (blood). Squeezing sensation in the calf muscles, thirst, excessive defaecation and micturition, heat on the body, internal burning sensation, falling down and fatigue are the features of Mamsagata Jvara (fever seated in the muscle tissue). Profuse sweat, thirst, syn¬ cope, irrelevant talk, vomitting, bad odour of the body, distatste, fatigue and intol¬ erance are seen in fever seated in medas (fat). Breaking sensation in the bones, wheezing sounds in breathe, diarrhoea, vomitting, inability to up keep the bodily limbs are present in fever which is made room in the Asthi (bone). Feeling of dark- ness, hiccup, cough, cold, vomitting, internal burning, severe dyspnoea and cutting pain in the vital parts are the signs and symptoms in fever situated in Majjā (mar- row). One will die when fever gets seated in Sukra (semen); there will be rigidity in the penis and profuse flow of semen in this condition. 48, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53, 54 (Su. u. 39) Fever, situated in Rasa (chyle), Rakta (blood), Māṃṣa (muscle) and Medas (fat) is curable while it is difficult for cure when situated in Asthi (bone) and majja (marrow). Sukrastha Jvara (fever lodged in the semen) is incurable. 55 (Ca. ci. 3) The Dosa- predominant fevers exhibit the features basing also on the tissue in which the fever is lodged. As said by Susruta, the physician should also know the qualities of fevers seated in various tissues like Rasa (chyle) etc. as those of Tridoşa origin (Su. u. 39). This is to plan the treatment without disturbing the tissues. Hrdayotklesa is the vomitting sensation that is felt like the Dosa seated in the heart is ready for expulsion, which is because the Rasa the main victim in fever is seated in the heart only. By saying ''Rasastha' it is implied that Rasa (chyle) is the exclusively vitiated factor here unlike the other fevers where Rasa is generally vitiated and spread the temperature all over the body. Profuse sweat in Medas- based fever is because sweat is the waste product (Mala) of the Medas (fat). Mahā Svāsa is the severe type of dyspnoea. Marmaccheda is the tearing pain in the vital part, heart, according to Kārtika. It is to be understood that death occurs when fever is seated in the Sukra, the semen. The place of Sukra is not specified particularly as it exists in the body like Ghee (clarified butter) in milk and jaggery (sugar?) in the juice of sugarcane (Su. śū. 4). 'अस्फुटध्वनि:' इति पा. । ४. अयं पाठ: क ख पुस्तकयोनोपलभ्यते । ५. ‘गुणश्चेक्षो रसो’ इति पा. । तथा नृणां शुक्रं विद्याद्विषग्वर:'—(सु. शा. अ. ४ इति) विशेषत इति पदेन शुक्रस्य बाहुल्येन विसर्गः, अन्यस्यापि रक्तादेरिति वदन्ति ।।४८-५४।। वर्षाशरद्वसन्तेषु वाताद्यैः प्राकृतः क्रमात् । वैकृतोऽन्यः स दुःसाध्यः प्राकृतश्चानिलोद्धवः ।।५५।।
