question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 151):

अवल्गुजो बाकुची स्यात्सोमराजी सुपर्णिका । शशिलेखा कृष्णफला सोमा पूतिफलीति च ।।२०६।। सोमवल्ली कालमेषी कुष्ठघ्नी च प्रकीर्त्तिता । बाकुची मधुरा तिक्ता कटुपाका रसायनी ।। २०७ ! । विष्टम्भहद्धिमा रुच्या सरा श्लेष्मास्रपित्तनुत् । रूक्षा हृद्या श्वासकुष्ठमेहज्वरकृमिप्रणुत् ।। २०८ ।। तत्फल पित्तल कुष्ठकफानिलहरं कटु । केश्यं त्वच्यकृमिश्वासकासशोथामपाण्डुनुत् ।। २०९।।
answer_text: Diseases of oral cavity: The gargles of rasāñjana with water, are beneficial in the Mükha and Gala roga (Ailments of the mouth and throat). Menstrual diseases: Its enema is beneficial in Sveta Pradara (Leucorroea). Eye diseases: In the diseases of the eyes like Netrābhiṣyanda (Conjuntivitiṣ), it is applied on the eyelids and mixed with rose water, can be instilled into the eyes, External uses: In case of Upadaṁśa (Gonorrhoea) Rasāñjana along with Śīrīṣa Haritaki and Madhu applied externally. In case of Raktarsas (Bleeding piles), it is applied externally. Mātra (Dosage): 500mg- 2gm. BĀKUCĪ Latin: Psoralea corylifolia Linn. Fam: Fabaceae Hindi: Bakuchi, Somaraji ng: Psoralea seed Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Avalgujā, Somarājī, Suparṇikā, Ṣaśilekshā, Kṛṣṇā phalā, Somā, Pūṭiphalī, Sōmavallī, Kālamēṣikī and Kuṣṭhaghnī. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Bākucī is Madhurā (Sweet) and Tiktā (Bitter) in taste, Katu vipāka (Pungent in post digestive), Rāsayana (Rejuvenators), Vistambi (Relieves Constipation), Rucya (Promotes taste), Sāra (Laxative), Subsides Pitta and Rakta dosa, Rūkṣā (Drying) and Hṛdya (Useful in cardiac disease). It cures Swāsa (Dysponea), Kuṣta (Leprosy), Prameha (Diabeties), Jwara (Fever) and Kṛmi (Worm infestations). It’s Fruits Increses Pitta dosa, Subsides Kapha and Vāta doṣa, Kaṭu (Pungent) in taste, Kesya (Good for hairs) and Twachya (Good for Skin). It cures Kuşta (Leprosy), Krmi (Worm infestations), Swāsa (Dyspnoea), Kāsa (Cough), Sotha (Inflammation), Āma (Undigested food) & Pāṇḍu (Anemia). Utpattisthāna(Natural territory): This is common in Bengal and all over the plains of India. 12 JA-413 Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is an erect annual herb reaches upto 2-4ft. high. Trunk is straight with gland dotted. Leaves are simple, 2.5 cm-7.5cm long, broadly- elliptical round, toothed margins, acuminate apex, glabrous & tomentosed on both sides with black dots. Flowers are arranged in axillary racemes blue in colour. Fruit is indehiscent subglobose pod measures about 0.5cm contains oblong, flat brown seeds. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Bīja (Seeds). Chemical constituents: Crystalline substances Psoralen, Iso-psoralen, Essential oils and Resins
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 151

Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Haritakyadi Varga, Chapter 1, verse 113):

उक्त कुटजबीजंत यवमिन्द्रयवं तथा । कलिङ्गं चापि क्रालिङ्गं तथा भद्रयवा अपि ।।१५६।। क्वचिदिन्द्रस्य नामैव भवेत्तदभिधायकम् । फलानीन्द्रयवास्तस्य तथा भव्रयवा अपि ।।१५७।। इन्द्रयवं त्रिदोषघ्नं संग्राहि कटु शीतलम् । । १५८ । । ज्वरातीसाररक्ताशोंदमिवीसर्पकुष्ठनुत् । दीपनं गुदकीलास्रवातास्वश्लेष्मशूलजित् ।। १५९।।
answer_text: Fam: Apocynaceae Latin: Holorrhena antidysentica Wall. Seeds Eng: Seeds of Kutaja Hin: Indrajava Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Kutajabīja, Yava, Indrayava, Kaliñga, Kāliñga and, Bhadra yavā. It has all synonyms of Indra and Its fruits are know as Indrayava and Bhadrayavā. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): It subsides all three doṣas, Grāhī (Absorbent), Kaṭu (Pungent) in taste, Sītavīrya (Cold in potency). It cures Jwara (Fever), Atisāra (Diarrhoea), Raktātisāra (Bloody diarrhoea), Arśas (Piles), Chardi (Vomiting), Visarpa (Herpes) and Kuṣta (Leprosy), it acts as Dīpana (Appetizers) and also cures Gudakeela (Peduncle in anus), Diseases of Rakta, Vātarakta (Gout), Diseases of Kapha ( doşa and Sūla (Abdominal colic). question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Dhanya Varga, Chapter 8, verse 806):

रक्तशालिवरस्तेष् बल्यो वर्ण्यखिदोषजित् । चक्षुष्यो मून्रलः स्वर्यः शुक्रलस्तृड्ज्वरापहः ।।१५।। विषव्रणश्वासकासदाहनुद् वह्निपुष्टिदः । तस्मादल्यान्तरगुणाः शालयो महदादयः ।।१६।। वर्षिका कण्डिताः शुक्ला ब्रीहयश्चिरपाकिनः । कृष्णब्रीहिः पाटलश्च कुक्कुटाण्डक इत्यपि ।।१७११ शालामुखो जतुमुख इत्याद्या ब्रीहयः स्मृताः । कृष्णव्रीहिः स विज्ञयो यत्कृष्णतुषतण्डुलः ।।१८।। पाटलः पाटलापुष्पवर्णको ब्रीहिरुच्यते । कुक्कुटाण्डाकृतिब्रीहिः कुक्कुटाण्डक उच्यते ।।१९।। शालामुखः कृष्णश्रूकः कृष्णतण्डुल उच्यते । लाक्षावर्गं मुखं यस्य ज्ञेयो जतमुखस्तु सः ।।२०११ व्रीहयः कथिताः पाके मधुरा वीर्यतो हिमाः । अल्पाभिष्यन्दिनो बद्धवर्चस्काः षष्टिकैः समाः ।। कृष्णव्रीहिर्वरस्तेषां तस्मादल्पगुणाः परे ।।२१।। गर्भस्था एव ये पाकं यान्ति ते षष्टिका मताः 11 २ २ 1 1 षष्टिकः शतपुष्पश्च प्रमोदकमुकुन्दकों । महाषष्टिक इत्याद्याः षष्टिकाः समुदाहताः ।। एतेऽपि ब्रीहयः प्रोक्ता ब्रीहिलक्षणदर्शनात् ।।२३।। षष्टिका मधुराः शीता लघवो वद्धवर्चसः । वातपित्तप्रशमनाः शालिभिः सदृशा गुणैः ।। २४।। षष्टिका प्रवरा तेषा लघ्वी स्निग्धा त्रिदोषजित् ।। २५ ।। स्वाद्वी मृद्दी याहिणी च बलदा ज्वरहारिणी । रक्तशालिगुणैस्तुल्या ततः स्वल्यगुणाः परे ।।२६.।।
answer_text: Rakta śāli (red variety of rice) is the best quality. It is Balya (Promotes strength), Vrnya (Promotes complexion), subsides all Tridosas, Cakṣuṣyā (Good for eyes), Mutrala (Diuretic), Swarya (Improves voice) and Sukrala (Improves seman) and Agnipustida (Appetizers). It cures Tṛṣṇā (Thrist), Jvara (Fever), Viṣa (Posionous manifestations), Vṛṇa (Wounds), Swāsa (Dyspnoea), Kāsa (Cough) and Dāha (Burning sensation). Mahaśāli etc, other varieties are compartively possess lessar qualties. Vrihik Dhānyam: Rice which is grown in Varşă rutu, it becomes white after pounding and which is hard to digest is know as Vrihi dhānya. Vrihik Dhānyam bheda (Varieties of Vrihi dhānya): Kṛṣṇā Vṛihī, Pāṭala, Kukutānadkā, Sālāmukha, Jatumukha etc. Krşna vrihi in which both husk and grains are black in colour. Pāṭala vrihi is that which resembles that of Pātāla puṣpā, Kukuṭānaḍkā vrihi is that which appear like size of a hens egg, Śālāmukha has spikes at the edges and both husk and grain parts are black in colour, Jatumukha has appear red like Läkṣa Guṇa karma (Properties and indication): Vrīhi dhānya is Madhura vipāka(Sweet in post digestive), Sīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Abhiṣyandi (Blocks the channels), Constipitive, Pouştika (Nutritive). In these Vrīhi dhānyas Kṛṣṇa vrihi is considered as best and othes are compartively lesser in qualties. Ṣaṣṭika Dhānya Latin: Oryza sativa Linn. Fam: Gramineae Hin: Chaval ng: Paddy A grain that gets germinated within the ovule and which is mature in duration of sixty days is know as Sastika Sastika Dhānya bheda (Varieties of Ṣasṭika Dhānya): Ṣatapuṣpā, Pramodaka, Mukuñdaka, Mahāṣaṣṭika etc. They are also called as Vrihi, because it has possess qualities similar to that of Vrihi dhanya. Guna karma (Properties and indication): Sastika dhanya is Mādhura (Sweet) in taste, Sīta vīrya (Cold in potency), Laghu (Light for digestion), Constipative, Subsides Vata and Pitta, qualities are similar to Salī Dhānya. Amongest all Sastika is considered the best. They are Laghu (Light in digestionaction), Snigdha (Oilyness), subsides Tridoṣas, Swādu (Palatable), Mrudu (Soft), Grāhī (Absorbent), Bālya (Promotes strength) and cures Jwara (Fever), properties are similar to Rakta śalī and remaining Ṣasṭika dhanya are posses lesser qualities. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Native to the tropics and subtropics of Southeast Asia. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is an annual grass, grow in a tuft of upright culms up to 2 m or more tall, with long, flat leaf blades. Flowers in terminal panicles. Fruit grain in spikelets, which each contain a solitary flower (that forms into a solitary kernel of grain), are sparse along the stem rather than forming dense clusters

question:

तुलसी सुरसा ग्राम्या सुलभा बहुमझरी । अपेतराक्षसी गौरी भूतघ्नी देवदुन्दुभिः ।।६२।। तुलसी कटुका तिक्ता हद्योष्णा दाहपित्तकृत् । दीपनी कुष्ठकृच्ड्रास्रपार्श्वर्सकफवातजित् ।। शुक्ला कृष्णा च तुलसी गुणैस्तुल्या प्रकीर्तिता ।।६३१।
answer_text: Digestive diseases: Leaves and flowers are indicated in Agnimāndya (Dyspepsia), Vibanda (Constipation) and Krmi (Worm infestations). The swarasa of the leaves is used to treat Krmi (Worm infestations) and Kāmalā (Jaundice). Respiratory disease: Leaf juice extract is used as Nasya to relieve, Pinasa (Common cold) associated with Sirasūla (Headache). Febrifuge action: Extracted leaf juice is used to cure Chaturtaka jwara (Intermittent fever). Mental illness: Leaf juice extract Nasya is also used in the treatment of Apasmāra (Epilepsy). Eye disease: Leaf juice is given internally and externally in Ratry dṛṣṭi (Nightblind ness). Mātrā (Dosage): Patra swarasa: 10-20ml., Kwātha: 50-100 ml. SUKLA AND KRSNĀ TULASĪ Latin: Ocimum sanctum Linn. Fam: Lamiaceae Hin: Tulasi Eng: Holy Basil Paryāynāma (Synonyms): Surasā, Grāmyā, Sulabh, Bahumañjarī, Apetarāksasī, Gourī, Bhūtaghnī and Devadundubhi. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Tulasī is Kaṭu (Pungent), Tikṭā (Bitter) in taste, Hṛdya (Useful in Cardiac diseases), Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), Dāha pittakrut (Subsides burning sensation and pitta doṣa), Dīpana (Appetizers). It cures Kuṣṭa (Leprosy), Mūtrakṛcchra (Dysuria), Diseases of Rakta, Pāśvaśūla (Pain in flanks) and Diseases of Kapha and Vāta. Both varieties have got similar Pharmacological actions. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It varies from sea level to an altitude of 2000 m. It is found growing naturally in moist soil nearly all over the globe. Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a much branched, fragrant, woody, erect, hairy herb, reaches upto 0.75-1m high. Leaves are nearly round up to 5 cm long, acute apex, entire or toothed margin. Flowers are arranged in axillary racemes, small purple - reddish in colour. Fruits are small subglobose or broadly oblong contains, yellow - reddish colour seeds. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Pañcāṅga (Whole plant). Chemical constituents: Leaves contain volatile oil. It contains Eugenol, Methyl eugenol, Carvacrol and Caryophyllene
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Puspa Varga, Chapter 4, verse 531
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Puspa Varga, Chapter 4, verse 531.

S. 17.18) Premonitory features of hikkā include heaviness of throat and chest, astringent taste in the mouth and gurgling noise in the abdomen. 5

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 15):

कफजामाहतन्द्रेत्यादि । आस्यमाधुर्यं मुखस्य मधुररसत्वम् । सन्तोष इति सन्तोष इव सन्तोषः अन्नानभिलाष इत्यर्थः तृप्तो हि नान्रमभिलषति । अरुचिरभ्यवहारासामर्थ्यम् । स्वादु मधुरम् । विशुद्धमतिशुभ्रं सुश्रुते शुक्लं हिमं सान्द्रकफं कफेन । सु०उ० इति पाठात् ।।८॥ शूलाविपाकारुचि-दाह-तृष्णा-श्वास-प्रमोहप्रबला प्रसक्तम् । छर्दिस्त्रिदोषाल्लवणाम्ल-नील-सान्द्रोष्ण-रक्तं वमतां नृणां स्यात् ॥॥ -
answer_text: The passage starting from tandra refers to the peculiar characteris¬ tics of the chardi that has been caused due to kapha. There is a feeling of santosa or satisfaction of having eaten a complete meal after which there is no desire of eating more. White colour of the vomited material is due to kapha. As opined by Suśruta, ‘in kapha variety of chardi, the vomited stuff is white and cold and it contains dense kapha’ (SS. Ut. 49.11). Tridoṣa type of chardi (CS. Ci. S. 20.15) A person with vomiting has a persistent and severe colic pain, indi¬ gestion, anorexia, a burning sensation, thirst, dyspnea and fainting. In addition, he brings out salted, sour, bluish, thick, warm, and san¬ guineous vomit. 9
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 15.
context: कफजामाहतन्द्रेत्यादि । आस्यमाधुर्यं मुखस्य मधुररसत्वम् । सन्तोष इति सन्तोष इव सन्तोषः अन्नानभिलाष इत्यर्थः तृप्तो हि नान्रमभिलषति । अरुचिरभ्यवहारासामर्थ्यम् । स्वादु मधुरम् । विशुद्धमतिशुभ्रं सुश्रुते शुक्लं हिमं सान्द्रकफं कफेन । सु०उ० इति पाठात् ।।८॥ शूलाविपाकारुचि-दाह-तृष्णा-श्वास-प्रमोहप्रबला प्रसक्तम् । छर्दिस्त्रिदोषाल्लवणाम्ल-नील-सान्द्रोष्ण-रक्तं वमतां नृणां स्यात् ॥॥ -

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Dhanya Varga, Chapter 8, verse 796):

शालिधान्यं ब्रीहिधान्यं शूकधान्यं तृतीयकम् । शिम्बीधान्यं क्षुद्रधान्यमित्युक्तं धान्यपञ्चकम् ।।१।। शालयो रक्तशाल्याद्या व्रीहयः षष्टिकादयः । यवादिक श्रूकधान्यं मुद्राद्यंशिम्बिधान्यकम् ।। कड्गवादिक क्षुद्रधान्यं तृणधान्यक्ष तत्स्मृतम् ।। १।।
answer_text: Dhānyas are mainly classified into five: a. Śāli dhānya. b. Vrīhi dhānya c. Śūka dhānya d. Śimbī dhānya e. Kṣudra dhānya. Śāli dhānya: It consist Rakta śāli (Red variety rice) etc. Vrīhi dhānya: It contains Saṣtika sali (Rice which matures in sixty days) etc. Śūka dhānya: It consists Barley etc cereals. Śimbī dhānya: It consists Mudga (Green gram) etc. Ksudra dhānya: It consist Kanguni etc
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Dhanya Varga, Chapter 8, verse 796
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Dhanya Varga, Chapter 8, verse 796.
context: शालिधान्यं ब्रीहिधान्यं शूकधान्यं तृतीयकम् । शिम्बीधान्यं क्षुद्रधान्यमित्युक्तं धान्यपञ्चकम् ।।१।। शालयो रक्तशाल्याद्या व्रीहयः षष्टिकादयः । यवादिक श्रूकधान्यं मुद्राद्यंशिम्बिधान्यकम् ।। कड्गवादिक क्षुद्रधान्यं तृणधान्यक्ष तत्स्मृतम् ।। १।।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 27):

मधुकोशः न केवलमेवविधं परमसाध्यं किंत्वन्यादुशमपीत्यत आह-उष्णाश्रुपात इत्यादि। पिडका च नेत्र इत्यन्त द्वित्वग्गतशुक्ले। तथाऽऽह विदेहः-'एकत्वग्गतमेवं स्याद् द्वित्वग्गतमिदं भवेत्। चोषोष्णस्त्रावदाहास्तु तृष्णा च पिडकोद्रमः’ इति। मुद्रनिभं च शुक्लमित्याकारेण, एतद्वित्वग्गतम्। तथा च विदेहः-‘व्यक्तमुद्रफलाकार’ शुक्ल द्वित्वग्गतं भवेत्’ इति। द्वित्रित्वग्गतस्याव्रणशुक्लस्य कृच्छुत्वे एतत् पिडकोद्रममुद्रफलाकारत्वेनैवासाध्यत्वं बोध्यम्। अन्ये पुनः सव्रणशुक्लस्य विच्छिन्नमध्यमित्यादिकमसाध्यलक्षणं वर्णयन्ति। अत्र पक्षे द्वित्वग्गतमिति केवलमेवा- साध्यलक्षणम्, एतन्न चावगाढमित्यस्य विपर्ययः। लोहितमन्ततः उष्णाश्रुपातः पिडिका चेत्यादि द्वित्वम्गतशुक्ल- लक्षणमिति; किंत्वियमत्रासंगतिः - विच्छिन्नमध्यं सच्छिन्न तद्यदि सच्छिन्नत्वं सव्रणशुक्लस्याभ्युपगम्यते, तदा निमग्नरूपमित्यनेनैव सिद्धत्वात् पुनरुक्त स्यात्, किंच सव्रणशुक्लानन्तरमस्य पाठो विफलः स्यात्। अन्ये तु सव्रणाव्रणशुंक्लविषयं सामान्यमसाध्यलक्षणमेतदाहुः; यथायोग्यतया क्वचिल्लिङ्गान्तरयोगेन च व्यवस्थेति च वर्णयन्ति। असाध्यत्वं विदेहादन्येषां मतेनाह-केचिदत्यिादि। तित्तिरिपक्षतुल्यमिति शबलम्, एतच्चानिषेधादनु- मंतम्॥ २६ ॥ श्वेतः समाक्रामति सर्वतो हि दोषेण यस्यासितमण्डलं च। तमक्षिपाकत्ययक्षिरोगं सर्वात्मकं वर्जयितव्यमाहुः॥ २७॥ ( सु.उ. ५ ) .
answer_text: Mādhavanidānaṃ Not only the above but also the avranasukra with the following symptoms be¬ come incurable and hence this added information in this stanza. The warmth in the tears and the vesicles in the eye occur when the śukra arises form the second layer as said by Videha- “The śukra originating in the second layer has the following symptoms-fuming sensation, warm discharge, burning sensation, thirst and association of vesicles”. The śukra taking the shape of a green gram occurs when it arises in the second layer, also as said by Videha, "when the sukra originates in the second layer, it takes the shape of a green gram”. The kṛcchrasādhyatā (difficulty for cure) is attributed to the śukra that originates in the second and third layers. This condition turns to incurability when it takes the shape of green gram and with origination of vesicles in the eye. Others take the sunken middle part of the cor¬ nea as the incurable symptom of Savranasukra also. As per this statement, the b origination of śukra in the second layer itself is a sign of incurability. This does not t oppose the curability symptom-"not being deep rooted". Being red in the ends, shedding warm tears and having vesicles in the eye are the symptoms of deeprooted śukra. Mentioning of broken centre part and having a hole is not necessary here. Having a hole indicates the Savraṇa śukla and this is understood by the word Nimagna rūpam (sunken centre part) which amounts to repetition and also useless to mention after Savraṇaśukra and the incurable symptoms of avraṇaśukra and as per suitability it has to be viewed with some difference of said symptoms. Incurability has been attributed here as per the view of others, which is indicated by the word “kecit”. Tittira pakṣa tulyam means black - which is not controversial. 26. Akṣipākātyaya (Panopthalmitis) When the total cornea is totally covered by the white colour that is resulted by the aggravation of doşa s, that condition is called akşipākātyaya caused by all the doşas and is not to be considered for treatment. 27. (Su.u.5)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 59, verse 27.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Taila Varga, Chapter 19, verse 1045):

अतसीतैलमानेयं ख़िग्धोष्णं कफपित्तकृत् । कटुपाकमचक्षुष्यं बल्यं वातहरं गुरु ।।१७।। मलकृद्रसतः स्वादु ग्राहि त्वग्दोषह्वद् घनम् ।।१८।। वस्तौ पाने तथाऽभ्यङ्गे नस्ये कर्णस्य पूरणे । अनुपानविधौ चापि प्रयोज्यं वातशान्तये ।।१९।।
answer_text: Atisi is Agneya (Fire like properties), Snigdha (Oilyness), Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency), Increases Kapha and Pitta, Kaṭu vipaka (Pungent in post digestive), Chaṣkuṣya (Good for eyes), Balya (Promotes strength), Increases Vāta doṣa, Malakrud (Promotes evacuation of stools), Madhura (Sweet) in taste, Grāhi (Absorbent) and Twakdoaṣaṛt (Cures diseases of skin). It is useful in procedures like Enemata, internal administration, external applicant, Nasal medication, administration in ear and used as Anupāna to subsides Vāta dosa. Note: Details about Atisī mentioned in Dhānya varga

कृच्छ्रात्पुन: पुनर्जन्तोरुष्णवातं ब्रुवन्ति तम् । (सु. उ. ५८) मधुकोश: उष्णवातमाह—व्यायामेत्यादि । व्यायामाद्विरोधिसौम्यधातुक्षयात्तेजोवृद्ध्या पित्तवृद्धिः । अनिलान्वितमनिल- संयुतम् । ‘अनिलावृतम्’, इति पाठान्तरं सुगमम् । सरक्तमीषल्लोहितम् ।।१५-१६।। पित्तं कफो द्वावपि वा संहन्येतेऽनिलेन चेत् ।।१७।।
answer_text: Due to excessive physical strain, walking and exposure to Sun, Pitta gets ag¬ gravated alongwith Vata and causes burning sensation in the bladder, penis and the anus resulting in down-ward flow of urine in the colour or turmeric or alongwith blood or there may be blood alone repeatedly with great difficulty. This is called, Uṣṇavāta (haematuria). 15, 16 (Su. u. 58) When urine comes out alongwith blood the colour will be slightly reddish. Mūtrasāda (Scanty urination)
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana, Chapter 31, verse 17.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 1) (Purvārdḍha, Chapter 1, verse 4):

निदानं पूर्वरूपाणि रूपाण्युपशयस्तथा । संप्राप्तिक्षेति विज्ञानं रोगाणां पश्चक्षा स्मृतम् ।।४।।
answer_text: Nidāna (aetiology), Pūrvarūpa (premonitory symptoms), Rūpa (symptomatology), Upaśaya (positive trial treatment), and Saṃprāpti (pathogenesis) are the five means of obtaining knowledge of diseases. These five principles, individually and collectively, help in diagnosing diseases. On the instruction of noble physicians, the valuable statements of various sages (of Ayurveda) are precisely compiled here containing complications, prognosis (bad¬ prognosis), aetiology and symptomatology of the diseases. This is used for deciding the diseases (This is called, the decider of diseases, Rogaviniscaya). For the physicians, who have no access to various treatises and also for those who are low in mental abilities, this will prove to be useful for understanding the diseases easily by them. 2, 3 Mādhavakara explains the content of this work and indicates its validity in the above two stanzas. The feit need for such a work containing, exclusively, the diagnostic principles of Ayurveda and the instruction of noble physicians as they also felt the importance of such work, this work which contains the details of upadrava (complications) etc. of diseases, is being composed by me- (by Mādhavakara). Upadrava is the complication of a disease which follows the main disease and can be cured with the same line of treatment meant for the main disease. Arista is the definite bad prognosis and on arising of which, the patient is bound to loose his life. Infact the five diagnostic principles, which will be detailed in the next stanza, are-Nidana, Purvarupa, Rupa, Upasaya and Samprapti. But, Upadrava, Arista, Nidāna and Liṅga are mentioned here as the contents. Upadrava and Ariṣṭa will be given in certain diseases wherever necessary. Nidana is causative factor of the dis¬ eases and Linga is the one by which the disease is known. The word Linga means by which the disease is known itself includes the four diagnostic principles other than Nidāna. Nidāna is sepārately told as it is the extrinsic factor. Though there are other works dealing with this subject, this book is a precise compilation of the sub- ject-matter, first of its kind, based on the valid statements of the sages. Munis or sages are those who are devoid of Rajas, the aggravating factor of the mind, by which they might over- say the facts and Tamas, the stupifying factor of the mind by which they might not percieve the truth at all. Whatever they pronounce would be the testimony and applicable to all times. As this work contains such valid state¬ ments, it will alone be useful for those who have no access to big treatises and have less intellect, in understanding/knowing the diseases easily. Nidāna (aetiology), Purvarūpa (premonitory symptoms/prodromata) Rūpa (signs and symptoms or symptomatology) upasaya (positive trial treatment) and Samprapti (pathogenesis) are the five means of getting the knowledge of diseases.4
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Purvārdḍha, Chapter 1, verse 4.
context: निदानं पूर्वरूपाणि रूपाण्युपशयस्तथा । संप्राप्तिक्षेति विज्ञानं रोगाणां पश्चक्षा स्मृतम् ।।४।।

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 899):

वाराही पित्तला बल्या कट्वी तिक्ता रसायनी । आयुःशुक्राग्निकृन्मेहकफकुष्ठानिलापहा ।।१०७।।
answer_text: Digestive disease: The stem is used to treat Sula (Abdominal colic), and Atisara (Diarrhoea). The powder of the dried tuber is mixed with rice powder and milk and boiled. It is given in Sotha (Inflammation) and Jalodara (Ascites). Diseases of Ear: The freshly expressed juice of the leaf of Mānakañda is warmed and used as ear drops to treat Karnaśūla (Earache). External uses: The leaf is made into poultice and applied externally in Sandhisūla (Joint pains) to relieve pain and swelling. Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrna: 5-10gm, Swarasa: 10-20ml. 66 JA-413 VĀRĀHIKANDA Guṇa Karma (Properties and indications): Vārāhā kanda increases Pitta dosa, Balya (Promotes strength), Kaṭu (Pungent) and Tikta (Bitter) in taste, Rāsayana (Rejuvenator), promotes Ayu (Life span), Sukra (Seman), Agni (Appetite) and cures Prameha (Diabeties), Diseases of Kapha and Vāta and Kuṣṭa (Leprosy). Note: Details of drug Vārāhikanda is explained in Guḍūcyādi varga
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 899
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 899.
context: वाराही पित्तला बल्या कट्वी तिक्ता रसायनी । आयुःशुक्राग्निकृन्मेहकफकुष्ठानिलापहा ।।१०७।।

answer_text: JALAJAMBUKĀ Latin: Eugenia heyneana Wall. Fam: Myrtaceae Hin: Chotijamun Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): The synonyms of Jalajambukā are Kṣudrajambū, Sūksmā patrā and Nādeyi. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): The fruit is Grāhī (Absorbent), Rūkṣā (Drying), cures diseases of kapha, pitta and Rakta and Dāha (Burning sensation). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): Throughout India along the river banks. Swarūpa (Botanical descríption): A small trees reaches upto 10 m. Bark is rough, greyish- brown in colour. Leaves are coriaceous, oppositely arranged, simple, oblong-lanceolate, acute apex and entire margin. Flower are white in axilliary cymes. Fruit- Berry, oblong-ellipsoid, 1 cm long, crowned by calyx lobes. Amayika prayoga (Therapeutic uses): Almost similar to Rājajambū, BADARĪ a. UNNĀVAH- SAUVĪRAM- RĀJABADARAM Latin: Zizyphus sativa Gaertn., Fam: Rhamnaceae Hin: Unnab b. KOLA- BADARĀ Latin: Zizyphus jujuba Lam. Fam: Rhamnaceae Eng: Indian jujube Hin: Ber c. KŞUDRA BADARI- KARKANDHU Latin: Zizyphus nummularia W & R. Fam: Rhamnaceae Hin: Jhar Beri Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): The term Karkañdhu is used in both masculine and feminine genders. Karkandh, Ajapriya, Kuhā, Koli, Viṣamā, and Ubhayakaṇtakā and that of Brhadbadarī are Phenilā, Kuvalā, Ghoṇtā and Sauvīra. The Bṛhadbadarī which is much smaller than Kṣudrabadarī is know as Kola. The Badara which is ripen, extremely sweet and larger is know as Souvira. It is Sitavīrya (Cold in potency), Bhedana (Purgative), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Sukrala (Increses quantity of seman) and Brhmana (Nourishing). It cures diseases of Pitta, Dāha (Burning sensation), Diseases of Rakta, Kṣaya (Emaciation) and Tṛṣṇā (Thrist). The similar sauvīra variety, which is smaller, Madhurā (Sweet in taste) when ripen is know as kola. lt is Grāhī (Absorbent), Rocana (Promotes taste), Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency), Increases kapha and pitta, Guru (Heavy for digestion), Sāra (Laxative) and Subsides vāta doṣa. Kṣudrabadarī is know as karkandhū. It is Amla (Sour), Tiktā (Bitter) and Kaṣāya (Astringent) and Kinchit Madhurā (Slightly sweet) in taste, Snigdha (Oilyness), Guru (Heavy for digestion) and subsides Vāta and Pitta. All varieties when dried it acts as Bhedaka (Purgative), Agnivardaka (Appetizers) and Laghu (Light for digestion). It cures Trsnā (Thrist), Klanti (Fatigue) and Raktavikara. Note: Mahatbadara has big fruits, identified as Zizyphus sativa Geartn. The second variety is know as kola has medium sized fruit and identified as Zizyphus jujuba Linn. Third variety is Kṣudrabadara, has very small fruits identified as Zizyphus nummularia W&A. otanical name Zizyphus sativa Geartn. Mahatbadara Zizyphus jujuba Lam. Medium sized fruits Zizyphus nummularia W & A Very small fruits sudrabadara

पाषाणभेदकोऽश्मघ्नो गिरिभिद्धिन्नयोजिनी । अश्मभेदो हिमस्तिक्तः कषायो बस्तिशोधनः ।।१८४।। भेदनो हन्ति दोषार्शोगुल्मकृच्छाश्महहुजः । योनिरोगान्प्रमेहांश्च प्लीहशूलव्रणानि च ।।१८५।।
answer_text: Respiratory disease: Decoction of leaves acts as bronchodilator and mucolytic used to break down phlegm and extra mucus. It is used to cure Pinasa (Common cold), Kāsa (Cough), Rājayakṣma (Tuberculosis), Swāsa (Dysponea) etc. chronic respiratory disorders. Paste of Bhārñgi prepared with Ghṛta and Madhu should be given for licking in case of Swāsa (Dyspnoea). In Pinasa (Common cold), and Kaphaja Swāsa (Dyspnoea), it is taken along with Sunthī and Vacā. Digestive disease: Bhārñgi root is collected in puṣya and pounded with Tushodaka. This is given orally to treat inguinal hernia. External uses: Root paste of Bhārñgi applied on forehead relieves Śirasūla (Headaces). Paste of leaves are applied externally over Vrna (Wounds). It is helpful in the quick healing and relieves burning sensation. It is also applied externally along with Kanjika in Galaganda (Goitre), Ganḍamāla (Lymphedinitits) and Mūtravṛddi (Hydrocele). Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrna: 3-6gms. PĀṢĀNABHEDA Latin: Berginia lingulata (Wall.) Engl. Fam: Saxifragaceae Hin: Pakanbheda, Vanapatraka, Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Aśmaghna, Giribhiṭ and Bhinnayōjanī. Guna karma (Properties and indications): Pashanabheda is Sītavīrya (Cold in potency), Tiktā (Bitter), Kaṣaya (Astringent) in taste, Bastiśodaka (Clears the bladder) and Bhedaka (Purgative). It cures diseases of Vāta doṣa, Arśas (Piles), Gulma (Abdominal tumors), Mūtrakṛcchra (Dysuria), Aśmari (Renal calculi), Hṛudroga (Cardiac diseases), Yoniroga (Female genital disorders), Prameha (Diabeties), Plīha roga (Spleen disorders), Sūla (Abdominal colic) and Vrna Wounds). Note: This is a highly contraversial drug. Following source plants equated with the Pāṣāṇabhēda Saxifraga lingulata wall. (Sagifragaceae). Aerva lanta Juss. (Amaranthaceae). Kalanchoe pinnata Pers. (Crassulaceae). Coleus aromaticus Benth. (Labiatae). Homonoia riparia Lour. (Euphorbiaceae). Rotula aquatic Lour. (Boraginaceae). Ocimum basilicum Linn (Labiatae). Iris Pseudacoras Linn (Iridaceae). Ammania baecifera Linn. (Lythraceae). Bridelia retusa Spreng. (Euphorbiaceae). Amongest the different plant taken, Bergenia lingulata Wall. is may considered as the original plant. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is found in temperate Himalayas from Kashmir to Bhutan and in Khasia hills at altitude of 1500 m. Swarūpa (Botanical description): A perennial herb with thick root stock.Stem short thick and fleshy. Leaves ovate or orbicular, 5-15 cm long, ciliate margin, cordate base, and glabrous. Flowers are arranged in cymose panicle, white, pink or purple in colour. Fruits round with long style. Prayojya anga (Part used): Mula (Roots). Chemical Constituents: Phenolic compound bergenin, Tannic acid, Flavonoids, Benzenoids, Gallic acid, Lactone, Glucose and Calcium oxalate

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 870):

पटोलपत्रं पित्तघं दीपनं पाचनं लघु । स्निग्थं वृष्यं तथोष्णं च ज्वरकासक्रिमिप्रणुत् ।।४०.।। गुडूचीपत्रमाग्नेयं सर्वज्वरहरं लघु । कषायं कटु तिक्त च स्वादुपाक रसायनम् ।।४१।। बल्यमुष्णं च संग्राहि हन्याद्दोषत्रयं तृषाम् । दाहप्रमेहवातासृक्कामलाकुष्ठपाण्डुताः ।।४२।। कासमर्दोऽरिमर्दश्च कासारिः कर्कशस्तथा । कासमर्ददलं रुच्यं वृष्यं कासविषास्त्रनुत् ।।४३।। मधुर कफवातघन पाचन कण्ङ्गशोधनम् । विशेषतः कासहर पित्तघन ग्राहक लघु ।।४४।।
answer_text: Guna karma (Properties and indications): Patola leaves Increases Pitta dosa, Dīpana (Appetizers), Pācana (Digestives), Laghu (Light for digestion), Snigdha (Oilyness), Vṛṣya (Aphrodisiac), Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency). It cures Jwara (Fever), Kāsa (Cough) and Kṛmi (Worm infestations). Note: Patola is described detail in Phala śāka varga. GUDÜCĪ PATRA Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): The leaves of Gudūcī are Agneya (Fire like property), Sarvajwarahara (Cures all types of fever), Laghu (Light for digestion), Kaṣāya (Astringent), Kaṭu (Pungent) and Tikta (Bitter) in taste, Madhura vīpaka (Sweet in post digestive), Rāsayana (Rejuvenators), Balya (Promotes strength), Uṣṇa vīrya (Hot in potency) and Grāhī (Absorbent). It cures diseases of Tridoṣas, Tṛṣṇā (Thirst), Dāha (Burning sensation), Prameha (Diabeties), Diseases of Vaṭa, Vātarakta (Gout), Kāmala (Jaundice), Kusta (Leprosy) and Pāndu (Anemia). Note: Details of drug Gudūcī is explained in Guḍūcyādī varga. KĀSAMARDA Latin: Cassia occidentalis Linn. Fam: Caesalpiniaceae Hin: Kasoundī Eng: The Negro coffee Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Arimarda, Kāsāri and Karkaśa. Guna karma (Properties and indications): Kāsamarda leaves are Rūcya (Promotes taste), Vrṣya (Aphrodisiac), Viṣānut (Cures posionous manifestations), Mādhura (Sweet) in taste, Subsides Kapha and Vaṭa, Pācana (Digestive), Kaṇṭaśodaka (Clears thoat), Grāhaka (Water absorbent) and Laghu (Light for digestion). Especially it cures Kāsa (Cough) and Diseases of Pitta. Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): A common weed found throughout india, Swarūpa (Botanical description): It is a smooth annual that can grow up to 2 m tall. Leaves are compound, leafilets, ovate lanceolate, 2.5-7.5 cm. long with a petiolar gland 3-5 mm., ovoid or subglobose. Flowers are 1-2 cm. across, yellow, arranged in axillary racems. Fruits are pods dark brown 8-12 cm long, 7-10 mm wide and curve slightly upward, contains dull brown 20-30 flattened seeds. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Mūla (Roots) Bīja (Seeds) Patra (Leaves). Chemical constituents: Cassiollin, Physcion, Occidentol I and II, Tannic acid, mucilage, Emodin

explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Saka Varga, Chapter 9, verse 870.

question:

answer_text: Digestive disease: The dried pulp is Kasaya (Astringent) in taste, brilliant cure in instances of Atisara (Diarrhoea) and Pravāhikā (Dysentery). Decoction of unripe bilva fruit added with Miśreya and Śuṇṭhī is administer in cases of Arsas (Piles). Diseases of Ear: Dried roots of Bilva is dipped in the neem oil and used as ear drops in case of Karnaşūla (Earache). Anti Diabetic: A prepared paste from bilva leaves and is well squeezed through a cloth and administer in the treatment of Prameha (Diabetes). External uses: Root bark is used in all types of Sotha (inflammation) and Vrna (Wounds). Mātrā (Dosage): Cūrṇa: 3-6gm, Swārasa: 10-20 ml, Kvatha: 10-50ml. GAMBHĀRĪ Latin: Gmelina arborea Linn. Fam: Verbenaceae Hin: Kambhar Eng: White teak Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Bhadraparṇī, Śriparṇī, Madhuparṇikā, Kāśmīrī, Kāśmarī, Hīra, Kāśmarya, Pītarohiṇī, Kṛṣṇavṛntā, Madhurasā and Mahākusumikā. Guṇa karma (Properties and indications): Gambhārī is Madhura (Sweet), Kaṣāya (Astringent) and Tikta (Bitter) in taste, Uşna vīrya (Hot in potency), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Dīpana (Appetizers), Pācana (Digestive), Mēdhya (Brain tonic) and Bhedaka (Purgative). It alleviates Brhma (Vertigo), Soṣa (Emaciation), Diseases of Vāta etc doṣa, Tṛṣṇā (Thrist), Āma (Undigested food), Śūla (Abdominal colic), Arśas (Piles), Viṣa (Poisonous manifestations), Dāha (Burning sensation) and Jvara (Fever). Gambhārī fruit is Bṛhmaṇa (Nourishing), Vrṣya (Aphrodisiac), Guru (Heavy for digestion), Keśya (Good for hairs), Rāsayana (Rejuvenator), subsides Vāta and Pitta doṣa. It is useful in Trṣṇā (Thrist), Diseases of Rakta, Kṣaya (Emaciation), Mūtraroga (Urinary diseases) and Vibandha (Constipation). It is Madhura vipaka (Sweet in post digestion), Sitā vīrya (Cold in potency), Singdha (Oilyness), Kaṣāya (Astringent) and Amla (Sour) in taste and Viśhuddhikrut (Laxitive). It relieves Dāha (Burning sensation), Tṛṣṇā (Thrist), diseases Vāta dosa, Rakta pitta (Haemorrage), Kṣata (Wounds) and Kṣaya (Emaciation). Utpattisthāna (Natural territory): It is available throughout india, common in southern india Konkan, Ceylon, Lower Himalayan regions, Eastern regions of Bengal and Bihar etc. Swarūpa (Botanical description): A medium sized deciduous tree grows upto 60ft high. Bark, corky, greenish outerside and yellowish within and young parts are covered without fine mealy pubescence. Leaves 10-20 cm by 7.5-15 cm, broadly ovate, accuminate apex, cordate base, and glabrous above when mature, tomentosed beneath. Petioles 5-8cm long, cylindrical puberulose glandular at the top. Flowers are small yellow colored usually 3- flowered cymes arranged in panicles. Fruit, Drupe, ovoid, 2-2.5 cm, smooth dark green turning yellow when ripe, consist 1-2 seeds. Prayojya aṅga (Part used): Mūlatvak (Root bark), Roots (Mūla)and Phala (Fruits). Chemical constituents: Resins, Alkaloids and Trace of Benzoic acid, Butyric acid and Tartaric acid
citation: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu — Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 289
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Guducyadi Varga, Chapter 3, verse 289.

Moreover, the patient has burning sensation and perianal suppuration in such cases
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 3.

question:

सात्रिपातिकमाह---महारुजमित्यादि । अश्मवद्धनोत्रतं पापाणवत् कठिनमुन्नतं च । मन इत्यादि मनोऽपहारिणं मनोवैकल्यकारिणं शरीरापहारिणं कुशत्ववैवर्ण्यकरम् अग्न्यपहारिण- मग्निवैषम्यकरें बलापहारिणमसामर्थ्यकरम् । ननु असाध्यमिति विरुद्धं सन्निपातोत्थिते मुल्मे न्निदोषघ्नो विधिहितः सु०३० इति सुश्रतवचनात् । नैवमु अयं च विकृति- विपमसमवेतोऽसाध्यः प्रकृतिसमसमवेतस्तु साध्य इत्याहुः । ननु सोऽप्यसाध्यः यदाह सुश्रतः--सर्वात्मके सर्वरुजोपपत्तिस्त चाप्यसाध्य प्रवदन्ति तज्जाः। सु०उ० इति । उच्यते तं चापीत्यपिशव्दादचिरोत्थितः साध्यो विश्वामित्रसंवादादिति गयदासः नवप्रसूताअहितभोजना या या चामगर्भ विस्जेदृतौं वा । वायुर्हि तस्याः परिग्रह्य रक्त करोति ग़ल्मं सरुजं सदाहम् । पेंतस्य - लिड़ेन - समानलिड़ेन - विशेषणं - चाप्यपरं - निबोध ॥ ॥ यः स्पन्दते पिणिडत एवं नालेष्ठिरात् सशूलः समगर्भलिङ्गः। स रोधिरः स्त्रीभव एव मुल्मो मारे व्यतीते दशमे चिकित्स्यः - - - - - - -
answer_text: Gulma Nidanam There could be doubt on the above narrative as one could ask how the incurability has been pronounced here when Susruta said, ‘Anti- Tridosa regimen should be followed in the treatment of gulma caused by tridosa (SS. Ut. 42.19). This issue has been addressed by the factor that the above (incurable variety) disease is of irregular origin while the one of regular origin is curable. However, Suśruta, himself has said that the gulma manifesting all the features is incurable (SS. UI. 42.13). According to Gayadasa and Visvamitra, the chronic gulma is incurable while the one, of a recent origin is to be considered curable. Rakta gulma (SS. Ut. 42. 13-14, CS. Ci. S. 5.19) The causes of raktagulma that resembles pittaja gulma in features are the vāta undergoing morbid increase along with rakta. It affects the women who have delivered recently and those indulging in un- suitable eatables, and the women who had frequent abortions or quick deliveries. In addition, it will have special features also such as emergence of a mass inside the stomach resembling a fetus. Never- theless, the palpating hand of the physician is unable to detect its different parts. The gulma causes pain at long intervals and has other features of pregnancy. After completion of ten months (of pseudo pregnancy) this raktagulma, special to women could be treated. (CS. Ci. 5.19) 15-16

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidana (Laghutrayi) (Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2):

तेषामेव प्राकृतज्वराणां चिकित्साविशेषार्थमुत्पत्तिक्रममाहवर्षास्वित्यादि । दृष्ट इति कपितः ग्रीष्मे संश्चितत्वात् । पित्तश्लेष्मान्वित इति तत्कालोचितपित्तकफानुबन्धः । यदुक्तं भबाष्पान्मेघनिष्यन्दात् पाकादम्लाज्जलस्य च । वर्षास्वग्निबले क्षीणे कुप्यन्ति पवनादयः ॥ ्रू च०सु० इति । कुर्यादिति छेदः । पित्तमित्यादि पित्तं च शरदि दुष्ट ज्वरं कुर्यादिति पर्वोक्तिन सम्बध्यते एवं कफो वसन्ते इत्यत्रापि योज्यम् । पित्तदुष्टिश्च शरदि वर्षासु सश्चितत्वात् । अनुबलोऽनुबन्धः तस्य च हेतुर्वार्षिकक्लेदानुवृत्तिरेव । तत्प्रकृत्येत्यादि तयोः पित्तश्लेष्मणोः प्रकृत्या स्वभावेन तत्कृतयोर्ज्वरयोरनशनाल्लङ्वनान्न भयं भवति । यदुक्तं कफपित्ते द्रवे धात् सहेते लड़्डनं महत् । आमक्षयादूध्वमतो वायुर्न सहते क्षणम् ।। इति । विसर्गाच्च हेतोर्नानशनाद्वयम् । वर्षाशरद्धेमन्ता विसर्गः तत्रोपचितवलाः प्राणिनो भवन्ति सोमस्य बलवत्त्वात शिशिर-वसन्त-ग्रीष्मास्त्वादानं तत्रापचितवलाः प्राणिनः सूर्यस्य बलवत्त्वादिति व्युत्पादितं शाख्रे । तत्प्रकृत्या विसर्गस्य इति पाठान्तरे तत्प्रकृत्या कफ-वात-पित्तप्रकृत्या विसर्गस्य च प्रकृत्येति योज्यम् । कफ इत्यादि । तं कफमनु वातपित्ते भवतः अनुबन्धरूपे भवत इत्यर्थः । हेतुश्चात्र वसन्तस्यादानमध्यत्वेनाग्नेयरूक्षत्वेन वातपित्तप्रकोपकत्वम् । यदुक्तं चरकेआदानमध्ये तस्यापि वातपित्तं भवेदनु। चचि इति । अत्र कफ- पित्तप्रकृत्या लङ्घनं युक्तमेव किन्त्वादानमध्यत्वेन न निर्भयं तत् कार्यम् । अत एव तत्र नानशनाद्रयम् इत्येतस्मात् पूर्वमेव पठितम् अन्यथा सर्वशेषे पठितं स्यादिति - यथास्वंश सर्वेषां प्रवृत्तिर्वृत्द्धिरेव वा । काले - - - - -
answer_text: To help decide the line of treatment this passage is suggesting the sequence of appearance of various features of the various Prakṛta (natural) fevers suggested above. The vata is accumulated in the summer season and gets provoked in the rainy season. As suggested by Caraka it happens so as the vapour is produced from earth's surface because of rains and because of the position of weakened digestion (owing to the water being acidic causing especial digestion or being amla vipāka) during the rainy season the vāla gets aggravated in this period (CS. Sii. 6.34). The pitta that is accumulated during the rainy season is vitiated in the sarat or winter season. In the fever naturally caused by pitta and kapha there would be no complications if the patient observes fasting and skips the regular meals. It is considered that kapha and pitta are liquid-based humours of the body. When these two are, vitiated langhan is the right choice until the ama (undigested food) is eliminated after which vāyu turns powerful and fasting appears impossible to continue. It may be noted that in the vāla jvara fasting does not help the patient. Fasting could be taken up without the fear of counter-effects when there is visargakāla or the rainy, winter, and autumn seasons. During this period, the human beings can easily withstand fasting. During the autumn, spring and summer seasons, the sun turns powerful and the living beings lose their strength. This period has been named as the Adāna Kāla. The reference ‘Due to the quality of Visargakāla’ is to be inferred as ‘due to the natural quality of kapha, vāta and pitta and also due to the quality of Visarga Kāla’. In the spring, kapha is followed by vāta and pitta because this season is the mid-period of Adāna Kāla and during that time vāta and pitta remain aggravated due to dryness in the atmosphere. It may be noted that Vasanta (spring) is the mid-period of Adāna Kāla and during this time dryness is predominant in the atmosphere (CS. Ci. 3.46). That is why the regulation ‘no fear of fasting’ is not to be adhered to during the spring season in the cases of fever. Hence, this statement has been made (by Vāgbhaṭa) before the description of kapha jvara in the spring and not at the end of the concerned passage in order to avoid generalization. (AH. Ni. 2.23/1) Only at the specified time during which the causative dosa is powerful, the fevers usually get their onset or exacerbation
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidānasthāna, Chapter 2.

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Madhava Nidanam (Part 2) (Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 51):

विरुद्धदुष्टाम्लविदाहिपित्तप्रकोपिपानान्नभुजो विदग्धमु। पित्तं स्वहेतूपचितं पुरा यत्तदम्लपित्तं प्रवदन्ति सन्तः॥ १॥ मधुकोशः कोठहेतौ पित्तश्लेष्मोल्लेखात् पित्तश्लेष्ममिलितरूपस्याम्लपित्तस्य निदानम्। निदानपूर्वकमम्लपित्तस्य स्वरूपमाह-विरुद्धेत्यादि। विरुद्ध क्षीरमत्स्यादि, दुष्ट व्यापन्नमन्ने, विदाहिस्थाने विदग्थेति पाठान्तरे विदग्धं भर्जित; पित्तप्रकोपिपानान्नभुज इति पित्तपकोपि पानं तक्रसुरादि, अन्नमाशुधान्यमाषादि; पित्तप्रकोपिपानान्नग्रहणे- नैवाम्लविदाहिनो ग्रहणे सिद्धे तदभिधानं विशेषार्थ, ‘पित्तप्रकोपणाद्यन्नभुज’ इति पाठान्तरे आदिशब्दात् कफादिप्रकोपणमन्नं गृह्यते। एवंविधपानान्नमुपभुझानस्य विदग्धं कुपितं, स्वहेतूपचितं पुरा यदिति वर्षास् जलौषधिगतविदाहादिभिः स्वहेतुभिरुपचितं संचयमापन्नम्। यदुक्त-‘वर्षास्वम्लविपाकित्वादद्विरोषधिभिस्तथा’ ( च.चि. ३) इति। विदाहाद्यम्लगुणोद्रिक्तं, पित्तमम्लपित्तम्॥ १॥ अविपाकक्लमोत्क्लेशतिक्ताम्लोद्रारगौरवैः । हृत्कण्ठदाहारुचिभिश्चाम्लपित्तं वदेद्विषक् ॥ २॥ मधुकोशः तस्य लिङ्गमाह-अविपाकेत्यादि। अविपाक ,इत्याहारापाकः, क्लमोऽनायासजः श्रमः । अम्लपित्ते पित्तं प्रधानं, वातकफावप्यत्रानुगौ गौरवोद्रारकम्पादिना जेयौ ॥ २ ॥ तृड्दाहमूर्च्छाभ्रममोहकारि प्रयात्यधो वा विविधप्रकारमु। ह्वल्लासकोठानलसादहर्षस्वेदाङुपीतत्वकरं कदाचित्॥ ३॥ मधुकोशः तस्य कदाचिदधऊर्ध्वगमनभेदाद्वि ( हिव ) विधस्याधोगतिं तावदाह-तुड्दाहेत्यादि । मूर्च्छा सर्वथा . ज्ञानशून्यत्वं, मोहो विपरीतज्ञानम्। प्रयात्यधो वेत्यत्र वातशब्दो भाव्यूर्ध्वगमनापेक्षया। विविधप्रकारमिति हरित्पीतकृष्णरक्तादिबहुवर्णत्वदुर्गन्धित्वयोगान्नानाविधम्। कदाचिदिति न सर्वकालम्॥ ३॥ वान्तं हरित्पीतकनीलकृष्णमारक्तरक्ताभमतीव चाम्लम्। मांसोदकाभं त्वतिपिच्छिलाच्छं श्लेष्मानुजातं विविधं रसेन॥ ४॥ भुक्ते विदग्धे त्वथवाऽप्यभुक्ते करोति तिक्ताम्लवमिं कदाचित्। करचरणदाहमौष्ण्यं महतीमरुचिं ज्वरं च कफपित्तम्। जनयति कण्डूमण्डलपिडकाशतनिचितगात्ररोगचयम्॥ ६॥ मधुकोशः ऊर्ध्वगतिमाह-वान्तमित्यादि। नीलं स्त्रिग्धकृष्णं, कृष्णं मर्दनाअनवंद्रक्षकृष्णं, आरक्तमीषल्लेहितं, रक्त- मन्तर्लोहितम्। मांसोदकाभमिति मांसधावनतोयाभं कृष्णलोहितमित्यर्थः। विविधं रसेनेति रसेन लवणकट्रतिक्ता- ख्येन नानारूपम्। करोति तिक्ताम्लवमिमिति तिक्तस्य अम्लस्य वा वमिं वान्तिं करोति। उद्रारमेवंविधमेवेति अत्र करोतीति संबध्यते, एवंविधमिति अम्लतिक्तम्। कण्ठहत्कुक्षिदाहं शिरसो रूजं चेति अत्रापि करोतीति संबध्यते। करचरणेत्यादि कण्ड्रमण्डलपिडकाशतनिचितमात्ररोगचयमिति कण्ड्वादिनिचितगात्रं च रोगचयं चेति द्वन्द्वः, तेन कण्ड्वादिनिचितगात्रं रोगचयं च करोतीत्यर्थः, रोगचयोऽविपाकोत्क्लेशादिः॥ ४–६॥ रोगोऽयमम्लपित्ताख्यो यत्नात् संसाध्यते नवः। चिरोत्थितो भवेद्याप्यः कृच्छूसाध्यः स कस्यचित्॥ ७॥ मधुकोशः साध्यत्वादिकमाह-रोग इत्यादि। कृच्छूसाध्यः स कस्यचिदिति हिताहाराचारशीलिनः कस्यचिच्चिरोत्थि- तोऽपि कृच्छ्रसाध्यः॥ ७॥ सानिलं सानिलकफं सकफं तच्च लक्षयेत्। दोषलिङ्गेन मतिमान् भिषङ्मोहकरं हि तत्॥ ८॥ कम्पप्रलापमूर्च्छांचिमिचिमिगात्रावसादशूलानि। तमसो दर्शनविभ्रमविमोहहर्षाण्यनिलकोपात् ॥ ९॥ कफनिष्ठीवनगौरवजडतारुचिशीतसादवमिलेपाः । दहनबलसादकण्डूनिद्राश्चिह्नं कफानुगते ॥ १० ॥ उभयमिदमेव चिह्नं मारुतकफसंभवे भवत्यम्ले। ( तिक्ताम्लकटुकोद्रारहत्कुक्षिकण्ठदाहकृत्॥ ११॥ ) भ्रमो मुर्च्छारूचिश्छर्दिरालस्यं च शिरोरुजा। प्रसेको मुखमाधुर्यं श्लेष्मपित्तस्य लक्षणम्॥ १२॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदानेऽम्लपित्तनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ५१॥ मधुकोशः तत्रैव , केवलानिलकफानिलकफमात्राणा संसर्गमाह-सानिलमित्यादि। भिषड्मोहकरमिति तस्योध्वाधः प्रवर्तमान्वेन च छर्द्यतीसाराभ्यां सकाशाद्वेदस्य दुर्जेयत्वाद्वैद्यमोहकरत्वम्। कफेत्यादि,सादवमिलेपा इत्यत्र सादोङ्कसादः, लेपः श्लेष्मलिप्तास्यता। दहनबलसादेति सादशब्दो दहनबलाभ्यां संबध्यते ॥ ८–१२ ॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायामम्लपित्तनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥ ५१ ॥
answer_text: The pitta which has already accumulated in the body gets further aggravated by consuming incompatible food-combinations, putrified foods, sour foods, over burnt (that cause over burning sensation) foods and pitta - aggravating foods and drinks and is called amlapitta. 1. Since pitta-slesma are mentioned as the aetiological factors of kotha, amlapitta which has the features like those of combination of pitta and Slesma is explained here. The aetiology and symptomatology of amlapitta are given. Viruddha (incompatible) means combinations of incompatible foods like milk and fish etc.. Dusta means stored and putrified. According to some other text, ‘Vidāha’ is replaced by Vidagdha' which means over fried or burnt. Pitta-aggravating drinks and foods means-takra (butter milk), surā (alcoholic bewerages) etc., fresh rice, black gram etc., foods. When amla (sour) and vidāhi (over-burnt) are included by saying, “pitta - aggravating drinks and food, specific mentioning of these is to denote the empha¬ sis.” If a different text, pitta prakopanādyannabhuja is taken, the word adi (etc., ) in this statement indicates the inclusion of kapha aggravating foods. Amlapitta Nidāna The pitta which is already accumulated due to its own accumulating factors, further becomes vidagdha (over burnt) by consumption of above drinks and food. The accumulation of pitta takes place due to factors causing over burning that take shelter in water, herbs etc., in the rainy season. Upacitam means accumulated. As t said by caraka, “during rainy season, ” the water and the herbs get amlapāki (sour nature)” Ca. Ci. 3. Pitta is called “amlapitta” due to enhanced amlatā (sourness) of vidāhi foods. 1. Symptomatology of Amlapitta Indigestion, fatigue, nausea, bitter and sour belching, heaviness of the body, burning sensation in the heart and throat and anorexia/distaste are to be pro¬ nounced by the physician as the feature of Amlapitta. 2. Avipāka means indigestion of the food. Klama is fatigue caused by no physical strain. Pitta is dominant dosa in amlapitta. Vāta and kapha are also followers here. These two are manifested by heaviness, belching and kampa etc.. 2. The downward movement of Amlapitta Associated with thirst, burning sensation, syncope, giddiness and delusion, it (Amlapitta) comes downwardly or otherwise with various types (colours and odours). There will be occassional manifestation of allergic patches on the skin, dullness of the digestive fire, horripilation, over sweating of the body and yellowish colour of the skin. There is occasional downward and upward movement of amlapitta. The downward movement is being explained here. Murccha (syncope) is having no senMādhavanidānaṃ sation at all; Moha (delusion) is perception of opposite sensation. Prayāti adho va (goes downwards or) vā is used here to indicate the future upward movement also. Vividhaprakāram (various types) means various colours like green, yellow and red and odours like bad odour etc., kadūcit means not always. 3. The upward movement of Amlapitta In the kapha associated amlapitta the vomitus is green, yellow, blue, black, light or dark red in colour, very sour in taste, the stuff looks like meat-washed water, very sticky, mixed with phlegm, some times salty, pungent and bitter in taste. On irregular digestion of food or even on empty stomach also, the patient vomits bitter and sour stuff; he belches with these tastes. He has associated symptoms like head ache. This kapha-associated amlapitta causes burning sensation in hands and feet, warmth in the body, distaste and fever. The body of the patient has itching, patches, innumerable vesicles and also indigestion, nausea etc., many other dis¬ eases. 4-6. Nilam means oily black; krsnam means dry, black like powdered collyrium. Araktam means slightly red; Raktābhaṃ means blood-red. Māṃsodakābhaṃ means like meat-washed water which is blackish - red in colour; Vividham rasena—with many tastes means - with salty, pungent, bitter etc., tastes. There will be vomitus of bitter or sour tasted stuff. The belching will also be of the same taste; karoti causes is related to burning sensation in the throat, heart and stomach. The body will be afflicted by itching, patches, vesicles etc., and also other diseases like indigestion, nausea etc.. 4-6. Amlapitta Nidāna Curability of Amlapitta This disease, called as Amlapitta is curable when it is of recent onset. The chronic one is prolonged and some times curable with difficulty. 7 Krcchra sadhyah sa kasyacit - some times, the yapya - prolongable chronic dis¬ eases is curable with difficulty when the individual follows homologous food habits and behavioural aspects. 7. The varieties of Amlapitta as per Vāta and Kapha affliction This disease which is confusing the physician is to be carefully identified as three type, viz., Sānila (associated with Vāta); Sānilakapha (associated with vāta and kapha) and Kakapha (associated with Kapha) basing on the symptoms of the con¬ cerned dosas. In Sanila type, there is trembling, delerium, syncope, pinning sensa¬ tion, looseness in the limbs, pain, darkness before the eyes, opposite perception, delusion and horrippulation. In sakapha type, there is dribbling of kapha from the mouth, heaviness in the body, lassitude, distaste, cold touch, looseness, vomittings, stickiness in the mouth, weakness of digestion, general weakness, itching sensation and sleep. In sānilakapha both of the above symptomatology is seen. In sakapha type which is also called slesmapitta there will also be belchings of bitter, sour and pungent tastes, burning sensation in the heart region, stomach and throat, giddi¬ ness, syncope, distaste, vomittings, lassitude, headache, salivation and sweet taste in the mouth. 8-12. Thus ends the chapter on diagnosis of Amlapitta (Hyperacidity) in Madhava's book on diagnosis written by Śrīmādhavakara. 51. Mādhavanidānaṃ “Bhisanmohakaram”-confusing the physician-means since there is upward and downward movement of Amlapitta which are similar to chardi (vomittings) and atisāra (diarrhoea), the physician will not be able to make out the differance and identify the real amlapitta. Thus it is puzzling to the physician. Sāda-depression is to the limbs, lepa - stickiness in the mouth. In the word dahanabala sāda, the term sada-depression or weakness applies to both dahana (digestive fire) and bala (general strength of the body). 8-12. Thus ends the diagnosis of Amlapitta in the Madhukosa commentary written by Srīkaṇṭha datta. 51. ****
explanation: Answer as given by the commentary on Nidanasthana (Uttarardha), Chapter 51.
context: विरुद्धदुष्टाम्लविदाहिपित्तप्रकोपिपानान्नभुजो विदग्धमु। पित्तं स्वहेतूपचितं पुरा यत्तदम्लपित्तं प्रवदन्ति सन्तः॥ १॥ मधुकोशः कोठहेतौ पित्तश्लेष्मोल्लेखात् पित्तश्लेष्ममिलितरूपस्याम्लपित्तस्य निदानम्। निदानपूर्वकमम्लपित्तस्य स्वरूपमाह-विरुद्धेत्यादि। विरुद्ध क्षीरमत्स्यादि, दुष्ट व्यापन्नमन्ने, विदाहिस्थाने विदग्थेति पाठान्तरे विदग्धं भर्जित; पित्तप्रकोपिपानान्नभुज इति पित्तपकोपि पानं तक्रसुरादि, अन्नमाशुधान्यमाषादि; पित्तप्रकोपिपानान्नग्रहणे- नैवाम्लविदाहिनो ग्रहणे सिद्धे तदभिधानं विशेषार्थ, ‘पित्तप्रकोपणाद्यन्नभुज’ इति पाठान्तरे आदिशब्दात् कफादिप्रकोपणमन्नं गृह्यते। एवंविधपानान्नमुपभुझानस्य विदग्धं कुपितं, स्वहेतूपचितं पुरा यदिति वर्षास् जलौषधिगतविदाहादिभिः स्वहेतुभिरुपचितं संचयमापन्नम्। यदुक्त-‘वर्षास्वम्लविपाकित्वादद्विरोषधिभिस्तथा’ ( च.चि. ३) इति। विदाहाद्यम्लगुणोद्रिक्तं, पित्तमम्लपित्तम्॥ १॥ अविपाकक्लमोत्क्लेशतिक्ताम्लोद्रारगौरवैः । हृत्कण्ठदाहारुचिभिश्चाम्लपित्तं वदेद्विषक् ॥ २॥ मधुकोशः तस्य लिङ्गमाह-अविपाकेत्यादि। अविपाक ,इत्याहारापाकः, क्लमोऽनायासजः श्रमः । अम्लपित्ते पित्तं प्रधानं, वातकफावप्यत्रानुगौ गौरवोद्रारकम्पादिना जेयौ ॥ २ ॥ तृड्दाहमूर्च्छाभ्रममोहकारि प्रयात्यधो वा विविधप्रकारमु। ह्वल्लासकोठानलसादहर्षस्वेदाङुपीतत्वकरं कदाचित्॥ ३॥ मधुकोशः तस्य कदाचिदधऊर्ध्वगमनभेदाद्वि ( हिव ) विधस्याधोगतिं तावदाह-तुड्दाहेत्यादि । मूर्च्छा सर्वथा . ज्ञानशून्यत्वं, मोहो विपरीतज्ञानम्। प्रयात्यधो वेत्यत्र वातशब्दो भाव्यूर्ध्वगमनापेक्षया। विविधप्रकारमिति हरित्पीतकृष्णरक्तादिबहुवर्णत्वदुर्गन्धित्वयोगान्नानाविधम्। कदाचिदिति न सर्वकालम्॥ ३॥ वान्तं हरित्पीतकनीलकृष्णमारक्तरक्ताभमतीव चाम्लम्। मांसोदकाभं त्वतिपिच्छिलाच्छं श्लेष्मानुजातं विविधं रसेन॥ ४॥ भुक्ते विदग्धे त्वथवाऽप्यभुक्ते करोति तिक्ताम्लवमिं कदाचित्। करचरणदाहमौष्ण्यं महतीमरुचिं ज्वरं च कफपित्तम्। जनयति कण्डूमण्डलपिडकाशतनिचितगात्ररोगचयम्॥ ६॥ मधुकोशः ऊर्ध्वगतिमाह-वान्तमित्यादि। नीलं स्त्रिग्धकृष्णं, कृष्णं मर्दनाअनवंद्रक्षकृष्णं, आरक्तमीषल्लेहितं, रक्त- मन्तर्लोहितम्। मांसोदकाभमिति मांसधावनतोयाभं कृष्णलोहितमित्यर्थः। विविधं रसेनेति रसेन लवणकट्रतिक्ता- ख्येन नानारूपम्। करोति तिक्ताम्लवमिमिति तिक्तस्य अम्लस्य वा वमिं वान्तिं करोति। उद्रारमेवंविधमेवेति अत्र करोतीति संबध्यते, एवंविधमिति अम्लतिक्तम्। कण्ठहत्कुक्षिदाहं शिरसो रूजं चेति अत्रापि करोतीति संबध्यते। करचरणेत्यादि कण्ड्रमण्डलपिडकाशतनिचितमात्ररोगचयमिति कण्ड्वादिनिचितगात्रं च रोगचयं चेति द्वन्द्वः, तेन कण्ड्वादिनिचितगात्रं रोगचयं च करोतीत्यर्थः, रोगचयोऽविपाकोत्क्लेशादिः॥ ४–६॥ रोगोऽयमम्लपित्ताख्यो यत्नात् संसाध्यते नवः। चिरोत्थितो भवेद्याप्यः कृच्छूसाध्यः स कस्यचित्॥ ७॥ मधुकोशः साध्यत्वादिकमाह-रोग इत्यादि। कृच्छूसाध्यः स कस्यचिदिति हिताहाराचारशीलिनः कस्यचिच्चिरोत्थि- तोऽपि कृच्छ्रसाध्यः॥ ७॥ सानिलं सानिलकफं सकफं तच्च लक्षयेत्। दोषलिङ्गेन मतिमान् भिषङ्मोहकरं हि तत्॥ ८॥ कम्पप्रलापमूर्च्छांचिमिचिमिगात्रावसादशूलानि। तमसो दर्शनविभ्रमविमोहहर्षाण्यनिलकोपात् ॥ ९॥ कफनिष्ठीवनगौरवजडतारुचिशीतसादवमिलेपाः । दहनबलसादकण्डूनिद्राश्चिह्नं कफानुगते ॥ १० ॥ उभयमिदमेव चिह्नं मारुतकफसंभवे भवत्यम्ले। ( तिक्ताम्लकटुकोद्रारहत्कुक्षिकण्ठदाहकृत्॥ ११॥ ) भ्रमो मुर्च्छारूचिश्छर्दिरालस्यं च शिरोरुजा। प्रसेको मुखमाधुर्यं श्लेष्मपित्तस्य लक्षणम्॥ १२॥ इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदानेऽम्लपित्तनिदानं समाप्तम्॥ ५१॥ मधुकोशः तत्रैव , केवलानिलकफानिलकफमात्राणा संसर्गमाह-सानिलमित्यादि। भिषड्मोहकरमिति तस्योध्वाधः प्रवर्तमान्वेन च छर्द्यतीसाराभ्यां सकाशाद्वेदस्य दुर्जेयत्वाद्वैद्यमोहकरत्वम्। कफेत्यादि,सादवमिलेपा इत्यत्र सादोङ्कसादः, लेपः श्लेष्मलिप्तास्यता। दहनबलसादेति सादशब्दो दहनबलाभ्यां संबध्यते ॥ ८–१२ ॥ इति श्रीकण्ठदत्तकृतायां मधुकोशव्याख्यायामम्लपित्तनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥ ५१ ॥

question:
Explain the meaning of the following verse from Bhavaprakasha Nighantu (Mamsa Varga, Chapter 10, verse 930):

वर्तीको वर्त्तकश्चित्रस्ततोऽन्या वर्त्तका स्मृता । वर्त्तकोऽग्निकरः श्रीतो ज्वरदोषत्रयापहः । सुरुष्यः शुक्रदो बल्यो वर्त्तकाऽल्पगुणा ततः ।।५३।। लावा विष्किरवर्गेंषु ते चतुर्धा मता बुधैः ।।५४।। पांशलो गौरकोऽन्यस्तु पौण्डुको दर्भरस्तथा । लावा वह्निकराः स्निग्धा गरघ्ना ग्राहका हिताः ।।५६।। पांशलः श्लेष्मलस्तेषु वीर्योष्णोऽनिलनाशनः । गौरो लघुतरो रूक्षो वह्निकारी त्रिदोषजित् ।।५६।। पौण्ड्रकः पित्तकृत्किञ्चिल्लधुर्वातकफापहः । दर्भरो रक्तपित्तघ्नो हृदामयहरो हिमः ।।५७।।
answer_text: Paryāyanāma (Synonyms): Vartīka and Citrā. Its another variety is Vartakā. Vartakā meat has possess lesser qualties. Lava (Common quail)

answer_text: Poisons of uccitinga and scorpion are predominant, in vata, those of insects are predominant in vata and pitta and hornets etc. are predominant in kapha. pr Treatment is given with, the measures having, qualities, contrary, to those of the doşa exhibiting predominant symptoms.
